title: Personal Finance
description: The fundamental principles of general business and related economic concepts are considered from the viewpoint of the consumer. Some of the topics studied are consumer buying and the use of credit, banking, insurance, investment, budgeting, and taxation.

title: Business Applications of Electronic Data Processing
description: An introductory course in electronic data processing with special emphasis on business applications. Effects of computers on business, systems analysis, FORTRAN machine language, comparison of data processing systems, and effect of computer on management decisionmaking. Special business problems are analyzed, programmed, and run on computers, and final reports are prepared from the information accumulated.

title: Interpretation of Business Data
description: An introductory course dealing with the collection, analysis, presentation, and interpretation of statistical data. Topics include frequency distributions, sampling, basic probability, decisionmaking, regression and correlation, and time series analysis. Prerequisites: ECON 200 and 201.

title: Principles of Business Law
description: The nature, role, and historical development of the law, and the structure and operation of our legal system. The essential elements of tort and contract law, and the effect of the law in the areas of consumer credit and economic relationships.

title: The Law of Business Associations
description: The principles of business law applicable to corporations, partnerships and agencies, in addition to the law of bankruptcy. Prerequisite: GBA 360.

title: Uniform Commercial Code Law
description: Principle articles of the Code including sales, commercial paper and security interests, in addition to the areas of creditor's rights and property law. Prerequisite: GBA 360.

title: Principles of Insurance
description: A survey of the major areas of insurance, such as fire, transportation, casualty, health, life insurance, and fidelity and surety bonds.

title: Life Insurance
description: Important methods of handling personal risks for business and individuals. An analysis of life insurance, annuities, pension plans, and social insurance. Special attention is given to the problems of underwriting, rate computation, and programming. Prerequisite: GBA 370.

title: Property Insurance
description: Study of fire and allied lines insurance, inland marine floaters, transportation, theft, and liability insurance, and employers' liability and workmen's compensation. Emphasis is placed on management of risks in business and on the use of insurance as a tool for handling these risks. Prerequisite: GBA 370.

title: Automobile Insurance
description: Analysis and evaluation of automobile insurance: the automobile hazard, principles underlying auto insurance, types of insurance, selection of risk, pricing, underwriting, marketing and claim administration and practices. The problem of the uninsured motorist. Crisis in auto insurance and reform proposals. Prerequisite: GBA 370.

title: Advanced Business Statistics
description: The more commonly used advanced statistical methods, with broad coverage of estimation, and tests of hypotheses, and including chisquare tests, analysis of variance, and advanced correlation and regression analysis. Prerequisite: GBA 320.

title: Real Estate
description: A survey of real estate with emphasis on the economic aspects of the development, marketing, and financing of real estate, valuation of resources, location and market analysis, and institutional influences on real estate activities. Attention is given to the growth and structure of urban areas and to emerging trends in all areas.

title: Business Administration
description: Integration at the senior level of fundamentals of operation or profitoriented firms producing goods in the private enterprise system. Emphasis is placed upon the case method in solving problems pertaining to decision making. Prerequisites recommended: ECON 200 and 201.

title: Independent Study in General Business Administration
description: An opportunity for students with superior scholastic records to study some special phase of business. The topic selected, methods of study, and credit hours allowed must be approved by the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Money and Banking
description: The role of money, historically and in our present economic system; history of the dual system of U. S. banking, and contrasting foreign banking systems; the Federal . Reserve System, including its checkcollection facilities and its management of bank reserves; economic significance of the volume of bank credit; interrelation of banking and government.

title: Consumer, Business, and Public Finance
description: The great importance in our national life of business credit, personal and consumer credit (including installment sales credit), bank credit, and public credit (federal, state, and municipal). Prerequisite: FIN 250.

title: Managerial Finance
description: Emphasis on principles and tools for analysis and decision making in the finance function.

title: International Finance
description: The foreign commerce of the United States (exports and imports); other factors affecting the international balance of payments and their settlement: services, capital movements, economic and military assistance; international banking; governmental and international agencies involved. Prerequisite: FIN 250. Prerequisite recommended: senior standing.

title: Business Finance
description: Principles underl ying the financial practices of business from the institutional and business manager points of view. Prerequisites: GBA 360 and ACC 203.

title: Investment Management
description: Problems of investment policy, including the study of types of investment risks, an introduction to security analysis, the analysis of investment requirements, and the kinds of investment policies.

title: Principles of Management
description: This course is founded on the four major managerial functions: planning, organizing, motivating, and controlling, which are applied to the process of management and the organic functions of a business enterprise primarily. Other significant concepts stressed are the importance of leadership, problem solving techniques applied to managerial situations, and the aspects of coordination, communica- Marketing 93 tion, and human relations necessary for an individual to be successful as a manager.

title: Personnel Administration
description: How to administer a personnel program in a business organization so as to deal effectively with such problems as selection, training, compensation, promotion, and transfer of workers; working conditions; employee services; and industrial relations. Prerequisites recommended: ECON 200 and 201.

title: Production Management
description: A basic study of methods of analysis applied in functional fields of production. Decision making and quantitative analysis of production problems arising in areas of methods analysis, work measurement, wage incentives, production planning and control, inventory control, plant layout, materials handling and quality control. Prerequisite: MGT 380 and GBA 320.

title: Office Management and Control
description: The management of the business office as a producing unit and the relation of the office routine to managerial control of the several other departments of a business through records, reports, and budgets. Prerequisites recommended: ECON 200 and MGT 380. Department of Marketing Lowry, Head; Ashley, Battle, Brown, Rink, Vanderleest, Venkatakrishna Business firms are rapidly adopting the marketing concept. Market forces and market opportunities are becoming the basis for designing whole systems of action. The marketing curriculum is planned with this viewpoint in mind. An opportunity is provided for the marketing student to acquire a sound foundation in liberal arts and a broad background in business and economics that will prepare him for work in most phases of business. In addition to this, the student has the opportunity to specialize in one of four areas: Option 1 is designed for those students interested in a career in the area of advertising; Option 2 provides the background for employment in marketing research; Option 3 emphasizes the training necessary for a career in retail store operation and management; and Option 4 is designed to prepare students for a career in sales and sales management. Advanced courses in marketing place particular emphasis on preparing students for advancement to management positions in marketing. The student will be guided by the curricular statements (see Curricula) and by the area requirements listed below. The student who is preparing for teaching business education will find marketing a part of the major and minor areas. Teaching areas are listed in the statement of the Department of Business Education and Office Administration. title: Principles of Marketing
description: A basic course in marketing which examines the roles of marketing in the fulfillment of the needs of consumers and industrial users. Marketing functions, marketing institutions, and changes in marketing brought about by economic and social forces.

title: Purchasing Management
description: A basic course in purchasing management. Principal topics considered are make or buy analysis, quality and quantity control, value analysis, price determination, sources of supply, the purchasing system, and legal aspects of purchasing. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Credits and Collections
description: Practices of business firms in granting credit both to other business firms and to individuals. Major sources of credit information, such as Dun and Bradstreet, and credit interchange bureaus will be examined. Credit limits, credit department operations, collection policy, and credit and collection problems are analyzed. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Selling and Consumer Behavior
description: Basic principles underlying the sales process. The role of selling in the economy, characteristics for success in selling, consumer motivation, the importance of prospecting, and emphasis on the stages of the sales presentation. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Sales Management
description: Functions of the sales manager: sales organization; recruiting, selecting, training, compensating, stimulating, controlling, and evaluating salesmen; planning sales quotas and territories. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Principles of Advertising
description: Analysis and evaluation of three concepts of advertising: as a factor in the marketing of goods and services, as a form of communications, and as an important social and economic institution. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Principles of Retailing
description: An investigation of store policies, organization, location, layout, buying, stock control, pricing, and sales promotion for retail stores. Prerequisite: MKT 270.

title: Marketing Simulation

To facilitate the learning and mastery of basic marketing management concepts and techniques by making decisions in a simulated marketingmanagementoriented environment. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Advertising Management
description: Promotional campaign building, determination of advertising effectiveness, and problems involving media selection and advertising appropriations. Prerequisite: MKT 340.

title: Retail Management—Cases and Problems
description: Investigation of such problems as the selection and training of retail personnel, accounting and stock control, retail pricing practices, product line selection, and coordination of retail store activities. Prerequisite: MKT 350.

title: Survey of Transportation
description: The economics of transportation—internal waterways, railways, highways, and airways in the United States; economic development of various means of transportation and accompanying regulatory problems. Rate, traffic service, and coordination problems of our transportation system. Advantages and disadvantages, trends, and peculiarities of each of the various modes of transportation.

title: International Marketing
description: Examines legal, economic, and cultural factors influencing marketing abroad. Commerical policies, practices, and techniques needed to locate and evaluate foreign markets, as well as the problems of pricing, promoting, and distributing products in international markets. Prerequisite: MKT 270. Marketing 95

title: Marketing Research
description: A basic course in marketing research. Nature and scope of marketing research; scientific method and research design; specific marketing research procedures; techniques of sampling; and research report, follow up, and evaluation of research process. Selected applications in areas of motivation, advertising, and product and sales control research. Prerequisites: MKT 270 and GBA 320.

title: Quantitative Marketing
description: Exploration of the various quantitative techniques that can be utilized in solving marketing problems. Principal topics considered are linear programming methods, game theory, Markov chains, probability theory in decision making, distribution cost analysis, and use of correlation. Prerequisite: GBA 320.

title: Marketing Management
description: Marketing by manufacturers as viewed from the marketing manager's position. Principal topics are selecting channels of distribution, determining demand, pricing policies, marketing legislation, advertising policies, and methods of selling. A case study approach. Prerequisites: MKT 340, 350, and GBA 320.

title: Internship in Marketing
description: The student works full time for a summer or a quarter as an intern on an approved program with a business firm under the supervision of the Department of Marketing. Periodic written reports of his job experiences are required. Open only to thirdquarter juniors and seniors with a major in marketing. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

description: For students who wish to conduct independent study in some phase of marketing. The course may consist of an experiment, library research, or the analysis of current marketing practices and methods. The programs of the college are administered through its five departments and two schools: the Departments of Art, Home Economics, Industrial Education and Technology, Library Science, and Nursing, the School of Music, and the School of Physical Education and Athletics. While teacher education is the objective of the greatest number of students enrolled in the college, curricula are available for professional preparation in each of the schools and departments represented in the college. The Department of Nursing, for example, is totally devoted to professional preparation of men and women for service in the field of nursing. Increasingly, the leadership and direction for the fine arts in America are emanating from college and university campuses. Outstanding artists and musicians are to be found on the faculties. The departments in the College of Fine and Applied Arts may be thought of as the "doing" or "performing" departments; thus the faculty and students are frequently engaged in displaying, demonstrating, or performing their skills and achievements before numerous publics attracted to them. The undergraduate program offers a core of experiences in the lower division dealing with a wide variety of exploration and investigation of ideas, principles, and materials. In the upper division more specific and concentrated experiences are provided in order that graduates may enter various art professions. The training of art teachers is a major responsibility of the department and provides a wide introduction and experience in art generally, and depth in one or two areas particularly. The emphasis is on the personal development of the student as an artist interested in the teaching process. A professional course of study in interior/ environmental design is offered to students seeking careers in this area. This fouryear course, which leads to a bachelor's degree, offers the students valuable inclass experience and the opportunity to work professionally. A program for the use of liberal arts students is also provided. The basic core is available as well as a number of general education offerings. The offerings provide an understanding of the institutions, practices, and devices of our past and present cultural systems and of the role, the duty, and the responsibility of professional artists in our contemporary society. The profession of home economics synthesizes knowledge drawn from its own research from the physical, biological, and social sciences and the arts and applies this knowledge to improving the lives of families and individuals. The breadth of the field of home economics emphasizes its importance. The eleven separate, but interrelated, fields of foods, nutrition, clothing, textiles, applied art, housing, household equipment, home management, family economics, child development, and family relations provide the foundations for the good health, satisfying and successful living, psychological balance, and good management which are essential for the development of the whole personality. Needs of individuals and families in the social environment of their time are of primary concern in determining the emphases given to the various aspects of home economics. Home economics aids in helping individuals and families to make intelligent decisions concerning all aspects of family life, including the social, economic, aesthetic, managerial, health, and ethical aspects of relations, child development, foods, clothing, and housing. Home economics prepares professional personnel to carry out its objectives through education, research, social welfare and public health, dietetics, and institutional administration and business. It shares with other fields the responsibility for developing perceptive, wellinformed citizens with the ability and the initiative to further conditions favorable to effective living. title: Teaching of Home Economics in the Secondary School
description: Analysis of pupil needs and the development of a home economics program to meet these needs. Organization of teaching units, selection and use of teaching methods, and development and use of devices for evaluating pupil growth.

title: Problems in Teaching Home Economics
description: Organization and administration of the total home economics program, including vocational homemaking program, city junior and senior high school programs, plans and equipment for the homemaking department. Prerequisite: HED 390.

title: Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of preparation stressed. Open to men and women.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Effects of different ingredients and/or methods on quality of products studied. Emphasis placed on recognition of a standard product and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve a standard product. Application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation stressed.

title: Meal Planning and Table Service
description: Principles and fundamentals in planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally ade- *See the professional education requirements for secondary teaching on the Teacher Education Curriculum for the requirement of an additional course in home economics: HED 390, the methods of teaching home economics. Home Economics 103 quate meals which are appetizing and appealing from the aesthetics standpoint. Economic factors considered. Attention is given to foods and types of table service for various occasions. Problems in food buying stressed. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental principles in nutrition and application to diets for children and normal adults.

title: Menu Planning for Quantity Food Service
description: Principles of nutrition applied to feeding of individuals and groups. Major emphasis placed on menu planning for institutions with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Limitations or problems relating to personnel, facilities, and type of patronage also stressed.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Stressed are the organization structure, application of principles of scientific management, and personnel administration. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning— Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping of food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industries and commercial operations. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Quantity Food Production and Purchasing
description: Offers opportunity for insight into factors related to quantity production and purchasing of foods. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Meal Planning and Food Preparation
description: Designed for the nonhome economics major. Basic principles of food buying, food preparation, meal planning and preparation, and table service, along with the study of nutritive value of food. Foods and service for different social occasions.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics. 1
description: Nutritional requirements of the individual from infancy through old age; energy value of foods in the light of chemistry and physiology of digestion; nutritive properties of foodstuffs. Dietaries are planned.

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Laboratory experience in university food service units. Prerequisites: HFN 220 and 340.

title: Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Problems pertaining to school lunchrooms, hospitals, and cafeterias as to personnel, management and organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens.

title: Institutional Equipment, Buying, and Layout
description: Stationary and small food equipment considered. Layouts of institutional kitchens planned. Field trips to institutional kitchens and equipment companies.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of the different foodstuffs so that their composition and physical and chemical properties can be understood. Recipes are investigated and methods of combining foods are developed and evaluated. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics 2
description: Food values with emphasis on mineral and vitamin content, recent literature in the field of nutrition. Prerequisites: HFN 340 and CHEM 231.

title: Diet in Disease
description: Pathological conditions resulting from various nutritional diseases, with emphasis upon causes and effects of malnutrition and its treatment. Planning and preparation of diets for abnormal conditions. Hospital laboratory experience provided. Prerequisite: HFN 340.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers; important considerations in purchasing foods and corresponding factors that determine them. Emphasis on ethics in buying.

title: Home Care of the Sick
description: Fundamentals of home nursing in relation to family living, including laboratory experience in nursing techniques. A Red Cross home nursing certificate may be earned by each student.

title: Principles of Home Art
description: Design and color principles, with practical application to home situations. Open to all students except those who have credit in ADS 104.

title: Family Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, art qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 1
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Emphasis on the management problems encountered by newly married couples in establishing a home. Open to all students.

title: Household Equipment
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Students will have an opportunity to plan, organize, and present demonstrations on household equipment.

title: Child Development
description: Understanding of the normal growth and development of preschool children. Emphasis on the child as a member of a family group. Principles of child guidance based on the physical, intellectual, emotional, and social needs of the child. Students observe children in daycare centers, kindergarten, or play school. Open to all students.

title: Infant Development
description: Processes of growth and development during the first two years with various physical, social, and emotional aspects being emphasized. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 2
description: Residence in the home management house offers opportunity to make practical application of the principles of homemaking. Prerequisite: HFN 220.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing for the consumer, including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, and factors to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Family Relations
description: Interpersonal relationships of family members, the forces impinging upon them today, and the changes that result in home and family living, courtship, and mate selection; preparation for marriage, marital adjustment, and parentchild relations. Open to all students.

title: Clothing Selection and Construction
description: Clothing selection and wardrobe planning. Fundamental principles of construction and their application to simple garments.

title: Advanced Clothing Construction
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HTC 104.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adaptation of standard patterns to individual proportions, designing of garments and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Prerequisite: HTC 104 and 203.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Clothing and Design
description: Special problems to meet students' needs in the clothing field. Unit on preparation of illustrative material for the teaching of clothing. Prerequisites: two other courses in clothing, or permission of the department head. Department of Industrial Education and Technology Sargent, Head; Bergman, Bumb, De- Keyser, Edwards, Gunderson, Gurbach, Henak, Kirkwood, Loats, Middleton, Nelson, Poucher, Reams, Ridgeway, South, Steele, Tomlinson, Tucker, Wagner, Wright The courses of the Department of Industrial Education and Technology are designed to meet the needs of students who are (1) qualifying for the teaching profession or allied professions of business and industry, (2) exploring the industrial world for possible occupations or vocations, or (3) seeking knowledge and understanding of our industrial society. The curricula for industrial education teachers are arranged in patterns which qualify persons as teachers of industrial arts at the elementary, junior high, and senior high school levels, vocationalindustrial education at the secondary and posthigh school levels, and technical education at the college level. To this end, curricula leading to the bachelor's degree, the master's degree, the specialist in education degree, and the joint doctor's degree are available. The offerings in graphic arts are used in preparation for positions in industry. The Two-Year Printing Technology Curriculum (see Curricula) provides for the development of technical skills essential in qualifying for supervisory positions. Upon successful corn- Pletion of the twoyear curriculum, each student receives the Associate in Science degree. Preparation for management positions in the graphic arts industry is provided in the fiveyear cooperative graphic arts management program leading to a baccalaureate degree (see the departmental major in cooperative graphic arts management following). A wide variety of industryrelated courses offers students many opportunities to explore occupational choices in the following industries: building construction, communications, manufacturing, power, and transportation. As part of a student's general studies program, the Department of Industrial Education and Technology offers courses which develop insight, understanding, and practical experience in regard to the production of goods and services, working conditions, industrial research and experimentation, and typical plant or factory organization. The student will be guided by the curricular statements (see Curricula) and by the area requirements listed below. title: Industry in Contemporary Society
description: An introduction to and an understanding of our complex industrial and technological society with emphasis on modern industrial organization, materials, processes, and related socioeconomic factors, including the development of manufacturing processes from crafts to automation. Laboratory experiences of a groupproblem type developed around typical industrial processes. Open to all students except those with teaching areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes which provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units are examined and evaluated.

title: Advanced Industrial Arts for Elementary Teachers
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of a wide variety of tools, materials, and industrial processes through the planning and organization of group activity units. Prerequisite: IED 364 or permission of the department head. GRAPHICS

title: Introduction to Graphics
description: Introductory experiences in the graphical representation of one-, two-, and threedimensional media. Theory of thirdangle projection, threedimensional coordinate notation, geometric constructions, orthographic projection, auxiliary projection, revolutions, and sections.

title: Advanced Graphics
description: A continuation of experiences gained in IED 103. Work in axonometric projection, oblique projection, perspective, intersections of planes and solids, lateral developments of geometric solids, and elements of graphical mathematics. Prerequisite: IED 103.

title: Architectural Drafting
description: Emphasis primarily on residential architecture. Basic principles of residential construction and planning, distinguishing features of different architectural styles, elementary load calculation, heat loss, and basic principles in use of transit.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Problems in Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in any of the following areas: structural design, gear design, graphic statics and dynamics, and architectural graphics. Prerequisite: IED 203.

title: Industrial Arts Design
description: Basic design principles are stressed, using both twoand threedimensional media; work with air brush, styrofoam, line drawings, and other types of materials. WOODS

title: Introduction to Woods
description: The nature and properties of wood and the manufacturing processes used to convert it from an extracted raw material to a wood product which fulfills a consumer need in American society. Some development of tool skills.

title: Woods 2
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213.

title: Advanced Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in processing modified wood materials. Additional emphasis upon mechanical and chemical conversion, particle and fiber processes, adhesives, treatments and coatings, drying, and wood production management. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Building Construction
description: Manufacture and use of building construction materials and products. Emphasis on problems of fabrication and materials in residence construction.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extensive study and experimentation in one or more of the following: wood lamination, wood treatment and coating, and production management of secondary wood processing. Prerequisite: IED 316. INDUSTRIAL CERAMICS

title: Introduction to Industrial Ceramics
description: Production and consumption of ceramic materials such as clay, glass, stone, plaster, abrasives, and cement in contemporary industrial technology. Experiences in casting, jiggering, throwing, extrusion, compression molding, glazing and firing, and lapidary processes.

title: Industrial Ceramics
description: Consideration of the importance of ceramics in modern technological advancements. Experiences in product design and moldmaking, advanced ceramic production forming processes, clay and glaze compounding, production decorating and glazing methods, and kiln maintenance and firing operations. Prerequisite: IED 127.

title: Research and Development in Industrial Ceramics
description: Extensive independent and group study and experimentation in the area of industrial ceramics. Prerequisite: IED 327. INDUSTRIAL PLASTICS

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: History, growth, organization, and future of the plastics industry. Thermoplastic and thermosetting materials and processes. Injection, extrusion, compression, blow and rotational molding, thermoforming and other processes. Common industrial plastics used.

title: Industrial Plastics Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problem solving approach. Injection, thermoforming, rotational, blow molding and/or extrusion dies constructed. Also fiberglass or foam molding. Prerequisite: IED 125.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. Mold making, materials testing and/or equipment design possible. Prerequisite: IED 325. METALS

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to metals with concentration in foundry, sheet metal, bench metal, art metal, forging, and spinning. Emphasis will also be placed on safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures.

title: Metals Machining
description: Work with the lathe, shaper, milling machines, surface grinder, metal cutting saws, and electrical discharge machine to develop a basic understanding of metal removal. Work will also involve the fundamentals of metallurgy and heat treating of carbon steels. Safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures will also be emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 231.

title: Foundry and Welding
description: Includes theory and techniques in welding a variety of welds in the flat position with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Limited work is done with TIG and MIG welding equipment. An introduction to the fundamentals of pattern design, permanent mold design, core design, and foundry techniques which provides a basic understanding of foundry practices. Emphasis will be placed on safety and maintenance. Prerequisite: IED 231.

title: Advanced Metals Machining
description: Includes cylindrical grinding, advanced milling machine work, electrical .discharge machining, tool design and grinding, metallurgy and materials testing. Emphasis is directed toward mathematics and science as it relates to machine setups and tool design. Setups relating to industrial production are discussed. Prerequisite: IED 333.

title: Problems in Sheet Metal and Machine Shop
description: Specialization in the theory and practice of sheet metal work, machine work, precision measurement, metal testing and inspection, and metallurgy. Prerequisite: IED 333 or 433.

title: Problems in Hot Metals
description: Specialization in advanced casting theory and techniques. Advanced welding will include horizontal, vertical, and overhead welding techniques with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Inert gas welding theory and techniques will be studied in depth. Will also include the fundamentals of forging practices. Prerequisite: IED 334. POWER

title: Introduction to Power and Transportation
description: Concentration on the internal combustion engine. A study of power sources, basic mechanisms, component systems, efficiencies and power measurement, and the utilization and application to transportation and industry, and direct energy converters.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: To acquire fundamental skills and teaching knowledge through experience related to power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasis on internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Factors involved in setting up a transportation unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite: IED 140.

title: Application of Power to Air Transportation
description: Airframe and aircraft engine systems involving limited maintenance experience in engine systems; instrumentation, principles of aerodynamics and flight control; internal reaction engines, and atmospheric effects on power output and avigation. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Application of Power to Water Transportation
description: Small boats, outboard engines, principles of operation, components systems, with particular attention to charging circuits, maintenance, boating laws and safety, inland waterways navigation, propeller theory, boat hulls, performance, and sailing. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate.

title: Special Problems in Hydraulics
description: An s int roduction to the fundamental principle of hydraulicircuitry. Characteristics of hydraulics, the functioning of component pa rts of hydraulic systems, and the aplication to power transmission and control. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Special Problems in Pneumatics
description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of pneumatic circuitry. Included -is a study of the characteristics of fluids, the functioning of components, and the development of pneumatic circuits and pneumatic logic control. ELECTRICITY-ELECTRONICS

title: Introduction to Electricity
description: Introductory experiences and exploration in the broad field of electricity with special emphasis upon means of producing and transmitting electron flow. Instruction in appropriate electrical projects and familiarization with electrical measuring instruments are important experiences in this course.

title: Applications of Electricity
description: Fundamental electrical theory, with special reference to applications in heating, lighting, electrolysis, electrical communication, and mechanical power. Individual and group experiences through the use of experiments and construction of appropriate projects. Prerequisite: IED 171.

title: Computer Fundamentals
description: Theory and basic circuits of computers. Laboratory activity will consist of group construction of basic computer circuits.

title: Advanced Applications of Electricity
description: Advanced experiences in electrical appliance design and repair, motor design and repair, and various types of interior wiring. Appropriate projects, teaching aids, and factors concerning the teaching of these areas. Prerequisite: IED 270.

title: Industrial Education Electronics
description: Theory of the vacuum tube and semiconductors, with special reference to their application in radio, television, and electronic circuits in industry. Individual and group experiences in project activity of the experimental, maintenance, and creative types. Prerequisite: IED 270.

title: Advanced Industrial Education Electronics
description: Special individual and group problems in advanced electrical circuitry involving most of the components of electrical circuits, with special emphasis upon thermionic emission tubes and photo emission devices. Complex problems assigned to groups of students will characterize the project activity. Prerequisite: IED 471. GRAPHIC ARTS

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: Introductory experiences in the various methods used by the graphic arts industry. These include letterpress and offset printing, drypoint and block etchings, silkscreen printing, embossing and gold leaf printing, marking devices, and bookbinding.

title: Letterpress Printing and Bookbinding
description: Fundamental letterpress theory is stressed, with experiences in layout, composition, imposition, presswork and bookbinding; single and twocolor platen presswork; and looseleaf and saddlestitch binding operations.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Principles and experiences involved in lithography as a printing process. Cold type composition, camera work, stripping, plate processing, and press work; line shots and halftones. Prerequisite: IED 281.

title: Problems in Graphic Arts
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisites: IED 385 and 386 except for students on the Printing Technology Curriculum. PROFESSIONAL

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: Manufacturing processes used by industries to convert raw materials into consumer products.

title: Characteristics of Industrial Materials
description: Experimental analysis of the mechanical properties of industrial materials. Laboratory experiences involve research and experimentation.

title: Introduction to American Industry
description: The American industrial complex. Emphasis on its organization, materials, processes, products, jigs and fixtures, and socioeconomic factors. For industrial education majors only. Prerequisites: 30 quarter hours of industrial education courses. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 161.

title: Instrumentation and Control
description: The basic principles of process instruments and control systems. Content includes measuring principles, electrical/electronic circuits, calibration and standards and fluidics.

title: Teaching Contemporary Industrial Education
description: Problems of organization and management related to industrial education learning activities. Objectives, terminology, evaluation methods, teaching devices, lesson plans, textbooks, equipment, and supplies are examined. Industrial education classes in public schools are observed. Prerequisites: A minimum of 12 quarter hours from the following courses: IED 103, 125, 127, 140, 171, 213, 231, or 281.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and • jobtraining programs are examined and evaluated.

title: American Industry Practicum
description: Advanced study of the American industrial complex with emphasis on designing and developing teaching materials and activities appropriate to class goals. Activities will be predominately studentidentified problems or research. Prerequisite: IED 361.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: A discussioncentered course in which individuals evaluate their internship experiences. Through these dialogues, individuals will become aware of a greater variety of situations. Prerequisite: a minimum of 4 hours in industrial internship courses. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned in this course. Open only to cooperative industrial technology majors.

title: Independent Studies in Industrial Education
description: Special investigation in industrial education on an independent basis. Experimental work, wide reading and development of research techniques and skills are emphasized. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Workshop in Industrial Education
description: Advanced study of new technological developments in related industries. Laboratory activities involve research and experimentation. Credit may be earned in the following areas: electricityelectronics, metals, graphics, power, building trades, graphic arts, and service occupations. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Curriculum Problems in Industrial Education
description: Criteria used in determining nature and content of learning experiences in industrial education classes. Teacher -pupil planning, group activities, and problemsolving methods. Textbooks and related industrial and government publications evaluated and course outlines developed. Prerequisites: A minimum of 12 quarter hours from the following courses: IED 103, 125, 127, 140, 171, 213, 231, or 281.

title: Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Individual and group studies of one or more major problems in the industrial education field, application of research techniques to the problems for solution, and reporting of findings.

title: Advanced Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Advanced study of problemsolving techniques in industrial education. Individual and group activities involving research and experimentation.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Education
description: Practice in various contemporary approaches to industrial education drawn from methods and curriculum problems courses. Students will plan and execute a teaching unit in one or more of the contemporary approaches to industrial education, preferably a public school. Prerequisites: IED 391 and 494.

title: Industrial Internship 1 (Quality Control)
description: Designed to give the trainee actual experience in quality control while on a work assignment in industry. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and Plant Manager.

title: Industrial Internship 1 (Sales, Promotion, and Advertising)
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual experience in the sales, promotion and advertising of a product while on a work assignment in industry. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and Plant Manager.

title: Theory and Practice in Letterpress Printing
description: Fundamentals of typography, handand powerfed presswork, basic bookbinding, and press maintenance and safety, while maintaining a production printing schedule.

title: Theory and Practice in Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Offset photolithographic experience covering the practice of camera operation, stripping, plate making, and offset press operation, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 181.

title: Theory and Practice in Commercial Printing
description: Use of the Franklin Price Catalog for letterpress and offset printing, paper schedules, postal rates, study of the Government Printing Office style book, and standard printing forms and correct terminology, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 182.

title: Quality Control in the Printing Industry
description: The ability to use the tools of quality control in the printing industry. Emphasis is given to the use of densitometry, correct register, proofreading, ink coverage, proper binding, cropping, paper and ink. Various other topics are considered.

title: Printing Estimating
description: Application of the Point System of Measurement; figuring the amount and cost of composition; basic size, thickness, and weight of paper stock; figuring and cutting paper stock; spoilage allowances; and figuring the cost of paper stock.

title: Internship in Printing Technology
description: A fiveweek internship in a printing industry, working under industrial standards and regulations in the type of printing industry preferred by the student, as much as possible. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Industrial Internship 2 (Work Measurement)
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual experience in work measurement while on a work assignment in industry. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and Plant Manager.

title: Industrial Internship 2 (Market Research)
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual experience in market research while on a work assignment in industry. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and Plant Manager.

title: Theory and Practice in Publications
description: Various publication formats that are commonly used by institutions and industries. Both offset and letterpress forms of makeup will be employed in maintaining publication schedules. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Theory and Practice in Estimating and Copyfitting
description: Participants will estimate costs, order appropriate stock, learn schedules, make layouts, compose forms, cut the stock, estimate waste, and other details in completely planning and executing a printing order on a previously made schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 281.

title: Theory and Practice in Color Printing and Process Work
description: Printing of letterpress and offset color work, involving technical procedures in color separation and the use of densitometer and the use of various kinds of printing plates for letterpress color work. The completion of the secondyear creative project is a requirement of this course. Prerequisite: ITE 282.

title: Color Process Printing
description: The photographic steps in making plates for photomechanical printing of color pictures. Both color reflection and color transparency copy are considered. Prerequisite: ITE 186.

title: Type Design and Copyfitting
description: The determination of the amount of area necessary for composition according to size and family of type by use of a slide rule. The study of modern type design and usage, as well as outstanding typographers and their contributions. The place of the advertising agency in modern display composition and its contributions. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Printing Mechanics and Press Design
description: Principles of operation of the platen, cylinder, and rotary printing presses. Presses and printing equipment will be studied, under four divisions: electricity and electronics; cams, gears, and pulleys; tools for adjustment and repair; and the proper use of lubricants. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Organized and orderly methods of planning production to gain more profit, sales, production, and work. Prerequisite: ITE 284.

title: Industrial Internship 3 (Plant Supervision)

School of Music Hargreaves, Director; Albright, Farley, Harmon, Niccum, Wakeland, Wolfe The School of Music embraces four departments: Music Education, Music History and Literature, Music Theory and Composition, and Musical Performance. Administrative efficiency and scholarly pursuits are enhanced by further subgroupings within these major areas, particularly in the case of Musical Performance with its several applied music committees. A full range of large and small performing ensembles—from the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, and the Ars Musica String Quartet to the Concert Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra—provides superb opportunities for listening or for active participation. Less usual groups such as the Harp Ensemble, the Collegium Musicum, the String Sinfonietta, the University Singers, and the Ball State Ballet accent the diversity of performing outlets on the Ball State campus. Any student on the campus, regardless of major, may audition for membership in the University concert organizations. In advance of selecting the field of music for concentration, the student will consult the Director of the School of Music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the University, a student with a concentration area in music must have proficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument, and a working knowledge of the rudiments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music will be given at times to be announced. If a student cannot meet requirements when he enters the University, he may make arrangements to meet them later. If he is lacking in the applied music requirement, he will study without credit until he can meet it. All students with a concentration area in music are expected to attend the weekly recital meeting and to perform there with a frequency advised by the individual teacher of applied music. Additional information will be found in the Music Student Handbook. In advance of completing registration procedure each quarter, the student will clear through the office of the Department of Musical Performance the names of the applied music teachers to whose classes he is to be assigned. Students wishing to qualify for certification as teachers of music in the public schools should refer to the appropriate curricular information listed under the Department of Music Education as well as in the area requirements which follow. Students wishing to prepare for careers in professional performance, in composition and arranging, or in scholarly activity and research, are encouraged to enroll in the appropriate departmental major. The departmental minors also may serve some of these goals, but the total number of hours required for their completion is kept at a level which will serve the student in a liberal arts orientation who seeks broad cultural development rather than specialized proficiency. When a student's work load permits, he may register for additional lessons in the selected minor field or in other minor fields, provided the approval of the Director of the School of Music has been secured. In advance of performing publicly, students are expected to consult their teachers of applied music. Practice rooms should be reserved in the office of the School of Music at the beginning of each quarter and term. Each student with a concentration area in music is advised to have a piano available for his use at a certain time daily, either at the University or elsewhere. All students with concentration areas in music will participate actively in ensembles according to their curricular requirements. Those planning to become directors of instrumental ensembles or supervisors of instrumental music ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the University bands and University orchestras, and vocalists preparing to become directors of choral activities ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the appropriate University choral groups. In addition, each student is expected to avail himself of the opportunities for musical broadening provided by membership in the ensembles outside his special field. Unless the foregoing conditions with respect to recital attendance and performance and with respect to the earning of ensemble credits are met, credit will not be given for major or minor study of instrument or voice. The student should make plans with the Director of the School of Music and with the several ensemble directors early in his University career to satisfy these requirements properly. Department of Music Education Carr, Acting Head; Burkart, Curt, Eberle, Nichols, Phillips, Wakeland The preparation of teachers of music for all scholastic levels is of primary concern within the School of Music. The task of becoming an effective music teacher not only involves developing a high degree of musicianship and scholarship, but requires of the teachermusician a sincere interest and skill in assisting others to develop musical responsiveness. Three major fields of specialization are provided for the student seeking to be certified as a music teacher. These include the teaching area major in music which prepares the student to teach instrumental, choral, and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve, the teaching major in choralgeneral music which prepares the student to teach choral and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve, and the teaching major in instrumental music which is preparation for teaching instrumental music in grades kindergarten through twelve. In addition to these three major fields of specialization, several minor • concentration areas in music are available to those who wish to attain a higher level of music competency by adding a minor concentration to a music teaching major, or for those who wish to combine the study of music with that of another subject. In order to graduate from Ball State University with a major or minor in any of the music teacher preparation fields a student must present evidence that he has equipped himself to handle certain musical and educational tasks. This evidence, in addition to the successful completion of the curriculum, is shown through the demonstration of a high level of proficiency in both his primary and secondary performance medias—symphonic instruments and/or voice, and piano.*

title: The Development and Administration of School Choral Activities
description: Analysis of the choral literature available for use in the secondary school as to its technical difficulty and suitability to choral groups of various sizes and musical backgrounds. The administration and supervision of choral activities, *Students completing a curriculum leading to teacher certification are expected to have completed a piano proficiency examination at the beginning of the junior year. A student may take the examination at any time during the freshman or sophomore year upon recommendation of his piano instructor. If after six terms of study for credit in the field of piano, as related to teacher education, the student is unable to pass the minimum entering proficiency, he will be advised to continue on the special applied basis without credit or to make other suitable arrangements so that he will be able to complete the minimum entering proficiency without which he will not be graduated. Music Education 119 including the general chorus, the selected groups, and the voice classes. Techniques of choral arranging.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Brass Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 221.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 223.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: Basic principle and application of piano tuning and the nomenclature and repair of the piano. An elective intended for students preparing for the field of music and others who may be interested in piano technology. Open to all students.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Advanced techniques of piano tuning, enabling the student to tune a piano independently. Principles of complete action adjustment and common minor repairs. Prerequisite: MUSED 240.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Complete repair and rebuilding of the piano. Prerequisite: MUSED 241. Open to all students.

title: Basic Musical Experiences for Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to develop creative musical responsiveness in students enrolled in the 2-year early elementary education program, and to demonstrate through laboratory experiences the application of creativity to the developmental characteristics of three-, four-, and fiveyear old children.

title: Children's Music: Lower Elementary Grades
description: Methods of teaching music to children in kindergarten and grades one through three. Basic theory of music, including notation; class participation in musical activities and in the use of simple musical instruments, song books, recordings, and audiovisual aids. Not open to those students who are majoring or specializing in music.

title: Keyboard Skills for Elementary Classroom Teachers
description: Preparation of students of varying musical backgrounds and abilities in the use of the piano for teaching music in the elementary schools. Not open to the student who is majoring or specializing in music.

title: Teaching and Administration of Instrumental Music
description: Using the skills developed in instrumental minor studies as a point of departure, the student in survey classes covers the techniques of related families of instruments. Proper care of equipment, organization of physical factors, teaching of instrumental classes, and developing instrumental ensembles are made the basis for lectures and class discussions. Piano and voice majors are advised to reserve this course for the senior year. Prerequisite: minor skills in brass, woodwind, and string instruments.

title: The Teaching of Music in the Elementary School
description: The problems of teaching and supervising music in the elementary school for music supervisors and special teachers of music. Lesson planning and teaching are done in the class, and contact is made with teaching situations through directed observation. Leading music series are studied. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113 or the equivalent.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Primary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in the first three grades; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors, which is a continuation of 351. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six: singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High School
description: An exploration of the scope and character of musical activities designed to supplement membership in the established performing groups of the public schools and to provide an outlet for the many students not concerned with public performance. Acquaintance with materials and techniques appropriate to the study of music literature and music theory.

title: Children's Music: Upper Elementary Grades
description: Music suitable for children in grades four, five, and six and methods of teaching this music. Partsinging and creative projects are given emphasis. New elements of musical theory are introduced and fundamentals are reviewed. Student participation in musical activities. Prerequisite: MUSED 264 and 265, or equivalent.

title: Music Appreciation, Materials, and Methods
description: Designed to enrich the musical background of the student in the common heritage of musical literature and to suggest methods for presenting these materials to children.

title: Administration and Planning of the Church Music Program
description: Formation and training of adult and children's choirs in churches. Congregational singing. Service planning. The clergy, the congregation, and the church musician.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 2
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in his handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, shortterm course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing. Contact with new materials and methods will be insured in part by the inclusion of two or more distinguished visiting instructors on the staff.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Second, ary
description: Provides experiences with the materials and activities of general music classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possibilities of instruction in music f or mstudents who are not active in the perfor ing groups of their schools. Prerequi site: MUSED 40.

title: The Orff Workshop—Beginning
description: opportunities for concentrated study, by m eans s of participation, observation, andiscu -sion, in some of the begining phases fresh and stimulating approach to children' s musical education created by Dr. Carl Orf. An emphasis is placed on the basic approaches to the Orff method of teaching mu -sic to children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The CO& Workshop—Intermediate
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the more advanced phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite: MUSED 443 or permission of the department head.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 2
description: Advanced study and experience in more specialized repairs on stringed instruments. Discussions and laboratory work including splicing, grafting, varnishing, carving and bow rehairing. Historical resume of stringed instruments and makers from the seventeenth to the twentieth century. Music History and Literature 121 Department of Music History and Literature Michael, Head; Fischer, Hodgson, Mackey, Pence, Tretick The music history and literature area of the School of Music serves the entire University through its program of general in education: the teacher n training through courses designed to broaden his understanding of the art he interprets to his students; the student of liberal arts through enhanced cultural and historical orientation; and the prospective graduate scholar or researcher through specialized courses exploring the great body of literature which has been accumulating in and about music for many centuries. MUSIC HISTORY AND LITERATURE (MUSLI) 100.Introduction to the Literature of Music. (2) An overview of the many forms of musical composition and of the media for their performance to be used as a basis for subsequent musical experiences. 101.Music for the Listener: An Introduction. 4) Introduction to the elements of music, followed by a study of musical styles through a survey of the literature of music. Lectures, films, classroom discussion, and recorded music supplemented by attendance concerts and recitals. No previous knowledge of music required. Not open to students with areas in music.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music Appreciation
description: Designed to help the student not majoring or specializing in music in his understanding and appreciation of the music with which he will come in contact through concerts, over the radio, and from other sources. Each student has access to a large collection of recorded music. Not open to students majoring or specializing in music.

title: Music History 1
description: The growth of music from its beginnings through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The origins of music, the development of notation, and the growth of early polyphonic forms. Open only to students with areas in music except by permission of the department head.

title: Music History 2
description: Changes in music from the late sixteenth century through the Baroque, the Rococo, and the Classical periods. The transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque, and the developments of opera, sonata, symphony, and the related forms. Prerequisite: MUSLI 101, 211, or permission of the department head.

title: Music History 3
description: Developments in music from the time of Beethoven to the present. Transition from the classical to romantic periods, the various reactions to Romanticism, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUSLI 101, 212, or permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Instrumental Music from the Time of Bach
description: The growth and development of musical forms and styles as they apply to music for orchestra and solo instruments from the late Baroque Period to our time. Prerequisite: MUSLI 100 or 200.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Following a brief survey of the early development of opera, there will be a more detailed consideration of examples of this genre from the middle of the eighteenth century to the present time. Prerequisite: MUSLI 100 or 200.

title: Choral and Vocal Solo Literature from Haydn to the Present
description: The development of the cantata, oratorio, mass, motet, anthem, and the lied; great masterworks in these forms. Prerequisite: MUSLI 100 or 200.

title: Ballet History
description: A history of ballet, tracing its beginnings, romantic heights, and contemporary trends.

title: Music Literature 2
description: A survey course in the major literature for solo performance. The contributions of major composers and schools of composition to each area of musical performance are explored in class activity. Individual members of the class are expected to pursue special projects in the literature of their performance majors. Prerequisite: MUSLI 100.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including the function of figured bass, significant contrapuntal developments, the evolution of opera, oratorio, and cantata, and the growth of various instrumental genres such as the concerto grosso, sonata, suite, and types of keyboard music. Prerequisite: MUSLI 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles which marked the transition from Baroque to Classic music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUSLI 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the nineteenth century and its relationship to the Romantic movement, the growth of chromatic harmony, the changes in traditional types such as the symphony and opera, the growth of the art song, the tone poem, and the character piece. Prerequisite: MUSLI 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Dance Notation 1
description: The beginnings of dance notation and an introduction to the main systems used today (Labonotation, Benesh, etc.). Prerequisite: some previous dance experience.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Restricted to students on the Honors Program.

title: Hymnody in Worship
description: Hymns in early Jewish and Western Christian tradition: their historical and liturgical context and contemporary use. A summary of Western religious thought as exposed in liturgical poetry. Prerequisites (except for auditors): HIST 151, 152 (or other courses in European or world history before 1914); or MUSLI 200, 211, 212, or 213; or equivalent background in history or music history. Technical proficiency in music is not required.

title: Church Choir Repertoire
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite (except for auditors): MUSLI 100, 200, 211, 212, or 213.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: Provides the superior student with an op_ portunity for guided reading and intensive study in an area of music history of particular interest to him and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisites (except for auditors): MUSLI 200, 211, 212, or 213; and the ability to read music.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 1
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Field Sources of American Musical Culture
description: Field study in major musical capitals, including the best known festival centers. Seminars scheduled in connection with planned travel are concerned with the orientation of members to the historic significance of composers native to the region, to the influence of nationalistic schools, and to the interaction of architectural and other physical matters with the musical output. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students on all curricula. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course. title: Form and Analysis
description: A survey of musical forms involving successively such units of structure as: the figure, motive, phrase, cadence, period. Song forms, singlemovement forms, contrapuntal forms, multimovement and multisectional forms are studied and performed in class. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Counterpoint
description: Exercises in melody writing using the ecclesiastical modes and the rhythmic organization of the sixteenth century liturgical style. Exercises in twoand threepart counterpoint incorporating the typical contrapuntal devices of the period as practiced by such composers as Lassus and Palestrina. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213. 371, 372, 373. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing short instrumental and vocal compositions with emphasis on developing the student's technical capacity to achieve freedom of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Musical Form
description: Study of the overall shaping of composition and of the variety of forces that can contribute to it such as: melodic structure, tonal organization, color, texture, thermatic development, and serialism. Special attention is paid to changing musical concepts and to newer techniques of analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 320.

title: Instrumentation
description: A study of the various instruments used in the orchestra and band with special attention to range, tone quality, dynamic range, methods of articulation, and the many unique characteristics requiring idiomatic treatment in notation and scoring.

title: Orchestration
description: Scoring for large and small orchestral ensembles. Particular attention is given to voice positioning, doubling, and textural deployment as regards harmonic weight and color. Prerequisite: MUSTH 441 or permission of the department head.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band and wind ensemble. Particular attention is given to voicing, sectional and crosssectional doubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 442.

title: Arranging for the Dance Band
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques as employed by current leading dance band and jazz arrangers, and the practice of writing and performing scores by members of the class. Prerequisite: MUSTH 442.

title: Styles of the Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: Investigation of stylistic devices of selected composers in the period between 1840 and the present. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213. 471, 472, 473. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing more complex and extended instrumental and voc al compositions with continued emphasis on the development of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 373.

title: Pedagogy of Music Theory
description: Review of the basic twoyear college theory sequence. Examination and Construction of methods for developing musical comprehension at educational levels from the prima ry grades through colege. Investigation of teaching aids including programmed material and electronic laboratory equipment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.
