title: German Literature in English Translation
description: Primarily a general education course. The aim of the course is to expose the non- German reader to great German writers and thinkers. The course may not be applied toward areas in German.

title: Hispanic Literature in Translation
description: Primarily a general education course, exposing the non-Spanish reader to the great writers of the Hispanic world. The course may not be applied toward areas in Spanish.

title: Linguistics and the Language Teacher
description: The application of general linguistic theory to the teaching and learning of foreign and second languages. Gives the language student some basic insights into how linguistics can help in the mastery of languages.

title: Introduction to Historical Linguistics
description: An introduction to the scientific study of language for students in foreign language. An elementary survey of the methods used in historical and comparative linguistic analysis with application to language usually taught in college. Gives the language student some basic insights into the linguistic principles that underline change in language.

title: Honors Colloquium in Foreign Literature
description: Selected readings and indepth exploration and discussion of literary currents, movements, authors, and themes found in foreign literature. Prerequisite: junior standing in the honors program' or permission of the department chairman. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Independent Study
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with individual instructor with Competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: The Teaching of Foreign Language in the Secondary School
description: Methods current in foreign language teaching in the junior and senior high schools. Directed observation of classes, specific problems of presentation, choice of texts, and organization of the teaching materials and supplementary aids are worked out in detail. Attention is given to the Report of the Foreign Language Study and to the courses of study recommended by the State Department of Education. Prerequisites: two years of college credit in French, German, Latin, or Spanish, or the equivalent.

title: The Teaching of Foreign Language in the Elementary School
description: Development of foreign language instruction in the elementary school. Curricula, training of teachers, and teaching methods; also phonemics, pronunciation, and a review of other basic language elements.

title: Beginning French
description: The first course in the French language.

title: Beginning French
description: Prerequisite: FR 101.

title: Beginning French (continued)
description: Prerequisite: FR 102 or one year of secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French
description: Prerequisite: one year of college French or two years of secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college French or two and onehalf years of •secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 20 hours of college French or two and onehalf years of secondary school French.

title: Conversation
description: Drill on pronunciation and speech patterns, dictation, and recording. The object of the course is to train in ability to speak French. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or FR 504.

title: Composition
description: Grammar and composition. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or FR 505.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the French language and the application of phonetics to the understanding and speaking of French. Use of the phonetic alphabet. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Civilization and Culture
description: Principal contributions made by the French nation in history, literature, music, and art. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Short Story
description: A study of the short story in French literature. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Classical Drama
description: The plays of Corneille, Racine, and Moliere. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: A study of French poetry with emphasis on the Symbolists and on contemporary poets. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Novel
description: Extensive reading in French novel. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in French drama. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Reading
description: Contemporary prose and poetry. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: French Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced French language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where French is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in French or by permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course with permission of the department chairman.

title: History of French Literature 1
description: From the beginnings to 1760. Literature of the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, and the Classical Age to 1760. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 2
description: The classical age from 1760 and the eighteenth century. Literature of the golden age of classicism and the eighteenthcentury philosophies. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 3
description: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The development of romanticism, realism, naturalism, and symbolism in French literature; literature of contemporary France. Prerequisites: two years of college or the equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college French or the equivalent, or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Beginning German
description: The first course i n the German language.

title: Beginning German
description: Prerequisite: GER 101.

title: Beginning German (continued)
description: Pre. requisite: GER 102 or one year of secondary school German.

title: Beginning German for Science Majors
description: Reading appropriate German texts to build the student's competence in reading and translating expository materials. Prerequisite: GER 105 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Intermediate German
description: Reading of representative German authors of moderate difficulty. Vocabulary, increased knowledge of German idiom, and practice in writing German are emphasized. Prerequisite: one year of college German or two years of secondary school German.

title: Intermediate German (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Intermediate German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of German authors in class. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Expository German
description: Review of essential German grammar. Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisite: one year of college German or two years of secondary school German.

title: Expository German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisites: 16 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German_

title: Expository German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Conversation
description: To increase fluency in speaking and ease of comprehension through, conversation. Prerequisites: two years of col: lege German or thequivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or GER 504.

title: Masterpieces
description: Classical and Romantic periods. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Drama
description: Drama and theories of the drama of Goethe, Schiller, Grillparzer, and Hebbel. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: Introduction to German lyric poetry and survey of historical development of this literary genre. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Prose
description: Growth and significance of modern prose writing in Germany. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in recent German drama. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Masterpieces
description: Realism, naturalism, and recent German literary periods. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Goethe
description: Intensive study of the life and of one or more of the works of Johann Wolfgang Goethe. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: German Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced German language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where German is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in German or by permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course with permission of the department chairman.

title: History of German Literature 1
description: From its beginnings to 1750. A survey of German literary trends from the earliest times to the Classical Period, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 2
description: From 1750 to 1850. A survey of the classical and romantic German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 3
description: From 1850 to the present. A survey of recent German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers, such as Moerike, Keller, Storm, Stifter, Thomas Mann, Hermann Hesse, and others. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Romanticism
description: Philosophical and historical background of German romanticism, the development of romantic poetry and prose. Prerequisite: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Poetic Realism
description: Emphasis on major works representative of Poetic Realism in German literature, including works of Adalbert Stif ter, Annette von Droste-Hulshoff, Gottfried Keller, C. F. Meyer, and Theodor Storm.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college German or the equivalent, or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Beginning Greek
description: The first course in the Greek language.

title: Beginning Greek
description: Prerequisite: GRK 101.

title: Beginning Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisite: GRK 102.

title: Intermediate Greek
description: Prerequisite: one year of college Greek or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of Greek or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 20 hours of Greek or the equivalent.

title: Advanced Greek
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Beginning Latin
description: The first course in the Latin language. Elements of Latin pronunciation, alphabet, rules of accent, syllabification, basic Latin grammar with oral and written exercises, reading of easy short selections from Latin authors, exercises in English derivatives, and consideration of the close connection of Latin and English vocabularies.

title: Beginning Latin
description: Continued emphasis on pronunciation, accent, and syllabification. Oral and written exercises of greater difficulty, reading of short selections from various Latin authors, exercises in dictation, practice in comprehension, with exercises requiring comprehension of speech patterns rather than memorization of single words, and presentation of more grammatical principles. Prerequisite: LAT 101.

title: Beginning Latin (continued)
description: Completion of presentation of the mechanics of Latin grammar. Stress on Latin syntax; logical structure in thought patterns. Rapid short readings illustrating grammatical principles. Emphasis on mastery of grammar through usage; oral and written exercises. Reading of relatively long essays, orations, and letters of Cicero, Pliny's letters, short poems of Horace, Catullus, and Vergil, longer reading selections chosen for importance in history of civilization rather than for illustration of grammatical principles. Prerequisite: LAT 102 or one year of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin
description: Rapid review of Latin grammar with oral and written exercises. Reading of selections from Caesar, Cicero, Pliny, Livy, Seneca, Vitruvius, and others, dealing with such topics as poetry, science, agriculture, medicine, religion, business, politics, history, private life, cooking, philosophy, education, and law. The aim is to interest Latin students in literary ideas drawn from representative works. Emphasis on vocabulary, increased knowledge of Latin idiom, and practice in writing Latin. Prerequisite: one year of college Latin or two years of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin (continued)
description: Emphasis on rapid reading for comprehension. Selected passages dealing with various aspects of man's life, together with comparisons taken from later periods. Celsus, De Medicina; Horace, Ars Poetica; Vitruvius, De Aqueductis; Pliny's Natural History; Cicero's De Officiis, De Republica, Epistulae, De Finibus, or Pro Archia; Juvenal, Satires; Pliny's letters (concerning the Christians), Terence's and Plautus' plays; and others. Prerequisites: 16 hours of college Latin or two and onehalf years of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin (continued)
description: Extensive reading of Roman comedies in class. Stress on rapid reading of Latin, particul arly of the dramatists, Plautus and Terence. Introduction to colloquial Latin and everyday idiomatic language. Development of plot, characterization, and artistic unity of Roman comedies. Background and originality of Roman comedy; contaminatio. Play production in Rome. Comparison of Greek and Roman comedy. Aristophanes' comedies; selected plays of Terence and Plautus. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college Latin or two and onehalf years of secondary school Latin.

title: The Latin Element in English
description: Latin borrowings, Latin prefixes, roots, and suffixes in English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required. Open to all students.

title: Roman Private and Public Life
description: All phases of Roman customs referred to in Latin commonly read in secondary school are carefully examined and understood. No reading knowledge of Latin required. Open to all students.

title: Classical Mythology
description: Primarily a general education course, dealing with myths of the Greeks and Romans and their use in literature and art. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required.

title: Prose Composition
description: For advanced students who are preparing to teach Latin. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or LAT 505.

title: Tacitus: Minor Works
description: Development of the ability to read Latin prose of moderate difficulty; literary style of Tacitus.

title: Suetonius: Lives of the Caesars
description: Reading with special reference to life and times of Suetonius.

title: Pliny: Letters
description: Selected letters by Pliny; Pliny's style.

title: Classical Literature in English Translation
description: Selected masterpieces of classical literature; historical development of the various types of literature as a background for further study in Latin and English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required.

title: Horace: Odes
description: Selections from the Odes, with emphasis on metrical forms, grammatical construction, and mythology.

title: The Latin Elegiac Poets
description: The elegies of Catullus, Tibullus, Propertius, and Ovid.

title: Ovid: The Metamorphoses
description: Selected readings from the Metamorphoses of Ovid, with special reference to the life and times of Ovid, and the poetic traditions of Classical Latin. Prerequisites: two years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Livy: History
description: Selected readings from Livy's Ab Urbe Condita, with a study of Livy's historial concept, and contrasted with the other greater Roman historians. Prerequisite: two years of college Latin or the equivalent. 420• Roman Comedy. (4) Selected plays of plautus and Terence with attention to influence on French and English literature.

title: Survey of Latin Literature
description: A comprehensive study of Latin literature through the reading of selections from Livius Andronicus to the church fathers. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Lucretius: De Rerum Natura
description: Selected readings from Lucretius' De Rerum Natura, with collateral studies in development of philosophic attitudes in classical times. Prerequisites: two years of college Latin Or the equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books I-VI
description: Readings from Books I-VI of the Aeneid of Vergil, with collateral studies in epic genre and the relationship to Homeric epic. Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books VII-XII
description: The last six books of the Aeneid, with collateral reading and reports. 435.Cicero: The Philosophic Works. (4) Readings from selected philosophic works of Cicero, as DeAnima, De Senectute, De Republica, with a related study of philosophical attitudes in classical times. Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Cicero: Selected Letters
description: Introduction to Roman epistolary style. Comparison with Pliny.

title: Caesar: The Civil War
description: Comparison with the Gallic wars.

title: Martial: Epigrams
description: Introduction to poetry of the Silver Age with emphasis on the epigram.

title: Juvenal: The Satires
description: Selected satires of Juvenal; study of Roman satire and its influence.

title: Medieval Latin Literature
description: Selected readings from the outstanding Latin authors of the Middle Ages, including Boethius, Cassiodorus, Walter Map, Ekkehart, and Hrotsvitha. Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Elementary Brazilian Portuguese
description: The first course in Brazilian Portuguese.

title: Elementary Brazilian Portuguese
description: Prerequisite: POR 101.

title: Elementary Brazilian Portuguese
description: Prerequisite: POR 102.

title: Beginning Russian
description: The first course in the Russian language.

title: Beginning Russian
description: Prerequisite: RUS 101.

title: Beginning Russian (continued)
description: Prerequisite: RUS 102 or one year of secondary school Russian.

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Prerequisite: one year of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Russian (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Russian (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 20 hours of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Conversation
description: Drill on pronunciation, dictation, and recording. The aim is to increase fluency in speaking and comprehension through conversation. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Composition
description: Grammar and composition to familiarize the student with the fine points of Russian grammar and to train him to express himself in the correct idiom. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the Russian language and the application of phonetics to the understanding and speaking of Russian. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Slavic Peoples and Cultures
description: A survey of the cultural developments of the Slays from ancient times to the present. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman. Not open to the student who has credit in RUS 509.

title: Short Story
description: The short story in Russian literature. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Drama
description: A survey of the plays and theories of drama in pre-Revolutionary Russia. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: Readings in Russian poetry from the nineteenth century to the present. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Soviet Russian Drama
description: Extensive reading in contemporary Soviet drama. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: History of the Russian Language
description: An introduction to the study of the historical development of the Russian language. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent. Not open to the student who has credit in RUS 520.

title: History of Russian Literature 1
description: A survey of Russian literature from the earliest times up to the nineteenth century, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: History of Russian Literature 2
description: A survey of Russian literature from the beginning of the nineteenth century to 1917, with illustrative readings from selected texts. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: History of Soviet Russian Literature
description: A survey of the period from 1917 to the present, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college Russian or the equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college Russian or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Beginning Spanish
description: The first course in the Spanish language.

title: Beginning Spanish
description: Prerequisite: SP 101.

title: Beginning Spanish (continued)
description: Prerequisite: SP 102 or one year of secondary school Spanish.

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: Prerequisite: one year of college Spanish or two years of secondary school Spanish.

title: Intermediate Spanish (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college Spanish or two and onehalf years of secondary school Spanish.

title: Intermediate Spanish (continued)

title: Phonetics
description: To investigate the formation of speech sounds in Spanish and the application of phonetics and phonemics to the understanding, speaking, and teaching of Spanish. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Spanish Civilization and Culture
description: An examination of Spanish history and culture through lectures, outside readings, and discussion. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Short Story
description: Selected short stories in Spanish literature. Prerequisites: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Novel
description: Selected novels in Spanish literature. Prerequisites: two years of collegegee Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Drama
description: Selected dramas in Spanish literature. Prerequisites: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: Selected poetry in Spanish literature. Prerequisites: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Latin-American Civilization and Culture
description: A panoramic view of the culture and customs of the various Latin-American countries. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Spanish Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced Spanish language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where Spanish is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in Spanish or by permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course with permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Conversation
description: Advanced practice in oral Spanish to increase fluency and authenticity through discussion and debate. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Golden-Age Theatre
description: An intensive study of Spain's greatest dramatists: Lope de Vega, Tirso de Molina, Alarcon, Calderon. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Literature of Ideas in Spanish
description: The literature of ideas of Spanish. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Contemporary Spanish-American Poetry
description: Some of the outstanding twentiethcentury Spanish-American poets from postmodernism to the present. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish Literature 1
description: Medieval period. The history of Spanish literature to the Golden Age. The theatre and its development. Didactic poetry and prose. Lyric poets. The Cancioneros. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish Literature 2
description: Classical period. The sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Prominent figures of the Golden Age of Spanish literature: Lope de Vega, Calderon de la Barca, Tirso de Molina, Gongora, Fray Luis de Leon, and others. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish Literature 3
description: Mod.- ern period. Espronceda, Zorrilla, Becquer, Perez Galdos, and others. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish-American Literature 1
description: Spanish-American literature from the discovery to the wars of independence. Emphasis on the major works of the period, including the cronicas, Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz, Alonso de Ercilla, and others. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish-American Literature 2
description: The history of Spanish-American literature from the wars of independence to modernism. Readings from Fernandez de Lizardi, Echeverria, Hernandez, Palma, Sarmiento, and others. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: History of Spanish-American Literature 3
description: Main trends in Spanish-American literature since the beginning of modernism, including modernism, realism, postmodernism and recent trends in social literature. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Don Quijote
description: The life of Cervantes and readings from Don Quijote. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Picaresque Novel
description: The picaresque novel and its origin in Spain; some attention to the modern picaresque. Reading of La Celestine, Vida de Lazarillo de Tormes, and others. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Mexican Theatre
description: Emphasis on Don Juan Ruiz de Alarcon. Some attention to minor writers and the present day movements. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Modernista Movement in Spanish America
description: Writers of the twentieth century. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Mexican and Spanish-American Novel
description: Novels of Spanish America and the Mexican Revolution. Prerequisites: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: The Generation of 1898 and Modern Spain
description: Selected readings from Azorin, Unamuno, Baroja, and others. Prerequisites; three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Nineteenth-Century Spanish Literature
description: Acquaints the student with the major literary works in all genres which reflect the changing currents of Spanish life and thought during the nineteenth century: romanticism, costumbrism, naturalism, and realism. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

title: Twentieth-Century Spanish Literature
description: Acquaints the 'student with the major literary works in all genres which reflect the changing currents of Spanish life and thought during this century. Readings will include works of the Generation of '98, the Generation of '27, Post-Civil War writers, contemporary authors, and assigned readings in critical and historical works about this period. Prerequisite: three years of college Spanish or the equivalent.

A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in Department of Geography and Geology 1.111•1n111n11111n Beatty, Chairman; Carmin, Cass, Dillon, Fisher, Grimes, Guha, Judy, Justham, Kane, Lyon, Martinson, Orr, Pal, Peterson, Roepke, Rothhaas, Samuelson, Showalter, Stevenson, VanMeter Geography, geology, and the earth sciences are concerned with the study of the earth and its resources. Geography focuses attention on the earth as the home of man, especially the interrelationships between the cultural and natural environments man has developed on the earth. The geography programs reflect these aspects of the discipline, offering general and specialized studies in cultural, physical, regional, and systematic topics. Curricular objectives are to educate and train geographers professionally for positions in elementary and secondary schools, colleges and universities, business and industry, and governmental agencies and to contribute to the liberal education of students. Geologists study the earth, with primary attention to its history, materials, processes, and structure. Today geologists are also concerned with the study of the moon and planets of our solar system. The geology programs are designed to train professional geologists for employment in colleges and universities, industry, and government, and to furnish professional and cultural education to students other than majors in the discipline. Earth science incorporates much of geology and the physical aspects of geography, as well as meteorology and astronomy. It provides a broad understanding of the physical environment for the student who does not expect to specialize in any one particular area of geology or geography. Earth science graduates are in increasing demand as teachers in secondary schools and colleges and universities throughout the United States. The geography and geology faculty specializes in various aspects within the discipline, including the cultural, physical, and systematic topics in geography; geomorphology, geophysics, mineralogy, petrography, paleontology, and oceanography in geology and in earth science. The Department of Geography and Geology prepares students for entrance to colleges or universities which offer degrees in meteorologic and oceanographic studies. A student who desires to pursue either of these fields towards an undergraduate degree should seek the advice of the departmental adviser as soon as possible after entering Ball State University. If he wishes to complete his undergraduate degree at Ball State, but to continue me- Geography and Geology 181 teorology or oceanography at the graduate level elsewhere, the student should seek this advice no later than the first quarter of his sophomore year. Basic minimum requirements to be included in first two years of undergraduate study at Ball State in preparation for study towards an undergraduate degree in meteorology elsewhere are generally 8 hours of geology, 8 hours of meteorology, 20 hours of mathematics, 12 hours of chemistry, 12 hours of physics, and 12 hours of foreign language. In addition to these 72 hours, the student who wishes to prepare for a graduate degree in meteorology elsewhere should include climatology and statistics. If the student plans to pursue a degree in agricultural meteorology at least 12 hours in biology will need to be included. Approximately 20 to 24 hours of advanced meteorology and climatology, not available at Ball State, is usually required for entrance to graduate work, and will be made up at the graduate level by assignment without credit. Acceptance into graduate work in oceanography will require a bachelor's degree in one of the sciences or mathematics, and generally including 4 hours of introductory oceanography, 23 hours of mathematics, inclusive of analytical geometry and calculus, 12 to 14 hours of general physics, and 15 to 16 hours of general chemistry. Students interested in oceanography should seek the advice of the departmental adviser. The adviser for physical and geological oceanography is located in the Department of Geography and Geology; the adviser for biological oceanography, in the Department of Biology.

title: Earth Science Field Problems
description: A series of meteorological, geological, pedological, and geodetic problems designed for beginning students in geography, earth sciences, and geology, as an introduction to physical processes in the atmosphere and near the surface of the earth and to the procedures by which the processes may be identified from their products. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110 or GEOL 101. Not open to the student who has credit in GEGE 383.

title: Seminar in Field Problems Design and Techniques
description: Discussion and identification of field problems in geography, geology, and earth science and the techniques and methods of solving these problems. Students are given the major responsibility of class plan development. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Field Methods
description: Methods and techniques of collecting, compiling, and analyzing geographic and geologic field data. Assignments include mapping projects and the use of field instruments in and near the campus and visits to places of pertinent course value within the state. Normal scheduling is Saturday mornings. Prerequisite: major or minor in geography, geology, or earth science, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Geography and Geology Field Camp
description: Extended application of field techniques to geographic and geologic problems in a specific area. Assignments include mapping projects, including a final written report and compilation of a map either on land use or general geology. Normal scheduling is first summer term (five weeks) in a selected area of western United States. Prerequisite: GEGE 382 or permission of the department chairman. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Teaching of Geography and Earth Science
description: Methods of teaching geography and earth science in secondary schools. Includes a review of appropriate textbooks, materials and equipment used in these disciplines, and problems of organization. Prerequisite: 24 hours of credit in geography or earth science, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Quantitative Methods
description: Application of quantitative techniques to geographical problems, with emphasis on the use of models in current geographic literature. Special emphasis will be given to the interpretation of recent findings in physical, urban, economic, and regional geography, and the preparation of the student to be able to apply these techniques to his research. Prerequisite: an elementary course in statistics, its equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Fundamentals of Physical Geography and Earth Science
description: Activities of man and his relationship to the physical environment. Selected topics from astronomy, geography, geology, meteorology, and climatology. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Elements of Physical Geography
description: The earth and its position in the universe, natural resources of climate, land forms, soils, vegetation, rocks and minerals, and animal life, with attention paid to the use and conservation of these resources.

title: World Economic Geography
description: World patterns of man's principal occupations and analysis of their distributional features. Emphasis on world interdependence on raw materials and finished products.

title: Cultural Geography
description: A spatial analysis of the interactions among selected elements of the physical and cultural environ. ment in relation to man. Special emphasis is placed on variations in these environmental relationships and their geographic significance.

title: Introductory Meteorology
description: Introducdon to meteorology, dealing with the general planetary circulation of the atmosphere, characteristics of the weather, and an examination of weather instruments. Includes a minimum of 4 hours assignment in the university weather station.

title: World Regional Geography
description: Geography of the world by regions, with selected regions given detailed analysis. Basic principles in the meaning of regions and ge o -graphic relationships within are given much emphasis.

title: Elements of Regional Geography
description: An introduction to the regional concept and regional method as related to elementary teaching. A geographic survey of the world, with selected topics and regions given detailed analysis. Prerequisite: major in elementary education or permission of the department chairman.

title: Geography of Exploration
description: Travels and discoveries of explorers who have made significant contributions to knowledge of the world and its geography, supplemented by selected readings from their works.

title: Map Reading and Interpretation
description: The reading and interpretation of maps, charts, and diagrams, how they are used as a major tool in geography, and how their use may be applied to other areas of study; also proper care and handling of maps.

title: Geography of the United States and Canada
description: A comprehensive survey of the geographic regions, settlement, land use, natural resources, and potentialities of the United States and Canada.

title: Geography of Europe
description: The physical and cultural environment of Europe with emphasis on the economic and political factors involved.

title: Geography of Soils and Vegetation
description: World patterns of soils and vegetation, with emphasis on regional differences and relationships to climate and physiography; their significance in man's use of the land. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, GEOL 101, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Land Utilization
description: The varied uses of the land, with emphasis on the major categories of rural use, but with attention given to urban and industrial uses. Water use in respect to the land. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, or permission of the department chairman. Geography and Geology 183

title: The Structure and Functions of Cities
description: A critical examination of the major structural and institutional parts of the city and of how topographic and climatic forces have influenced their development. An understanding of the city as a functionally interdependent structure and as a physical monument to its contemporary culture is fostered. 323.The Urban and Regional Form. (4) A survey of the origins of the urban and regional form and its relation to economic, social, and functional factors with special emphasis upon the modern American metropolis and its region. Prerequisite: GEOG 322 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Agricultural and Rural Geography
description: Agricultural development and the pattern of agriculture, particularly in respect to rural areas of the world. Attention is given the conflict of rural and agricultural development with urbanization and industrialization. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, 120, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Conservation
description: Distribution, utilization, and management of the natural resources with emphasis on the United States. Natural resources include minerals, air, soils, water, plants, animals, and man. Regularly scheduled laboratory and field work. Not open to the student who has credit in BIO 325 or NR 325.

title: Synoptic Meteorology
description: Application of the principles of meteorology to the development and analysis of weather maps and charts and the making of weather forecasts. Includes a minimum of 6 hours assignment in the university weather station. Prerequisite: GEOG 130 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Climatology
description: Introduction to the analysis and classification of climate, with emphasis on regional distribution. Basic techniques in handling climatic data. Prerequisite: GEOG 130, its equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Cartography and Graphics
description: Projections and other map elements, and the construction of maps, charts, and diagrams, with emphasis on the placement of distributional data.

title: Geography of Caribbean America
description: Physical and cultural landscape regions of Mexico, Central America, northern South America. and the islands of the Caribbean.

title: Geography of Australia and Oceania
description: A survey and analysis of the physical and cultural environment of Australia, New Zealand, and the southeast Pacific area. 354.Geography of East Asia. (4) A geographic survey and analysis of the physical and cultural environment of China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and coastal Asia.

title: Geography of South Asia
description: A geographic survey and analysis of the physical, economic, and human elements of the Indian subcontinent and adjacent countries to the east and west.

title: Geography of South America
description: Diverse natural and human environment of South America with special focus on the Amazon Basin, arid northeastern and industrial southern Brazil, the Argentine Pampa, and the ancient Indian cultures of Peru and Ecuador.

title: World Political Geography
description: Analysis of the physical and cultural characteristics of the nations of the world as these factors contribute to domestic and foreign relations and problems.

title: Geography of Transportation
description: Geographic considerations of the major modes of transportation of the world, and of transportation patterns.

title: Urban Geography
description: The distribution, classification, structure, and function of urban centers. Special attention is given to the geographic factors affecting urban development and growth.

title: Population Geography
description: A systematic and regional analysis of areal patterns of population distribution, composition, migration and growth, as well as the causes and consequences of these aspects on cultural landscape.

title: Geography of Regional Development
description: Geographical factors in the identity and development of specific regions of the world, both historical and modern. Special attention given to resource and river valley development. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, 120, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Meteorology
description: Air mass and storm analysis, with attention given to the physical characteristics of the air layers. Detailed forecasting techniques. Prerequisites: GEOG 330, one year of college physics, and mathematics through calculus, or permission of the department chairman. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Applied Climatology
description: The practical relationships of climate to the activities of man, especially in his adjustment to the physical and cultural environment. Included are the relationships pertinent to industrial development, and to local and regional planning, and the microrelationships of climate and architecture. Prerequisite: GEOG 110, 130, 331, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Aerial Photo Interpretation
description: Introduction to the interpretation of aerial photos as applied to studies in geography, geology, and related fields, including the physical and social sciences.

title: Geography of the Soviet Union
description: A, survey and analysis of the physical and cultural features of the Soviet Union, and the economic development of the country.

title: Geography of Africa
description: A survey and analysis of the physical and cultural environment of Africa, with special emphasis on recent political divisions.

title: Geography of Indiana
description: Topography, soils, climate, industries, commerce, and population of Indiana, with emphasis on physiography and economy.

title: Geography of Northwest Europe
description: Survey of the geography of the countries of northwestern Europe. Analysis of land use, physical landscape, and the economic and political development relationships.

title: Advanced Regional Geography
description: Ad.- vanced study of the geography of a selected region or regions of the world, with emphasis on the interrelationships of the physical, cultural, and human phenomena. Individual assignments. Prerequisite: introductory regional geography course or permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Advanced Cultural Geography
description: Influences of geographic environment on the development of man in major cultural regions of the world.

title: Distant Areas Field Studies
description: Study of physical, economic, and cultural geography in areas distant from the campus. Includes seminars arranged during travel. Prerequisite: major or minor in earth science, geography, or geology, or permission of the department chairman. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned, with repeated enrollment only by permission of the department chairman.

title: Seminar in Selected Studies in Geography
description: Small group discussion of geographic studies selected by instructional staff. Studies vary according to staff assignment. Prerequisite: an area in geography or earth science or permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: Readings and Special Studies in Geography and Earth Science
description: Assigned special studies in geography and earth science, including readings, research projects, teaching problems, and assignment to an undergraduate class. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course, as much as 4 hours of credit may be taken at one time.

title: Library Research in Geography
description: Basic research and teaching materials of geography. Designed to stimulate competence in understanding the availability and these materials.

title: History and Philosophy of Geograph y
description: The development of geographic knowledge and the status of the profession as e x_ pressed in the writings of the past and present by geographers and other individuals in related fields.

title: Physical Geology
description: An introductory study of the materials, structure, and surface features of the earth and the processes responsible for their development. Local area field trips. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Historical Geology
description: An introduction to the physical history of the earth in relationship to the development of life throughout geologic time. Emphasis on North America. Local area field trips. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Geomorphology
description: Landforms and the geologic processes responsible for their development. Local area field trips.

title: Mineralogy
description: Principles of crystallography and mineralogy and the relationships of minerals to the composition and types of rocks of the earth's crust. Laboratory work concerned with crystallographic operations and the identification of minerals by physical and chemical properties. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Hand Specimen Petrography
description: Principles concerning the formation, occurrence, and classification of rocks in the earth's crust. Description and identification of rocks in the laboratory and field. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 220 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Invertebrate Paleontology 1
description: Principles of paleontology as revealed by the invertebrate animal fossils of the earth. Fossils, fossilization, evolution, morphology, and invertebrate life associations of all the phyla from the Protozoa through the Brachiopoda throughout the various periods of earth history. Collection and identification of fossils in the field. Local area field trips. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Invertebrate Paleontology 2
description: Principles of paleontology as revealed by the invertebrate animal fossils of the earth. An extension of GEOL 308 to include all the phyla from the Mollusca through the Protochordata as they have occurred throughout the various periods of earth history. Collection and identification of fossils in the field. Local area field trips. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 308 or permission of the department chairman. use 0 f Geography and Geology 185

title: Structural Geology
description: An introduction to rockdeformation theory, analysis of deformed systems, and structural interpretation of mapped areas of deformed rocks. Prerequisite: GEOL 101 and 102 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Optical Mineralogy
description: Optical theory as it applies to the polarizing microscope and procedures for identification of minerals by Oil immersion and in thin section. Laboratory practice will be emphasized. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 220 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Stratigraphy
description: Principles, nomenclature, and practices of stratigraphy. The genesis and history of stratified rocks, sedimentation, induration, weathering, and methods of correlation. Local area field trips. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 101 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Geomorphology of North America
description: Emphasis on the occurrence, description, and geological and geomorphological problems of the geomorphic regions of North America. Nearby area field trips. Prerequisite: GEOL 101 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Oceanography
description: Description of the physical and organic environments of the oceans, and related problems. Prerequisite: GEOL 101 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Introduction to Geophysics
description: Physics of the earth; origin, age, gravity, magnetism, radioactivity, seismology, dynamics and internal structure; relation to processes active on or near the earth's surface. Prerequisites: GEOL 101, 102, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Geotectonics
description: Worldwide activity of the earth's interior, paleomagnetism, lower crust and upper mantle relations, sea floor spreading (continental drift), and theories of mountain building. Prerequisite: GEOL 101, 102, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Petrography-Petrology
description: Microscopic analyses of textures and mineralogies of rocks, together with a review of experimental and field data, provide the basis for constructing and evaluating thermodynamic theories of rock origins. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 320 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Sedimentology
description: Qualitative and quantitative description and statistical analysis of sediments and sedimentary rocks for the purpose of determining their depositional environments. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOL 320 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Geology of Indiana
description: The structure, rocks, fossils, landforms, economic resources, and geologic history of Indiana. Emphasis upon physical processes involved, especially Pleistocene glaciation. Designed for nonmajor students in the earth sciences, particularly teachers.

title: Geohydrology
description: Occurrence and movement of surface water and groundwater, with special reference to the effect of the geologic environment. Prerequisite: GEOL 101, MATH 111, NR 211, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Special Studies and Field Problems
description: Selected detailed geologic problems under the guidance of a qualified instructor. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. title: Roots of the Western Tradition
description: A survey of the principal historical and cultural developments of ancient and medieval times to 1300, with emphasis on those institutions and events of western civilization which furnish our own cultural heritage.

title: Birth of the Modern World
description: From 1300 to 1815, including such major topics as History 187 the Renaissance, Reformation, rise of modern nations, discovery and exploration, the Enlightenment, the French Revolution, nationalism, and the industrial revolution.

title: The World in Recent Times
description: Major world events and issues since 1815; industrialization and resulting ideologies; background, causes, and results of the two world wars; the rise and decline of the colonial empires with emerging nationalism; the impact of democratic, fascist, and communistic doctrines; nineteenth and twentieth century trends in thought; the effect of science on our age; arts; attempts at international organization and cooperation; and the revolution in expectations in the oneworld today.

title: Foundations of the United States, 1492- 1829
description: Survey of American history to 1829.

title: Development of the United States, 1829- 1900
description: Survey of the history of the United States from the era of Andrew Jackson to 1900.

title: The Recent Past in the United States, 1900 to the Present
description: Political, diplomatic, economic, cultural, and sociological forces and adjustments that have composed the history of the United States since 1900.

title: The Black Experience in America
description: A. survey of the negro in America from the sixteenth century to the present. Emphasis will be placed upon the impact of the negro on American culture and vice versa.

title: A Laboratory Course in American History
description: Designed to use documents and manuscripts to teach the nature of history and historical research. A complete departure from the regular lecture and textbook method. The student through his own research learns how the historian defines areas of research, selects sources, both primary and secondary, evaluates materials, and describes the findings. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course.

title: American Leaders
description: A biographical approach to American history. An evaluation of some of the leading Americans and their contributions in the fields of politics, business, letters, the arts, pure and applied science, and education.

title: History of Latin America, 1492 to Independence
description: The colonial history of Latin American (discovery, conquest, colonial system, independence movement), 1492-1825. Not open to the student who has credit in HIST 323.

title: History of Latin America, 1825 to Present
description: The history (political, economic, religious, intellectual) of Latin America, 1825 to the present. Not open to the student who has credit in HIST 323.

title: United States Urban History
description: Examines the inner dynamics of American cities and their place in the history of the United States. Provides students with an historical perspective and acquaints them with historical methods of examining cities.

title: Honors Colloquium in History
description: Exploration of selected issues in history. with emphasis upon individualized study and reporting. Restricted to honors students.

title: Colonial History of the United States, 1492-1754
description: The ideas and institutions developed in British North America whi( -h in the course of colonial development form ed a basis for American culture. Prerequisite: HIST 201.

title: The United States from Colony to Nation, 1754-1789
description: The political, constitutional, and economic issues that developed in the thirteen British colonies of North America and culminated in revolution, independence, and the founding of a new nation in the latter part of the eighteenth century. Prerequisite: HIST 201.

title: The Rise of Nationalism in the United States, 1789-1824
description: An analysis of the foundations of the United States as a new nation with emphasis upon the major social, political, economic, and diplomatic events of the period. Prerequisite: HIST 201.

title: Nationalism versus Sectionalism in the United States 1820-1860
description: An analysis of the major social, political, economic, and cultural developments in the United States with emphasis upon the major leaders and events involving the sectional conflict leading to the Civil War, 1820-1860. Prerequisite: IIIST 202.

title: The American Civil War and Reconstruction
description: Survey, analysis, and discussion of events, leaders, and movements, with special emphasis on causes, interpretation, and historiography of the period of national crisis and war followed by national reconstrw lion.

title: Progressivism and Imperialism: The United States, 1878-1918
description: America's rise to world significance at home and abroad b e_ tween 1878 and 1918, the political, Sucial, and economic problems entailed therein, and various efforts at reform.

title: From New Freedom through the New Deal
description: United States history from 1912 to 1940. The impact on the American people of the problems created by continuing industrialization at home and continued in`.olvement in a chaotic world. Prerequisite: MIST 203.

title: Recent United States History: World War II and Afterward
description: The role Of the United States in World War II and the reaction of the American people to poll tical economic, cultural, and social issues confronting the nation since that war. Prerequisite: HIST 203.

title: History of Indiana
description: Exploration, colonization, and development of the State from the earliest time to the present. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in United States history.

title: History of the Ante-Bellum South
description: History, institutions, political themes, and problems of the antebellum south. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in United States history.

title: History of the New South
description: Reconstruction, industrial and agricultural progress, social life, and the new leadership after 1865. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in United States history.

title: The Colonial and Trans-Appalachian Frontiers
description: American territorial expansion in the region east of the Mississippi River from the time of the first European penetration to about 1830. Emphasis on the geographic continuity in the settlement process and on the frontier's impact upon the settler in particular and American society in general.

title: The Trans-Mississippi Frontier
description: American territorial expansion in the region west of the Mississippi River, with emphasis on the nineteenth century. Focuses on exploration, the movement of settlers and the events which influenced their migration, and on the impact these events and the frontier had upon national development.

title: The History of Canada
description: A survey of the political, social, and economic history of Canada from the sixteenth century to the present. Emphasis will be placed on the events leading to the establishment of Canada and on United States-Canadian relations and problems.

title: History of Mexico
description: Mexico from the pre-Columbian era to the present with emphasis on the twentieth century and the Revolution of 1910.

title: The Spanish Borderlands
description: The area of cultural contact in North America among the Spanish, Anglo-American, and French empires from 1550 to 1850.

title: The Caribbean
description: The Central American republics and Cuba, Haiti, Santo Domingo, Venezuela, and Colombia since 1810, with emphasis on the twentieth century and the Cuban revolution.

title: United States Diplomatic History to 1914
description: History of United States diplomacy from the late colonial period to the eve of World War I. Prerequisite: 8 hours of United States history.

title: United States Diplomatic History since 1914
description: Survey of the foreign relations of the United States since the outbreak of World War I. Prerequisite: 8 hours of United States history.

title: Social and Intellectual History of the United States, 1607-1865
description: Survey of history of the ideas, knowledge, and values developed in philosophy, religion, literature, education, and science, and relationships to the total social milieu. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in United States history.

title: Social and Intellectual History of the United States, 1865 to the Present
description: Survey of the history of the ideas, knowledge, and values developed in philosophy, religion, literature, education, and science, and relationships to the total social milieu. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in United States history.

title: The History of American Culture
description: The history of pictorial art, architecture, music, literature, and science, and the impact of these areas on the social, economic, and political history of the country.

title: Economic History of the United States
description: Survey of our commercial, financial, agricultural, and industrial history. Prerequisites: ECON 200 and 201 or a combination of ECON 200 and 4 hours of credit in United States history, or 8 hours of credit in United States history. Not open to the student who has credit in ECON 410.

title: Historical Method and Bibliography
description: Techniques of research and documentation.

title: History and Historians
description: Historians whose writings are basic in major fields of history.

title: American Culture—Field Studies
description: A study of American culture, its art, economic life, educational systems, geography, history, industry, languages, music, and society. Students will travel through designated areas in North America. Prior to the trip, considerable reading in various fields relative to the nature of the course will be required. At the conclusion, papers will be required.

title: Reading and Special Study
description: Open only to seniors of special aptitude and interest which qualify them to do pregraduate investigation. Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with the individual instructor with special competence within the area involved.

title: The Rise of Modern Europe, 1500-1815
description: Political, social, and economic history of Europe from the Age of Discovery to the Congress of Vienna. Emphasis on political and economic events, the rise of national states, absolutism, religious developments, and the expansion of Europe overseas.

title: The Rise of Modern Europe, 1815 to the Present
description: Political, economic, social, and cultural history of Europe from the Congress History 189 of Vienna to the contemporary scene. Emphasis on political and economic events, the liberal and nationalist movements, industrialism, imperialism, World Wars I and II, and the conflict of national interests.

title: Cultural and Intellectual History of Modern Europe
description: Discovery, analysis, and discussion of major cultural and intellectual trends in the western world since 1815. Development of concepts and ideas that have shaped modern European history. Particular attention will be given to origins of contemporary problems and situations in the fine arts, literature, scholarship, political and economic philosophies, science, and social reform.

title: Diplomatic History of Europe, 1870- 1918
description: Background, immediate causes, and the course of World War I. Prerequisites: 8 hours of European history or permission of the department chairman.

title: European Diplomatic History from 1918 to the Present
description: Ideological, economic, social, and political factors which explain the current world situation. Prerequisites: 8 hours of European history. These prerequisites may be waived for students who convince the department chairman that they are in other ways qualified to take the course.

title: The Development of Ancient Greece
description: Greek political, social, and intellectual development in the Hellenic and Hellenistic periods. Emphasis on the rise and fall of Greek democracy. Prerequisite: one year of history.

title: The Development of Ancient Rome
description: Political, social, and intellectual development of Rome from the beginning of the Republic to approximately 500 A.D. Emphasis on the development of the characteristics of the Romans during the Republic and the effect on them of Greek ideas and world domination. Prerequisite: one year of history.

title: Medieval Civilization
description: Political, social and cultural developments of Europe from the late Roman Empire through the thirteenth century, with special emphasis on the history of medieval thought and art. Material covered in this course is basic for any further work in medieval history.

title: The Development of Byzantine Civilization
description: Surveys the eastern Roman Em pire from A.D. 329 to the fall of Constantin- - ople in A.D. 1453. Emphasis is placed on the history, social, political, and religious development as well as cultural contribution to western civilization. Prerequisite: HIST 151.

title: The Age of Renaissance, 1300-1600
description: Specialized study of the crises, changes, and cultural achievements of Europe in an age of transition. Particular attention will be given to such major topics as the late medieval crises, Italian and Northern Renaissance thought and art, the religious crisis of the sixteenth century, political, social, and economic problems of Renaissance Europe.

title: European Culture—Field Studies
description: A study of European culture, its art, economic life, educational systems, geography, industry, languages, music, and society. Students will travel through Europe. Prior to the trip, considerable reading in the various fields of European cultures will be required. At the conclusion, papers will be required.

title: Studies in European Culture
description: This offering is designed to take advantage of exchange professors who are on the Ball State University campus. Under their leadership students have a unique opportunity to learn about selected aspects of European life. Since the content of this course will vary from year to year with the background and training of the exchange professor, this course may be repeated by special arrangement with the curricular adviser and the Vice President for Instructional Affairs and Dean of Faculties.

title: History of France
description: A survey of the political, economic, and diplomatic history of France from Roman times to the present.

title: France in the Classical Age: The History of France from 1461 to the Death of Louis XIV in 1715
description: Origins and process of development of French politics, classic culture, society, and the State of France as a governed unit. Foundations of famous institutions such as monarchy, aristocracy, bourgeoisie, and Gallican Catholicism. The classic character, society, and culture of the modern Frenchman is described as it develops and influences the European character as a whole.

title: The French Revolution
description: Cultural implications of the French Revolution for mod-. ern times as well as the rise of the bourgeoisie.

title: The Rise of Modern Britain, 1485-1763
description: A survey of the political, social, and economic history of England in the Tudor, Stuart, and early Hanoverian periods. Emphasis on the rise of the national state, religious conflicts, the development of the power of Parliament, and overseas exploration and colonization.

title: History of England since 1763
description: A survey of the political, social, and economic development of England since the end of the Seven Years War. Emphasis on the modernization of the administrative machinery following the American Revolution, the development of the limited monarchy, the welfare state, and England's part in the two world wars of the twentieth century.

title: Constitutional History of England
description: A tracing of the development of the British constitutional system to the present time: development of the kingship, the common law, parliament, the Tudor and Stuart theories of government, the cabinet system, and political parties.

title: The Modern British Commonwealth and Empire
description: British imperial and Commonwealth development, 1815 to the present. The post-Napoleonic empire, the development of dominion status, the special problem of India, the Commonwealth, the world wars, the shrinking empire, the growing Commonwealth, and the situation today. Prerequisite: HIST 153 or the equivalent.

title: Modern Germany
description: Germany from 1890 to the present. The Reign of William II, the Weimar Republic, the Third Reich, and the period since World War II. Specific attention is given to social, intellectual, and cultural developments.

title: History of Tzarist Russia
description: The Russian state and her people from her earliest beginnings to the Revolution of 1917; basic chronology of political development; other phases of Russian culture; ethnology, religion, social changes, economic structure, education, literature, and diplomacy.

title: History of the Soviet Union
description: The development of the Soviet Union from the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 to the present, with emphasis on Soviet political and economic institutions and the role of the U.S.S.R. in world affairs. Prerequisite: HIST 486.

title: Modern History of East-Central Europe
description: Modern history of peoples who constitute present Poland, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, and the Baltic Republics. Stress is on their struggle for and preservation of national independence and the influence of the great powers on East-Central Europe. Topics are projected against the background of the m ost dominant European trends and problems. Prerequisite: HIST 153.

title: The Development of Post-Byzantine Civilization
description: Surveys the Post-Byzantine p e -riod from A.D. 1453 to 1821. Emphasis o n the role of Church in preserving the cultural, religious, and national identity and traditions of the Christian subjects in the Ottoman Empire. Prerequisite: HIST 151 or 464.

title: The Near East in Modern Times
description: The Turkish, Persian, and Arab world with particular emphasis on the period since 1800: the decay of traditional Near-Eastern institutions, the expansion of European influence, modernization, and the rise of national states in the Near East. Mainly an analytical study of the Eastern Question from 1774 to 1923. Deals with the causes (geographic, ethnic, religious, rise of nationalism) of the fall of the Ottoman Empire and its effects on all phases of European history in the period covered. Prerequisite: 8 hours of history or permission of the department chairman.

title: History of the Balkans since 1453
description: The development of the Balkans from the time of the Ottoman Conquest to the present with emphasis on the diversity of cultural and national development during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

title: The Far East
description: Survey of India, China, and Japan, and contiguous areas. Historical development of these countries, with an emphasis on their relations with Europe and America.

title: Introduction to Non-Western Civilizations
description: A broad survey of the Soviet Union and of the principal areas of the Middle East, Asia, Africa, and Latin America, with particular emphasis on contemporary political, economic, and social developments. title: Mass Communications Media
description: An overview of mass communications media as they exist, with emphasis paid to their historical development, structure, contemporary function, and operating methods. Not open to the student who has credit in RTV 100.

title: Reporting
description: Theory and practice in use of reporting skills and techniques as they apply to news gathering processes. Prerequisite or parallel recommended: JOURN 111.

title: Newswriting
description: Theory of newspaper writing, supplemented by practice in writing for the University student newspaper. If possible, students earning a journalism major or minor should enroll in JOURN 110 before taking JOURN 111, or be enrolled in both courses during the same term or quarter.

title: Copy Editing
description: Theory of newspaper copy editing, proofreading, and headline writing, supplemented by editing practice for the University student newspaper. 230§. Photojournalism. title: Journalistic Management
description: Theory of newspaper advertising, printing specifications, printing estimates, sales distribution, mailing budgets, bookkeeping, staff management, office management, and newspaper departmentalization.

title: History of Journalism
description: History of journalism in the United States from colonial times to the present, presenting the press as an institution against the background of the history of the nation.

title: Feature Writing
description: Types of feature articles suitable for newspaper and magazine use, supplemented by practice assignments for the University student newspaper. Prerequisite: JOURN 111 or permission of the director.

title: Advanced Newswriting
description: Theory and practice of writing specialized stories for news media. Supplemented by practical assignments for the University newspaper and radio station. Prerequisite: JOURN 111 or permission of the director.

title: Advertising Presentations and Research
description: Analysis of and practical experience in modern techniques of research in advertising and readership of publications with mass coverage. Approved methods for presenting research material and advertising data in an interesting and effective manner.

title: Yearbook
description: Theory of staff organization, illustrations, picture use, offset and letterpress yearbooks, typography, gathering and binding processes, style, theme, contents, and other production problems.

title: Journalism Practicum: Newseditorial
description: Advanced journalism practice in production activities for student staff members of student publications. Prerequisite: JOURN 111 or permission of the director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned in this course. No more than 6 hours of credit may be earned in combinations with JOURN 380, 381, 382, 383, and 384.

title: Journalism Practicum: Publication Management and Newspaper Advertising
description: Advanced journalism practice in production activities for student staff members of student publications. Prerequisite: JOURN 250 or permission of the director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned in this course. No more than 6 hours of credit may be earned in combinations of JOURN 380, 381, 382, 383, and 384.

title: Journalism Practicum: Photojournalism
description: Advanced journalism practice in production activities for student staff members of student publications. Prerequisite: JOURN 230 or permission of the director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned in this course. No more than 6 hours of credit may be earned in combinations of JOURN 380, 381, 382, 383, and 384.

title: Journalism Practicum: Yearbook
description: Advanced journalism practice in production activities for student staff members of student publications. Prerequisite: JOURN 370 or permission of the director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned in this course. No more than 6 hours of credit may be earned in combinations of JOURN 380, 381, 382, 383, and 384.

title: Journalism Practicum: Magazine
description: Advanced journalism practice in the production activities for student staff members of student publications. Prerequisite: JOURN 111 or permission of the director. Mathematics was defined by Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777-1855) as "the queen of the sciences." This statement reflects the interdependency of mathematics and the sciences. While still true, this observation must now be extended to cover all areas of human endeavor in the second half of the twentieth century. The student considering mathematics as a career should realize that emphasis in mathematics courses will change as he progresses through undergraduate and graduate school. The early emphasis on solving problems is later subordinated to the more important tasks of formulating and dealing effectively with mathematical structures and abstract ideas. Every prospective mathematician should plan to pursue his undergraduate and graduate training to the highest level of which he is capable.
