PREPHARMACY PROGRAM The Prepharmacy Program is for those students who wish to apply for admission to the School of Pharmacy of Butler University or the School of Pharmacy of Purdue University. The courses designated, when completed satisfactorily, will meet the preprofessional curricular requirements of either of these institutions at the end of the first year or at the end of the second year. The student is advised, however, that the number of applicants to a school of pharmacy usually exceeds the capacity of the school and that a selection of students is therefore necessary, taking into consideration such factors as scholastic standing, character, and professional aptitude. The student's attention is directed to the admission and residence requirements set forth in the Bulletins of the Butler and Purdue Schools of Pharmacy. This Prepharmacy Program does not lead to graduation from Ball State University. It merely provides a student with an approved sequence of courses for the first or the first two years of the complete fiveyear pharmacy program of either of the two universities. Furthermore, physical education is not a part of this program, but a student who drops out of the prepharmacy program and elects to follow a degree program of Ball State University will be expected to meet physical education general course requirements and all other requirements of the elected University curriculum. A careful arrangement of the program for each year is essential in order that courses may be completed in sequence and in the allotted time. Copies of the program arranged by quarters may be obtained from the Chairman of the Biology Department or the member of the Biology Department appointed by the chairman to serve as preprofessional adviser for students on this program. The program is subject to minor differences between the School of Pharmacy of Purdue University and the School of Pharmacy of Butler University as to admission requirements. General requirements in the first year at Ball State University are a minimum of 46 quarter hours of course credits, including two courses in English and one course in general psychology. Specific courses in science include two courses in biology, three courses in human anatomy, and two courses in mathematics. General requirements for the second year are a minimum of 52 hours of course credits, including one course in business education, three courses in history, and one course in economics. Specific requirements in science include five courses in chemistry and three courses in physics.

title: Man and the Life Sciences
description: Basic biological ideas and knowledge aimed at an understanding of the life processes held in common by all organisms. The physical basis of life, development, heredity, and evolution, and consideration of current biological problems confronting man. Not open to the student who has credit in BIO 102 or 111.

title: Introduction to Biological Sciences
description: Fundamentals of major areas of biology. The nature of the cell and protoplasm, reproduction, development, genetics, and evolution. Open only to students with a major in elementary education.

title: Field Biology and Conservation
description: Principles of ecology and conservation and survey of the plant and animal kingdoms. Field and laboratory work dealing with trees, other plants, insects, birds, ecological processes, and conservation practices. Open only to students with a major in elementary education.

title: Principles of Biology
description: Principles of biology including the physical basis of life, cell structure and function, genetics, reproduction, development, evolution, ecology, and systematics. Not open to the student who has credit in BIO 100 or 102.

title: Principles of Biology
description: Continuation of BIO 111. Prerequisite: BIO 111 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Animal Biology
description: Major animal phyla with emphasis on structure, function, classification and phylogenetic relationships. Some consideration is given to local forms. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Plant Biology
description: Major plant groups with emphasis on structure, function, classification and phylogenetic relationships. Some consideration is given to local forms. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Microbiology
description: Microorganisms including representative protozoa, bacteria, viruses, fungi, and algae. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Genetics
description: Basic principles of heredity and variation with emphasis on meiosis, the mechanisms of heredity, Mendelian principles, linkage and crossingover, mutation, and the nature of the hereditary material. Some attention to human and applied genetics. Prerequisite: BIO 112.

title: Developmental Biology
description: Normal development in plant and animal systems. Synthesis of current knowledge of the factors contributing to the development of a single cell into a differentiated organism in addition to the related phenomena of metamorphosis, regeneration, and growth. Prerequisites: BIO 211; BIO 212 (or permission of the department chairman); and CHEM 130 or 2:30.

title: Ecology
description: The relation of organisms to their physicalchemical environment and to each other. Plant and animal societies. Some attention to human and applied ecology. One weekend field trip required in addition to regular laboratory periods. Prerequisites: BIO 211 and 212, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Conservation
description: Distribution, utilization, and management of the natural resources with emphasis on the United States. Natural resources including minerals, air, soils, water, plants, animals, and man. Laboratory and field work included. Not open to the student who has credit in GEOG 325, NR 101, or 325.

title: Bacteriology
description: Bacteria with emphasis on morphology and physiology. Laboratory techniques in culturing, isolating, and identifying bacteria. Prerequisites: BIO 213, and CHEM 130 or 230, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Microtechnique 1
description: Methods and preparation of biological materials for teaching and research, including work in hematology, vital staining, photomicrography, and preparation of smears, squashes, and whole mounts. Three twohour laboratorylecture periods per week. Prerequisite: BIO 213 and two courses in college chemistry.

title: Microtechnique 2
description: Preparation of sectioned tissues and histochemical treatment of materials, including the preparation of paraffin and frozen plant and animal sections, and photomicrography. Recommended for students in research or in medical or laboratory fields. Three twohour laboratorylecture periods per week. Prerequisite: BIO 213, and 12 quarter hours of college chemistry.

title: The Teaching of Biology in the Secondary School
description: Philosophy and methods in biology teaching. Emphasis on laboratory investigations. Concepts and conceptual schemes in biology. Levels of organization in secondary school biology courses. Evaluation of learning in biology. Supplies, equipment, and facilities. Prerequisites: BIO 211, 212, and 213. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Developments in Modern Biology
description: Designed to integrate and enhance understanding of basic principles of biology. Recent discoveries in biology and their implications in the biological sciences are stressed. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairman.

title: Cell Biology
description: An introduction to the biology of the cell, including the nature of the organization of the cell, cell environment, plasma membrane and transport, cell metabolism, and the work performed by cells. Prerequisites: BIO 211, 212, and CHEM 130 or 230.

title: Field Biology of Distant Areas
description: Includes study of the sciences peculiar to selected geographic areas. Ecology, flora, and fauna. Travel may be by air. Seminars may be scheduled regularly throughout the course. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Radiobiology
description: The use of radiation equipment and radioactive isotopes in the biological sciences. Experiments and projects involving living plants and animals. Prerequisite: BIO 211, 212, CHEM 130 or 230, and PHYCS 110 or 120.

title: Biophysics
description: Physics of motion and locomotion in organisms, concept of wave motion, principles of sound and hearing, atomic structure, electrochemical phenomena in biological systems, electromagnetic spectrum and ramifications in biology and medicine, artificial and natural radioactivity, tracer techniques, atomic fallout, and biological problems of space flight. Prerequisites: BIO 211, 212, CHEM 130 or 230, and PHYCS 110 or 120.

title: Evolution
description: The principles of evolution. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 100, 102, or 111.

title: Cytology
description: Structural organization of the basic unit of living organisms in both plants and animals. The cell, cytoplasmic organelles, the nucleus, mitosis, and meiosis. Prerequisites: BIO 211 and 212.

title: Molecular Biology 1
description: The mechanisms which coordinate and control the activities of microorganisms. Emphasis on recent research in bacterial genetics, the nature and origin of DNA and RNA, protein synthesis, enzyme mechanisms and controls, and permease systems. Prerequisite: BIO 411 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Molecular Biology 2
description: The interrelationships of metabolic pathways, with particular emphasis on bacteria. Emphasis on the use of energy, activation processes, and biosynthetic mechanisms. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 457 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Museum Techniques
description: Methods of preparing plant and animal specimens for display. Maintenance of museum records. Use of museum materials for educational and research functions. Taxidermy not included. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Limnology
description: The dimensions of the physical, chemical, and biological factors of inland waters. One twohour laboratory per week and two or three fullday field trips will be devoted to exploring techniques for the evaluation of representative aquatic ecosystems. Prerequisite: BIO 313 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Water Pollution Biology
description: Water pollution with emphasis on analysis of trophic structure in polluted and nonpolluted ecosystems. Ecological change and eutrophication as affected by pollutants from industrial, municipal, urban, and rural sources. Prerequisite: BIO 480 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Internship in Medical Technology
description: The fourth year of the Professional Arts Curriculum with a major in medical technology consists of a fiftytwo week rotating internship, gaining theory and experience in an affiliated clinical laboratory. Approximately two thousand clock hours are spent in laboratory and classroom lectures, discussions, and demonstrations. Prerequisite: completion of the third year of the Professional Arts Curriculum with a major in medical technology. A total of 45 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Designed to give undergraduate biology students with special aptitude an opportunity to participate in scientific investigation. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned; as much as 4 hours of credit may be taken at one time. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Plant Anatomy
description: Origin and structure of cells, tissues, and organs of higher plants. Prerequisite: BIO 212.

title: Taxonomy of Flowering Plants
description: The identification of native flowering plants. Emphasis on the distinguishing features of the major plant groups and use of manuals. Prerequisite: BIO 212 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Forestry
description: Study and identification of native trees. Problems of general forestry and forest conservation. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisite: BIO 100, 102, or 111.

title: Paleobotany
description: Morphology and anatomy of fossil plants. Correlation of extinct and living plants with emphasis on evolutionary trends. Prerequisite: BIO 212 and BOT 330 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Plant Morphology
description: Forms, life cycles, and evolution of the major plant groups. Prerequisite: BIO 212 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Ornamental Plants
description: Identification and uses of ornamental trees, shrubs, and vines. Selection, special characteristics, adaptability, and maintenance of ornamentals.

title: Plant Physiology
description: An introductory treatment of the physiological activities of green plants as related to plant structures and environmental influences. Prerequisites: BIO 212, and CHEM 130 or 230.

title: Intermediate Plant Physiology
description: A continuation of BOT 451. A treatment of selected physiological activities of green plants with emphasis on plant growth substances, photosynthesis, and intermediate metabolism. Prerequisite: BOT 451 or 551.

title: Teaching of Science in the Elementary School
description: Recent elementary science texts, courses of study, and supplementary books are examined. Development and use of science teaching units. The use of experiments, field studies, demonstrations, and other special methods.

title: The Teaching of Science in the Junior High School
description: Recent curriculum developments in junior high school science. Science curriculum instruction related to the physical, mental, and emotional characteristics of the junior high school student. Prerequisite: 36 hours of credit in courses in the sciences.

title: History and Philosophy of Science
description: The history of natural science. Emphasis is given to the influence of science on general philosophy.

title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
description: Comparative study of the anatomy, development, and relationships of vertebrates. Three lecture periods and two twohour laboratory periods. Prerequisite: BIO 211 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Invertebrate Zoology
description: Invertebrate groups. Phylogeny, comparative morphology, and life histories. Three lecture periods and two twohour laboratory periods weekly. Prerequisite: BIO 211 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: A comparison of vital activities in the animal groups, particularly the invertebrates. Prerequisites: BIO 211, and CHEM 130 or 230.

title: Ornithology
description: Birds. Field identification, classification, behavior, and economic relationships. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisites: BIO 100, 102, or 111.

title: Entomology
description: Anatomy, physiology, taxonomy, life histories, habits, and adaptations of insects. Prerequisite: BIO 211.

title: Ichthyology
description: The study of fish with emphasis on identification, classification, anatomy and physiology, and ecology. Indiana species will be emphasized but other important species will be included. Prerequisite: BIO 211 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Mammalogy
description: The evolutionary origin, characteristics, and distribution of recent mammals. The behavior of individuals and of populations. The economic relationships of mammals. Additional field work, including one extended field trip, may be required. Chemistry 173

title: Animal Parasitology
description: Helminth and arthropod parasites of animals. Emphasis on identification, life cycles, and hostparasite relationships. Prerequisites: BIO 211 and 213, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Protozoology
description: An - introduction to aspects of the morphology, physiology, ecology, and development of protozoa. Prerequisites: BIO 211 and 213.

title: Wildlife Biology
description: The identification, population dynamics, and geographic distribution of wildlife species with particular emphasis on the terrestrial vertebrates of the United States. The management and harvest of wildlife. title: Man and Chemistry
description: Nonmathematical treatment of fundamental concepts of chemistry, such as: organization of chemistry, language of chemistry, atomic structure, nature of matter, classification of matter, radioactivity, and the relevancy of these to everyday living. Three onehour lectures and one twohour laboratory weekly.

title: General Chemistry
description: Chemistry of the elements and their compounds with emphasis on basic principles. Atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, and the nature of matter stressed. Three onehour lectures and one twohour laboratory per week. Prerequisite: one year of secondary school algebra or the equivalent.

title: General Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 110, including properties of solutions, colloids, chemical kinetics, chemical equilibrium, and electrochemistry. Prerequisite: MATH 110 and CHEM 110 or the equivalent.

title: General Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 111, including chemistry of metals and nonmetals, chemistry of carbon compounds, nuclear structure, and radioactivity. Laboratory work includes qualitative analysis. Prerequisite: CHEM 111 or the equivalent.

title: Chemical Principles 1
description: A comprehensive treatment of the fundamentals of chemistry, with emphasis on periodic relationships and stoichiometry. Recommended for preprofessional and science majors who plan to take more than one year of college chemistry. Three lectures, two threehour laboratories weekly. Prerequisite: one year of high school chemistry or CHEM 110. Prerequisite or parallel: MATH 111 or the equivalent.

title: Chemical Principles 2
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 113, with emphasis on solutions, chemical kinetics, energetics, and equilibria. Laboratory work includes qualitative analysis. Three lectures, two threehour laboratories weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 111 or 113.

title: A Brief Course in Organic Chemistry
description: Especially for nurses, biology and general science majors. Three lectures, one twohour laboratory weekly. Prerequisite: 4 hours of collegelevel general chemistry.

title: Chemical Analysis
description: Theory and practice of representative quantitative chemical measurements. Includes gravimetry, visual and potentiometric titrations (neutralization, complexation, precipitation, and redox), ionexchange, coulometric and conductometric titrations, and visibleregion spectrophotometry. Prerequisite: CHEM 112 or 114.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: The aliphatic hydrocarbons and their derivatives, including nomenclature, chemical and physical properties, and their practical application. Three lectures, one threehour laboratory weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 112 or 114.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 230, including optical activity and the chemistry of carbohydrates and proteins. Prerequisite: CHEM 230. }MATH 172 and PHYCS 114 must be elected prior to CHEM 340. Chemistry 175

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 231, including the chemistry of aromatic hydrocarbons, heterocyclic compounds, natural products, dyes, medicinals, and plastics. Prerequisite: CHEM 231.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: A beginning course in organic chemistry for chemistry majors. Lecture material deals with covalent bonding, molecular structure, and the chemistry of elementary organic compounds. Three hours of lecture and two threehour laboratory periods a week. Prerequisite: CHEM 225 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in CHEM 230.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: A continuation of CHEM 233. Lecture material covers the chemistry of common functional groups, stereochemistry, and the carbohydrates. Three hours of lecture and two threehour laboratory periods a week. Prerequisite: CHEM 233 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in CHEM 231.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: A continuation of CHEM 234. Lecture material covers the chemistry of amines and phenols. Selected advanced topics will be discussed. Three hours of lecture and two threehour laboratory periods a week. Prerequisite: CHEM 234 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in CHEM 232.

title: Chemical Calculations
description: Provides experience in solving practical chemical problems of widely varied mathematical types, including dimensional and error analysis, graphical presentation, chemical examples of simple calculus procedures, series, and symmetry. Two class discussions per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 225 or permission of the department head.

title: Instrumental Methods of Analysis
description: Practical applications of modern chemical instrumentations, i.e., electrometric, chromatographic, and spectroscopic methods, to industrial and environmental situations. Two lectures and four hours of arranged laboratory weekly, including a prelaboratory discussion period. Prerequisite: CHEM 225. Applicable only to chemical or medical technology programs, or to the departmental minor for life science students.

title: Physical Chemistry
description: The thermodynamic, kinetic, and structural description of chemical processes and properties of solids, liquids, gases, and solutions. Three lectures and one threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 225, MATH 172, and PHYCS 114 or 124. One year of college physics recommended.

title: Physical Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 340. Prerequisite: CHEM 340.

title: Physical Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 341. Prerequisite: CHEM 341.

title: Selected Principles of Physical Chemistry
description: Introduction to the properties of solids, liquids, gases, and solutions, and to the basic concepts of thermodynamics and kinetics, presented at a level which does not require use of calculus. Especially for premedical, biology, and general science majors. Three lectures and one threehour laboratory weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 225. Not open to the student who has credit in CHEM 340.

title: Essentials of Biochemistry
description: Chemistry of biological compounds, their metabolism and the regulation of metabolic processes. Three hours of lecture and one threehour laboratory period weekly. Designed for students majoring in biology and medical technology. Prerequisite: CHEM 230 and 231, or the equivalent. Not open to the student with a departmental major in chemistry or the student who has credit in CHEM 462.

title: Scientific Glass Working
description: Laboratory work in the fundamental techniques of glass working. Prerequisite: CHEM 230 or 233 and junior standing.

title: The Teaching of Chemistry in the Secondary School
description: Methods of chemistry teaching organization of subject matter, construction and equipment of laboratories, and examination of secondary school texts. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisites: 24 hours of credit in chemistry.

title: Chemical Technology Practicum
description: Practical experience in real or simulated industrial laboratory situations for the chemical technology trainee. Prerequisite: CHEM 325 and permission of the department head. Not applicable toward majors or minors in chemistry.

title: Chemical Instrumentation
description: Theoretical principles and application of selected chromatographic, spectroscopic, and electroanalytical methods, with illustrative experiments. Two lectures and four hours of arranged laboratory weekly, including a prelaboratory discussion period. Prerequisite or parallel: CHEM 342 or permission of the department head.

title: Analytical Chemistry
description: Analytical sampling, separations, statistical treatment of experimental data; selection of experimental methods; multicomponent analysis of complex materials, i.e., rocks, minerals, alloys, industrial mixtures; organic quantitative analysis. Three hours of lecture and one threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 420.

title: Qualitative Organic Analysis
description: Theory and practice in separating and identifying organic compounds. Four twohour laboratories weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 232.

title: Physical-Organic Chemistry
description: An advanced course devoted to the theoretical aspects of structure, resonance, stereochemistry, acidity, basicity, and reaction rates in organic chemistry. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 232.

title: Inorganic Chemistry
description: The structure of matter and its relationship to properties, including considerations of modern atomic structure, bonding crystal structure, radioactivity, periodicity, oxidationreduction, and acid base relationships. Prerequisite: CHEM 342 or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Continuation and extension of CHEM 450. Application of basic principles to study of specific inorganic materials. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 450.

title: Inorganic Preparations
description: The preparation and study of inorganic compounds. Stress is on the preparation, purification, and identification of these compounds. Sufficient instrumental studies of compounds will be included to acquaint the student with methods of identification used in inorganic chemistry. Four threehour laboratory periods weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 340 or the equivalent.

title: Principles of Biochemistry
description: Chemistry of proteins, enzymes, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids. Stress is on the techniques of isolation, purification, and identification of these substances. Three hours of lecture and one threehour laboratory period weekly. Recommended for students seeking a major or minor in chemistry and for students in premedical and predental areas. Prerequisite: one year of organic chemistry.

title: Principles of Biochemistry
description: Continuation of CHEM 462. Biological oxidations and energy transfers; metabolic patterns of proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids; metabolic interrelationships. Three hours of lecture and one threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: CHEM 462.

title: Special Studies in Chemistry
description: Designed to give undergraduate chemistry students an opportunity to pursue specific lines of scientific investigation on an individual basis. Experimental work, wide reading and development of research techniques and skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Economics Jost, Chairman; Caron, Cheng, Girgis, Lawson, Pickerill, Rocha, Scheer Economics is the scientific study of economic institutions and systems. It is a study of human wants and of efforts to satisfy those wants through alternative uses of the scarce resources of production. The key phrase is "scarce resources of production" and scarcity is relative — relative to human wants. The discipline of economics is dominated by a comprehensive body of theory that interrelates human wants and the means for their fulfillment. Economic theory is founded upon a set of assumptions that permit rigorous analysis of the use of all resources or of any one category of them. It is a useful study in an intellectual sense because it trains students to think carefully and logically about complex social phenomena. By such knowledge it is possible to understand the impact on economic systems and institutions of broad social and economic developments or of new economic policies and the responses of these units to them. Given the complicated economic and social problems of the modern world, an understanding of this subject is important for intelligent citizenship and for practical application in industry, government, research, and the professions. To achieve a basic comprehension of how our economy operates, the department offers a core of courses aimed at providing (1) a sound grasp of the tools of analysis and measurement, (2) an understanding of institutional development and the interrelations of economic and social factors, and (3) an ability to apply systematic analysis and understanding to problems of public policy. College of Business students can select the economics major option B (see curricula below). The option B major is designed for those choosing a professional career in business and requires 90 hours of course work, part of which satisfies the core requirements of the College of Business. The option A major is designed for the liberal arts student and is comprised of 48 hours, part of which may be taken in other departments. In addition, the department offers a departmental minor which students may elect as well as an interdepartmental mathematical economics major. title: The Economics of the Ghetto
description: The causes of segregation of residences according to income and race. The reasons for the level of income of ghetto residents and for the lack of efficiency with which society serves their economic needs. The effect of ghetto life on economic motivation. Not applicable toward major or minor concentrations in economics.

title: The Economic Development of Communist China
description: Systematic survey of the institutions, policies, and performances of the Chinese economy since 1949. Emphasis on the strategies and institutional innovations the Chinese Communists have adopted to overcome familiar problems encountered by all developing economies.

title: Survey of Economic Ideas
description: The important conclusions of modern economics are surveyed along with the general lines of thinking upon which those conclusions are founded. Especially designed to serve the needs and interest of the general education student. Not open to the student who has credit in ECON 201.

title: Elements of Economics
description: A survey of the major institutions, of the theoretical explanations for fluctuations in general business conditions, of money and banking, and a brief introduction to the market determination of output and prices. Public policy relating to each area is explained and evaluated. Prerequisite: sophomore standing or credit in ECON 116.

title: Elements of Economics
description: Intensive study of the theory of price determination in various kinds of markets. The theory of wages, rent, interest, and profits. The principles of international trade and comparative economic organization. Prerequisite: ECON 200.

title: Economic and Political Problems of Emerging Nations
description: A survey of historical and contemporary problems of the lessdeveloped nations. Factors related to economic, political, and social change. Problems of economic development policies and programs within the institutional structure. Internal and external pressures that influence patterns of development. Not open to the student who has credit in POLS 281.

title: National Income Analysis
description: The substance of the course is macroeconomic theory. Major stress will be on the meaning and measurement of national income, output and employment, the Keynesian system, inflation, and the theory of investment. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: The Price System and Resource Allocation
description: Investigation of the ways in which economic units direct resources into production. Involved are analyses of product pricing and output and resource pricing and employment in the various market structures. Graphic techniques are developed without recourse to higher mathematics. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Quantitative Methods in Economics
description: The development of mathematical concepts and tools, including a brief treatment of the calculus, most useful in economics. At each stage the concepts developed are applied to problems in economic theory. Designed to provide preparation for ECON 421 and 521 for students who lack the necessary background in mathematics. Prerequisite: ECON 201. Not open to the student who has credit in MATH 171.

title: Economic Policies and Problems of Agriculture
description: Examination of the special economic conditions of demand and supply pertaining to agriculture and of problems created by changing national and international situations. Analysis of agricultural policy programs and implications of farm policy for consumers. Prerequisite recommended: ECON 200 or 201.

title: Economic Growth
description: An analysis of the causes, mechanisms, and patterns of economic growth. Growth rates of various countries will be compared and analyzed. Prerequisite: ECON 200 and 201.

title: Economic History of the United States
description: Survey of our commercial, financial, agricultural, and industrial history. Prerequisites: ECON 200 and 201, or a combination of ECON 200 and 4 hours of credit in United States history, or 8 hours of credit in United States history. Not open to the student who has credit in HIST 436.

title: History of Economic Doctrines
description: The history of how man has looked at his economic life surveys the changing ways economists have rationalized, articulated, and criticized economic organization from Biblical times to the present. The successive reformulations place a major emphasis on the economic doctrines of the recent past and the present. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Mathematical Economics
description: Utilization of mathematics in the development of selected economic theories. Survey of input -output analysis and examination of the application of linear programming and the theory of games to selected economic problems. Prerequisite: ECON 201. Prerequisite or parallel: MATH 172.

title: Labor Economics
description: Economic problems of the wage earner; growth, structure, and policies of labor organization; and the employer and governmental policies toward labor. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Labor Law
description: Origins and status of the major aspects of law as the law concerns the relations of unions and management. Major emphasis is on federal law as derived from the Management Labor Relations Act of 1947 and its interpretation by the National Labor Relations Board.

title: Economics and Practice of Collective Bargaining
description: Analysis of the interaction of the trade union, the employer, and the government. The legal, economic, and social framework of collective bargaining, negotiation, administration, and enforcement of the labor agreement. Prerequisite: ECON 431.

title: The Theory of Monetary Policy
description: A theoretical presentation of how the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System modifies the economic climate within which the institutions of the nation operate, and of the problems of government finance as they relate to the Board's goal of general economic stability. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: The Economics of Government Budgets
description: Analysis of economic theory behind alternative methods of financing government budgets and debt management. Emphasis on economic consequences of budgets by examining incidence, shifting, and incentives as regards provision of public services and alleviation of economic insecurity. Inflation as tax considered. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: International Economics
description: International trade, finance, and commercial policy. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Economic Cycles and Forecasting
description: Techniques for forecasting the trend of activity for the entire economy are presented. Institutional factors of the society are viewed as the determinants of total spending within the theoretical framework. This is followed by a seminar exercise and forecast for one sector of the economy. Prerequisite: ECON 200.

title: Comparative Economic Systems
description: Historical and comparative study of economic theories and systems. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Economics of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
description: Evaluation of economic growth and efficiency of the Soviet economy and its pattern of evolution from 1917 to the present. Planning mechanism in industry as well as contributions and problems of agriculture investigated. Examination of Soviet significance for other nations. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Industrial Organization
description: Monopolistic, oligopolistic, and competitive market structures. Unsettled issues concerning structure and conduct of industry: concentration, vertical integration, and problems of economic regulation by government. Prerequisite: ECON 200 and 201.

title: Economic Development in Latin America
description: The evaluation of theories of economic development. Sources and consequences of the economic growth and development process in Latin America analyzed in the context of economic theory. Attention to Common Market possibilities monetaryfiscal factors, and trade and exchange. Examination of current national and international programs as promoters of development.

title: Economic Development of China, Japan, and India
description: Comparative analysis of the economic systems and strategies of development in three major economies in Asia — China, a centralplanning economy; Japan, a freemarket economy; and India, a mixed economy.

title: National Income and Capital Formation in China
description: Examines and compares basic concepts and methodology concerning national income accounting and capital formation in Communist China. Utilizes a combination of computation methods, growth theory, and a case study of modern Chinese economy. Prerequisite: ECON 200, 201, and 300, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Urban Economics
description: The systematic economic structure of cities and the component parts of that structure. Attention is given to the ways in which the economic structure of cities and regions obstruct or facilitate the attainment of the goals of the community. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Readings and Directed Study in Economics
description: Interest in a specialized economics subject will be pursued under the direction of a member of the economics staff. Subjects studied will differ from or be studied in greater depth than subjects treated in other economics courses. Prerequisites: 8 hours of credit in economics. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. In each of these areas the Department of English has definite responsibilities not only to its own majors and minors but also to all other Ball State University students. Literature provides a perspective gained only through intimacy with the thoughts and feelings of writers of all times and all cultures. To help students gain this perspective, the Department of English offers a wide variety of courses in American, British, and world literature. There are at least two good reasons for becoming better acquainted with how one's own language works. One is that a knowledge of the various patterns of language should contribute to a facility in writing and speaking. Equally important, however, is the fact that the history and structure of our language are important parts of our cultural heritage. Realizing the increasing necessity for successful college graduates to express themselves clearly in writing, the Department of English requires all students to develop skill in expository writing. This is a primary purpose of both the general education classes and the classes in advanced composition. For students interested in creative writing, special courses are provided on both the undergraduate and graduate levels. These students are also encouraged to contribute to the Department's literary magazine, Grub Street, and to compete for annual awards made possible through the Royalty Memorial Fund and Lambda Iota Tau, the English honorary fraternity. title: English as a Foreign Language
description: Stress on sounds, structure, and vocabulary of the English language in order to increase the student's facility in use of the English language. Cannot be counted toward general education requirements in English. Nonnative speakers of English who wish to pursue either undergraduate or graduate studies are required to demonstrate proficiency in English by examination. Those with deficiencies will enroll in ENG 100 until proficiency is demonstrated. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 103 or 104.

title: Literature and Composition for Foreign Students
description: Written and oral composition through reading, discussion, and interpretation of selected pieces of literature. Continued attention to the problems of syntax, pronunciation, and vocabulary which are difficult for foreign students. (This course is the equivalent of ENG 103 for foreign students.) Prerequisite: ENG 100 or satisfactory score on proficiency test in English as a foreign language.

title: Fundamentals of English Composition
description: Special attention to the problems of grammar and mechanics. Required of all students with a score of 360 or lower on the SAT verbal examination and who ranked in the lower half of their high school class as prerequisite for ENG 103. Does not substitute for ENG 103 or 104.

title: Literature and Composition
description: English composition stressing the sentence, the paragraph, and the organization of the various types of expression through reading, discussion, and interpretation of selected pieces of literature.

title: Literature and Composition
description: Guided exploration in the various forms of literature. Also, oral and written interpretation and analysis by individuals and groups. Prerequisite: ENG 103.

title: Humanities 1: Western Thought from Homer to Dante
description: Some major texts in the literature, philosophy, history, and general thought of the Greek, Roman, and Christian civilizations through the Middle Ages.

title: Humanities 2: Western Thought from Montaigne to Rousseau
description: Some major texts in the literature, philosophy, history, and science during the Renaissance and through the eighteenth century.

title: Humanities 3: Western Thought from Dostoyevsky to Sartre
description: Some major writing in literature, philosophy, and science from 1800 until the present.

title: World Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of world literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 206.

title: Survey of World Literature
description: A survey of the literature of western civilization, exclusive of English and American literature for students who are majors or minors in English. Prerequisite: ENG 103 and 104. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 205.

title: American Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of American literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104.

title: British Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of British literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104.

title: Grammar for Secondary School Teachers
description: Basic course in traditional English grammar and usage. Not to be counted as part of the total hours in a major or minor program.

title: American Literature, 1607-1860
description: A survey of American literature from its beginning through the middle nineteenth century. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, 207, or 209.

title: English Literature of the Middle Ages and Renaissance
description: British literature of the Middle Ages and Renaissance emphasizing major works of a number of the literary figures in their historical and philosophical contexts. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, 207, or 209.

title: English Literature of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: An extensive study of English literature of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, or from 1600 to 1780, with attention to the social, historical, and philosophical backgrounds of the periods. A close reading of the works of major writers is emphasized, but not to the exclusion of the works of minor writers. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, 207, or 209.

title: English Literature of the Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: British literature of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries emphasizing major works of a number of the literary figures in their historical and philosophical contexts. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, 207, or 209.

title: Advanced Composition and Literature
description: An intensive study of contemporary exposition, problems of English usage, techniques of composition for advanced college and professional work, and prose fiction as a type of world literature. Required of exemptees from ENG 103 who are not English majors or minors.

title: Advanced Composition
description: Instruction in writing techniques beyond that provided for the general student. Introduction to literary research and criticism. Open only to English majors and minors. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, 207, or 209.

title: The Teaching of Language Arts in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: Modern viewpoints and approaches in teaching language attitudes, habits, and skills. Consideration of written and oral expression, language usage, spelling, writing, and reading.

title: The English Language
description: The study of modern English with emphasis upon the application of the methods of descriptive linguistics to an understanding of modern vocabulary, usage, grammar, and phonology. Prerequisite: A satisfactory grade on the English Qualifying Test. Prerequisite waived for students with areas in elementary education or journalism.

title: The Development of the English Language
description: Introduction to the historical development of the English language with attention to changes in vocabulary, grammar, and sounds. Prerequisite: ENO 321. Prerequisite waived for departmental majors in English, option 2, and for departmental minors in English. English 183

title: Children's Literature
description: An overview of the field of children's literature and an intensive study of types at various levels. The classics are emphasized.

title: American Literature, 1860 - 1960
description: A survey of selected writers and the various literary movements in America during the last hundred years. Prerequisite: ENG 240. Prerequisite waived for departmental majors in English, option 2, and for departmental minors in English.

title: Nineteenth-Century American Fiction
description: An intensive reading in the works of two or three major writers of the period, such as Irving, Cooper, Hawthorne, Melville, Twain, and James.

title: Twentieth -Century American Fiction
description: An intensive reading in the works of three major writers of the period such as Anderson, Faulkner, Fitzgerald, Hemingway, Steinbeck, Wolfe, and Dos Passos.

title: Twentieth-Century American Drama
description: The themes and techniques of selected American playwrights with pertinent critical and biographical information. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Twentieth-Century American Poetry
description: The themes and techniques of selected American poets with pertinent critical and biographical information. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Literature of Black America
description: An investigation of the literature written by black authors in the United States. Those authors to be studied will be determined by the instructor on the basis of literary merit.

title: English Drama from Medieval Times to 1642
description: English drama from medieval times to the closing of the theatres in 1642, excluding Shakespeare. Special attention is given to the plays of Marlowe, Jonson, Dekker, Beaumont and Fletcher, and Webster.

title: The English Novel in the Eighteenth Century
description: Introduction to earliest English prose fiction and study of eighteenthcentury novels including the works of Defoe, Richardson, Fielding, Smollett, and Sterne. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: English Drama of the Restoration and Eighteenth Century
description: English drama from 1660 to 1780, including plays of Dryden, Etherege, Wycherley, Congreve, Steele, Goldsmith, and Sheridan.

title: The English Novel in the Nineteenth Century
description: Nineteenth century novels including works by Austen, Dickens, Thackeray, Eliot, the Brontes, Meredith, and Hardy. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: English Drama of the Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: A wide range of British drama, from Shelley's The Cencie, to Tennyson's Becket, to the plays of the Angry Young Men, with special attention given to the works of Shaw, Synge, Barrie, and O'Casey.

title: The Contemporary English Novel
description: Twentiethcentury novels, including the works of Conrad, James, Joyce, Lawrence, Forster, and others. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Honors Colloquium in English
description: Exploration of selected issues in English, with emphasis upon individualized study and reporting. Restricted to honors students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Creative Writing
description: The fundamentals of the short story, such as the use of language, image, and structure. Emphasis is put on the student's ability to write clearly and dramatically. Prerequisite: ENG 103.

title: Fiction Writing
description: Open to students who already have had some experience with the short story, the novel, or the play. Primary emphasis will be placed on instructor evaluation and class discussion of individual manuscripts. Prerequisite: ENG 405 or permission of the department chairman.

title: The Teaching of English in the Secondary School
description: Materials, methods, and resources used in the teaching of composition, language, and literature in the secondary school.

title: The Teaching of English as a Foreign Language
description: Background in modern linguistic science as applied to the teaching of English to nonnative speakers of English. Survey of methods and materials. Practice in development of teaching materials. Observation of classes in English for foreign students. Prerequisite: ENG 321, 420, or 520.

title: Literature for Adolescents
description: Recent literature suitable for students of varying ability in the secondary school. Emphasis on the actual reading of selections with some attention given to methodology. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Introduction to Linguistic Science
description: The basic concepts, scope, and methodology of the science of language in its descriptive and historical aspects.

title: Short Story
description: The short story as a type of world literature. Not open to English majors and minors.

title: The Essay
description: Representative essays by English and American authors. Not open to English majors and minors.

title: American Folklore
description: Materials and techniques for presenting the American heritage of folklore and folk literature at the public school level. Books, films, filmstrips, recordings, and pictorial collections are among the materials studied.

title: Emerson, Thoreau, Whitman
description: An intensive reading of their principal works, and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of transcendentalism. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Poe, Hawthorne, Melville
description: An intensive reading of their principal works, and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of romanticism. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Twain, James, Adams, Crane
description: An intensive reading of their principal works, and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of the varieties of realism. Prerequisite: ENG 340.

title: American Literature, 1945 to Present
description: A survey of the works of major writers and literary trends in America since World War II. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Renaissance and Seventeenth-Century Studies
description: The nondramatic literature of the Tudor, Stuart, and Puritan periods (1485-1660), exclusive of Shakespeare and Milton. Major writers such as Spenser, Donne, and Jonson will be considered in terms of their influence and of their political and philosophical backgrounds.

title: Chaucer
description: A study of The Canterbury Tales, Troilus and Criseyde, and several of the minor poems. Emphasis upon the structure, the sources, and the significance of the works included. Aspects of medieval culture pertinent to the works will be considered. 464, Shakespeare (to 1600). (4) The earlier plays and poems, providing insights into the development of Shakespeare. Some plays such as Hamlet will be studied closely.

title: Shakespeare (from 1600)
description: The later plays, with close study of Othello, Macbeth, and King Lear.

title: Studies in English Literature of the Restoration and Augustan Periods
description: An extensive study of the nondramatic works of Dryden, Swift, and Pope, with possible supplementary readings from other British authors of the period 1660-1745. Attention will be given to philosophical, aesthetic, and political currents in the works studied and to the distinctive character of Neo-Classicism. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Milton
description: A study of Milton's family background, political service, and poetic apprenticeship, culminating in close analytical investigation of Paradise Lost and Samson Agonistes. Attention is given also to Milton's aesthetic propositions and to his social and political prose works.

title: Studies in English Literature of the Age of Johnson
description: An intensive survey of the nondramatic works of Samuel Johnson and other British authors of the later eighteenth century, 1744-1800. Prerequisites: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Romantic Studies
description: The poetry and prose of Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Keats, and Shelley.

title: Victorian Studies
description: An intensive study of the works of Carlyle, Tennyson, Browning, Ruskin, and Arnold.

title: Twentieth-Century British Studies
description: A study in depth of several significant twentiethcentury authors (such as Shaw, Conrad, Lawrence, Joyce, Woolf, Waugh, Durrell, Beckett, and Auden) and the intellectual and literary movements closely associated with them.

title: The Modern Continental Novel
description: Novels in translation over the last hundred years. Novels will be related to major historical, political, and intellectual currents.

title: Modern British Poetry
description: Important poets of Great Britain from World War Ito the present, focusing on Yeats, Eliot, Auden, and Thomas, with additional attention given to Hopkins, Owen, Lawrence, Graves, Ted Hughes, and others. title: Introduction to the Classical World
description: Introduces the student to the cardinal features of the Greek and Roman civilization.

title: German Literature in English Translation
description: Primarily a general education course. The aim of the course is to expose the non-German reader to great German writers and thinkers. The course may not be applied toward areas in German. fGER 204, 205, 206 may be substituted for 201, 202, 203.

title: Hispanic Literature in Translation
description: Primarily a general education course, exposing the non-Spanish reader to the great writers of the Hispanic world. The course may not be applied toward areas in Spanish.

title: The Old Testament as Literature
description: Considers the Old Testament as typical of, related to, and sources of some of the major literary genres, such as: history and biography, prophetic literature, lyric poetry, dramatic literature, and short stories and tales.

title: Foreign Literatures through Motion Pictures
description: Presentations of the literary matter of many nations through the medium of films. Ten films will be shown. Selected ones will be compared to the works of literature. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Linguistics and the Language Teacher
description: The application of general linguistic theory to the teaching and learning of foreign and second languages. Gives the language student some basic insights into how linguistics can help in the mastery of languages.

title: Introduction to Historical Linguistics
description: An introduction to the scientific study of language for students in foreign language. An elementary survey of the methods used in historical and comparative linguistic analysis with application to language usually taught in college. Gives the language student some basic insights into the linguistic principles that underlie change in language.

title: Honors Colloquium in Foreign Literature
description: Selected readings and indepth exploration and discussion of literary currents, movements, authors, and themes found in foreign literature. Prerequisite: junior standing in the honors program or permission of the department chairman. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Romance Linguistics
description: Deals with a short history of Vulgar Latin and with the phonological, morphological, and syntactical evolution of the Romance Languages. Basic knowledge of a Romance language is desirable.

title: Cultural Life of Ancient Greece
description: Introduces the student to the cultural achievements of the ancient Greeks and their contribution to the modern world.

title: Cultural Life of Ancient Rome
description: Provides the student with a fundamental knowledge of the social, cultural, and economic framework within which the ancient Romans lived.

title: Independent Study
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with individual instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: The Teaching of Foreign Language in the Secondary School
description: Methods current in foreign language teaching in the junior and senior high schools. Directed observation of classes, specific problems of presentation, choice of texts, and organization of teaching materials and supplementary aids are worked out in detail. Attention is given to the Report of the Foreign Language Study and to the courses of study recommended by the State Department of Education. Prerequisites: two years of college credit in French, German, Latin, or Spanish, or the equivalent.

title: The Teaching of Foreign Language in the Elementary School
description: Development of foreign language instruction in the elementary school. Curricula, training of teachers, and teaching methods; also phonemics, pronunciation, and a review of other basic language elements.

title: Beginning French
description: The first course in the French language.

title: Beginning French
description: Prerequisite: FR 101.

title: Beginning French (continued)
description: Prerequisite: FR 102 or one year of secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French
description: Prerequisite: one year of college French or two years of secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college French or two and onehalf years of secondary school French.

title: Intermediate French (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 20 hours of college French or two and onehalf years of secondary school French.

title: Conversation
description: Drill on pronunciation and speech patterns, dictation, and recording. The object of the course is to train in ability to speak French. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or FR 504.

title: Composition
description: Grammar and composition. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or FR 505.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the French language and the application of phonetics to the understanding and speaking of French. Use of the phonetic alphabet. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Civilization and Culture: The Old Regime
description: Contributions made by France from the beginnings to the French Revolution. Origins of historical and cultural traditions. Supplemental literary selections. Prerequisite: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Civilization and Culture: Modern France
description: Development of modern France from the French Revolution to the present. Assimilation of traditions into the culture of the industrial age. Supplemental literary selections. Prerequisite: two years of college French or the equivalent. Not open to the student who has credit in FR 309 prior to September, 1973.

title: Short Story
description: A study of the short story in French literature. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Classical Drama
description: The plays of Corneille, Racine, and Moliere. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: A study of French poetry with emphasis on the Symbolists and on contemporary poets. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Novel
description: Extensive reading in French novel. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in French drama. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Modern Reading
description: Contemporary prose and poetry. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: French Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced French language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where French is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in French or by permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairman.

title: History of French Literature 1
description: From the beginnings to 1760. Literature of the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, and the Classical Age to 1760. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 2
description: The classical age from 1760 and the eighteenth century. Literature of the golden age of classicism and the eighteenthcentury philosophies. Prerequisites: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 3
description: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The development of romanticism, realism, naturalism, and symbolism in French literature; literature of contemporary France. Prerequisites: two years of college or the equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college French or the equivalent, or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Beginning German
description: The first course in the German language.

title: Beginning German
description: Prerequisite: GER 101.

title: Beginning German (continued)
description: Prerequisite: GER 102 or one year of secondary school German.

title: Beginning German for Science Majors
description: Introduction to the basic German grammar needed for the reading of German texts required for science majors.

title: Beginning German for Science Majors
description: Completion of the basic German grammar needed for the reading of German texts required for science majors and some selected readings of appropriate texts. Prerequisite: GER 104 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Beginning German for Science Majors
description: Reading appropriate German texts to build the student's competence in reading and translating expository materials. Prerequisite: GER 105 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Basic Conversational German for Travelers
description: Beginning spoken German for travelers or those seeking employment in Germany. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate German
description: Reading of representative German authors of moderate difficulty. Vocabulary, increased knowledge of German idiom, and practice in writing German are emphasized. Prerequisite: one year of college German or two years of secondary school German.

title: Intermediate German (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Intermediate German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of German authors in class. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Expository German
description: Review of essential German grammar. Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisite: one year of college German or two years of secondary school German.

title: Expository German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisites: 16 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Expository German (continued)
description: Extensive reading of technical German material. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college German or two and onehalf years of secondary school German.

title: Conversation
description: To increase fluency in speaking and ease of comprehension through conversation. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or GER 504.

title: Composition
description: To familiarize students with the fine points of German grammar and to train them to express themselves in the correct idiom. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or GER 505.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the German language and the application of phonetics and phonemics to the understanding and speaking of German. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Civilization and Culture
description: Civilization and cultural development of the Germans from ancient times to the present. Taught in German. Prerequisite: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Masterpieces
description: Classical and Romantic periods. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Drama
description: Drama and theories of the drama of Goethe, Schiller, Grillparzer, and Hebbel. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: Introduction to German lyric poetry and survey of historical development of this literary genre. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Prose
description: Growth and significance of modern prose writing in Germany. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in recent German drama. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Modern Masterpieces
description: Realism, naturalism, and recent German literary periods. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Goethe
description: Intensive study of the life and of one or more of the works of Johann Wolfgang Goethe. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: German Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced German language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where German is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in German or by permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairman.

title: History of German Literature 1
description: From its beginnings to 1750. A survey of German literary trends from the earliest times to the Classical Period, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 2
description: From 1750 to 1850. A survey of the classical and romantic German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 3
description: From 1850 to the present. A survey of recent German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers, such as Moerike, Keller, Storm, Stifter, Thomas Mann, Hermann Hesse, and others. Prerequisites: two years of college German or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Romanticism
description: Philosophical and historical background of German romanticism, the development of romantic poetry and prose. Prerequisite: two years of college German or the equivalent.

title: Poetic Realism
description: Emphasis on major works representative of Poetic Realism in German literature, including works of Adalbert Stifter, Annette von Droste-Hulshoff, Gottfried Keller, C. F. Meyer, and Theodor Storm.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisites: three years of college German or the equivalent, or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Beginning Greek
description: The first course in the Greek language.

title: Beginning Greek
description: Prerequisite: GRK 101.

title: Beginning Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisite: GRK 102.

title: Intermediate Greek
description: Prerequisite: one year of college Greek or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 16 hours of Greek or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: 20 hours of Greek or the equivalent.

title: Advanced Greek
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Greek (continued)
description: Prerequisites: two years of college Greek or the equivalent, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Beginning Italian
description: The first course in the Italian language.

title: Beginning Italian
description: Prerequisite: ITAL 101.

title: Beginning Italian
description: Prerequisite: ITAL 102 or the equivalent.

title: Beginning Latin
description: The first course in the Latin language. Elements of Latin pronunciation, alphabet, rules of accent, syllabification, basic Latin grammar with oral and written exercises, reading of easy short selections from Latin authors, exercises in English derivatives, and consideration of the close connection of Latin and English vocabularies.

title: Beginning Latin
description: Continued emphasis on pronunciation, accent, and syllabification. Oral and written exercises of greater difficulty, reading of short selections from various Latin authors, exercises in dictation, practice in comprehension, with exercises requiring comprehension of speech patterns rather than memorization of single words, and presentation of more grammatical principles. Prerequisite: LAT 101.

title: Beginning Latin (continued)
description: Completion of presentation of the mechanics of Latin grammar. Stress on Latin syntax; logical structure in thought patterns. Rapid short readings illustrating grammatical principles. Emphasis on mastery of grammar through usage; oral and written exercises. Reading of relatively long essays, orations, and letters of Cicero, Pliny's letters, short poems of Horace, Catullus, and Vergil, longer reading selections chosen for importance in history of civilization rather than for illustration of grammatical principles. Prerequisite: LAT 102 or one year of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin
description: Rapid review of Latin grammar with oral and written exercises. Reading of selections from Caesar, Cicero, Pliny, Livy, Seneca, Vitruvius, and others, dealing with such topics as poetry, science, agriculture, medicine, religion, business, politics, history, private life, cooking, philosophy, education, and law. The aim is to interest Latin students in literary ideas drawn from representative works. Emphasis on vocabulary, increased knowledge of Latin idiom, and practice in writing Latin. Prerequisite: one year of college Latin or two years of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin (continued)
description: Emphasis on rapid reading for comprehension. Selected passages dealing with various aspects of man's life, together with comparisons taken from later periods. Celsus, De Medicina; Horace, Ars Poetica; Vitruvius, De Aqueductis; Pliny's Natural History; Cicero's De Officiis, De Republica, Epistulae, De Finibus, or Pro Archia; Juvenal, Satires; Pliny's letters (concerning the Christians), Terence's and Plautus' plays ; and others. Prerequisites: 16 hours of college Latin or two and onehalf years of secondary school Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin (continued)
description: Extensive reading of Roman comedies in class. Stress on rapid reading of Latin, particularly of the dramatists, Plautus and Terence. Introduction to colloquial Latin and everyday idiomatic language. Development of plot, characterization, and artistic unity of Roman comedies. Background and originality of Roman comedy; contaminatio. Play production in Rome. Comparison of Greek and Roman comedy. Aristophanes' comedies; selected plays of Terence and Plautus. Prerequisites: 20 hours of college Latin or two and onehalf years of secondary school Latin.

title: The Latin Element in English
description: Latin borrowings, Latin prefixes, roots, and suffixes in English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required. Open to all students.

title: Greek and Latin in Scientific Terminology
description: Considers the composition of technical words used by the physical, biological, medical, and technical sciences.

title: Roman Private and Public Life
description: All phases of Roman customs referred to in Latin commonly read in secondary school are carefully examined and understood. No reading knowledge of Latin required. Open to all students.

title: Classical Mythology
description: Primarily a general education course,. dealing with myths of the Greeks and Romans and their use in literature and art. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required.

title: The Classical World in Film, Fiction, and Fact
description: A broad survey of life in the classical Mediterranean world through the media of motion pictures, fiction, nonfiction (such as historical, archaeological, and anthropological studies).

title: Prose Composition
description: For advanced students who are preparing to teach Latin. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or LAT 505.

title: Tacitus: Minor Works
description: Development of the ability to read Latin prose of moderate difficulty; literary style of Tacitus.

title: Suetonius: Lives of the Caesars
description: Reading with special reference to life and times of Suetonius.

title: Pliny: Letters
description: Selected letters by Pliny; Pliny's style.

title: Classical Literature in English Translation
description: Selected masterpieces of classical literature; historical development of the various types of literature as a background for further study in Latin and English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required.

title: Horace: Odes
description: Selections from the Odes, with emphasis on metrical forms, grammatical construction, and mythology.

title: The Latin Elegiac Poets
description: The elegies of Catullus, Tibullus, Propertius, and Ovid.

title: Ovid: The Metamorphoses
description: Selected readings from the Metamorphoses of Ovid, with special reference to the life and times of Ovid, and the poetic traditions of Classical Latin. Prerequisites: two years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Livy: History
description: Selected readings from Livy's Ab Urbe Condita, with a study of Livy's historical concept, and contrasted with the other greater Roman historians. Prerequisite: two years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Roman Comedy
description: Selected plays of Plautus and Terence with attention to influence on French and English literature.

title: Survey of Latin Literature
description: A comprehensive study of Latin literature through the reading of selections from Livius Andronicus to the church fathers. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Lucretius: De Rerum Natura
description: Selected readings from Lucretius' De Rerum Natura, with collateral studies in development of philosophic attitudes in classical times. Prerequisites: two years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books I-VI
description: Readings from Books 1-VI of the Aeneid of Vergil, with collateral studies in epic genre and the relationship to Homeric epic. Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books VII-XII
description: The last six books of the Aeneid, with collateral reading and reports.

title: Cicero: The Philosophic Works
description: Readings from selected philosophic works of Cicero, as DeAnima, De Senectute, De Republica, with a related study of philosophical attitudes in classical times. Prerequisites: three years of college Latin or the equivalent.

title: Cicero: Selected Letters
description: Introduction to Roman epistolary style. Comparison with Pliny.

title: Caesar: The Civil War
description: Comparison with the Gallic wars.

title: Martial: Epigrams
description: Introduction to poetry of the Silver Age with emphasis on the epigram.
