title: Art: An Introduction
description: Introduces the general education student to the areas of art: architecture, city planning, industrial design, the home, painting, sculpture, and related arts. It is academic in nature and presents the ideational and technical approach the artist takes in creative activity. Not open to students with areas in art.

title: Honors Colloquium in Art
description: A planned reading and discussion program dealing with the aesthetic problems of contemporary art. Open only to students on the Honors Program,

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of the department head. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Aesthetics in the Visual Arts
description: Principles underlying twentieth century art products. Prerequisites : for art majors, 12 hours of credit in art history and appreciation; for other students, none.

title: Ancient Art
description: Focuses on the diverse styles of architecture, sculpture, and painting of three early civilizations ; Egyptian, Greek, and Roman. Open to all students.

title: Medieval Art
description: Major European movements and personalities in architecture, painting, and sculpture from early Christian times through the Gothic period. Styles to be considered include early Christian, Byzantine, Romanesque, and Gothic. Open to all students.

title: Renaissance Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of the Early and High Renaissance in Italy and Northern Europe. Emphasis on the growth of the artistic heritage of the western world through the inventions and creations of Renaissance genius. Open to all students.

title: Mannerism, Baroque, and Rococo Art
description: Special emphasis on the works of the leading exponents of these styles in architecture, painting, and sculpture as they appeared in Italy, France, Germany, Spain, Flanders, Holland, And England. Open to all students. 455.Nineteenth Century Art. (3) Painting, sculpture, and architecture in Europe including the Palladian Revival through Symbolism and the forerunners of Cubism and Expressionism, Cexanne, and Munch. Other movements to be considered are Neo-Classicism, Romanticism, Realism, Pre-Raphaelites, and Impressionism. Open to all students.

title: Twentieth Century Art to 1945
description: European architecture, sculpture, and painting from 1900 to 1945. Special attention to the development of those styles leading to the contemporary art of the midcentury and later. Open to all students.

title: Art Since 1945
description: Deals with the major movements and personalities in two and threedimensional art in the United States and Europe since 1945. Emphasis on an understanding of the conceptual problems, materials, techniques and their relationship to early twentieth century art. Open to all students.

title: History of Art in the United States
description: A survey of American cultural traditions through an examination of three hundred years of architecture, painting, sculpture, folk art, and related forms. Open to all students except the student who has credit in AHS 411.

title: Expanded Cinema
description: Comparative study of cinema as related to the arts. Includes the expressive potential of nontraditional and mixedmedia which is explored through viewing and analysis of significant examples for consideration of aesthetic consequences within the field of visual arts.

title: Gallery Techniques
description: Basic techniques involved in such gallery work as administration, collecting, exhibitions, temporary shows. Open only to students with areas in art.

title: Art in Living
description: A field course in which the student will have the opportunity of studying at first hand the handicrafts, industrial arts, and the arts of a particular geographic area. Open to all students. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Art History
description: Seminar study, individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite : completion of 39 hours of credit in art or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Home Economics Miller, Chairman; Adams, Bruner, Caylor, Finn, Kim, Lacey, Nixon, Quesenberry, Simpson, Smith, Steele, Wittig Home economics is the field of knowledge and service that is fundamentally concerned with strengthening home and family life through educating the individuals for family living; improving the services and goods used by families; conducting research to discover the changing needs of individuals and families and to determine means of satisfying these needs; and furthering community, national, and world conditions favorable to family living. The profession of home economics synthesizes knowledge drawn from its own research from the physical, biological, and social sciences and the arts and applies this knowledge to improving the lives of families and individuals. The breadth of the field of home economics emphasizes its importance. The eleven separate, but interrelated, fields of foods, nutrition, clothing, textiles, applied art, housing, household equipment, home management, family economics, child development, and family relations provide the foundations for the good health, satisfying and successful living, psychological balance, and good management which are essential for the development of the whole personality. Needs of individuals and families in the social environment of their time are of primary concern in determining the emphases given to the various aspects of home economics. Home economics aids in helping individuals and families to make intelligent decisions concerning all aspects of family life, including the social, economic, aesthetic, managerial, health, and ethical aspects of relations, child development, foods, clothing, and housing. Home economics prepares professional personnel to carry out its objectives through education, research, social welfare and public health, dietetics, and institutional administration and business. It shares with other fields the responsibility for developing perceptive, wellinformed citizens with the ability and the initiative to further conditions favorable to effective living. Prerequisite: HED 390.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economics related work chosen by the individual student.

title: Meal Planning and Food Preparation
description: Designed for the nonhome economics major. Basic ininciples of food buying, food preparation, and table service, along with the study of nutritive value of food. Foods and service for different social occasions. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 110.

title: Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of preparation stressed. Open to men and women.

title: Meal Planning and Table Service
description: Principles and fundamentals in planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate meals which are appetizing and appealing from the aesthetics standpoint. Economic factors considered. Attention is given to foods and types of table service for various occasions. Problems in food buying stressed. Prerequisite : HFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental principles in nutrition and application to diets for children and normal adults.

title: Menu Planning for Quantity Food Service
description: Principles of nutrition applied to feeding of individuals and groups. Major emphasis placed on menu planning for institutions with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Limitations or problems relating to personnel, facilities, and type of patronage also stressed.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Stressed are the organization structure, application of principles of scientific management, and personnel administration. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning—Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping of food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industries and commercial operations. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Quantity Food Production and Purchasing
description: Offers opportunity for insight into factors related to quantity production and purchasing of foods. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics. 1
description: Nutritional requirements of the individual from infancy through old age; energy value of foods in the light of chemistry and physiology of digestion; nutritive properties of foodstuffs. Dietaries are planned.

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Laboratory experience in university food service units. Prerequisites : HFN 220 and 340.

title: Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Problems pertaining to school lunchrooms, hospitals, and cafeterias as to personnel, management and organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens.

title: Institutional Equipment, Buying, and Layout
description: Stationary and small food equipment considered. Layouts of institutional kitchens planned. Field trips to institutional kitchens and equipment companies.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of the different foodstuffs so that their composition and physical and chemical properties can be understood. Recipes are investigated and methods of combining foods are developed and evaluated. Prerequisite : HFN 110.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics 2
description: Food values with emphasis on mineral and vitamin content, recent literature in the field of nutrition. Prerequisites: HFN 340 and CHEM 231.

title: Diet in Disease
description: Pathological conditions resulting from various nutritional diseases, with emphasis upon causes and effects of malnutrition and its treatment. Planning and Home Economics 123 preparation of diets for abnormal conditions. Hospital laboratory experience provided. Prerequisite : HFN 340.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers; important considerations in purchasing foods and corresponding factors that determine them. Emphasis on ethics in buying.

title: Home Care of the Sick
description: Fundamentals of home nursing in relation to family living, including laboratory experience in nursing techniques. A Red Cross home nursing certificate may be earned by each student.

title: Principles of Home Art
description: Design and color principles, with practical application to home situations. Open to all students except those who have credit in ADS 104.

title: Family Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, art qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 1
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Emphasis on the management problems encountered by newly married couples in establishing a home. Open to all students.

title: Household Equipment
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Students will have an opportunity to plan, organize, and present demonstrations on household equipment.

title: Child Development
description: Understanding of the normal growth and development of preschool children. Emphasis on the child as a member of a family group. Principles of child guidance based on the physical, intellectual, emotional, and social needs of the child. Students observe children in daycare centers, kindergarten, or play school. Open to all students.

title: Infant Development
description: Processes of growth and development during the first two years with various physical, social, and emotional aspects being emphasized. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 2
description: Residence in the home management house offers opportunity to make practical application of the principles of homemaking. Prerequisite: HFN 220.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing for the consumer, including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, arid factors to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Family Relations
description: Interpersonal relationships of family members, the forces impinging upon them today, and the changes that result in home and family living, courtship, and mate selection; preparation for marriage, marital adjustment, and parentchild relations. Open to all students.

title: Clothing Construction for Non-Majors
description: Fundamental techniques applied in the construction and fitting of simple garments. Not open to the student who has credit in HTC 104.

title: Clothing Selection and Construction
description: Clothing selection and wardrobe planning. Fundamental principles of construction and their application to simple garments.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Learn creative skills in stitchery by embellishing existing fabrics or originating new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, simple weaving, tie dyeing, stenciling, batik, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, needlepoint, rya braided and hooked rugs. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HTC 104.

title: Motivations of Fashion
description: A history of fashion from its earliest beginnings to the present. Explores the factors—social, political, psychological, economical, technological— which have motivated what was worn at any given time. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adaptation of standard patterns to individual proportions, designing of garments and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Prerequisite: HTC 104 and 203.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Textile Testing
description: Experience in planning and conducting textile tests and in evaluating resulting data; development, present status, and importance of textile testing. Prerequisite : HTC 330 or ADS 222.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: The business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, merchandising, promotion, and the consumer. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Clothing and Design
description: Special problems to meet students' needs in the clothing field. Unit on preparation of illustrative material for the teaching of clothing. Prerequisites : two other courses in clothing, or permission of the department head. Department of Industrial Education and Technology Wagner, Head; Barella, Bergman, Bumb, DeKeyser, Edwards, Gurbach, Henak, Kirkwood, Loats, Middleton, Nelson, Poucher, Reams, Ridgeway, Sargent, Smith, South, Steczak, Steele, Tomlinson, Tucker, Wright The courses of the Department of Industrial Education and Technology are designed to meet the needs of students who are (1) qualifying for the teaching profession or allied professions of business and industry, (2) exploring the industrial world for possible occupations or vocations, or (3) seeking knowledge and understanding of our industrial society. A wide variety of industryrelated courses offers students many opportunities to explore occupational choices in the following industries : building construction, communications, manufacturing, power, and transportation. As part of a student's general studies program, the Department of Industrial Education and Technology offers courses which develop insight, understanding, and practical experience in regard to the production of goods and services, working conditions, industrial research and experimentation, and typical plant or factory organization. Students who intend to have concentration areas in industrial education should take at least four of the following courses in their first year : IED 103, 125, 140, 171, 213, 231, and

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes which provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units are examined and evaluated.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Industrial Arts
description: A classroom involvement experience for industrial arts majors in the elementary school. To familiarize the student with the philosophy, history, and principles of industrial arts in the elementary school. Affords the student the opportunity to teach a short unit of instruction in cooperation with an elementary teacher to elementary age children in the local community. Prerequisite: industrial arts major or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Industrial Arts for Elementary Teachers
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of a wide variety of tools, materials, and industrial processes through the planning and organization of group activity units. Prerequisite: IED 364 or permission of the department head. INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION

title: Industry in Contemporary Society
description: An introduction to and an understanding of our complex industrial and technological society with emphasis on modern industrial organization, materials, processes, and related socioeconomic factors, including the development of manufacturing processes from crafts to automation. Laboratory experiences of a groupproblem type developed around typical industrial processes. Open to all students except those with teaching areas in industrial education.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: Manufacturing processes used by industries to convert raw materials into consumer products.

title: Characteristics of Industrial Materials
description: Experimental analysis of the mechanical properties of industrial materials. Laboratory experiences involve research and experimentation.

title: Introduction to American Industry
description: The American industrial complex. Emphasis on its organization, materials, processes, products, jigs and fixtures, and socioeconomic factors. For industrial education majors only. Prerequisites: 30 quarter hours of industrial education courses. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 161.

title: Instrumentation and Control
description: The basic principles of process instruments and control systems. Content includes measuring principles, electrical/electronic circuits, calibration and standards and fluidics.

title: World of Construction
description: A study of the industrial Arts Curriculum Project's "World of Construction" course. Centers on planning, organizing and controlling people and resources to produce constructed products.

title: American Industry Practicum
description: Advanced study of the American industrial complex with emphasis on designing and developing teaching materials and activities appropriate to class goals. Activities will be predominately studentidentified problems or research. Prerequisite : IED 361.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: A discussioncentered course which focuses primarily on internship experiences. Through these dialogues, individuals will become aware of a greater variety of situations which may be encountered in their chosen field. Open only to students with areas in industrial supervision. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: World of Manufacturing
description: A study of the Industrial Arts Curriculum Project's "World of Manufacturing" course. Class activities are centered around actual teaching of the units included in the IACP course. INDUSTRIAL MATERIALS AND PROCESSES Industrial Ceramics

title: Introduction to Industrial Ceramics
description: Production and consumption of ceramic materials such as clay, glass, stone, plaster, abrasives, and cement in contemporary industrial technology. Experiences in casting, jiggering, throwing, extrusion, compression molding, glazing and firing, and lapidary processes.

title: Industrial Ceramics: Product Design and Mold Making
description: Individual and group problemsolving approach. Production forming processes, clay and glazing compounding, glazing and kiln operations. Prerequisite : IED 127.

title: Advanced Industrial Ceramics Technology
description: Advanced industrial techniques in ceramic processing and production with emphasis on compression, injection and extrusion molding, and glazing. Prerequisite: IED 127.

title: Research and Development in Industrial Ceramics
description: Extensive independent and group study and experimentation in the area of industrial ceramics. Prerequisite: IED 327. Industrial Metals

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to metals with concentration in foundry, sheet metal, bench metal, art metal, forging, and spinning. Emphasis will also be placed on safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures.

title: Metals Machining
description: Work with the lathe, shaper, milling machines, surface grinder, metal cutting saws, and electrical discharge machine to develop a basic understanding of metal removal. Work will also involve the fundamentals of metallurgy and heat treating of carbon steels. Safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures will also be emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 231.

title: Foundry and Welding
description: Includes theory and techniques in welding a variety of welds in the flat position with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Limited work is done with TIG and MIG welding equipment. An introduction to the fundamentals of pattern design, permanent mold design, core design, and foundry techniques which provides a basic understanding of foundry practices. Emphasis will be placed on safety and maintenance. Prerequisite: IED 231.

title: Advanced Metals Machining
description: Work includes cylindrical grinding, advanced milling machine work, electrical discharge machining, tool design and grinding, metallurgy and materials testing. Emphasis is directed toward mathematics and science as it relates to machine setups and tool design. Setups relating to industrial production are discussed. Prerequisite : IED 333.

title: Problems in Sheet Metal and Machine Shop
description: Specialization in the theory and practice of sheet metal work, machine work, precision measurement, metal testing and inspection, and metallurgy. Prerequisite : IED 333 or 433.

title: Problems in Hot Metals
description: Specialization in advanced casting theory and techniques. Advanced welding will include horizontal, vertical, and overhead welding techniques with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Inert gas welding theory and techniques will be studied in depth. Will also include the fundamentals of forging practices. Prerequisite : IED 334. Industrial Plastics

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: History, growth, organization, and future of the plastics industry. Thermoplastic and thermosetting materials and processes. Injection, extrusion, compression, blow and rotational molding, thermoforming and other processes. Common industrial plastics used.

title: Industrial Plastics: Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problemsolving approach. Injections thermoforming, rotational blow molding and/or extrusion molds, and die construction. Fiberglass and foam molds may also be made Appropriate moldmaking techniques and equipment are demonstrated. Prerequisites : IED 125.

title: Advanced Industrial Plastics Technology
description: Advanced techniques in plastics processing. Use of automatic molding equipment, molds, and engineering plastics. Mass production techniques will be employed. Prerequisite: IED 225.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. Mold making, materials testing and/or equipment design possible. Prerequisite: IED 325. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Industrial Woods

title: Introduction to Woods
description: The nature and properties of wood and the manufacturing processes used to convert it from an extracted raw material to a wood product which fulfills a consumer need in American society. Some development of tool skills.

title: Woods 2
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213.

title: Advanced Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in processing modified wood materials. Additional emphasis upon mechanical and chemical conversion, particle and fiber processes, adhesives, treatments and coatings, drying, and wood production management. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Construction Technology
description: A survey of construction as a managed production system with emphasis on production techniques.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extensive study and experimentation in one or more of the following: wood lamination, wood treatment and coating, and production management of secondary wood processing. Prerequisite: IED 316. INDUSTRIAL COMMUNICATION Graphics

title: Introduction to Graphics
description: Various graphical representation and problem solving techniques and their application to the design process. Included are the theory of orthographic projection, sketching, lettering, geometric constructions, section views, English and metric dimensioning, fasteners, and working drawings. Problem solving includes experiences with elementary descriptive geometry topics. Elementary design problems are included.

title: Technical Drawing 1
description: Allows the student to develop drawing skills and acquire knowledge in the areas of lettering, use and care of instruments, geometrical constructions, multiview projection, sectional views, auxiliary views, and elementary isometric pictorials. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 103.

title: Technical Drawing 2
description: A continuation of the knowledge and skills needed to reach a minimal level of proficiency in technical drawing. Builds on the experiences covered in IED 105 and includes revolutions, shop processes, dimensioning, tolerancing, fasteners, design process, and working drawings. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Technical Sketching
description: A basic course in freehand drawing techniques designed to allow students to gain skills in the rapid representation of three dimensional objects. Orthographic views, pictorial views, exploded views, and simple shading techniques are covered.

title: Advanced Graphics
description: A continuation of experiences gained in IED 103. Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; lateral developments of geometric solids; and selected areas of descriptive geometry. Prerequisite: IED 103.

title: Architectural Drafting
description: Emphasis primarily on residential architecture. Basic principles of residential construction and planning, distinguishing features of different architectural styles, elementary load calculation, heat loss, and basic transit. principles in use of

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Technical Drawing 3
description: A study and application of cams, gears and gear trains, bearings, welding representation, standard machine components, linkages, and applied mechanisms. The design process with an individual and team design project are included. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Jig and Fixture Design
description: The study and application of the principles used in designing jigs and fixtures for manufacturing operations such as drilling, reaming, milling, turning, tapping, boring, and assembling. Prerequisite: IED 105 and 106 or equivalent. 307. Die Design. (4) The study and application of the principles used in designing dies for manufacturing operations such as blanking, piercing, forming, drawing, and bending. Progressive dies are included in the coverage. Prerequisite : IED 105 and 106 or equivalent. 308. Contemporary Concepts in Drafting and Design. (4) Contemporary topics in the field of drafting and design. Topics covered will be changed to keep current with innovative practices employed by industry. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Problems in Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in any of the following areas: structural design, gear design, graphic statics and dynamics, and architectural graphics. Prerequisite : IED 203.

title: Industrial Arts Design
description: Basic design principles are stressed, using both twoand threedimensional media; work with air brush, styrofoam, line drawings, and other types of materials. Graphic Arts

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: Introductory experiences in the various methods used by the graphic arts industry. These include letterpress and offset printing, drypoint and block etchings, silkscreen printing, embossing and gold leaf printing, marking devices, and bookbinding.

title: Letterpress Printing and Bookbinding
description: Fundamental letterpress theory is stressed, with experiences in layout, composition, imposition, presswork and bookbinding; single and twocolor platen presswork; and looseleaf and saddlestitch binding operations.

title: Photography
description: Fundamentals of photography, including camera work, black and white film processing, enlarging composition, and basic color photography.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Fundamental theory, exposure techniques, film processing, printmaking, and composition considerations in color photography. Prerequisite : IED 386.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Principles and experiences involved in lithography as a printing process. Cold type composition, camera work, stripping, plate processing, and press work; line shots and halftones. Prerequisite : IED 281.

title: Problems in Graphic Arts
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisites : IED 385 and 386 except for students on the Printing Technology Curriculum. Electronics

title: Computer Fundamentals
description: Theory and basic circuits of computers. Laboratory activity will consist of group construction of basic computer circuits.

title: Industrial Education Electronics
description: Theory of the vacuum tube and semiconductors, with special reference to their application in radio, television, and electronic circuits in industry. Individual and group experiences in project activity of the experimental, maintenance, and creative types. Prerequisite: IED 270. 472. Advanced Industrial Education Electronics. (3) Special individual and group problems in advanced electrical circuitry involving most of the components of electrical circuits, with special emphasis upon thermionic emission tubes and photo emission devices. Complex problems assigned to groups of students will characterize the project activity. Prerequisite: IED 471. INDUSTRIAL POWER Electricity

title: Introduction to Electricity
description: Introductory experiences and exploration in the broad field of electricity with special emphasis upon means of producing and transmitting electron flow. Instruction in appropriate electrical projects and familiarization with electrical measuring instruments are important experiences.

title: Applications of Electricity
description: Fundamental electrical theory, with special reference to applications in heating, lighting, electrolysis, electrical communication, and mechanical power. Individual and group experiences through the use of experiments and construction of appropriate projects. Prerequisite : IED 171.

title: Advanced Applications of Electricity
description: Advanced experiences in electrical appliance design and repair, motor design and repair, and various types of interior wiring. Appropriate projects, teaching aids, and factors concerning the teaching of these areas. Prerequisite : IED 270. Power and Transportation

title: Introduction to Power and Transportation
description: Concentration on the internal combustion engine. A study of power sources, basic mechanisms, component systems, efficiencies and power measurement, and the utilization and application to transportation and industry, and direct energy converters.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: To acquire fundamental skills and teaching knowledge through experience related to power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasis on internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Factors involved in setting up a transportation unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite: IED 140.

title: Application of Power to Air Transportation

title: Special Problems in Hydraulics

title: Vocational Guidance

title: Independent Studies in Industrial Education

title: Theory and Practice in Commercial Printing
description: Use of the Franklin Price Catalog for letterpress and offset printing, paper schedules, postal rates, study of the Government Printing Office style book, and standard printing forms and correct terminology, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite : ITE 182.

description: The ability to use the tools of quality control in the printing industry. Emphasis is given to the use of densitometry, correct register, proofreading, ink coverage, proper binding, cropping, paper and ink. Various other topics are considered.

title: Industrial Internship 2 (Market Research)
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual experience in market research while on a work assignment in industry. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and Plant Manager.

title: Industrial Internship 4 (Sales Management)

Department of Library Science Axeen, Chairman ; Armitage, Barr, Coil, Hsu, Kirby, Wetmore, Yeamans Library science is concerned with the selection, acquisition, processing, organization, and maintenance of materials in library collections and with the maximum use of these materials in serving a library's clientele. Knowledge of bibliographic aids, skill in their use, and the ability to work effectively with associates and library patrons are characteristics of the successful librarian. Thorough familiarity with materials suitable for various types of library users must be acquired by the student of library science, in addition to the mastery of technical routines necessary for efficient organization. The purpose of the undergraduate program in library science at Ball State University is the preparation of school librarians. Students are qualified to meet Indiana state certification requirements for school library and audiovisual services. Continuing reassessment of elementary and secondary education has resulted in a renewed appreciation of the school library as a media center where educational materials in a variety of media are available to students, teachers, and administrators. School media centers at all levels have increased in number with the growth of school systems. Progress is being made in the establishment of elementary school libraries since it has been demonstrated that younger children benefit greatly from a variety of learning materials. Library Science 133 The school librarian is educated as a teacher and must meet state requirements for a teaching certificate. The school librarian must understand fundamental learning processes, teaching methods, and child psychology. In addition, a basic knowledge of school curricula and special training in the analysis, evaluation, selection, organization, dissemination, and use of instructional materials for young people are essential. Library science courses are designed to help the student acquire this special training. The student will be guided by the curricular statements (see Curricula) and by the area requirements given below. The minor and the endorsement patterns in school library and audiovisual services are the same, except for electives that are chosen for their pertinence to the students' objectives. The minor on the Teacher Education Curriculum prepares for the provisional certificate in school library and audiovisual services on the secondary level. When elementary education is the major on the Teacher Education Curriculum, the endorsement prepares for such services at the elementary school level. The school library and audiovisual services minor may be used also as an area on other curricula, but, in this instance, it does not prepare for public school certification. The recognized professional degree in librarianship is the Master of Library Science degree. For details of this program see Library Science, Graduate Catalog. A basic understanding of library methods, procedures, and materials is especially important to the teacher who may not be interested in qualifying for certification as a school librarian. Courses in reference materials and materials in subject areas enable the teacher to add breadth and depth to lesson plans and to cooperate with the school librarian in making the school library an integral part of the educative process. Library science courses may be selected as electives on a program of teacher preparation. The courses in library science prepare students for service in accordance with the concept of school libraries as media centers rather than as collections limited to books and printed matter. Upon completion of the minor area in school library and audiovisual services, the prospective school librarian should be ready to administer school collections of teaching materials whether they include books only or incorporate such nonbook teaching tools as motion pictures, film strips, recordings, slides, pictures, etc. The student who plans to become a school librarian should arrange for a conference with the Chairman, Department of Library Science, or with some person designated by the Department Chairman for purposes of program planning, before enrolling in any library science course.

School of Music Hargreaves, Director; Albright, Baker, Dunn, Niccum, Wolfe, Woodrum The School of Music embraces four departments: Music Education, Music History and Musicology, Music Theory and Composition, and Musical Performance. Administrative efficiency and scholarly pursuits are enhanced by further subgroupings within these major areas, particularly in the case of Musical Performance with its several applied music committees. A full range of large and small performing ensembles—from the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, and the Ars Musica String Quartet to the Concert Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra—provides superb opportunities for listening or for active participation. In advance of selecting the field of music for concentration, the student will consult the Director of the School of Music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the University, a student with a concentration area in music must have proficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument, and a working knowledge of the rudiments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music will be given at times to be announced. If a student cannot meet requirements when entering the University, arrangements may be made to meet them later. title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles which carry one hour of credit and which normally rehearse 5 hours per week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, the Marching Show Band, the Symphony Orchestra, and the Concert Orchestra.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles which carry onehalf of credit and which normally rehearse 2 hours per week. Included in this category are the Concert Band, Varsity Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensemble, and Training Orchestra.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles which carry one hour of credit and which normally rehearse 5 hours per week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera Chorus, and the University Singers.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles which carry onehalf hour of credit and which normally rehearse 2 hours per week. Included in this category are the Chorale, Women's Chorus, University Debs, the Men's Glee Club, and the Choral Union.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 372.

title: Planning and Producing the Musical Show
description: Designed to familiarize the student with standard operating procedures within the field of musical theatre. Provides a well structured approach to musical theatre production techniques.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, carrying one hours of credit and rehearsing normally 5 hours per week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, the Marching Show Band, the Symphony Orchestra, and the Concert Orchestra.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying onehalf hour of credit and normally rehearsing 2 hours per week. Included in this category are the Concert Band, Varsity Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensemble, and the Training Orchestra.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles carrying one hour of credit and normally rehearsing 5 hours per week. Included in this category are 'the Concert Choir, Opera Chorus, and the University Singers.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying onehalf hour of credit and normally rehearsing 2 hours per week. Included in this category are the Chorale, Women's Chorus, University Debs, the Men's Glee Club, and the Choral Union.

title: The Singing Actor
description: The application of stage convention and acting method for the vocal musician.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 172.

title: Music Theatre in America : A Survey of the Repertoire
description: An overview of the genre of musical theatre in America : its history and contemporary trends, together with the Music Education 141 study of individual works and the preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

title: Costuming for Musical Theatre and Dance
description: Costume design and construction for musical theatre and dance.

title: Recital
description: Attendance at recitals and concerts as specified in the music student handbook is the basis for the earning of Recital credit. Department of Music Education Carr, Head; Burkart, Caldwell, Curt, Dunn, Eberle, Griner, Karjala, Nichols, Phillips, Wakeland The preparation of teachers of music for all scholastic levels is of primary concern within the School of Music. The task of becoming an effective music teacher not only involves developing a high degree of musicianship and scholarship, but requires of the teachermusician a sincere interest and skill in assisting others to develop musical responsiveness. Three major fields of specialization are provided for the student seeking to be certified as a music teacher. These include the teaching area major in music which prepares the student to teach instrumental, choral, and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve, the teaching major in choralgeneral music which prepares the student to teach choral and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve, and the teaching major in instrumental music which is preparation for teaching instrumental music in grades kindergarten through twelve. In addition to these three major fields of specialization, several minor concentration areas in music are available to those who wish to attain a higher level of music competency by adding a minor concentration to a music teaching major, or for those who wish to combine the study of music with that of another subject. In order to graduate from Ball State University with a major or minor in any of the music teacher preparation fields, a student must present evidence of an ability to execute certain musical and educational tasks. This evidence, in addition to the successful completion of the curriculum, is shown through the demonstration of a firm commitment to teaching and a high level of competency on both primary and secondary performance media—symphonic instruments and/or voice, and piano. *

title: Sensory Awareness and Response to Music
description: For the elementary classroom teacher emphasizing sensory experiences based on learning sequences appropriate for children. Constitutes a basis for musical experiences to be explored in succeeding courses. Not open to the student who has credit in MUSED 350, 351, 352.

title: The Development and Administration of School Choral Activities
description: Analysis of the choral literature available for use in the secondary school as to its technical difficulty and suitability to choral groups of various sizes and musical backgrounds. The administration and supervision of choral activities, including the general chorus, the selected groups, and the voice classes. Techniques of choral arranging.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Brass Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 221. *Students are required to have completed a proficiency examination on piano and attained junior standing on their major medium of musical expression prior to enrolling in student teaching.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 223.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: Basic principle and application of piano tuning and the nomenclature and repair of the piano. An elective intended for students preparing for the field of music and others who may be interested in piano technology. Open to all students.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Advanced techniques of piano tuning, enabling the student to tune a piano independently. Principles of complete action adjustment and common minor repairs. Prerequisite : MUSED 240.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Complete repair and rebuilding of the piano. Prerequisite : MUSED 241. Open to all students.

title: Basic Musical Experiences for Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to develop creative musical responsiveness in students enrolled in the 2-year early elementary education program, and to demonstrate through laboratory experiences the application of creativity to the developmental characteristics of three-, four-, and fiveyear old children.

title: Children's Music: Lower Elementary Grades
description: Methods of teaching music to children in kindergarten and grades one through three. Basic theory of music, including notation ; class participation in musical activities and in the use of simple musical instruments, song books, recordings, and audiovisual aids. Parallel : MUSED 265. Not open to the student who is majoring or specializing in music.

title: Keyboard Skills for Elementary Classroom Teachers
description: Preparation of students of varying musical backgrounds and abilities in the use of the piano for teaching music in the elementary schools. Parallel: MUSED 264. Not open to the student who is majoring or specializing in music.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teachers sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled for individual study and exploration. Prerequisite : MUSED 164.

title: Teaching and Administration of Instrumental Music
description: Using the skills developed in instrumental minor studies as a point of departure, the student in survey classes covers the techniques of related families of instruments. Proper care of equipment, organization of physical factors, teaching of instrumental classes, and developing instrumental ensembles are made the basis for lectures and class discussions. Piano and voice majors are advised to reserve this course for the senior year. Prerequisite: minor skills in brass, woodwind, and string instruments.

title: The Teaching of Music in the Elementary School
description: The problems of teaching and supervising music in the elementary school for music supervisors and special teachers of music. Lesson planning and teaching are done in the class, and contact is made with teaching situations through directed observation. Leading music series are studied. Prerequisite : MUSTH 113 or the equivalent.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Primary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in the first three grades; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors, which is a continuation of 351. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six : singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High School
description: An exploration of the scope and character of musical activities designed to supplement membership in the established performing groups of the public schools and to provide an outlet for the many students not concerned with public performance. Acquaintance with materials and techniques appropriate to the study of music literature and music theory.

title: Introduction to Orff Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities will be explored in movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative utilization of simple percussion instruments. Music Education 143

title: Children's Music: Upper Elementary Grades
description: Music suitable for children in grades four, five, and six, and methods of teaching this music. Part singing and creative projects are given emphasis. New elements of musical theory are introduced and fundamentals are reviewed. Student participation in musical activities. Parallel : MUSED 362. Prerequisite : MUSED 264 and 265, or the equivalent.

title: Music Appreciation, Materials, and Methods
description: Designed to enrich the musical background of the student in the common heritage of musical literature and to suggest methods for presenting these materials to children. Parallel: MUSED 361.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary School
description: Designed to enrich the musical background of the student in the common heritage of music and to suggest methods for presenting suitable musical materials and experiences to children. More intensive involvement with music exemplars, including appreciation and specific musical skills, is given emphases. Prerequisite : MUSED 164 and 266.

title: Administration and Planning of the Church Music Program
description: Formation and training of adult and children's choirs in churches. Congregational singing. Service planning. The clergy, the congregation, and the church musician.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano. 2
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods for Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction situations. Prerequisite : credit in classical guitar.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, shortterm course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing. Contact with new materials and methods will be insured in part by the inclusion of two or more distinguished visiting instructors on the staff.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experiences with the materials and activities of general music classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possibilities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: The Orff Workshop—Beginning
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the beginning phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on the basic approaches to the Orff method of teaching music to children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The Orff Workshop—Intermediate
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the more advanced phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite : MUSED 443 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyear old children.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite and parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 1
description: Provides a fundamental working knowledge of skills required in maintaining stringed instruments at the elementary and secondary school levels. Study and application of school repair problems in regard to the violin, viola, cello, and doublebass. General techniques in making adjustments, gluing, and using tools properly. Analyses of the various woods used in instruments and bows.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 2
description: Advanced study and experience in more specialized repairs on stringed instruments. Discussions and laboratory work including splicing, grafting, varnishing, carving and bow rehairing. Historical resume of stringed instruments and makers from the seventeenth to the twentieth century.

title: Psychology of Music
description: Presentation of materials as an aid to the understanding of the nature and extent of individual differences in musical talent. Specific preparation in the psychology of audition, motor control, and in the analysis of the musical mind leading to a natural application in the psychology of musical training.

title: Tests, Measurements, and Guidance in Music
description: Acquaints the teacher with tests of sensory capacities, appreciation, and achievement. Briefly reviews such statistical and other data as make for an enlightened evaluation of the various tests and of their results.

title: Music in Therapy and Special Education
description: The theoretical aspects of music therapy and their appropriate application to special education in the public schools. Emphasizes the power of music to elicit normal interaction with peers from the child with a learning difficulty.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis on those specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: Provides the superior student with an opportunity for intensive study and research in a particular aspect of music education. Prerequisite : permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Music History and Musicology Michael, Head; Hodgson, Korf, Mackey, Pence, Tretick The music history and musicology area of the School of Music serves the entire University through its program of general education : the teacher in training through courses designed to broaden understanding of the art interpreted to students; the student of liberal arts through enhanced cultural and historical orientation; and the prospective graduate scholar or researcher through specialized courses exploring the great body of literature which has been accumulating in and about music for many centuries.

title: Introduction to the Literature of Music
description: An overview of the many forms of musical composition and of the media for their performance to be used as a basis for subsequent musical experiences.

title: Music for the Listener : An Introduction
description: Introduction to the elements of music, followed by a study of musical styles through a survey of the literature of music. Lectures, films, classroom discussion, and recorded music supplemented by attendance at concerts and recitals. No previous knowledge of music required. Not open to students with areas in music.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite : permission of the department head.

title: Music History 1
description: The growth of music from its beginnings through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The origins of music, the development of notation, and the growth of early polyphonic forms. Open only to students with areas in music except by permission of the department head. Music History and Musicology 145

title: Music History 3
description: Developments in music from the time of Beethoven to the present. Transition from the classical to romantic periods, the various reactions to Romanticism, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 212, or permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Instrumental Music from the Time of Bach
description: The growth and development of musical forms and styles as they apply to music for orchestra and solo instruments from the late Baroque period to our time. Prerequisite : MUHIS 101 or 213.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Following a brief survey of the early development of opera, there will be a more detailed consideration of examples of this genre from the middle of the eighteenth century to the present time. Prerequisite : MUHIS 101 or 213.

title: Choral and Vocal Solo Literature from Haydn to the Present
description: The development of the cantata, oratorio, mass, motet, anthem, and the lied ; great masterworks in these forms. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 213.

title: Ballet History
description: A history of ballet, tracing its beginnings, romantic heights, and contemporary trends.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including the function of figured bass, significant contrapuntal developments, the evolution of opera, oratorio, and cantata, and the growth of various instrumental genres such as the concerto grosso, sonata, suite, and types of keyboard music. Prerequisite : MUHIS 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles which marked the transition from Baroque to Classic music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the nineteenth century and its relationship to the Romantic movement, the growth of chromatic harmony, the changes in traditional types such as the symphony and opera, the growth of the art song, the tone poem, and the character piece. Prerequisite : MUHIS 213 or permission of the department head.

title: History and Development of Jazz
description: A survey of the evolutionary process in jazz music in the United States. Includes discussion of the styles and characteristics of each period of jazz history and the contributions of selected groups and individuals. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 213, or permission of the department head.

title: Dance Notation 1
description: The beginnings of dance notation and an introduction to the main systems used today (Labonotation, Benesh, etc.) Prerequisite: some previous dance experience.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Restricted to students on the Honors Program.

title: Hymnody in Worship
description: Hymns in early Jewish and Western Christian tradition: their historical and liturgical context and contemporary use. A summary of Western religious thought as exposed in liturgical poetry. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 211, 212, or 213.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite : MUHIS 101, 211, 212, or 213.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite : permission of the department head.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: Provides the superior students with an opportunity for guided reading and intensive study in an area of music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisites : MUHIS 101, 211, 212, or 213.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 1
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites : Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites : Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Field Sources of American Musical Culture
description: Field study in major musical capitals, including the best known festival centers. Seminars scheduled in connection with planned travel are concerned with the orientation of members to the historic significance of composers native to the region, to the influence of nationalistic schools, and to the interaction of architectural and other physical matters with the musical output. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students on all curricula. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Music Theory and Composition Sherman, Head; Foley, Hoffmann, Knight, Pellegrini, Scott The Department of Music Theory and Composition has gained prominence for its leadership role in the development of innovative practices relating to teaching and learning in music theory and composition. The department has developed the nation's first contemporized basic music theory curriculum. The Electronic Music Theory Laboratory provides individualized instruction in the aural and visual perception of music through "Aural Comprehension in Music," a unique program of instruction developed in the lab and used nationally. The Electronic Music Studio is another facility which is rapidly growing and assuming an important role in the evolving curricula of the School of Music. The studio is fully equipped for the production and processing of electronic and concrete sounds. The ARP synthesizer is interfaced with a digital computer for full digitalanalog control. The facility is used for undergraduate and graduate research as well as electronic composition.

title: Music Fundamentals
description: Recommended for those entering freshmen whose background of experience in the fundamentals of music theory is thought to be too limited for the successful completion of MUSTH 111 or MUSED 264 and MUSED 265. The course deals with such fundamentals as music reading, spelling (intervals, scales, triads, meter signatures, key signatures), terminology, and notation. 111, 112, 113. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) Review of terminology and fundamentals precedes an extensive study of the tonal, rhythmic, motivic, and formal structure of melody through composition and analysis. The basic elements of music are studied through the analysis and writing of music in two, three, and four parts. Elementary work in transposition, scoring, and harmonic alterations. Music reading, aural discernment, and rhythmic training provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. These courses must be taken in course number sequence. 211, 212, 213. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) More complex elements of nineteenth and twentieth century music studied through composition and analysis. Advanced work in music reading and aural discernment provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. Prerequisite : MUSTH 113. These courses must be taken in course number sequence.

title: Acoustics: Natural
description: The natural acoustical phenomena related to the sound production, amplification, and characteristics of conventional instruments in the natural environment of the studio and concert hall. Prerequisites: PHYCS 184.

title: Acoustics: Electronic
description: The elctronic production, reproduction, and alteration of sound as it is related to the production and reproduction of music. Prerequisite : PHYCS 184. Music Theory and Composition 147

title: Music Calligraphy
description: Practical experience in calligraphic skills and layout procedures pertinent to the preparation of music scores and parts. Prerequisite : MUSTH 113.

title: Compositional Practices : The Baroque
description: The theoretical principles, stylistic forces, and aesthetics that characterize the compositional practices of the Baroque period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Compositional Practices: Eighteenth-Century Classicism
description: The theoretical principles, stylistic forces, and aesthetics that characterize the compositional practices of eighteenthcentury classicism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic Music
description: A workshop in current practices of producing music by electronic means. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213. 371, 372, 373. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing short instrumental and vocal compositions with emphasis on developing the student's technical capacity to achieve freedom of style. Prerequisite : MUSTH 213.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Analysis will be applied to a broad representation of musical masterworks from various periods with examination of the macroand microstructure and construction of selected works. Special attention is given to musical practices before and after the period of tertian harmony. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Orchestration
description: Scoring for large and small orchestral ensembles. Particular attention given to voice positioning, doubling, and textural deployment as regards harmonic weight and color. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band and wind ensemble. Particular attention is given to voicing, sectional and crosssectional doubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 442.

title: Arranging for the Dance Band
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques as employed by current leading dance band and jazz arrangers, and the practice of writing and performing scores by members of the class. Prerequisite: MUSTH 442.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisites : MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Medieval and Renaissance Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of Medieval and Renaissance music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Electronic Music Studio 1
description: An introductory course in the fundamentals of sound, its physical and perceptual dimensions, as a basis for the electronic synthesis and analysis of musical sounds. Studio laboratory time required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Electronic Music Studio 2
description: Structured to allow the student an individualized approach in the application of electronic sound synthesis compositionally or in educational research. Studio laboratory time required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 461. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. 471, 472, 473. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing more complex and extended instrumental and vocal compositions with continued emphasis on the development of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 373.

title: Music Theory in the Secondary School
description: An investigation of pedagogical precepts and problems relating to music theory in the secondary school. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Independent Study
description: Independent study in any area of music theory via readings, analysis, and/or research. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 and permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Musical Performance Marsh, Head; Albright, Anderson, E. Bourgeot, M. In solo and in ensemble performances, members of the Ball State music faculty and their students have received acclaim throughout this country and in many other areas of the world. The departmental majoOs designed to meet the needs of the increasing number of students each year who enter Ball State with aspirations to careers in professional performance. Students preparing for licensing as teachers of music share fully in the environment of artist teachers and outstanding musical organizations.

title: I Major Study (Brass)
description: One halfhour lesson (private or small class at the discretion of the department head) on a brass instrument weekly. Taken each quarter of the freshman year by students majoring in brass instrument performance. 102.* fi Major Study (Percussion). (1) One halfhour lesson (private or small class at the discretion of the department head) on a percussion instrument weekly. Taken each quarter of the freshman year by students majoring in percussion instrument performance. 103.*I Major Study (Strings). (1) One halfhour lesson (private or small class at the discretion of the department head) on a string instrument weekly. Taken each quarter of the freshman year by students majoring in string instrument performance. 104. * I Major Study (Harp). (1) One halfhour lesson (private or small class at the discretion of the department head) on the harp weekly.
