(3) A broad study of the methods used to process the natural polymer, wood, including forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing. Laboratory activities are directed toward helping students acquire basic understanding and skills related to wood processing, and the careers in the area. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 213 and 316.

title: Industrial Furniture and Cabinet Production
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Advanced Wood Processing
description: Involves units of study in modifying wood materials, bentwood laminations, and wood finishing. Additional opportunities provided for individual problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in wood processing particularly in the areas where the student lacks confidence and experience. Individual problemsolving emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 316. COMMUNICATION Introductory

title: Introduction to Industrial Communication
description: A focus on the elements common to industrial communication. Classroom and laboratory activities are related to the design, production, and distribution of printed graphic, photographic, electronic, and technical graphic communications.

title: Industrial Design
description: A study of major factors involved in creating an appealing design which can be manufactured economically. Topics include the design process, sketching, creativity, elements and principles of design, materials and processes, and human and environmental factors. *Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education. Graphic Arts (Printed Graphic and Photographic) 254. * Printed Graphic Communication. (4) A study of printed graphic communications with major emphasis on design and developing messages, preparing messages for production, and producing messages using lithographic, relief, intaglio, and screen processes. Prerequisite: IED 154. 255. * Photographic Communications in Industry. (3) Designed to familiarize students with the applications of photography to industrial communications. Students will study basic techniques, equipment, processes, and materials utilized by contemporary industry in communication. Prerequisite: IED 154.

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: Introductory experiences in the various methods used by the graphic arts industry. These include letterpress and offset printing, drypoint and block etchings, silkscreen printing, embossing and gold leaf printing, marking devices, and bookbinding.

title: Letterpress Printing and Bookbinding
description: Fundamental letterpress theory is stressed, with experiences in layout, composition, imposition, presswork and bookbinding ; single and twocolor platen presswork ; and looseleaf and saddlestitch binding operations. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Photography
description: Fundamentals of photography, including camera work, black and white film processing, enlarging, composition, and basic color photography.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Fundamental theory, exposure techniques, film processing, printmaking, and composition considerations in color photography. Students must provide their own cameras. Prerequisite: IED 386.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Principles and experiences involved in lithography as a printing process. Cold type composition, camera work, stripping, plate processing, and press work ; line shots and halftones. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Problems in Printed Graphics
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281. Technical Graphics

title: Introduction to Graphics
description: Various graphical representation and problem solving techniques and their application to the design process. Included are the theory of orthographic projection, sketching, lettering, geometric constructions, section views, English and metric dimensioning, fasteners, and working drawings. Problem solving includes experiences with elementary descriptive geometry topics. Elemeptary design problems are included.

title: Introduction to Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing basic production drawings. Topics include lettering, sketching, geometric construction, design process, isometric drawing, orthographic multiview projection, sectional views, dimensions, fasteners, and working drawings. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 103.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing productionrelated drawings in selected specialized areas. Topics include auxiliary views, revolutions, cams, gears, bearings, machine components, welding drawing, structural drawing, piping drawing, and electrical drawing. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Advanced Technical Graphics
description: Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection ; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; and lateral developments of geometric solids. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256.

title: Manufacturing Design
description: Focuses on the process of design and principles of drafting as applied to manufacturing industry. Included are product and tool design. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256. 256. * Technical Graphics Communications. (4) A study of the various graphical methods used to transmit technical ideas and information in industry. Included are sketching, pictorials, orthographics for manufacturing and construction, charts and graphs, reprographics, and industrial practices. Prerequisite: IED 154.

title: Residential Drafting and Design
description: Included is a survey of basic principles of residential planning and designing; methods of construction; and preparation of preliminary design sketches, perspective drawings, models, and selected working drawings.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Contemporary Concepts in Drafting and Design
description: Contemporary topics in the field of drafting and design including computer graphics; reproduction, storage, and retrieval of *Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education. drawings; modeling; photodrafting; and other recently implemented industrial practices. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256.

title: Problems in Technical Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in technical graphic areas based on the needs of the student and the approval of the instructor. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256. Electronics 257. * Industrial Electronic Communication Systems. (2) Electronics as it is used in the field of industrial communication. Students will learn about principles, components, and operation of industrial communications systems and will develop skill in operating some electronic test equipment. Prerequisite: IED 154.

title: Computer Fundamentals
description: Theory and basic circuits of computers. Laboratory activity will consist of group construction of basic computer circuits.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Theory of the vacuum tube and semiconductors, with special reference to their application in radio, television, and electronic circuits in industry. Individual and group experiences in project activity of the experimental, maintenance, and creative types. Prerequisite: IED 257 or 370.

title: Problems in Industrial Electronics
description: Special individual and group problems in advanced electrical circuitry involving most of the components of electrical circuits, with special emphasis upon thermionic emission tubes and photo emission devices. Complex problems assigned to groups of students will characterize the project activity. Prerequisite: IED 257 or 370. POWER Introductory

title: Introduction to Power
description: An overview of the development and utilization of power in terms of energy, energy conversion, transmission, control and applications, with continual concern for energy conservation and environmental quality. Electricity

title: Introduction to Electricity
description: Introductory experiences and exploration in the broad field of electricity with special emphasis upon means of producing and transmitting electron flow. Instruction in appropriate electrical projects and familiarization with electrical measuring instruments are important experiences. 258. * Industrial Electrical Power. (4) The conversion, transmission, and control of electrical power with an emphasis on developing knowledge and skill in control and utilization circuitry. A companion course to IED 259. Prerequisite: IED 158.

title: Applications of Electricity
description: Fundamental electrical theory, with special reference to applications in heating, lighting, electrolysis, electrical communication, and mechanical power. Individual and group experiences through the use of experiments and construction of appropriate projects. Prerequisite: IED 171 or 258.

title: Servicing Electrical Applicances and Motors
description: Practices and careers in the appliance and motor repair fields. Laboratory experiences include servicing of electrical applicances and motors. Prerequisite: IED 370 or 258. Mechanical and Fluid Power

title: Introduction to Power and Transportation
description: Concentration on the internal combustion engine. A study of power sources, basic mechanisms, component systems, efficiencies and power measurement, and the utilization and application to transportation and industry, and direct,- energy converters.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: To acquire fundamental skills and teaching knowledge through experience related to power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasis on internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Factors involved in setting up a transportation unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite: IED 140 or 259.

title: Mechanical and Fluid Power
description: Energy conversion, transmission, and control within the mechanical and fluid power parameters. A companion course to IED 258. Prerequisite: IED 158.

title: Advanced Automechanics
description: The maintenance, repair, and theory underlying power train and power transmission units, air conditioning systems, emission control systems, and compression ignition engines. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Applications of Power to Air Transportation
description: Airframe and aircraft engine systems involving limited maintenance experience in engine systems; instrumentation, principles of * Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education. aerodynamics and flight control; internal reaction engines, and atmospheric effects on power output and navigation. Prerequisite: IED 240 or 259.

title: Application of Power to Water Transportation
description: Small boats, outboard engines, principles of operation, components systems, with particular attention to charging circuits, maintenance, boating laws and safety, inland waterways navigation, propeller theory, boat hulls, performance, and sailing. Prerequisite: IED 240 or 259.

title: Introduction to Fluid Power
description: Fundamental theory of fluids, fluid conditioning, components, symbology and basic circuitry. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 444 or 445.

title: Special Problems in Hydraulics
description: An introduction to the fundamental principles of hydraulic circuitry. Characteristics of hydraulics, the functioning of component parts of hydraulic systems, and the application to power transmission and control.

title: Special Problems in Pneumatics
description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of pneumatic circuitry. Included is a study of the characteristics of fluids, the functioning of components, and the development of pneumatic circuits and pneumatic logic control. SPECIAL

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to individuals currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: A discussioncentered course which focuses primarily on internship experiences. Through these dialogues, individuals will become aware of a greater variety of situations which may be encountered in their chosen field. Open only to students with areas in industrial supervision. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Manual Arts Therapy Clinical Training
description: A field assignment with opportunities to work with qualified manual arts therapists at the Veterans' Administration Hospital in Marion, Indiana. Credit for 10 hours is awarded for minimum of 8 weeks fulltime training. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299 and IED 391. PROFESSIONAL Elementary School Industrial Arts

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes which provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units are examined and evaluated.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Industrial Arts
description: A classroom involvement experience for industrial arts majors in the elementary school. To familiarize the student with the philosophy, history, and principles of industrial arts in the elementary school. Affords the student the opportunity to teach a short unit of instruction in cooperation with an elementary teacher to elementary age children in the local community. Prerequisite: industrial arts major or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Industrial Arts for Elementary Teachers
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of a wide variety of tools, materials, and industrial processes through the planning and organization of group activity units. Prerequisite: IED 364 or permission of the department head Secondary School Industrial Education

title: Exploring Industrial Education
description: Focuses on teaching industrial education as a career. Students learn about the development and types of industrial education programs offered in public schools and the undergraduate industrial teacher education program at Ball State University.

title: Student Organizations Practicum
description: A practicum in the organization, maintenance, and evaluation of student vocational organizations. A total of 4 quarter hours must be taken by persons seeking certification as a teacher of vocational trade, industrial and technical laboratory programs, and an endorsement as a cooperative coordinator. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: An introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Legislation will be analyzed in light of past and present issues of vocational education and its relationship as a vital component of the total educational system. Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education.

title: Curriculum Development in Industrial Education
description: Designed to provide prospective industrial education teachers with the tools for rational decisionmaking relative to curriculum development for industrial education programs. The emphasis is on developing an adequate conceptual framework within which to design courses. Prerequisite: IED 198. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 394.

title: Industrial Safety
description: Provides an awareness of the regulations governing health and safety and the methods and practices used in industry in general and industrial education specifically to comply with these regulations. Designed primarily for students choosing concentration areas in the Department of Industrial Education and Technology.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by a breakdown into components of jobs, tasks, and processes will be examined.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs are examined and evaluated.

title: Curriculum Problems in Industrial Education
description: Criteria used in determining nature and content of learning experiences in industrial education classes. Teacherpupil planning, group activities, and problemsolving methods. Textbooks and related industrial and government publications evaluated and course outlines developed. Prerequisite: a minimum of 12 quarter hours from the following courses: IED 103, 125, 127, 140, 171, 213, 231, or 281.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Industrial Education
description: Problems of organization and management related to industrial education learning activities. Objectives, terminology, evaluation methods, teaching devices, lesson plans, textbooks, equipment, and supplies are examined. Industrial education classes in public schools are observed. Prerequisite: IED 198 and 298 and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Education
description: Practice in various contemporary approaches to industrial education drawn from methods and curriculum problems courses. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in one or more of the contemporary approaches to industrial education, preferably a public school. Prerequisite: IED 198, 298, and 395.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Discipline oriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of industrial education evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of industrial education in the secondary school curriculum (grades 5 through 12). Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: IED 298 and 395.

title: Independent Studies in Industrial Education
description: Special investigation in industrial education on an independent basis. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques and skills are emphasized. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department head. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis is placed upon state functions.

title: Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Individual and group studies of one or more major problems in the industrial education field, application of research techniques to the problems for solution, and reporting of findings.

title: Advanced Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Advanced study of problem -solving techniques in industrial education. Individual and group activities involving research and experimentation.

title: Theory and Practice in Letterpress Printing
description: Fundamentals of typography, hand -and powerfed presswork, basic bookbinding, and press maintenance and safety, while maintaining a production printing schedule.

title: Theory and Practice in Photo -Offset Lithography
description: Offset photolithographic experience covering the practice of camera operation, stripping, plate making, and offset press operation, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 181.

title: Theory and Practice in Commercial Printing
description: Use of the Frankline Price Catalog for letterpress and offset printing, paper schedules, postal rates, study of the Government Printing Office style book, and standard printing forms and correct terminology, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 182.

title: Quality Control in the Printing Industry
description: The ability to use the tools of quality control in the printing industry. Emphasis is given to the use of densitometry, correct register, proofreading, ink coverage, proper binding, cropping, paper and ink. Various other topics are considered.

title: Printing Estimating
description: Application of the Point System of Measurement; figuring the amount and cost of composition; basic size, thickness, and weight of paper stock; figuring and cutting paper stock; spoilage allowances; and figuring the cost of paper stock.

title: Internship in Printing Technology
description: A fiveweek internship in a printing industry, working under industrial standards and regulations in the type of printing industry preferred by the student, as much as possible. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Theory and Practice in Publications
description: Various publication formats that are commonly used by institutions and industries. Both offset and letterpress forms of makeup will be employed in maintaining publication schedules. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Theory and Practice in Estimating and Copyfitting
description: Participants will estimate costs, order appropriate stock, learn schedules, make layouts, compose forms, cut the stock, estimate waste, and other details in completely planning and executing a printing order on a previously made schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 281.

title: Theory and Practice in Color Printing and Process Work
description: Printing of letterpress and offset color work, involving technical procedures in color separation and the use of densitometer and the use of various kinds of printing plates for letterpress color work. The completion of the secondyear creative project is a requirement. Prerequisite: ITE 282.

title: Color Process Printing
description: The photographic steps in making plates for photomechanical printing of color pictures. Both color reflection and color transparency copy are considered. Prerequisite: ITE 186.

title: Type Design and Copyfitting
description: The determination of the amount of area necessary for composition according to size and family of type by use of a slide rule. The study of modern type design and usage, as well as outstanding typographers and their contributions. The place of the advertising agency in modern display composition and its contributions. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Organized and orderly methods of planning production to gain more profit, sales, production, and work. Prerequisite: ITE 284.

title: Industrial Internship
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual work experience in industry which is related to the objectives of the curriculum. The trainee is supervised by the University Coordinator and the Plant Manager. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned, but not more than 4 hours may be earned at one time.

title: Printing Management
description: Business facts needed for profitable management of a printing or lithographic business and the procedures to supply these facts accurately, promptly, and with laborsaving shortcuts. Prerequisite: ITE 289.

title: Industrial Internship
description: The student will work full time for one quarter in a position involving the supervision of production employees in a printing industry under supervision of the Department of Industrial Education and Technology. Prerequisite: ITE 484. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance, to make simple modifications and installations in the areas of plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climate control systems of the home. Department of Library Science Axeen, Chairman; Cox, Hsu, Kirby, Rite, Tevis, Wetmore, Yeamans Library science is concerned with the selection, acquisition, processing, organization, and maintenance of materials in library collections and with the maximum use of these materials in serving a library's clientele. Knowledge of bibliographic aids, skill in their use, and the ability to work effectively with associates and library patrons are characteristics of the successful librarian. Thorough familiarity with materials suitable for various types of library users must be acquired by the student of library science, in addition to the mastery of technical routines necessary for efficient organization. The purpose of the undergraduate program in library science at Ball State University is the preparation of school librarians. Students are qualified to meet Indiana state certification requirements for school library and audiovisual services. Library Science 143 Continuing reassessment of elementary and secondary education has resulted in a renewed appreciation of the school library as a media center where educational materials in a variety of media are available to students, teachers, and administrators. School media centers at all levels have increased in number with the growth of school systems. Progress is being made in the establishment of elementary school libraries since it has been demonstrated that younger children benefit greatly from a variety of learning materials. The school librarian is educated as a teacher and must meet state requirements for a teaching certificate. The school librarian must understand fundamental learning processes, teaching methods, and child psychology. In addition, a basic knowledge of school curricula and special training in the analysis, evaluation, selection, organization, dissemination, and use of instructional materials for young people are essential. Library science courses are designed to help the student acquire this special training. description: History and overview of the utilization of media in instruction, commercial enterprises, and industry with a discussion of job requirements and opportunities.

description: Instruction in the operation of projection, video, and audio equipment. Laboratory practice in maintenance and minor repair of equipment.

title: Multimedia Design and Display
description: Principles of media design and perception patterns. Application of these principles to the construction of twoand threedimensional displays for library and instructional uses.

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work in the development of multimedia materials for teaching and presentation. Students will have laboratory experience in various mounting, laminating, lettering, coloring, and transparencymaking techniques.

title: Multimedia Production 3

description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment, accessories, and related software. Preparation of bid specifications.

description: Supervised practical experiences at an offcampus media center in various phases of media technology.

description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of materials in school libraries by use of the Dewey Decimal Classification and the construction of a library catalog. Consideration is given to book and nonbook materials.

description: The principles and practice of the cataloging and organization of multimedia materials. Prerequisite: LIB 342 or the equivalent.

title: Methods and Materials for Student Use of School Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching students the skills necessary to the use of the media center. Prerequisite: LIB 100, 101, 102, 133, 201, 202, 203, 342, 460 or the equivalent and EDSEC 299 and the identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Utilization of Media Center Resources in the Curriculum
description: The curriculum role of the school media center, its unique contributions to learning, its supportive services, and its responsibilities shared with all other aspects of the educational program. Prerequisite: LIB 395.

title: Audiovisual Materials
description: Provides an acquaintance with and an appreciation for instructional materials such as films, filmstrips, slides, transparencies, and recordings. Practice in utilizing various types of audiovisual equipment and in preparing inexpensive teaching materials.

title: Production' of Audiovisual Media
description: Basic principles, skills, and techniques of still and motion picture photography. Practical applications of the audio and video tape recorders.

title: Materials Selection in School Media Centers
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection of materials for school media centers. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials.

title: Materials for Children
description: The reading and examining of book and nonbook materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examination of book and nonbook materials for young adult programs.

description: The function, organizational patterns, maintenance, control, planning, and equipment of school media centers. The application of administrative principles to school media centers. Prerequisite: LIB 133, 342, 460, 461, 462, or the equivalents.

School of Music Hargreaves, Director; Baker, Burkart, Dunn, Karjala, Niccum, Strawbridge, Woodrum The School of Music embraces two departments: Academic Studies in Music and Applied Studies in Music. Administrative efficiency and scholarly pursuits are enhanced by further subgroupings within these major areas. Thus, the divisions of music education, music history and musicology, and music theory and composition are identified in the Department of Academic Studies in Music, and divisions of keyboard, voice and guitar, symphonic instruments, and ensembles and conducting in the Department of Applied Studies in Music. A full range of large and small performing ensembles — from the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, and the Ars Musica String Quartet, the Concert Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra — provides superb opportunities for listening or for active participation. Less usual groups such as the Harp Ensemble, the Colleguim Musicum, the String Sinfonietta, the University Singers, and the Ball State Ballet accent the diversity of performing outlets on the Ball State campus. Any student on campus, regardless of major, may audition for membership in the University concert organizations. In advance of selecting the field of music for concentration, the student will consult with the Coordinator of Undergraduate Programs in Music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the University, a student with a concentration area in music must have proficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument, and a working knowledge of the rudiments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music will be given at times to be announced. If a student cannot meet requirements when entering the University, arrangements may be made to meet them later. If lacking in the applied music requirement, the individual will study without credit until it can be met. All students with a concentration area in music are expected to attend the weekly recital meeting and to perform there with a frequency recommended by the individual teacher of applied music. Additional information will be found in the Music Student Handbook. In advance of completing registration each quarter, the student will clear requests for applied music instruction through the office of the Coordinator of Undergraduate Programs ; asignmento specific instructors wil be made by the Department of Aplied Studies in Music. Students wishing to qualify for certification as teachers of music in the public schools should refer to the appropriate curricular information listed under the Department of Academic Studies in Music as well as in the area requirements which follow. Students wishing to prepare for careers in professional performance, in composition and arranging, or in scholarly activity and research, are encouraged to enroll in the appropriate departmental major. The departmental minors also may serve some of these goals, but the total number of hours required for their completion is kept at a level which will serve the student in a liberal arts orientation who seeks broad cultural development rather than specialized proficiency. A student whose work load permits may register for additional lessons in the selected minor field or in other minor fields, provided the approval of the Head of the Department of Applied Studies in Music has been secured. Practice rooms should be reserved in the office of the School of Music at the beginning of each quarter or term. Each student with a concentration area in music is advised to have a piano available for use at a certain time daily, either at the University or elsewhere. All students with concentration areas in music will participate actively in ensembles according to their curricular requirements. Those planning to become directors of instrumental ensembles or supervisors of instrumental music ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the University bands and University orchestras, and vocalists preparing to become directors of choral activities ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the appropriate University choral groups. In addition, students are expected to take advantage of the opportunities for musical broadening provided by membership in the ensembles outside their special field. Department of Academic Studies in Music Hodgson, Head; Burkart, Caldwell, Carr, Curt, Dunn, Eberle, Foley, Griner, Hoffmann, Karjala, Knight, Korf, Mackey, Michael, Nichols, Pellegrini, Pence, Phillips, Scott, Sherman, Tretick, Wakeland. The Department of Academic Studies in Music includes studies in music education, music therapy, music history, music literature, music theory, music composition, electronic music, and several special areas including Collegium Musicum. These studies are grouped fot convenient reference into the curricular divisions which follow this general introduction to the department. The preparation of teachers of music for all scholastic levels is a primary concern of this department. The task of becoming an effective music teacher not only involves developing a high degree of musicianship and scholarship, but requires of the teachermusician a sincere interest and skill in assisting others to develop musical responsiveness. Four fields of specialization are provided the student seeking certification as a music teacher in the public schools. These include: the allgrade teaching major in music, the teaching major in instrumental music, the teaching major in choral music and the teaching major in general music. The allgrade teaching major prepares the student to teach instrumental, choral and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve. The instrumental teaching major prepares the student to teach instrumental music in grades kindergarten through twelve. The teaching major in choral music prepares the student to teach choral music in grades kindergarten through twelve with particular emphasis in the area of performing groups at these grade levels. The teaching major in general music provides the student with preparation in teaching general music classes in grades kindergarten through twelve. In addition to these four major fields of specialization, several minor concentration areas in music are available to those who wish to attain a higher level of music competency by adding a minor concentration to a music teaching major, or for those who wish to combine the study of music with that of another subject. In order to graduate from Ball State University with a major or minor in any of the music teacher preparation fields, a student must present evidence of an ability to execute certain musical and educational tasks. This evidence, in addition to the successful completion of the curriculum, is shown through the demonstration of a firm commitment to teaching and high level of competency on both primary and secondary performance media — symphonic instruments and/or voice, and piano. * Courses in music history and music literature serve the entire University through the program of general education. The teacher in training is afforded opportunity to broaden his/her understanding of the art of music through a variety of more specialized history courses, and the liberal arts student may gain cultural and historical enrichment in music through selection of courses appropriate to his/her needs. The prospective graduate scholar or researcher may take advantage of numerous opportunities to develop new insights into and a deeper knowledge of the large body of literature in and about music which has been accumulating for several centuries. The basic twoyear music theory sequence offered by this department provides courses to be pursued concomitantly with other programs in the School of Music and, additionally, affords a background of fundamental musical knowledge for the nonmusic student. Furthermore, the basic twoyear music theory sequence is designed to prepare the student thoroughly for subsequent musical experience in three broad categories: further undergraduate studies of music, graduate studies in music, and classroom and studio music teaching. Beyond the basic twoyear music theory sequence, courses in music theory and composition are available to the student in a variety of compositional styles and practices. The student intending to pursue graduate work in music theory and composition is afforded numerous opportunities to prepare in both general and more specialized terms through courses offered by this department. The Electronic Music Studio has developed rapidly in recent years and plays a significant role in the evolving curricula of the School of MusiC. The ARP synthesizer is interfaced with a digital computer for full digitalanalog control. The curricular patterns, programs, and offerings of the Department of Academic Studies in Music are under constant scrutiny for improvement. Changes will be implemented where these enhance the program and serve the student more effectively.

title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Designed for the potential music teacher.

title: Sensory Awareness and Response to Music
description: For the elementary classroom teacher emphasizing sensory experiences based on learning sequences appropriate for children. Constitutes a basis for musical experiences to be explored in succeeding courses. Not open to the student who has credit in MUSED 350, 351, 352.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: A basic inquiry into the value of craftsmanship and the principles of piano tuning. The problems and remedies of new and used pianos will be discussed. An introductory course open to all students interested in the care and maintenance of the piano.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Application of piano temperament tuning theory with emphasis on the development of proper tuning techniques. Prerequisite: MUSED 240 or permission of the department head.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Principles of basic action regulation and common minor repairs. Prerequisite: MUSED 241 or permission of the department head.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Brass Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 250.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 252.

title: The Development and Administration of School Choral Activities
description: Analysis of the choral literature available for use in the secondary school as to its technical difficulty and suitability to choral groups of various sizes and musical backgrounds. The administration and supervision of choral activities, including the general chorus, the selected groups, and the voice classes. Techniques of choral arranging.

title: Basic Musical Experiences for Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to develop creative responsiveness in students enrolled in educational programs for young children, and to demonstrate through laboratory experiences the application of creativity to the developmental characteristics of threefour-, and fiveyear old children.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teachers sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled for individual study and exploration. Prerequisite: MUSED 164.

title: The Teaching of Music in Elementary School
description: The problems of teaching and supervising music in the elementary school for music supervisors and special teachers of music. Lesson planning and teaching are done in the class, and contact is made with teaching situations through directed observation. Leading music series are studied. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113 or the equivalent.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Primary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in the first three grades; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors, which is a continuation of 351. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six: singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High School
description: An exploration of the scope and character of musical activities designed to supplement membership in the established performing groups of the public schools and to provide an outlet for the many students not concerned with public performance. Acquaintance with materials and techniques appropriate to the study of music literature and music theory.

title: Teaching and Administration of Instrumental Music
description: Using the skills developed in instrumental minor studies as a point of departure, the student in survey classes covers the techniques of related families of instruments. Proper care of equipment, organization of physical factors, teaching of instrumental classes, and developing instrumental ensembles are made the basis for lectures and class discussions. Piano and voice majors are advised to reserve this course for the senior year. Prerequisite: minor skills in brass, woodwind, and string instruments.

title: Introduction to Orff Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities will be explored in movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative utilization of simple percussion instruments.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary School
description: Designed to enrich the musical background of the student in the common heritage of music and to suggest methods for presenting suitable musical materials and experiences to children. More intensive involvement with music exemplars, including appreciation and specific musical skills, is given emphases. Prerequisite: MUSED 164 and 266.

title: Administration and Planning of the Church Music Program
description: Formation and training of adult and children's choirs in churches. Congregation singing. Service planning. The clergy, the congregation, and the church musician.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, short -term course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing. Contact with new materials and methods will be insured in part by the inclusion of two or more distinguished visiting instructors on the staff.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experiences with the materials and activities of general music classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possibilities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: The Orff Workshop — Beginning
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the beginning phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on the basic approaches to the Orff method of teaching music to children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The Orff Workshop — Intermediate
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the more advanced phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite: MUSED 443 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyear old children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 2
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods for Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction situations. Prerequisite: credit in classical guitar.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite and parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Methods for Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods for teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level, or permission of the department head.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students ; singing and conducting opportunities of standard choral literature ; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Handbell Techniques
description: An introduction to the history, literature, and playing techniques of handbells. Includes opportunities to conduct and to perform with handbell choirs. Discussion of administering handbell choirs in church and school situations.

title: Basic Movement and Choreography
description: Designed to acquaint the music therapist or teacher with the fundamentals of physical interpretations of music. Deals with techniques appropriate for swing choirs, small ensembles, and general staging practices in performance preparation.

title: Introduction to the Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school comprise the framework of this course designed for the music specialist. A study of the Hungarian system of music education forms the basis of analyzing the structure of the materials for American schools.

title: Introduction to Contemporary Music Techniques in the Elementary School
description: Exploring the use of nonconventional, nontraditional, experimental musical sound sources and procedures in music education. Students participate in classroom projects using creative and contemporary symbolization, instrumentation, and vocal setting, including an introduction to electronic music.

title: Stage Band Techniques
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the techniques and style characteristics of popular and jazz band performance. Includes preparation in the administration of school jazz ensembles.

title: Guitar for Social Use
description: Designed for development of basic skill in playing the guitar for accompanying. Focuses on chordal styles and their application to music such as folk songs and popular songs. Open to all students.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 1
description: Provides a fundamental working knowledge of skills required in maintaining stringed instruments at the elementary and secondary school levels. Study and application of school repair problems in regard to the violin, viola, cello, and doublebass. General techniques in making adjustments, gluing, and using tools properly. Analyses of the various woods used in instruments and bows.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 2
description: Advanced study and experience in more specialized repairs on stringed instruments. Discussions and laboratory work including splicing, grafting, varnishing, carving and bow rehairing. Historical resume of stringed instruments and makers from the seventeenth to the twentieth century.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis on those specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Tests, Measurements, and Guidance in Music
description: Acquaints the teacher with tests of sensory capacities, appreciation, and achievement. Briefly reviews such statistical and other data as make for an enlightened evaluation of the various tests and of their results.

title: Psychology of Music
description: Presentation of materials as an aid to the understanding of the nature and extent of individual differences in musical talent. Specific preparation in the psychology of audition, motor control, and in the analysis of the musical mind leading to a natural application in the psychology of musical training.

title: Music in Therapy and Special Education
description: The theoretical aspects of music therapy and their appropriate application to special education in the public schools. Emphasizes the power of music to elicit normal interaction with peers from the child with a learning difficulty.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: Provides the superior student with an opportunity for intensive study and research in a particular aspect of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Introduction to Music
description: Introduction to the art of listening to music. Some elementary instruction in musical materials will be related to the listening aspects of the course, although the course is designed primarily to introduce students to the sound of music through the ages. No previous knowledge of music required. Open to students with areas in music by permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music History 1
description: The growth of music from its beginnings through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The origins of music, the development of notation, and the growth of early polyphonic forms. Open only to students with areas in music except by permission of the department head.

title: Music History 2
description: Changes in music from the late sixteenth century through the Baroque, the Rococo, and the Classical periods. The transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque, and the developments of opera, sonata, symphony, and the related forms. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, or permission of the department head.

title: Music History 3
description: Developments in music from the time of Beethoven to the present. Transition from the classical to romantic periods, the various reactions to Romanticism, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 231, or permission of the department head.

title: Instrumental Music from the Time of Bach
description: The growth and development of musical forms and styles as they apply to music for orchestra and solo instruments from the late Baroque period to our time. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 232.

title: Choral and Vocal Solo Literature from Haydn to the Present
description: The development of the cantata, oratorio, mass, motet, anthem, and the lied; great masterworks in these forms. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 232.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Following a brief survey of the early development of opera, there will be a more detailed consideration of examples of this genre from the middle of the eighteenth century to the present time. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 232.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including the function of figured bass, significant contrapuntal developments, the evolution of opera, oratorio, and cantata, and the growth of various instrumental genres such as the concerto grosso, sonata, suite, and types of keyboard music. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles which marked the transition from Baroque to Classic music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the nineteenth century and its relationship to the Romantic movement, the growth of chromatic harmony, the changes in traditional types such as the symphony and opera, the growth of the art song, the tone poem, and the character piece. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: History and Development of Jazz
description: A survey of the evolutionary process in jazz music in the United States. Includes discussion of the styles and characteristics of each period of jazz history and the contributions of selected groups and individuals. Prerequisite: MUHIS 231 or permission of the department head.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Restricted to students on the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 1
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on Baroque instruments, and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Rameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study, or permission of the department head.

title: Field Sources of American Musical Culture
description: Field study in major musical capitals, including the best known festival centers. Seminars scheduled in connection with planned travel are concerned with the orientation of members to the historic significance of composers native to the region, to the influence of nationalistic schools, and to the interaction of architectural and other physical matters with the musical output. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students on all curricula. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: Provides superior students with an opportunity for guided reading and intensive study in an area of music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but not more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Hymnody in Worship
description: Hymns in early Jewish and Western Christian tradition: their historical and liturgical context and contemporary use. A summary of Western religious thought as exposed in liturgical poetry. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students with deficiencies in elementary musical knowledge. Provides, at the simplest levels, a language for communication and a background of rudimentary information, historical and systematic. Designed primarily for students intending to pursue courses in music education, history, theory, and performance. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. Open to all students except those with credit in MUSTH 111 or above; MUHIS 211 or above. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. 111, 112, 113. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) Review of terminology and fundamentals precedes an extensive study of the tonal, rhythmic, motivic, and formal structure of melody through composition and analysis. The basic elements of music are studied through the analysis and writing of music in two, three, and four parts. Elementary work in transposition, scoring, and harmonic alterations. Music reading, aural discernment, and rhythmic training provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. These courses must be taken in course number sequence. 211, 212, 213. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) More complex elements of nineteenth and twentieth century music studied through composition and analysis. Advanced work in music reading and aural discernment provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. Prerequisite:

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: The components of the recording chain are introduced both theoretically and practically. A complete and thorough review of the recording process, the mixing process, and editing formats is presented. Prerequisite: PHYCS 246 or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An introduction to multichannel recording techniques, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing is presented. Requires laboratory time for recording practice and a final recording project. Prerequisite: MUSTH 225.

title: Music Calligraphy
description: Practical experience in calligraphic skills and layout procedures pertinent to the preparation of music scores and parts. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113.

title: Compositional Practices: The Baroque
description: The theoretical principles, stylistic forces, and aesthetics that characterize the compositional practices of the Baroque period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Compositional Practices: Eighteenth -Century Classicism
description: The theoretical principles, stylistic forces, and aesthetics that characterize the compositional practices of eighteenthcentury classicism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213. 321, 322, 323 (371, 372, 373). Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing short instrumental and vocal compositions with emphasis on developing the student's technical capacity to achieve freedom of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic Music
description: A workshop in current practices of producing music by electronic means. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band and wind ensemble. Particula r atention is given to voicing, sectional and crosdoubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 422.

title: Arranging for the Dance Band
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques as employed by current leading dance bands and jazz arrangers, and the practice of writing and performing scores by members of the class. Prerequisite: MUSTH 422.

title: Theory of Medieval and Renaissance Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of Medieval and Renaissance music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Nineteenth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Twentieth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Music Theory in the Secondary School
description: An investigation of pedagogical precepts and problems relating to music theory in the secondary school. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Analysis will be applied to a broad representation of musical masterworks from various periods with examination of the macroand microstructure and construction of selected works. Special attention is given to musical practices before and after the period of tertian harmony. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Orchestration
description: Scoring for large and small orchestral ensembles. Particular attention given to voice positioning, doubling, and textural deployment as regards harmonic weight and color. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Electronic Music Studio 1
description: An introductory course in electronic music. The physical and perceptual dimensions of sound are presented as a basis for sound synthesis. An introduction to musique concrete operations and voltage controlled systems provides the basis for class projects. Studio laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Electronic Music Studio 2
description: An advanced course in electronic music synthesis. An introduction to large voltage controlled systems, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing. Projects in composition, educational applications of electronic music, and research. Laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 425. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Computer Applications in Music
description: Presents an overview of computer systems and languages appropriate for (1) musical analysis; (2) musical composition; and (3) sound synthesis. Presents an historical prespective, computer applications in the areas stated, and introduces simple programming procedures. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Composition-Project Recital
description: Public performance of the student's compositions and/or public presentation of the student's music theory research. Prerequisite: MUSTH 422. 431, 432 (472), 433 (473). Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing more complex and extended instrumental and vocal compositions with continued emphasis on the development of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 323.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. The synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound are studied as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Independent study in any area of music theory via readings, analysis, and/or research. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 and permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term. Department of Applied Studies in Music Marsh, Head; Albright, Anderson, E. Bourgeot, M. Bourgeot, Boye, Boyer, Campbell, Ewart, Greenhoe, Hanson, Hargreaves, Hill, Knight, Kohler, Koriath, Kuhn, Leedham, Legbandt, Manford, McConnell, McWilliams, Meadows, Milford, Minor, Mueller, Pressler, Prokop, Reilly, Rutledge, Saunders, Scheuer, Sebastiani, Slaughter, Strobel, Varner For many years a hallmark of the School of Music has been its outstanding record in musical performance. The departmental major is designed to meet the needs of the increasing number of students each year who enter Ball State with aspirations to careers in professional performance. Students preparing for licensing as teachers of music share fully in the environment of artist teachers and outstanding musical organizations.

description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, the Marching Show Band, the Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble 1, and the Concert Orchestra all of which normally rehearse 5 hours per week.

description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles. Included in this category are the Concert Band, Varsity Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensembles 2 and 3, and Training Orchestra all of which normally rehearse 2 hours per week.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the upper division ensembles. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera Chorus, and the University Singers all of which normally rehearse 5 hours per week.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 372.

title: Planning and Producing the Musical Show
description: Designed to familiarize the student with standard operating procedures within the field of musical theatre. Provides a well structured approach to musical theatre production techniques.

description: The application of stage convention and acting method for the vocal musician.

title: Music Theatre in America: A Survey of the Repertoire
description: An overview of the genre of musical theatre in America: its history and contemporary trends, together with the study of individual works and the preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

A student indicating an intent to major in nursing begins study in the areas of English, social sciences, physical and biological sciences, and the fine arts. Approximately two years of academic work in humanities and behavorial and biological sciences are required. The major in nursing has been concentrated in the student's junior and senior years. Cooperative programs in nursing have been arranged between Ball State University and Anderson College, Bethel College, Grace College, Huntington College, Manchester College, St. Francis College, Taylor University and Tri-State College. A student interested in the cooperative program may enroll at one of these institutions for the freshman and sophomore years and transfer these credits to Ball State University. The curriculum for the professional nursing student is classified under the Professional Arts Curriculum and consists of three options. The Bachelor of Science Degree is earned and may be completed with the minimum requirements of the curriculum (186 hours); free and directed elective hours range from 61-79 quarter hours. The student will meet the general requirements of the University in the professional nursing major and required minor for graduation (minimum of 2.0 scholastic ratio if major, required minor, and overall grade point average); in addition, the student will present a minimum grade of in each clinical nursing course and in Options 2 and 3, grades in CHEM 106; ANAT 201; PHYSL 210; and BIO 213. Application for admission to the clinical nursing sequence occurs during the quarter that the student will have completed 93 quarter hours. All options require a minimal 2.0 cumulative grade point average in the required minor and a minimal cumulative grade point average of 2.0 for admission to clinical nursing. Option I, with the minor in biological sciences, requires seven courses to be completed (CHEM 105, 106; BIO 111, 112, 213; ANAT 201 and PHYSL 210) to proceed into the clinical nursing sequence. Option II, requiring the minor in psychology, specifies twelve (12) quarter hours to be completed (GXPSY 213, 241 and a directed elective) to proceed into the clinical nursing sequence. Option III, requiring either a minor in sociology or a minor in cultural anthropology, requires twelve (12) quarter hours to be completed (SOC 100, 242; ANTH 160) to proceed into the clinical nursing sequence. Clinical nursing course repetition will be permitted one time, for only one course. Eighty students are admitted to the clinical nursing sequence twice a year, Autumn and Spring quarters. Students are selected on the basis of G. P.A. earned the first two years. Additional information about the selection process is available in the Department of Nursing. The possibility of postponement or not being selected should be considered by the student. The philosophy and objectives of Ball State University are supported by the Department of Nursing which focuses on the total development of the student in nursing. The faculty of the Department of Nursing accepts the responsibility for preparing a professional nurse who possesses the ability to creatively utilize the knowledge gained through a synthesis of the strands of a broad cultural experience in the professional content of nursing. The nurse will function in the holistic care of the client and recognize the everchanging needs and expectations of society through the utilization of the nursing process. Inherent in the nursing process is the development of a system of care which will be both a companion to and a parallel with the broad system of health care. The result of such a system will be the nurse who is able to give quality care by contributing constructively to provide health services to the client — the individual, the family, and the community — in the societies of the world of today and tomorrow. The faculty believe that in present and future society the professional nurse has a commitment to initiate change and bring about resolutions of issues for better client care. Through these endeavors the nurse achieves greater satisfaction and accepts a role in the ever expanding responsibilities of nursing. In making progressively effective contributions and adjustments in a changing society, the basic needs of man — dignity, selffulfillment and right to optimal health — will be fulfilled. The accomplishment of these beliefs is through the acquisition of a solid knowledge base and a continuation of that base in nursing which is validated by research in nursing practice and client care. We further believe that the professional nurse should be prepared to recognize the need to fulfill a moral commitment toward the well being of the world population. Through understanding of the different values and customs of people everywhere the nurse learns to cope with health problems peculiar to clients from a variety of national and social origins. Through this conviction comes the responsibility of the nurse to assure quality service for mankind. The Department of Nursing accepts the responsibility to provide and foster learning activities and experiences which will enable the student to: 1. acquire knowledge, skills and attitudes which will provide the foundation for the administration of holistic care to the client and family; Nursing 169 2. develop a concept of nursing which encompasses a respect for the dignity of man and rights to selfdecision and selffulfillment; 3. develop and utilize a concept of nursing which includes the prevention of illness, its detection and treatment, and the promotion of health for the individual, the family and the community; 4. develop an understanding of self for effective human relations and communications with clients, families, and colleagues; 5. acquire an understanding and recognition of the nurse's responsibility for leadership roles as well as being a contributing member of the health team; 6. develop ability for creativity, critical thinking, value judgments, and selfdirection which will enable the student to become a contributing member in the nursing profession and society; and 7. develop an understanding of the need for continuous professional and personal growth which includes participation and leadership in the social, cultural, and educational world.
