title: Man and Physical Activity
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge about the motor movement field.

title: Individualized Exercise and Figure Control
description: An exercise course including individual analysis of fitness problems, development and maintenance of a fitness level. Prerequisite: PEG 106. t This course to be taken first.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to help students develop a personalized program for developing and maintaining muscular strength and the physique.

title: Jogging
description: Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through jogging.

title: Adapted Physical Education
description: Assignment will be made after the University Health Service recommends to the Physical Education Department that the student be placed in adapted physical education. A total of 4 hours credit may be earned.

title: Beginning/Intermediate Judo
description: Designed to give the student an appreciation of judo, both as a sport and as an art. Emphasis placed on understanding basic judo techniques, the development of selfconfidence, and selfdefense throughout the course.

title: Beginning Karate
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of karate.

title: Beginning Modern Jazz Dance
description: Understanding and skill in basic techniques and styles (cool, hot, blues, urban, primitive) of the jazz dance.

title: Swimnastics
description: Physical conditioning through water exercise, using high potential fitness activities which can be used in a small pool or in a limited area of a crowded instructional pool. Prerequisite: ability to put face in water, float on front and/or back in shallow water, and ability to regain standing position after floating.

title: Beginning Tap Dance
description: Designed to teach the basic tap steps and combinations along with their rhythmic analysis and style to be used in composition. Designed for the student with no experience in tap dancing.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through yoga exercises and yoga relaxation techniques.

title: Paddle Sports
description: Basic skills, rules, and strategies involved in playing racket ball, paddle tennis, and other paddle sports.

title: Badminton
description: Introductory skills for the playing of singles and doubles badminton. Basic strategy, rules and courtesy will be stressed. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 122 or PGW 124.

title: Beginning Bowling
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of bowling. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 123 or PGW 123.

title: Beginning Horsemanship
description: Schooling in three gaits: walk, trot, and canter.

title: Bicycling
description: Bicycling techniques involving maintenance of equipment; city, open country, and endurance riding primarily to introduce the student to family bicycling for lifetime use. A total of 3 hours credit may be earned.

title: Field Handball
description: An international team field sport similar to soccer.

title: Flag Football
description: Introducton to fundamentals and rules of football through flag football; instruction in techniques, terminology, strategies, and rules.

title: Beginning Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: For students desiring information, practice, and experience in basic skills, strategies, and knowledge. Course includes passing, shooting, dribbling, offense, defense.

title: Beginning Fencing
description: Basic techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and courtesies. Includes positions, footwork, parries, and lunges.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control.

title: Volleyball/Coed Rules
description: Provides beginner with an understanding of rules and skills underlying optimal enjoyment for power volleyball.

title: Pocket Billiards
description: Assists the student in the rudimentary skills and knowledges of the sport.

title: Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginner the mechanics of snow skiing, equipment choice, and care of equipment, plus offering a laboratory experience of several days of skiing on available slopes. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Orienteering
description: Designed to introduce the student to the activity of orienteering, a sport in which the participant utilizes the skills of land navigation using maps and compass reading skills. Circulorespiratory fitness is emphasized in distance running for time.

title: Gymnastics
description: Elementary movement performance on flat mats and apparatus

title: Beginning Gymnastics (Women's Apparatus)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, uneven parallel bars, ropes, and rings. Prerequisite: PEG 107 or equivalent.

title: Rhythmic Gymnastics
description: Combines gymnastics, dance, and implement manipulation with basic movement skills aimed at body control and grace in developing individual and group routines. Implements include hoops, wands, Indian clubs, ropes, scarves, and balls.

title: Weight Training (Women's Activities)
description: Designed to help students develop a basic personalized program for developing and maintaining strength for both overall conditioning and for activities in which women participate.

title: Casting and Angling
description: An introduction to the basic principles of casting and angling along with the practical application of how to catch fish.

title: Sports Acrobatics
description: A course designed to provide men and women with instruction in the rules and techniques of sports acrobatics.

title: Track and Field
description: A beginning course in track and field which includes skills, rules, and knowledge of conditioning and training associated with individual activities.

title: Swimming 1
description: Students who can swim 75 feet are eligible. Students must sign up at the Aquatics Office in the University Pool.

title: Swimming 2
description: Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 202 or PGW 202.

title: Aquatic Lifeguarding
description: Develops knowledge and ability for the protection of individuals participating in aquatic activities. Certification for Senior Red Cross Life Saving is covered. Prerequisite: PEG 202, or permission of the department head.

title: Aquatic Art Techniques
description: Introduces the student to the stroke modifications, standard figures and sculling techniques, and floating patterns of aquatic art. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head.

title: Springboard Diving
description: Safe performance of aerial dives from aquatic springboards. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 205 or PGW 205.

title: Scuba
description: Selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus techniques and the laws pertaining to the activity. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 206, or PGW 206.

title: Aquatic Sports and Games
description: Low organizational games, contests, and more advanced aquatic sports, with special emphasis on application for aquatic programs in schools and other organizations. Prerequisite: PEG 202, or current lifesaving certificate from nationally recognized certifying organization.

title: Basic Canoeing
description: Includes an introduction to the basic canoeing theory, skills, and safety rules necessary for the efficient and safe handling of a canoe. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or equivalent or permission of the department head.

title: Intermediate Judo
description: Prerequisite: PEG 210 or permission of the department head.

title: Intermediate Folk Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 112.

title: Intermediate Square Dance
description: Prerequisite: PGC 113.

title: Advanced Judo
description: Emphasis placed on understanding and practicing intermediate judo techniques, international contest rules and skills, and teaching methods that will enable one to teach beginning judo. Prerequisite: PEG 211.

title: Intermediate Modern Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 115 or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Modern Dance
description: For students already skilled in dance who wish to increase their performing and technical aptitude in dance either for a vocational or vocational reasons. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Handball
description: Introductory skills for playing handball. Basic skills, strategy, rules, and courtesy measures stressed. Designed for the student with little prior experience.

title: Racquetball
description: Instruction in the basic skills, strategies, and knowledges required to play racquetball.

title: Intermediate Badminton
description: Presents skills in badminton beyond the beginning level and is designed to provide opportunities to learn advanced technique and strategy. Prerequisite: PEG 124 or PEP 173 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 122.

title: Intermediate Bowling
description: Designed to give the student knowledge and experience in bowling on a team, in a league, keeping league records, team standings, and computing and figuring handicaps as well as review of basic fundamentals.

title: Bicycle Touring
description: Designed to develop touring physical fitness and camping skills associated with the touring aspects of bicycling. Prerequisite: PEG 130 or equivalent. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate Golf
description: Designed to offer the golfing student an opportunity to learn and practice the finer points of the game.

title: Intermediate Horsemanship
description: Work toward perfecting form in the three gaits: walk, trot, and canter. Harness driving. Stable management.

title: Intermediate Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: An intermediate course in basketball designed to include a review of fundamental skills, further development of these skills, and the introduction of advanced skills and strategies. Prerequisite: PEG 137 or PEP 182 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Power Volleyball (Women's Rules)
description: Instruction in intermediate techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and competition. Includes individual and team offensive and defensive techniques, offensive and team game strategies, and competition. Prerequisite: PEG 131 or PEP 183 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach intermediate skiers the skills necessary to become advanced level skiers plus affords them the opportunity to ski on longer, higher, open, and trail type slopes provided by ski areas in the west (Rocky Mountains) or the east (White Mountains). Prerequisite: PEG 142 or permission of the department head. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intercollegiate Athletics
description: Actual participation in the organized practice sessions and competitions during the regular season for the varsity sport as directed by the coach for that sport. A total of 2 hours credit may be earned.

title: Sport Scuba Diving
description: Provides opportunities for refining techniques and skills necessary for using selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus. Prerequisite: PEG 206.

title: White Water Canoeing
description: Designed to develop skills and knowledge (beyond the beginner level) to a level which will permit safe white water canoeing, portaging, and may include camping. Field trips will involve overnight camping. Prerequisite: PEG 209 or permission of the department head.

title: General Safety Education
description: Designed to prepare prospective teachers for the comprehensive general safety education program.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control. Designed to aid the student to develop a fitness philosophy, to structure physical fitness programs, and to recognize individual physiological limitations.

title: Gymnastics (Balance Beam and Floor Exercise)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastics (Trampoline, Vaulting, Uneven Bars)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, flying rings, and uneven parallel bars. Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Foundations of Physical Education
description: An introductory course for professional physical education students that covers the psychomotor, cognitive, and affective scope of physical education and its relationship to education. An attempt is made to assist students in assessing those qualities of motor and physical fitness expected of physical education majors as they commence their vocational study.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 1
description: Content, methods, materials, organization, and administration of the classroom and laboratory phase of the secondary school program.

title: Principles and Problems of Coaching Sports for Girls and Women
description: Introduces students to the following: the principles and problems of coaching girls' team and individual sports at the junior and senior high school level; the philosophies and principles which underlie the development of such a program.

title: Coaching Observation (Girls'/Women's Athletics)
description: Guided observation of coaching techniques and practices with analyzation of teaching/coaching philosophies for competitive sports in schools. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Practicum in Aquatics
description: Gives the student supervised experience in aquatic programs. The student will work specificially in aquatic programs in existence at Ball State or other established organizations. Prerequisite: PEG 202 and 203. A total of 2 hours credit may be earned.

title: Officiating Competitive Aquatic Sports
description: Gives students an understanding of desired officiating practices, a comprehension of particular aquatic performance techniques related to decision making by officials, and laboratory experience in officiating. The student is presented the opportunity for certification in various aquatic officiating areas.

title: Tumbling and Apparatus (Women's Events)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 158 and 159 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastic Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has two hours of credit in PEP 256 or 258.

title: Dance Theatre
description: Provides the dance student with experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance performances. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Folk Dance
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 112.

title: The Teaching of Folk Dance
description: Materials and techniques of teaching folk dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEP 262 or equivalent.

title: Folk Dance Theatre
description: Provides opportunities and experiences in participating with a company of dancers who plan and perform in both informal and formal folk dance presentations. Prerequisite: PEG 112 and permission of the department head. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Square Dance Methods
description: The development of teaching skills for beginning and intermediate classes in square dancing. The development of techniques of calling square dance (patter and singing). Prerequisite: PEP 263.

title: Dance Composition 1
description: Principal elements of dance composition. Simple compositional forms for small groups and solo work. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Badminton
description: Prerequisite: PEP 173 or permission of the department head.

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 177 or permission of the department head.

title: Baseball/Softball Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 179.

title: Track and Field Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 180.

title: Anatomy
description: Basic concepts in anatomy for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching.

title: Physiology
description: Basic concepts in physiology for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching. Prerequisite: PEP 292, or permission of the department head.

title: Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze activity for the purpose of improving physical skills. Prerequisite: PEP 292.

title: First Aid
description: First aid as outlined by the American Red Cross leading to standard certification. Designed for the student pursuing a major or minor program in the School of Physical Education and Athletics. Not open to the student who has credit in HSC 250.

title: First Aid Instructor
description: Instructor's course in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, and including the instructor's course in Multimedia First Aid as established by the American Red Cross. Designed for the professional student pursuing a major or minor in physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 299 or HSC 250, or valid certification in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, Standard First Aid and Multimedia, or Advanced First Aid and Emergency Care.

title: Simulation in Driver and Traffic Safety Education
description: Designed to meet the needs of prospective teachers in the simulation phase of driver and traffic safety education. Prerequisite: PEP 124.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Gymnastics, Volleyball, and Track and Field
description: Coaching techniques involved in gymnastics, volleyball, and track and field. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Volleyball, Basketball, and Softball
description: Coaching techniques involved in volleyball, basketball, and softball. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Swimming, Golf, Gymnastics, and Tennis
description: Coaching techniques involved in swimming, golf, gymnastics, and tennis. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Organization and Management of Women's Athletics
description: Understanding and appreciation of: the responsibilities and desirable characteristics of competent officials; organizing and managing competitive events and tournaments; relationships among coach, officials, players, and spectators; local, state, and national organizations involved in officiating and management.

title: Aquatic Art Production
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of management and staging activities involved in an aquatic art production at the high school and college levels.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head.

title: Red Cross Water Safety Instructor
description: Prerequisite: current Red Cross senior lifesaving certificate.

title: Instructional Techniques and Analysis of Aquatic Performance
description: Selected learning theory, teaching strategies, and physical laws which affect learning and performance in the aquatic medium. Analysis of basic safety skills and stroke and diving techniques, and approaches to planning and evaluating aquatic performance by age and skill levels.

title: Field and/or Laboratory Experience
description: Provides the student with administrative aquatic experience outside the present offerings. These experiences will place the student in a leadership role. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 259.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 261.

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the lower level of the elementary school.

title: History of Dance
description: Basic dance forms and functions from the primitive era into the 20th century.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and the use of accompaniment in dance. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or the equivalent.

title: Dance Production
description: Various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or the equivalent.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Techniques)
description: Fundamental modern dance techniques, elements of rhythmic patterns, materials of space, design, and improvisation.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Composition)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on composition. Prerequisite: PEP 365.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Methodology)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on teaching modern dance in the public schools, camps, and others. Dance composition. Prerequisite: PEP 366.

title: Aquatics for the Elementary School Child
description: Assist the student to acquire an understanding of safety factors, developmental stroke and diving sequences, and teaching strategies for aquatic instruction of the young child. Prerequisite: PEP 353 or equivalent certification.

title: Diagnostic Techniques and Athletic Injury Mechanisms
description: An introduction to predisposing anatomical, kinesiological, growth stress, and other such factors that contribute to athletic injuries. Procedures for accurate recognition and evaluation of not only these factors, but also the extent of an athletic injury are presented. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Administration and Organization of Programs for the Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Problems, principles, and objectives in the designing, planning, and operation of a program for the prevention and care of athletic injuries. There will also be an examination of the code of ethics of the National Athletic Trainer's Association. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Athletic Training Modalities and Therapeutic Techniques
description: An introduction to mechanical therapies, thermal therapy, cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, and therapeutic exercise. Only those modalities and their clinical uses that have special implications for the athletic trainer in the treatment or injuries to the athlete will be considered. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Methods of Teaching Team Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following team sports: basketball, field hockey, flag football, soccer, softball, speedball, team handball, volleyball. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in team sports included.

title: Methods of Teaching Individual Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following individual sports: archery, badminton, bowling, golf, tennis, track. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in individual sports included.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 276.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball and Softball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 279.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 280.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 281.

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 282.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 283.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 284.

title: Gymnastic Judging (Women's Events)
description: The development of gymnastics judging techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and or NAGWS (Class) official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 157, 158, 159.

title: Track and Field Officiating
description: The development of track and field officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 180.

title: Softball Umpiring
description: The development of softball umpiring techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA, ASA, and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Volleyball Officiating
description: The development of volleyball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 183.

title: Basketball Officiating
description: The development of basketball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 182.

title: Principles of Physical Education
description: General concepts based upon the scientific facts and philosophic judgments which underlie physical education.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, utilizing task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include the factors of purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the student to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate an array of teaching strategies that would be utilized in creating a freesafe environment for a public school physical education Program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Principles; practice of athletic training principles and techniques necessary for care and prevention of athletic injuries.

title: Remedial Exercises and Rehabilitation
description: An introduction to the objectives and principles involved in designing and planning conditioning programs for the athlete. Therapeutic exercises essential in planning the rehabilitation program of the injured athlete are introduced and developed. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed as a practicum that involves comprehensive planning of instruction, designing teaching implementation strategies, classroom management techniques, and evaluation of teaching behaviors and materials • in physical education. Opportunities for students to work with children in a classroom setting. Prerequisite: PEP 395 and junior level status.

title: Practicum in Recreation
description: Supervised, practical, professional leadership experience designed for the recreation oriented person. Experiences include: work activities in federal, state, county, or community parks or with private camps. Close supervision supplied by the University and the participating agency. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 2
description: Presentation of materials and information designed to prepare for teaching driver education in the secondary schools.

title: Coaching Internship (Girl's/Women's Athletics)
description: Assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teaching/coaching process. (May not be taken during student teaching). Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Problems in Aquatic Programs Development
description: Programs and problems of the physical educator working in aquatics.

title: Dance for the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Advanced Studio in Contemporary Dance
description: Advanced technique in contemporary dance. Designed for the student who is interested in advancing his/her skills in contemporary dance technique beyond those developed in the regular college classes. Choreographic forms, performance, and production, using such allied fields as costuming, lighting, and accompaniment. Prerequisite: some previous study of modern dance or ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Swimming for the Handicapped
description: Adaptations of strokes for people with various limitations, swimming as a rehabilitation program, facilities and pool design adaptations. Prerequisite: Current Water Safety Instructor's Certificate.

title: Sports Development
description: Organizational patterns in program development and exploration of current problems in girls' and women's sports.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching of a Modern Day Athletic Program
description: Designed to explore the historical development of modern athletics, to develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program, and learn to deal with everyday coaching and administration problems. Not open to the student who has credit in PPM 290 and 492.

title: Scientific Foundation for Athletic Performance
description: Scientific knowledge available to be used perfecting performance in athletics.

title: Program Development for Intramural and Recreational Activities
description: Initiation, organization, and administration of intramural and recreational programs in the secondary school.

title: Physical Education for the Mentally Retarded
description: Establishes a physical education curriculum for the mentally retarded child. Includes understanding the child's experience in physical education, teaching methods, and a teaching experience.

title: Recreation
description: Presentation of the various concepts of recreation. Arts and crafts, camping, dramatics, music, and the problems of increased leisure time are discussed. Emphasis is placed upon enabling the physical education student to conduct recreational programs.

title: Skill Analysis, Theory and Practice of Play
description: Scientific principles involved in movement as they apply to specific skills in elementary school physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Fundamental play needs of children; research into the play interests of children; and evaluation of space, equipment, and supervision. Results sought are appreciation of the educational values of play, necessity of adequate provisions for it, ability to select appropriate equipment, and formation of a tentative curriculum of play forms.

title: Physical Education Theory and Practice for Upper Elementary and Middle School Children

Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the human organism. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294, or by permission of the department head.

title: Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitations of each. Physical education and recreational activities for each type.

description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage and other athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

description: Students are assigned to on -the -job experience as student athletic trainers in conjunction with their student teaching assignments in an Indiana high school that is qualified to provide students with both experiences. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

description: Methods of measuring and evaluating physical education results in terms of directing philosophy. Tests and uses of test results.

title: Laboratory and Field Experience in Athletic Training 2
description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage, and other therapeutic techniques used by the athletic trainer in the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Man and Physical Activity
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge about the motor movement field. 101 (PGW or PGM 101). Water Adjustment for Swimming. (1)

title: Individualized Exercise and Figure Control
description: An exercise course including individual analysis of fitness problems, development and maintenance of a fitness level. Prerequisite: PEG 106.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to help students develop a personalized program for developing and maintaining muscular strength and the physique.

title: Jogging
description: Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through jogging. 105 (PGM or PGW 105). Adapted Physical Education. (1) Assignment will be made after the University Health Service recommends to the Physical Education Department that the student be placed in adapted physical education. A total of 4 hours credit may be earned.

title: Beginning/Intermediate Judo
description: Designed to give the student an appreciation of judo, both as a sport and as an art. Emphasis placed on understanding basic judo techniques, the development of selfconfidence, and selfdefense throughout the course.

title: Beginning Karate
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of karate.

title: Beginning Modern Jazz Dance
description: Understanding and skill in basic techniques and styles (cool, hot, blues, urban, primitive) of the jazz dance.

title: Swimnastics
description: Physical conditioning through water exercise, using high potential fitness activities which can be used in a small pool or in a limited area of a crowded instructional pool. Prerequisite: ability to put face in water, float on front and/or back in shallow water, and ability to regain standing position after floating.

title: Beginning Tap Dance
description: Designed to teach the basic tap steps and combinations along with their rhythmic analysis and style to be used in composition. Designed for the student with no experience in tap dancing.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through yoga exercises and yoga relaxation techniques.

title: Paddle Sports
description: Basic skills, rules, and strategies involved in playing racket ball, paddle tennis, and other paddle sports.

title: Badminton
description: Introductory skills for the playing of singles and doubles badminton. Basic strategy, rules, and courtesy will be stressed. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 122 or PGW 124. * PEP 233 is not required for physical education majors.

title: Beginning Bowling
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of bowling. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 123 or PGW 123.

title: Beginning Horsemanship
description: Schooling in three gaits: walk, trot, and canter.

title: Bicycling
description: Bicycling techniques involving maintenance of equipment; city, open country, and endurance riding primarily to introduce the student to family bicycling for lifetime use. A total of 3 hours credit may be earned.

title: Field Handball
description: An international team field sport similar to soccer.

title: Flag Football
description: Introduction to fundamentals and rules of football through flag football; instruction in techniques, terminology, strategies, and rules.

title: Beginning Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: For students desiring information, practice, and experience in basic skills, strategies, and knowledge. Course includes passing, shooting, dribbling, offense, defense.

title: Beginning Fencing
description: Basic techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and courtesies. Includes positions, footwork, parries, and lunges.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control.

title: Volleyball/Coed Rules
description: Provides beginner with an understanding of rules and skills underlying optimal enjoyment for power volleyball.

title: Pocket Billiards
description: Assists the student in the rudimentary skills and knowledges of the sport.

title: Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginner the mechanics of snow skiing, equipment choice, and care of equipment, plus offering a laboratory experience of several days of skiing on available slopes. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Orienteering
description: Designed to introduce the student to the activity of orienteering, a sport in which the participant utilizes the skills of land navigation using maps and compass reading skills. Circulorespiratory fitness is emphasized in distance running for time.

title: Gymnastics
description: Elementary movement performance on flat mats and apparatus

title: Beginning Gymnastics (Women's Apparatus)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, uneven parallel bars, ropes, and rings. Prerequisite: PEG 107 or equivalent.

title: Rhythmic Gymnastics
description: Combines gymnastics, dance, and implement manipulation with basic movement skills aimed at body control and grace in developing individual and group routines. Implements include hoops, wands, Indian clubs, ropes, scarves, and balls.

title: Weight Training (Women's Activities)
description: Designed to help students develop a basic personalized program for developing and maintaining strength for both overall conditioning and for activities in which women participate.

title: Casting and Angling
description: An introduction to the basic principles of casting and angling along with the practical application of how to catch fish.

title: Sports Acrobatics
description: A course designed to provide men and women with instruction in the rules and techniques of sports acrobatics.

title: Track and Field
description: A beginning course in track and field which includes skills, rules, and knowledge of conditioning and training associated with individual activities. 201 (PGM or PGW 201). Swimming 1. title: Swimming 2
description: Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 202 or PGW 202.

title: Aquatic Lifeguarding
description: Develops knowledge and ability for the protection of individuals participating in aquatic activities. Certification for Senior Red Cross Life Saving is covered. Prerequisite: PEG 202, or permission of the department head.

title: Aquatic Art Techniques
description: Introduces the student to the stroke modifications, standard figures and sculling techniques, and floating patterns of aquatic art. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head.

title: Springboard Diving
description: Safe performance of aerial dives from aquatic springboards. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 205 or PGW 205.

title: Scuba
description: Selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus techniques and the laws pertaining to the activity. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PGM 206, or PGW 206.

title: Aquatic Sports and Games
description: Low organizational games, contests, and more advanced aquatic sports, with special emphasis on application for aquatic programs in schools and other organizations. Prerequisite: PEG 202, or current lifesaving certificate from nationally recognized certifying organization.

title: Basic Canoeing
description: Includes an introduction to the basic canoeing theory, skills, and safety rules necessary for the efficient and safe handling of a canoe. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or equivalent or permission of the department head.

title: Intermediate Judo
description: Prerequisite: PEG 210 or permission of the department head.

title: Intermediate Folk Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 112.

title: Intermediate Square Dance
description: Prerequisite: PGC 113.

title: Advanced Judo
description: Emphasis placed on understanding and practicing intermediate judo techniques, international contest rules and skills, and teaching methods that will enable one to teach beginning judo. Prerequisite: PEG 211.

title: Intermediate Modern Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 115 or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Modern Dance
description: For students already skilled in dance who wish to increase their performing and technical aptitude in dance either for avocational or vocational reasons. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Handball
description: Introductory skills for playing handball. Basic skills, strategy, rules, and courtesy measures stressed. Designed for the student with little prior experience.

title: Racquetball
description: Instruction in the basic skills, strategies, and knowledges required to play racquetball.

title: Intermediate Badminton
description: Presents skills in badminton beyond the beginning level and is designed to provide opportunities to learn advanced technique and strategy. Prerequisite: PEG 124 or PEP 173 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 122.

title: Intermediate Bowling
description: Designed to give the student knowledge and experience in bowling on a team, in a league, keeping league records, team standings, and computing and figuring handicaps as well as review of basic fundamentals.

title: Bicycle Touring
description: Designed to develop touring physical fitness and camping skills associated with the touring aspects of bicycling. Prerequisite: PEG 130 or equivalent. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate Golf
description: Designed to offer the golfing student an opportunity to learn and practice the finer points of the game.

title: Intermediate Horsemanship
description: Work toward perfecting form in the three gaits: walk, trot, and canter. Harness driving. Stable management.

title: Intermediate Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: An intermediate course in basketball designed to include a review of fundamental skills, further development of these skills, and the introduction of advanced skills and strategies. Prerequisite: PEG 137 or PEP 182 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Power Volleyball (Women's Rules)
description: Instruction in intermediate techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and competition. Includes individual and team offensive and defensive techniques, offensive and team game strategies, and competition. Prerequisite: PEG 131 or PEP 183 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach intermediate skiers the skills necessary to become advanced level skiers plus affords them the opportunity to ski on longer, higher, open, and trail type slopes provided by ski areas in the west (Rocky Mountains) or the east (White Mountains). Prerequisite: PEG 142 or permission of the department head. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intercollegiate Athletics
description: Actual participation in the organized practice sessions and competitions during the regular season for the varsity sport as directed by the coach for that sport. A total of 2 hours credit may be earned.

title: Sport Scuba Diving
description: Provides opportunities for refining techniques and skills necessary for using selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus. Prerequisite: PEG 206.

title: White Water Canoeing
description: Designed to develop skills and knowledge (beyond the beginner level) to a level which will permit safe white water canoeing, portaging, and may include camping. Field trips will involve overnight camping. Prerequisite: PEG 209 or permission of the department head.

title: General Safety Education
description: Designed to prepare prospective teachers for the comprehensive general safety education program.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control. Designed to aid the student to develop a fitness philosophy, to structure physical fitness programs, and to recognize individual physiological limitations.

title: Gymnastics (Balance Beam and Floor Exercise)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastics (Trampoline, Vaulting, Uneven Bars)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, flying rings, and uneven parallel bars. Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Foundations of Physical Education
description: An introductory course for professional physical education students that covers the psychomotor, cognitive, and affective scope of physical education and its relationship to education. An attempt is made to assist students in assessing those qualities of motor and physical fitness expected of physical 'education majors as they commence their vocational study.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 1
description: Content, methods, materials, organization, and administration of the classroom and laboratory phase of the secondary school program.

title: Principles and Problems of Coaching Sports for Girls and Women
description: Introduces students to the following: the principles and problems of coaching girls' team and individual sports at the junior and senior high school level; the philosophies and principles which underlie the development of such a program.

title: Coaching Observation (Girls'/Women's Athletics)
description: Guided observation of coaching techniques and practices with analyzation of teaching/coaching philosophies for competitive sports in schools. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Practicum in Aquatics
description: Gives the student supervised experience in aquatic programs. The student will work specifically in aquatic programs in existence at Ball State or other established organizations. Prerequisite: PEG 202 and 203. A total of 2 hours credit may be earned.

title: Officiating Competitive Aquatic Sports
description: Gives students an understanding of desired officiating practices, a comprehension of particular aquatic performance techniques related to decision making by officials, and laboratory experience in officiating. The student is presented the opportunity for certification in various aquatic officiating areas.

title: Tumbling and Apparatus (Women's Events)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 158 and 159 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastic Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has two hours of credit in PEP 256 or 258.

title: Dance Theatre
description: Provides the dance student with experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance performances. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Folk Dance
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 112.

title: The Teaching of Folk Dance
description: Materials and techniques of teaching folk dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEP 262 or equivalent.

title: Folk Dance Theatre
description: Provides opportunities and experiences in participating with a company of dancers who plan and perform in both informal and formal folk dance presentations. Prerequisite: PEG 112 and permission of the department head. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Square Dance Methods
description: The development of teaching skills for beginning and intermediate classes in square dancing. The development of techniques of calling square dance (patter and singing). Prerequisite: PEP 263.

title: Dance Composition 1
description: Principal elements of dance composition. Simple compositional forms for smaller groups and solo work. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

description: Prerequisite: PEP 173 or permission of the department head.

description: Prerequisite: PEP 177 or permission of the department head.

description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 179.

title: Track and Field Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 180.

title: Physiology
description: Basic concepts in physiology for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching. Prerequisite: PEP 292, or permission of the department head.

title: Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze activity for the purpose of improving physical skills. Prerequisite: PEP 292.

title: First Aid

title: First Aid Instructor

Prerequisite: PEP 299 or HSC 250, or valid certification in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, Standard First Aid and Multimedia, or Advanced First Aid and Emergency Care.

title: Simulation in Driver and Traffic Safety Education
description: Desgined to meet the needs of prospective teachers in the simulation phase of driver and traffic safety education. Prerequisite: PEP 124.

description: Coaching techniques involved in gymnastics, volleyball, and track and field. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: StiNategies and Techniques in Coaching Volleyball, Basketball, and Softball
description: Coaching techniques involved in volleyball, basketball, and softball. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Swimming, Golf, Gymnastics, and Tennis
description: Coaching techniques involved in swimming, golf, gymnastics, and tennis. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Organization and Management of Women's Athletics
description: Understanding and appreciation of: the responsibilities and desirable characteristics of competent officials; organizing and managing competitive events and tournaments; relationships among coach, officials, players, and spectators; local, state, and national organizations involved in officiating and management.

title: Field and/or Laboratory Experience
description: Provides the student with administrative aquatic experience outside the present offerings. These experiences will place the student in a leadership role. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling

description: Exploration and the use of accompaniment in dance. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or the equivalent.

title: Dance Production
description: Various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or the equivalent.

description: Fundamental modern dance techniques, elements of rhythmic patterns, materials or space, design, and improvisation.

description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on composition. Prerequisite: PEP 365.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Methodology)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on teaching modern dance in the public schools, camps, and others. Dance composition. Prerequisite: PEP 366.

title: Aquatics for the Elementary School Child
description: Assist the student to acquire an understanding of safety factors, developmental stroke and diving sequences, and teaching strategies for aquatic instruction of the young child. Prerequisite: PEP 353 or equivalent certification.

title: Diagnostic Techniques and Athletic Injury Mechanisms
description: An introduction to predisposing anatomical, kinesiological, growth stress, and other such factors that contribute to athletic injuries. Procedures for accurate recognition and evaluation of not only these factors, but also the extent of an athletic injury are presented. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Administration and Organization of Programs for the Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Problems, principles, and objectives in the designing, planning, and operation of a program for the prevention and care of athletic injuries. There will also be an examination of the code of ethics of the National Athletic Trainer's Association. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Athletic Training Modalities and Therapeutic Techniques
description: An introduction to mechanical therapies, thermal therapy, cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, and thereapeutic exercise. Only those modalties and their clinical uses that have special implications for the athletic trainer in the treatment of injuries to the athlete will be considered. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following team sports: basketball, field hockey, flag football, soccer, softball, speedball, team handball, volleyball. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in team sports included.

title: Methods of Teaching Individual Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following individual sports: archery, badminton, bowling, golf, tennis, track. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in individual sports included.

description: Prerequisite: PEP 276.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball and Softball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 279.

description: Prerequisite: PEP 280.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 281.

description: Prerequisite: PEP 282.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 283.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 284.

description: The development of gymnastics judging techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and or NAGWS (Class) official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 157, 158, 159.

title: Track and Field Officiating
description: The development of track and field officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 180.

title: Softball Umpiring
description: The development of softball umpiring techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA, ASA, and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Volleyball Officiating
description: The development of volleyball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 183.

title: Basketball Officiating
description: The development of basketball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 182.

title: Principles of Physical Education
description: General concepts based upon the scientific facts and philosophic judgments which underlie physical education.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, utilizing task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include the factors of purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation.

description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the student to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate an array of teaching strategies that would be utilized in creating a freesafe environment for a public school physical education Program. description: Designed as a practicum that involves comprehensive planning of instruction, designing teaching implementation strategies, classroom management techniques, and evaluation of teaching behaviors and materials in physical education. title: Practicum in Recreation
description: Supervised, practical, professional leadership experience designed for the recreation oriented person. Experiences include: work activities in federal, state, county, or community parks or with private camps. Close supervision supplied by the University and the participating agency. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 2
description: Presentation of materials and information designed to prepare for teaching driver education in the secondary schools.

title: Coaching Internship (Girls'/Women's Athletics)
description: Assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teaching/coaching process. (May not be taken during student teaching). Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Problems in Aquatic Programs Development
description: Programs and problems of the physical educator working in aquatics.

title: Dance for the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Advanced Studio in Contemporary Dance

Diedrich The College of Sciences and Humanities provides courses and programs for either a liberal education or for specialized and professional curricula. The liberal arts programs permit the student to elect more freely and to explore the "idea" subject matter. "Liberal" stems from the Latin liber, to free. By definition, a liberal arts education should free people from ignorance by providing them an intelligent grasp of the experiences of the past and an understanding of the interrelationship of branches of knowledge. The individual is educated to think objectively, critically, and creatively. The liberal arts include the study of foreign languages, the physical and social environment, the evolution of Western civilization, the foundations of modern science, and the classical works. The wide range of courses offered by the College of Sciences and Humanities provides the basis for specialized and professional curricula—offered both within the college and in the other colleges requiring service courses. Within the College, preprofessional programs are specified—for medicine, dentistry, engineering, and law. A variety of specialist programs is offered, including medical technology and social work. Also, the departments within the College have programs designed for those planning graduate study in the field of their choice. The College includes the following departments: Anthropology, Biology, Chemistry, Criminal Justice and Corrections, Economics, English, Foreign Languages (French, German, Greek, Latin, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish), General and Experimental Psychology, Geography and Geology, History, Journalism, Mathematical Sciences, Natural Resources, Philosophy, Physics and Astronomy, Physiology and Health Science, Political Science, Center for Radio and Television, Social Work, Sociology, Speech and Theatre, Speech Pathology and Audiology. In addition, the College offers programs in the Social Sciences and in three Institutes—Environmental Studies, International Studies, and Urban and Regional Studies. Today's college student, to be an effective individual, must be aware of the varying and constantly changing cultural conditions of other societies. Urban and Regional Studies 197 Institute for Urban and Regional Studies Mitchell, Director Nearly threequarters of all Americans live and work in metropolitan areas. Complex social and economic activity in these areas has created a host of largescale problems. Meaningful analysis of these difficult problems requires a spirit of collaboration among experts with different backgrounds. At Ball State, this orientation translates into an interdisciplinary undergraduate program in Urban and Regional Studies. The Urban and Regional Studies program draws on the strengths of various disciplines such as economics, geography, history, political science, and sociology. The scope of inquiry includes the nature of an urban economy, the structure and function of cities, historical perspective on urban development, the organization of local government, city politics, and the dynamics of urban communities. Students receive instruction in the use of various tools for analyzing urban areas and their regions. One goal of the program is to prepare students for entry level or preprofessional positions in planning, urban administration, community development, and social programs. The experiences are designed primarily to educate rather than train students, for regular training in urban affairsrelated professions is normally at the graduate level. A second goal of this program is to provide an educational foundation for those students who desire to pursue graduate training in planning, law, social work, public administration, or other urbanrelated disciplines. Another goal is to encourage student involvement in community affairs and to provide learning experiences outside the classroom. Students participate in projects with public agencies or other urban institutions. They also gain valuable work experiences through internships with plan commissions, community development agencies, local governments, and the like. Urban and Regional Studies is a departmental major on the Professional Arts Curriculum. A departmental minor is also offered as a useful alternative for students having a more casual interest in urban affairs. This general background gives students, many if not most of whom will settle in large metropolitan areas, a degree of understanding about their urban environment which should be reflected in their future civic and professional activities. Department of Anthropology Izmirlian, Chairman; Coffin, Flores-Meiser, Genz, Glenn, Hicks, Scruton, Swartz, Whitehead Anthropology is scarcely a hundred years old as a formal academic discipline. Its origins are in the nineteenth century's growing awareness of non-European societies, the revelation that man's social past is of great antiquity, and the discovery of Charles Darwin of the biological mechanisms which have produced the human species. From these several awakenings has emerged a field which, as developed in this country, is exclusively neither a biological nor a social science, but is uniquely both. It is, in fact, the singular amalgamation of the two areas which is responsible for the name of the field, the Study of Man. Although the anthropologist, as a practicing scholar, develops a specialty, the field itself remains convinced that the human phenomenon is a sociobiological whole and must finally be studied as such. This belief prompts the anthropologist and the student to examine a very wide range of content areas. Modern cultural anthropology has grown out of the nineteenth century's interest in the accounts by travelers, explorers, missionaries, merchants, and soldiers of the frequently astonishing and sometimes hostile people whom they had met. Much of the early work of the cultural anthropologist, or ethnologist, has been the gathering of accurate information about the world's nonliterate peoples. Modern ethnology, it should be noted, places little stress on the word "primitive," having been driven by the data to the conclusion that it does not separate categories of people very efficiently. But from this early interest in different societies has developed anthropology's increasingly sophisticated analysis of culture, and the study of contemporary peoples, whether they be peasants in such places as Mexico, India, the Philippines, and Africa, or urbanites living in Muncie, Indiana, and its environs. Much comparative work has been done, and courses in anthropology departments reflect this, in crosscultural studies of religion, kinship and family systems, governments, technologies, value and belief systems, literatures, modes of aesthetic expression in song, dance, and the graphic and plastic arts, among other institutions. Anthropology wrestles with countless unsolved problems in the area of relations between personalities and the social milieu in which they occur and in the area of cultural dynamics. The possibilities of practical application are numerous, and are, increasingly, being exploited. Much of cultural anthropology is closely related to history and no branch of anthropology illustrates this fact more clearly than archaeology. Courses in this area provide the student of the human past with techniques which enable many of the limitations of conventional historiography to be overcome, with the result that we now possess knowledge of human behavior during times antedating writing by sometimes hundreds of thousands of years. Of course, this knowledge is rarely of the detailed and specific sort sought by the historian. But although archaeologists are commonly deprived of historical personalities, they have the compensation of seeing the great sweep of human affairs with perhaps greater clarity. The archaeologist reminds the student that it was during prehistoric times that most of the great steps in human progress were made: the development of technology, the creation of forms of government, kinship, religion, philosophy, and art. The archaeologist also reminds the student Anthropology 199 through appropriate courses of the long and fruitful cooperation between the historian and the prehistorian, which has been responsible for the bulk of our knowledge of the ancient world of classical times, including Egypt, the Near East, Greece, Crete, and early Rome. In physical anthropology attention is commonly focused on such topics as the nature of the evolutionary process which is responsible, through the action of natural selection, hybridization, genetic drift and artificial selection, for the development of the large, tailless, terrestrial, bipedal, orthograde primate which man is. Course work is commonly devoted to the fossil evidence of recent human evolution, especially during the Pleistocene period. Without doubt, that aspect of physical anthropology which has the greatest potential contribution to make to human selfunderstanding, and the aspect likeliest to be of practical application, is the study of contemporary varieties, or races of humanity. This is a subject about which people seem to have the most fundamental convictions, and commonly one in which the unfortunate effects of total ignorance are clearly seen. The anthropologist is deeply involved in all phases of this study, from the determination of the nature of the phenomenon itself, through the eventual genetic classification of races, to the delicate and vexing questions having to do with the significance of race differences. The pursuit of truth is the goal of the scientist. But the application of knowledge which has been secured through the scientific method is hardly avoidable. Preparation in anthropology might involve some work in the field of linguistics. This is a highly specialized area, and thorough preparation through detailed courses is less common than in the other areas. It is linguistics which, in recent years, has begun to make students aware that talking is more than simply a method of communicating ideas between speakers of the same language; it is the vehicle of thought itself, and it provides the speaker not only with categories of expression, but also with the means at once of perceiving and of ordering his universe. At this point linguistics is very close to cultural anthropology. These several areas, and others which may develop, are all related through anthropology's constant emphasis on the "wholeness" of man.
