Knowledge of sound job control techniques, disciplinary techniques, verbal and nonverbal communications, supervisorunion relationships, and other topics which are the common denominator of all supervisors and bases for the course. Prerequisite: MGT 280.

title: International Management and Multinational Operations
description: Comparative management practices around the world; international business behavior and problems confronting multinational executives and corporations; analysis of corporate structures and operations in foreign environments. Study of management functions, organizations, structures, policies, operations, and multinational practices and global strategies. Prerequisite: MGT 380 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Principles of Management
description: This course examines in detail the four major managerial functions: planning, organizing, motivating and controlling as they are applied to the process of management and the organic functions of a business enterprise. Other significant concepts stressed are the importance of leadership and problem solving techniques applied to managerial situations and the aspects of coordination, communication, human relations and production/ operations management necessary for an individual to be successful as a manager. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Production/Operations Management 1
description: A basic study of functional fields of production. Decision making and quantitative analysis of production problems arising in areas of methods analysis, work measurement, wage incentives, production planning and control, inventory control, plant layout, materials handling and quality control. Prerequisite: MGT 380.

title: Business and Society
description: An interdisciplinary approach toward developing a philosophy concerning the role of business in society. Emphasis on contemporary issues requiring business people to reexamine their role and the role of the corporation in community and national life. Prerequisite: MGT 380.

title: Organizational Behavior
description: Focuses on the dynamics of human behavior in business organizations, with concentration on problems of motivation and leadership. Emphasis is on the behavior of individuals and groups within organizations, and the practical interpretation and management of behavioral phenomena. Prerequisite: MGT 380 or permission of the department chairman. Management Science 119

title: Production/Operations Management 2
description: An intermediate study of the functional areas of production. Emphasis on decisionmaking and quantitative analysis of production problems arising in the areas of incentives, production planning and control, inventory control, plant layout, materials handling and quality control. Prerequisite: MGT 383; MS 221.

title: Small Business Ventures
description: Provides essential knowledge for students interested in small business. Topics include searching for venture opportunities; economic, technical, and operational feasibility of the venture; financing; negotiations; and operations. Emphasizes characteristics of the small business enterprise. Prerequisite: BL 360, MGT 380, FIN 350, MKT 370 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Small Business Practicum
description: Teams of students consult with local small businesses. Cases are assigned by Small Business Administration. Students work on problems of the particular small business. Problems may be office administration, accounting, production, marketing, personnel, finance, insurance, legal, or information systems. Prerequisite: senior standing and MGT 380 or permission of the department head.

title: Internship in Management
description: Under a program approved and supervised by the Department of Management Science, a student majoring in management science will work full time for a quarter as an intern in an organization operating either in the private or public sector. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to third quarter juniors or seniors.

title: Internship in Computer Management
description: Under a program approved and supervised by the Department of Management Science, a student majoring in management science will work halftime two quarters as an intern in Ball State University Computer Center. Prerequisite: MS 220, 382, four hours of experience working in the Ball State University Computer Center or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Personnel Planning and Selection
description: Focuses on organization and manpower planning. Includes determination of organization and manpower needs, analysis and development of job requirements and necessary qualifications for recruitment and selection, selection procedures, placement and orientation, and evaluation of selection programs. Prerequisite: MGT 481.

title: Personnel Administration
description: How to administer a personnel program in a business organization so as to deal effectively with such problems as selection, training, compensation, promotion, and transfer of workers; working conditions; employee services; and industrial relations. Prerequisite: MGT 380.

title: Case Problems in Personnel Management
description: Case studies depicting complex personnel issues and problems faced by organizations. Provides the student an opportunity to apply personnel policies, theories, concepts, and techniques to actual personnel situations. Prerequisite: MGT 481.

title: Problems in Production/Operations Management
description: An integration of all the production/ operations management principles, theories, and techniques gained from previous courses as applied to actual production problems. Major teaching methods include case study, discussion, and individual projects. Current topics may be discussed. Prerequisite: MGT 386 and permission of the department chairman.

title: Quality Assurance
description: Application of statistical control charts, sampling plans, and reliability analysis to problems of planning, feedback, and control of product quality, process performance, operation effectiveness, and related areas of management activities. Prerequisite: MS 221.

title: Work Design
description: The design of office and industrial jobs to meet the needs and preferences of the worker and the management. Included are methods improvement techniques, layout of work stations, incentive and motivation techniques and the setting of output standards. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Comparative Administration
description: Comparative analysis of managing complex organizations and service industries; emphasizing environmental and organizational factors affecting the management process, firm structure, and administration functions. Study of administration crossculturally (internationally) and crossinstitutionally (service industries). Prerequisite: MGT 380 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Office Management and Control
description: The management of the business office as a producing unit and the relation of the office routine to managerial control of the several other departments of a business through records, reports, and budgets. Prerequisite: MGT 380.

title: Case Problems in Office Management
description: Develops skill in identifying the key problem of a complicated office situation and in formulating a practical solution to this problem. The interrelatedness of major office management activities is stressed as well as the broad scope of problems pertaining to the office. Prerequisite: MGT 488.

title: Independent Study in Management
description: An opportunity for supervised study of some phase of management. May consist of an experiment, library research, or an analysis of current management practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Management
description: Explores in depth current problems, theory, research, and trends in the management field. The topics of the seminar will vary depending upon the current status of managerial research, the instructor, and the needs and desires of the students. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Business Applications of Computer Data Processing
description: An introductory course in computer data processing with special emphasis on business problem solving. Includes study of the effects of computers on business and management decisionmaking, of computer hardware and software, concepts and procedures for business systems analysis, and computer programming. Special problems in the areas of accounting, production, marketing, banking, finance, and management are analyzed and run on computers.

title: Interpretation of Business Data
description: An introductory course dealing with the collection, presentation, analysis, and interpretation of statistical data. Topics include descriptive statistics, basic probability, probability distributions, sampling, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, regression, and correlation. Prerequisite: MATH 131 and 132 or permission of the department head. Prerequisite recommended: MS 220.

title: Business Application Programming
description: Basic COBOL and programming skills using illustrative examples, exercises, and topics which emphasize applications in commercial data processing. Prerequisite: MS 220 or CS 220, or CS 200. Not open to the student who has credit in CS 210.

title: Business Computer Systems and Applications
description: Acquaints students with current business use of computer. Deals with selected properties of systems design and file design. Presents a general framework from singlepurpose to integrated business applications, such as accounting, operationscontrol, productionscheduling, personnel, and marketing. Prerequisite: MS 220.

title: Quantifying Management Decisions
description: A study and critical evaluation of operations research techniques for solving managerial problems found in business administration. Prerequisite: MS 220 and 221.

title: Simulating Management Decisions
description: A study and critical evaluation of simulation techniques for solving managerial problems found in business administration. Prerequisite: MS 220 and 221.

title: Management Information Systems
description: Systems theory and practice as they are applied to satisfying information needs for management decisionmakers through the analysis and design of manual and computerbased systems. Influence of information systems upon management and organization as well as upon managerial decisionmaking. Prerequisite: MGT 380, MS 220, or permission of the department chairman.

title: Data Base: Structures and Management
description: Logical and physical organization of data. Describes data description, command and interrogation languages. Examines function of data bases in information systems. Prerequisite: MS 220 or permission of the department chairperson

title: Administration of Management Information Systems
description: Topics include equipment selection, equipment acquisition, computer operations management, project management, computer personnel management, financial control, systems security and control, and the relationship of the information systems functions to the organization as a whole. Prerequisite: MS 382 and 411 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Communications Based Information Systems
description: Describes computer related communication equipment, transmission services and protocols. Studies the uses, features, control, benefits and costs of online and realtime information systems. Prerequisite: MS 220 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Business Systems Analysis and Design
description: An introductory course in business systems analysis and design. Introduces elementary systems techniques and tools. Explains in detail the key steps in the systems development cycle. Deals with some of the practical applications and considerations in systems within the business environment. Prerequisite: MS 220 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Business Statistics
description: The application to business problems of the most commonly used advanced statistical methods including goodnessoffit, contingency tables, analysis of variance, nonparametric techniques, advanced regression and correlation as applied to time series, and index numbers. Prerequisite: MS 221. Prerequisite recommended: MS 220. Marketing 121

title: Getting and Keeping a Job in Business

Department of Marketing Lowry, Head; Baird, Brown, Clabaugh, Moser, Riecken, Sparling, Vanderleest, Yavas Marketing is a business function concerned with the management of the flow of goods and services from the producer to the consumer. The marketing process provides an efficient way for producers to meet the needs of consumers. Marketing activities which a firm performs to satisfy its consumers include offering the right product, promoting it properly, selling it at the right price, and distributing it in the right place. Marketing courses at Ball State University are designed to allow students to develop their abilities to recognize, define, and solve creatively marketing problems. Because the majority of Ball State marketing graduates go directly into business, the marketing curriculum is career oriented. Students majoring in marketing choose one of four options within the marketing curriculum. Each option emphasizes different career opportunities. The sales and advertising management option prepares students for careers in areas such as consumer and industrial product selling, sales training, transportation, purchasing, advertising agency management, and public relations. Career opportunities for students selecting the retail management option include chain store management, merchandising, fashion coordination, small business management, and buying. The marketing planning and research option prepares students for careers in marketing analysis, marketing research management, sales forecasting, advertising research, new product research, and product planning. The general marketing option is for students who want a foundation for a career in the marketing field. After obtaining a foundation in marketing, students are qualified to pursue many different phases of the marketing process. The Department of Marketing, in cooperation with selected business firms, offers a professional practice program which allows juniors and seniors to relate classroom theory to practical experience by working for one quarter in a variety of meaningful assignments. Students who are working as interns receive from two to eight quarter hours of credit and are paid by the firm for their work experience. The Student Marketing Association (SMA) is an organization which provides opportunities for participating in marketing discussions and programs and developing friendships with students who have similar interests. In the past, the SMA has conducted a series of minicourses on career planning and has brought selected speakers to the campus to discuss job qualifications and career opportunities in various marketing fields. In cooperation with local civic organizations, the SMA has also conducted studies that have assisted in identifying the market needs of minority groups and senior citizens. The United States Department of Labor indicates that the need for individuals with college level training in marketing will continue to grow. Sales and retail store management opportunities offer the greatest potential for Ball State marketing graduates in the future. For the student interested in preparing for teaching marketing and/or distributive education, it is possible to earn a departmental major in marketing along with the teaching major in distributive education. For the student preparing for teaching business education, marketing is a part of the major and minor areas. Teaching areas are listed in the statement of the Department of Business Education and Office Administration. A departmental minor in marketing is available to students with a major in any academic area other than business. The minor consists of 24 quarter hours in marketing and is intended to provide a valuable supplement to students majoring in nonbusiness fields. title: Salesmanship
description: Fundamentals of retail, wholesale, outside, and service selling. Sales approaches, presentation, closings, and postsale service are emphasized. Prerequisite: GBA

description: Introduction to the field of advertising with emphasis on the preparation, appeal, and media selection of retail advertising. Prerequisite: GBA 101. Not open to the student who has credit in MKT 370.

description: Analysis of the consumer issues which affect marketing. Includes the marketing implications of consumerism, ecology, and the disadvantaged consumers. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Industrial Procurement Management
description: A basic course in industrial procurement management. Principal topics considered are make or buy analysis, quality and quantity control, value analysis, price determination, sources of supply, the purchasing system, and legal aspects of purchasing. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

description: Practices of businesses in granting credit both to other business firms and to individuals. Credit limits, department operations, and collection policies are analyzed. title: Buyer Behavior
description: Practical business implications of the various aspects of consumer motivation and behavior. The student is provided with information to understand how and why a buyer reacts in a purchasing situation. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Selling and Sales Management
description: Practices in recruiting, selecting, training, compensating, and controlling the sales force. An analysis of the stages of a sales presentation. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Advertising Management
description: Use of advertising as a communication tool in marketing management. Analysis of media selection production and layout, measurement of effectiveness, and social and economic aspects of advertising. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Retail Management
description: An investigation of store policies, organization, location, layout, buying, stock control, pricing, and sales promotion for retail stores. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Principles of Marketing
description: A basic course that examines marketing as a productive system within our economy. Promotional activities, product policies, retail and wholesale activities, pricing policies, international marketing, and marketing's role in society are studied. Prerequisite: ECON 201 or junior standing.

title: Materials Management
description: The organizational concept that integrates the management of the flow of materials through a business enterprise into consumer markets. Content includes: anticipating, sourcing, obtaining, and monitoring the current status of materials in an enterprise. Prerequisite: MKT 370. Prerequisite recommended: MKT 310.

title: Marketing Simulation Game
description: A simulation game where students are divided into teams or companies. Management in each company makes decisions in marketing, finance, and production. Does not involve writing computer programs or utilizing information from a data processing class. Prerequisite: MKT 370 and junior standing.

title: Promotion Strategy
description: Use of cases and problems to provide experience in making decisions on a firm's promotional mix. Analysis of markets, media scheduling, budget allocation, campaign design, and promotion research. Prerequisite: MKT 340.

title: Channel Strategy
description: An analysis of the alternative channels of distribution available to manufacturers and producers. Management decisions necessary for an effective channel organization are stressed with emphasis upon the use of retailing and wholesaling intermediaries. Prerequisite: MKT 350.

title: Survey of Transportation
description: The economics of transportation — internal waterways, railways, highways, and airways in the United States; economic development of various means of transportation and accompanying regulatory problems. Rate, traffic service, and coordination problems of our transportation system. Advantages and disadvantages, trends, and peculiarities of each of the various modes of transportation. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Physical Distribution Management
description: Physical distribution systems in the marketing environment; system components and the total cost approach; customer service objectives ; physical distribution systems design and administration. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: International Marketing
description: Examines legal, economic, and cultural factors influencing marketing abroad. Commercial policies, practices, and techniques needed to locate and evaluate foreign markets, as well as the problems of pricing, promoting, and distributing products in international markets. Prerequisite: MKT 370.

title: Marketing Research
description: A basic course in marketing research. Nature and scope of marketing research; scientific method and research design ; specific marketing research procedures; techniques of sampling; and research report, followup, and evaluation of research process. Selected applications in areas of motivation, advertising, and product and sales control research. Prerequisites: MKT 370 and MS 221.

title: Quantitative Marketing
description: Exploration of the various quantitative techniques that can be utilized in solving marketing problems. Principal topics considered are linear programming methods, game theory, Markov chains, probability theory in decision making, distribution cost analysis, and use of correlation. Prerequisite: MS 221.

title: Marketing Management
description: Marketing by manufacturers as viewed from the marketing manager's position. Principal topics are selecting channels of distribution, determining demand, pricing policies, marketing legislation, advertising policies, and methods of selling. A case study approach. Prerequisite: 16 quarter hours in marketing, including MKT 330, 340, and senior standing.

title: Professional Practice in Marketing
description: The student receives professional practice during a summer or a quarter as an intern on an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization under the supervision of the Department of Marketing. Periodic written reports of job experiences are required. Open only to thirdquarter juniors and seniors with a major in marketing. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Marketing
description: For students who wish to conduct independent study in some phase of marketing. May consist of an experiment, library research, or the analysis of current marketing practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing, a scholastic ratio of 3.0, or permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

description: Emphasizes the vital role of business in our society through a discussion of both the external environment of business and the internal environment of the business enterprise. Hoyt The College of Fine and Applied Arts is dedicated to the education of professional personnel in the various areas represented, and also contributes to the cultural development of students throughout the University. The programs of the college are administered through its five departments and two schools: the Departments of Art, Home Economics, Industrial Education and Technology, Library Science, and Nursing, the School of Music, and the School of Physical Education and Athletics. While, traditionally, teaching has been the objective of most of the students enrolled in the college, curricula for other professional preparation in each of the schools and departments are increasingly popular. The Department of Nursing, for example, is totally devoted to professional preparation of men and women for service in the field of nursing. In recent years, the leadership and direction for the fine arts in America are emanating from college and university campuses. Therefore, at Ball State as elsewhere, outstanding artists and musicians are to be found on the faculties. The departments in the College of Fine and Applied Arts may be thought of as the "doing" or "performing" departments; thus the faculty and students are frequently engaged in displaying, demonstrating, or performing their skills and achievements before numerous publics attracted to them. Army Reserve Officers Training Corps (AROTC) York, O'Neill, Stone, Whitworth The Army ROTC Program provides qualified male and female students with an opportunity to obtain a commission in the United States Army and its reserve components. Students may obtain this commission by enrolling in the Army ROTC program along with their regular undergraduate studies in the field of their choice. The program consists of two elements: basic and advanced courses. The basic course, normally taken during the freshman (Militaiy Science 1) and sophomore (Military Science 2) academic years, provides students with essential background information concerning organization and operations of the U.S. Defense Establishment. Students in the basic course do not incur any military obligations by enrolling in these classes. Completion of the basic course, or constructive credit for Junior AROTC (3 years), or attendance at a basic summer camp, or prior military service, is a prerequisite for admission into the advanced course. The advanced course, normally taken during the junior and senior academic years, provides students with leadership and management skills not available in other curricula and with concepts of military tactics, operations, and organizations. Advanced course students are obligated to attend an advanced summer camp (6 weeks) and to accept a commission as an officer, if tendered. Advanced course students receive subsistence and pay approximating $2,500 during the two years. All necessary equipment and books are furnished by the Department of the Army at no cost to the student. Credits earned in the military science (AROTC) program may apply toward degree requirements. For specific information, students are advised to consult with their advisers in their major field of study. The U.S. Army offers financial assistance in the form of one, two, and three year scholarships. Each scholarship provides tuition, textbooks, laboratory fees, and supplies in addition to subsistence pay of $100 per month for the period that the scholarship is in effect. Applications for these scholarships may be submitted by anyone who is enrolled in the AROTC program. Graduates who have completed the advanced course may be called upon to serve a fouryear active duty tour and four years in the U.S. Army Reserve. Others will serve three months active duty for training in lieu of four years active duty and may be required to participate satisfactorily in the ready reserve until the eighth anniversary date of the initial appointment in the Army Reserve. Entry to active duty may be deferred to obtain an advanced degree. Departmental minor in military science, 24 hours MIL 110, 120, 130, 210, 220, 230, 310, 320, 330, 410, 420, 430 21 hrs. title: Leadership and Management 2
description: Analysis of selected leadership and management problems. Principles of organization, informal organizations, formal organizations, nature and use of committees, communications techniques, and systems concepts. Application of leadership principles to practical situations. Prerequisite: MIL 320.

title: Dynamics of the Military Team 4
description: Continuation of the study of combat operations with emphasis on the command and staff functions at division level and higher; orientation for branch assignments, personal management responsibilities and the responsibilities of a commissioned officer. title: Seminar in Crafts

title: Foundations 1
description: Exploration and use of basic art elements (line, shape, value, texture, color) to organize space on the twodimensional plane. Also employed are basic tools and techniques, with emphasis on craftsmanship. Not open to the student who has credit in ADS

title: Foundations 2
description: Continued exploration of the basic art elements (line, form, texture, color, value) to organize the threedimensional aspects of design and structure in space. Prerequisite: ADS 101.

title: Foundations 3
description: Advanced problems in design involving both twoand threedimensional areas. Emphasis on problem recognition and solution through comprehensive design methods and aesthetic considerations. Personal initiative and craftsmanship are stressed. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Color
description: Primarily a laboratory course concerned with an indepth study of contemporary color theory and practice, color and light, and color in the environment. Prerequisite: ADS 101,

title: Graphic Design
description: Utilization of esthetic visual communication elements achieved through photographic, typographic, and lithographic processes. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102, 103.

title: Design Problems
description: Introduction to the esthetic considerations applied by the designer in visual problem solving. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102, 103.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Advanced problems in communication design with emphasis on visual problem solving. Prerequisite: ADS 212.

title: Advanced Design Problems
description: Comprehensive design problem recognition with emphasis on individual initiative and resolution. Prerequisite: ADS 213.

title: Design Presentation and Delineation 1
description: An introduction to the principles of perspective as applied to the areas of interior/environmental design and visual communications. Emphasis on graphic representation and design with various media and techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 201 or 202.

title: Design Presentation and Delineation 2
description: An introduction to principles of rendering as applied to the areas of interior/environmental design and visual communications. Emphasis on delineation of presentation techniques with such media as watercolor and markers. Prerequisite: ADS 205.

title: Typography
description: Underlying principles of design applied to typographic problems. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102, 103.

title: Visual Communications 1
description: Problems in visual communications from roughs to comprehensives with stress on practical and technical limitations and possibilities. Prerequisite: ADS 201, 202, 211.

title: Visual Communications 2
description: Problems in visual communications such as trademarks, layouts, posters, and folders. Exploration of the influence of reproduction procedures on the design. Prerequisite: ADS 212, 332.

title: Package Design
description: Design developments of single packages, labels, and package lines from the sketch to the dummy. Models of display pieces. Variations and redesign of existing packages. Prerequisite: ADS 213.

title: Environmental Theory
description: Studies in human scale, science of human settlements, and theories of man's use of space. Not open to the student who has credit in ADS 330.

title: Interior Materials
description: Basic concepts of the physical properties and uses of various materials in interior environment.

title: Interior/Environmental Design 1
description: An exploration of environmental needs and creative design problems involving simple residential interiors including graphic presentations. Enrollment limited to students specializing in interior design or permission of the department head. Prerequisite: AFA 201; ARCH 217; TED 302.

title: Photography 1
description: Beginning and intermediate study in photography as an expressive art form. Courses must be taken in sequence. Each student must furnish his/her own light meter and camera with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: for students with areas in art, ADS 101; for others, permission of the department head.

title: Typography 2
description: Advanced typographic considerations encompassing both practical application and free experimentation in the design of the written message. Prerequisite: ADS 204, 214.

title: Visual Communications 3
description: Advanced problems in visual communications. Emphasis is on the application of esthetic concerns to practical problems faced by the professional designer. Prerequisite: ADS 311.

title: Interior/Environmental Design 2
description: Creative design problems involving simple commercial and institutional interiors such as single retail outlets, exhibitions, small shops, private offices, classrooms, including space planning and graphic representation. Enrollment limited to students specializing in interior design or permission of the department head. Prerequisite: ADS 223.

title: Design and Fabrication of Furniture
description: Anthropometrics and systems analysis as related to the design, construction, and production of furniture. Includes working drawings and scale models. Prerequisite: ADS 324. 332, 433. Photography 2, 3. (3) Beginning and intermediate study in photography as an expressive art form. Courses must be taken in sequence. Each student must furnish his/her own light meter and camera with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: for students with areas in art, ADS 101, 102, 103; for others, permission of the department head.

title: Independent Study in Design
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of the department head. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Interior/Environmental Design 3
description: Advanced design problems in complex residential, commercial or institutional interiors such as hotel, motel, nursing home, restaurant, shopping center, office building, religious building, school, university, airport, and hospital, with basic understandings in space analysis and planning. Enrollment limited to students specializing in interior design or permission of the department head.

title: Interior/Environmental Design 4
description: Design analysis of nonresidential spaces of increased complexity using systematic analysis of human factors as determinants of the design solution. Prerequisite: ADS 425.

title: Interior/Environmental Design 5
description: Advanced design analysis of nonresidential large scale complex spaces using systematic analysis of human factors as determinants of the design solution. Prerequisite: ADS 426.

title: Photography 3

title: Photography 4
description: Major emphasis on students learning to generate and intensify their personal statement through the medium of color and black and white photography. Students select their own projects and work with their individual ideas under the guidance of an instructor. Class discussions focus on relevant problems found in working with this medium. Each student must furnish his/her own light meter and camera with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 231, 332, 433.

title: Cinematography as an Art Form
description: A practical study of the use of cinematography and video as a medium of art expression. Students will be expected to develop and organize the film with an emphasis on the art form.

title: Professional Practices
description: Ethics, business mechanics, office management, merchandising, verbal presentations, computer programming, and space analysis in interior/environmental design. Prerequisite: ADS 425. Not open to the student who has credit in ADS 400.

title: Visual Communications Senior Seminar
description: Seminar study involving individual investigation and experience in visual communications problems. Prerequisite: ADS 312.

title: Senior Seminar
description: A creative design analysis encompassing both residential and nonresidential planning consideration written and programmed by the student as a culminating effort to develop an indepth design concept. Prerequisite: ADS 427.

title: Seminar in Design

title: Introductory Drawing and Painting
description: A studio course of twodimensional experiences designed to develop beginning students' potentials for mature visual perception, aesthetic responses, skills of expression, and creative problemsolving. Open to all students except those with areas in art.

title: Introductory Printmaking and Sculpture
description: A studio course designed to introduce the student to basic printmaking and sculptural techniques and media. Prerequisite: AED 100. Open to all students except those with areas in art.

title: Studio Materials and Techniques Applied to Teaching
description: Relating materials, techniques, and tools to the teaching concepts relevant to art classes in the various developmental levels of students from elementary through high school. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102; AFA 101.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Art
description: Offers direct experiences in teaching art and art appreciation to elementary children. Discussions of developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum, learning environments, and strategies of teaching will be applied to actual teaching experiences. Three twohour classes per week plus assigned teaching time. Prerequisite: AED 201, sophomore standing, and 18 hours of credit in art courses.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint the student with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques are stressed. Prerequisite: AED 100, 200.

title: Curriculum Materials for Teaching Art
description: A laboratory course designed to develop the student's ability to produce his/her own materials for teaching art to any age level. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202 or permission of the department head.

title: Teaching Art Awareness in the Public Schools
description: An analysis of current thinking, approaches and methodologies of fostering art appreciation in elementary and secondary schools with emphasis on designing instructional strategies. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202, and 6 hours of credit in art history or permission of the department head.

title: The Exceptional Person and Art
description: Designed to investigate art for the exceptional person. Special emphasis given to the understanding of the unique contributions which art can make for the gifted, disadvantaged, physically handicapped, mentally retarded, and emotionally disturbed. Three weekly meetings plus an assigned time for teaching. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202 or permission of the department head.

title: Art for the Middle School/Junior High
description: An exploration of the methods of teaching art at the middle school/junior high age level. Laboratory experiences directing students in art awareness and art experiences. Three weekly meetings plus an assigned time for teaching junior high students. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202 or permission of the department head and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, an introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 202 and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Not open to the student who has credit in AED 303.

title: Independent Study in Art Education

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to representational drawing with an emphasis on developing observation, awareness of structure, technical facility, and familiarity with a variety of media. Not open to the student who has credit in AFA 100.

title: Perspective and Rendering
description: Designed to acquaint the student through lectures and problems with the principles of perspective, shades and shadows, together with a variety of graphic rendering techniques. Not open to the student who has credit in AFA 103.

Assignments are intended to lead the student to the solution of pictorial problems. In the advanced courses the student pursues independent investigation leading to a personal expression. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102; AFA 101. AFA 313 is not open to the student who has credit in AFA 213 and AFA 314 is not open to the student who has credit in AFA 214. 217, 218. Watercolor. (3) Basic exploration of the techniques and materials used in watercolor painting as they relate to problems in the various degree areas: advertising art, interior design, art teaching, painting, and architecture. The development of transparent and opaque watercolor techniques will be stressed. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102; AFA 101. Not open to the student who has credit in AFA 210.

title: Life Sculpture

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: A survey of the painting, sculpture, and architectural styles of the ancient Mediterranean peoples through the Gothic age of France and Germany.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: A continuation of AHS 101 starting with the creations and personalities of the Renaissance both in Italy and the North. The painting, sculpture, and architecture up to 1800 will be covered. Prerequisite: AHS 101.

title: Survey of Art History 3
description: The development of modern painting, architecture, and sculpture from the beginning of the 19th century to the present. Prerequisite: AHS 102.

title: History of Furniture
description: A sequential study of function and design as applied to furniture with emphasis on the contemporary period.

title: Art: An Introduction
description: Introduces the general education student to the areas of art: architecture, city planning, industrial design, the home, painting, sculpture, and related arts. It is academic in nature and presents the ideational and technical approach the artist takes in creative activity. Not open to students with areas in art.

title: Historical Interiors
description: Furnishings and interiors from antiquity to the Victorian period with primary emphasis on English and American design. Prerequisite: AHS 101, 102, and 103.

title: Contemporary Interiors
description: History of furnishings, designers, and interiors from the Victorian period to the present. Prerequisite: AHS 330.

title: Honors Colloquium in Art
description: A planned reading and discussion program dealing with the aesthetic problems of contemporary art. Prerequisite: open only to students on the Honors Program.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of the department head. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Aesthetics in the Visual Arts
description: Principles underlying twentieth century art products. Prerequisites: for art majors, 12 hours of credit in art history and appreciation; for other students, none.

title: Ancient Art
description: Focuses on the diverse styles of architecture, sculpture, and painting of three early civilizations; Egyptian, Greek, and Roman. Open to all students.

title: Medieval Art
description: Major Euorpean movements and personalities in architecture, painting, and sculpture from early Christian times through the Gothic period. Styles to be considered include early Christian, Byzantine, Romanesque, and Gothic. Open to all students.

title: Renaissance Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of the Early and High Renaissance in Italy and Northern Europe. Emphasis on the growth of the artistic heritage of the western world through the inventions and creations of Renaissance genius. Open to all students.

title: Mannerism, Baroque, and Rococo Art
description: Special emphasis on the works of the leading exponents of these styles in architecture, painting, and sculpture as they appeared in Italy, France, Germany, Spain, Flanders, Holland, and England. Open to all students.

title: Nineteenth Century Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture in Europe including the Palladian Revival through Symbolism and the forerunners of Cubism and Expressionism, Cezanne, and Munch. Other movements to be considered are Neo-Classicism, Romanticism, Realism, Pre-Raphaelites, and Impressionism. Open to all students.

title: Twentieth Century Art to 1945
description: European architecture, sculpture, and painting from 1900 to 1945. Special attention to the development of those styles leading to the contemporary art of the midcentury and later. Open to all students.

title: Art Since 1945
description: Deals with the major movements and personalities in twoand threedimensional art in the United States and Europe since 1945. Emphasis on an understanding of the conceptual problems, materials, techniques and their relationship to early twentieth century art. Open to all students.

title: History of Art in the United States

Department of Home Economics Smith, Chairperson; Adams, Carr, Caylor, Finn, Kim, Lacey, Miller, Nixon, Quesenberry, Rendina, Roepke, Spangler, Steele, Whitaker, Wittig Home economics is the field of knowledge and service that is fundamentally concerned with strengthening home and family life through educating the individuals for family living; improving the services and goods used by families; conducting research to discover the changing needs of individuals and families and to determine means of satisfying these needs; and furthering community, national, and world conditions favorable to family living. The profession of home economics synthesizes knowledge drawn from its own research from the physical, biological, and social sciences and the arts and applies this knowledge to improving the lives of families and individuals. The breadth of the field of home economics emphasizes its importance. The eleven separate, but interrelated, fields of foods, nutrition, clothing, textiles, applied art, housing, household equipment, home management, family economics, child development, and family relations provide the foundations for the good health, satisfying and successful living, psychological balance, and good management which are essential for the development of the whole personality. Needs of individuals and families in the social environment of their time are of primary concern in determining the emphases given to the various aspects of home economics. Home economics aids in helping individuals and families to make intelligent decisions concerning all aspects of family life, including the social, economic, aesthetic, managerial, health, and ethical aspects of relations, child development, foods, clothing, and housing. Home economics prepares professional personnel to carry out its objectives through education, research, social welfare and public health, dietetics, and institutional administration and business. It shares with other fields the responsibility for developing perceptive, wellinformed citizens with the ability and the initiative to further conditions favorable to effective living. title: Principles of Home Art
description: Design and color principles, with practical application to home situations. Open to all students except those who have credit in ADS 104.

title: Independent Study
description: Permits the student to select, investigate, and explore more intensively an area of home economics on an independent basis. Extensive reading and the development of research skill are emphasized. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Home Economics Field Studies
description: Designed to combine a background of reading knowledge with field experiences where students will have an opportunity to study special areas of home economics in a particular location. Open to all students with permission of the department chairman. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision f May be acquired prior to college entrance. CHEM 225 is waived as a prerequisite for the departmental major in dietetics. § BIO 112 is waived as a prerequisite for the departmental major in dietetics. in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the individual student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Family Life and Nutrition in Early Childhood Guidance
description: Helps leaders and workers in kindergarten or preschool community groups understand the sequential growth and development of young children and the interrelationship of family meal patterns to their physical, mental, emotional, social, and motor growth.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: The development of vocational education in which principles and philosophies of vocational education are related to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image. Prerequisite: junior standing.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Home Economics
description: Analysis of pupil needs and the development of a home economics program to meet these needs. Organization of teaching units, selection, and use of teaching methods, and development and use of devices for evaluating pupil growth. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Discipline oriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of home economics, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of home economics in the secondary school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: HED 395.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis will be placed on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395, and 399.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: A study of how to coordinate class instruction and work experience; includes selecting and recruiting students, selecting training stations, role of the coordinator, techniques of coordination, and placement and follow up of graduates. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395, 399, 492.

title: Meal Planning and Food Preparation
description: Designed for the non -home economics major. Basic principles of food buying, food preparation, and table service, along with the study of nutritive value of food. Foods and service for different social occasions. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 110.

title: Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods' of preparation stressed. Open to men and women.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Effects of different ingredients and/or methods on quality of products studied. Emphasis placed on recognition of a standard product and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve a standard product. Application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation stressed.

title: Meal Management
description: Principles and fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals, with emphasis on resource management and on the purchase and storage of food. Attention given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental principles in nutrition and application to diets for children and normal adults.

title: Menu Planning for Quantity Food Service
description: Principles of nutrition applied to feeding of individuals and groups. Major emphasis is placed on menu planning for institutions with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Limitations or problems relating to personnel, facilities, and type of patronage also stressed.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Stressed are the organization structure, application of principles of scientific management, and personnel administration. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning—Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping of food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industries and commercial operations. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Quantity Food Production and Purchasing
description: Offers opportunity for insight into factors related to quantity production and purchasing of foods. Experiences in actual laboratory situation in quantity food production kitchens on campus under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics 1
description: A study of the nutritive value of foods and the utilization of food in the human body. The nutritional needs of people throughout the life cycle will be investigated. Prerequisite: junior/senior level standing or a major in nursing, food management, or dietetics technology, or by permission of the department chairman.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Designed to acquaint the student with nutrition problems and nutrition programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Practical experience will include investigation, observation, and participation in nutrition programs in the local community. Prerequisite: HFN 340.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Principles of dietary modification needed by individuals with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: HFN 340. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 441.

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Laboratory experience in university food service units. Prerequisites: HFN 220 and 340.

title: Institutional Administration and Accounting
description: Problems pertaining to school lunchrooms, hospitals, and cafeterias as to personnel, management and organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens.

title: Institutional Equipment, Buying, and Layout
description: Stationary and small food equipment considered. Layouts of institutional kitchens planned. Field trips to institutional kitchens and equipment companies.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of the different foodstuffs so that their composition and physical and chemical properties can be understood. Recipes are investigated and methods of combining foods are developed and evaluated. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics 2
description: Advanced course in nutrition emphasizing the utilization of metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Current research in the field of nutrition will be included. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and CHEM 231.

title: Diet in Disease
description: Pathological conditions resulting from various nutritional diseases, with emphasis upon causes and effects of malnutrition and its treatment. Planning and preparation of diets for abnormal conditions. Hospital laboratory experience provided. Prerequisite: HFN 440.

title: Seminar in Dietetics
description: The professions involved in food service and dietetics ; the roles and responsibilities of personnel and their relationships with other professionals ; the standards to be attained; the code of professional ethics and the resources for continuing professional education. Prerequisite: 2 hours of credit in HE 498 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Maternal and Infant Nutrition
description: Information about maternal, prenatal, and infant (birth to 36 months) nutrition ; nutritional requirements of expectant mothers and infants investigated. Emphasis is placed on readings in current periodicals. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Child Nutrition
description: Principles of child nutrition (preschool through adolescence); nutritional requirements of children and problems in nutrition will be investigated. Current professional periodicals will be researched. Prerequisite: junior standing, HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Geriatric Nutrition
description: Nutritional needs of older adults will be discussed based upon physiological and social changes and research in the field. Students will review some recent literature in the field, evaluate the food intakes of elderly citizens in certain situations, and study and evaluate nutrition programs designed for older adults in terms of meeting nutritional needs. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers; important considerations in purchasing foods and corresponding factors that determine them. Emphasis on ethics in buying.

title: Home Care of the Sick
description: Includes concepts which affect the quality of life of individuals and families in prevention of illness, current major health problems and their costs, and procedures to follow when illness occurs.

title: Parent-Infant Development
description: Growth and development during first two years. Emphasizes practical aspects of infant caregiving and resources and information for developing confidence and competence in parenting. Limited to parents with infants under one year and those expecting baby in 8 months or less. Parents bring infants to class.

title: Child Development
description: Emphasis on the preschool child as a member of a family group. Includes principles of natural growth and development and child guidance based on the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual needs of the preschool child. Students will participate and observe in various early childhood programs and centers. Open to all students.

title: Infant Development
description: Processes of growth and development during the first two years with various physical, social, and emotional aspects being emphasized. Open to all students.

title: Marriage
description: The dynamics of the marital relationship, the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasis is focused on the following: the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection and singlehood, marital communication, sexual adjustment in marriage, marriage adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasis is placed on marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment.

title: Assisting with Family Problems
description: The major areas of adjustment in marriage and family relationships, problems of adjustment and philosophy and practice of techniques for clientcentered assistance with family problems.

title: Family Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, art qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects for home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 1
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Emphasis on the management problems encountered by newly married couples in establishing a home. Open to all students.

title: Household Equipment
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Students will have an opportunity to plan, organize, and present demonstrations on household equipment.

title: Home Management 2
description: Residence in the home management house offers opportunity to make practical application of the principles of homemaking. Prerequisite: HFN 220.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing for the consumer, including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, and factors to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Clothing Construction for Non-Majors
description: Fundamental techniques applied in the construction and fitting of simple garments. Not open to the student who has credit in HTC 104.

title: Introduction to Clothing
description: Provides basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, the apparel industry, and social psychological aspects of clothing.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Learn creative skills in stitchery by embellishing existing fabrics or originating new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, simple weaving, tie dyeing, stenciling, batik, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, needlepoint, rya braided and hooked rugs. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HTC 104 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Motivations of Fashion
description: A history of costume from its earliest beginnings to the present. The emphasis will be on the motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adaptation of standard patterns to individual porportions, designing of garments and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Prerequisite: HTC 104 and 203.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Textile Testing
description: Experience in planning and conducting textile tests and in evaluating resulting data; development, present status, and importance of textile testing. Prerequisite: HTC 330 or ADS 222.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: The business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, promotion, and the consumer. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Clothing Problems
description: Special problems to meet students' needs in clothing construction. Includes units in machine attachments and adjustments, draperies, career projects, problem fabrics. Prerequisite: HTC 104. title: Introduction to Industrial Materials
description: An introductory study of three major types of industrial materials: metallic, polymeric, and ceramic. Characteristics of various materials are identified, studied, contrasted, and compared. Laboratory activities involve conducting tests on materials.

title: Introduction to the Construction Industry
description: A focus on the broad range of processes utilized in the construction industry. Students learn about and engage in activities related to managing, designing, building, and maintaining structures.

title: Industry in Contemporary Society
description: An introduction to and an understanding of our complex industrial and technological society with emphasis on modern industrial organization, materials, processes, and related socioeconomic factors, including the development of manufacturing processes from crafts to automation. Laboratory experiences of a groupproblem type developed around typical industrial processes. Open to all students except those with teaching areas in industrial education.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: Manufacturing processes used by industries to convert raw materials into consumer products.

title: Characteristics of Industrial Materials
description: Experimental analysis of the mechnical properties of industrial materials. Laboratory experiences involve research and experimentation. Manufacturing

Laboratory activities emphasize developing, producing, and marketing student selected products. Major emphasis on laboratory activities. Open only to students with a teaching major in industrial education. Prerequisite: IED 150, 151, 156.

title: Industrial Product Research and Development
description: Focuses on the industrial activities of research, development, and product engineering as it relates to manufacturing enterprises. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with product research and development. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263 and 105 or 256.

title: American Industry Practicum
description: Advanced study of the American industrial complex with emphasis on designing and developing teaching materials and activities appropriate to class goals. Activities will be predominately studentidentified problems or research. Prerequisite: IED 263.

title: Developing Production Systems
description: Focuses on the activities associated with the design and installation of industrial production methods and facilities. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with developing a production system. Major emphasis On laboratory experiences. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263, 150 or 162.

title: Building Construction Projects

title: World of Construction

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to metals with concentration in foundry, sheet metal, bench metal, art metal, forging, and spinning. Emphasis will also be placed on safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures.

title: I Industrial Processing of Metals
description: A study of the basic industrial processes used in manufacturing metal products. Laboratory activities will be used to provide concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151.

title: Metal Forming and Assembly Practices
description: Sheet metal, wrought metal, forging, and assembly processes. Classroom and laboratory activities in safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures will be used to provide conceptual and concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 or 162 or permission of the department chairman. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 231.

title: Metals Machining
description: Work with the lathe, shaper, milling machines, surface grinder, metal cutting saws, and electrical discharge machine to develop a basic understanding of metal removal. Work involves the fundamentals of metallurgy and heat treating of carbon steels. Safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures will also be emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250.

title: Casting and Bonding Metal
description: Includes theory and techniques in welding a variety of welds in the flat position with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Limited work is done with TIG and MIG welding equipment. An introduction to the fundamentals of pattern design, permanent mold design, core design, and foundry techniques which provides a basic understanding of foundry practices. Emphasis placed on safety and maintenance. Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250.

title: Advanced Metals Machining
description: Work includes cylindrical grinding, advanced milling machine work, electrical discharge machining, tool design and grinding, metallurgy and materials testing. Emphasis is directed toward mathematics and science as it relates to machine setups and tool design. Setups relating to industrial production are discussed. Prerequisite : IED 3.

title: Problems in Sheet Metal and Machine Shop

title: Problems in Hot Metals

Advanced welding will include horizontal, vertical, and overhead welding techniques with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Inert gas welding theory and techniques will be studied in depth. Will also include the fundamentals of forging practices. Prerequisite: IED 334.

title: Problems in Metals
description: Individualized, advanced study, and experimentation in one or more of the following: characteristics of metals, casting, separating, forming, conditioning, assembly, and/or finishing. Prerequisite: IED 333 or 250. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 434 or 435. Industrial Plastics

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: A study of the basic industrial plastics processes and materials. Injection, extrusion, blow and compression molding, and thermoforming. Laboratory activities for all processes included.

title: Industrial Plastics: Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problemsolving approach. The construction of molds and dies for injection, rotational and blow molding, extruding and/or thermoforming are studied. Fiberglass and foam molds may also be made. Appropriate moldmaking techniques and equipment are demonstrated. Prerequisite: IED 125 or 253. 253. § Industrial Processing of Plastics. (3) History, growth, organization, and future of the plastics (synthetic polymer) industry. Molding, forming, casting, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing techniques common to the plastics industry will be studied. Laboratory activities provide experiences with most processes and many materials. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 125.

title: Advanced Industrial Plastics Technology
description: Advanced techniques in plastics processing. Use of automatic molding equipment, molds, and engineering plastics. Mass production techniques will be employed. Prerequisite: IED 225.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. Mold making, materials testing and/or equipment design possible. Prerequisite:

title: Introduction to Woods
description: A basic course in wood processing for individuals interested in consumer information related to woods products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for student designed product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 251, 316, 317. 251. § Industrial Processing of Wood. (3) A broad study of the methods used to process the natural polymer, wood, including forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing. Laboratory activities are directed toward helping students acquire basic understanding and skills related to wood processing, and the careers in the area. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 213 and 316.

title: Industrial Furniture and Cabinet Production
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Advanced Wood Processing
description: Involves units of study in modifying wood materials, bentwood laminations, and wood finishing. Additional opportunities provided for individual problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in wood processing particularly in the areas where the student lacks confidence and experience. Individual problemsolving emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 316. COMMUNICATION Introductory

title: Introduction to Industrial Communication
description: A focus on the elements common to industrial communication. Classroom and laboratory activities are related to the design, production, and distribution of printed graphic, photographic, electronic, and technical graphic communications.

title: Industrial Design
description: A study of major factors involved in creating an appealing design which can be manufactured economically. Topics include the design process, sketching, creativity, elements and principles of design, materials and processes, and human and environmental factors. Graphic Arts (Printed Graphic and Photographic) 254. § Printed Graphic Communication. (4) A study of printed graphic communications with major emphasis on design and developing messages, preparing messages for production, and producing messages using lithographic, relief, intaglio, and screen processes. Prerequisite: IED 154. 255. § Photographic Communications in Industry. (3) Designed to familiarize students with the applications of photography to industrial communications. Students will study basic techniques, equipment, processes, and materials utilized by contemporary industry in communication. Prerequisite: IED 154.

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: Introductory experiences in the various methods used by the graphic arts industry. These include letterpress and offset printing, drypoint and block etchings, silkscreen printing, embossing and gold leaf printing, marking devices, and bookbinding.

title: Letterpress Printing and Bookbinding
description: Fundamental letterpress theory is stressed, with experiences in layout, composition, imposition, presswork and bookbinding; single and twocolor platen presswork; and looseleaf and saddlestitch binding operations. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Photography
description: Fundamentals of photography, including camera work, black and white film processing, enlarging, composition, and basic color photography.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Fundamental theory, exposure techniques, film processing, printmaking, and composition considerations in color photography. Students must provide their own cameras. Prerequisite: IED 386.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Principles and experiences involved in lithography as a printing process. Cold type composition, camera work, stripping, plate processing, and press work; line shots and halftones. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Problems in Printed Graphics
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281. Technical Graphics

title: Introduction to Graphics
description: Various graphical representation and problem solving techniques and their application to the design process. Included are the theory of orthographic projection, sketching, lettering, geometric constructions, section views, English and metric dimensioning, fasteners, and working drawings. Problem solving includes experiences with elementary descriptive geometry topics. Elementary design problems are included.

title: Introduction to Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing basic production drawings. Topics include lettering, sketching, geometric construction, design process, isometric drawing, orthographic multiview projection, sectional views, dimensions, fasteners, and working drawings. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 103.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing productionrelated drawings in selected specialized areas. Topics include auxiliary views, revolutions, cams, gears, bearings, machine components, welding drawing, structural drawing, piping drawing, and electrical drawing. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Advanced Technical Graphics
description: Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection ; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; and lateral developments of geometric solids. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256. § Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education.

title: Manufacturing Design
description: Focuses on the process of design and principles'of drafting as applied to manufacturing industry. Included are product and tool design. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256. 256. § Technical Graphics Communications. (4) A study of the various graphical methods used to transmit technical ideas and information in industry. title: Residential Drafting and Design
description: Included is a survey of basic principles of residential planning and designing; methods of construction; and preparation of preliminary design sketches, perspective drawings, models, and selected working drawings.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Computer Graphics in Drafting and Design
description: A study of methods used to make technical drawings and other graphical representations by employing the computer and computerrelated devices. Use of the graphics display terminal and plotter is emphasized in Problem solving activities. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105.

title: Problems in Technical Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in technical graphic areas based on the needs of the student and the approval of the instructor. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256. Electronics 257. § Industrial Electronic Communication Systems. (2) Electronics as it is used in the field of industrial communication.
