Course descriptions are listed in regular numerical order under the prefixes General Industrial Studies (GIS), Industrial Education (IED), and Industrial Technology (ITE).

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance, to make simple modifications and installations in the areas of plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climate control systems of the home.

title: Introduction to Graphics
description: Various graphical representation and problem solving techniques and their application to the design process. Included are the theory of orthographic projection, sketching, lettering, geometric constructions, section views, English and metric dimensioning, fasteners, and working drawings. Problem solving includes experiences with elementary descriptive geometry topics. Elementary design problems are included.

title: Introduction to Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing basic production drawings. Topics include lettering, sketching, geometric construction, design process, isometric drawing, orthographic multiview projection, sectional views, dimensions, fasteners, and working drawings. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 103.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing productionrelated drawings in selected specialized areas. Topics include auxiliary views, revolutions, cams, gears, bearings, machine components, welding drawing, structural drawing, piping drawing, and electrical drawing. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or equivalent.

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: A study of the basic industrial plastics processes and materials. Injection, extrusion, blow and compression molding, and thermoforming. Laboratory activities for all processes included.

title: Introduction to Power and Transportation
description: Concentration on the internal combustion engine. A study of power sources, basic mechanisms, component systems, efficiencies and power measurement, and the utilization and application to transportation and industry, and direct energy converters.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Processes
description: A focus on the six processes as they are used to provide form utility to metallic, polymeric, and ceramic materials. Classroom and laboratory activities are designed to provide a conceptual understanding of each process.

title: Introduction to Industrial Materials
description: An introductory study of three major types of industrial materials: metallic, polymeric, and ceramic. Characteristics of various materials are identified, studied, contrasted, and compared. Laboratory activities involve conducting tests on materials.

title: Introduction to the Construction Industry
description: A focus on the broad range of processes utilized in the construction industry. Students learn about and engage in activities related to managing, designing, building, and maintaining structures.

title: Introduction to Industrial Communication
description: A focus on the elements common to industrial communication. Classroom and laboratory activities are related to the design, production, and distribution of printed graphic, photographic, electronic, and technical graphic communications.

title: Industrial Design
description: A study of major factors involved in creating an appealing design which can be manufactured economically. Topics include the design process, sketching, creativity, elements and principles of design, materials and processes, and human and environmental factors.

title: Introduction to Power
description: An overview of the development and utilization of power in terms of energy, energy conversion, transmission, control, and applications, with continual concern for energy conservation and environmental quality.

title: Industry in Contemporary Society
description: An introduction to and an understanding of our complex industrial and technological society with emphasis on modern industrial organization, materials, processes, and related socioeconomic factors, including the development of manufacturing processes from crafts to automation. Laboratory experiences of a groupproblem type developed around typical industrial processes. Open to all students except those with teaching areas in industrial education.

title: Introduction to Electricity
description: Introductory experiences and exploration in the broad field of electricity with special emphasis upon means of producing and transmitting electron flow. Instruction in appropriate electrical projects and familiarization with electrical measuring instruments are important experiences.

title: Exploring Industrial Education
description: Focuses on teaching industrial education as a career. Students learn about the development and types of industrial education programs offered in public schools and the undergraduate industrial teacher education program at Ball State University.

title: Advanced Technical Graphics
description: Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; and lateral developments of geometric solids. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256.

title: Manufacturing Design
description: Focuses on the process of design and principles of drafting as applied to manufacturing industry. Included are product and tool design. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256.

title: Introduction to Woods
description: A basic course in wood processing for individuals interested in consumer information related to wood products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for studentdesigned product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 251, 316, 317.

title: Industrial Plastics: Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problemsolving approach. The construction of molds and dies for injection, rotational and blow molding, extruding and/or thermoforming are studied. Fiberglass and foam molds may also be made. Appropriate moldmaking techniques and equipment are demonstrated. Prerequisite: IED 125 or 253.

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to metals with concentration in foundry, sheet metal, bench metal, art metal, forging, and spinning. Emphasis will also be placed on safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: To acquire fundamental skills and teaching knowledge through experience related to power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasis on internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Factors involved in setting up a transportation unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite: IED 140 or 259. 2504 Industrial Processing of Metals. (4) A study of the basic industrial processes used in manufacturing metal products. The processes of casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing will be studied, contrasted, and compared to provide a conceptual understanding of each. Laboratory activities will be used to provide concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. 2 51.$ Industrial Processing of Wood. (3) A broad study of the methods used to process the natural polymer, wood, including forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing. Laboratory activities are directed toward helping students acquire basic understanding and skills related to wood processing, and the careers in the area. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 213 and 316.

title: Industrial Processing of Ceramics
description: A study of ceramic materials as components in industrial production processes such as casting, separating, forming, conditioning, assembly, and finishing will be examined. Prerequisite: IED 150. 253.T Industrial Processing of Plastics. (3) History, growth, organization, and future of the plastics (synthetic polymer) industry. Molding, forming, casting, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing techniques common to the plastics industry will be studied. Laboratory activities provide experiences with most processes and many materials. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 125. 254.$ Printed Graphic Communication. (4) A study of printed graphic communications with major emphasis on design and developing messages, preparing messages for production, and producing messages using lithographic, relief, intaglio, and screen processes. Prerequisite: IED 154. 255.$ Photographic Communications in Industry. (3) Designed to familiarize students with the applications of photography to industrial communications. Students will study basic techniques, equipment, processes, and materials utilized by contemporary industry in communication. Prerequisite: IED 154. 2564 Technical Graphics Communications. (4) A study of the various graphical methods used to transmit technical ideas and information in industry. Included are sketching, pictorials, orthographies for manufacturing and construction, charts and graphs, reprographics, and industrial practices. Prerequisite: IED 154. 2574 Industrial Electronic Communication Systems. (2) Electronics as it is used in the field of industrial communication. Students will learn about principles, components, and operation of industrial communications systems and will develop skill in operating some electronic test equipment. Prerequisite: IED 154. 2584 Industrial Electrical Power. (4) The conversion, transmission, and control of electrical power with an emphasis on developing knowledge and skill in control and utilization circuitry. A companion course to IED 259. Prerequisite: IED 158. 2594 Mechanical and Fluid Power. (4) Energy conversion, transmission, and control within the mechanical and fluid power parameters. A companion course to IED 258. Prerequisite: IED 158.

title: Introduction to American Industry
description: Organization and management in American industry with emphasis on teaching the content in public school industrial arts programs. Laboratory activities emphasize developing, producing, and marketing studentselected products. Major emphasis on laboratory activities. Open only to students with a teaching major in industrial education. Prerequisite: IED 150, 151, 156.

title: Computer Fundamentals
description: Theory and basic circuits of computers: ,Laboratory activity will consist of group construction of basic computer circuits.

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: Introductory experiences in the various methods used by the graphic arts industry. These include letterpress and offset printing, drypoint and block etchings, silkscreen printing, embossing and gold leaf printing, marking devices, and bookbinding.

title: Student Organizations Practicum
description: A practicum in the organization, maintenance, and evaluation of student vocational organizations. A total of 4 quarter hours must be taken by persons seeking certification as a teacher of vocational trade, industrial and technical laboratory programs, and an endorsement as a cooperative coordinator. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: An introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Legislation will be analyzed in light of past and present issues of vocational education and its relationship as a vital component of the total educational system.

title: Curriculum Development in Industrial Education
description: Designed to provide prospective industrial education teachers with the tools for rational decision making relative to curriculum development for industrial education programs. The emphasis is on developing an adequate conceptual framework within which to design courses. Prerequisite: IED 198. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 394. T. Prerequisite waived for students other than those with areas in industrial education.

title: Residential Drafting and Design
description: Included is a survey of basic principles of residential planning and designing; methods of construction; and preparation of preliminary desi gn sketches, perspective drawings, models, and selected working drawings.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Computer Graphics in Drafting and Design
description: A study of methods used to make technical drawings and other graphical representations by employing the computer and computerrelated devices. Use of the graphics display terminal and plotter is emphasized in problem solving activities. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256 or ITE 300.

title: Construction Utility Systems
description: The design, installation, operation, and maintenance of heating, air conditioning, ventilating, electrical, plumbing, and communication systems in construction projects. Emphasis on installation. Prerequisite: IED 152.

title: Building Construction Projects
description: Emphasis on the skills, materials, equipment, processes, and careers associated with the construction industry. Course activities involve the building of onsite construction projects within the community. Prerequisite: IED 152.

title: Industrial Furniture and Cabinet Production
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Advanced Wood Processing
description: Involves units of study in modifying wood materials, bentwood laminations, and wood finishing. Additional opportunities provided for individual problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Advanced Industrial Plastics Technology
description: Advanced techniques in plastics processing. Use of automatic molding equipment, molds, and engineering plastics. Mass production techniques will be employed. Prerequisite: IED 225.

title: Advanced Industrial Ceramics Technology
description: Industrial techniques in ceramic processing and production with emphasis on compression, injection and extrusion molding, and glazing. Prerequisite: IED 252.

title: Industrial Ceramics: Product Design and Mold Making
description: Individual and group problemsolving approach. Production forming processes, clay and glazing compounding, glazing, and kiln operation. Prerequisite: IED 127 or 252.

title: Metal Forming and Assembly Practices
description: Sheet metal, wrought metal, forging, and assembly processes. Classroom and laboratory activities in safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures will be used to provide conceptual and concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 or ITE 162 or permission of the department chairman. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 231.

title: Metal Machining
description: Focuses on metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling machines, grinding machines, bandsawing and EDM to develop understanding of each process. Discussions include tool design, precision measuring, basic NC, fundamentals of metallurgy and heat treating, and safety. Four hours of lecture and approximately 4 hours of laboratory per week. Safety glasses required. Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250 or ITE 330.

title: Casting and Bonding Metal
description: Theory and techniques in flat position welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work done with TIG and MIG. Various casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques are studied. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory per week. Safety glasses required. Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250 or ITE 330.

title: Advanced Automechanics
description: The maintenance, repair, and theory underlying power train and power transmission units, air conditioning systems, emission control systems, and compression ignition engines. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Applications of Power to Air Transportation
description: Airframe and aircraft engine systems involving limited maintenance experience in engine systems; instrumentation, principles of aerodynamics and flight control; internal reaction engines, and atmospheric effects on power output and navigation. Prerequisite: IED 240 or 259.

title: Application of Power to Water Transportation
description: Small boats, outboard engines, principles of operation, components systems, with particular attention to charging circuits, maintenance, boating laws and safety, inland waterways navigation, propeller theory, boat hulls, performance, and sailing. Prerequisite: IED 240 or 259. 344, Private Pilot Ground Training. (4) Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to individuals currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Safety
description: Provides an awareness of the regulations governing health and safety and the methods and practices used in industry in general and industrial education specifically to com ply with these regulations. Designed primarily for students choosing concentration , areas in the Department of Industrial Education and Technology.

title: Industrial Product Research and Development
description: Focuses on the industrial activities of research, development, and product engineering as it relates to manufacturing enterprises. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with product research and development. F our hours of lecture and approximately 4 hours of laboratory per week. Safety glasses required. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263, and 105 or 256 or ITE 300.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes which provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units are examined and evaluated.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Industrial Arts
description: A classroom involvement experience for industrial arts majors in the elementary school. To familiarize the student with the philosophy, history, and principles of industrial arts in the elementary school. Affords the student the opportunity to teach a short unit of instruction in cooperation with an elementary teacher to elementary age children in the local community. Prerequisite: industrial arts major or permission of the department head.

title: Applications of Electricity
description: Fundamental electrical theory, with special reference to applications in heating, lighting, electrolysis, electrical communication, and mechanical power. Individual and group experiences through the use of experiments and construction of appropriate projects. Prerequisite: IED 171 or 258.

title: Servicing Electrical Appliances and Motors
description: Fundamental theory and application of motors and appliance circuitry. Four hours of lecture and approximately 4 hours of laboratory per week. Prerequisite: IED 258 or 370 or ITE 270.

title: Letterpress Printing and Bookbinding
description: Fundamental letterpress theory is stressed, with experiences in layout, composition, imposition, presswork, and bookbinding; single and twocolor platen presswork; and looseleaf and saddlestitch binding operations. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Photography
description: A basic course in black and white photography focusing on camera handling, film exposure and processing, printmaking, basic photographic composition, and print finishing processes. Related areas covered include introduction to color photography, applications of photography, types of photographic equipment, and information related to careers in photography. Four hours of lecture and approximately 4 hours of laboratory per week.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Fundamental theory, exposure techniques, film processing, printmaking, and composition considerations in color photography. Students must provide their own cameras. Prerequisite: IED 386.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by a breakdown into components of jobs, tasks, and processes will be examined.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs are examined and evaluated.

title: Curriculum Problems in Industrial Education
description: Criteria used in determining nature and content of learning experiences in industrial education classes. Teacherpupil planning, group activities, and problemsolving methods. Textbooks and related industrial and government publications evaluated and course outlines developed. Prerequisite: a minimum of 12 quarter hours from the following courses: IED 103, 125, 140, 171, 213, 231, 252, or 281.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Industrial Education
description: Problems of organization and management related to industrial education learning activities. Objectives, terminology, evaluation methods, teaching devices, lesson plans, textbooks, equipment, and supplies are examined. Industrial education classes in public schools are observed. Prerequisite: IED 198 and 298 and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Education
description: Practice in various contemporary approaches to industrial education drawn from methods and curriculum problems courses. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in one or more of the contemporary approaches to industrial education, preferably a public school. Prerequisite: IED 198, 298, and 395.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Disciplineoriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of industrial education evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of industrial education in the secondary school curriculum (grades 5 through 12). Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: IED 298 and 395.

title: Problems in Technical Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in technical graphic areas based on the needs of the student and the approval of the instructor. Prerequisite: IED 103 or 105 or 256.

title: Problems in Computer Graphics
description: Advanced study in computer graphics as it applies to design and drafting. Emphasis on writing interactive programs. Prerequisite: IED 308.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in wood processing particularly i n g the ar eas where student lacks confidence and experience. Individual problemsolvin emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: World of Construction
description: A study of the Industrial Arts Curriculum Project's -World of Construction" course. Centers on planning, organizing, and controlling people and resources to produce constructed products.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. Mold making, materials testing and/or equipment design possible. Prerequisite: IED 325. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Research and Development in Industrial Ceramics
description: Extensive independent and group study and experimentatiion in the area of industrial ceramics. Prerequisite: IED 328.

title: Advanced Metals Machining
description: Work includes cylindrical grinding, advanced milling machine work, electrical discharge machining, tool design and grinding, metallurgy, and materials testing. Emphasis is directed toward mathematics and science as they relate to machine setups and tool design. Setups relating to industrial production are discussed. Prerequisite: IED 333.

title: Problems in Sheet Metal and Machine Shop
description: Specialization in the theory and practice of sheet metal work, machine work, precision measurement, metal testing and inspection, and metallurgy. Prerequisite: IED 333 or 433.

title: Problems in Hot Metals
description: Specialization in advanced casting theory and techniques. Advanced welding will include horizontal, vertical, and overhead welding techniques with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Inert gas welding theory and techniques will be studied in depth. Will also include the fundamentals of forging practices. Prerequisite: IED 334.

title: Problems in Metals
description: Individualized, advanced study and experimentation in one or more of the following: characteristics of metals, casting, separating, forming, conditioning, assembly, and/or finishing. Laboratory: dictated by nature of study. Safety glasses required. Prerequisite: IED 250 or ITE 330. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Problems in Hydraulics
description: An introduction to the fundamental principles of hydraulic circuitry. Characteristics of hydraulics, the functioning of component parts of hydraulic systems, and the application to power transmission and control.

title: Special Problems in Pneumatics
description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of pneumatic circuitry. Included is a study of the characteristics of fluids, the functioning of components, and the development of pneumatic circuits and pneumatic logic control.

title: American Industry Practicum
description: Advanced study of the American industrial complex with emphasis on designing and developing teaching materials and activities appropriate to class goals. Activities will be predominately studentidentified problems or research. Prerequisite: IED 263.

title: Developing Production Systems
description: Focuses on the activities associated with the design and installation of industrial production methods and facilities. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with developing a production system. Major emphasis on laboratory experiences. Four hours of lecture and approximately 4 hours of laboratory per week. Safety glasses required. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263, 150 or ITE 162.

title: Advanced Industrial Arts for Elementary Teachers
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of a wide variety of tools, materials, and industrial processes through the planning and organization of group activity units. Prerequisite: IED 364 or permission of the department head.

title: World of Manufacturing
description: A study of the Industrial Arts Curriculum Project's -World of Manufacturing" course. Class activities are centered around actual teaching of the units included in the IACP course.

title: Manual Arts Therapy Clinical Training
description: A field assignment with opportunities to work with qualified manual arts therapists at the Veterans' Administration Hospital in Marion, Indiana. Credit for 10 hours is awarded for minimum of 8 weeks fulltime training. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299 and IED 395.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Theory of the vacuum tube and semiconductors, with special reference to their application in radio, television, and electronic circuits in industry. Individual and group experiences in project activity of the experimental, maintenance, and creative types. Prerequisite: IED 257 or 370.

title: Problems in Industrial Electronics
description: Special individual and group problems in advanced electrical circuitry involving most of the components of electrical circuits, with special emphasis upon thermionic emission tubes and photo emission devices. Complex problems assigned to groups of students will characterize the project activity. Prerequisite: IED 257 or 370.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Principles and experiences involved in lithography as a printing process. Cold type composition, camera work, stripping, plate processing, and press work; line shots and halftones. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Problems in Printed Graphics
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisite: IED 254 or 281.

title: Independent Studies in Industrial Education
description: Special investigation in industrial education on an independent basis. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques and skills are emphasized. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis is placed upon state functions.

title: Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Individual and group studies of one or more major problems in the industrial education field, application of research techniques to the problems for solution, and reporting of findings.

title: Advanced Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Advanced study of problemsolving techniques in industrial education. Individual and group activities involving research and experimentation.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: An introduction to and a conceptual understanding of manufacturing processes used by industry to convert raw materials into consumer products. Four hours of lecture and approximately two hours of laboratory each week. Safety glasses required. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 150.

title: Theory and Practice in Letterpress Printing
description: Fundamentals of typography, handand powerfed presswork, basic bookbinding, and press maintenance and safety, while maintaining a production printing schedule.

title: Theory and Practice in Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Offset photolithographic experience covering the practice of camera operation, stripping, plate making, and offset press operation, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 181.

title: Theory and Practice in Commercial Printing
description: Use of the Frankline Price Catalog for letterpress and offset printing, paper schedules, postal rates, study of the Government Printing Office style book, and standard printing forms and correct terminology, while maintaining a production printing schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 182.

title: Quality Control in the Printing Industry
description: The ability to use the tools of quality control in the printing industry. Emphasis is given to the use of densitometry, correct register, proofreading, ink coverage, proper binding, cropping, paper and ink. Various other topics are considered.

title: Printing Estimating
description: Application of the Point System of Measurement; figuring the amount and cost of composition; basic size, thickness, and weight of paper stock; figuring and cutting paper stock; spoilage allowances; and figuring the cost of paper stock.

title: Internship in Printing Technology
description: A fiveweek internship in a printing industry, working under industrial standards and regulations in the type of printing industry preferred by the student, as much as possible. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Characteristics of Industrial Materials
description: Focuses on providing a broad understanding of the mechanical properties of industrial materials as they relate to processing and application. Research and experimentation are conducted through laboratory experiences by performing standardized tests. Four hours of lecture and approximately 2 hours of laboratory work each week. Safety glasses required. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 151.

title: Introduction to Industrial Electricity and Electronics
description: A study of the fundamentals of electricity and electronics. Included are theory, power sources, instrumentation, applications, and employment opportunities. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 370.

title: Theory and Practice in Publications
description: Various publication formats that are commonl y used by institutions and industries. Both ofset leterpres forms of makeup wil bemployed in maintaining publication schedules. Prerequisite: ITE 183.

title: Theory and Practice in Estimating and Copyfitting
description: Participants will estimate costs, order appropriate stock, learn schedules, make layouts, compose forms, cut the stock, estimate waste, and other details in completely planning and executing a printing order on a previousl y made schedule. Prerequisite: ITE 281.

title: Theory and Practice in Color Printing and Process Work
description: Printing of letterpress and offset color work, involving technical procedures in color separation and the use of densitomete r and the use of various kinds printing plates for leterpres color work. The completion of the secondyear creative project is a requirement. Prerequisite: ITE 282.

title: Color Process Printing
description: The photographic steps in making plates for photomechanic al printing of color pictures. Both color reflection and color transparency copy are considered. Prerequisite: ITE 186.

title: Type Design and Copyfitting
description: The determination of the amount of area necessary for composition according to size and family of type by use of a slide rule. The study of modern type design and usage, as well as outstanding typographers and their contributions. The place of the advertising agency in modern display composition and its contributions. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Organized and orderly methods of planning production to gain more profit, sales, production, and work. Prerequisite: ITE 284.

title: Blueprint Reading for the Manufacturing Industries
description: Emphasis placed on reading and interpreting detail drawings, assembly drawings, schematics, and numerical control documentation used in the manufacturing industries.

title: Fundamentals of Metals Processing
description: Metal manufacturing processes used in making metal products. The characteristics of casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing will be studied to provide a conceptual understanding of each major processing technique. Product applications and design factors will be studied to determine how they relate to process selection constraints and tradeoffs that are frequently necessary in manufacturing. Approximately 4 hours per week of activities will be used to provide actual experiences. Students will provide their own safety glasses. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 250.

title: Introduction to Fluid Power
description: Fundamental theory of fluids, fluid conditioning, components, symbology, and basic circuitry. Four hours of lecture and approximately 2 hours of laboratory work each week. Safety glasses required. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 444 or 445.

title: Industrial Internship
description: Designed to provide the trainee actual work experience in industry which is related to the objectives of the curriculum. The trainee is supervised by the university coordinator and the plant manager. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned, but not more than 4 hours may be earned at one time.

title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Manufacturing
description: The basic principles of computer numerical control, computeraided process planning, robotics, and other computeraided manufacturing systems. Prerequisite: CS 200 or IED 308 and ITE 270, 300, and 330.

title: Screen Printing
description: A basic course designed to provide a comprehensive overview of the screen printing process with emphasis on theory, materials, equipment, and techniques of printing by the screen process as found in contemporary graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITE 181, 182, or IED 281.

title: Training and Development in Industry
description: The activities of training and development in industry and their relationship to the job and the organization. Skills needed to systematically plan, implement, evaluate, and revise training and development programs are emphasized. Opportunities for practical application and practice are provided.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: A discussioncentered course that relates primarily to the process of identifying, seeking, and obtaining employment in industry. Open only to industrial technology majors. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Printing Management
description: Business facts needed for profitable management of a printing or lithographic business and the procedures to supply these facts accurately, promptly, and with laborsaving shortcuts. Prerequisite: ITE 289.

title: Industrial Internship
description: The student will work full time for one quarter in a position involving the supervision of production employees in a printing industry under supervision of the Department of Industrial Education and Technology. Prerequisite: ITE 484. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. Library Science 153 Department of Library Science Cox, Chairman; Beilke, Holzberlein, Hsu, Kennedy, Kirby, Rike, Tevis, yearn ans The Department of Library Science offers four educational programs at the undergraduate level. Course offerings may be applied (1) to gaining background and enrichment in liberal arts education, (2) to developing communications and production skill competencies needed for success in coping with life or career goals, (3) to learning or extending competencies in using information and libraries effectively, or (4) to preparing for a career in librarianship, information management, or information and audiovisual technology. Electives which apply to liberal education should be carefully selected by reading course descriptions and seeking further information from advisers in and outside the department. Electives which may apply to other majors and minors should be selected with advice from both departments. The teaching majors, minors, and endorsements and Associate of Arts degree requirements are based on requirements geared to approved programs for teaching certification and vocational technologies. The program leading to School Media Services certification prepares one to serve in school libraries and media centers as a school faculty member with full responsibility for directing all of the school library/media programs or as a member of the media center faculty in a school building or district. School library and media services personnel play significant roles as educators and must be well qualified in curricular planning and supportive services in addition to possessing the skills required of librarians in media management and design. Persons interested in professions in the field of library and information science should consider completing professional programs at the undergraduate level along with majors in the humanities and sciences and pursuit of an MLS degree after completion of a baccalaureate. There are many challenging and rewarding opportunities in library science and related professions for wellqualified persons. Any student considering library science courses or programs should arrange for a conference with the chairman or a designated faculty adviser in the Department of Library Science. Students should also request printed descriptions of course and program offerings for further details. Studies in library science are changing rapidly and new sources of information will be prepared frequently. Such changes may bring about changes in courses and programs at Ball State University and other institutions. Interaction of students and staff in the department and student participation in librarysponsored events and exhibits help students to become aware of the important role which library science may play in the intellectual life of the community. title: Introduction to Media Science
description: History and overview of the utilization of media in instruction, commercial enterprises, and industry with a discussion of job requirements and opportunities.

title: Operation and Maintenance of Audovisual Equipment
description: Instruction in the operation of projection, video, and audio equipment. Laboratory practice in maintenance and minor repair of equipment.

title: Multimedia Design and Display
description: Principles of media design and perception patterns. Application of these principles to the construction of twoand threedimensional displays for library and instructional uses.

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

title: Multimedia Production 1
description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work in the development of multimedia materials for teaching and presentation. Students will have laboratory experience in various mounting, laminating, lettering, coloring, and transparencymaking techniques.

title: Multimedia Production 2
description: Basic photographic and cinematographic techniques. Advanced transparencymaking utilizing photographic processes.

title: Multimedia Production 3
description: Advanced photographic and cinematographic practices. Production of multimedia utilizing electronic devices.

title: Selection and Management of Audiovisual Equipment and Software
description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment, accessories, and related software. Preparation of bid specifications.

title: Media Technician Practicum
description: Supervised practical experiences at an offcampus media center in various phases of media technology.

title: Organization of Library Materials
description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of materials in school libraries by use of the Dewey Decimal Classification and the construction of a library catalog. Consideration is given to book and nonbook materials.

title: Cataloging and Organization of Multimedia Materials
description: The principles and practice of the cataloging and organization of multimedia materials. Prerequisite: LIB 342 or the equivalent.

title: Methods and Materials for Student Use of School Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching students the skills necessary to the use of the media center. Prerequisite: LIB 100, 101, 102, 133, 201, 202, 203, 342, 460 or the equivalent and EDSEC 299 and the identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Utilization of Media Center Resources in the Curriculum
description: The curriculum role of the school media center, its unique contributions to learning, its supportive services, and its responsibilities shared with all other aspects of the educational program. Prerequisite: LIB 395.

title: Selection of Audiovisual Materials
description: Selection and evaluation of audiovisual media such as films, filmstrips, slides, microforms, audio and video recordings, educational games, simulations. 4 hrs. 16 hrs. 8 hrs. Military Science 155

title: Production of Audiovisual Media
description: A project course that meets the individual needs of undergraduate students in the production of such instructional media as 8 and 16 mm films, filmstrips, slide sets, and tape recordings.

title: Selection of Library Materials
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection for library materials. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials for public, academic, and school libraries.

title: Materials for Children
description: The reading and examining of book and nonbook materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examination of book and nonbook materials for young adult programs.

title: School Media Center Administration
description: The function, organizational patterns, maintenance, control, planning, and equipment of school media centers. The application of administrative principles to school media centers.

title: Introduction to Library Automation
description: An introduction to computer in library automation; working knowledge of OCLC terminal for searching, input, and manipulation of cataloging data; survey of other automated systems. Department of Military Science Bergin, Chairman; Avellina, Hozey, Jacobsen, Lavender, Nelson, Simpson, Stahle, Whitworth The Army ROTC Program provides qualified male and female students with an opportunity to obtain a commission in the United States Army and its reserve components. Students may obtain this commission by enrolling in the Army ROTC program along with their regular undergraduate studies in the field of their choice. The program consists of two elements: basic and advanced courses. The basic course, normally taken during the freshman (Military Science 1) and sophomore (Military Science 2) academic years, provides students with essential background information concerning organization and operations of the U.S. Defense Establishment. Students in the basic course do not incur any military obligations by enrolling in these classes. Completion of the basic course, or constructive credit for Junior AROTC (3 years), or attendance at a basic summer camp, or prior military service, is a prerequisite for admission into the advanced course. The advanced course, normally taken during the junior and senior academic years, provides students with leadership and management skills not available in other curricula and with concepts of military tactics, operations, and organizations. Advanced course students are obligated to attend an advanced summer camp (6 weeks) and to accept a commission as an officer, if tendered. Advanced course students receive subsistence and pay approximating $2,500 during the two years. All necessary equipment and books are furnished by the Department of the Army at no cost to the student. Credits earned in the military science (AROTC) program may apply toward degree requirements. For specific information, students are advised to consult with their advisers in their major field of study. The U.S. Army offers financial assistance in the form of one-, two-, and threeyear scholarships. Each scholarship provides tuition, textbooks, laboratory fees, and supplies in addition to subsistence pay of $100 a month for the period the scholarship is in effect. Applications for these scholarships may be submitted by anyone enrolled in the AROTC program or nonenrolled students who agree to compress the first two years of the program. Students may also enter the Army Reserve or National Guard under the Simultaneous Membership Program to gain additional experience and financial assistance. Most graduates who have completed the Advanced Course will be called upon to serve a threeyear tour of active duty and three years in the U.S. Army Reserve. Others will serve three months active duty for training in lieu of three years active duty and be required to participate in the Ready Reserve until the eighth anniversary date of the initial appointment in the Army Reserve. Entry to active duty may be deferred to obtain an advanced degree. Departmental minor in military science, 24 hours MIL 110, 120, 130, 210, 220, 230, 310, 320, 330, 410, 420, 430 21 hrs. title: U.S. Defense Establishment 1
description: Organization of the Department of Defense, Departme nt of the Army and Army ROTC; military service obligations, responsibilities of an officer; and the army education program.

title: U.S. Defense Establishment 2
description: Introduction to the history and mission of the Department of Defense. The philosophy of national power in international policies. Prerequisite : MIL 10.

title: U.S. Defense Establishment 3
description: History and mission of the fourteen branches of the U.S. Army. The organization of the Army Division. Prerequisite: MIL 120.

title: U.S. Defense Establishment 4
description: Significance of the military arts, military customs and courtesy, and traditions of the military and an introduction to military discipline. Prerequisite : MIL 130.

title: Maps and Aerial Photographs
description: Basic cartographic principles emphasizing terrain evaluation, marginal information and symbols, reference systems and aerial photograph interpretation.

title: Tactics and Operations
description: Introduction to troop leading procedures; mission, organization and composition of basic military teams; principles of offensive and defensive combat stressing firepower, movement, and communications.

title: Dynamics of the Military Team 1
description: Fundamentals of military instruction and instructional techniques; study of combat operations, with emphasis on major military teams. Analysis and application of leader's role in planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating efforts of individuals and small units. Prerequisite: MIL 210, 220, 230.

title: Leadership and Management 1
description: The psychological, physiological, and sociological factors which affect organizational behavior; individual and group solution of leadership and management problems common to small groups; case studies.

title: Dynamics of the Military Team 2
description: Continuation of study of combat operations, with emphasis on leadership responsibilities for planning and coordination. Fundamental techniques of internal defense and development in developing nations. Practical exercises emphasizing duties and responsibilities of junior leaders. Prerequisite: MIL 310.

title: Dynamics of the Military Team 3
description: Introduction to army administration, readiness programs, and military justice; continuation of the study of combat operations, with emphasis on the planning and coordination requirements at division level. Prerequisite: MIL 330.

title: Leadership and Management 2
description: Analysis of selected leadership and management problems. Principles of organization, informal organizations, formal organizations, nature and use of committees, communications techniques, and systems concepts. Application of leadership principles to practical situations. Prerequisite: MIL 320.

title: Dynamics of the Military Team 4
description: Continuation of the study of combat operations with emphasis on the command and staff functions at division level and higher; orientation for branch assignments, personal management responsibilities and the responsibilities of a commissioned officer. Prerequisite: MIL 410. School of Music Rubin, Director; Burkart, Dunn, Karjala The School of Music embraces two departments: Academic Studies in Music and Applied Studies in Music. Administrative efficiency and scholarly pursuits are enhanced by further subgroupings within these major areas. Thus, the divisions of music education, music history and musicology, and music theory and composition are identified in the Department of Academic Studies in Music, and divisions of keyboard, voice and guitar, symphonic instruments, and ensembles and conducting in the Department of Applied Studies in Music. A full range of large and small performing ensembles—the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, the Ars Musica String Quartet, the Concert Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra—provides superb opportunities for listening or for active participation. Less usual groups such as the Harp Ensemble, the Collegium Musicum, the String Sinfonietta, the University Singers, and the Ball State Ballet accent the diversity of performing outlets on the Ball State campus. Any student on campus, regardless of major, may audition for membership in the university concert organization. In advance of selecting the field of music for concentration, the student will consult with the coordinator of Undergraduate Programs in Music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the university, a student with a concentration area in music must have nroficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument, and a working knowledge of the 'ru diments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music will be given at times to be announced. If a student cannot meet requirements when entering the university, arrangements may be made to meet them later. All students with a concentration area in music are expected to attend a weekly recital meeting and to perform there with a frequency recommended by the individual teacher of applied music. Additional information will be found in the Music Student Handbook. In advance of completing registration each quarter, the student will clear requests for applied music instruction through the office of Applied Studies in Music; assignment to specific instructors will be made by this department. Students wishing to qualify for certification as teachers of music in the public schools should refer to the appropriate curricular information listed under the Department of Academic Studies in Music as well as in the area requirements which follow. Students wishing to prepare for careers in professional performance, in composition and arranging, or in scholarly activity and research are encouraged to enroll in the appropriate departmental major. The departmental minors also may serve some of these goals, but the total number of hours required for their completion is kept at a level which will serve the student in a liberal arts orientation who seeks broad cultural development rather than specialized proficiency. A student whose work load permits may register for additional lessons in the selected minor field or in other minor fields, provided the approval of the head of the Department of Applied Studies in Music has been secured. Practice rooms should be reserved in the office of the School of Music at the beginning of each quarter or term. Each student with a concentration area in music is advised to have a piano available for use at a certain time daily, either at the university or elsewhere. All students with concentration areas in music will participate actively in ensembles according to their curricular requirements. title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Designed for the potential music teacher.

title: Sensory Awareness and Response to Music
description: For the elementary classroom teacher emphasizing sensory experiences based on learning sequences appropriate for children. Constitutes a basis for musical experiences to be explored in succeeding courses. Not open to the student who has credit in MUSED 350, 351, 352.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: A basic inquiry into the value of craftsmanship and the principles of piano tuning. The problems and remedies of new and used pianos will be discussed. An introductory course open to all students interested in the care and maintenance of the piano.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Application of piano temperament tuning theory with emphasis on the development of proper tuning techniques. Prerequisi,te: MUSED 240 or permission of the department head.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Principles of basic action regulation and common minor repairs. Prerequisite: MUSED 241 or permission of the department head.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Brass Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 250.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 252,

title: The Development and Administration of School Choral Activities
description: Analysis of the choral literature available for use in the secondary school as to its technical difficulty and suitability to ral groups of various sizes and musical backgrounds. The administration and supervision of -h°0ral activities, including the general chorus, the selected groups, and the voice classes. Techniques of choral arranging.

A correlated laboratory session is scheduled for individual study and exploration. Prerequisite: MUSED 164. 350. The Teaching of Music in Elementary School. (3) The problems of teaching and supervising m usic in the elementary school for music supervisors and special teachers of music. Lesson planning and teaching are done in the class, and contact is made with teaching situations through directed observation. Leading music series are studied. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six: singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High School
description: An exploration of the scope and character of musical activities designed to supplement membership in the established performing groups of the public schools and to provide an outlet for the many students not concerned with public performance. Acquaintance with materials and techniques appropriate to the study of music literature and music theory.

title: Teaching and Administration of Instrumental Music
description: Using the skills developed in instrumental minor studies as a point of departure, the student in survey classes covers the techniques of related families of instruments. Proper care of equipment, organization of physical factors, teaching of instrumental classes, and developing instrumental ensembles are made the basis for lectures and class discussions. Piano and voice majors are advised to reserve this course for the senior year. Prerequisite: minor skills in brass, woodwind, and string instruments.

title: Introduction to Orff-Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities will be explored in movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative utilization of simple percussion instruments.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary School
description: Designed to enrich the musical background of the student in the common heritage of music and to suggest methods for presenting suitable musical materials and experiences to children. More intensive involvement with music exemplars, including appreciation and specific musical skills, is given emphasis. Prerequisite: MUSED 164 and 266.

title: Administration and Planning of the Church Music Program
description: Formation and training of adult and children's choirs in churches. Congregational singing. Service planning. The clergy, the congregation, and the church musician.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, shortterm course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing. Contact with new materials and methods will be insured in part by the inclusion of two or more distinguished visiting instructors on the staff.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experiences with the materials and activities of general music classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possibilities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: Workshop Series: Current Practices in Orff-Schulwerk
description: A special series of workshops given in association with the Indiana Orff-Schulwerk Association, which explore and give practical experience with current practices in Orff-Schulwerk in America, through workshop participation and related individual curricular development projects. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. Ball State fees are at the offcampus rate and are in addition to any fees which are required by the IOSA.

title: The Orff Workshop—Beginning
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the beginning phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on the basic approaches to the Orff method of teaching music to children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The Orff Workshop—Intermediate
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the more advanced phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. An emphasis is placed on creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Considerable time will be devoted to the techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite: MUSED 443 or permission of the department head.

title: Practicum: Rehearsal Materials and Techniques for the Secondary School Music Director
description: An intensive review of current practices in the development and musical advancement of school choral and instrumental ensembles. Emphasis on recent additions to available musical literature under guidance of distinguished guest conductors and with active cooperation of high school clinic groups. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned with the approval of the department head.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 2
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods for Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction situations. Prerequisite: credit in classical guitar.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite and parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Methods for Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods for teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level, or permission of the department head.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; singing and conducting opportunities of standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Handbell Techniques
description: An introduction to the history, literature, and playing techniques of handbells. Includes opportunities to conduct and to perform with handbell choirs. Discussion of administering handbell choirs in church and school situations.

title: Basic Movement and Choreography
description: Designed to acquaint the music therapist or teacher with the fundamentals of physical interpretations of music. Deals with techniques appropriate for swing choirs, small ensembles, and general staging practices in performance preparation.

title: Introduction to the Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school comprise the framework of this course designed for the music specialist. A study of the Hungarian system of music education forms the basis of analyzing the structure of the materials for American schools.

title: Introduction to Contemporary Music Techniques in the Elementary School
description: Exploring the use of nonconventional, nontraditional, experimental musical sound sources and procedures in music education. Students participate in classroom projects using creative and contemporary symbolization, instrumentation, and vocal setting, including an introduction to electronic music.

title: Stage Band Techniques
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the techniques and style characteristics of popular and jazz band performance. Includes preparation in the administration of school jazz ensembles.

title: Guitar for Social Use
description: Designed for development of basic skill in playing the guitar for accompanying. Focuses on chordal styles and their application to music such as folk songs and popular songs. Open to all students.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 1
description: Provides a fundamental working knowledge of skills required in maintaining stringed instruments at the elementary and secondary school levels. Study and application of school repair problems in regard to the violin, viola, cello, and doublebass. General techniques in making adjustments, gluing, and using tools properly. Analyses of the various woods used in instruments and bows.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments 2
description: Advanced study and experience in more specialized repairs on stringed instruments. Discussions and laboratory work including splicing, grafting, varnishing, carving, and bow rehairing. Historical resume of stringed instruments and makers from the seventeenth to the twentieth century.

title: Psychology of Music I
description: An introduction to the study of human musical processing with emphasis on the underlying principles of musical behavior. Fundamental laboratory experiences are included in the course work.

title: Psychology of Music 2
description: A continuation of MUSED 476 with emphasis on survey of the pertinent current research in the field. Prerequisite: MUSED 476.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis on those specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Tests, Measurements, and Guidance in Music
description: Acquaints the teacher with tests of sensory capacities, appreciation, and achievement. Briefly reviews such statistical and other data as make for an enlightened evaluation of the various tests and their results.

title: Psychology of Music
description: Presentation of materials as an aid to the understanding of the nature and extent of individual differences in musical talent. Specific preparation in the psychology of audition, motor control, and in the analysis of the musical mind leading to a natural application in the psychology of musical training.

title: Music in Therapy
description: Provides acquaintance with specific processes and procedures for the uses of music in therapy. Investigation of case studies, musical techniques, the use of music in behavior modification, and application of appropriate musical components in therapy.

title: Influence of Music on Behavior
description: The therapeutic uses of music in facilitating interaction patterns in afflicted persons. A behavioral approach to the processes of the use of music in therapy.

title: Introduction to Music Therapy 1
description: The foundations upon which music therapy rests. Deals with the basic concepts of the discipline and provides a working definition of music therapy for prospective music therapists.

title: Introduction to Music Therapy 2
description: A continuation of MUSED 484 with investigation of the basic premises of the profession in greater depth. Aids in the clarification of the role of the music therapist in society. Prerequisite: MUSED 484.

title: Clinical Experience 1
description: Actual field experience assisting in a functioning music therapy situation under the direction of a qualified music therapist. Corresponds to the participation experience for the prospective teacher.

title: Clinical Experience 2
description: Actual field experience assisting in a functioning music therapy situation under the direction of a qualified music therapist. Corresponds to the participation experience for the prospective teacher. Prerequisite: MUSED 486.

title: Music in Therapy and Special Education
description: The theoretical aspects of music therapy and their appropriate application to special education in the public schools. Emphasizes the power of music to elicit normal interaction with peers from the child with a learning difficulty.

title: Recreational Music
description: Particularly for students interested in the function of music in recreational leadership at any level. Explored will be materials, sources, elements of a recreational music program, organizational procedures, individual and group activities, and utilization of community musical resources. Open to all; musical background not required.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: Provides the superior student with an opportunity for intensive study and research in a particular aspect of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Internship in Music Therapy
