A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned. y

title: Introduction to Music
description: Introduction to the art of listening to music. Some elementary instruction in musical materials will be related to the listening aspects of the course, although the course is designed primarily to introduce students to the sound of music through the ages. No previous knowledge of music required. Open to students with areas in music by permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Music History 1
description: The growth of music from its beginnings through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The origins of music, the development of notation, and the growth of early polyphonic forms. Open only to students with areas in music except by permission of the department head.

title: Music History 2
description: Changes in music from the late sixteenth century through the Baroque, the Rococo, and the Classical periods. The transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque, and the developments of opera, sonata, symphony, and the related forms. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, or permission of the department head.

title: Music History 3
description: Developments in music from the time of Beethoven to the present. Transition from the classical to romantic periods, the various reactions to Romanticism, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 231, or permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Restricted to students on the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 1
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisites: Some music literature background and an ability to read music will be expected of the student.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: A comprehensive study of vocal and instrumental music of western Europe during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including the function of figured bass and important theoretical and contrapuntal developments. The evolution of opera, oratorio, and cantata and the development of instrumental genres such as concerto, sonata, and suite (both orchestral and keyboard) will be considered, with important representative works studied. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eithteenth century, including the various styles which marked the transition from Baroque to Classic music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in western civilization in the nineteenth century emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Important composers and works will be studied from the various time periods: early, middle, and late romanticism, and post romanticism. Prerequisites: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and the student will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisites: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department head.

title: History and Development of Jazz
description: A survey of the evolution of jazz music in the United States. Includes study of the stylistic innovations and contributions of selected groups and individuals. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque instruments, and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Bameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study, or permission of the department head.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: Provides superior students with an opportunity for guided reading and intensive study in an area of music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but not more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Hymnody in Worship
description: Hymns in early Jewish and Western Christian tradition: their historical and liturgical context and contemporary use. A summary of Western religious thought as exposed in liturgical poetry. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department head.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department head.

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students with deficiencies in elementary musical knowledge. Provides, at the simplest levels, a language for communication and a background of rudimentary information, historical and systematic. Designed primarily for students intending to pursue courses in music education, history, theory, and performance. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. Open to all students except those with credit in MUSTH 111 or above; MUHIS 230 or above. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. 111, 112, 113. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) Review of terminology and fundamentals precedes an extensive study of the tonal, rhythmic, motivic, and formal structure of melody through composition and analysis. The basic elements of music are studied through the analysis and writing of music in two, three, and four parts. Elementary work in transposition, scoring, and harmonic alterations. Music reading, aural discernment, and rhythmic training provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. These courses must be taken in course number sequence. 211, 212, 213. Music Theory. (3 hours each quarter) More complex elements of nineteenthand twentiethcentury music studied through composition and analysis. Advanced work in music reading and aural discernment provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. Prerequisite:

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: The components of the recording chain are introduced both theoretically and practically. A complete and thorough review of the recording process, the mixing process, and editing formats is presented.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An introduction to multichannel recording techniques, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing is presented. Requires laboratory time for recording practice and a final recording project. Prerequisite: MUSTH 225.

title: Music Calligraphy
description: Practical experience in calligraphic skills and layout procedures pertinent to the preparation of music scores and parts. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113. 321, 322, 323. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing short instrumental and vocal compositions with emphasis on developing the student's technical capacity to achieve freedom of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic Music
description: A workshop in current practices of producing music by electronic means. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Composing based on examples studied is optional. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band and wind ensemble. Particular attention is given to voicing, sectional and crosssectional doubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Commercial Arranging Concepts
description: The study and analysis of arranging technique s employed in comercial music. Conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in comercial idioms will be emphasized. Particular attention will be given to the composerarranger in the recording studio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Music Theory in the Secondary School
description: An investigation of pedagogical precepts and problems relating to music theory in the secondary school. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Analysis will be applied to a broad representation of musical masterworks from various periods with examination of the macroand microstructure and construction of selected works. Special attention is given to musical practices before and after the period of tertian harmony. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Electronic Music Studio 1
description: An introductory course in electronic music. The physical and perceptual dimensions of sound are presented as a basis for sound synthesis. An introduction to musique concrete operations and voltagecontrolled systems provides the basis for class projects. Studio laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Electronic Music Studio 2
description: An advanced course in electronic music synthesis. An introduction to large voltagecontrolled systems, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing. Projects in composition, educational applications of electronic music, and research. Laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 425. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Computer Applications in Music
description: Presents an overview of computer systems and languages appropriate for (1) musical analysis; (2) musical composition; and (3) sound synthesis. Presents a historical perspective and computer applications in the areas stated and introduces simple programming procedures. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department head.

title: Composition-Project Recital
description: Public performance of the student's compositions and/or public presentation of the student's music theory research.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire are presented. Each project requires seminar and laboratory participation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 226. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. 431, 432, 433. Composition. (2 hours each quarter) Experience in writing more complex and extended instrumental and vocal compositions with continued emphasis on the development of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 323.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. The synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound are studied as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: A laboratory for skill development in arranging. This course is individualized and projectoriented to prepare musicians in scoring spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, background and mood sequence, and composition requirements of music for filming TV, radio, and media productions. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Independent study in any area of music theory via readings, analysis, and/or research. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 and permission of the department head. title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, carrying one hour of credit and rehearsing normally 5 hours per week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, Concert Band, the Marching Show Band, the Symphony Orchestra, the Concert Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble 1.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the advanced ensembles. Included in this category are the Symphonic Band, University Concert Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensembles 2 and 3, and Training Orchestra, all of which normally rehearse 2 hours per week.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the advanced ensembles. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera Chorus, and the University Singers, all of which normally rehearse 5 hours per week.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: An apprenticeship course to the advanced ensembles. Included in this category are the Chorale, Women's Chorus, University Debs, the Men's Glee Club, and the Choral Union, all of which normally rehearse 2 hours per week.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 372.

title: Planning and Producing the Musical Show
description: Designed to familiarize the student with standard operating procedures within the field of musical theatre. Provides a wellstructured approach to musical theatre production techniques.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, carrying one hour of credit and rehearsing normally 5 hours per week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, Concert Band, the Marching Show Band, the Symphony Orchestra, the Concert Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble 1.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying onehalf hour of credit and normally rehearsing 2 hours per week. Included in this category are the Symphonic Band, University Concert Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensembles 2 and 3, and the Training Orchestra.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble

The graduate also possesses the background knowledge and skill needed for progression into firstlevel administrative positions and graduate study. Classroom and laboratory instruction for the curriculum is provided by the univeristy, and the program uses the facilities of Ball Memorial Hospital, adjacent to the university campus, and other nearby community health agency facilities. A student indicating an intent to major in nursing begins study in the areas of English, social sciences, physical and biological sciences, and the fine arts. Approximately two years of academic work in humanities and behavioral and biological sciences is required. The major in nursing has been concentrated in the student's junior and senior years. Cooperative programs in nursing have been arranged between Ball State University and Anderson College, Bethel College, Grace College, Huntington College, Manchester College, St. Francis College, Taylor University, and Tri-State College. A student interested in the cooperative program may enroll at one of these institutions for the freshman and sophomore years and transfer these credits to Ball State University. The curriculum for the professional nursing student is classified under the Professional Arts Curriculum. The Bachelor of Science degree is earned and may be completed with the minimum requirements of the curriculum (186 hours). A minimum scholastic ratio of 2.0 in the major and overall point average is required. In addition the student will present a minimum of C in each clinical nursing course and in ANAT 201, PHYSL 210, 211, BIO 213, CHEM 106, and NUR 210. Application for admission to the junior clinical courses occurs during the quarter in which the student will have completed 93 quarter hours. The philosophy and objectives of Ball State University are supported by the Department of Nursing, which focuses on the total development of the student in nursing. Statement of Philosophy The faculty believes that the human is an integrated biopsychosocial being, selfregulating and holistic, in dynamic, continuous interaction with the environment. Recognizing that there are individual differences arising from genetic, social, psychological, and environmental factors, the faculty believes that humans are endowed with the ability to learn, make decisions, and assume responsibility for personal actions. Inherent in this belief is respect for the dignity and worth of individuals. The faculty believes that nursing is a scientific biopsychosocial process which identifies evolutionary and entropic forces within a system. Nursing aids the client in learning to maximize personal health potential along a wellnessillness continuum. In times of illness, nursing assists the client in identifying and utilizing coping mechanisms in such a way that independence is gained as rapidly as possible. Nursing provides continual support through the life cycle and death when adaptation for survival is not possible. Nursing collaborates with other professions and the client in identifying, planning, and assisting in meeting and evaluating goals for the promotion and maintenance of client health. In the performance of these activities, nursing is accountable to the client for quality care. Nursing, as a profession, is organized to set professional goals, establish standards for professional practice and education, generate new knowledge, and enhance its unique heritage. Membership in a profession demands personal responsibility for continued learning and sharing of knowledge and experience gained from practice, research, and health teaching. The faculty believes that health is a state of dynamic biopsychosocial interplay of evolutionary and entropic forces within a system, as well as between systems. The maintenance of optimal health depends upon adaptation to stress within the individual's environment. The faculty believes that the environment is the spectrum of surrounding matter acting upon a system in an interlocking hierarchy. Changes within the environment have an increasing impact on health and changing wellnessillness patterns. The goals of nursing are to maintain and improve health by minimizing or preventing adverse effects of the environment. Health teaching, health screening, and identification of evolutionary and entropic forces are methods by which nursing meets the needs of people as adaptation occurs. The faculty believes that the purpose of the undergraduate program is the preparation of a generalist who functions both independently and interdependently with health team members. The nursing curriculum builds upon the general studies background of the student, integrating it with professional nursing courses. The application of general systems theory provides a framework for the study of the major concepts of environment, health, humans, nursing, and the relationships of suprasystems and subsystems. Through analysis and synthesis of observations and knowledge derived from the care of clients in a variety of settings, the nurse is able to function in the holistic approach to health. The faculty believes that the generalist integrates knowledge of nursing with knowledge from other disciplines in applying the nursing process. This broad base enables the student to utilize interpersonal skills in collaborating with clients and other personnel and in applying leadership principles in the delivery of health care. The baccalaureate graduate analyzes research findings for relevance to nursing practice and for the improvement of consumer health. Through the acquisition of these competencies the nurse becomes responsible for continued personal and professional growth. The faculty believes that baccalaureate nursing education is the basis for entry into the profession of nursing. It is also recognized that there are multiple entry points into baccalaureate nursing education, and the faculty has responsibility for assisting individuals in the educational process. The purpose of the graduate program is preparation of teachers and administrators in nursing. The faculty believes that graduate education in nursing is founded upon baccalaureate education in nursing. The graduate student, as an independent learner, assumes responsibility for personal growth, selfdirection, and selfevaluation. Graduate education at the master's level provides the student with a foundation for specialization in a chosen functional role and enhancement of clinical knowledge and skills. Graduate education in nursing aims to integrate and synthesize knowledge and skills from the biological and social sciences with the advanced art and science of nursing within the health care delivery system. The application of General Systems Theory in graduate education provides a framework for advanced study and inquiry into the concepts and theories supporting human beings in relation to environment, health, and nursing. The individual is an open system with universal traits that facilitate study, inquiry, and application of concepts and theories from nursing and related health fields. The faculty believes that the integration of past experiences and graduate study enables the student to extend, reinforce, and reorganize knowledge, techniques, and skills in nursing. Graduate education actively involves the student in studying issues and research in nursing and related fields. A firm foundation in research techniques prepares the student to make systematic inquiries, evaluate current and future studies and trends in nursing, and identify implications for practice. The graduate practitioner assumes leadership responsibility in sharing research findings. The master's graduate needs a foundation in the chosen functional role with advanced clinical knowledge and skills. This broad base prepares the student for leadership and critical analysis of issues and trends as they relate to human health and as a contributor to the consumer of research. Continuing Education offerings are based on needs that arise from expanded scientific technology and health care trends, as well as those expressed by registered nurses, professional organizations, and health agencies. Continuing education in nursing consists of planned learning experiences designed to promote the development of knowledge, skills, and attitudes for the enhancement of nursing practice, thus improving health care to the public. Continuing education in nursing is built upon adult education principles and is distinct from education toward an academic degree, of shorter duration, and specific to the individual's immediate or rapidly changing needs, and has immediate application to the goals of the learner. The goal of continuing education in nursing is to assist nursing personnel in maintaining and improving competence in the practice of nursing. In order to implement the objectives of continuing education, providers of continuing education in nursing collaborate with other health professionals, nursing personnel, community agencies, and consumers of health care services in the development of continuing education offerings. Objectives of the Undergraduate Program The Department of Nursing accepts the responsibility to provide and foster learning activities and experiences which will enable the student: I. To integrate the concept of the holistic human being into nursing practice. 2. To integrate knowledge of nursing theory with knowledge from other disciplines. 3. To utilize the nursing process in the promotion and maintenance of health and the prevention of disease. 4. To collaborate with clients and others for the improvement of health care and its systems. 5. To assist the individual to adapt within the environmental systems. 6. To utilize communication skills in establishing relationships with individuals and groups. 7. To apply leadership/management principles in the delivery of health care. 8. To utilize research findings for beginning application in nursing practice. 9. To assume responsibility for professional practice. 10. To develop an understanding of the need for continuous professional and personal growth. description: Prerequisite: PEG 210 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 108 or PEG 214.

title: Intermediate Folk Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 112.

title: Intermediate Square Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 113.

title: Advanced Judo
description: Emphasis placed on understanding and practicing intermediate judo techniques, international contest rules and skills, and teaching methods that will enable one to teach beginning judo. Prerequisite: PEG 211.

title: Intermediate Modern Dance
description: A progression of technical skills in modern dance movement beyond the beginning level and in preparation for an advanced level of movement skill. Prerequisite: PEG 115.

title: Advanced Modern Dance
description: For students already skilled in dance who wish to increase their performing and technical aptitude in dance either for vocational or nonvocational reasons. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Handball
description: Introductory skills for playing handball. Basic skills, strategy, rules, and courtesy measures stressed. Designed for the student with little prior experience.

title: Racquetball
description: Instruction in the basic skills, strategies, and knowledge required to play racquetball.

title: Intermediate Badminton
description: Presents skills in badminton beyond the beginning level and is designed to provide opportunities to learn advanced technique and strategy. Prerequisite: PEG 124 or PEP 173 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 122.

title: Intermediate Bowling
description: Designed to give the student knowledge and experience in bowling on a team, in a league, keeping league records, team standings, and computing and figuring handicaps as well as review of basic fundamentals.

title: Bicycle Touring
description: Designed to develop touring physical fitness and camping skills associated with the touring aspects of bicycling. Prerequisite: PEG 130 or equivalent. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate Golf
description: Designed to offer the golfing student an opportunity to learn and practice the finer points of the game.

title: Intermediate Horsemanship
description: Work toward perfecting form in the three gaits: walk, trot, and canter. Harness driving. Stable management.

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 128.

title: Intermediate Hatha Yoga
description: Designed for the student wishing to perfect previously learned asanas and to learn new ones. Prerequisite: PEG 119 or permission of the department head

title: Intermediate Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: An intermediate course in basketball designed to include a review of fundamental skills, further development of these skills, and the introduction of advanced skills and strategies. Prerequisite: PEG 137 or PEP 182 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Power Volleyball (Women's Rules)
description: Instruction in intermediate techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and competition. Includes individual and team offensive and defensive techniques, offensive and team game strategies, and competition. Prerequisite: PEG 131 or PEP 183 or equivalent. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 140.

title: Intermediate Fencing
description: Prerequisite: beginning fencing or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach intermediate skiers the skills necessary to become advanced skiers; affords them the opportunity to ski on longer, higher open and trail slopes provided by ski areas in the west (Rocky Mountains) or the east (White Mountains). Prerequisite: PEG 142 or permission of the department head.

title: Intercollegiate Athletics
description: Actual participation in the organized practice sessions and competitions during the regular season for the varsity sport as directed by the coach for that sport. A total of 2 hours credit may be earned.

title: Selected Seasonal Sports Activities
description: Designed to be offered only at an offcampu s location with a great deal oflexibility in course content order to acomodate the neds of individuals and to adapt to the facilities available and the weather conditions existing at the time the course is being offered. Students will be provided activity and instruction in physical fitness activities and two lifetime sports activities.

title: Sport Scuba Diving
description: Provides opportunities for refining techniques and skills for using selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus. Prerequisite: PEG 206 or permission of the department head.

title: White Water Canoeing
description: Designed to assist students to develop skills and gain knowledge necessary for white water canoeing and portaging. Field trips may involve overnight camping. Prerequisite: PEG 209 or permission of the department head.

title: Advanced Tennis
description: Designed for the student wishing to perfect previously learned skills and to learn more indepth strokes and playing strategies. Prerequisite: PEG 227 or 128 or permission of the department head.

title: General Safety Education
description: Designed to prepare prospective teachers for the comprehensive general safety education program.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control. Designed to aid the student to develop a fitness philosophy, to structure physical fitness programs, and to recognize individual physiological limitations.

title: Gymnastics (Balance Beam and Floor Exercise)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastics (Trampoline, Vaulting, Uneven Bars)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, flying rings, and uneven parallel bars. Prerequisite: PEP 157 or permission of the department head.

title: Studio of Contemporary Dance Theatre
description: Provides training toward the act of performance, through varied choreographic dance experiences. Students plan, rehearse, and perform in studio hour presentations. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or permission of the department head. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Folk Dance Studio Theatre
description: The third course in folk dance. Designed to emphasize the different styles existing in folk dance. Introduces the student to elements of folk dance choreography. Prerequisite: PEG 112, 212, or PEP 262. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foundations of Physical Education
description: An introductory course for professional physical education students that covers the psychomotor, cognitive, and affective scope of physical education and its relationship to education. An attempt is made to assist students in assessing those qualities of motor and physical fitness expected of physical education majors as they commence their vocational study.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 1
description: Content, methods, materials, organization, and administration of the classroom and laboratory phase of the secondary school program.

title: Developmental Game Activities
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the application of the principles of movement and to provide a knowledge of basic skills and appropriate activities for the development of these skills as applied to game activities. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Principles and Problems of Coaching Sports for Girls and Women
description: Introduces students to the following: the principles and problems of coaching girls' team and individual sports at the junior and senior high school level, the philosophies and principles which underlie the development of such a program.

title: Coaching Observation (Girls/Women's Athletics)
description: Guided observation of coaching techniques and practices with analysis of teaching/coaching philosophies for competitive sports in schools. Prerequisite: PEP 231. 2 55, Practicum in Aquatics. (1) An internship in aquatics at Ball State or other approved aquatic programs. Prerequisite: PEP 353 and permission of the department chairman. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Officiating Competitive Aquatic Sports
description: Introduces the student to officiating practices, the decisionmaking role of the official, and laboratory experience in officiating. Opportunities exist for certification in various aquatic areas. 257, Gymnastics for Children. (2) Designed to acquaint the student with teaching methodology, developmental skills, and activities for gymnastics at the elementary school level. Prerequisite: PEP 157.

title: Tumbling and Apparatus (Women's Events)
description: Prerequisite: PEP 158 and 159 or permission of the department head.

title: Gymnastic Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has 2 hours of credit in PEP 256 or 258.

title: Contemporary Dance Theatre
description: Provides the dance student with experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance performances. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Folk Dance
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 112.

title: The Teaching of Folk Dance
description: Materials and techniques of teaching folk dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEP 262 or equivalent.

title: Folk Dance Theatre
description: Provides opportunities and experiences in participating with a company of dancers who plan and perform in both informal and formal folk dance presentations. Prerequisite: PEG 112 and permission of the department head. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: The Teaching of Square Dance
description: The development of teaching skills for beginning and intermediate classes in square dancing. The development of techniques of calling square dance (patter and singing). Prerequisite: PEP 263.

title: Teaching of Recreational Dance
description: An introduction to folk, square, round, and other types of recreational dance, and methods of teaching recreational dance.

title: Dance Composition 1
description: Principal elements of dance composition. Simple compositional forms for small groups and solo work. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Intermediate Badminton
description: Prerequisite: PEP 173 or permission of the department head.

title: Folk and Square Dance Methods for Elementary School Children
description: Movement experiences in the forms of folk and square dance for the elementary school child. Emphasis is on the selection of dance materials and methods of teaching dance for the elementary school child.

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 177 or permission of the department head.

title: Baseball/Softball Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 179.

title: Track and Field Performance Techniques
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 180.

title: Games and Activities for the Handicapped
description: Designed to familiarize the student with games and activities commonly used with the handicapped. Prerequisite: SPCED 201.

title: Recreation Playground Activities
description: Provides a knowledge of playground operation. equipment, and supplies. Presentation of a wide variety of activities for effective playground leadership.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Physical Education
description: Offers the student supervised experience in basic movementoriented activities generally included in elementary school physical education programs (suggested range K-6). Course work will be contracted among the student, the department, and the school/agency through the appropriate campus office. Prerequisite: PEP 230 or permission of the department head. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Physiology
description: Basic concepts in physiology for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching. Prerequisite: PEP 292, or permission of the department head.

title: Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze activity for the purpose of improving physical skills. Prerequisite: PEP 292.

title: First Aid
description: First aid as outlined by the American Red Cross, leading to standard certification. Designed for the student pursuing a major or minor program in the School of Physical Education and Athletics. Not open to the student who has credit in HSC 250.

title: First Aid Instructor
description: Instructor's course in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, including the instructor's course in Multimedia First Aid as established by the American Red Cross. Designed for the professional student pursuing a major or minor in physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 299 or HSC 250, or valid certification in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, Standard First Aid and Multimedia, or Advanced First Aid and Emergency Care.

title: Camping
description: Acquaints the student with various aspects of organized and individual camping. One weekend field trip may be required in addition to regular laboratory periods.

title: Simulation in Driver and Traffic Safety Education
description: Designed to meet the needs of prospective teachers in the simulation phase of driver and traffic safety education. Prerequisite : PEP 124.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Gymnastics, Volleyball, and Track and Field
description: Coaching techniques involved in gymnastics, volleyball, and track and field. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Volleyball, Basketball, and Softball
description: Coaching techniques involved in volleyball, basketball, and softball. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Swimming, Golf, Gymnastics, and Tennis
description: Coaching techniques involved in swimming, golf, gymnastics, and tennis. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Organization and Management of Women's Athletics
description: Understanding and appreciation of the responsibilities and desirable characteristics of competent officials; organizing and managing competitive events and tournaments; relationships among coach, officials, players, and spectators; local, state, and national organizations involved in officiating and management.

title: Sports Information 1
description: Designed primarily for the sports information student. Develops the student's knowledge and background in the terminology, basic strategy, scoring, and officiating in gymnastics (men's), basketball, golf, ice hockey, boxing, wrestling, horseracing, billiards, cross country, baseball, and football. Not open to the student with teaching areas in physical education.

title: Sports Information 2
description: Designed for the sports information student. Includes the following sports areas: gymnastics (women's), volleyball, tennis, track and field, swimming, lacrosse, field hockey, softball, soccer, badminton, and bowling. Geared to increase the student's knowledge in these sports, especially in regard to terminology, basic rules, strategy, scoring, and officiating, to assist them in "covering" these activities. Not open to physical education majors and minors.

title: Aquatic Art Production
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of management and staging activities involved in an aquatic art production at the high school and college levels.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head.

title: American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor
description: Students have the opportunity to earn the American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor Certificate. Prerequisite: an unexpired American National Red Cross advanced lifesaving certificate.

title: Instructional Techniques and Analysis of Aquatic Performance
description: Selected learning theories, teaching strategies, and physical laws which affect learning and performance in the aquatic medium. Analysis of basic safety skills and stroke and diving techniques receive major emphasis.

title: Field and/or Laboratory Experience
description: Permits the student to receive credit for aquatic experiences in categories of leadership, administration, and/or operation of aquatic programs or facilities. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 259.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 261,

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the lower level of the elementary school.

title: History of Dance
description: Basic dance forms and functions from the primitive era into the 20th century.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and the use of accompaniment in dance. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or equivalent.

title: Dance Production 1
description: Designed to acquaint the student with various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or equivalent.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Techniques)
description: Fundamental modern dance techniques, elements of rhythmic patterns, materials of space, design, and improvisation.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Composition)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on composition. Prerequisite: PEP 365.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Methodology)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on teaching modern dance in the public schools, camps, and others. Dance composition. Prerequisite: PEP 366.

title: Aquatics for the Elementary School Child
description: Introduces the student to safety factors, developmental strokes, diving sequences, and teaching strategies for aquatic instruction of the young child. Prerequisite: PEP 353 or equivalent certificate from a nationally recognized organization such as the Young Men's Christian Association or the Boy Scouts of America.

title: Diagnostic Techniques and Athletic Injury Mechanisms
description: An introduction to predisposing anatomical, kinesiological, growth stress, and other such factors that contribute to athletic injuries. Procedures for accurate recognition and evaluation of not only these factors, but also the extent of an athletic injury are presented. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Administration and Organization of Programs for the Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Problems, principles, and objectives in the designing, planning, and operation of a program for the prevention and care of athletic injuries. There will also be an examination of the code of ethics of the National Athletic Trainers' Association. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Athletic Training Modalities and Therapeutic Techniques
description: An introduction to mechanical therapies, thermal therapy, cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, and therapeutic exercise. Only those modalities and their clinical uses that have special implications for the athletic trainer in the treatment of injuries to the athlete will be considered. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Methods of Teaching Team Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following team sports: basketball, field hockey, flag football, soccer, softball, speedball, team handball, volleyball. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in team sports included.

title: Methods of Teaching Individual Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following individual sports: archery, badminton, bowling, golf, tennis, track. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in individual sports included.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 276.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball and Softball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 279.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 280.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 28E

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 282.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 283.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 284.

title: Gymnastics Judging (Women's Events)
description: The development of gymnastics judging techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and or NAGWS (Class) official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 157, 158, 159.

title: Track and Field Officiating
description: The development of track and field officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 180.

title: Softball Umpiring
description: The development of softball umpiring techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA, ASA, and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Volleyball Officiating
description: The development of volleyball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 183.

title: Basketball Officiating
description: The development of basketball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining an IHSAA and/or NAGWS official's rating. Prerequisite: PEP 182.

title: Principles of Physical Education
description: General concepts based upon the scientific facts and philosophic judgments which underlie physical education.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children, emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, utilizing task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Neurophysiological Approach to Physical Education for the IIandicapped
description: Designed to provide the student with an understanding of the theoretical basis of selected neurophysiologi cai programs for treatment of motor decrements of various handicapping conditions, and to teach the student how to administer such programs.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include the factors of purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the student to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate an array of teaching strategies that would be utilized in creating a freesafe environment for a public school physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence and EDSEC 299 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Principles; practice of athletic trainin g principles and techniques necesary for care prevention of athletic injuries.

title: Remedial Exercises and Rehabilitation
description: An introduction to the objectives and principle s involved in designing and planing conditioning programs for the athlete. Therapeutic exercises essential in planning the rehabilitation program of the injured athlete are introduced and developed. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed as a practicum that involves comprehensive planning of instruction, designing teaching implementation strategies, classroom management techniques, and evaluation of teaching behaviors and materials in physical education. Opportunities for students to work with children in a classroom setting. Prerequisite: PEP 395 and juniorlevel status.

title: Exercise Technician and Leader Practicum
description: To provide training for potential leaders of physical fitness programs, emphasis will be on administering exercise tests in the laboratory and in field situations, prescribing exercise based on test results and scientific principles, and leading exercise sessions. Prerequisite: PEP 293 or equivalent course or permission of the department head.

title: Practicum in Recreation
description: Supervised, practical, professional leadership experience designed for the recreationoriented person. Experiences include: work activities in federal, state, county, or community parks or with private camps. Close supervision supplied by the university and the participating agency. Prerequisite: permission of the department head. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 2
description: Presentation of materials and information designed to prepare for teaching driver education in the secondary schools.

title: Motorcycle Safety Education
description: Will prepare prospective teachers to conduct motorcycle rider education courses.

title: Coaching Internship
description: Assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teaching/coaching process. (May not be taken during student teaching.) Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Sports Information Statistics
description: Designed for the sports information student. Consists of the identification, computation, practical application, and communication of various sport statistics in selected sports, such as ERA, match play, difficulty rating, various percentages. Not open to students with teaching areas in physical education,

title: Athletic Governance
description: Directed mainly towards the sports information student. Designed to discuss the various organizations which govern amateur and professional sports in the United States. The emphasis for the course is on the sports information student's role in shaping sports in this country and in international competition. Not recommended for Physical Education majors and minors.

title: Swimming Pool Operation and Maintenance
description: Water circulation and filtration, chemical treatment for disease control, sanitation, and administrative procedures for personal safety receive major emphasis in this course.

title: Teaching Modern Dance for Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or equivalent.

title: Advanced Studio in Contemporary Dance
description: Advanced techniques in contemporary dance. Designed for the student who is interested in advancing his/her skills in contemporary dance technique beyond those developed in the regular college classes. Choreographic forms, performance, and production, using such allied fields as costuming, lighting, and accompaniment. Prerequisite: some previous study of modern dance or ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Implementation of Elementary School Physical Education Programs
description: Designed for advanced students, giving an overview of educationally sound elementary physical education programs; history, curriculum, assessment, objectives, methodology, planning, progressions, and evaluations. Prerequisite: senior standing, or permission of the department head.

title: Mainstreaming in Elementary School Physical Education
description: Designing physical education programs to meet the requirements of Public Law 94-142 mandating that all handicapped children have an individualized physical education program.

title: Teaching the Handicapped in Aquatic's
description: Adaptation of strokes for people with various limitations, swimming as a rehabilitation program, facilities and pool design adaptations. Prerequisite: an unexpired American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certificate.

title: Sports Development
description: Organizational patterns in program development and exploration of current problems in girls' and women's sports.

title: Practicum in Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Designed to provide the student with practical experience in working with handicapped children in a physical education setting. Prerequisite: PEP 488 and 494.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching of a Modern Day Athletic Program
description: Designed to explore the historical development of modern athletics, to develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program, and learn to deal with everyday coaching and a dministration problems.

title: Program Development for Intramural and Recreational Activities
description: Initiation, organization, and administration of intramural and recreational programs in the secondary school.

title: Teaching Physical Education for the Mentally Retarded
description: Establishing a physical education curriculum for the mentally retarded child. Includes understanding the child's experience in physical education, teaching methods, and a teaching experience.

title: History and Philosophy of Recreation
description: The history of recreation in the United States from the first settlers in America to modern times. A study of various philosophies which have influenced the development of the new leisure principles.

title: Skill Analysis, 'Theory and Practice of Play
description: Scientific principles involved in movement as they apply to specific skills in elementary school physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Fundamental play needs of children; research into the play interests of children; and evaluation of space, equipment, and supervision. Results sought are appreciation of the educational values of play, necessity of adequate provisions for it, ability to select appropriate equipment, and formation of a tentative curriculum of play forms. Not open to physical education majors and minors except by permission of department head.

title: Physical Education Theory and Practice for Upper Elementary and Middle School Children
description: Application of basic movement skills (controlled and refined motor patterns) to individual, dual, self testing, lead up and team games, sports, dance, aquatics, gymnastics and/or combination thereof, including assessment, activities, program planning and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department head.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the human organism. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294, or by permission of the department head.

title: Teaching Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitation of each. Physical education and recreational activities for each type. 49 5. Laboratory and Field Experience in Athletic Training 1. (1) An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage, and other therapeutic techniques used by the athletic trainer in the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training
description: Students are assigned to onthejob experience as student athletic trainers in conjunction with their student teaching assignments in an Indiana high school that is qualified to provide students with both experiences. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Evaluation in Physical Education
description: Methods of measuring and evaluating physical education results in terms of directing philosophy. Tests and uses of test results.

title: Laboratory and Field Experience in Athletic Training 2
description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage, and other therapeutic techniques used by the athletic trainer in the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Independent Study in Physical Education
description: An opportunity to investigate an area of particular interest to the individual, under supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. title: Physical Conditioning
description: Designed to help the students become aware of their present fitness status and to appreciate the role of physical exercise in everyday life. Students are expected to improve their conditioning through a program of rigorous exercise. 101.$$ Water Adjustment for Swimming. (1) Phase one of a program designed to assist the nonswimmer toward becoming an efficient swimmer. Only students who cannot swim in deep water are eligible.

title: Individualized Exercise and Figure Control
description: An exercise course including individual analysis of fitness problems, development and maintenance of a fitness level.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to help students develop a personalized program for developing and maintaining muscular strength and the physique.

title: Jogging
description: Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through jogging.

title: Adapted Physical Education
description: Intended for students with physical handicaps and/or limiting conditions that would prevent full and unlimited participation. Students assigned to Adapted Physical Education by the University Health Service consult with a member of one of the physical education departments and are assigned to a regular activity class or to physical therapy according to their interests, needs, and qualifications. Regular course requirements are adjusted for the individual. This course may be repeated. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Beginning/Intermediate Judo
description: Designed to give the student an appreciation of judo, both as a sport and as an art. Emphasis placed on understanding basic judo techniques, the development of selfconfidence, and selfdefense throughout the course.

title: Beginning Karate
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of karate. a regular activity class or to physical tt Plus a senior creative project directed by a member of the dance faculty. $$ This course is administered as a learning and/or testout program during the regular school year (September-May). title: Beginning Modern Dance
description: Designed to introduce the student to the basic skills of modern dance through movement techniques and creative projects.

title: Beginning Modern Jazz Dance
description: Understanding and skill in basic techniques and styles (cool, hot, blues, urban, primitive) of the jazz dance.

title: Swimnastics
description: Physical conditioning through water exercise, using highpotential fitness activities which can be used in a small pool or in a limited area of a crowded instructional pool. Prerequisite: ability to put face in water, float on front and/oT back in shallow water, and ability to regain standing position after floating.

title: Beginning Tap Dance
description: Designed to teach the basic tap steps and combinations along with their rhythmic analysis and style to be used in composition. Designed for the student with no experience in tap dancing.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through yoga exercises and yoga relaxation techniques.

title: Badminton
description: Introductory skills for playing singles and doubles badminton. Basic strategy, rules, and courtesy will be stressed.

title: Beginning Bowling
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of bowling.

title: Beginning Badminton
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 122.

title: Beginning Horsemanship
description: Schooling in three gaits: walk, trot, and canter.

title: Beginning Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 128.

title: Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 127.

title: Bicycling
description: Bicycling techniques involving maintenance of equipment; city, open country, and endurance riding primarily to introduce the student to family bicycling for lifetime use.

title: Volleyball (Women's Rules)
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 140.

title: Cross Country Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginning skier the skills necessary to reach the more advanced level of cross country skiing. Takes the skier from short, closein trails to longer, more challenging trails offered at several Indiana State Parks.

title: Field Handball
description: An international team field sport similar to soccer.

title: Distance Running
description: Designed for people who like to run for physical fitness. Students are expected to start at 1-2 mile distances and progress up to 35-40 minutes of running. Prerequisite: must be in condition to run 2 miles on first day.

title: Flag Football
description: Introduction to fundamentals and rules of football through flag football; instruction in techniques, terminology, strategies, and rules.

title: Beginning Basketball (Women's Rules)
description: For students desiring information, practice, and experience in basic skills, strategies, and knowledge. Course includes passing, shooting, dribbling, offense, defense.

title: Beginning Fencing
description: Basic techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and courtesies. Includes positions, footwork, parries, and lunges.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and/or increase physical fitness and aid in weight control.

title: Volleyball (Coed Rules)
description: Provides beginner with an understanding of rules and skills underlying optimal enjoyment for power volleyball.

title: Pocket Billiards
description: Assists the student in the rudimentary skills and knowledge of the sport.

title: Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginner the mechanics of snow skiing, equipment choice, and care of equipment, plus offering a laboratory experience of several days of skiing on available slopes. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Orienteering
description: Designed to introduce the student to the activity of orienteering, a sport in which the participant utilizes the skills of land navigation using maps and compassreading skills. Circulorespiratory fitness is emphasized in distance running for time.

title: Gymnastics
description: Elementary movement performance on flat mats and apparatus.

title: Beginning Gymnastics (Women's Apparatus)
description: Instruction in the basic stunts and creative routines on the following pieces of apparatus: trampoline, balance beam, uneven parallel bars, ropes, and rings. Prerequisite: PEG 107 or equivalent.

title: Rhythmic Gymnastics
description: Combines gymnastics, dance, and implement manipulation with basic movement skills aimed at body control and grace in developing individual and group routines. Implements include hoops, wands, Indian clubs, ropes, scarves, and balls.

title: Weight Training (Women's Activities)
description: Designed to help students develop a basic personalized program for developing and maintaining strength for both overall conditioning and activities in which women participate.

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic exercise routines performed to music.

title: Casting and Angling
description: An introduction to the basic principles of casting and angling along with the practical application of how to catch fish.

title: Sports Acrobatics
description: A course designed to provide men and women with instruction in the rules and techniques of sports acrobatics.

title: Basic Roller Skating
description: 201.$$ Swimming 1. (1) Phase two of a program designed to assist the student toward becoming an efficient swimmer. Students who can swim in deep water are eligible.

title: Swimming 2
description: Students who are interested in advancing their swimming skills or are preparing to specialize in aquatics should consider this course. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Aquatic Lifeguarding
description: A preparatory course for students who are highly skilled swimmers and are interested in becoming lifeguards. The American National Red Cross certification in lifesaving may be earned in this course. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Synchronized Swimming Techniques
description: Introduces the student to stroke modifications, standard figures, sculling techniques, and floating patterns. Prerequisite: PEG 201, or permission of the department head.

title: Beginning Springboard Diving
description: Designed to assist the student in developing the basic skills used in dives from a onemeter height springboard. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Scuba
description: Selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus techniques and the scientific laws pertaining to that activity. Nationally recognized association divers certification may be earned in this class. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Aquatic Sports and Games
description: Low organizational games, contests, and more advanced aquatic sports. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Basic Canoeing
description: An introduction to movement control of a canoe as a type of small craft. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department head.

title: Beginning Judo
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 108 or PEG 214.

title: Intermediate Judo
description: Prerequisite: PEG 210 or permission of the department head. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 108 or PEG 214.

title: Intermediate Folk Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 112.

title: Intermediate Square Dance
description: Prerequisite: PEG 113.

title: Advanced Judo
description: Emphasis placed on understanding and practicing intermediate judo techniques, international contest rules and skills, and teaching methods that will enable one to teach beginning judo. Prerequisite: PEG 211.

title: Intermediate Modern Dance
description: A progression of technical skills in modern dance movement beyond the beginning level and in preparation for an advanced level of movement skill. Prerequisite: PEG 115.

title: Advanced Modern Dance
description: For students already skilled in dance who wish to increase their performing and technical aptitude in dance either for vocational or nonvocational reasons. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Handball
description: Introductory skills for playing handball. Basic skills, strategy, rules, and courtesy measures stressed. Designed for the student with little prior experience.

title: Racquetball
description: Instruction in the basic skills, strategies, and knowledge required to play racquetball. tt This course is administered as a learning and/or testout program during the regular school year (September-May).
