EDPSY 290 (may be taken prior to enrollment in EDSEC 299, EDJHM 312, o r EDEL 360, but paralel enrolment is recomended) Teacher education programs at Ball State University have been designed to include a number of planned, sequential courses which incorporate laboratory experiences in educational settings as integral parts of curricular offerings. These prestudent teaching laboratory experiences culminate in the EDEL 360, EDSEC 299, and EDJHM 312 courses which require assignment to classrooms in appropriate educational settings for one quarter to observe, prepare instructional presentations, and undertake other instructional tasks appropriate for students prior to student teaching. Ball State University provides laboratory settings for EDEL 360, EDJHM 312, and EDSEC 299 in the oncampus Burris Laboratory School, as well as in affiliated public school systems. Burris is an opendistrict school with an educational program for children from kindergarten through grade twelve. University students who are preparing to become teachers may have these experiences in the Burris School, in Muncie City Schools, and/or in other school corporations within commuting distance. Weekly seminars with a college supervisor are integral parts of the laboratory experiences for these courses. General Considerations The student must be free of outside commitments that might interfere with fulltime student teaching obligations. This means that students cannot be regularly employed, nor should they carry a heavy load of extracurricular activities. Enrollment for course overload during the quarter is permitted only with approval of the Coordinator for Student Teaching. A predetermined number of days in seminars conducted by the university supervisor, both at the beginning and the end of the quarter, are a part of the student teaching requirement. Increased demands for professionally licensed supervising teachers resulting from increased enrollment in student teaching have made assignments more difficult in many schools throughout the state, while assignments in Muncie public schools have been difficult for several years. Therefore, students should be ready to accept assignments wherever the university supervisor can situate them for the best professional experience. Department of Counseling Psychology and Guidance Services Hollis, Chairperson; Anzivino, Ballenger, Barrick, Baumann, Beyerl, Cartwright, Daly, Dirnick, Donn, Duckworth, Dunham, Ervin, Hayes, Hendrickson, Hulse, Hutchinson, Krause, Mitchell, Nunnelly, Randolph, Shapiro, Suozzi, White, Zimmerman The Department of Counseling Psychology and Guidance Services is one of two psychology departments within the Teachers College. The department offers an undergraduate minor in interpersonal relations. The minor is available for students seeking a combination and integration of didactic and experiential work dealing with basic psychological principles and techniques for understanding and developing interpersonal relationships. Emphasis is placed on understanding oneself and the dynamics of interaction with others. Opportunity is provided for an individual to explore his/her own strengths and weaknesses in interpersonal relationships within groups of varying ages, races, and ethnic backgrounds. The focus is applied and interdisciplinary. The program focuses also on strategies for gaining life satisfaction and meaning. Undergraduate courses are offered to students as electives or as courses applicable toward a certification program as a school counselor. The department offers graduate programs in counseling psychology and counseling and guidance, with emphasis on the interdisciplinary approach and with depth in psychology. Programs are designed for students wishing to qualify for positions as counselors, directors of counseling and guidance programs, and counseloreducators, as well as for those pursuing a degree in counseling psychology. The department also offers courses and programs in social psychology. title: Career and Life Planning
description: Focus is on helping the individual to make career and life plans. A series of techniques (role playing, psychodrama, sociodrama, value clarification, and decision making) will be utilized to help each student to examine his or her interrelated value systems associated with education, work, leisure, and self expression. (4) Focus on helping the individual student consider the special problems confronting women in making career and life plans. Would also be helpful for males who will be associated with women in nontraditional roles. A series of techniques (role playing, group interaction, value clarification, and decisionmaking strategies) will be utilized to facilitate students' examining their interrelated value system associated with education, career, family, leisure, and selfexpression.

title: Intrapersonal Relationships
description: An introduction to the examination of one's thoughts and feeling about self and how these internal processes relate to behavior. Particular attention will be given to understanding selflimiting behaviors such as anxiety, shyness, and selfdoubt and Educational Administration and Supervision 343 potential strategies for change. The course will assist students in understanding how they limit their own accomplishments, thus freeing them for a more successful academic career.

title: Interrelational Aspects of Sexuality
description: Emphasizes the psychological aspects of human sexuality especially in relation to emotions, attitude, and values. The psychological importance of responsibility for self, in the area of sexuality, will be stressed. This course will further consider the psychological aspects of human sexual development, adjustment, dysfunction, and remediation. The course is designed to increase the students' understanding and acceptance of their own sexuality and that of others. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Effective Interpersonal Relationship Development
description: An introduction to the basic psychological principles and techniques of developing interpersonal relationships. Emphasis on understanding oneself and the dynamics of interaction with others. Opportunity is provided for an individual to explore his/her strengths and weaknesses in interpersonal relationships within groups of varying ages, races, and ethnic background.

title: Fundamentals of Counseling and Guidance
description: Exploration of the principles, purposes, and nature of counseling and guidance in the public school with emphasis upon ways in which teachers can contribute to and profit from the school's guidance program.

title: Psychological Processes and Techniques of Interviewing
description: Basic psychological principles and techniques of the therapeutic interviewing process. Intended primarily as an exploratory didactic and experiential course for undergraduate students planning to do graduate work in counseling and related areas, or for those in other fields requiring skills in interviewing.

title: Techniques of Crisis Intervention
description: Basic theory, skills, and techniques of emergency psychological intervention and counseling with persons who experience intense situational and emotional distress. Emphasis placed on anxiety reactions, psychology of suicide, suicide prevention, special crisis situations, psychology of referral, community resources, use of listening and responding skills, and techniques of training crisis counselors.

title: Problems in Counseling
description: Intensive study in selected areas of student need and interest within the field of counseling. Opportunity for students to choose particular areas for indepth study under faculty supervision. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned,

title: Interdisciplinary Issues in Social Psychology and History
description: A unified approach through social psychology and history relating to selected areas of current interest. Deals with contemporary research and publications from both foreign and American cultures. title: Human Growth and Development
description: Development of personality in the Western world from birth through adolescence and application to life in the family, school, community, and in broader social situations. Emphasis is placed upon physical, motor, social, emotional, and cognitive development and their interweaving relationships, particularly as they apply to the school setting. Should be taken during the sophomore year. PSYSC 100 is a highly recommended elective.

title: Human Growth and Development
description: Development of personality in the Western world, beginning at birth, but placing special emphasis upon the period from preadolescence through adolescence. Emphasis is placed upon physical, motor, social, emotional, and cognitive development and their interweaving relationships, particularly as they apply to the school setting. Should be taken during the sophomore year and is intended for students planning to teach in secondary schools. PSYSC 100 is a highly recommended elective.

title: Educational Psychology
description: Psychological principles underlying learning and the improvement of teaching, tests and measurements. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250 or 251, except that students with a departmental major in dietetics or junior high/middle school education need not take EDPSY 250 or 251. PSYSC 100 is a highly recommended elective.

title: Independent Study: Educational Psychology
description: Individually planned experiences, extensive study in the area of independent research in educational psychology. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Behavior Analysis in Education
description: Assists students to translate learning principles into teaching practices, to design and implement behavior analysis procedures which enhance motivation and learning in educational settings and decrease behavior problems, and to assess the effects of such instructional techniques.

title: Psychology of Later Life
description: A study of the later years of life with emphasis on the adaptations required. Includes theories of aging, physical and social changes taking place, and coping strategies. Not open to the student who has credit in EDGER 325.

title: Educational Tests and Measurement
description: Standard educational tests and the use of such tests as instruments for the evaluation of learning. Techniques of test construction.

title: Individual and Group Intelligence Testing
description: Nature of intelligence and its measurement. Study of selected tests for normal and exceptional persons with special emphasis on development of elementary psychometric skills.

title: Child Psychology
description: Developmental study of the psychology of childhood, giving special attention to children from five to fourteen years of age.

title: Adolescent Psychology
description: A study of childhood influences upon the adolescent period, of the psychology of the adolescent period, and of the effects of that development during young adulthood. Emphasis is placed upon various psychological influences contributing to adolescent development.

title: Adult Psychology
description: Developmental study of psychological stages of adulthood. Not open to the student who has credit in EDAC 355.

title: Honors Colloquium in Educational Psychology
description: Designed to acquaint honors students with concepts and issues in educational psychology. Emphasis on independent study to culminate in a product representative of the student with honors. Prerequisite: students on the Honors Program or by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Mental Hygiene
description: Psychological principles underlying mental health and the application of these principles in and out of the classroom . Prerequisite: 8 hours of psychology.

title: Seminar in Educational Psychology
description: Group or individual investigation and study of current issues, problems, and developments in human development, classroom learning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. title: Introduction to Teaching in the Elementary School: Seminar and Laboratory
description: Work with elementary schoolage children of a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds with opportunities through seminars and counseling to plan and evaluate experiences and to begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children as an orientation to teaching in the elementary school. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Lower-Division Laboratory Experience in Early Childhood Education
description: Supervised field experience for staff working in educational settings for young children. Open only to students enrolled on the twoyear early elementary education program. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Interaction Skills for the Young Child
description: Introduces students to basic skills which each young child needs to acquire in order to use language competently in society. Deals with materials, methods, principles of learning, and conditions necessary for optimum learning.

title: Lower-Division Practicum in Early Childhood Education
description: Focuses on the young child and his/her learning environment and how adults apply this knowledge in early childhood education. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Elementary School Classroom Organization and Management: Laboratory and Seminar
description: The role of the teacher as the facilitator for learning in the elementary classroom with particular attention to understanding the child as a growing, learning person and to affirming and expediting his/her growth and learning goals. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Writing
description: Development of skills in manuscript and cursive writing, methods of teaching handwriting in the elementary school, and relationship of manuscript and cursive writing to the language arts.

title: Human Relations in School
description: Development of understandings and skills needed for effective teacherpupil, teacherparent, and teacherteacher relationships in school settings for young children. Open to students enrolled on the twoyear elementary education program, or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Child Care Services 1
description: Selection and organization of learning experiences appropriate for individual children. Need identification, identification of appropriate child care facilities, and the students' roles as members of a staffing team. Open only to students on the twoyear early elementary education program.

title: Child Care Services 2
description: Selection and organization of learning experiences appropriate for individual children. Need identification, identification of appropriate child care facilities, and the students' roles as members of a staffing team. Prerequisite: EDEL 240. Open only to students on the twoyear early elementary education program.

title: Creative Experiences for Young Children
description: Designed to develop awareness of, and skill in, providing creative experiences for the young child. Working with children is an integral part of the course.

title: Lower Division Laboratory Experience in Early Elementary Education 2
description: Provides experience in assisting the classroom teacher in the implementation of educational opportunities for young children under supervision of a university faculty member and/or an agency representative. Emphasizes evaluation of the child and the program in conjunction with the classroom teacher. Role differentiation is stressed. Prerequisite: minimum of 36 hours in early elementary education courses, always including EDEL 160.

title: Materials and Techniques for Teaching Children of Multiethnic Backgrounds
description: Designed to offer multisensory approaches to learning. Attempts will be made to identify learning methods and materials best suited to the student's style of learning.

title: Mediation of Instructional Design
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology to improvement of teaching and learning in elementary school classrooms.

title: Principles of Teaching and Classroom Management: Elementary School
description: Problems of school organization, management, control, and environment in relation to the learning activities of children. Legal rights and responsibilities of teachers and use of instructional media are stressed. Prerequisite: approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290, except for majors in Special Education.

title: The Teaching of Language Arts in the Lower Elementary Grades
description: Development of language arts skills—listening, speaking, reading, and writing—in the primary grades.

title: The Social, Historical, and Philosophical Foundations of Elementary Education
description: Emphasizes historical and social derivations of contemporary educational ideas, philosophical foundations for educational practices, alternatives for ethical decisions in education, and formulation of a personal philosophical position related to educational issues in elementary education.

title: Discipline and Classroom Management: Some Practical Approaches
description: Designed to help beginning elementary school teachers create and maintain effective learning environments. Emphasizes practical approaches to prevention and remediation of disruptive classroom behavior.

title: The Parent in Early Childhood Education
description: Explores important and complex roles of parents and parent substitutes in the educational development of young children. Factors affecting parent/child interactions and skills needed for effective parenting are studied and related to the educational process. Parent involvement as a significant factor in early childhood education is included. 440g. Kindergarten Education. (4) Development of the kindergartenprimary curriculum with special emphasis on kindergarten children and procedures to be used in their development. 442g. Nursery School Education. (4) Guidance of young children. Observation and evaluation of the activities of children between the ages of two and six. Organization, administration, and educational program of nursery schools. Child development and parent education as parts of nursery school education. Use of the physician, nurse, and nutritionist.

title: Home, School, and Community Relationships in Early Childhood Education
description: Involves experiences to enrich the relationships among parents, teachers, and children in the home, school, and community environments and to acquaint and involve students with the variety of community resources concerned with the welfare of young children and their families.

title: Education of the Culturally Different Child
description: Provides students in elementary education with a broad understanding of characteristics of economically disadvantaged and culturally different children requisite to dealing realistically with their needs. Stresses consideration of teacher self attitudes towards economically disadvantaged and culturally different children as well as examination of promising instructional changes and approaches for improving learning opportunities for these children. Motivation, classroom organization, discipline, parentteacher relationships, school integration, and nonstandard dialect are emphasized. 452g. Psychology of Early Childhood. (4) Study of young children of nursery school and kindergarten age involving lectures, readings, discussions, and conferences to give individual guidance to students and help them interpret their study of the physical, mental, social, and emotional development of selected young children. Consideration is given to growth in perception, language, expression, and interests.

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 460 (4) and EDEL 464 (10) for a total of 14 quarter hours, requiring 11 weeks of fulltime student teaching. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 464 (10) and EDEL 460 (4) for a total of 14 quarter hours, requiring 11 weeks of fulltime student teaching. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Elementary
description: Parttime student teaching for 11 weeks in an area of endorsement. Taken in a different quarter and in addition to the regular student teaching requirement for elementary education. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Pre-Kindergarten
description: Designed to provide students preparing to teach children in prekindergarten the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program, Prerequisite: EDEL 360.

title: Student Teaching: Primary Grades
description: Designed to provide students preparing to teach in primary grades the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Must be taken in conjunction with EDEL 468. Prerequisite: EDEL 360.

title: Student Teaching: Kindergarten
description: Designed to provide students preparing to teach in kindergarten the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Must be taken in conjunction with EDEL 467. Prerequisite: EDEL 360.

title: Practicum in Elementary Education
description: Laboratory and seminar course involving a study of progressive school practices, the philosophy of education underlying, and the possibilities of using, progressive practices in the public school. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Elementary Education
description: Independent study and research in the field of elementary education. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Elementary Education
description: An analysis of one's professional preparation for teaching, identifying areas in which students need to bolster weaknesses and augment strengths, and arranging for more preparation in these areas. Prerequisite: one term of student teaching, EDUCATION: READING (f.DRDG) 105, Self-Improvement in Reading. (2) Individualized evaluation and diagnosis of specific strengths and weaknesses in reading is followed by practice to improve comprehension skills, reading speed, vocabulary, notetaking, and content reading. Enrollment with approval of the director of reading. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Prereading Development
description: Basic understanding of environments and planned activities that foster positive attitudes and interests related to reading, procedures that stimulate prereading development, and related practical experiences with young children.

title: The Teaching of Reading in Today's Schools
description: Designed to review the current thinking, approaches, and methodology of teaching reading in today's schools. Attention is directed to readiness, word recognition and analysis, comprehension, and planning of the total developmental reading program, with emphasis on reading at the elementary level.

title: Study of Selected Aspects of the Elementary School Reading Program
description: Designed to review the current thinking and approaches to teaching reading in the elementary school, and the relationship of basic psychological principles to teaching practices. Prerequisite or parallel: one term of student teaching at the elementary school level.

title: Corrective Reading in the Classroom
description: Provides prospective teachers with understanding of difficulties in reading plus practical experience in assessing reading difficulties and in study of corrective treatment. Includes guided laboratory situations with students exhibiting reading limitations who can be aided by the regular classroom teacher. Prerequisite: EDRDG 400 or EDRDS 420 or EDRDM 421.

title: Reading Approaches and Strategies
description: Provides prospective classroom teachers (K-12) with opportunities to study and utilize various approaches and strategies used in teaching reading. Includes evaluation of related instructional materials. Prerequisite: EDRDG 430.

title: Practicum in Reading
description: Provides experiences for prospective teachers (K-12) in (1) grouping students of varying abilities in reading; (2) planning arid implementing a classroom reading program appropriate for these students. Prerequisite: EDRDG 435.

title: Independent Study in Reading
description: Designed to meet the needs of students wishing to study in individually selected areas of reading education. Enrollees must have completed 8 hours in reading education. Prerequisite: permission of the director of reading. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. EDUCATION: READING SECONDARY (EDRDS)

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: See the Department of Secondary, Higher, a nd Foundations of Education. EDUCATION: READING MIDDLE (EDRDM)

title: Improving General Reading Skills in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: See the Department of Secondary, Higher, and Foundations of Education. Smith, Swanger, Veselack, Watson, Weber, Wickersham Burris School, the laboratory school of Ball State University, has the following responsibilities: First, the school is obligated to provide for the teacher education program at Ball State University: —a center in which both preservice and inservice teachers can observe sound educational practices; —a laboratory in which prospective teachers can gain firsthand experiences with youth in teachinglearning situations prior to student teaching; —a center for experimentation in which diverse hypotheses and methods for improving education can be formulated, studied, and tested critically and reconstructed continuously in the light of the evidence gathered; and —a center which contributes to the improvement of educational practices in the state and nation by publicizing new practices and research findings of the laboratory school and by providing consultant and leadership services for the public schools. Second, the school is obligated to provide for all youth who attend the school from kindergarten through grade twelve: —an effective and sound community school which respects the worth of each individual and provides opportunities for the development of the wide range of individual potentialities found in youth; —a living and learning environment in which all youth have opportunities for cooperative living and for the development of those values and skills vital to all citizens in a free society; and —a curricular program which, in keeping abreast of contemporary problems and in strengthening the foundations of a free society, results in functional understanding of technological development, practical knowledge of economic problems, broad appreciation for world cultures, real appreciation for beauty in the arts, deep respect for human relationships, and sincere concern for the development of a workable philosophy of life coupled with respect for self. Burris School maintains a working relationship with all of the colleges of the university. Center for Lifelong Education Craddock, Chairman; Atwood, Bailey, Danglade, Fallon, Fisher, Foster, Greenwood, Hatton, Hoyt, Janove, Kaluzynski, Lucas, McClure, McElhinney, McGinnis, Murk, Nisbet, Ratliff, Rawlings, Thompson, Van Ness, Weaver, Wood Learning neither starts nor terminates with formal education. It is a lifelong process. Recognizing this, the Center for Lifelong Education is concerned with encompassing and unifying all stages of education. Lifelong education includes both formal and informal patterns of education and experiential learning. Education begins with the family and moves into society as a child begins to interact with nonfamily individuals. The formal institutions of education are important but they constitute only part of many social agencies providing opportunities for individuals to learn, To promote lifelong education, Ball State University established the Center for Lifelong Education and specifically charged it with providing formal and informal programs which would prepare individuals to design, implement, and coordinate educational opportunities throughout their lives. In the formal portion of this task, the center either offers or directs the following programs of study, mostly at the graduate level: M.A. Adult Education; M.A. Applied Gerontology; M.A. Community Education; M.A. Executive Development for Public Service ; M.A.E. Curiculum; Ed.S. Doctoral Cognates in Curiculum; Ed.D. Adult and Community Education; Departmental Minor in Gerontology (see Interdepartmental); and seminars for the older returning undergraduate students. In addition, the center serves as a vehicle within the Teachers College through which interdisciplinary educational services, both formal and informal, not traditionally offered by a ny curent Teachers Colege department or service unit, may be developed, implemented, and coordinated. Current informal programs include: research, school curriculum studies, program evaluation, nontraditional students, inservice professional development programs, retirement planning, and related service activities. EDUCATION: ADULT AND COMMUNITY (EDAC)

title: Seminar in Facilitating Lifelong Learning
description: A seminar course for nontraditional students which will provide an opportunity to explore, discuss, and reenforce new changes in self as a learner and as a group participator. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar on the Evolving Roles of American Men and Women
description: A course for nontraditional students which provides an indepth look at a history of rights and roles of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and twentiethcentury American men and women. Prerequisite: EDAC 101 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar on Investigation into Job Opportunities
description: A field course for nontraditional students which will provide opportunities for exploration into job opportunities or advancements through placement experiences in work settings, depth interviews and visitations, and directed readings. Emphasis is on problem solving, acquiring firsthand knowledge in order to make realistic career decisions by older male and female students. Prerequisite: EDAC 101, 102, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar on Comprehensive Programming for Lifelong Learning
description: Assist nontraditional students to prepare portfolios on learning obtained through life experiences and to develop comprehensive plans for continuous learning throughout their life spans.

title: The Adult Learner in the Undergraduate Classroom
description: A seminar for the adult learner which will provide an opportunity to examine the university setting, values expressed in the classroom by faculty and students, and the dynamics of higher education in terms of the student's own developing values.

title: Adult Education
description: The history and current status of adult education in the United States and in selected foreign countries; the nature, scope, purposes, and historical development of adult education institutions and program areas; an introduction to and overview of adult education as a field of study and practice.

title: The Adult as a Learner
description: Designed to familiarize students with implications of learning theories for education of adults in a variety of learning situations and to develop skills in use of applicable methods and techniques.

title: Adult Psychology
description: Developmental study of psychological stages of adulthood. Not open to the student who has credit in EDPSY 355.

title: Volunteers and Voluntarism
description: An analysis of the historical, theoretical, philosophical, and operational perspectives of voluntarism. Attention will be given to developing new and innovative models for volunteer programs based on field experience, readings, and course sessions.

title: The Community Educator
description: Designed to familiarize the student with the structure, purpose, and processes of community education development with emphasis on the development of skills and competencies required of a community education coordinator.

title: Workshop in Adult and/or Community Education
description: A course for persons who wish to participate in preservice or inservice training in the areas of adult and/or community education. Specific content will depend upon interests of the participants. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. EDUCATION: CURRICULUM (EDCUR)

title: Curriculum Construction
description: Principles to be used in determining the nature and content of the learner's experiences in the public school. The issue of essentialism and progressivism, teacherpupil planning, the larger use of group action in the solution of problems, and betterment of relation between problem solving and principles operative in these problems.

title: Psychology of Later Life
description: A study of the later years of life with emphasis on the adaptations required. Includes theories of aging, physical and social changes taking place, and coping strategies. Not open to the student who has credit in EDPSY 325.

title: Educational Gerontology
description: A study of education and aging with emphasis on a lifespan approach. Topics include education about aging for children and youth, career educational opportunities in gerontology, education for paraprofessionals and volunteers in the field of aging, retirement planning education, and educational opportunities for older adults.

title: Workshop in Applied Gerontology
description: Preservice or inservice education in selected areas of applied gerontology using a workshop format of concentrated study, presentation, demonstrations, and practice. Specific content will depend upon the problems or interest area to which the workshop is addressed. The learner is encouraged to work out a program of personal study with help from other workshop participants and resource persons. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned. Credit may be applied to the minor in gerontology only with permission of the director of the Institute of Gerontology.

title: Topical Seminar in Applied Gerontology
description: Individual and group investigation of topics, problems, or issues in applied gerontology with discussion of them by all seminar participants under the guidance of the instructor. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. Credit may be applied to the minor in gerontology only with permission of the director of the Institute of Gerontology.

title: Internship in Gerontology
description: Experience in one or more of the agencies, institutions, or programs now providing gerontological services or otherwise related to the field of gerontology. The internship is carried out under the joint supervision of the Institute of Gerontology and a practitioner representing the agency, institution, or program. The student chooses the internship setting with the guidance of a faculty sponsor and the approval of the practitioner. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. PREPARATION OF TEACHERS FOR MULTICULTURED SECONDARY SCHOOLS (MULTICUL) The MULTICUL program at Ball State University offers young people an opportunity to translate objectives, expressions, and demonstrations into actuality. 'The ultimate objectives lead toward possible solutions to one of America's crucial problems, developing racial and cultural harmony. The program is designed to deal not only with black and white relations, but with as many ethnic groups as possible. Multiculturism is a basic characteristic of our society as well as our schools; therefore, potential teachers should prepare themselves to meet realistic situations. Three of the experiences that the MULTICUL program utilizes in the preparation of potential teachers are as follows: 1. Specialized or elective courses offered in many major departments. 2. Courses designed especially for MULTICUL students by the Department of Secondary, Higher, and Foundations of Education. 3. Laboratory experiences in multicultural communities, social and professional organizations, and schools. Prerequisite waived for students enrolled for this endorsement. Along with learning how to understand and how to coexist peacefully with fellow Americans, the participants in MULTICUL should he more employable, not only in Indiana, but across the nation. MULTICUL does not prohibit students from majoring in their areas of interest. MULTICUL is offered as a departmental minor, and it can be scheduled along with any teaching major at Ball State. Departmental minor in the preparation of teachers for multicultured secondary schools, 24 hours EDSEC 200 (4 hrs.), 206, 301, 400 15 hrs. Electives approved by the department 9 hrs.

title: School in the American Culture
description: An introduction to the theory, scope, organization, and functions of the public school in the United States. The student will examine the role of public education at all levels at which it operates and the responsibilities carried out by the professional teachers in their educational work.

title: International Dialogue on American Education and Life
description: Perspectives on American education and its cultural setting developed through interaction among international and American students and comparative study of educational and other social institutions as they relate to education.

title: The Role of Women in the Past, Present, and Future Development of Education
description: A survey of the role of women in education with an emphasis on analysis of career development, styles of work, and job satisfaction. EDUCATION: HIGHER (EDHI)

title: Introduction to Personnel Services in Residence Halls
description: Principles involved in understanding and working with individuals and student groups in residence halls, social forces affecting college students, and the relationship of the residence hall program to the total university. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned; a maximum of 1 credit hour per quarter.

title: Leadership and Development of Student Organizations
description: Examines philosophical bases, group processes, and skills relevant to leadership and development of student organizations in higher education. Focuses on understandings and skills requisite for effective involvement in student groups. EDUCATION: JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE (EDJHM)

title: Exploration of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Analyzes factors which influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis will be on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American junior high/middle schools. Not open to the student with credit in EDSEC 205.

title: Teaching in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Develops basic instructional strategies for junior high/middle schools. Topics include general methods, problems of student advisement, legal considerations, classroom management, and instructional media, in the light of study of the nature of junior high/middle school children. Specific laboratory experiences are emphasized. Prerequisite: EDJHM 205, EDPSY 351 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Application of Instructional Strategies and Approaches in Junior High/Middle School
description: Factors affecting the total instructional responsibilities in junior high/middle schools are studied. Students are required to develop skills in individualizing instruction to serve the full range of students, the ability to work cooperatively with other professional personnel, and instructional techniques and evaluation procedures especially appropriate for junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDJHM 205 or EDSEC 205 and EDPSY 251 or 351. Not open to the student who has credit in EDSEC 313.

title: Mediation of Instructional Design: Junior High/Middle School
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology in the improvement of teaching and learning in junior high/middle school classrooms.

title: The Junior High/Middle School Curriculum
description: Several curricular approaches appropriate for pupils in the age group 10 to 14 years will be examined in relation to current research. Legal rights and the significance of positive human relations are studied. Direct development of alternative curricular programs and appropriate use of merging structures and nontraditional materials will be emphasized. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312.

title: Foundations of Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Junior high/middle school education as an institution in society and its relationship to the individual and American culture from the perspective of the sociological, philosophical, historical, legal, economic, political, and anthropological foundations of junior high/middle schools and teachers are stressed. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312.

title: Discipline: Practical Approaches to Improving Student Behavior in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective junior high/middle school educators to cope with discipline problems in all junior high/middle school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures in preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by junior high/middle school students and ways to create positive environments for learning.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Junior High/Middle School
description: This elective student teaching experience will enable a student to complete a full quarter assignment in fullday student teaching assignments in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDJHM 466.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the Standard License in Junior High/Middle School Education. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Advanced Undergraduate Practicum in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Provides direct, supervised experiences for students wishing to gain increased skill and knowledge regarding junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312 or EDSEC 299 or EDEL 360. EDUCATION: READING MIDDLE (EDRDM)

title: Improving Reading Skills in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: A general course for all junior high/middle school teachers which examines reading problems and provides specific methodology for improvement of reading skills in junior high/middle schools. General diagnostic teaching techniques appropriate for teachers in all curricular areas are to be achieved. Exit competencies are required. EDUCATION: READING SECONDARY (EDRDS)

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: Practical procedures for developing effective reading skills to be applied by all secondary classroom teachers. Focuses on relationships between the process of reading and learning of content, on planning to meet total range of student reading needs, and on methods and materials to enhance comprehension and study skills in all areas of secondary school curriculum. EDUCATION: SECONDARY (EDSEC)

title: Introduction to Secondary Education for Paraprofessionals
description: Study of American junior and senior high schools from the standpoint of the paraprofessional in secondary education. Prerequisite: admission to the secondary paraprofessional program. Parallel: EDSEC 111.

title: Freshman Paraprofessional Practicum
description: The organization and operation of secondary schools and the duties, procedures, and problems of secondary school faculty and staff. Provides initial experiences in assisting secondary faculty and staff. Prerequisite: admission to the secondary paraprofessional program. Parallel: EDSEC 110.

title: Basic Concepts of Secondary Education
description: Examines through classroom investigation and practical field experiences the structure, function, and development of secondary education in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about preparing for and functioning in a teaching career by studying professionalism, job requirements, employment opportunities, secondary school curriculum, and the role of secondary education within the entire educational process.

title: Introduction to Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Introduces prospective teachers to responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 100 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Intermediate Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Continued study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 200 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Advanced Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Advanced study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 201 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Exploration of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Secondary Schools
description: Analyzes factors which influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis will be on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American secondary schools. Not open to students with credit in EDJHM 205.

title: Advanced Study of Concepts in the Exploration of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Schools
description: Course will focus on indepth analyses of many of the concepts introduced in EDSEC 205. Particular emphasis placed on variables which contribute to the development and maintenance of prejudice, stereotypes, racism, and oppressive conditions. Equally emphasized will be instructional strategies for combating such behaviors. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or EDJHM 205 or permission of the department chairman. Not open to the student who has credit in EDSEC 100.

title: Laboratory Experience in Secondary Education
description: Provides direct experiences in working with students, teachers, paraprofessionals, community agencies, and other appropriate assignments for undergraduate students who plan to enter secondary school teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned; no more than 4 hours may be taken in one quarter.

title: The Secondary Paraprofessional and the Use of Instructional Technology
description: The use of instructional technology and the preparation of instructional materials as these skills are employed by the paraprofessional.

title: Secondary Paraprofessional Internship
description: Practical experiences in the duties, responsibilities, and related problems of the secondary school paraprofessional. The intern will be assigned to a secondary school during a regular school year for a period of one quarter. Prerequisite: EDSEC 110, 111.

title: Principles of Teaching and Classroom Management: Secondary School
description: Inducts the student into the teaching act. Includes specific technical skill development, legal implications, study of principles of teaching, application of instructional media, curriculum development and organization, classroom management, and discipline. Intensive inschool assignments, observation, skills, participation, and direct contact with adolescents are required. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205, EDPSY 251, and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290.

title: Instructional Strategies in Multicultured Schools
description: Theory and application of special instructional strategies of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms with special emphasis on multicultured educational situations. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or EDJHM 205 or permission of the department chairman.

title: American Education: A Critical Examination
description: The complex educational system and alternatives to the traditional system, featuring an individualized, issueoriented instructional approach. Designed for students who do not plan to teach but open to those in t eacher education.

title: Mediation of Instructional Design
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology to improvement of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms.

title: Planning and Assessing Instructional Programs
description: Designed to provide secondary school teachers with methods of establishing instructional programs with feedback networks which will encourage continuous assessment and appropriate alterations of the educational environment. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Independent Study in Secondary Education
description: Independent study and research in the field of secondary education. Topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an individual instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of four hours of credit may be earned.

title: Contemporary Problems in Education and Professional Concerns of the Beginning Teacher
description: Provides opportunity to examine critically and to focus educational experience and knowledge on contemporary and personally significant problems of education. Emphasizes immediate professional concerns of prospective firstyear teachers. Prerequisite: EDSEC 301 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Social Foundations of Secondary Education
description: Education as an institution in society and its relationship to the individual and American culture from the perspective of the sociological, philosophical, historical, economic, political, and anthropological foundations of secondary education. Contemporary issues such as cultural values, social class, legal aspects, ethnic groups, political pressure, and the role of the teachers will be stressed. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299.

title: High School Curriculum
description: General perspectives of curriculum principles, practices, and procedures common to secondary schools. Organizational structures, innovations, and intimate relationships between instruction and curriculum. Concurrently, students will choose areas of concentration or preparation as they relate to the total high school curriculum.

title: Student Activities Programs in Secondary Schools
description: Student activities will be studied in terms of historical development, philosophical foundations, objectives, functions, current role and status, principles and procedures of development, organizational patterns, and innovative programs. Accommodates needs and interests of individuals preparing to be involved in student activities programs in secondary schools.

title: The School Community and Secondary School Teaching
description: Focuses on the total school community as a broad teaching resource for every classroom teacher. Examines a variety of resources available, importance of establishing solid relationships, impact of community on classroom and classroom on community, significance of the schoolcommunity interaction both for individual teacher and total school.

title: Discipline: Practical Approaches to Improving Student Behavior in Secondary Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective secondary teachers to cope with discipline problems in all secondary school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures for preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by secondary students and ways to create a positive environment for learning.

title: Career Education: Content and Processes for Secondary Educators
description: Career education concepts and attitudes and their effects analyzed in relation to effective implementation of career education in secondary schools. Techniques, methods, and materials identified and developed enabling prospective teachers to see meaningful relationships between career education and secondary curricular areas. The teaching of career identification skills and development of meaningful student work values examined. Course participants will develop a model for the inclusion of career education in their areas.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the Standard License in Secondary Education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the Standard License in Secondary Education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Secondary
description: Prerequisite or parallel: EDSEC 460, 462 or EDJHM 466; and admission to student teaching.

title: General Innovations in Secondary Education
description: Innovative practices will be identified, defined, and analyzed relative to their impact on secondary schools. Creative, innovative instructional approaches will be employed. Field trips or visitations to innovative secondary schools will be arranged when practical, and students will concentrate upon innovative practices.

title: Practicum in Boys' Club Administration
description: Offered in cooperation with Boys' Clubs of America. Students are assigned to Boys' Clubs where they are given an opportunity in all phases of program and administration with certain responsibilities for advanced problems in each of these areas. The course is largely under the direction of a visiting professor representing Boys' Clubs of America. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. Department of Special Education Lawyer, Chairperson; Ahlersmeyer, Duncan, Hargrove, Hoops, Merbler, Osgood, Poteet, Seitz, Spencer, A. Twining, J. Twining, Ulman, VanEvery, VanTassel The philosophy of special education encompasses the right of all children, youth, and adults to participate in educational and career planning experiences that will develop their capabilities to the fullest extent. Gradual acceptance of this philosophy by society has created an everincreasing demand for highly skilled personnel who are certified in the various exceptionality areas represented within special education. The Department of Special Education offers undergraduate programs leading to teacher certification in the areas of deaf education; mentally handicapped; moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped; and physically handicapped. Graduate programs are offered in areas of learningdisabled and emotionally disturbed as well as in the area of undergraduate preparation. These programs are designed in accordance with Indiana teacher licensure requirements. Elective courses in special education open to future teachers, psychologists, speech and hearing therapists, and social workers include a survey course of exceptional children, courses in the education of gifted children, a course in the education of slow learners, and a course in the education of children with learning disabilities. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE HEARING-IMPAIRED Mandatory legislation on the rights of all children to an appropriate education has created a nationwide need for additional teachers of the hearingimpaired. The emphasis on "mainstreaming" of exceptional children in the regular classroom developed a need for teachers of the hearingimpaired with more general preparation in addition to the specialized coursework for teachers of the deaf. Also, the growth of different communication philosophies made it essential to provide additional coursework options within the majors and minors. A major in the education of the deaf is offered to those who prefer some level of elementary teaching and a minor is available for persons who wish to teach an academic subject at the junior high and high school levels. The State of Indiana, Ball State University, and the Department of Special Education have adopted more extensive requirements for licensing and, at the same time, more flexible programs which can accommodate the above needs. The Ball State University program for training teachers of the hearingimpaired meets the approval of (I) The Indiana Teacher Training and Licensing Commission, (2) The Council on the Education of the Deaf (CED), and (3) the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE MENTALLY HANDICAPPED Acceptance of the philosophy of special education has led to the development of specialized programs for mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults. These programs have provided the impetus to prepare specially trained teachers to work effectively with mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped children, youth, and adults in the least restrictive instructional setting. Teachers and other interested professional personnel are taught the necessary skills to implement accepted intervention strategies for appropriately meeting the mentally handicapped individual's learning style and educational and career needs. In response to the nationwide demand for qualified teachers to serve mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults, the Department of Special Education offers a teaching area major in the area of the mildly handicapped and teaching minors in both the mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped areas. The teaching minor also serves as an endorsement in each of the exceptionality areas represented within the mentally handicapped area. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN WITH PHYSICAL AND/OR SPECIAL HEALTH PROBLEMS Within the group of children who have special educational needs are those who are physically handicapped (mildly and severely) and those who have other health conditions which make special class placement necessary. A typical classroom for these handicapped or healthimpaired children presents the teacher with a challenging variety of physical impairments as well as learning difficulties. To profit from their educational experience, these children are in need of specially prepared teachers with an understanding of the physical, psychological, and educational problems encountered in such a classroom, as well as knowledge of curriculum and methodology to meet these problems. The teacher education program is designed to offer comprehensive professional preparation to future teachers of physically handicapped (mildly and severely) or healthimpaired children so that these children will have the opportunity to learn and grow to the best of their ability under the guidance of competent, special teachers. title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: A survey of the educational needs of children who deviate from the normal in mental, physical, and social characteristics. Designed as an introduction to the field of special education.

title: Strategies for Developing Positive Concepts in Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool handicapped child's social and emotional stability. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Child Management Strategies for Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for more effectively managing the preschool handicapped child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Strategies for Individualizing Learning Opportunities for Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for serving preschool handicapped children in the least restrictive learning environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Practicum-Teaching Young Handicapped Children
description: Student works with handicapped children six years of age or younger in a supervised practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of handicapped children in the classroom. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned. t Students are expected to meet the prerequisite for MATH 391.

title: Strategies for Fostering Developmental Competence of Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool handicapped child's cognitive, language, and general learning environments. These developmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool handicapped children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: History of Education of the Deaf and the Psychology of Deafness
description: A brief study of educational provisions for the deaf from the beginning to the present and a survey of the social, educational, and vocational problems of deafness.

title: Education of Preschool Hearing/Language-Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Ear and Vocal Mechanism
description: Physical structure of the parts of the body used in speech and hearing. An equal stress on related physical defects and how they affect speech and understanding. Not open to the student who has credit in SPAA 261.

title: Practicum in Special Education
description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or may be taken parallel with SPCED 425. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Psychology of Mental Retardation
description: Various types and degrees of retardation. The psychological, environmental, and cultural factors which contribute toward retardation. Emphasis on etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate retarded children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 for majors in Special Education; SPCED 201 and EDPSY 290 for all other majors.

title: Characteristics of the Moderately, Severely, and Profoundly Retarded Individuals
description: Aspects of the intellectual, perceptualmotor, communication, academic, and personal social characteristics of the moderately, severely, and profoundly retarded. Procedures for formulating realistic instructional objectives will be explained. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 372.

title: Educational Methods with Moderately, Severely, and Profoundly Retarded Individuals
description: Current instructional planning for the moderately, severely, and profoundly retarded will be reviewed and evaluated. Attention will be focused upon techniques for effecting innovative curricula for individuals at the preschool through post school levels. Prerequisite: SPCED 373.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of definitions, characteristics, and identification procedures relating to gifted and talented children in school and society. Research findings pertaining to these topics will be reviewed and analyzed.

title: Education of Slow Learners
description: Major topics include identification, characteristics, and practices and procedures for meeting the needs of the slow learning child. Emphasis is placed on techniques and methods of instruction as well as research findings concerned with the slow learner and the culturally disadvantaged.

title: Learning Disabilities Techniques for the Regular Classroom Teacher
description: Emphasis on the role of the regular classroom teacher in relationship to legal, federal, and state mandates for identification, instruction, and programming for learning disabled students in the regular classroom. Prerequisite: senior status.

title: Basic Audiology
description: Methods of measuring hearing. Practice in use of various types of audiometers. Interpretation of test results for reeducation and necessary followup measures in an educational hearing program. Prerequisite: SPAA 261 or SPCED 261, SPAA 440, or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in SPAA 442.

title: Aural Rehabilitation
description: Fundamentals of the visible movements involved in speech and the various methods, techniques, and materials for teaching lipreading to the deaf and the hardofhearing. Use of auditory training and hearing aids for rehabilitation. Prerequisite: SPAA 440. Not open to the student who has credit in SPAA 444.

title: Speech Development for the Deaf
description: The International Phonetic Alphabet, Northhampton Charts, diacritical markings, and other methods and techniques used to teach speech to the deaf. Prerequisite: SPCH 216 and SPCED 240, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum in Speech for the Deaf
description: Observation of an individual working with preschool children in developmental speech. Time will also be devoted to speech improvement for older children. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 and 446 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Manual Communications
description: Theory and research underlying the language of signs and fingerspelling (manual alphabet) is considered. Development of receptive and expressive skills in manual communications is required. Required of students intending to student teach in schools or classes using total communication.

title: Advanced Manual Communication
description: A course in manual communication designed to improve conversational skill in signs and fingerspelling to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in a classroom for hearingimpaired children. Prerequisite: SPCED 451 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Language for the Deaf
description: Compares language development of hearing children with that of deaf children. Levels of abstraction and the difficulty encountered in both receptive and expressive language are examined. The philosophy underlying various methods of language teaching is studied. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and SPAA 370 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Language Methods for the Deaf
description: Language systems are studied and used in practice situations. Includes Fitzgerald Straight Language for the Deaf, Barry Five-Slate, Wing Symbols, and the Natural Method. Language outlines from different schools are used as supplementary aids. Prerequisite: SPCED 240, 266, and 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to the Deaf
description: Principles and methods of teaching reading to deaf children in the lower and higher grades; methods of teaching subjects such as arithmetic and science. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and 266 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Special Education
description: May be repeated by students fulfilling requirements for certification in a second exceptionality area. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Areas of Exceptionality
description: May be repeated by students fulfilling requirements for certification in a second exceptionality area. A total of 20 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Interpreting for the Deaf
description: A survey course to acquaint students with the fundamentals of interpreting for the deaf in special situations, familiarize them with professional behavioral guidelines unique to each setting, and develop beginning interpretive skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Expressive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Provides students who have basic manual communication skills with intensive training and practice in expressive interpreting for the deaf. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairman.

title: Receptive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Designed to provide students who have basic manual communication ability with professional skill for interpreting manual language in special situations. Opportunity for extensive practice and evaluation will be provided. Prerequisite: SPCED 468 or permission of the department chairman.

title: Educational Methods with the Mentally Retarded 1
description: Special class organization, curriculum practices and procedures, and the methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mentally retarded. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (2 hrs.) and 372.

title: Educational Methods with the Mentally Retarded 2
description: Continuation of SPCED 474, with emphasis on the curriculum. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (4 hrs.) and 474.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: This course is designed for future teachers of crippled or other healthimpaired children. Topics include etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate children with physical disabilities. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290 for majors other than in Special Education.

title: Educational Methods with Physically Handicapped Children
description: Special class organization, curriculum, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of orthopedically handicapped children. Prerequisite: SPCED 482; prerequisite or parallel: EDEL 380 and MATH 391.

title: Teaching Multiply Handicapped Children
description: Studies the problems of multiply handicapped children and youth. Symptomatology, assessment, and educational programming of multiply handicapped children will be emphasized. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 373, and 482.
