title: Introduction to Home Economics
description: Career opportunities available in the profession of Home Economics; introduction to Ball State Home Economics programs, facilities, staff ; development of homeconomics as a profesion. Activityoriented clas involving field trips, using practicing home economists as resource persons, with indepth exploration of one area of the profession.

title: Principles of Home Art
description: Design and color principles, with practical application to home situations. Open to all students except those who have credit in ADS 104.

title: Home Economics Field Studies
description: Designed to combine a background of reading knowledge with field experiences in which students will have an opportunity to study special areas of home economics in a particular location. Open to all students with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Workshop: Home Economics
description: Activityoriented study of one area of home economics. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Independent Study in Home Economics
description: Permits the student to investigate and explore more intensively an area of home economics independently. Emphasizes extensive reading and the development of research skills. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Seminar in Home Economics
description: Student presentations and discussions on selected topics of current interest in the field of home economics. Emphasis will focus on a different area of home economics each quarter offered. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of department chairperson. A total of4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Applies the principles and philosophies of vocational education to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image.

title: Home Economics Presentation Techniques
description: Analysis of audience and business needs and the development of presentations and projects to meet these needs. Includes selection and use of presentation methods, development and use of devices, and professional roles and expectations. Open to all departmental majors in home economics and dietetics. Not open to students with a teaching major in vocational home economics.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Home Economics
description: Analysis of pupil needs and the development of a home economics program to meet these needs. Organization of teaching units, selection and use of teaching methods, and development and use of devices for evaluating pupil growth. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: E DS EC 299.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Discipline -oriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of home economics, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of home economics in the secondary school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: HED 395.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economics–related work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis will be placed on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395, and 399.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: A study of how to coordinate class instruction and work experience; includes selecting and recruiting students, selecting training stations, role of the coordinator, techniques of coordination, and placement and followup of graduates. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395.

title: Food Preparation and Meal Planning
description: Designed for students not majoring in home economics. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation stressed. Fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 110.

title: Principles of Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation stressed.

title: Food Experimentation and Comparison
description: Effects of different ingredients and methods of determining quality of products studied. Emphasis on recognition of a standard product and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve a standard product. Application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation stressed. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Meal Management
description: Principles and fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals, with emphasis on resource management and on the purchase and storage of food. Attention given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental principles of nutrition and application to diets for children and normal adults.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning—Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industry, and commercial operations. Experience in quantity food production kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Dietetic technology and food management major must take this course parallel with HFN 362. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 292.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration
description: Emphasis on organizational structure, scientific management, and personnel administration. Experience in quantity food production kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 363. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 293.

title: Normal and Therapeutic Nutrition Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to normal and therapeutic nutrition in clinical and community settings. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 342.

title: Equipment Use, Sanitation and Employee Training Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to quantity food equipment use, sanitation, and employee training in a quantity food service setting. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 262 and 362.

title: Quantity Food Service Personnel Management Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience in personnel management in a quantity food service setting. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permi s _ sion of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 263 and 363.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Purchasing Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to quantity menu planning and purchasing in a variety of quantity food service organizations. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 364 and 367.

title: Nutrition
description: The nutritive value of foods and the use of food by the human body. The nutritional needs of people throughout the life cycle will be investigated. Prerequisite : y, junior/senior level standing or a major inursing, fod management, or dietetic technolog or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Principles of dietary modifications needed by people with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: HFN 340. Parallel: HFN 282 for dietetic technology students. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 441.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Designed to acquaint the student with nutrition problems and nutrition programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Practical experience will include investigation and observation of and participation in nutrition programs in the local community. Prerequisite: HFN 340.

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Laboratory experience in university food service units. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Institutional Equipment, Buying, and Layout
description: Stationary and small equipment for food preparation considered. Layouts of quantity food production kitchens planned. Field trips to quantity food kitchens and equipment companies. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 262. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 292.

title: Institutional Administration
description: Concepts of quantity food service in restaurants, schools, hospitals, and cafeterias. Emphasis is placed on personnel, management, organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 263. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 293.

title: Menu Planning for Quantity Food Service
description: Principles of nutrition applied to feeding individuals and groups. Major emphasis on menu planning for food services with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Explores problems relating to type of patronage and to limited personnel and facilities. Prerequisite: HFN 220 and 340. Parallel: HFN 294 and 367 for dietetic technology students.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers and important considerations in purchasing foods. Emphasis on ethics in buying. Parallel: HFN 294 and 364 for dietetic technology students.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of foods in relation to their composition, physical and chemical properties, and circumstances affecting food quality. Recipes are investigated and methods of combining ingredients are developed and evaluated. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Advanced Nutrition
description: Advanced course in nutrition, emphasizing the use and metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Current research in the field of nutrition will be included. Laboratory experiences provided. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and CHEM 231; senior standing.

title: Diet in Disease
description: A study of the dietary modifications necessary for treating various nutritional diseases and problems. Planning therapeutic diets for abnormal conditions. Laboratory experiences provided. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and permission of the department chairperson; senior standing. Prerequisite recommended: HFN 440 and CHEM 231.

title: Nutrition Assessment
description: A didactic and laboratory course employing the techniques needed to identify persons at risk of nutritional deficiency; to estimate the nutrient content of the diet; to evaluate anthropometric measures and tissue and excretory levels of certain nutrients, functional proteins, and metabolites used as indicators of nutrition status; and to determine appropriate nutrition therapies. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and 342 or 441, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Dietetics
description: The professions involved in food service and dietetics; the roles and responsibilities of personnel and their relationships with other professionals; the standards to be attained; the code of professional ethics and the resources for continuing professional education. Prerequisite: 2 hours of credit in HE 490 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition, Weight Control, and Exercise
description: Designed for students in dietetics, physical education and healthrelated fields ; information and experience for students preparing to provide nutrition counseling to persons in weight control and exercise training programs. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Maternal and Infant Nutrition
description: Information about maternal, prenatal, and infant (birth to thirtysix months) nutrition ; nutritional requirements of expectant mothers and infants investigated. Emphasis on readings in current periodicals. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Child Nutrition
description: Principles of nutritional requirements of children from preschool age through adolescence. Investigates problems in nutrition. Researches current professional periodicals. Prerequisite: HFN 340, junior standing, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Geriatric Nutrition
description: Nutritional needs of older adults in the light of physiological and social changes and research in the field. Students review some recent literature in the field, evaluate the food intake of elderly citizens in certain situations, and study and evaluate nutrition programs designed for older adults in terms of meeting nutritional needs. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition Counseling Practicum
description: Students provide nutrition counseling for pregnant women; families with infants; young and teenage children; and persons seeking guidance for weight control and special problems. Students are supervised by a member of the American Dietetic Association. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course, but no more than 4 credit hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Food Service Management Practicum
description: Provides experience in a food service organization, either in the private or public sector. Emphasizes development for food management expertise. Practicum approved and supervised by the Department of Home Economics. Prerequisite: HFN 360, 364, 367; senior standing; permission of department chairperson; and documented completion of at least 500 hours of appropriate food service work experience.

title: Seminar in Foods and Nutrition
description: Student presentations and discussions on specific topics of current interest in the field of foods and nutrition. Prerequisite: senior level or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Home Care of the Sick
description: Includes concepts that affect the quality of life of individuals and families in prevention of illness, current major health problems and their costs, and procedures to follow when illness occurs.

title: Parent-Infant Development
description: Growth and development during the first two years. Emphasizes practical aspects of infant care and resources and information for developing confidence and competence in parenting. Limited to parents with infants under one year and those expecting babies in eight months or less. Parents bring infants to class.

title: Infant Development
description: Growth and development from conception through the second year of life. Includes physical, social, emotional, and cognitive aspects of development. Students observe and interact with infants and toddlers. Open to all students.

title: Child Development
description: Emphasis on the preschool child as a member of a family group. Includes principles of natural growth and development and child guidance based on the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual needs of the preschool child. Students will participate and observe in various early childhood programs and centers. Open to all students.

title: Marriage
description: The dynamics of the marital relationship and the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasis on the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection and singlehood, marital communication, sexual adjustment in marriage, marriage adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasis on marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment.

title: Assisting With Family Problems
description: The major areas of adjustment in marriage and family relationships, problems of adjustment, and philosophy and practice of techniques for clientcentered assistance with family problems.

title: Seminar in Family Relations
description: History and recent trends and developments in family life education, career opportunities involved in family life education, professional organizations, and ethical standards in the field. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson and senior standing.

title: Family Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, aesthetic qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnish - ings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 1
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Emphasis on the management problems encountered by newly married couples in establishing a home. Open to all students.

title: Household Equipment
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Students will have an opportunity to plan, organize, and present demonstrations on household equipment.

title: Home Management 2
description: Residence in the home management house offers opportunity to make practical application of the principles of homemaking. Prerequisite: HFN 220. Prerequisite or parallel: HHM 340.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing for the consumer, including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, and points to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Functional Home Design Practicum
description: Gives the student onthejob work experience with professional supervision in areas of functional home design. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Clothing
description: Provides basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, the apparel industry, and social and psychological aspects of clothing.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Learn creative skills in stitchery by embellishing existing fabrics or originating new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, needlepoint, and rya, braided, and hooked rugs. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HTC 104 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Costume History
description: A history of costume from its earliest beginnings to the present. Emphasis on the motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Prerequisite: HTC 230 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: A survey of the business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, and promotion. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat. Pattern Method
description: Adaptation of standard patterns to individual proportions, designing of garments, and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Prerequisite: HTC 104 and 203.

title: Textile Testing
description: Experience in planning and conducting textile tests and in evaluating resulting data; development, present status, and importance of textile testing. Prerequisite: HTC 230.

title: Household Textiles
description: The selection, use, and care of drapery and curtain fabric, upholstery fabrics, household linens, and carpets and rugs. Investigates the thermal comfort and energy conservation of selected household textiles.

title: Clothing Problems
description: Special problems to meet students' needs in clothing construction. Includes units in machine attachments and adjustments, draperies, career projects, and problem fabrics. Prerequisite: HTC 104.

title: Fashion Merchandising Practicum
description: Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in an establishment chosen by the student. Prerequisite: HTC 270 and permission of the department chairperson. A wide variety of industryrelated courses offers students many opportunities to explore occupational choices in construction, manufacturing, communications, computer applications, and power. Courses in these areas will also be of interest to students as part of the General Studies Program. Students who intend to pursue a concentration in teaching industrial education should take the following courses during their first year: IED 150, 151, 152, 154, 156, 158, and

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance, and to make simple modifications and installations in plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climate control systems of the home.

title: Introduction to Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing basic production drawings. Topics include lettering, sketching, geometric construction, design process, isometric drawing, orthographic multiview projection, sectional views, dimensions, fasteners, and working drawings.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing productionrelated drawings in selected specialized areas. Topics include auxiliary views, revolutions, cams, gears, bearings, machine components, welding drawing, structural drawing, piping drawing, and electrical drawing. Prerequisite: IED 105 or equivalent.

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: A study of the basic industrial plastics processes and materials. Injection, extrusion, blow and compression molding, and thermoforming. Laboratory activities for all processes included.

title: Introduction to Power and Transportation
description: Concentration on the internal combustion engine. The use and application of power sources, basic mechanisms, component systems, direct energy converters, and efficiencies and power measurement to transportation and industry.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Processes
description: A focus on the six processes used to provide form to metallic, polymeric, and ceramic materials. Classroom and laboratory activities are designed to provide a conceptual understanding of each process.

title: Introduction to Industrial Materials
description: An introductory study of three major types of industrial materials: metallic, polymeric, and ceramic. Characteristics of various materials are identified, studied, contrasted, and compared. Laboratory activities involve conducting tests on materials.

title: Introduction to the Construction Industry
description: A focus on the broad range of processes used in the construction industry. Students learn about and engage in activities related to managing, designing, building, and maintaining structures.

title: Introduction to Industrial Communication
description: A focus on the elements common to industrial communication. Classroom and laboratory activities are related to the design, production, and distribution of printed graphic, photographic, electronic, and technical graphic communications.

title: Industrial Design
description: A study of major elements involved in creating an appealing design that can be manufactured economically. Topics include the design process, sketching, creativity, elements and principles of design, materials and processes, and human and environmental factors.

title: Introduction to Power
description: An overview of the development and use of power in terms of energy, energy conversion, transmission, control, and applications, with continual concern for energy conservation and environmental quality.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Industries
description: Introduction to manufacturing and its managed activities of research and development, production, marketing, industrial relations, and finance in manufacturing industries. Laboratory experiences involve organizing, staffing, and operating a model manufacturing enterprise. Open to all students except teaching majors in industrial education.

title: Introduction to Electricity
description: Introductory experiences and exploration in the broad field of electricity with special emphasis upon means of producing and transmitting electron flow. Instruction in appropriate electrical projects and familiarization with electrical measuring instruments are important experiences.

title: Exploring Industrial Education
description: Focuses on teaching industrial education as a career. Students learn about the development and types of industrial education programs offered in public schools and the undergraduate industrial teacher education program at Ball State University.

title: Advanced Technical Graphics
description: Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; and lateral developments of geometric solids. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Manufacturing Design
description: Focuses on the process of design and principles of drafting as applied to manufacturing industry. Included are product and tool design. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Introduction to Computer -Aided Drafting
description: An introduction to computer drafting using an interactive software package on a microcomputer. The user creates 2-D technical drawings on a system that emulates a major industrial turnkey system. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256 or ITE 300 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Woods
description: A basic course in wood processing for persons interested in consumer information related to wood products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for studentdesigned product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 251, 316, 317.

title: Industrial Plastics: Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problemsolving approach. Studies construction of molds and dies for injection, rotational, and blow molding, extruding, and thermoforming. May also make fiberglass and foam molds. Demonstrates appropriate moldmaking techniques and equipment. Prerequisite: I E D 105 or 256 and TED 125 or 253.

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to metals with concentration on foundry, sheet metal, bench metal, art metal, forging, and spinning. Also places emphasis on safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: Relates power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasizes internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Steps involved in setting up a transportation unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite: IED 140 or 259.

title: Industrial Processing of Metals
description: Basic industrial processes used in manufacturing metal products. Studies, contrasts, and compares the processes °feasting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing to provide a conceptual understanding of each. Laboratory activities used to provide concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 and 151. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Processing of Wood
description: A broad study of the methods used to process the natural polymer, wood, including forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing. Laboratory activities are directed toward helping students acquire basic understanding and skills related to wood processing, and the careers in the area. Prerequisite: TED 150 and 151. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 213 and 316.

title: Industrial Processing of Ceramics
description: A study of ceramic materials as components in such industrial production processes as casting, separating, forming, conditioning, assembly, and finishing. Prerequisite: IED 150.

title: Industrial Processing of Plastics
description: History, growth, organization, and future of the plastics (synthetic polymer) industry. Studies molding, forming, casting, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing techniques common to the plastics industry. Laboratory activities provide experiences with most processes and many materials. Prerequisite: TED 150 and 151. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 125.

title: Printed Graphic Communication
description: A study of printed graphic communications with major emphasis on design and developing messages, preparing messages for production, and producing messages using lithographic, relief, intaglio, and screen processes. Prerequisite:

title: Photographic Communications in Industry
description: Designed to acquaint students with the applications of photography to industrial communications. Students study basic techniques, equipment, processes, and materials used by contemporary industry in communication. Prerequisite: IED 154. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education,

title: Technical Graphics Communications
description: A study of the various graphical methods used to transmit technical ideas and information in industry. Included are sketching, pictorials, orthographies for manufacturing and construction, charts and graphs, reprographics, and industrial practices. Prerequisite: IED 154. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Electronic Communication Systems
description: Electronics as it is used in the field of industrial communication. Students learn about principles, components, and operation of industrial communications systems and develop skills in operating some electronic test equipment. Prerequisite: IED 154. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Electrical Power
description: The conversion, transmission, and control of electrical power with an emphasis on developing knowledge and skill in control and utilization circuitry. A companion course to IED 259. Prerequisite: IED 158. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Mechanical and Fluid Power
description: Energy conversion, transmission, and control within the mechanical and fluid power parameters. A companion course to IED 258. Prerequisite:

title: Introduction to American Industry
description: Organization and management in American industry with emphasis on teaching the content of public school industrial arts programs. Laboratory activities emphasize developing, producing, and marketing studentselected products. Major emphasis on laboratory activities. Open only to students with a teaching major in industrial education. Prerequisite: IED 150, 151, 156.

title: Computer Circuitry Fundamentals
description: Students construct basic digital electronic and computer circuits based on theories and principles in combinational and sequential computer circuitry. Prerequisite: IED 258 or ITE 270.

title: Student Organizations Practicum
description: A practicum in the organization, maintenance, and evaluation of student vocational organizations. A total of 4 quarter hours must be taken by persons seeking certification as teachers of vocational trade, industrial, and technical laboratory programs, and endorsement as cooperative coordinators. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: An introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Analyzes legislation in the light of past and present issues of vocational education and its function as a vital component of the educational system.

title: Curriculum Development in Industrial Education
description: Designed to give prospective i n dustrial education teachers the tools for rational decision making in developing curricula for industrial education programs. Emphasis on developing an adequate conceptual framework within which to design courses. Prerequisite: TED 198. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 394.

title: Residential Drafting and Design
description: Focuses on the basic principles of residential planning and design with emphasis on room design and arrangement, traffic patterns, lighting, heating, alternate energy forms, plumbing, and construction techniques. Students make working drawings, perspectives, and models.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography,

title: Computer Graphics in Drafting and Design
description: A study of methods used to make technical drawings and other graphical representations by employing the computer and computerrelated devices. Use of the graphics display terminal and plotter is emphasized in problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256 or ITE 300.

title: Construction Utility Systems
description: The design, installation, operation, and maintenance of heating, air conditioning, ventilating, electrical, plumbing, and communication systems in construction projects. Emphasis on installation. Prerequisite: IED 152.

title: Building Construction Projects
description: Emphasis on the skills, materials, equipment, processes, and careers associated with the construction industry. Course activities involve the building of onsite construction projects within the community. Prerequisite: TED 152.

title: Industrial Furniture and Cabinet Production
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Advanced Wood Processing
description: Involves units of study in modifying wood materials, bentwood laminations, and wood finishing. Additional opportunities provided for individual problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Advanced Industrial Plastics Technology
description: Advanced techniques in plastics processing. Use of automatic molding equipment, molds and engineering plastics. Mass production techniques will be employed. Prerequisite: IED 225.

title: Industrial Plastics: Advanced Mold and Die Making
description: Designing and building automatic injection molds, extrusion dies, and compression molds with such features as ejection pins, stripper plates, and cooling lines. Field trips to mold shops and molding plants. Requires drafting skills. A laboratory class requiring safety glasses. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256; 125 or 253; and 225, 333, or ITE 330. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Metal Forming and Assembly Practices
description: Sheet metal, wrought metal, forging, and assembly processes. Uses classroom and laboratory activities in safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures to provide conceptual and concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 150 or ITE 162 or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 231.

title: Metal Machining
description: Focuses on metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling machines, grinding machines, bandsawing and E DM to develop understanding of each process. Discussions include tool design, precision measuring, basic NC, fundamentals of metallurgy and heat treating, and safety. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Requires safety glasses, Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250 or ITE 330.

title: Casting and Bonding Metals
description: Flat position welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work with TIC and MIG. Studies vari6us casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Requires safety glasses. Prerequisite: IED 231 or 250 or ITE 330.

title: Advanced Automechanics
description: The maintenance, repair, and theory underlying power train and power transmission units, air conditioning systems, emission control systems, and compression ignition engines. Prerequisite: TED 240.

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to persons currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Safety
description: Provides an awareness of the regulations governing health and safety and the methods and practices used in industry in general and industrial education specifically to comply with these regulations. Designed primarily for students choosing concentration areas in the Department of Industry and Technology.

title: Industrial Product Research and Development
description: Focuses on the industrial activities of research, development, and product engineering as they relate to manufacturing enterprises. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with product research and development. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Requires safety glasses. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263, and 105 or 256 or ITE 300.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes that provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Examines and evaluates methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Industrial Arts
description: Acquaints the student with the philosophy, history, and principles of industrial arts in the elementary school. Affords the students the opportunity to teach a short unit of instruction in cooperation with an elementary teacher to elementary age children in the local community. Prerequisite: industrial arts major or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Applications of Electricity
description: Fundamental electrical theory, with special reference to applications in heating, lighting, electrolysis, electrical communication, and mechanical power. Individual and group experiences through the use of experiments and construction of appropriate projects. Prerequisite: IE D 171 or 258.

title: Servicing Electrical Appliances and Motors
description: Fundamental theory and application of motors and appliance circuitry. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Prerequisite: TED 258 or 370 or ITE 270.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by a breakdown into components ofjobs, tasks, and processes.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Examines and evaluates educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs.

title: Curriculum Problems in Industrial Education
description: Criteria used in determining nature and content of learning experiences in industrial education classes. Teacherpupil planning, group activities, and problemsolving methods. Textbooks and related industrial and government publications evaluated and course outlines developed. Prerequisite: a minimum of 12 quarter hours from the following courses: IED 125, 140, 171, 213, 231, 252; ITE 280.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Industrial Education
description: Problems of organization and management related to industrial education learning activities. Examines objectives, terminology, evaluation methods, teaching devices, lesson plans, textbooks, equipment, and supplies. Students observe industrial education classes in public schools. Prerequisite: IED 198 and 298 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Education
description: Practice in various contemporary approaches to industrial education drawn from methods and curriculum problems courses. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in one or more of the contemporary approaches to industrial education, preferably a public school. Prerequisite: IED 198, 298, and 395.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Discipline -oriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of industrial education, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of industrial education in the secondary school curriculum (grades 5 through 12). Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: IED 298 and 395.

title: Problems in Technical Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in technical graphic Areas based on the needs of the student and the approval of the instructor. Prerequisite: 1ED 105 or 256. 4C 8. Problems in Computer Graphics. (4) Advanced study in computer graphics as it applies to )design and drafting. Emphasis on writing interactive programs . Prerequisite: I E D 308.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extension of knowledge and skill in woods, particularly in proce sse s in which the student lacks confidence and experience. Individual problem solving emphasized. Prerequisite: IED 316.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. Mold making, materials testing, and equipment design possible. Prerequisite:

title: Research and Development in Industrial Ceramics
description: Extensive independent and group study and experimentation in industrial ceramics. Prerequisite: IED 328.

title: Advanced Metals Machining
description: Work includes cylindrical grinding, advanced milling machine work, electrical discharge machining, tool design and grinding, metallurgy, and materials testing. Emphasis on mathematics and science as they relate to machine setups and tool design. Discusses setups relating to industrial production. Department of Military Science Bergin, Chairperson; Davenport, Fraites, Hozey, Jackson, Johnson, Kelley, Treneman, Willey The Army ROTC program gives qualified students—both men and women—an opportunity to obtain a commission in the United States Army and its reserve components. Students may obtain this commission by enrolling in the Army ROTC program along with their regular undergraduate studies in fields of their choice. The program consists of two elements: basic and advanced courses. The basic course, normally taken during the freshman (Military Science 1) and sophomore (Military Science 2) academic years, provides essential background information concerning organization and operations of the U.S. defense establishment. Students in the basic course do not incur any military obligations by enrolling in these classes. Completion of the basic course, constructive credit for Junior AROTC (three years), attendance at a basic summer camp, or prior military service is a prerequisite for admission into the advanced course. The advanced course, normally taken during the junior and senior academic years, provides students with leadership and management skills not available in other curricula and with concepts of military tactics, operations, and organizations. Advanced course students are obligated to attend an advanced summer camp (six weeks) and to accept a commission as an officer, if tendered. Advanced course students receive subsistence and pay of about $2,500 during the two years. All necessary equipment and books are furnished by the Department of the Army at no cost to the student. Credits earned in the military science (AROTC) program may apply toward degree requirements. For specific information, students should consult with their advisers in their major fields of study. The U.S. Army offers financial assistance in the form of two-, threeand fouryear scholarships. Each scholarship provides tuition, textbooks, laboratory fees, and supplies in addition to subsistence pay of $100 a month for the period the scholarship is in effect. Applications for these scholarships may be submitted by anyone enrolled in the AROTC program or nonenrolled students who agree to compress the first two years of the program. Students may also enter the Army Reserve or National Guard under the Simultaneous Membership Program to gain additional experience and financial assistance. Most graduates who have completed the advanced course will be called upon to serve a threeyear tour of active duty and three years in the U.S. Army Reserve. Others will serve three months active duty for training in lieu of three years active duty and be required to participate in the Ready Reserve until the eighth anniversary date of the initial appointment in the Army Reserve, Entry to active duty may be deferred to obtain an advanced degree. Graduates of the program are awarded an Associate in Science degree and are qualified to take the State Board Test Pool Examination for licensure as a registered nurse. To assist clients who have commonly occurring, welldefined health needs to maximize their health potential. 4. title: Physical Conditioning
description: Designed to help the students become aware of their present fitness status and to appreciate the role of physical exercise in everyday life. Students are expected to improve their conditioning through a program of rigorous exercise.

title: Beginning Fencing
description: Basic techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and courtesies. Includes positions, footwork, parries, and lunges.

title: Conditioning and Exercise
description: An exercise course designed to maintain and increase physical fitness and aid in weight control.

title: Volleyball (Coed Rules)
description: Provides the beginner with an understanding of rules and skills underlying optimal enjoyment for power volleyball. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 131.

title: Pocket Billiards
description: Assists the student in the rudimentary skills and knowledge of the sport.

title: Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginner the mechanics of snow skiing, equipment choice, and care of equipment; also offers a field experience of several days of skiing on available slopes. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Orienteering
description: Introduces the student to the activity of orienteering, a sport in which the participant uses such land navigation skills as mapand compassreading. Circulorespiratory fitness is emphasized in distance running for time.

title: Weight Training (Women's Activities)
description: Designed to help students develop a basic personalized program for building and maintaining strength for both overall conditioning and activities in which women participate.

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic exercise routines performed to music.

title: Casting and Angling
description: An introduction to the basic principles of casting and angling along with the practical application of how to catch fish.

title: Sports Acrobatics
description: Provides both men and women with instruction in the rules and techniques of sports acrobatics.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to introduce students to a basic program for developing muscular strength for the entire body.

title: Weight Lifting
description: Designed to help students progress on an individual program for developing muscular strength, body building, or competitive lifting. Prerequisite: PEG 151.

title: Individualized Physical Education
description: Limited to nontraditional students with special problems that may keep them from enrolling in conventional physical education classes. Registration is by permission of the department. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Swimming 1

During the regular school year (September through May) the course is administered as either a learning or a testout program. Students enroll at the aquatics office of the Lewellen Aquatics Center. After students meet the skill performance standards, further attendance is not required, and they may register for credit and grade in either the current quarter or a future quarter; however, registration must be completed at least two weeks before the end of the quarter chosen. title: Synchronized Swimming Techniques

title: Intermediate Modern Dance

title: Advanced Modern Dance
description: For students already skilled in dance who wish to increase their performing and technical aptitude in dance either for vocational or nonvocational reasons. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or the equivalent.

title: Fitness Swimming

title: Racquetball

title: Intermediate Bowling

title: Intermediate Golf

title: Intermediate Horsemanship

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 128.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Physical Education
description: Offers the student supervised experience in basic movementoriented activities generally included in elementary school physical education programs (suggested range: K-6). Course work is contracted among the student, the department, and the school or agency. Prerequisite: PEP 230 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foundations of Exercise Leadership
description: Designed to provide basic knowledge in physical fitness and related areas for students pursuing nonteaching areas, such as corporate fitness programs, private fitness centers, and YMCA's. Prerequisite: PEP 190.

title: Anatomy
description: Basic concepts of anatomy for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching.

title: Physiology
description: Basic concepts of physiology for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze activity for the purpose of improving physical skills. Prerequisite : PEP 292.

title: First Aid
description: First aid as outlined by the American Red Cross, leading to standard certification. Designed for the student pursuing a major or minor program in the School of Physical Education and Athletics. Not open to the student who has credit in HSC 250.

title: First Aid Instructor
description: Instructor's course in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, including also the instructor's course in Multimedia First Aid as established by the American Red Cross. Designed for the professional student pursuing a major or minor in physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 299 or HSC 250, or valid certification in Standard First Aid and Personal Safety, Standard First Aid and Multimedia, or Advanced First Aid and Emergency Care.

title: Camping
description: Acquaints the student with various aspects of organized and individual camping. May require one weekend field trip in addition to regular laboratory periods.

title: Simulation in Driver and Traffic Safety Education
description: Designed to meet the needs of prospective teachers in the simulation phase of driver and traffic safety education. Prerequisite: PEP 124.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Gymnastics; Volleyball; Track and Field
description: Coaching techniques involved in gymnastics, volleyball, and track and field. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Strategies and Techniques in Coaching Volleyball, Basketball, and Softball
description: Coaching techniques involved in volleyball, basketball, and softball. Strategies are presented, discussed, and practiced. Prerequisite: four skill courses from directed list.

title: Physical Therapy Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze "normal" motor performance. Prerequisite: PHYCS 110, 112, 114; ANAT 330, 331, 405.

title: Organization and Management of Women's Athletics
description: Explores the concepts and practices inherent in the organization and management of a women's athletic program.

title: Sports Information 1
description: Designed primarily for the sports information student. Develops the student's knowledge and background in the terminology, basic strategy, scoring, and officiating in gymnastics (men's), basketball, golf, ice hockey, boxing, wrestling, horseracing, billiards, cross country, baseball, and football. Not open to the student with teaching areas in physical education.

title: Sports Information 2
description: Designed for the sports information student. Includes the following sport areas: gymnastics (women's), volleyball, tennis, track and field, swimming, lacrosse, field hockey, softball, soccer, badminton, and bowling. Geared to increase the student's knowledge in these sports, especially in regard to terminology, basic rules, strategy, scoring, and officiating, which will assist them in reporting on these activities. Not open to physical education majors or minors.

title: Aquatic Art Production
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of management and staging activities involved in aquatic art productions at the high school and college levels.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor
description: Provides the opportunity for students to earn the American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certificate. Prerequisite: an unexpired American National Red Cross Advanced Lifesaving certificate.

title: Instructional Techniques and Analysis of Aquatic Performance
description: Selected learning theories, teaching strategies, and physical laws that affect learning and performance in the aquatic medium. Emphasis on analysis of basic safety skills and stroke and diving techniques.

title: Field and Laboratory Experience
description: Permits the student to receive credit for aquatic experiences in categories of leadership, administration, and operation of aquatic programs or facilities. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 259.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 261.

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the early grades of the elementary school.

title: History of Dance
description: Basic dance forms and functions from the primitive era into the twentieth century.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and the use of accompaniment in dance. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or equivalent.

title: Dance Production 1
description: Designed to acquaint the student with various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: PEG 115 or equivalent.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Techniques)
description: Fundamental modern dance techniques, elements of rhythmic patterns, materials of space, design, and improvisation.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Ed ucator (Composition)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on composition. Prerequisite: PEP 365.

title: Modern Dance for the Physical Educator (Methodology)
description: Continued development of modern dance techniques. Emphasis on teaching modern dance in the public schools, camps, and others. Dance composition. Prerequisite: PEP 366.

title: Aquatics for the Elementary School Child
description: Introduces the student to safety factors, developmental strokes, diving sequences, and teaching strategies for aquatic instruction of the young child. Prerequisite: PEP 353 or equivalent certificate from a nationally recognized organization such as the Young Men's Christian Association or the Boy Scouts of America.

title: Diagnostic Techniques and Athletic Injury Mechanisms
description: An introduction to predisposing anatomical, kinesiological, growth stress, and other such conditions that contribute to athletic injuries. Presents the procedures needed to accurately recognize and evaluate these conditions and the extent of an athletic injury. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Administration and Organization for Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Problems, principles, and objectives in the designing, planning, and operation of a program for the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Examines the code of ethics of the National Athletic Trainers' Association. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Athletic Training Modalities and Therapeutic Techniques
description: Introduces mechanical therapies, thermal therapy, cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, and therapeutic exercise. Considers only those modalities and their clinical uses that have special implications for the athletic trainer in the treatment of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Methods of Teaching Team Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following team sports: basketball, field hockey, flag football, soccer, softball, speedball, team handball, and volleyball. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in team sports included.

title: Methods of Teaching Individual Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in the following individual sports: archery, badminton, bowling, golf, tennis, and track. Prerequisite: beginning courses or equivalency in individual sports included.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 276.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball and Softball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 279.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 280.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 281.

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 282.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: 283.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 284.

title: Gymnastics Judging (Women's Events)
description: The development of gymnastics judging techniques with the opportunity for obtaining IHSAA and NAGWS (Class) official's ratings. Prerequisite: PEP 157, 158, 159.

title: Softball Umpiring
description: The development of softball umpiring techniques with the opportunity for obtaining IHSAA, ASA, and NAGWS official's ratings. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Volleyball Officiating
description: The development of volleyball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining IHSAA and NAGWS official's ratings. Prerequisite: PEP 183.

title: Basketball Officiating
description: The development of basketball officiating techniques with the opportunity for obtaining IHSAA and NAGWS official's ratings. Prerequisite: PEP 182.

title: Principles of Physical Education
description: General concepts based upon the scientific facts and philosophic judgments that underlie physical education.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children, emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, using task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Neurophysiological Approach to Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Designed to give the student an understanding of the theoretical basis of selected neurophysiological programs for treatment of various handicaps and to teach the student how to administer such programs.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the student to plan, implement, and evaluate an array of teaching strategies that would be used in creating a safe environment for a public school physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended : EDSEC 29.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Principles; practice of athletic training principles and techniques necessary for care and prevention of athletic injuries.

title: Remedial Exercises and Rehabilitation
description: Introduces the objectives and principle s involved in designing and planing conditioning programs for the athlete. Introduces and develops therapeutic exercises essential in planning the rehabilitation program of the injured athlete. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Methods and Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary School
description: Designed as a practicum that involves comprehensive planning of instruction, designing teaching implementation strategies, classroom management techniques, and evaluation of teaching behaviors and materials in physical education. Opportunities for students to work with children in a classroom setting. Prerequisite: PEP 395 and juniorlevel status.

title: Exercise Leader Internship
description: An indepth practical experience in the application of exercise leadership knowledge and skills as related to fitness and rehabilitation programs owned and operated by private and corporate business firms, as well as municipal organizations. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Exercise Technician and Leader Practicum
description: To provide training for potential leaders of physical fitness programs, emphasis will be on administering exercise tests in the laboratory and in field situations, prescribing exercise based on test results and scientific principles, and leading exercise sessions. Prerequisite: PEP 293 or equivalent course or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum in Recreation
description: Supervised, practical, professional leadership experience designed for the recreationoriented person. Experiences include work activities in federal, state, county, or community parks or with private camps. Close supervision supplied by the university and the participating agency. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Driver and Traffic Safety Education 2
description: Presentation of materials and information designed to prepare for teaching driver education in the secondary schools.

title: Driver Education for Special Populations
description: Designed to provide information for prospective teachers of special populations. Prerequisite: PEP 424.

title: Motorcycle Safety Education
description: Will prepare prospective teachers to conduct motorcycle rider education courses.

title: Coaching Internship
description: Students assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teachingcoaching process. May not be taken parallel with student teaching. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Sports Information Statistics
description: Designed for the sports information student. Consists of the identification, computation, practical application, and communication of statistics in selected sports, such as ERA, match play, difficulty rating, and percentages. Not open to students with teaching areas in physical education.

title: Athletic Governance
description: Directed mainly toward the sports information student. Designed to discuss the various organizations that govern amateur and professional sports in the United States. Emphasis on the sports information student's role in shaping sports in this country and in international competition. Not recommended for physical education majors and minors.

title: Swimming Pool Operation and Maintenance
description: Emphasizes water circulation and filtration, chemical treatment for disease control, sanitation, and administrative procedures for personal safety.

title: Teaching Modern Dance for the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEG 215 or equivalent.

title: Advanced Studio in Contemporary Dance
description: Advanced techniques in contemporary dance. Designed for students interested in improving skills in contemporary dance technique beyond those developed in the regular college classes. Choreographic forms, performance, and production, using such allied fields as costuming, lighting, and accompaniment. Prerequisite: some previous study of modern dance or ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may

title: Implementation of Elementary School Physical Education Programs
description: Designed for advanced students, giving an overview of educationally sound elementary physical education programs; history, curriculum, assessment, objectives, methodology, planning, progressions, and evaluations. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Mainstreaming in Elementary School Physical Education
description: Designing physical education programs to meet the requirements of Public Law 94-142 mandating that all handicapped children have an individualized physical education program.

title: Teaching the Handicapped in Aquatics
description: Adaptation of swimming strokes for people with physical limitations. Provides swimming as a rehabilitation program. Analyzes facilities and pool design adaptations. Prerequisite: an unexpired American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certificate.

title: Sports Development
description: Organizational patterns in program development and exploration of current problems in girls' and women's sports.

title: Practicum in Physical Ed ucation for the Handicapped
description: Designed to provide the student with practical experience in working with handicapped children in a physical education setting. Prerequisite: PE P 488 and 494.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching of a Modern Athletic Program
description: Explores the historical development of modern athletics. Students develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program and learn to deal with everyday coaching and administration problems.

title: Program Development for Intramural and Recreational Activities
description: Initiation, organization, and administration ofintramural and recreational programs in the secondary school.

title: Teaching Physical Education for the Mentally Retarded
description: Establishing a physical education curriculum for the mentally retarded child. Includes understanding the child's e xperience in physical education, teaching methods, and a teaching experience.

title: History and Philosophy of Recreation
description: The history of recreation in the United States from the first settlers in America to modern times. A study of various philosophies that have influenced the development of the new leisure principles.

title: Skill Analysis, Theory and Practice of Play
description: Scientific principles involved in movement as they apply to specific skills in elementary school physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Fundamental play needs of children; research into the play interests of children; and evaluation of space, equipment, and supervision. Explores the educational values of play, necessity of adequate provisions for it, ability to select appropriate equipment, and formation of a tentative curriculum of play forms. Not open to physical education majors and minors except with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Theory and Practice for Upper Elementary and Middle School Children
description: Application of basic movement skills (controlled and refined motor patterns) to individual, dual, selftesting, leadup and team games, sports, dance, aquatics, gymnastics or combination thereof, including assessment, activities, program planning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the human body. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Teaching Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitation each causes. Physical education and recreational activities for each type.

title: Laboratory and Field Experience in Athletic Training 1
description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage, and other therapeutic techniques used by the athletic trainer in the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training
description: Students receive on -the -job experience as student athletic trainers in conjunction with their student teaching assignments in an Indiana high school that is qualified to provide students with both experiences. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Evaluation in Physical Education
description: Methods of measuring and evaluating physical education results in terms of directing philosophy. Tests and uses of test results.

title: Laboratory and Field Experience in Athletic Training 2
description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as bandaging, adhesive strapping, massage, and other therapeutic techniques used by the athletic trainer in the prevention and care of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, 372, 396, and 397.

title: Independent Study in Physical Education
description: An opportunity to investigate an area of particular interest to the student, under supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of4 hours of credit may be earned. title: Physical Conditioning
description: Designed to help the students become aware of their present fitness status and to appreciate the role of physical exercise in everyday life. Students are expected to improve their conditioning through a program of rigorous exercise.

title: Individualized Exercise and Figure Control
description: An exercise course including individual analysis 0ffitness problems and development and maintenance of a fitness level. 104. jogging. (2) Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through jogging.

title: Adapted Physical Education
description: Intended for students with physical handicaps or limiting conditions that would prevent full and unlimited participation as determined by the University Health Service. Students consult with a physical education faculty member and are assigned according to their interests, needs, and qualifications. Regular course requirements are adjusted for the individual. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. 107.Stunts and Tumbling. (1)

title: Beginning/Intermediate judo
description: Designed to give the student an appreciation of . udo, both as a sport and as an art. Emphasis on understanding basic judo techniques and the development of selfconfidence and selfdefense. 109.Beginning Karate. (2) Introductory skills for enjoyment of karate. 110.Wrestling. title: Beginning Modern Dance
description: Introduces the student to the basic skills of modern dance through movement techniques and creative projects.

title: Beginning Modern Jazz Dance
description: Understanding and skill in basic techniques and styles (cool, hot, blues, urban, primitive) of the jazz dance.

title: Swimnastics
description: Physical conditioning through water exercise, using high potential fitness activities that can be used in a small pool or in a limited area of a crowded instructional pool. Prerequisite: ability to put face in water, ability to float on front or back in shallow water, and ability to regain standing position after floating.

title: Beginning Tap Dance
description: Designed to teach the basic tap steps and combinations along with their rhythmic analysis and style to be used in composition. Intended for the student with no experience in tap dancing.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through yoga exercises and yoga relaxation techniques. 121.Archery. (1)

title: Badminton
description: Introductory skills for playing singles and doubles badminton. Stresses basic strategy, rules, and courtesy. 123.Beginning Bowling.
