Examines the history of graphic design and current trends in the profession. Prerequisite: ADS 313.

title: Environmental Space Design
description: Studio exploration of interiorspace design with analysis of human activity for the threedimensional design of simple spaces. Prerequisite: ADS 223.

title: Interior -Space Materials and Processes
description: Research on problems of interior space and conceptualization stressing the interaction of users and space with interiorspace technology. Prerequisite: ADS 324.

title: Photography 2
description: Emphasis on the further exploration of photographic vision, technical concerns, aesthetic aspects of photography and further study of photo history; introduction to advertising photography. Prerequisite: ADS 102 and 231 for art majors; for others, ADS 231 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Color Photography
description: Focus on ideas and assigned problems expressed through color photography. Students should have a basic knowledge of processing color film and color prints. Prerequisite: ADS 332 and ITE 387 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Commercial Photography
description: Investigates commercial applications of photographic medium with historical perspective. Weekly problems assigned with emphasis on practical application of photography to advertising. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Large Format Photography
description: Familiarizes students with cameras larger than 35mm for personal expression and illustration. Emphasis will be on the 4" x 5" camera and its individual strengths and weaknesses. Students need not have large format camera but will find it helpful. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Independent Study in Design
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Interior Environments 1
description: Design of multiunit spaces emphasizing the understanding of their relationships to each other and the users. Consideration of detailing and specifying. Prerequisite: ADS 330.

title: Interior Environments 2
description: Design analysis and synthesis of complex interior spaces. Consideration of human activity as the determinant of the design solution. Prerequisite: ADS 425.

title: Interior Environments 3
description: Studio in which students demonstrate their proficiency and grasp of previous subject matter in a largescale project approved by the instructor. Prerequisite: ADS 426.

title: Photography 3
description: Major emphasis on students' personal statements in color and blackandwhite photography through selection of their own projects under the guidance of an instructor. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332 for art majors: for others, permission of the department chairperson.

title: Photography 4
description: A further intensification of students' personal statements. Students given occasional assignments to introduce new and varied directions in art. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 433.

title: Cinematography as an Art Form
description: Explores the use of video and super-8 media as sources of creative exploration with concerns for artistic expression, content, form, and technique. Covers a brief survey of film history. Prerequisite: ADS 332 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Professional Practices/Portfolio Organization
description: Study of the mechanics of a professional design practice and the function of a portfolio with emphasis upon a portfolio's content and format. Prerequisite: ADS 427. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Senior Thesis
description: A senior project chosen by the student with faculty approval that allows for indepth study and concentration on a single design problem. Designed to provide enough research time to enable the student to attain a closer resolution to the problem. Prerequisite: ADS 313.

title: Concept 20 Design Studio
description: A practicum studio designed to provide students with opportunities to deal with clients on design and advertising projects. Intended to give students work experience in their field that will enhance their marketability upon graduation. Requires portfolio review. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Design
description: Group or individual investigation and experiences in the fine arts beyond the scope of regular course work. Prerequisite: completion of 40 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introductory Drawing and Painting
description: Designed to develop the beginning student's potential for mature visual perception, aesthetic response, skills of expression, and creative problem solving. Not open to art majors.

title: Introductory Printmaking and Sculpture
description: A studio course designed to introduce the student to basic printmaking and sculptural techniques and media. Prerequisite: AED

title: Creative, Material, and Technical Processes Related to Teaching Art
description: Introduction to art education as a teaching profession. Relates materials, techniques, and tools to the teaching concepts relevant to art classes at various developmental levels, concentrating on how to develop creative abilities, technical skills, and aesthetic judgements. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102; AFA 101.

title: Art and the Individual
description: Designed to investigate artistic growth of normal and special populations. Special emphasis given to understanding the unique contributions that art can make for gifted, disadvantaged, and handicapped students. Also includes strategies appropriate for teaching art to these students. Prerequisite: AED 201 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint the student with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Stresses the developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques. Prerequisite: AED 100, 200.

title: Art Curriculum and Instruction
description: Designed to develop the art student's ability to make artcurricular judgments by developing artcurriculum plans and designing art experiences. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Art Teaching and Learning
description: Direct experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating teaching strategies. Includes observation of students participating in an artrelated environment. Laboratory teaching time is arranged. Prerequisite: AED 201, 202, and 304 for majors; permission of the department chairperson for minors.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary public school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 305 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum for majors; permission of department chairperson for minors. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: Art Curriculum and Supervision
description: A practical development of curriculum construction for elementary, middle, and secondary school art. Major focus is on curriculum organization for classroom practice. Also includes experience in analyzing and supervising teaching. Prerequisite: AED 399 or permission of the department chairperson. 415, Independent Study in Art _Education. (1) Permits the professionally oriented art student to select and explore more intensively an area of art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Seminar in Art Education
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in the various ideas, methods, and research in the field of art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: completion of 40 hours of credit in art and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to drawing to develop skills, perceptual awareness, and familiarity with media and techniques emphasizing the application of basic art elements as they relate to drawing concepts.

title: Perspective and Rendering
description: Introduction to objective graphic presentation through freehand perspective drawing; principles and techniques of rendering with emphasis on the convincing description of forms, surfaces, and textures. Prerequisite: AFA 101.

title: Drawing 2
description: Stressing perception of art elements through a variety of media, techniques, and subject matter with an introduction to drawing the human figure. Prerequisite: AFA 101.

title: Painting 1
description: Study of the basic considerations in painting: media, techniques, design elements, and concepts. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Painting 2
description: Explorations in painting designed to build on initial experiences by studio practice and through slide lectures on contemporary painting. Prerequisite: AFA 202 and 211.

title: Watercolor 1
description: Exploration of materials and techniques of transparent watercolor as they apply toward the solution of painting problems. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Watercolor 2
description: Continued exploration of painting problems in watercolor with emphasis on the unique character of the medium. Prerequisite: AFA 217.

title: Sculpture 1
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of clay portraiture, relief sculpture, armature, and plaster construction, mold making, and wood finishing. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Wood and Stone Carving
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of stone and wood carving, including the use of both power and hand tools; appropriate application of form to material; lamination; and critical analysis.

title: Life Sculpture
description: Development of a sculptural figurative statement through exploration of armature building, plastic media, and critical analysis of finished form. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Beginning printmaking techniques with an emphasis on intaglio and relief processes. Prerequisite: ADS 101; AFA 101.

title: Relief Printmaking 1
description: Fundamental procedures of relief printing from the woodblock and other surfaces with emphasis on the use of color and new approaches. Students are expected to develop images which have a relationship to this print medium. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Relief Printmaking 2
description: Continued exploration of printmaking designed to increase the student's sophistication in relief printing techniques and concepts. Images are developed that exploit relief process characteristics. Prerequisite: AFA 232. 243, Intaglio Printmaking 1. (4) Intermediatelevel printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques. Emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 2
description: Advanced printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques including line etching, drypoint, engraving, softground, and aquatint. Openended problem solving and indepth study with emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 243.

title: Lithography 1
description: Fundamental processes of drawing and printing lithographs using stones and aluminum plates. Drawing and painting techniques are used to develop images. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Drawing 3
description: Life drawing. An intensive study of the human figure, continuing the exploration of various drawing techniques and media. Prerequisite: AFA 202.

title: Drawing 4
description: Drawing experiences exploring varied materials and concepts related to drawing as a personal visual statement. Prerequisite: AFA 303.

title: Painting 3
description: Individualized instruction aimed at the continued mastery of technical skills and progress toward the solution of pictorial problems. Prerequisite: ADS 104; AFA 212.

title: Painting 4
description: Continued interest in the development of technical skills and the solution of pictorial problems with new emphasis on individual creative solutions. Prerequisite : AFA 313.

title: Painting 5
description: Emphasis on advancing from technical proficiency toward the development of individual conceptual goals relating to painting. Prerequisite: AFA 314.

title: Plastic Construction
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of plastic construction to include mold making, resin casting, pigmentation, and sheet forming. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Metal Welding and Forging
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, equipment, safety precautions, and concepts of forged and welded sculpture. Students develop an understanding of both ferrous and nonferrous metals. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 3
description: Advanced printmaking emphasizing aesthetic decision making involving the intaglio process through the knowledge of technique and use of personal artistic choices. Prerequisite: AFA 244.

title: Lithography 2
description: Further development and investigation of the processes of lithography, including color. Exploration of stone and metal plate techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 251.

title: Lithography 3
description: Investigation of additional drawing and painting techniques as they relate to lithography. Further development of printing skills and the lithographic image. Prerequisite: AFA 352.

title: Serigraphy 1
description: Introductory printmaking dealing with the processes of serigraphy, including the four basic stencil techniques and their variation. Silkscreen as a fine art form. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Serigraphy 2
description: Continued exploration of printmaking designed to increase the student's sophistication in serigraphic techniques, concepts, and use of color. Prerequisite: AFA 361.

title: Drawing 5
description: Continuation of the drawing experience for advanced students developing further expertise in drawing skills while encouraging research into and experimentation with more personal imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 304.

title: Drawing 6
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 405.

title: Drawing 7
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 406.

title: Drawing 8
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 407.

title: Independent Study in Fine Arts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Painting 6
description: Individualized instruction, continuing the emphasis on student identification and development of personal concepts in painting. Prerequisite: AFA 315.

title: Metal Founding
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of metal founding with both aluminum and bronze to include green sand, ceramic shell, and traditional lostwax investment. Prerequisite: AFA 221 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Problems in Sculpture
description: Designed for students who wish to extend their technical understanding and aesthetic development beyond the fundamental level. Prerequisite: AFA 425 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Exploration of Sculptural Alternatives
description: Designed for students to develop an awareness of current sculptural trends and to experiment with nontraditional sculptural materials. Prerequisite: AFA 425 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 4
description: Application of the technical and aesthetic aspects of advanced intaglio printmaking with emphasis on individualized instruction and problem solving. Prerequisite: AFA 345.

title: Lithography 4
description: Emphasis on color printing. Skills as an artist and as a printer in the lithographic medium more fully developed. Prerequisite: AFA 353.

title: Senior Project in Drawing
description: Synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in drawing, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 28 studio hours beyond the art core. Sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Painting
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in painting, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 24 credit hours in painting, sponsorship by a painting faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Sculpture
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in sculpture, with an exhibition as the concluding effort at the u ndergraduate level. Prerequisite: 28 credit hours in sculpture, sponsorship by a sculpture faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Printmaking
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experience in printmaking, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 28 credit hours in printmaking, sponsorship by a printmaking faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Fine Arts
description: Individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 40 hours of credit in art and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours ofcredit may be earned.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: A survey of the painting, sculpture, and architectural styles of the ancient Mediterranean people through the Early Christian, Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque ages of Europe.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: A continuation of AHS 101, starting with the Mannerist period and continuing through the twentieth century. Discusses the major architects, sculptors, and painters in relation to the religious, economic, and political ideas of their times. Prerequisite: AHS 101.

title: Art: An Introduction
description: Introduces the general education student to the areas of art: architecture, city planning, industrial design, the home, painting, sculpture, and related arts. Presents the ideational and technical approach the artist takes in creative activity. Not open to students with areas in art.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Ancient Art
description: Focuses on the diverse styles of architecture, sculpture, and painting of three early civilizations: Egyptian, Greek, and Roman. Open to all students.

title: Medieval Art
description: Studies major European movements and personalities in architecture, painting, and sculpture from late antique times through the Gothic period; styles include Early Christian, Byzantine, Carolingian, Romanesque, and Gothic. Open to all students.

title: Renaissance Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of the Early and High Renaissance in Italy and Northern Europe. Emphasis on the growth of the artistic heritage of the Western world through the inventions and creations of Renaissance genius. Open to all students.

title: Mannerism and Baroque Art
description: Special emphasis on the works of the leading exponents of mannerism and baroque styles in architecture, painting, and sculpture as they appeared in Italy, France, Germany, Spain, Flanders, Holland, and England. Open to all students.

title: Nineteenth -Century Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture in Europe and the United States including the Palladian Revival through Symbolism and the forerunners of Cubism and Expressionism, Cezanne, and Munch. Other movements to be considered are Neo-Classicism, Romanticism, Realism, the Pre-Raphaelites, and Impressionism. Open to all students.

title: Twentieth -Century Art to 1945
description: European painting and sculpture from 1900 to 1945. Special attention to the development of styles leading to the contemporary art of the midcentury and later. Open to all students.

title: Art Since 1945
description: Deals with the major movements and personalities in twoand threedimensional art in the United States and Europe since World War II. Emphasizes an understanding of the conceptual problems, materials, and techniques and their relationship to early twentiethcentury art and ideas. Open to all students.

title: History of Art in the United States
description: A survey of American cultural traditions as reflected in 350 years of art, architecture, and related forms. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Film History
description: Traces the history of the cinema from its beginning to contemporary times. Emphasizes the role of technique and art in film.

title: History of Photography
description: Surveys the history of photography from 1839 to present. Explores the relationship between equipment and conceptual progress.

title: Art in Living
description: A field course in which the student will have the opportunity to study at first hand the handicrafts, industrial arts, and the arts of a particular geographic area. Open to all students. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Art History
description: Individual or group investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 40 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. School of Music Rubin, Director The School of Music embraces two departments: Academic Studies in Music and Applied Studies in Music. Administrative efficiency and scholarly pursuits are enhanced by subgroupings within these major areas. Thus, the divisions of music education, music history and musicology, and music theory and composition are in the Department of Academic Studies in Music, and divisions of keyboard, voice and guitar, symphonic instruments, and ensembles and conducting in the Department ofApplied Studies in Music. A full range of large and small performing ensembles—the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, the Ars Musica String Quartet, the American Piano Trio, the Aeolian Trio, the Concert Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra—provide superb opportunities for listening or for active participation. Other groups, such as the Harp Ensemble, the Collegium Musicum, the String Sinfonietta, the University Singers, and the Ball State Ballet, accent the diversity of performing outlets on the Ball State campus. Any student on campus, regardless of major, may audition for membership in the university concert organization. Before selecting the field of music for concentration, the student will consult with the coordinator of undergraduate programs in music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the university, a student with a concentration area in music must have proficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument, and a working knowledge of the rudiments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music will be given at times to be announced. If a student cannot meet requirements when entering the university, arrangements may be made to meet them later. All students with a concentration area in music are expected to attend a weekly recital meeting and to perform there with a frequency recommended by the individual teacher of applied music. Additional information will be found in the Music Student Handbook . Before completing registration each quarter, the student will clear requests for applied music instruction through the office of Applied Studies in Music; assignment to specific instructors will be made by this department. Students wishing to qualify for certification as teachers of music in the public schools should refer to the curricular information listed under the Department of Academic Studies in Music the Division of Music Education, as well as to the area requirements that follow. Students wishing to prepare for careers in professional performance, in composition and arranging, or in scholarly activity and research are encouraged to enroll in the appropriate departmental major. The departmental minors may serve some of these goals as well, but the total number of hours required for their completion is kept at a level that will serve the student with a liberal arts orientation who seeks broad cultural development rather than specialized proficiency. A student whose work load permits may register for additional lessons in the selected minor field or in other minor fields, but only with the approval of the chairperson of the Department of Applied Studies in Music. Practice rooms should be reserved in the office of the School of Music at the beginning of each quarter or term. Each student with a concentration area in music is advised to have a piano available for use at a certain time daily, either at the university or elsewhere. All students with concentration areas in music will participate actively in ensembles according to their curricular requirements. Those planning to become directors of instrumental ensembles or supervisors of instrumental music ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the university bands and university orchestras, and vocalists preparing to become directors of choral activities ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the appropriate university choral groups. In addition, students are expected to take advantage of the opportunities for musical broadening provided by membership in the ensembles outside their special fields. The student should make plans early with the coordinator of undergraduate programs (confirmed with the Department of Applied Studies in Music) to satisfy these requirements properly. Department of Academic Studies in Music Sherman, Chairperson; Burkart, Dunn, Eberle, Foley, Griner, Jackson, Karjala, Knight, Mackey, Nichols, Pellegrini, Pence, Rubin, Scott, Vincent, Wakeland The Department of Academic Studies in Music is an administrative unit that comprises three instructional divisions, each of which contributes to the School of Music, the university, and the community in distinctly different ways toward the common goal of musical and academic excellence. The Division of Music Education An essential mission of the Division of Music Education at the undergraduate level is to prepare students for state certification and licensing for teaching music in the public schools. The task of becoming an effective music teacher not only involves developing a high degree of musicianship and scholarship, but requires of the teachermusician a sincere interest and skill in assisting others to develop musical reponsiveness. Four fields of specialization are offered the student seeking certification: The teaching area major prepares the student to teach instrumental, choral, and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve ; the teaching major in instrumental music prepares the student to teach instrumental music in grades kindergarten through twelve; the teaching major in choral music prepares the student to teach choral music in grades kindergarten through twelve with particular emphasis in the area of performing groups at these grade levels; the teaching major in general music prepares the student to teach general music classes in grades kindergarten through twelve. These four major fields of specialization can be combined with several minor concentration areas in music, including music therapy, for those who wish to attain a higher level of musical competency or who wish to combine the study of music with that of another subject. To graduate from Ball State University with a major in any of the music teaching preparation fields, a student must present evidence of an ability to execute certain musical and educational tasks. This evidence, in addition to the successful completion of the curriculum, is shown through the demonstration of a firm commitment to teaching and a high level of competency in one's primary and secondary performance media—a symphonic instrument, a keyboard instrument, or voice. The tenweek student teaching experience, which occurs during the senior year, is generally arranged so as to satisfy the student's desires with respect to the choice of quarter and location within the state. The Division of Music History and Musicology Courses in music history and musicology serve the entire university through the program of general education. The teacher in training is afforded the opportunity to broaden his or her understanding of the art of music through a variety of more specialized history courses, and the liberal arts student may gain cultural and historical enrichment in music through a selection of courses appropriate to his or her needs. The prospective graduate scholar or researcher may take advantage of numerous opportunities to develop new insights into and a deeper knowledge of the large body of literature in and about music that has been accumulating for several centuries. Practical experience in the performance of medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music using instruments appropriate to the times may be gained through membership in the Collegium Musicum. The Division of Music Theory and Composition The basic twoyear music theory sequence offered by the Division of Music Theory and Composition primarily serves students who are working toward undergraduate degrees in music. Through these courses, students develop the manipulative and aural skills necessary for an understanding of the nature and function of available sound materials used in the creative act of composition, acquire a basic understanding of the fundamental premises of conventions that underlie the music of present and past cultures, and learn to adapt their skills and understanding for the specific needs of the professional degrees they seek. Thus, the basic twoyear music theory sequence is designed to prepare the student for additional study at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Beyond the basic twoyear theory sequence required of all students majoring in music there are specialized upperlevel undergraduate courses that serve the needs of the variou s n undergraduate curicula of the Schol Music; majors and minors are also available i music theory and composition. Specialized graduate courses are designed to methe neds of students enrolled in the various master's and doctoral curricula. The Electronic Systems for Music Synthesis, a facility that has developed rapidly i n recent years, plays a significant role in thevolving curicula of the Schol Music. The ESMS is an interdisciplinary studio complex supporting education and research in electronic, electroacoustic, and intermedia performance in pedagogy. The studio is fully equipped for the production and processing of electronic and concrete sounds. The Arp synthesizer is interfaced with a digital computer for full digitalanalog control. 1. title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Designed for the potential music teacher.

title: Sensory Awareness and Response to Music
description: Designed for the elementary classroom, teacher emphasizing sensory experiences based on learning sequences appropriate for children. Constitutes a basis for musical experiences to be explored in succeeding courses. Not open to the student who has credit in MUSED 350, 351, 352.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: A basic inquiry into the value of craftsmanship and the principles of piano tuning. Discusses the problems and remedies of new and used pianos. An introductory course open to all students interested in the care and maintenance of the piano.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Application of piano temperament tuning theory with emphasis on the development of proper tuning techniques. Prerequisite: MUSED 240 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Principles of basic action regulation and common minor repairs. Prerequisite: MUSED 241 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Brass Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the brass instruments with emphasis, on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 250.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: A continued study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly. Prerequisite: MUSED 252.

title: The Development and Administration of School Choral Activities
description: Analysis of the choral literature available for use in the secondary school as to its technical difficulty and suitability to choral groups of various sizes and musical backgrounds. The administration and supervision of choral activities, including the general chorus, the selected groups, and the voice classes. Techniques of choral arranging.

title: Basic Musical Experiences for Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to develop creative responsiveness in students enrolled in educational programs for young children, and to demonstrate through laboratory experiences the application of creativity to the developmental characteristics of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Basic Music and Methods for Special Education
description: Designed to build on the experience of future teachers toward development o f basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and specific music skills, combined with methods for present suitable musical materials and experiences for children in the area of special education. Not open to the student who has credit in MUSED 266.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled for individual study and exploration. Prerequisite: MUSED 164.

title: The Teaching of Music in the Elementary School
description: The problems of teaching and supervising music in the elementary school for music supervisors and special teachers of music. Lesson planning and teaching are done in the class, and contact is made with teaching situations through directed observation. Leading music series are studied. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113 or the equivalent.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Primary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in the first three grades ; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: Methods of Teaching and Supervising Music in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: A methods course for vocal music education majors, which is a continuation of 351. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six: singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High School
description: An exploration of the scope and character of musical activities designed to supplement membership in the established performing groups of the public schools and to provide an outlet for the many students not concerned with public performance. Acquaintance with materials and techniques appropriate to the study of music literature and music theory.

title: Teaching and Administration of Instrumental Music
description: Applies the skills developed in instrumental minor studies to the techniques needed for related families of instruments. Stresses proper care of equipment, organization of physical factors, teaching of instrumental classes, and developing instrumental ensembles. Piano and voice majors should take this course during the senior year. Prerequisite: minor skills in brass, woodwind, and string instruments.

title: Introduction to Orff-Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities involve movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative utilization of simple percussion instruments.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary School
description: Designed to enrich the student's musical background in the common heritage of music and to suggest methods for presenting suitable musical materials and experiences to children. More intensive involvement with music exemplars, including appreciation and specific musical skills. Prerequisite: MUSED 164 and 266.

title: Administration and Planning of the Church Music Program
description: Formation and training of adult and children's choirs in churches. Congregational singing. Service planning. The clergy, the congregation, and the church musician.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, short -term course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing. Includes two or more distinguished visiting instructors on the staff, who present new materials and methods.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experiences with the materials and activities of general music classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possibilities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: Workshop Series: Current Practices in Orff -Schulwerk
description: A special series of workshops in association with the Indiana Orff-Schulwerk Association explores and gives practical experience with current practices in Orff-Schulwerk in America, through workshop participation and related individual curricular development projects. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Ball State fees are at the offcampus rate and are in addition to any fees required by the IOSA.

title: The Orff Workshop—Beginning
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the beginning phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. Stresses the basic approaches to the Orff method of teaching music to children in grades one through six. Emphasizes techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The Orff Workshop—Intermediate
description: Opportunities for concentrated study, by means of participation, observation, and discussion, in some of the more advanced phases of the fresh and stimulating approach to children's musical education created by Dr. Carl Orff. Emphasis on creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Includes techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite: MUSED 443 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum: Materials and Techniques for the Secondary School Music Director
description: An intensive review of current practices in the development and musical advancement of school choral and instrumental ensembles. Emphasis on recent additions to available musical literature under guidance of distinguished guest conductors and with active cooperatio n of high schol clinic groups. A total of 4 hours credit may bearned with the aproval of the department chairperson.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 2
description: Designed to improve the work of the teacher of piano in the handling of class and private instruction. Areas of interest include the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods for Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction. Prerequisite: credit in classical guitar.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite and parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Methods for Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods for teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; singing and conducting opportunities of standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Handbell Techniques
description: An introduction to the history, literature, and playing techniques of handbells. Includes opportunities to conduct and to perform with handbell choirs. Discussion of administering handbell choirs in church and school situations.

title: Basic Movement and Choreography
description: Designed to acquaint the music therapist or teacher with the fundamentals of physical interpretations of music. Deals with techniques appropriate for swing choirs, small ensembles, and general staging practices in performance preparation.

title: Introduction to the Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school form the framework of this course designed for the music specialist. A study of the Hungarian system of music education is the basis for analysis of the structure of the materials for American schools.

title: Introduction to Contemporary Music Techniques in the Elementary School
description: Exploring the use of nonconventional, nontraditional, experimental musical sound sources and procedures in music education. Students participate in classroom projects using creative and contemporary symbolization, instrumentation, and vocal setting, including an introduction to electronic music.

title: Stage Band Techniques
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the techniques and style characteristics of popular and jazz band performance. Includes preparation in the administration of school jazz ensembles.

title: Guitar for Social Use
description: Designed for development of basic skill in playing the guitar for accompanying. Focuses on chordal styles and their application to music such as folk songs and popular songs. Open to all students.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments
description: Provides a fundamental working knowledge of skills required in maintaining stringed instruments at the elementary and secondary school levels. Study and application of school repair problems in regard to the violin, viola, cello, and double bass. General techniques in making adjustments, gluing, and using tools properly. Analysis of the various woods used in instruments and bows. 476. psychology of Music 1. (3) An introduction to the study of human musical processing with emphasis on th e underlying principles of musical behavior. Fundamental laboratory experiences are included in the course work.

title: Psychology of Music 2
description: A continuation of MUSED 476 with emphasis on the survey of the pertinent current research in the field. Prerequisite: MUSED 476.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis on those specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Tests, Measurements, and Guidance in Music
description: Acquaints the teacher with tests of sensory capacities, appreciation, and achievement. Briefly reviews such statistical and other data as make for an enlightened evaluation of the various tests and of their results.

title: Psychology of Music
description: Presentation of materials as an aid to the understanding of the nature and extent of individual differences in musical talent. Specific preparation in the psychology of audition, motor control, and in the analysis of the musical mind leading to a natural application in the psychology of musical training.

title: Music in Therapy
description: Provides acquaintance with specific processes and procedures for the uses of music in therapy. Investigation of case studies, musical techniques, the use of music in behavior modification, and application of appropriate musical components in therapy.

title: Influence of Music on Behavior
description: The therapeutic uses of music in facilitating interaction patterns in afflicted persons. A behavioral approach to the processes of the use of music in therapy.

title: Introduction to Music Therapy 1
description: The foundations upon which music therapy rests. Deals with the basic concepts of the discipline and provides a working definition of music therapy for prospective music therapists.

title: Introduction to Music Therapy 2
description: A continuation of MUSED 484 with investigation of the basic premises of the profession in greater depth. Aids in the clarification of the role of the music therapist in society. Prerequisite: MUSED 484.

title: Clinical Experience 1
description: Actual field experience assisting in functioning music therapy under the direction of a qualified music therapist. Corresponds to the participation experience for the prospective teacher.

title: Clinical Experience 2
description: Actual field experience assisting in functioning music therapy under the direction of a qualified music therapist. Corresponds to the participation experience for the prospective teacher. Prerequisite: MUSED 486.

title: Music in Therapy and Special Education
description: The theoretical aspects of music therapy and their appropriate application to special education in the public schools. Emphasizes the power of music to elicit normal interaction with peers from the child with a learning difficulty.

title: Recreational Music
description: Particularly for students interested in the function of music in recreational leadership at any level. Explores materials, sources, and elements of a recreational music program, organizational procedures, individual and group activities, and utilization of community musical resources. Open to all students; musical background not required.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: An opportunity for the superior student to do intensive study and research in a particular aspect of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Internship in Music Therapy
description: Six months of fulltime music therapy training in a qualified institutional setting under the guidance of that institution's registered music therapist. Placement and supervision are arranged through conference with the faculty music therapy instructor. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Music
description: Introduction to the art of listening to music. Some elementary instruction in musical materials will be related to the listening aspects of the course, although the course is designed primarily to introduce students to the sound of music through the ages. No previous knowledge of music required. Open to students with areas in music by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Music History 1
description: The growth of music from its beginnings through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The origins of music, the development of notation, and the growth of early polyphonic forms. Open only to students with areas in music except by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Music History 2
description: Changes in music from the late sixteenth century through the Baroque, the Rococo, and the Classical periods. The transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque, and the developments of opera, sonata, symphony, and the related forms. Prerequisite: M U HIS 101, 230, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Music History 3
description: Developments in music from the time of Beethoven to the present. Transition from the classical to romantic periods, the various reactions to Romanticism, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 231, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Open only to students on the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano I
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisite: some music literature background and an ability to read music.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. It is not necessary for the student to be a pianist to take this course. Prerequisite: some music literature background and an ability to read music.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: A comprehensive study of vocal and instrumental music of western Europe during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including the function of figured bass and important theoretical and contrapuntal developments. The evolution of opera, oratorio, and cantata and the development of instrumental genres such as concerto, sonata, and suite (both orchestral and keyboard). Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles which marked the transition from Baroque to Classic music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Music in Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in Western civilization in the nineteenth century, emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Studies important composers and works from the various time periods: early, middle, and late Romanticism, and post Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUHIS 232 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and the student will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisite: M UHIS 232 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Jazz History I
description: Historic examination of jazz from 1890 to 1950. Explores chronological innovations and personalities. Analyzes outstanding style characteristics of each period from their earliest beginnings to the 1950s, including ragtime, the "Jazz Age," "Swing Era," "Bebop," and "Cool" periods. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Jazz History 2
description: Continuation of MUHIS 439 beginning with the 50s through the 80s. Progressive 50s, the Rock Jazz/Fusions of the 60s, 70s and 80s—today's trends. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque instruments and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Rameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: An opportunity for superior students to do guided reading and intensive study in an area of music history of particular interest to them for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned but not more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Hymnody in Worship
description: Hymns in early Jewish and Western Christian tradition; their historical and liturgical context and contemporary use. A summary of Western religious thought as exposed in liturgical poetry. Prerequisite: MU HIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231, 232, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students with deficiencies in elementary musical knowledge. Provides, at the simplest levels, a language for communication and a background of rudimentary information, historical and systematic. Designed primarily for students intending to pursue courses in music education, history, theory, and performance. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open to all students except those with credit in MUSTH 111 or above; MUHIS 230 or above. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Music Theory
description: Review of terminology and fundamentals precedes an extensive study of the tonal, rhythmic, motivic, and formal structure of melody through composition and analysis. The basic elements of music are studied through the analysis and writing of music in two, three, and four parts. Elementary work in transposition, scoring, and harmonic alterations. Music reading, aural discernment, and rhythmic training provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. These courses must be taken in course number sequence.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of Music Theory 111. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of Music Theory 112. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Music Theory
description: More complex elements of nineteenthand twentiethcentury music studied through composition and analysis. Advanced work in music reading and aural discernment provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of Music Theory 211. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of Music Theory 212. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: The components of the recording chain are introduced both theoretically and practically. A complete and thorough review of the recording process, the mixing process, and editing formats is presented.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An introduction to multichannel recording techniques, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing is presented. Requires laboratory time for recording practice and a final recording project. Prerequisite: MUSTH 225.

title: Music Calligraphy
description: Practical experience in calligraphic skills and layout procedures pertinent to the preparation of music scores and parts. Prerequisite: MUSTH 113.

title: Composition
description: Experience in writing short instrumental and vocal compositions with emphasis on developing the student's technical capacity to achieve freedom of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of Composition 321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of Composition 322. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic Music
description: A workshop in current practices of producing music by electronic means. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Composing based on examples studied is optional. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic hand and wind ensemble. Gives particular attention to voicing, sectional and crosssectional doubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Commercial Arranging Concepts
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques employed in commercial music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms. Particular attention will be given to the composerarranger in the recording studio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Theory of Nineteenth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Theory of Twentieth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Music Theory in the Secondary School
description: An investigation of pedagogical precepts and problems relating to music theory in the secondary school. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213,

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Analysis will be applied to a broad representation of musical masterworks from various periods with examination of the macroand microstructure and construction of selected works. Special attention is given to musical practices before and after the period of tertian harmony. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213.

title: Twentieth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to principles and procedures of twentiethcentury music.

title: Electronic Music Studio 1
description: An introductory course in electronic music. The physical and perceptual dimensions of sound are presented as a basis for sound synthesis. An introduction to musique concrete operations and voltagecontrolled systems provides the basis for class projects. Studio laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Electronic Music Studio 2
description: An advanced course in electronic music synthesis. An introduction to large voltagecontrolled systems, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing. Projects in composition, educational applications of electronic music, and research. Laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 425. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Computer Applications in Music
description: Presents an overview of computer systems and languages appropriate for (1) musical analysis; (2) musical composition; and (3) sound synthesis. Presents a historical prespective, computer applications in the areas stated, and introduces simple programming procedures. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Composition -Project Recital
description: Public performance of the student's compositions and/or public presentation of the student's music theory research.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire. Each project requires seminar and laboratory participation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 226. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Composition
description: Experience in writing more complex and extended instrumental and vocal compositions with continued emphasis on the development of style. Prerequisite: MUSTH 323.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of Composition 431. Prerequisite: MUSTH 431.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of Composition 432. Prerequisite: MUSTH 432.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. Studies the synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: A laboratory for skill development in arranging. This course is individualized and projectoriented to prepare musicians in scoring spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, background and mood sequence, and composition requirements of music for filming TV, radio, and media productions. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Independent study in any area of music theory via readings, analysis, and/or research. Prerequisite: MUSTH 213 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term. title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, carrying no credit and normally rehearsing five hours per week. Included in this category are Wind Ensemble, Symphonic Band, The Marching Show Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I. Registration will satisfy curriculum participation requirements but will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation. Prerequisite: open only to music majors carrying 17 or more hours.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying no credit and normally rehearsing two hours per week. Included in this category are University Concert Band, Variety Band, Training Band, Training Orchestra, and the Jazz Ensemble II and III. Registration will satisfy curriculum participation requirements but will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation. Prerequisite: open only to music majors carrying 17 or more hours.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles carrying no credit and normally rehearsing five hours per week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera Chorus, and the University Singers. Registration will satisfy curriculum participation requirements but will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation. Prerequisite: open only to music majors carrying 17 or more hours.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying no credit and normally rehearsing two hours per week. Included in this category are Choral Union, Women's Chorus, and Men's Glee Club. Registration will satisfy curriculum participation requirements but will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation. Prerequisite: open only to music majors carrying 17 or more hours.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 372.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying onehalf hour of credit and normally rehearsing two hours per week. Included in this category are the Symphonic Band, University Concert Band, the Training Band, the Jazz Ensembles 2 and 3, and the Training Orchestra.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles carrying one hour of credit and normally rehearsing five hours per week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera/Musical Theatre Chorus, and the University Singers.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations for performance or training purposes carrying onehalf hour of credit and normally rehearsing two hours per week. Included in this category are the Chorale, Women's Chorus, University Debs, the Men's Glee Club, and the Choral Union.

title: The Singing Actor
description: Acting techniques specifically related to musical theatre/opera. Vocal exercises, movement, song interpretation. Preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer and/or technician. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with MUSCH 172.

title: Musical Theatre in America
description: A study of the history of the American musical theatre. A general overview of the repertoire.

title: Acting for the Musical Stage
description: A lecturelaboratory class dealing with basic acting techniques as applied to dialogue portions of musical shows. Transition into song, character building, timing, dialogue over music.

title: Recital
description: Attendance at recitals and concerts as specified in the music student handbook is the basis for the earning of recital credit.

title: Small Ensemble (Woodwind)
description: Players of woodwind instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing. These groups may include trios and quartets of like instruments, or quintets, sextets, and octets of mixed woodwinds.

title: Small Ensemble (Brass)
description: Players of brass instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of the brass ensemble literature. These groups may include trios and quartets of like instruments, or quintets, sextets, and octets of mixed brasses.

title: Small Ensemble (Percussion)
description: Players of the family of percussion instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of the literature designed for their public performance. These groups may range in size from trios and quintets to larger ensembles and may include the entire range of percussion instruments.

title: Small Ensemble (Strings)
description: Players of string instruments are organized into groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing. In addition to the standard string quartet, a variety of combinations of like and unlike instruments may be arranged, according to the nature of the student enrollment.

title: Small Ensemble (Harp)
description: Groups of four and five harpists are organized to perform the specialized literature for this unusual combination of instruments. Original compositions and transcriptions are presented in public performance.

title: Small Ensemble (Piano)
description: The study of sonata literature in conjunction with another instrument or literature for multiple piano. Students will be organized into small groups according to proficiency and the demands of the literature. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Ensemble for New Music
description: Players of all instruments are organized into small groups for the study of contemporary chamber music. Open to all students with sufficient proficiency. May be used for fulfillment of small ensemble requirements.

title: Small Ensemble (Organ and Church Music)
description: Performance projects of interest to the organist and church musician. Reading of anthems, motets, oratorio movements; music for organ and instruments; music for graded church choirs; conducting from the keyboard. Material varies each quarter.

description: Quartets, sextets, octets, and multiples of these units are arranged as student enrollment indicates. Music studied and performed ranges from the traditional quartet literature to material appropriate for glee clubs. Madrigal Singers. Polyphonic music is studied and sung with emphasis on the development of individual singing in a small group. Music of English, French, Italian, and Spanish composers is included. Radio broadcasts and concert programs are given. Membership, limited to twelve students, is by audition. Opera Workshop. Fosters appreciation of and familiarity with operatic literature through public performance of roles in chamber operas and excerpts from standard operas. Participation in the opera chorus supplements the smaller ensembles. Open to voice and piano majors as well as others proved capable through audition.

The Opera Productions class combines the art forms of music, drama, stagecraft, and dance in the study of coaching, acting, and stage techniques. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson on the recommendation of the director following audition or previous experience. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in the combination of this course and MUSPE 270, 370, and 470.

description: An overview of the field of theatre with special reference to the origins of drama.

Sargent The College of Sciences and Humanities provides courses and programs for either a liberal e ducation or specialized and professional curricula. The liberal arts programs permit the student to elect more freely and to explore the "idea" subject matter. Liberal stems from the Latin liber, free. By definition, a liberal arts education should free people from ignorance by allowing them to acquire an intelligent grasp of the experiences of the past and an understanding of the interrelationship of branches of knowledge. The individual is educated to think objectively, critically, and creatively. The liberal arts include the study of foreign languages, the physical and social environment, the evolution of Western civilization, the foundations of modern science, and the classical works. The wide range of courses offered by the College of Sciences and Humanities provides the basis for specialized and professional curricula—offered both within the college and in the other colleges requiring service courses.
