EDUCATION: FOUNDATIONS (EDFON)

title: School in the American Culture
description: An introduction to the theory, scope, organization, and functions of the public school in the United States. The student will examine the role of public education at all levels at which it operates and the responsibilities carried out by the professional teachers in their educational work.

title: International Dialogue on American Education and Life
description: Perspectives on American education and its cultural setting developed through interaction among international and American students and comparative study of educational and other social institutions as they relate to education.

title: The Role of Women in the Past, Present, and Future Development of Education
description: A survey of the role of women in education with an emphasis on analysis of career development, styles of work, and job satisfaction. EDUCATION: HIGHER (EDHI)

title: Introduction to Personnel Services in Residence Halls
description: Principles involved in understanding and working with individuals and student groups in residence halls, social forces affecting college students, and the relationship of the residence hall program to the total university. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned; a maximum of 1 credit hour per quarter.

title: Leadership and Development of Student Organizations
description: Examines philosophical bases, group processes, and skills relevant to leadership and development of student organizations in higher education. Focuses on understanding and skills requisite for effective involvement in student groups. EDUCATION: JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE (EDJHM)

title: Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Junior High/Middle School
description: Analyzes factors which influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American junior high/middle schools. Not open to the student with credit in EDSEC 205.

title: Independent Study in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Independent study and research in the field of Junior High/Middle School topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Develops basic instructional strategies for junior high/middle schools. Topics include general methods, problems of student advisement, legal considerations, classroom management, and instructional media, in the light of study of the nature of junior high/middle school children. Specific laboratory experiences are emphasized. Prerequisite: EDJHM 205, EDPSY 351, and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: Instructional Strategies and Approaches in Junior High/Middle School
description: Factors affecting the total instructional responsibilities in junior high/middle schools are studied. Students are required to develop skills in individualizing instruction to serve the full range of students, the ability to work cooperatively with other professional personnel, and instructional techniques and evaluation procedures especially appropriate for junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDJHM 205 or EDSEC 205 and EDPSY 251 or 351. Not open to the student who has credit in E DS EC 313.

title: Mediation of Instructional Design: Junior High/Middle School
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology in the improvement of teaching and learning in junior high/middle school classrooms.

title: The Junior High/Middle School Curriculum
description: Several curricular approaches appropriate for pupils in the age group ten to fourteen years will be examined in relation to current research. Legal rights and the significance of positive human relations are studied. Direct development of alternative curricular programs and appropriate use of merging structures and nontraditional materials will be emphasized. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312.

title: Foundations of Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Junior high/middle school education as an institution in society and its relationship to the individual and American culture from the perspective of the sociological, philosophical, historical, legal, economic, political, and anthropological foundations of junior high/middle schools and teachers are stressed. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Juniiir High/Middle School
description: Designed to prepare prospective junior high/middle school educators to cope with discipline problems in all junior high/middle school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures in preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by junior high/middle school students and ways to create positive environments for learning.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Junior High/Middle School
description: This elective student teaching experience will enable a student to complete a full quarter assignment in fullday student teaching assignments in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDJHM 466.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the Standard License in Junior High/Middle School Education. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Advanced Undergraduate Practicum in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Provides direct, supervised experiences for students wishing to gain increased skill and knowledge regarding junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDJHM 312 or EDSEC 299 or EDEL 360. EDUCATION: READING MIDDLE (EDRDM)

title: Improving General Reading Skills in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: A general course for all junior high/middle school teachers which examines reading problems and provides specific methodology for improvement of reading skills in junior high/middle schools. General diagnostic teaching techniques appropriate for teachers in all curricular areas are to be achieved. Exit competencies are required. EDUCATION: READING SECONDARY (EDRDS)

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: Practical procedures for developing effective reading skills to be applied by all secondary classroom teachers. Focuses on relationships between the process of reading and learning of content, on planning to meet total range of student reading needs, and on methods and materials to enhance comprehension and study skills in all areas of secondary school curriculum. EDUCATION: SECONDARY (EDSEC)

title: Introduction to Secondary Education for Paraprofessionals
description: Study of American junior and senior high schools from the point of view of the paraprofessional in secondary education. Prerequisite: admission to the secondary paraprofessional program. Parallel: EDSEC 111.

title: Freshman Paraprofessional Practicum
description: The organization and operation of secondary schools and the duties, procedures, and problems of secondary school faculty and staff. Provides initial experiences in assisting secondary faculty and staff. Prerequisite: admission to the secondary paraprofessional program. Parallel: EDSEC 110.

title: Introduction to Teaching in Secondary and Junior High/Middle School
description: Examines the structure, function, and development of schools in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about career choices and about preparing for a teaching career. Focuses on professionalism, job requirements, and employment opportunities. Specific planning for the Ball State University program is included. Not open to the student who has credit in EDSEC 150.

title: Initial Direct Experiences in Schools
description: Provides initial opportunities for prospective teachers to gain direct, firsthand experience through school assignments. Students will be assigned to local secondary and junior high/middle schools. Experiences are designed to assist students in making appropriate career decisions. Prerequisite: EDSEC 148. Not open to the student who has credit in EDSEC 150.

title: Basic Concepts of Secondary Education
description: Examines through classroom investigation and practical field experiences the structure, function, and development of secondary education in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about preparing for and functioning in a teaching career by studying professionalism, job requirements, employment opportunities, secondary school curriculum, and the role of secondary education within the entire educational process.

title: Introduction to Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Introduces prospective teachers to responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 100 or 206 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intermediate Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Continued study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, supporting personnel, and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 200 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Advanced study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, supporting personnel, and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 201 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Secondary Schools
description: Analyzes factors which influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American secondary schools. Not open to students with credit in EDJHM 205.

title: Advanced Study of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior
description: Focuses on indepth analyses of many of the concepts introduced in EDSEC 205. Particular emphasis on variables that contribute to the development and maintenance of prejudice, stereotypes, racism, and oppressive conditions. Equal emphasis on instructional strategies for combating such behaviors. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or EDJHM 205 or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in EDSEC 100.

title: Laboratory Experience in Secondary Education
description: Provides direct experiences in working with students, teachers, paraprofessionals, community agencies, and other appropriate assignments for undergraduate students who plan to enter secondary school teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned; no more than 4 hours may be taken in one quarter.

title: The Secondary Paraprofessional and the Use of Instructional Technology
description: The use of instructional technology and the preparation of instructional materials as these skills are employed by the paraprofessional.

title: Secondary Paraprofessional Internship
description: Practical experiences in the duties, responsibilities, and related problems of the secondary school paraprofessional. The intern will be assigned to a secondary school during a regular school year for a period of one quarter. Prerequisite: EDSEC 110, 111.

title: Principles of Teaching and Classroom Management: Secondary School
description: Inducts the student into the teaching act. Includes specific technical skill development, legal implications, study of principles of teaching, application of instructional media, curriculum development and organization, classroom management, and discipline. Intensive inschool assignments, observation, skills, participation, and direct contact with adolescents are required. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205, EDPSY 251, and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290.

title: Instructional Strategies in Multicultured Schools
description: Theory and application of special instructional strategies of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms with special emphasis on multicultured educational situations. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or EDJHM 205 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Education: A Critical Examination
description: The complex educational system and alternatives to the traditional system, featuring an individualized, issueoriented instructional approach. Designed for students who do not plan to teach but open to those in teacher education.

title: Mediation of Instructional Design
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology to improvement of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms.

title: Planning and Assessing Instructional Programs
description: Designed to provide secondary school teachers with methods of establishing instructional programs with feedback networks that will encourage continuous assessment and appropriate alterations of the educational environment. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Independent Study in Secondary Education
description: Independent study and research in the field of secondary education. Topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Education and Professional Concerns of the Beginning Teacher
description: Provides opportunity to examine critically and to focus educational experience and knowledge on contemporary and personally significant problems of education. Emphasizes immediate professional concerns of prospective firstyear teachers. Prerequisite: EDSEC 301 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Social Foundations of Secondary Education
description: Education as an institution in society and its relationship to the individual and American culture from the perspective of the sociological, philosophical, historical, economic, political, and anthropological foundations of secondary education. Contemporary issues such as cultural values, social class, legal aspects, ethnic groups, political pressure, and the role of the teachers will be stressed. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299.

title: High School Curriculum
description: General perspectives of curriculum principles, practices, and procedures common to secondary schools. Organizational structures, innovations, and intimate relationships between instruction and curriculum. Concurrently, students will choose areas of concentration or preparation as they relate to the total high school curriculum.

title: Student Activities Programs in Secondary Schools
description: Student activities will be studied in terms of historical development, philosophical foundations, objectives, functions, current role and status, principles and procedures of development, organizational patterns, and innovative programs. Accommodates needs and interests of persons preparing to be involved in student activities programs in secondary schools.

title: The School Community and Secondary School Teaching
description: Focuses on the total school community as a broad teaching resource for every classroom teacher. Examines a variety of resources available, importance of establishing solid relationships, impact of community on classroom and classroom on community, significance of the schoolcommunity interaction both for individual teacher and total school.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Secondary Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective secondary teachers to cope with discipline problems in all secondary school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures for preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by secondary students and ways to create a positive environment for learning.

title: Career Education: Content and Processes for Secondary Educators
description: Career education concepts and attitudes and their effects analyzed in relation to effective implementation of career education in secondary schools. Techniques, methods, and materials identified and developed enabling prospective teachers to see meaningful relationships between career education and secondary curricular areas. The teaching of career identification skills and development of meaningful student work values examined. Course participants will develop -a model for the inclusion of career education in their areas.

title: Use of Microcomputers for Teaching in the Secondary School
description: Provides prospective teachers a basic understanding of the general applications of microcomputers in junior high/ middle school and in secondary school classrooms; includes evaluation of various hardware and software.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the Standard License in Secondary Education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the Standard License in Secondary Education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for nine weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Secondary
description: Prerequisite or parallel: EDSEC 460, 462 or EDJHM 466; and admission to student teaching.

title: General Innovations in Secondary Education
description: Innovative practices will be identified, defined, and analyzed relative to their impact on secondary schools. Creative, innovative instructional approaches will be employed. Field trips or visitations to innovative secondary schools will be arranged when practical, and students will concentrate on innovative practices.

description: Offered in cooperation with Boys' Clubs of America. Students are assigned to Boys' Clubs where they are given an opportunity in all phases of program and administration with certain responsibilities for advanced problems in each of these areas. The course is largely under the direction of a visiting professor representing Boys' Clubs of America. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Twining, Ulman, VanEvery, VanTassel The philosophy of special education encompasses the right of all children, youth, and adults to participate in educational and career planning experiences that will develop their capabilities to the fullest extent. Gradual acceptance of this philosophy by society has created an everincreasing demand for highly skilled personnel who are certified in the various exceptionality areas represented within special education. The Department of Special Education offers undergraduate programs leading to teacher certification in the areas of deaf education; mentally handicapped; moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped; and physically handicapped. Graduate programs are offered in teaching of learningdisabled and emotionally disturbed in addition to undergraduate preparation. These programs are designed in accordance with Indiana teacher licensure requirements. Elective courses in special education open to future teachers, psychologists, speech and hearing therapists, and social workers include a survey course of exceptional children, courses in the education of gifted chlidren, a course in the education of slow learners, and a course in the education of children with learning disabilities. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE HEARING -IMPAIRED The legal right of all children to an appropriate education has created a need for teachers of the hearingimpaired. The emphasis on "mainstreaming" exceptional children into the regular classroom developed a need for teachers of the hearingimpaired with more general preparation in addition to the specialized coursework for teachers of the deaf. The growth of different communication philosophies made it essential to provide additional coursework options within the majors and minors. A major in the education of the deaf is offered to those who prefer some level of elementary teaching, and a minor is available for persons who wish to teach an academic subject at the junior high and high school levels. The state of Indiana, Ball State University, and the Department of Special Education have adopted extensive requirements for licensing and have developed flexible programs that can accommodate the above needs. The Ball State University program for training teachers of the hearingimpaired meets the approval of the Indiana Teacher Training and Licensing Commission, the Council on the Education of the Deaf (CE D), and the U. S. Department of Health and Human Services. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE MENTALLY HANDICAPPED Acceptance of the philosophy of special education has led to the development of specialized programs for mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults. These programs have provided the impetus to prepare specially trained teachers to work effectively with mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped children, youth, and adults in the least restrictive instructional setting. Teachers and other interested professional personnel are taught the necessary skills to implement accepted intervention strategies for appropriately meeting the mentally handicapped person's learning style and educational and career needs. In response to the nationwide demand for qualified teachers to serve mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults, the Department of Special Education offers a major in the teaching of the mildly handicapped and minors in the teaching of the mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped. The teaching minor also serves as an endorsement in each of the exceptionality areas represented within the mentally handicapped area. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN WITH PHYSICAL OR SPECIAL HEALTH PROBLEMS Among children who have special educational needs are the physically handicapped (mildly and severely) and those who have other health conditions that make special class placement necessary. A typical classroom for these handicapped or healthimpaired children presents the teacher with a challenging variety of physical impairments as well as learning difficulties. To profit from their educational experience, these children are in need of specially prepared teachers with an understanding of the physical, psychological, and educational problems encountered in such a classroom, as well as knowledge of curriculum and methodology to meet these problems. The teacher education program is designed to offer comprehensive professional preparation to future teachers of physically handicapped (mildly and severely) or healthimpaired children so that these children will have the opportunity to learn and grow to the best of their ability under the guidance of competent, special teachers. title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: A survey of the educational needs of children who deviate from the normal in mental, physical, and social characteristics. Designed as an introduction to the field of special education.

title: Strategies for Developing Positive Concepts in Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool handicapped child's social and emotional stability. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Child Management Strategies for Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for more effectively managing the preschool handicapped child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Individualizing Learning Opportunities for Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for serving preschool handicapped children in the least restrictive learning environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Practicum-Teaching Young Handicapped Children
description: Student works with handicapped children six years of age or younger in a supervised practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of handicapped children in the classroom. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 16 hours

title: Fostering Developmental Competence of Preschool Handicapped Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool handicapped child's cognitive, language, and general learning environments. These developmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool handicapped children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Microcomputers and the Exceptional Learner
description: Introduces students to uses of microcomputers with exceptional children. Includes uses of microcomputers in special education ; elements of programing with emphasis on computerasisted instruction; andirect programming experience with exceptional children. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: History of Education of the Deaf and the Psychology of Deafness
description: A brief study of educational provisions for the deaf from the beginning to the present and a survey of the social, educational, and vocational problems of deafness.

title: Education of Preschool Hearing/Language-Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Ear and Vocal Mechanism

description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or may be taken parallel with

title: Psychology of Mental Retardation
description: Studies various types and degrees of retardation, the psychological, environmental, and cultural factors which contribute to retardation. Emphasizes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate retarded students. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, BIO 453 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Characteristics of Moderately, Severely, and Profoundly Retarded Individuals
description: Aspects of the intellectual, perceptualmotor, communication, academic, and personal social characteristics of the moderately, severely, and profoundly retarded. Procedures for formulating realistic instructional objectives will be explained. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 372.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of definitions, characteristics, and identification procedures relating to gifted and talented children in school and society. Research findings pertaining to these topics will be reviewed and analyzed.

title: Education of Slow Learners
description: Major topics include identification, characteristics, and practices and procedures for meeting the needs of the slow learning child. Emphasis on techniques and methods of instruction as well as research findings concerned with the slow learner and the culturally disadvantaged.

title: Learning Disabilities Techniques for the Regular Classroom Teacher
description: Emphasis on the role of the regular classroom teacher in relationship to legal, federal, and state mandates for identification, instruction, and programming for learningdisabled students in the regular classroom. Prerequisite: senior status.

title: Basic Audiology
description: Methods of measuring hearing. Practice in use of various types of audiometers. Interpretation of test results for reeducation and necessary followup measures in an educational hearing program. Prerequisite: SPAA 261 or SPCED 261, SPAA 440, or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in SPAA 442.

title: Aural Rehabilitation
description: Fundamentals of the visible movements involved in speech and the various methods, techniques, and materials for teaching lipreading to the deaf and the hardofhearing. Use of auditory training and hearing aids for rehabilitation. Prerequisite:

title: Speech Development for the Deaf
description: The International Phonetic Alphabet, Northhampton Charts, diacritical markings, and other methods and techniques used to teach speech to the deaf. Prerequisite: SPCH 216 and SPCED 240, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum in Speech for the Deaf
description: Observation of an individual working with preschool children in developmental speech. Time will also be devoted to speech improvement for older children. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 and 446 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Manual Communications
description: Theory and research underlying the language of signs and fingerspelling (manual alphabet) is considered. Development of receptive and expressive skills in manual communications is required. Required of students intending to student teach in schools or classes using total communication.

title: Advanced Manual Communication
description: A course in manual communication designed to improve conversational skill in signs and fingerspelling to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in a classroom for hearingimpaired children. Prerequisite: SPCED 451 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Language for the Deaf
description: Compares language development of hearing children with that of deaf children. Levels of abstraction and the difficulty encountered in both receptive and expressive language are examined. The philosophy underlying various methods of language teaching is studied. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and SPAA 370 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Language Methods for the Deaf
description: Language systems are studied and used in practice situations. Includes Fitzgerald Straight Language for the Deaf, Barry Five-Slate, Wing Symbols, and the Natural Method. Language outlines from different schools are used as supplementary aids. Prerequisite: SPCED 240, 266, and 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to the Deaf
description: Principles and methods of teaching reading to deaf children in the lower and higher grades; methods of teaching subjects such as arithmetic and science. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and 266 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Special Education
description: May be repeated by students fulfilling requirements for certification in a second exceptionality area. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Areas of Exceptionality
description: May be repeated by students fulfilling requirements for certification in a second exceptionality area. A total of 20 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Interpreting for the Deaf
description: A survey course to acquaint students with the fundamentals of interpreting for the deaf in special situations, familiarize them with professional behavioral guidelines unique to each setting, and develop beginning interpretive skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Expressive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Provides students who have basic manual communication skills with intensive training and practice in expressive interpreting for the deaf. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Receptive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Designed to provide students who have basic manual communication ability with professional skill for interpreting manual language in special situations. Opportunity for extensive practice and evaluation will be provided. Prerequisite: SPCED 468 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Handicapped
description: Special class organization, curriculum practices and procedures, and the methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (2 hrs.), 372; EDRDG 430; and MATH 391.

title: Diagnostic/Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Handicapped
description: Continuation of SPCED 474, emphasizing curriculum modifications and prescriptive teaching. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (2 hrs. ) and 474.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: Designed for future teachers of crippled or other healthimpaired students. Includes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate students with physical disabilities. Prerequisite SPCED 372.

title: Educational Methods With Physically/Multiply Handicapped Children
description: Special class organization, curriculum, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of multiply handicapped and/or orthopedic and special health problem children. Prerequisite: SPCED

title: Teaching Multiply Handicapped Children
description: Studies the problems of multiply handicapped children and youth. Symptomatology, assessment, and educational programming of multiply handicapped children will be emphasized. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 373, and

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Handicapped
description: Required for licensure in SPCED: Mildly Mentally Handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 14 hours of credit may be earned. Not open to the student who has credit in SPCED 465, 466.

title: Student Teaching: Physically/Multiply Handicapped
description: Required for licensure in SPCED: Physically/Multiply Handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 14 hours of credit may be earned. Not open to the student who has credit in SPCED 465, 466.

title: Colloquium in Humanities
description: Guided experiences in the arts and humanities.. An investigation of the major ideas and themes of specific works of art that are available and an attempt to demonstrate the interrelationships among the arts. Entails informed attendance at concerts, plays, art exhibits, and lectures.

title: Colloquium in Social and Behavioral Sciences
description: Students participate directly in the formulation and investigation of questions about man and society so that they can better understand human affairs now and in the future. The interrogations deal with matters such as violence, dissent and rebellion, university life, the cities, race relations, environmental pollution, people and political processes, and fundamental human traits.

title: Colloquium in Science and Mathematics
description: A study of "New Perspectives in the Sciences" designed to sensitize students to the implications of scientific thought for the student who is not pursuing a special area of science. One twohour lecture and two hours arranged weekly.

title: Colloquium in Business, Technology, and Applied Fields
description: A consideration of the interrelationships among business, technology, and other applied fields, and the major forces affecting the world at the present and in the future. Discussion of ways individuals may or should influence a more effective society in the United States and the world in order to live with meaning, purpose, and identity.

title: Colloquium in the Arts
description: Guided experiences in the arts and humanities. An investigation of the major ideas and themes of specific works of art that are available and an attempt to demonstrate the interrelationships among the arts. Entails informed attendance at concerts, plays, art exhibits, and lectures. Not open to the student who has credit in GENED 200.

title: Honors Symposium in Contemporary Civilization
description: An examination of some of the critical issues that confront contemporary civilization. Open only to freshmen participating in the Honors College.

title: Introduction to Sport in American Life
description: A thorough examination of the various historical, sociological, and psychological aspects of sport in our society. Not sportappreciation oriented, but rather an examination of what occurs to both competitors and spectators as they become involved with a sport activity. Open to all undergraduate students.

title: Women's Studies
description: An analysis of the role of American women in sociology, history, and literature, and an attempt to define the woman biologically and psychologically.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experiences meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the Office of Undergraduate Admission and Orientation and the registrar accordingly. The Office of Advising and scheduling is informed how the credit is to be applied to the student's program. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foreign Study
description: Foreign study provides a means of granting Ball State University credit for course work undertaken abroad at institutions of higher learning (e.g., universities, centers, and institutes) as part of approved study programs. Applicable toward majors, minors, or general education with departmental approval. Prerequisite: acceptance on a Ball State exchange program or approved studyabroad program. A total of 48 hours of credit may be earned. The course is offered for credit/no credit only.

title: Honors Candidate
description: May be taken each quarter by the honors candidate who has already registered in previous quarters for all his/her undergraduate course work, including ID 499, but has not yet completed his/her senior honors project. Enrollment in this course entitles the enrollee to ordinary undergraduate student use of library, health, and other university facilities.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An inquiry culminating in an honors paper prepared in accordance with accepted standards of documentation and presentation under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to seniors participating in the Honors College or completing the requirements for departmental honors. title: Introduction to Home Economics
description: Career opportunities available in home economics; introduction to Ball State home economics programs, facilities, staff; development of home economics as a profession. Activityoriented class involving field trips, using practicing home economists as resource persons, with indepth exploration of one area of the profession.

title: Principles of Home Art
description: Design and color principles, with practical application to home situations. Open to all students except those who have credit in ADS 104.

title: Home Economics Field Studies
description: Designed to combine a background of reading knowledge with field experiences in which students will have an opportunity to study special areas of home economics in a particular location. Open to all students with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Workshop: Home Economics
description: Activityoriented study of one area of home economics. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Independent Study in Home Economics
description: Permits the student to investigate and explore more intensively an area of home economics independently. Emphasizes extensive reading and the development of research skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Seminar in Home Economics
description: Student presentations and discussions on selected. topics of current interest in home economics. Emphasis on a different area of home economics each quarter offered. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Professional Development in Home Economics
description: Examines the skills needed in securing a job with emphasis on résumé writing, interviewing, and dress. Provides information on adjusting, succeeding, and growing as a professional in one's chosen career. Prerequisite: senior standing.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Applies the principles and philosophies of vocational education to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image.

title: Home Economics Presentation Techniques
description: Analysis of audience and business needs and the development of presentations and projects to meet these needs. Includes selection and use of presentation methods, development and use of devices, and professional roles and expectations. Open to all departmental majors in home economics and dietetics. Not open to students with a teaching major in vocational home economics. 395, Methods and Materials for Teaching Home Economics. (4) Organization of teaching units and lesson plans and selection and use of teaching methods and materials. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Recommended prerequisite: EDSEC 299. 399. Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials. (4) Disciplineoriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of home economics and development and use of devices for evaluating pupil growth. Topics will be developed in the context of field experience whenever possible. Prerequisite: HED 395.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Involves individual or group studies and experiences. Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis will be placed on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395, and 399.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: A study of how to coordinate class instruction and work experience ; includes selecting and recruiting students, selecting training stations, role of the coordinator, techniques of coordination, and placement and followup of graduates. Prerequisite: HED 392, 395.

title: Food Preparation and Meal Planning
description: Designed for students not majoring in home economics. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation stressed. Fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 110.

title: Principles of Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation stressed.

title: Food Experimentation and Comparison
description: Effects of different ingredients and methods of determining quality of products studied. Emphasizes recognition of standard products and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve standard products. Stresses the application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation. Prerequisite:

title: Meal Management
description: Principles and fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals, with emphasis on resource management and on the purchase and storage of food. Attention given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental princples of nutrition and application to diets for children and normal adults.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning—Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industry, and commercial operations. Experience in quantity food production kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Dietetic technology and food management major must take this course parallel with HFN 362. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 292,

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration
description: Emphasis on organizational structure, scientific management, and personnel administration. Experience in quantity food production kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 363. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 293.

title: Nutrition Care Practicum
description: Development of skills in interviewing clients, obtaining nutrition assessment data, and evaluating dietary intakes of people in all phases of the life cycle. Parallel: HFN 340. Open only to dietetic technician/nutrition care students.

title: Normal and Therapeutic Nutrition Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to normal and therapeutic nutrition in clinical and community settings. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 342.

title: Equipment Use, Sanitation and Employee Training Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to quantity food equipment use, sanitation, and employee train ing in a quantity food service setting. Gives the student experience under professional stan- - dards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 262 and 362.

title: Quantity Food Service Personnel Management Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience in personnel management in a quantity food service setting. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 263 and 363.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Purchasing Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience related to quantity menu planning and purchasing in a variety of quantity food service organizations. Gives the student experience under professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HFN 364 and 367.

title: Food and Nutrition Education Practicum
description: Develops and implements strategies for counseling and teaching individuals and groups emphasizing weight control, anorexia, neurologic disorders, exercise, malnutrition, alcoholism, allergies, food quackery, and wellness. Develops resource and product files related to management of these topics. Prerequisite: HFN 282, 342, 344. Parallel: HFN 345. Open only to dietetic technician/clinical nutrition students.

title: Nutritional Management of Disease Practicum
description: Experience in implementing nutritioncare plans for patients who have specific nutritional needs related to surgery; burn ; infection; diseases of the skeletal, gastrointestinal, liver, renal, and cardiovascular systems; diabetes; cancer; enteral and parenteral nutrition; nutrientdrug interaction. Prerequisite: HFN 295, 345. Parallel: HFN 346. Open only to dietetic technician/clinical nutrition students.

title: Nutrition
description: The nutritive value of foods and the use of food by the human body. The nutritional needs of people throughout the life cycle will be investigated. Prerequisite: junior/ senior level standing or a major in nursing, food management, or dietetic technology, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Principles of dietary modifications needed by people with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: HFN 340. Parallel: HFN 282 for dietetic technology students. Not open to the student who has credit in HFN 441.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Designed to acquaint the student with nutrition problems and nutrition programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Practical experience will include investigation and observation of and participation in nutrition programs in the local community. Prerequisite: HFN 340.

title: Food and Nutrition Education for the Dietetic Technician
description: Provides strategies for nutrition counseling and teaching of individuals and groups. Stresses nutritional management specifically for weight control, anorexia, neurologic disorders, exercise, malnutrition, alcoholism, allergies, food quackery, and wellness. Prerequisite: HFN 282, 342, 344; HED

title: Nutritional Management of Disease
description: Explains physiological basis for nutritional management of patients who have needs related to surgery; burn; infection; diseases of the skeletal, gastrointestinal, liver, renal, and cardiovascular systems; diabetes; cancer; enteral and parenteral nutrition; nutrientdrug interaction. Prerequisite: HFN 295, 345. Parallel:

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Laboratory experience in university food service units. Prerequisite: HFN 110 and 220.

title: Institutional Equipment, Buying, and Layout
description: Stationary and small equipment for food preparation considered. Layouts of quantity food production kitchens planned. Field trips to quantity food kitchens and equipment companies. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 262. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 292.

title: Institutional Administration
description: Concepts of quantity food service in restaurants, schools, hospitals, and cafeterias. Emphasis is placed on personnel, management, organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens. Dietetic technology and food management majors must take this course parallel with HFN 263. Dietetic technology students must take this course parallel with HFN 293.

title: Menu Planning for Quantity Food Service
description: Principles of nutrition applied to feeding individuals and groups. Major emphasis on menu planning for food services with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Explores problems relating to type of patronage and to limited personnel and facilities. Prerequisite: HFN 220 and 340. Parallel: HFN 294 and 367 for dietetic technology students.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers and important considerations in purchasing foods. Emphasis on ethics in buying. Parallel: HFN 294 and 364 for dietetic technology students.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of foods in relation to their composition, physical and chemical properties, and circumstances affecting food quality. Recipes are investigated and methods of combining ingredients are developed and evaluated. Prerequisite: HFN 110.

title: Advanced Nutrition
description: Advanced course in nutrition, emphasizing the use and metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Current research in the field of nutrition will be included. Laboratory experiences provided. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and CHEM 231; senior standing.

title: Diet in Disease
description: A study of the dietary modifications necessary for treating various nutritional diseases and problems. Planning therapeutic diets for abnormal conditions. Laboratory experiences provided. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and 440, CHEM 231, and permission of the department chairperson; senior standing.

title: Nutrition Assessment
description: A didactic and laboratory course employing the techniques needed to identify persons at risk of nutritional deficiency; to estimate the nutrient content of the diet; to evaluate anthropometric measures and tissue and excretory levels of certain nutrients, functional proteins, and metabolites used as indicators of nutrition status; and to determine appropriate nutrition therapies. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and 342 or 441, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Dietetics
description: The professions involved in food service and dietetics; the roles and responsibilities of personnel and their relationships with other professionals; the standards to be attained; the code of professional ethics and the resources for continuing professional education. Prerequisite: 2 hours of credit in HE 490 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition, Weight Control, and Exercise
description: Designed for students in dietetics, physical education, and healthrelated fields; information and experience for students preparing to provide nutrition counseling to persons in weight control and exercise training programs. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Maternal and Infant Nutrition
description: Information about maternal, prenatal, and infant (birth to thirtysix months) nutrition; nutritional requirements of expectant mothers and infants investigated. Emphasis on readings in current periodicals. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Child Nutrition
description: Principles of nutritional requirements of children from preschool age through adolescence. Investigates problems in nutrition. Researches current professional periodicals. Prerequisite: HFN 340, junior standing, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Geriatric Nutrition
description: Nutritional needs of older adults in the light of physiological and social changes and research in the field. Students review some recent literature in the field, evaluate the food intake of elderly citizens in certain situations, and study and evaluate nutrition programs designed for older adults in terms of meeting nutritional needs. Prerequisite: HFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition Counseling Practicum
description: Students provide nutrition counseling for pregnant women; families with infants; young and teenage children; and persons seeking guidance for weight control and special problems. Students are supervised by a member of the American Dietetic Association. Prerequisite: HFN 340 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in this course, but no more than 4 credit hours may be earned in one quarter or term.

title: Food Service Management Practicum
description: Provides experience in a food service organization, either in the private or public sector. Emphasizes development for food management expertise. Practicum approved and supervised by the Department of Home Economics. Prerequisite: HFN 360, 364, 367; senior standing; permission of department chairperson; and documented completion of at least 500 hours of appropriate food service work experience.

title: Seminar in Foods and Nutrition
description: Student presentations and discussions on specific topics of current interest in the field of foods and nutrition. Prerequisite: senior level or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Home Care of the Sick
description: Includes concepts that affect the quality of life of individuals and families in prevention of illness, current major health problems and their costs, and procedures to follow when illness occurs.

title: Infant Development
description: Growth and development from conception through the second year of life. Includes physical, social, emotional, and cognitive aspects of development. Students observe and interact with infants and toddlers. Open to all students.

title: Child Development
description: Emphasis on the preschool child as a member of a family group. Includes principles of natural growth and development and child guidance based on the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual needs of the preschool child. Students will participate in and observe various early childhood programs and centers. Open to all students.

title: Marriage
description: * The dynamics of the marital relationship and the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasizes the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection, marital communication, sexual adjustment in marriage, marriage adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasizes marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assisting with Family Problems
description: The major areas of adjustment in marriage and family relationships, problems of adjustment, and philosophy and practice of clientcentered assistance with family problems. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Family Relations
description: History and recent trends and developments in family life education, career opportunities involved in family life education, professional organizations, and ethical standards in the field. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson and senior standing.

title: Family Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, aesthetic qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Home Management 1
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Emphasis on the management problems encountered by newly married couples in establishing a home. Open to all students.

title: Household Equipment
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Students will have an opportunity to plan, organize, and present demonstrations on household equipment.

title: Home Management 2
description: Residence in the home management house offers opportunity to make practical application of the principles of homemaking. Prerequisite: HFN 220. Prerequisite or parallel: HHM 340.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing for the consumer, including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, and points to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Functional Home Design Practicum
description: Gives the student onthejob work experience with professional supervision in areas of functional home design. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Clothing
description: Provides basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, the apparel industry, and social and psychological aspects of clothing.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Learn creative skills in stitchery by embellishing existing fabrics or originating new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, needlepoint, and rya, braided, and hooked rugs. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HTC 104 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Costume History
description: A history of costume from its earliest beginnings to the present. Emphasis on the motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Prerequisite: HTC 230 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: A survey of the business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, and promotion. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adaptation of standard patterns to individual proportions, designing of garments, and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Prerequisite: HTC 104 and 203.

title: Textile Testing
description: Experience in planning and conducting textile tests and in evaluating resulting data; development, present status, and importance of textile testing. Prerequisite: HTC 230. 350• Household Textiles. (4) The selection, use, and care of drapery and curtain fabric, upholstery fabrics, household linens, and carpets and rugs. Investigates the thermal comfort and energy conservation of selected household textiles.

title: Clothing Problems
description: Special problems to meet students' needs in clothing construction. Includes units in machine attachments and adjustments, draperies, career projects, and problem fabrics. Prerequisite: HTC 104.

title: Fashion Merchandising Practicum
description: Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in an establishment chosen by the student. Prerequisite: HTC 270 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Fashion
description: Various facets of fashion merchandising emphasizing problems and issues facing the modern fashion merchandiser. Offers students an opportunity to work and consult with practitioners in fashion. Prerequisite: HTC 270 and senior standing or permission of department chairperson. Department of Industry and Technology Smith, Chairperson; Baldwin, Barella, Byers, DeKeyser, Edwards, Gurbach, Henak, Kirkwood, Kovac, Middleton, Reams, Ridgeway, Shackleford, South, Steele, Tang, Tomlinson, Tucker, Vickery, Wright The programs of the Department of Industry and Technology are designed to meet the needs of students who are qualifying for the teaching profession or technical or managerial positions in business and industry, exploring the industrial world for possible occupations or vocations, or seeking knowledge and understanding of our industrial society. A wide variety of industryrelated courses offers students many opportunities to explore occupational choices in construction, manufacturing, communications, computer applications, and power. Courses in these areas will also be of interest to students as part of the General Studies Program. Students who intend to pursue a concentration in teaching industrial education should take the following courses during their first year: IED 152, 153, 154, 156, 158, and 198. Students who intend to pursue a concentration in one of the several technological programs should contact the department chairperson to obtain recommendations of courses to take the first year. Students who have no intention of concentrating in the Department of Industry and Technology are encouraged to take IED 161 as an elective. For those who earn credit in IED 161 and later choose to take a concentration within the department, credit will count toward their concentration area as recommended by the department chairperson. In addition to the baccalaureate degree programs, the Department of Industry and Technology has two associate degree programs, manufacturing technology and printing technology. The manufacturing technology program has four options: computerintegrated manufacturing (CIM), manufacturing design, metals manufacturing, and plastics manufacturing. Note: Students are required to wear industrial safety glasses in all classes where they are exposed to sparks, flying chips, hot materials, and other hazardous substances. ASSOCIATE DEGREES ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE—MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY This twoyear program prepares students for careers in computerintegrated manufacturing (CIM), drafting and design, and the metals and plastics industries. Students will meet the standards of Ball State University with respect to admission, orientation, residence, and scholastic standards. Upon completion of this degree students may transfer to the fouryear industrial technology curriculum with little or no loss in university credit. Persons designated by the chairperson of the Department of Industry and Technology will act as counselors. General requirements: CHEM 110; CS 118 or 120; ENG 103; MATH 108, 112, and 114 or 161; PHYCS 110 28 hrs. Physical education (from PEG or PEGF) 2 hrs. ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE-PRINTING TECHNOLOGY This twoyear curriculum offers preparation for entrance into salaried technical positions in the printing industry and leads to the Associate in Science degree. Emphasis is placed on new techniques and on developments taking place in the printing industry. Persons designated by the chairperson of the Department of Industry and Technology will act as counselors for students in this program. General requirements: CHEM 100; ENG 103, 104 12 hrs. INDUSTRIAL TECHNOLOGY To prepare for management or technical positions in industry, the student will take the Professional Arts Curriculum with a department major in industrial technology; options are available in management and in manufacturing technology. Students in the manufacturing technology option can specialize in computerintegrated manufacturing (CIM), drafting and design, factory electronics, metals, and plastics. Students in the management option take a sequence of courses in business administration from the College of Business. Cooperative work experience (industrial internship) is open to selected students pursuing the industrial technology major. Students must work through the industrial technology program coordinator at Ball State to obtain the coop job. However, the university cannot guarantee industrial coop assignments. Students who complete four or more cooperative work quarters may enroll in ITE 363 for a maximum of 4 hours of elective credit. The time normally required for completing the curriculum ranges from four years for students with adequate high school preparation who spend full time on campus to five years for students following the cooperative work experience (industrial internship) option.
