Course descriptions are listed in regular numerical order under the prefixes General Industrial Studies (GIS), Industrial Education (IED), and Industrial Technology (ITE).

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance, and to make simple modifications and installations in plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climate control systems of the home.

title: Technical Drawing and Print Reading
description: The theory and practice of reading, interpreting, and preparing production drawings. Topics include lettering, multiview and pictorial drawings, dimensioning, sections, fasteners, and an introduction to computeraided drafting (CAD).

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing productionrelated drawings in selected specialized areas. Topics include auxiliary views, revolutions, cams, gears, bearings, machine components, welding drawing, structural drawing, piping drawing, and electrical drawing. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Introduction to Industrial Plastics
description: Basic industrial plastics processes and materials. Injection, extrusion, blow and compression molding, thermoforming, and thermofusion. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 253.

title: Introduction to the Construction Industry
description: A focus on the broad range of processes used in the construction industry. Students learn about and engage in activities related to managing, designing, building, and maintaining structures.

title: Introduction to Industrial Materials and Processes
description: Properties and characteristics of four major types of industrial materials: metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composites; and the industrial casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing processes used to convert these basic materials into finished products. 154.Introduction to Industrial Communication. (4) A focus on the elements common to industrial communication. Classroom and laboratory activities are related to the design, production, and distribution of printed graphic, photographic, electronic, and technical graphic communications.

title: Industrial Design
description: A study of major elements involved in creating an appealing design that can be manufactured economically. Topics include the design process, sketching, creativity, elements and principles of design, materials and processes, and human and environmental factors.

title: Introduction to Power
description: An overview of the development and use of power in terms of energy, energy conversion, transmission, control, and applications, with continual concern for energy conservation and environmental quality.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Industries
description: Introduction to manufacturing and its managed activities of research and development, production, marketing, industrial relations, and finance in manufacturing industries. Laboratory experiences involve organizing, staffing, and operating a model manufacturing enterprise. Open to all students except teaching majors in industrial education.

title: Exploring Industrial Education
description: Focuses on teaching industrial education as a career. Students learn about the development and types of industrial education programs offered in public schools and the undergraduate industrial teacher education program at Ball State University.

title: Advanced Technical Graphics
description: Includes work in axonometric, oblique, and perspective projection; intersections of lines, planes, and solids; and lateral developments of geometric solids. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Drafting
description: An introduction to computer drafting using an interactive software package on a microcomputer to create 2-D technical drawings on a system that emulates a major industrial turnkey system. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Manufacturing Design
description: The process of design and principles of drafting as applied to manufacturing industry. Includes product and tool design created on a CAD system. Prerequisite: IED 208 and 233.

title: Introduction to Woods
description: A basic course in wood processing for persons interested in consumer information related to wood products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for studentdesigned product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 251, 316, 317.

title: Industrial Plastics: Design and Mold Making
description: Introduction to plastics design and mold making. Individual problemsolving approach to construction of molds and dies for injection, rotational, and blow molding, extruding, and thermoforming. May include fiberglass and foam molds. Demonstrates appropriate moldmaking techniques and equipment. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256, 125 or 253, and 233 or 250.

title: Metal Machining
description: Metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling and grinding machines, bandsawing, and EDM. Discussions include tool design, precision measuring, basic NC, fundamentals of metallurgy, heat treating, and safety. Prerequisite: ITE 162 or IED 153.

title: Application of Power to Land Transportation
description: Relates power development for uses applicable to land transportation. Emphasizes internal combustion engines; power development and transmission; thermal, volumetric, and mechanical efficiency; and operation and maintenance. Bicycle maintenance and repair. Steps involved in setting up a transportatio n IED 259. unit in the industrial education program. Prerequisite:

title: Industrial Processing of Metals
description: Basic industrial processes used in manufacturing metal products. Studies, contrasts, and compares the processes of casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing to provide a conceptual understanding of each. Laboratory activities used to provide concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 153. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Processing of Wood
description: Methods used to process the natural polymer, wood, including casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing. Laboratory activities are directed toward helping students acquire basic understanding and skills related to wood processing, and the careers in the area. Prerequisite: IED 153. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 213 and 316.

title: Industrial Processing of Plastics
description: The molding, forming, casting, separating, conditioning, assembly, and finishing techniques of the plastics industry, including injection, extrusion, blow, compression and transfer molding, thermoforming, thermofusion, and expansion. Includes laboratory activities and discussion of employment opportunities. Prerequisite: IED 153. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 125.

title: Printed Graphic Communication
description: A study of printed graphic communications with major emphasis on design and developing messages, preparing messages for production, and producing messages using lithographic, relief, intaglio, and screen processes. Prerequisite:

title: Photographic Communications in Industry
description: The concepts and applications of photography as it applies to the communication system. Includes photographic techniques, visual systems, visual literacy and aesthetics, material applications, and subtractive color theory.

title: Technical Graphics Communications
description: A study of the various graphical methods used to transmit technical ideas and information in industry. Included are sketching, pictorials, orthographics for manufacturing and construction, charts and graphs, reprographics, and industrial practices. Prerequisite: IED 154. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Industrial Electronic Communication Systems
description: Electronics as it is used in the field of industrial communications. Major emphasis on telecommunication, information processing, and acoustical systems. Prerequisite: IED 154. Prerequisite applies only to students with areas in industrial education.

title: Introduction to Electronics
description: Fundamentals of electricity and electronics including terminology, concepts, theories, electromagnetism, application of DC circuits and their basic measurements, and an introduction to AC circuits. Includes laboratory activities. Prerequisite: one mathematics course from general studies. Not open to the student who has credit in ITE 270.

title: Mechanical and Fluid Power
description: Energy conversion, transmission, and control within the mechanical and fluid power parameters. A companion course to IED 258. Prerequisite:

title: Introduction to American Industry
description: Organization and management in American industry with emphasis on teaching the content of public school industrial arts programs. Laboratory activities emphasize developing, producing, and marketing studentselected products. Major emphasis on laboratory activities. Open only to students with a teaching major in industrial education. Prerequisite: IED 153, 156.

title: Computer Fundamentals
description: Computer hardware and applications, including computer structure and digital electronics and circuits. Laboratory activities include digital circuits construction using SSI and MSI chips. Prerequisite: IED 258 or ITE 270.

title: Student Organizations Practicum
description: A practicum in the organization, maintenance, and evaluation of student vocational organizations. A total of 4 quarter hours must be taken by persons seeking certification as teachers of vocational trade, industrial, and technical laboratory programs, and endorsement as cooperative coordinators. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. 992 . principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education. (4) An introduction to the founda - tion and operation of various vocational educational programs. Analyzes legislation in the light of past and present issues of vocational education and its function as a vital component of the educational system. 2 97 Technological Futuring. (4) The technology of the future. Presents futuring and -decisionmaking techniques that are useful in describing alternative futures, studying trends, assessing technology, and preparing forecasts.

title: Curriculum Development in Industrial Education
description: Designed to give prospective industrial education teachers the tools for rational decision making in developing curricula for industrial education programs. Emphasis on developing an adequate conceptual framework within which to design courses. Prerequisite: IED 198. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 394.

title: Residential Drafting and Design
description: Focuses on the basic principles of residential planning and design with emphasis on room design and arrangement, traffic patterns, lighting, heating, alternative energy forms, plumbing, and construction techniques. Students make working drawings, perspectives, and models.

title: Descriptive Geometry
description: Experiences in the graphical solution of coplaner and noncoplaner force systems, architectural graphics, bearing and slope notation of lines, geology, mining, and topology problems, and elementary problems in nomography.

title: Computer Graphics in Drafting and Design
description: Methods used to make technical drawings and other graphical representations by employing the computer and computerrelated devices. Emphasizes the use of the graphics display terminal and plotter in problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 208 and a computer programming language.

title: Construction Utility Systems
description: The design, installation, operation, and maintenance of heating, air conditioning, ventilating, electrical, plumbing, and communication systems in construction projects. Emphasis on installation. Prerequisite: IED 152.

title: Building Construction Projects
description: Emphasis on the skills, materials, equipment, processes, and careers associated with the construction industry. Course activities involve the building of onsite construction projects within the community. Prerequisite: IED 152.

title: Industrial Furniture and Cabinet Production
description: The conversion of primary and secondary wood materials into a consumer product. Application and understanding of basic wood product design, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, equipment maintenance, and safety. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Advanced Wood Processing
description: Units of study in bentwood, bentwood laminations, modifying wood, and wood finishing. Additional opportunities provided for individual problemsolving activities. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Interior Environmental Products
description: For students with areas in interior design, architecture, and home economics. Interior furnishings, furniture, and lighting are examined as elements of function. Exploratory laboratory activities include construction and evaluation of selected components commonly found in interior environments, and the materials from which they are made.

title: Advanced Industrial Plastics Technology
description: Advanced techniques of automatic production plastics processing. Includes short production runs of parts and test samples, analysis of part quality, and field trips. Prerequisite: IED 225.

title: Industrial Plastics: Advanced Mold and Die Making
description: Designing and building automatic injection molds, extrusion dies, and compression molds with such features as ejection pins, stripper plates, and cooling lines. Field trips to mold shops and molding plants. Requires drafting skills. Prerequisite: IED 225 and ITE 331.

title: Metal Forming and Assembly Practices
description: Sheet metal, wrought metal, forging, and assembly processes. Uses classroom and laboratory activities in safety, maintenance, and industrial procedures to provide conceptual and concrete experiences. Prerequisite: IED 153 or ITE 162 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Casting and Bonding Metals
description: Flat position welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work with TIG and MIG. Emphasizes various casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques. Prerequisite: ITE 162 or IED 153.

title: Advanced Metal Machining
description: Factors affecting metal manufacturing machine systems. Content includes chip formation; force work and power requirements; cutting fluids and application; machinability, tool life measurement and control; and factors affecting finish. Prerequisite: IED 233.

title: Problems in Metals
description: Individualized study of the characteristics of metals processing. Prerequisite: IED 233 or 250.

title: Advanced Automechanics
description: The maintenance, repair, and theory underlying power train and power transmission units, air conditioning systems, emission control systems, and compression ignition engines. Prerequisite: IED 240.

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to persons currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Safety
description: Provides an awareness of the regulations governing health and safety and the methods and practices used in industry in general and industrial education specifically to comply with these regulations. Designed primarily for students choosing concentration areas in the Department of Industry and Technology.

title: Industrial Product Research and Development
description: Focuses on the industrial activities of research, development, and product engineering as they relate to manufacturing enterprises. Laboratory activities will provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with product research and development. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Requires safety glasses. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263, and 105 or 256 or ITE 300.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes that provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Examines and evaluates methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units.

title: Practicum in Elementary School Industrial Arts
description: Acquaints the student with the philosophy, history, and principles of industrial arts in the elementary school. Affords students the opportunity to teach a short unit of instruction in cooperation with an elementary teacher to elementary age children in the local community. Prerequisite: industrial arts major or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Electric Machines and Controls
description: Principles and applications of power transformers, DC and AC generators, and DC and AC motors; controls and testing of various machines. Laboratory experiments. Prerequisite: IED 258 or ITE 270.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by a breakdown into components of jobs, tasks, and processes.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Examines and evaluates educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs.

title: Curriculum Problems in Industrial Education
description: Criteria used in determining nature and content of learning experiences in industrial education classes. Teacherpupil planning, group activities, and problemsolving methods. Textbooks and related industrial and government publications evaluated and course outlines developed. Prerequisite: IED 125, 213; ITE 180.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Industrial Education
description: Problems of organization and management related to industrial education learning activities. Examines objectives, terminology, evaluation methods, teaching devices, lesson plans, textbooks, equipment, and supplies. Students observe industrial education classes in public schools. Prerequisite: IED 198 and 298 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Education
description: Practice in various contemporary approaches to industrial education drawn from methods and curriculum problems courses. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in one or more of the contemporary approaches to industrial education, preferably a public school. Prerequisite: IED 198, 298, and 395.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Disciplineoriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of industrial education, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of industrial education in the secondary school curriculum (grades 5 through 12). Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: IED 298 and 395.

title: Problems in Technical Graphics
description: Detailed and extensive study in technical graphic areas based on the needs of the student and the approval of the instructor. Prerequisite: IED 105 or 256.

title: Computer Design of Plastics Molds
description: Design of molds for plastics products by computer. Plastics flow analysis, cooling analysis, part shrinkage, and cost analysis using computer programs. Use of electronic component and data base catalogs. Prerequisite: IED 208. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned. 408• Problems in Computer Graphics. (4) Advanced study in computer graphics as it applies to design and drafting. Emphasis on writing interactive programs. Prerequisite: IED 308.

title: Problems in Woods
description: Extended development of knowledge and skill in woods, particuarly those processes in which the student lacks confidence and experience. Emphasis on individual problem solving. Prerequisite: IED 213 or 251.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 1
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. May include mold making, materials testing, and equipment design. Prerequisite: IED 325 and 326.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 2
description: A continuation of IED 425. Development of the research started in IED 425. Material or process tests made, equipment or molds developed, and equipment installed. Prerequisite: IED 425.

title: Problems in Sheet Metal and Machine Shop
description: Specialization in the theory and practice of sheet metal work, machine work, precision measurement, metal testing and inspection, and metallurgy. Prerequisite: IED 233 or 335.

title: Problems in Hot Metals
description: Specialization in advanced casting theory and techniques. Advanced welding includes horizontal, vertical, and overhead welding techniques with electric and oxyacetylene welding equipment. Studies inert gas welding theory and techniques in depth. Also includes the fundamentals of forging practices. Prerequisite: IED 334.

title: Research and Development in Metals
description: Research and development of problems related to metals manufacturing. Prerequisite: IED 334 and 335, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Developing Production Systems
description: Focuses on activities associated with design and installation of industrial production methods and facilities. Laboratory activities provide opportunities to perform basic tasks associated with developing a production system. Major emphasis on laboratory experiences. Four hours of lecture and approximately four hours of laboratory a week. Requires safety glasses. Prerequisite: IED 153 or ITE 162; IED 161 or 263; and IED 363.

title: Manual Arts Therapy Clinical Training
description: A field assignment with opportunities to work with qualified manual arts therapists at the Veterans' Administration Hospital in Marion, Indiana. Credit for 10 hours is awarded for minimum of eight weeks fulltime training. Prerequisite: EDSEC 299 and IED 395.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Semiconductor devices, rectifiers, SCR, frequency conversion, digital and analog transducers, optoelectronics, operational amplifiers and the industrial applications of these devices. Prerequisite: IED 258 or ITE 270.

title: Problems in Industrial Electronics
description: Special individual and group problems in advanced electrical circuitry involving most of the components of electrical circuits, with special emphasis upon thermionic emission tubes and photo emission devices. Complex problems assigned to groups of students will characterize the project activity. Prerequisite: IED 257.

title: Problems in Printed Graphics
description: Problems in letterpress and photooffset lithography as applied to conventional form in contrast with design. Composition by linotype and color separation as applied to photooffset lithography. Prerequisite: IED 254 or ITE 180.

title: Independent Studies in Industrial Education
description: Special investigation in industrial education on an independent basis. Emphasizes experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques and skills. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. 491.Obtaining Employment in Industrial Education. (1) The process of identifying, seeking, and obtaining employment in industrial education. Open only to industrial education majors.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis on state functions.

title: Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Individual and group studies of one or more major problems in the industrial education field, application of research techniques to the problems for solution, and reporting of findings.

title: Advanced Practicum in Industrial Education
description: Advanced study of problem -solving techniques in industrial education. Individual and group activities involving research and experimentation.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: An introduction to and conceptual understanding of manufacturing processes used by industry to convert raw materials into consumer products. Four hours of lecture and approximately two hours of laboratory each week. Requires safety glasses. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 153.

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: The basic reproduction processes, materials, and equipment used in graphic arts industries. Includes layout and design, relief printing, photooffset printing, screen printing, the reproduction of color, and finishing operations.

title: Theory and Practice of Letterpress Printing
description: Introduction to letterpress/relief printing in the contemporary graphic arts industries. Includes layout and design, copy preparation, typesetting, platemaking, automatic presswork, introduction to paper and inks, basic estimating, and company organization.

title: Theory and Practice in Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Photooffset lithographic printing in contemporary graphic arts industries. Includes layout and design, copy preparation, phototypesetting, camerawork (line and halftone), stripping, platemaking, presswork (duplicator and press), introduction to process color, multicolor printing, and related photographic processes.

title: Quality Control in the Printing Industry
description: Studies the process of quality control for printed products including the instruments used in evaluating materials and printed products, inspection and sampling techniques, manufacturing specifications of various printed products, and quality control systems found in the graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITE 181 or 182.

title: Printing Estimating 1
description: Studies printing estimates including identification of steps involved in the production of printed products, the development of estimating standards, corn_ putation of production costs (material, labor, and overhead), and the preparation of estimates, proposals, and quotations. Prerequisite: ITE 181 or 182.

title: Internship in Printing Technology
description: A fiveweek internship in a printing industry, working under industrial standards and regulations. As far as possible, the internship will be in the type of printing industry preferred by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Characteristics of Industrial Materials
description: Focuses on providing a broad understanding of the mechanical properties of industrial materials as they relate to processing and application. Research and experimentation are conducted through laboratory experiences by performing standardized tests. Four hours of lecture and approximately two hours of laboratory work each week. Requires safety glasses. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 153.

title: Applied Quality Control
description: Variables, procedures, and processes of total quality control within the manufacturing industries: Topics include instrumentation for material evaluation, attribute inspection and sampling, supervising for organizational quality improvements, and statistical control. Emphasizes directed laboratory experiences.

title: Introduction to Industrial Electricity and Electronics
description: Fundamentals of electricity and electronics, including theory, power sources, instrumentation, applications, and employment opportunities. Prerequisite: MATH 108 and PHYCS 110.

title: AC Circuits Analysis
description: Studies the behaviors of inductors and capacitors under DC and AC, RLC circuits, series and parallel resonance, diodes and transistors, and power supplies and filters. Includes handson experiences and project construction. Prerequisite: ITE 270 or IED 258.

title: Theory and Practice in Publications
description: Studies the various publication formats of books, magazines, and newspapers and their production systems as incorporated by commercial printing and publishing companies. Prerequisite: ITE 285.

title: Printing Estimating 2
description: Advanced study to establish production standards, hour cost of various production centers, and the estimator's role in purchasing. Students must estimate and plan production while interacting with production management and scheduling. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Commercial Printing
description: The organization and production systems of commercial printing and publishing companies. Includes basic management systems, printing production systems, quality control, material control, estimating, production scheduling, manufacturing specifications, and current trends in graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITE 181 or 182.

title: Type Design and Copyfitting
description: The determination of the amount of area necessary for composition according to size and family of type by use of a slide rule. The study of modern type design and usage, as well as outstanding typographers and their contributions. The place of the advertising agency in modern display composition and its contributions. Prerequisite: ITE 187.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Studies production control systems used in contemporary graphic arts industries. Includes production scheduling, production sequence analysis, work and material flow for printing production, cost analysis of production, and the effective use of personnel and equipment resources. Prerequisite: ITE 181 or 182.

title: Blueprint Reading for the Manufacturing Industries
description: Emphasis on reading and interpreting detail drawings, assembly drawings, schematics, and numerical control documentation used in the manufacturing industries.

title: Introduction to Computer-Integrated Systems
description: Computeraided design (CAD) and computeraided manufacturing (CAM) and their integration into a complete manufacturing system. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263; 233. 30• Fundamentals of Metals Processing. (4) Characteristics of casting, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling,a anndd f inishing of major manufacturing processing techniques. Relates product applications design processes to selection constraints and tradeoffs freciuently necessary in manufacturing. Prerequisite: IED 233. Not open to the student who has credit in IED 250.

title: Fundamentals of Computerized Numerical Control
description: The fundamentals of NC and CNC processes. Activities include programming of NC and CNC equipment and preparing tapes both manually and with computers. Prerequisite: MATH 112; IED 208 and 233.

title: Introduction to Fluid Power
description: Fluid statics and applications of fluid dynamics to the analysis and design of power systems. Four hours of lecture and approximately two hours of laboratory work each week. Prerequisite: ITE 270.

title: Industrial Internship
description: A student works in an industry related to his curriculum with the approval of the program coordinator. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microprocessors and Microcomputers: Fundamentals
description: Provides student with an understanding of microprocessors and microcomputers. Includes the development of microprocessors as an electronic component; the evolution of 4-, 8-, 16-, and 32-bit microprocessors; the basic structure and architecture of various microcomputers; and microprocessor/microcomputer applications. Prerequisite: IED 271.

title: Fundamentals of Industrial Robots
description: The technology (manipulator, mechanism, sensors, controls, programming, machine vision, etc.), application (welding, material handling, inspection, etc.), and management (justification, implementation, human factors) of industrial robots. Prerequisite: IED 161 or 263; ITE 270 or IED 258 and a computer programming language.

title: Screen Printing
description: A basic course designed to provide a comprehensive overview of the screen printing process with emphasis on theory, materials, equipment, and techniques of printing by the screen process as found in contemporary graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITE 180, 181, 182.

title: Relief Printing and Bindery
description: Stresses fundamental letterpress/relief theory with experiences in layout and design, typesetting, imposition, single color and multicolor presswork, and finishing operations including binding techniques, bookbinding, and looseleaf and saddlestitch operations. Prerequisite: IED 254; ITE 180 or 181.

title: Photography
description: Blackandwhite photography focusing on camera handling, film exposure and processing, printmaking, basic composition, and print finishing. Includes introduction to color photography, applications of photography, types of photographic equipment, and careerrelated information in photography.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Fundamental theory, exposure techniques, film processing, printmaking, and composition considerations in color photography. Students must provide their own cameras. Prerequisite: ITE 386.

title: Color Separation and Process Printing
description: Focuses on the additive and subtractive theories of color, direct and indirect methods of color separation, color measurement and evaluation, films, plates, registration systems, offset presswork for process color, and quality control for color reproduction. Prerequisite: ITE 182, 387.

title: Training and Development in Industry
description: The activities of training and development in industry and their relationship to the job and the organization. Emphasizes skills needed to systematically plan, implement, evaluate, and revise training and development programs. Provides opportunities for practical application and practice.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: A discussioncentered course that relates primarily to the process of identifying, seeking, and obtaining employment in industry. Open only to industrial technology majors. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Industrial Programmable Controls
description: Technical knowledge of both discrete industrial controls and programmable controls. Uses motor control panel and programmable controller panel for handson activities in control applications. Prerequisite: IED 271; ITE 271.

title: Introduction to Computer -Aided Manufacturing
description: Application of computer numerical control, computeraided design and manufacturing, robotics and other computer based manufacturing systems. Prerequisite: IED 308; ITE 301 and 331.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography
description: Indepth study of the contemporary application of photooffset lithography in the commercial printing and publishing industries. Includes theory of lithographic printing, layout and design, copy preparation, phototypesetting, camera work (line and halftone), stripping, platemaking, offset presswork, and multicolor/process color applications. Prerequisite: IED 254; ITE 180 or 181.

title: Printing Management
description: Business facts needed for profitable management of a printing or lithographic business and the procedures to supply these facts accurately and promptly, with laborsaving shortcuts. Prerequisite: ITE 289.

title: Industrial Internship
description: The student will work full time for one quarter under supervision of the Department of Industry and Technology in a position involving the supervision of production employees in a printing industry. Prerequisite: ITE 484. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. Department of Library and Information Science Suput, Chairperson; Beilke, Garland, Hsu, Tevis, Yeamans The Department of Library and Information Science and its offerings are in the process of being phased out.

title: Introduction to Media Science
description: History and overview of the use of media in instruction, commercial enterprises, and industry with a discussion of job requirements and opportunities.

title: Operation and Maintenance of Audiovisual Equipment
description: Instruction in the operation of projection, video, and audio equipment. Laboratory practice in maintenance and minor repair of equipment.

title: Multimedia Design and Display
description: Principles of media design and perception patterns. Application of these principles to the construction of twoand threedimensional displays for library and instructional uses.

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

title: Reference Materials for Information Centers and Libraries
description: The role and function of the information specialist in information centers and libraries. Evaluation and selection of information resources, and directed experience using representative materials essential to information centers and libraries.

title: Multimedia Production 1
description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work in the development of multimedia materials for teaching and presentation. Provides laboratory experience in various mounting, laminating, lettering, coloring, and transparencymaking techniques.

title: Multimedia Production 2
description: Basic photographic and cinematographic techniques. Advanced transparencymaking using photographic processes.

title: Multimedia Production 3
description: Advanced photographic and cinematographic practices. Production of multimedia using electronic devices.

title: Selection and Management of Audiovisual Equipment
description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment and related devices. Preparation of bid specifications.

title: Media Technician Practicum
description: Supervised practical experiences at an offcampus media center in various phases of media technology.

title: Library Administration
description: Introductory principles of library administration, functions of planning, decision making, organizing, directing, controlling, and evaluating.

title: Global Information Resources and Systems
description: Experience in exploration of library information resources and documentation systems related to other countries. Examination of cultural, business, scientific, and technological automated information systems and selected documents related to individual interests and vocational choices.

title: Organization of Library Materials
description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of materials in school libraries by use of the Dewey Decimal Classification and the construction of a library catalog. Consideration is given to other materials as well as books.

title: Cataloging and Organization of Multimedia Materials
description: The principles and practice Library and Information Science 95 of the cataloging and organization of multimedia materials. Prerequisite: LIB 342 or the equivalent.

title: Introduction to Library Automation
description: An introduction to computers in library automation; working knowledge of OCLC terminal for searching, input, and manipulation of cataloging data; survey of other automated systems.

title: New Multimedia and Information Technologies
description: New technologies for storing, processing, retrieving, and transmitting information. Applications and implications of new multimedia and information technologies in various professions.

title: Online Information Retrieval Techniques
description: An overview of online information services and principles of information retrieval. Students develop search strategies to meet clients' information needs and conduct online searches in a supervised laboratory.

title: Methods and Materials for Student Use of School Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching students the skills necessary for using the media center. Prerequisite: LIB 100, 101, 102, 133, 201, 202, 203, 342, 460 or the equivalent and the identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: Utilization of Media Center Resources in the Curriculum
description: The curriculum role of the school media center, its unique contributions to learning, its supportive services, and its responsibilities shared with all other aspects of the educational program. Prerequisite: LIB 395.

title: Selection of Audiovisual Materials and Microcomputer Software
description: Selection and evaluation of audiovisual materials and microcomputer software for instructional and management use in libraries. Systematic identification of sources and selection tools. Practice in selection and evaluation.

title: Production of Audiovisual Media
description: A project course that meets the individual needs of undergraduate students in the production of such instructional media as 8 and 16 mm films, filmstrips, slide sets, and tape recordings.

title: Selection of Library Materials
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection of library materials. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials for public, academic, and school libraries.

title: Materials for Children
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for young adult programs.

title: Indexing and Abstracting
description: Principles and methods of indexing and abstracting, including the use of new technologies (e.g., computer and videodisc). The effects of indexing and abstracting practices on information retrieval. Applications for inhouse files as well as commercial databases.

title: Contemporary Issues in Multimedia and Information Technology
description: The current major issues and problems in multimedia and information technologies; various contemporary opinions about their causes and solutions are presented to illustrate various interpretations and corrective approaches.

title: School Media Center Administration
description: The function, organizational patterns, maintenance, control, planning, and equipping of school media centers. The application of administrative principles to school centers.

title: Information Center Management
description: The functions, organizational patterns, planning, and equipment needs of information centers. Applies management principles to an information center that serves a business, industrial, governmental, or nonprofit agency.

title: Planning Information Center Facilities
description: The information center's physical plant as influenced by multimedia and information technologies used in response to contemporary needs. Planning processes for new and remodeled facilities; visits to information centers.

title: Advanced Online Information Retrieval
description: Advanced methods for online searches in selected data bases. Procedures for establishing and evaluating online services. Relates to the career goals of the student. Prerequisite: LIB 392 or permission of instructor.

title: Special Topics in Multimedia and Information Technology
description: Special topics related to multimedia and information technology not covered in the regular course offerings. A total of 8 credit hours may be earned.

title: Multimedia/Information Technology Internship
description: Supervised field experience for students who wish to enhance their career development in multimedia/information technology. Department of Military Science Flynn, Chairperson; Davenport, Fountain, Fraites, Johnson, Kelley, Tooley, Willey The Army ROTC program gives qualified students—both men and women—an opportunity to obtain a commission in the United States Army and its reserve components. Students may obtain this commission by enrolling in the Army ROTC program along with their regular undergraduate studies in fields of their choice. The program consists of two elements: basic and advanced courses. The basic course, normally taken during the freshman (Military Science 1) and sophomore (Military Science 2) academic years, provides essential background information concerning organization and operations of the U.S. defense establishment. Students in the basic course do not incur any military obligations by enrolling in these classes. Completion of the basic course, constructive credit for Junior AROTC (three years), attendance at a basic summer camp, or prior military service is a prerequisite for admission into the advanced course. The advanced course, normally taken during the junior and senior academic years, provides students with leadership and management skills not available in other curricula and with concepts of military tactics, operations, and organizations. Advanced course students are obligated to attend an advanced summer camp (six weeks) and to accept a commission as an officer, if tendered. Advanced course students receive subsistence and pay of about $2,500 during the two years. All necessary equipment and books are furnished by the Department of the Army at no cost to the student. Credits earned in the military science (AROTC) program may apply toward degree requirements. For specific information, students should consult with their advisers in their major fields of study. The U.S. Army offers financial assistance in the form of two-, three-, and fouryear scholarships. Each scholarship provides tuition, textbooks, laboratory fees, and supplies in addition to subsistence pay of $100 a month for the period the scholarship is in effect. Applications for these scholarships may be submitted by anyone enrolled in the AROTC program or nonenrolled students who agree to compress the first two years of the program. Students may also enter the Army Reserve or National Guard under the Simultaneous Membership Program to gain additional experience and financial assistance. Most graduates who have completed the advanced course will be called upon to serve a threeyear tour of active duty and three years in the U.S. Army Reserve. Others will serve three months active duty for training in lieu of three years active duty and be required to participate in the Ready Reserve until the eighth anniversary date of the initial appointment in the Army Reserve. Entry to active duty may be deferred to obtain an advanced degree. Departmental minor in military science, 27 hours MIL 110, 120, 130, 210, 220, 230, 310, 320, 330, 410, 420, 430 24 hrs. N. accredited baccalaureate program of studies in nursing is the preparation of a professional nurse generalist who functions independently and interdependently with people and with health team members in a variety of hospital and community settings. The graduate also possesses the background knowledge and skill for progression into firstlevel administrative positions and graduate study. Graduates are awarded Bachelor of Science degrees and are eligible to take the State Board Test Pool Examination for licensure as a registered nurse. Classroom and laboratory instruction is provided by the university. The program also uses hospital facilities adjacent to campus and other nearby community health agencies. A student indicating an intent to major in nursing begins study in English, social sciences, physical and biological sciences, and the fine arts. Approximately two years of academic work in humanities and behavioral and biological sciences is required. The major in nursing is concentrated in the student's junior and senior years. For registered nurses wishing to obtain a baccalaureate degree, the School of Nursing offers a professional nursing program. The plan of studies for the R.N. takes into account past educational endeavors and work experience. The program is flexible and will accommodate either the fulltime or parttime student. Interested R.N.'s should write the Associate Director, Baccalaureate Program. BACCALAUREATE DEGREE Objectives of the Baccalaureate Program 1. To integrate knowledge of nursing theory with knowledge from other disciplines for improved health care of clients. 2. To use concepts of general systems theory in applying the nursing process to clients of diverse ages in a variety of settings for the restoration, maintenance, and promotion of health. 3. To assist people in maximizing health potential congruent with their needs and environmental influences. 4. To use effective communication in establishing relationships with people and their support systems. 5. To implement leadership and management principles to influence individual health and health care systems effectively. 6. To use teachinglearning strategies to promote health in a variety of settings with individuals and small groups. 7. To apply research findings for improved nursing practice. 8. To manifest personal accountability for nursing practice. 9. To develop personal responsibility for potential as a member of the nursing profession. The curriculum for the professional nursing program is classified under the Professional Arts Curriculum and leads to the baccalaureate degree.
