title: Level 3 Listening Comprehension
description: Continued practice in comprehension of normal spoken English. Increased use of recorded unadapted materials and radio, television, and film. Prerequisite: ENEFL 125 or approval of program director.

title: Level 3 Pronunciation
description: Review of American English segmental and prosodic systems. Practice for accuracy in production of diphthongs, unstressed syllables, and reduced segments. Prerequisite: ENEFL 126 or approval of program director.

title: Level 4 Writing
description: Development of paragraph forms, with emphasis on logic and coherence, grammatical variations, diction, and idiom. Prerequisite: ENEFL 131 or approval of program director.

title: Level 4 Grammar
description: Development of grammatical variants and increasingly complex and specialized structures. Prerequisite: ENEFL 132 or approval of program director.

title: Level 4 Readings
description: Readings in both prepared and unadapted English. Selections from literary genres as well as from technical fields. Emphasis on linguistic and cultural problems and critical response. Prerequisite: ENEFL 133 or approval of program director.

title: Level 4 Conversation
description: Continued conversation practice with emphasis on building vocabulary and developing oral fluency. Increasing use of newspaper and magazine articles as sources of topics. Emphasis on current events and cultural activities. Prerequisite: ENEFL 134 or approval of program director.

title: Cross-Cultural Studies 1
description: Classes will deal with dating, sports, entertainment, U.S. and international politics, civil and human rights, individual freedom and responsibility, and other current topics through such activities as short papers, group discussion, guest speakers, and attendance at appropriate events. Prerequisite: ENEFL 134 or approval of program director.

title: Study Skills for Foreign Students 1
description: Taking notes, impromptu writing in English as a foreign language, preparing for tests, and using library resources. Prerequisite: ENEFL 133 and 135 or approval of program director.

title: Level 5 Writing
description: Paragraph and essay writing. Practice in rhetorical modes of American English. Prerequisite: ENEFL 141 or approval of program director.

title: Level 5 Grammar
description: Parallel structures; use of grammatical variants and rhetorical devices. General grammar review. Prerequisite: ENEFL 142 or approval of program director.

title: Level 5 Readings
description: Readings in unadapted selections from American literature, current magazines, and semispecialized writing. Emphasis on linguistic and cultural problems and critical response. Prerequisite: ENEFL 143 or approval of program director.

title: Cross-Cultural Studies 2
description: Classes will deal with dating, sports, entertainment, U.S. and international politics, civil and human rights, individual freedom and responsibility, and other current topics, through such activities as short papers, group discussion, guest speakers, and attendance at appropriate events. Prerequisite: ENEFL 147 or approval of program director.

title: Study Skills for Foreign Students 2
description: Research methods and research paper writing using standard style sheets. American cultural views on such academic issues as documentation and plagiarism. Prerequisite: ENEFL 148 or approval of program director.

title: TOEFL Preparation
description: Review of English grammar and vocabulary with special practice in aural and written comprehension to prepare for the Test of English as a Foreign Language. Prerequisite: TOEFL score of 500 or approval of program director.

title: Fundamentals of English Composition
description: Focuses on the fundamentals of composition with special attention to the problems of grammar and mechanics. Required of all students with SAT (V) scores of 360 or lower and TSWE scores of 36 or lower; or ACT English scores of 15 or lower. The course is offered on a credit/no credit basis and credit hours do not count toward graduation requirements.

title: English Composition 1
description: Introduction to composition with an emphasis on writing short essays. Includes assigned readings. Specific competencies are measured by the English department at the beginning and end of the quarter. Prerequisite: SAT (V) above 360, or TSWE above 36, or ACT English score above 15, ENG 099 or placement according to a test administered by the Department of English.

title: English Composition 2
description: Further instruction in composition with an emphasis on writing longer essays. Includes assigned readings. Introduction to basic research methods. Specific competencies are identified at the beginning of the quarter and measured at the end of the quarter. Prerequisite: ENG 103.

title: English Composition 3
description: Continued instruction in composition skills through oral and written work. Includes assigned readings. Further instruction in research techniques. Specific competencies are identified at the beginning of the quarter and measured at the end of the quarter. Prerequisite: ENG 104 or 114.

title: Honors English Composition 2
description: Instruction in composition with emphasis on writing essays. Assigned readings. Introduction to basic research methods. Specific competencies will be identified at the beginning of the quarter and measured at the end of the quarter. Prerequisite: SAT Verbal Score of 530 or above. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 104.

title: Honors Humanities 1: Western Thought from Homer to Dante
description: Some major texts in the literature, philosophy, history, and general thought of the Greek, Roman, and Christian civilizations through the Middle Ages.

title: Honors Humanities 2: Western Thought from Montaigne to Rousseau
description: Some major texts in literature, philosophy, history, and science during the Renaissance and through the eighteenth century.

title: Honors Humanities 3: Western Thought from Dostoyevsky to Sartre
description: Some major writing in literature, philosophy, and science from 1800 until the present.

title: World Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of world literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 206.

title: World Literature Masterpieces
description: Selected major works of world literature, exclusive of English and American literature, for students who are majors or minors in English. Prerequisite: ENG 103 and 104. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 205.

title: American Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of American literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104.

title: British Literature
description: Introduction to selected pieces of British literature for class and individual oral and written interpretation and evaluation for those who are not English majors or minors. Prerequisite: ENG 104.

title: Fundamentals of English Grammar and Usage
description: Basic course in English grammar and usage for the student whose knowledge of grammatical terminology, structure, and usage is deficient. Not to be counted as part of the total hours in a major or minor program in English.

title: Advanced Composition and Creative Writing
description: Instruction in critical writing about literature beyond that provided for the general student, including the study of techniques of literary research, criticism, and documentation; and instruction in creative writing, particularly fiction and poetry. Open only to English majors and minors, except by permission of the department chairperson. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, or the equivalent, and sophomore standing.

title: Professional Writing
description: Discussion of principles of organization, structure, and style in writing reports and papers. Intensive practice in writing different types of reports and papers. Designed primarily for students pursuing the general arts or the professional arts curriculum. Prerequisite: ENG 104 or the equivalent.

title: Advanced Expository Writing
description: Intensive study of the essay and guided practice in the techniques of expository writing for students not majoring or minoring in English. Prerequisite: ENG 104 or the equivalent. Not open to the student with areas in English.

title: Introduction to American Literature
description: Introduction to selected American writers and their works with an emphasis on those that junior high/middle school teachers should know and be able to read skillfully. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Introduction to British Literature
description: Introduction to selected writers and periods in British literature with an emphasis on those that junior high/middle school teachers should know. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: American Literature, 1607 -1860
description: A survey of American literature from its beginning through the middle nineteenth century, including selections from a broad range of major and minority traditions. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, or the equivalent.

title: English Literature of the Middle Ages and Renaissance
description: Emphasizes major works of a number of the writers of the period in their historical and philosophical contexts. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: English Literature of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: An extensive study of English literature from 1600 to 1780 with attention to the social, historical, and philosophical backgrounds of the periods. A close reading of the works of major writers is emphasized, but not to the exclusion of the works of minor writers. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: English Literature: 1780 to the Present
description: British literature from 1780 to the present, with attention to the social, historical, and philosophical backgrounds. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Literature and the Narrative Media
description: A consideration of the ways in which the narrative media have been used to develop fictional and nonfictional literature. Special attention to works that have been adapted from one medium to another and to works of lasting significance. Attention will be given to the narrative media and the language arts curriculum in junior high/middle and secondary schools.

title: Practicum in Peer Tutoring
description: Offers strategies for working with grammar, mechanics, and the larger rhetorical elements, practice in peer evaluation, and a forum for discussing the role and responsibilities of peer tutors. Credit in this course does not apply to a major or minor in English. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to students assigned to tutor at the Writing Center.

title: The Teaching of Language Arts in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: Modern methods and materials for teaching written and oral expression, language use, spelling, handwriting, and literature. Cannot be counted as an elective in major or minor programs in English.

title: Literature for Young Children
description: An introduction to literature for young children. Designed for elementary and early childhood education programs and endorsements and for parents and future parents. Cannot be counted as an elective in major or minor programs in English.

title: English Linguistics
description: Modern English grammar, with emphasis on the application of the methods of uptodate descriptive linguistics to an understanding of basic grammatical terminology, relationships, and structure, including morphology (wordbuilding) and phonology (sound system).

title: The Development of the English Language
description: Introduction to the historical development of the English language with attention to changes in vocabulary, grammar, and sounds. Prerequisite: ENG 321. Prerequisite waived for departmental majors in English, option 2, and for departmental minors in English.

title: The English Language: Past and Present
description: An introduction to the history and structure of the English language: a survey of important historical changes in the structure of English; a scientific study of the structure of modern English; and a survey of the dialectal variations in modern English. Designed for elementary and junior high/middle school education programs and endorsements. Cannot be counted as an elective in other major or minor programs in English. Not open to the student who has credit in ENG 321 or 322.

title: Children's Literature
description: An overview of children's literature and an intensive study of various types. Designed for elementary education programs and endorsements. Cannot be counted as an elective in major or minor programs in English. Junior or senior standing recommended.

title: Linguistic Phonetics
description: Speech sounds and the linguistic methods employed in their description, classification, and analysis as elements in language systems.

title: American Literature, 1860-1960
description: A survey of selected American writers and the various literary movements since 1860, including selections from a broad range of major and minority traditions. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, or equivalent.

title: Nineteenth-Century American Fiction
description: Intensive reading in the works of two or three major writers of the period, such as Irving, Cooper, Hawthorne, Melville, Twain, and James.

title: Twentieth-Century American Fiction
description: Intensive reading in the works of three major writers of the period, such as Anderson, Faulkner, Fitzgerald, Hemingway, Steinbeck, Wolfe, and Dos Passos.

title: Twentieth-Century American Drama
description: The themes and techniques of selected American playwrights with pertinent critical and biographical information. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Twentieth-Century American Poetry
description: The themes and techniques of selected American poets with pertinent critical and biographical information. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Special Methods for Teaching Language Arts in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Concentrates on the selection and application of specialized materials and methods appropriate for teaching language arts in junior high/middle schools. Cannot be counted as an elective in other major or minor programs in English. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDJHM 312.

title: Literature of Black America
description: An investigation of the literature written by black authors in the United States. Authors to be studied will be determined by the instructor on the basis of literary merit.

title: American Indian Literature
description: A literary study of short stories, novels, and poetry by twentiethcentury American Indian authors, with supplementary background readings in mythology, tales, and poetry from the oral traditions. The emphasis will be on works by American Indians, but some works about Indians by white authors may also be included.

title: English Drama from Medieval Times to the Restoration
description: English drama from medieval times to 1700, excluding Shakespeare. Special attention is given to The Second Shepherds' Play and Everyman, and to the plays of Marlowe, Jonson, Dekker, Beaumont and Fletcher, Webster, Dryden, and Congreve.

title: The English Novel in the Eighteenth Century
description: Introduction to earliest English prose fiction and study of eighteenthcentury novels including the works of Defoe, Richardson, Fielding, Smollett, and Sterne. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: English Drama from the Restoration to the Present
description: English drama from 1700 to the present. Special attention is given to the plays of Steele, Goldsmith, Sheridan, Wilde, Shaw, Synge, O'Casey, Osborne, Beckett, and Pinter.

title: The English Novel in the Nineteenth Century
description: Nineteenthcentury novels including works by Austen, Dickens, Thackeray, Eliot, the Brontes, Meredith, and Hardy. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Studies in British Drama
description: Special topics in contemporary British drama. Prerequisite: open only to students at the London Centre.

title: Honors Colloquium in English
description: Exploration of selected issues in English, with emphasis upon individualized study and reporting. Open only to honors students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching English
description: Materials, methods, and resources used in teaching composition, language, and literature in the secondary school. Cannot be counted as an elective in major or minor programs in English. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: The Contemporary English Novel
description: Twentiethcentury novels, including works of Conrad, James, Joyce, Lawrence, Forster, and others. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Teaching the English Bible as Literature
description: Teaching resources and selections from the English Bible designed especially for students preparing to teach the Bible as literature in English classes in junior high, middle school, or senior high school. Prerequisite: ENG 205, 206, or the equivalent.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials
description: Englishoriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of English, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of English in the secondary school curriculum. Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Cannot be counted as an elective in major or minor programs in English. Prerequisite: ENG 395.

title: Special Topics in World Literature
description: Special research topics in world literature, with emphasis on selected writers as they reflect the social, scientific, philosophical, and religious attitudes of the age. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or the equivalent.

title: Special Topics in English Education
description: Emphasis on current issues and problems at the elementary, middle, junior high, or senior high school level. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or the equivalent.

title: Special Topics in American Literature
description: Special research topics in American literature, with emphasis on selected writers as they reflect the social, scientific, philosophical, and religious attitudes of the age. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or the equivalent.

title: Special Topics in British Literature
description: Special research topics in British literature, with emphasis on selected writers as they reflect the social, scientific, philosophical, and religious attitudes of the age. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or the equivalent.

title: Independent Study in English
description: Designed for the student who wishes to conduct independent study and research in English. Prerequisite: 36 hours of credit in English at the 200 level or above at Ball State University and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Creative Writing Workshop
description: The fundamentals of the short story, such as the use of language, image, and structure. Emphasis on the student's ability to write clearly and dramatically. Prerequisite: ENG 103.

title: Fiction Writing Workshop
description: Open to students who already have had some experience with the short story, the novel, or the play. Primary emphasis on instructor evaluation and class discussion of individual manuscripts. Prerequisite: ENG 405 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Poetry Writing Workshop
description: Practice, analysis, and criticism of the craft of poetry, with attention to prosody, traditional form, significant idea, the life of the poetic imagination, and the state of the art. Prerequisite: ENG 103 and 104.

title: Independent Study in English Education
description: Designed for the student who wishes to conduct independent study and research in English education, preschool through the secondary level. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Reading Printed Materials in the English Classroom
description: Provides an overview of the process of reading printed materials with practical suggestions for developing analytic skills for reading and interpreting written communications, including literary and popular materials used in the English classroom.

title: Literature for Adolescents
description: Recent literature suitable for students of varying ability in junior high/middle and secondary schools. Emphasis on the actual reading of selections with some attention given to methodology. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Old English
description: An introduction to Old English with readings in representative texts.

title: American Indian Folklore
description: Stories, tales, and rituals from American Indian oral traditions, selected to represent major themes, types, and culture areas.

title: American Folklore
description: Materials and techniques for presenting the American heritage of folklore and folk literature at the public school level. Books, films, filmstrips, recordings, and pictorial collections are among the materials studied.

title: Teaching English as a Foreign Language 1: Theory
description: The psychological and linguistic bases of language learning and recent theories concerning the application of linguistic science to methodology and materials in second language teaching. Prerequisite: knowledge of a foreign language. Prerequisite or parallel: ENG 321 or 420.

title: Methods and Materials in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description: Study and practice of a variety of methods in teaching English as a foreign language. Discussion of pedagogical issues in language teaching. Topics vary each quarter; consult the English department for schedule of offerings. Prerequisite: ENG 420 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Contrastive Analysis
description: Language universals and a comparison of the structural systems of language. Examines and compares languages to note the differing ways in which meaning can be expressed. Students may work on a general topic or on a comparison of two or more languages of their choice.

title: Emerson, Thoreau, Whitman
description: An intensive reading of the principal works of these authors and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of transcendentalism. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Poe, Hawthorne, Melville
description: An intensive reading of the principal works of these authors and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of romanticism. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Twain, James, Adams, Crane
description: An intensive reading of the principal works of these authors and a study of the philosophical and literary implications of the varieties of realism. Prerequisite: ENG 340.

title: American Literature, 1945 to Present
description: A survey of the works of major writers and literary trends in America since World War II. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Renaissance and Seventeenth-Century Studies
description: Nondramatic literature of the English Renaissance (1485-1660), exclusive of Shakespeare and Milton. Emphasizes such writers as Wyatt, Surrey, Spenser, Sidney, Donne, Herrick, Bacon, Jonson, and other appropriate figures.

title: Chaucer
description: A study of The Canterbury Tales, Troilus and Criseyde, and several of the minor poems. Emphasis on the structure, the sources, and the significance of the works included. Aspects of medieval culture pertinent to the works will be considered.

title: Shakespeare
description: An introductory study of representative plays (comedies, histories, tragedies) and some selections from the sonnets by Shakespeare.

title: Studies in Shakespeare
description: Special topics in a selection of Shakespeare's tragedies, comedies, and histories. Prerequisite: open only to students at the London Centre.

title: Studies in English Literature of the Restoration and Eighteenth Century
description: An extensive study of the nondramatic works of Dryden, Swift, Pope, and Johnson, with possible supplementary readings from other British authors of the period 1660-1800. Prerequisite: ENG 205 or 206.

title: Milton
description: Indepth, analytical study of Paradise Lost, Paradise Regained, Samson Agonistes, Lycidas, and Areopagitica, as well as a brief study of The Christian Doctrine and other selected poems and prose by John Milton.

title: Romantic Studies
description: The poetry and prose of Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Keats, and Shelley.

title: Victorian Studies
description: An intensive study of the works of Carlyle, Tennyson, Browning, Ruskin, and Arnold.

title: Women in Literature
description: Investigation of various ways women have been portrayed in the literature of the Western world.

title: Twentieth-Century British Studies
description: A study in depth of several significant twentiethcentury authors (such as Shaw, Conrad, Lawrence, Joyce, Woolf, Waugh, Durrell, Beckett, and Auden) and the intellectual and literary movements closely associated with them.

title: The Modern Continental Novel
description: Novels in translation over the last hundred years. Novels will be related to major historical, political, and intellectual currents.

title: Modern British Poetry
description: Important poets of Great Britain from World War I to the present, focusing on Yeats, Eliot, Auden, and Thomas, with additional attention given to Hopkins, Owen, Lawrence, Graves, Ted Hughes, and others. Department of Foreign Languages Gardiol, Chairperson; Barnette, Brown, Finney, Fritz, Gilman, Hightower, Johnson, Kadletz, Magrath, Moskalew, Shea, Sotiropoulos, Warner The Department of Foreign Languages is equipped to offer a varied program of excellent instruction in both ancient and modern foreign languages. Close cooperation with other departments on campus makes possible the combining of foreign language training with other disciplines. Classroom and library language laboratories provide for class instruction as well as selfinstruction. Opportunities exist for exchanges with schools in other countries, academic summer study abroad, and foreign language house residence with homelike accommodations and native speaking directors in French, German, and Spanish. Language proficiency tests make it possible to award credit based on previous language study and place students in classes at appropriate levels. The Department of Foreign Languages offers indepth training for languageoriented students: • those desiring to enrich their professional preparedness by acquiring a knowledge of a foreign language; • those desiring a broad liberal education; • preprofessional students in such areas as law, medicine, library science, and business; • graduate students who need reading competency in a foreign language to meet program requirements; • students seeking an elementary knowledge of less frequently taught languages; • students in the teaching program seeking permanent certification for teaching at the elementary and secondary levels; • students planning to acquire skills for further study at other graduate schools offering the Ph.D. in language; • those desiring to improve their abilities in English through the transfer value of classical and modern foreign languages; and • those desiring practical training in translation skills. Students who begin their study of a foreign language at Ball State University will start with the initial course in the 100-level sequence. Students with secondary school credit in a foreign language or other previous noncollege language training will be placed in appropriate courses through the placement examination administered by the Department of Foreign Languages. No placement credit is given for 101, but students placed in 103 or any higherlevel course may receive Ball State University credit for 102 and each higherlevel course thereafter by earning a grade of C or better in the course in which they are placed. Both undergraduate and graduate students should regularly consult with foreign language departmental advisers about sequencing of courses in accordance with individual needs. The 100-200-level courses in foreign languages are sequential and should be taken in order except in special cases. title: Introduction to the Classical World
description: Introduces the student to the main features of the Greek and Roman civilizations.

title: Word Origins and Vocabulary Development
description: Latin borrowings, Latin prefixes, roots, and suffixes in English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin is required. Open to all students.

title: Scientific Terminology, the Greek Element
description: Considers the composition of Greekbased words used by the physical, biological, medical, and technical sciences.

title: Scientific Terminology, the Latin Element
description: Considers the composition of Latinbased words used by the physical, biological, medical, and other technical sciences.

title: Roman Private and Public Life
description: Examines all phases of Roman customs referred to in Latin commonly read in secondary school. No reading knowledge of Latin required. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Mythology
description: Primarily a general education course, dealing with myths of the Greeks and Romans and their use in literature and art. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required.

title: The Old Testament as Literature
description: Considers the Old Testament as typical of, related to, and a source of some of the major literary genres, such as history and biography, prophetic literature, lyric poetry, dramatic literature, and short stories and tales.

title: Mythologies of the World
description: Classical mythology (Greek and Roman) will represent Western tradition in a comparative study with other mythologies of the world. Emphasizes mythologies as symbolic cultural systems expressing the values and concerns of societies. A total of 8 hours may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in any one quarter or term.

title: Women in Ancient Greece and Rome
description: Famous women in literature and history. Observes and traces the emergence of contemporary Western attitudes toward women; explores and evaluates the status and role of the Greco-Roman woman as determined by social, political, and legal institutions.

title: The Classical World in Film, Fiction, and Fact
description: A broad survey of life in the classical Mediterranean world through the media of motion pictures, fiction, and nonfiction (historical, archaeological, and anthropological studies).

title: Classical Literature in English Translation
description: Selected masterpieces of classical literature; historical development of the various types of literature as a background for further study in Latin and English. No reading knowledge of Greek and Latin required. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Cultural Life of Ancient Greece
description: Introduces the student to the cultural achievements of the ancient Greeks and their contributions to the modern world.

title: Cultural Life of Ancient Rome
description: Provides the student with a fundamental knowledge of the social, cultural, and economic framework within which the ancient Romans lived.

title: Reading Course
description: An arranged course in selected readings. Permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours may be earned.

title: Beginning Mandarin Chinese 1
description: Intensive training in elementary spoken Chinese through sentence patterns and simple conversation, using Hanyu pinyin for correct pronunciation and intonation. Emphasizes recognition and writing of about one hundred Chinese characters. Includes some study of cultural traditions, everyday customs, and rudimentary background information about China.

title: Beginning Mandarin Chinese 2
description: Intensive training in elementary spoken Chinese with emphasis on recognition and writing of about one hundred Chinese characters. Introduces elementary readings in Chinese, using graded readers. Continues study of cultural traditions, everyday customs, and rudimentary background information about China. Prerequisite: CH 101 or equivalent.

title: Beginning Mandarin Chinese 3
description: Intensive training in elementary spoken Chinese with emphasis on recognition and writing of about one hundred Chinese characters. Continues elementary readings using graded Chinese readers and introduces use of the Chinese dictionary. Continues study of cultural traditions, everyday customs, and rudimentary background information about China. Prerequisite: CH 102 or equivalent. 201.Intermediate Chinese 1. (4) Intermediate training designed to develop greater fluency in oral language, increase vocabulary, practice sentence patterns, and develop skills in reading both old and simplified forms of writing. Traditional and cultural aspects of the language will be presented. Prerequisite: CH 103 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Chinese 2
description: Designed to increase oral fluency on conventional topics, increase vocabulary and familiarity with sentence structures, introduce literature through simple modern essays, short stories, and newspaper articles, and develop the ability to write short compositions. Cultural traditions will be presented. Prerequisite: CH 201 or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Chinese 3
description: Designed to increase conversational skills and expand vocabulary. Students will be required to write short compositions in hanzi and to read newspapers and short stories by modern authors with the help of a dictionary. Traditional cultural aspects will be studied. Prerequisite: CH 202 or equivalent.

title: Beginning Guided Self-Instruction in Commonly Taught Foreign Languages
description: Guided selfinstruction in beginning French, German, Greek, Latin, or Spanish using audiovisual materials, texts, workbooks, tests, and tutors by arrangement. Designed to meet the needs of students who cannot otherwise study languages. Not open to native speakers. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: German Literature in English Translation
description: Primarily a general education course designed to expose the non-German reader to great German writers and thinkers. The course may not be applied toward areas in German.

title: Hispanic Literature in Translation
description: Primarily a general education course designed to expose the non-Spanish reader to the great writers of the Hispanic world. The course may not be applied toward areas in Spanish.

title: Intermediate Guided Self-Instruction in Commonly Taught Foreign Languages
description: Guided selfinstruction in intermediate French, German, Greek, Latin, or Spanish, using audiovisual materials, texts, workbooks, tests, and tutors by arrangement. Designed to meet the needs of students who cannot otherwise study these languages. Not open to native speakers. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foreign Literatures through Motion Pictures
description: Presentations of the literary matter of many nations through the medium of films. Ten films will be shown. Selected ones will be compared to the works of literature. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Historical Linguistics
description: An introduction to the scientific study of language for students in foreign language. An elementary survey of the methods used in historical and comparative linguistic analysis with application to language usually taught in college. Gives the language student some basic insights into the linguistic principles that underlie change in language.

title: Indochina: Traditions and Languages of Laos and Vietnam
description: A survey of the high traditions and values of the peoples of Indochina. World view through folklore, literature, arts, and language. Conducted in Lao and Vietnamese. Prerequisite: conversational knowledge of Lao or Vietnamese.

title: Guided Self-Instruction Studies in Less Commonly Taught Languages
description: Languages such as Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew (Modern), Greek (Modern), Russian, and Portuguese are offered at basic spoken levels by guided selfinstruction (GSI). Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned in one language and as many as 12 hours may be earned in any one quarter or term. Not open to the student who is a native speaker.

title: Special Methods for Teaching Foreign Language in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: Concentrates on the selection and applications of specialized materials and methods appropriate for teaching foreign language in junior high/middle schools. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDJHM 312.

title: Honors Colloquium in Foreign Literature
description: Selected readings and indepth exploration and discussion of literary currents, movements, authors, and themes found in foreign literature. Prerequisite: junior standing in the Honors College or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Foreign Language
description: Methods current in foreign language teaching in the senior high school. Directed observation of classes, specific problems of presentation, choice of texts, and organization of teaching materials and supplementary aids. Reviews the Report of the Foreign Language Study and courses of study recommended by the state Department of Education. Prerequisite: two years of college credit in French, German, Latin, or Spanish, or equivalent and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 299.

title: Classroom Utilization of Methods and Materials in Teaching Foreign Languages
description: Disciplineoriented classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in the teaching of foreign languages, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of foreign languages in the secondary school curriculum. Topics developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: FL 395.

title: Independent Study
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with individual instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foreign Language House Living and Learning
description: Offers students the option of earning a limited amount of credit for the language learning experience provided by the foreign language houses. A total of 3 hours of credit per language may be earned in any one house, but no more than 1 credit may be earned at one time. Offered on credit/nocredit basis only.

title: The Teaching of Foreign Language in the Elementary School
description: Development of foreign language instruction in the elementary school. Curricula, training of teachers, and teaching methods; also phonemics, pronunciation, and a review of other basic language elements.

title: Beginning French 1
description: The first course in the French language.

title: Beginning French 2
description: Prerequisite: FR 101.

title: Beginning French 3
description: Prerequisite: FR 102.

title: Intermediate French 1
description: Prerequisite: one year of college French.

title: Intermediate French 2
description: Prerequisite: 16 hours of college French.

title: Intermediate French 3
description: Prerequisite: twenty hours of college French.

title: Conversation 1
description: Prerequisite: two years of college French or the equivalent. Students wishing additional instruction should register for FR 404.

title: Composition 1
description: Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent. Students wishing additional instruction should register for FR 405.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the French language and the application of phonetics to the understanding and speaking of French. Use of the phonetic alphabet. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Business French
description: Designed to familiarize the advanced French student with commercial forms and terminology used in business, banking, and industry. Prerequisite: FR 203 or equivalent.

title: Civilization and Culture: The Old Regime
description: Contributions made by France from the beginnings to the French Revolution. Origins of historical and cultural traditions. Supplemental literary selections. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Civilization and Culture: Modern France
description: Development of modern France from the French Revolution to the present. Assimiliation of traditions into the culture of the industrial age. Supplemental literary selections. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Short Story
description: A study of the short story in French literature. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Classical Drama
description: The plays of Corneille, Racine, and Moliere. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: A study of French poetry with emphasis on the Symbolists and on contemporary poets. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Modern Novel
description: Extensive reading in the French novel. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in French drama. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Contemporary French Civilization
description: Presentday France and French institutions viewed in the context of French perception of the family, education, politics, the judicial system, the economy, and religion. Supplementary readings in current newspapers and periodicals. Lectures in English; readings in French and English. Prerequisite: FR 203 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Modern Reading
description: Contemporary prose and poetry. Prerequisite: two years of college French or the equivalent.

title: Literary Heritage of France
description: Selections from various periods of French literature, designed to develop an appreciation of the literary heritage of France. Prerequisite: two years of college French or the equivalent. Not open to the student who has credit in two of the following courses: FR 421, 422, and 423 or equivalent.

title: French Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced French language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where French is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in French or by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Conversation 2
description: A continuation of FR 304. Prerequisite: FR 304.

title: Composition 2
description: A continuation of FR 305. Prerequisite: FR 305.

title: History of French Literature 1
description: From the beginnings to 1760. Literature of the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, and the Classical Age to 1760. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 2
description: The classical age from 1760 and the eighteenth century. Literature of the golden age of classicism and the eighteenthcentury philosophies. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: History of French Literature 3
description: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The development of romanticism, realism, naturalism, and symbolism in French literature; literature of contemporary France. Prerequisite: two years of college French or equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisite: three years of college French or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Beginning German 1
description: The first course in the German language.

title: Beginning German 2
description: Prerequisite: GER 101.

title: Beginning German 3
description: Prerequisite : GER 102.

title: Intermediate German 1
description: Reading of representative German authors of moderate difficulty. Emphasizes vocabulary, increased knowledge of German idiom, and practice in writing German. Prerequisite: one year of college German.

title: Intermediate German 2
description: Prerequisite: 16 hours of college German.

title: Intermediate German 3
description: Extensive reading of German authors in class. Prerequisite: 20 hours of college German.

title: Business German
description: Introductory course specializing in German business language and topics. Emphasizes the use and understanding of German business expressions through specialized vocabulary. Focuses on German-American similarities and differences, current issues, and German business practices. Prerequisite: GER 103.

title: Conversation
description: To increase fluency in speaking and ease of comprehension through conversation. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or GER 504.

title: Composition
description: To familarize students with the fine points of German grammar and to train them to express themselves in the correct idiom. Prerequisite: two years of college German or the equivalent. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or GER 505.

title: Phonetics
description: Formation of speech sounds in the German language and the application of phonetics and phonemics in the understanding and speaking of German. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Contemporary German Culture
description: A variety of lectures, readings, and audiovisual materials introducing the student to presentday social mores of Germany. Discusses similarities and differences between American and German cultures.

title: Civilization and Culture
description: Civilization and cultural development of the Germans from ancient times to the present. Taught in German. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Poetry
description: Introduction to German lyric poetry and survey of historical development of this literary genre. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Modern Prose
description: Growth and significance of modern prose writing in Germany. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading in recent German drama. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Modern Masterpieces
description: Realism, naturalism, and recent German literary periods. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Goethe
description: Intensive study of the life and of one or more of the works of Johann Wolfgang Goethe. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: German Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced German language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where German is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in German or by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairperson.

title: History of German Literature 1
description: From its beginnings to 1750. A survey of German literary trends from the earliest times to the Classical period, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 2
description: From 1750 to 1850. A survey of classical and romantic German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: History of German Literature 3
description: From 1850 to the present. A survey of recent German literature, with illustrative readings from selected writers, such as Moerike, Keller, Storm, Stifter, Thomas Mann, Hermann Hesse, and others. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Romanticism
description: Philosophical and historical background of German romanticism, the development of romantic poetry and prose. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent.

title: Poetic Realism
description: Emphasis on major works representative of Poetic Realism in German literature, including works of Adalbert Stifter, Annette von Droste-Hulshoff, Gottfried Keller, C. F. Meyer, and Theodor Storm.

title: Practical Materials and Techniques
description: Presentation and development of materials of practical value in special interest areas. Various topics of current interest will be covered in miniworkshop situations. Prerequisite: two years of college German or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisite: three years of college German or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Beginning Greek 1
description: The first course in the Greek language.

title: Beginning Greek 2
description: Prerequisite: GRK 101.

title: Beginning Greek 3
description: Prerequisite: GRK 102.

title: Introduction to New Testament Greek 1
description: Beginning course in New Testament Greek. The alphabet, pronunciation, basic grammar, and vocabulary. Not open to the student who has credit in GRK 101, 102, 103.

title: Introduction to New Testament Greek 2
description: A review of grammar, vocabulary building, and development of reading skills in the Greek of the New Testament. Prerequisite: GRK 104. Not open to the student who has credit in GRK 101, 102, 103.

title: Intermediate Greek 1
description: Prerequisite: one year of college Greek or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek 2
description: Prerequisite: 16 hours of Greek or equivalent.

title: Intermediate Greek 3
description: Prerequisite: 20 hours of Greek or equivalent.

title: Advanced Greek 1
description: Prerequisite: two years of college Greek or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Greek 2

title: Advanced Greek 3
description: Prerequisite: two years of college Greek or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Beginning Italian 1
description: The first course in the Italian language.

title: Beginning Italian 2
description: Prerequisite: ITAL 101.

title: Beginning Italian 3
description: Prerequisite: ITAL 102 or equivalent.

title: Beginning Latin 1
description: The first course in the Latin language. Elements of Latin pronunciation, alphabet, rules of accent, syllabification, basic Latin grammar with oral and written exercises, reading of easy short selections from Latin authors, exercises in English derivatives, and consideration of the close connection of Latin and English vocabularies.

title: Beginning Latin 2
description: Continued emphasis on pronunciation, accent, and syllabification. Oral and written exercises of greater difficulty, reading of short selections from various Latin authors, exercises in dictation, practice in comprehension with emphasis on speech patterns and continuation of grammatical principles. Prerequisite: LAT 101.

title: Beginning Latin 3
description: Completion of presentation of the mechanics of Latin grammar. Stress on Latin syntax; logical structure in thought patterns. Emphasis on grammar through oral and written exercises. Readings of Cicero, Pliny's letters, Horace, Catullus, and Vergil. Longer reading selections with emphasis on history of civilization. Prerequisite: LAT 102.

title: Intermediate Latin 1
description: Rapid review of Latin grammar with oral and written exercises. Reading of selections from Caesar, Cicero, Pliny, Livy, Seneca, Vitruvius, and others to express literary ideas drawn from representative works. Emphasis on vocabulary, Latin idiom, and practice in writing Latin. Prerequisite: one year of college Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin 2
description: Emphasis on rapid reading for comprehension. Selected passages from Celsus, De Medicina; Horace, Ars Poetica; Vitruvius, De Aqueductis; Pliny's Natural History; Cicero's De Officiis, De Republica, Epistulae, De Finibus, or Pro Archia; Juvenal, Satires; Pliny's letters (concerning the Christians), Terence's and Plautus's plays; and others. Prerequisite: 16 hours of college Latin.

title: Intermediate Latin 3
description: Extensive reading of Roman comedies in class. Stress on rapid reading of Latin, particularly of the dramatists, Plautus and Terence. Introduction to colloquial Latin and everyday idiomatic language. Development of plot, characterization, artistic unity, and production of Roman comedies. Comparison of Greek and Roman comedy. Prerequisite: 20 hours of college Latin.

title: Prose Composition
description: For advanced students who are preparing to teach Latin. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned in this course and/or LAT 505.

title: Suetonius: Lives of the Caesars
description: Reading with special reference to life and times of Suetonius.

title: Horace: Odes
description: Selections from the Odes, with emphasis on metrical forms, grammatical construction, and mythology.

title: The Latin Elegiac Poets
description: The elegies of Catullus, Tibullus, Propertius, and Ovid.

title: Ovid: The Metamorphoses
description: Selected readings from The Metamorphoses of Ovid, with special reference to the life and times of Ovid, and the poetic traditions of Classical Latin. Prerequisite: two years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Livy: History
description: Selected readings from Livy's Ab Urbe Condita, with a study of Livy's historical concept and contrast with the other great Roman historians. Prerequisite: two years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Roman Comedy
description: Selected plays of Plautus and Terence with attention to influence on French and English literature.

title: Survey of Latin Literature
description: A comprehensive study of Latin literature through the reading of selections from Livius Andronicus to the church fathers. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Lucretius: De Rerum Natura
description: Selected readings from Lucretius's De Rerum Natura, with collateral studies in development in philosophic attitudes in classical times. Prerequisite: two years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books I-VI
description: Readings from Books I-VI of the Aeneid of Vergil, with collateral studies in epic genre and the relationship to Homeric epic. Prerequisite: three years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Vergil: Aeneid, Books VII-XII
description: The last six books of the Aeneid, with collateral reading and reports.

title: Cicero: The Philosophic Works
description: Readings from such selected philosophic works of Cicero as De Anima, De Senectute, and De Republica, with a related study of philosophical attitudes in classical times. Prerequisite: three years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Cicero: Selected Letters
description: Introduction to Roman epistolary style. Comparison with Pliny.

title: Caesar: The Civil War
description: Comparison with the Gallic wars.

title: Martial: Epigrams
description: Introduction to poetry of the Silver Age with emphasis on the epigram.

title: Juvenal: The Satires
description: Selected satires of Juvenal; study of Roman satire and its influence.

title: Medieval Latin Literature
description: Selected readings from the outstanding Latin authors of the Middle Ages, including Boethius, Cassiodorus, Walter Map, Ekkehart, and Hrotswitha. Prerequisite: three years of college Latin or equivalent.

title: Reading Course
description: Prerequisite: three years of college Latin or equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Phonetics
description: The formation of speech sounds in Spanish and the application of phonetics and phonemics to the understanding, speaking, and teaching of Spanish. Prerequisite : two years of colege Spanish or equivalent, permision of the department chairperson.

title: Business Spanish
description: Commercial forms and terminology used in business, banking, and industry. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or equivalent.

title: Spanish Civilization and Culture
description: An examination of Spanish history and culture through lectures, outside readings, and discussion. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or equivalent.

title: Short Story
description: Selected short stories in Spanish literature. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or equivalent.

title: Novel

description: A panoramic view of the culture and customs of the various Latin-American countries. Prerequisite: two years of college Spanish or equivalent.

title: Spanish for Medical Personnel
description: Spanish as needed by doctors, nurses, and others in the medical professions who deal with Hispanic persons. Previous knowledge of Spanish is not needed.

title: Spanish Study Abroad
description: Study of intermediate or advanced Spanish language, literature, and culture in a foreign country where Spanish is the native language. May include seminars arranged during travel. Travel may be by air. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Open to students with areas in Spanish or by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Spanish Literature
description: Advanced seminar studies by author, genre, period, or theme; topic to be announced. A total of 20 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 8 hours in one quarter or term.

title: Seminar in Latin American Literature
description: Advanced seminar studies by author, genre, period, or theme; topic to be announced. A total of 20 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 8 hours in one quarter or term.

title: Seminar in Spanish Language
description: Advanced seminar studies in composition, conversation, grammar, linguistics, or translation; topic to be announced. A total of 20 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 8 hours in one quarter or term.

Department of Geography Showalter, Chairperson; Grimes, Lyon, Martinson, Schoen, Slack, Sullivan, Wheeler Geography is an integrative discipline that focuses on the interrelationships of man and the environment. Although the undergraduate program is comprehensive and requires students to demonstrate competencies in both physical and social geography, the department encourages students to specialize during their last two years of study. The department has four major areas of specialization: (1) earth science, (2) urban/economic studies, (3) geographic data analysis, (4) international studies, and (5) traveltourism. The earth science program meets the needs of two kinds of students: those seeking certification to teach earth sciences in the elementary and secondary schools, and those seeking entrylevel positions in applied geography in industry or government. For students interested in the meteorological sciences and weather forecasting, the department offers 20 hours of course work. The urban/economic program gives students background and experiences that train them to assume positions as city and regional planners and marketing and site location analysts. The department maintains working relationships with various other departments and encourages urban/economic geographers to minor in planning or business. One of the fastest growth areas in geography is geographic data analysis. The department currently offers 24 hours of course work covering cartography, remote sensing, and statistical analyses. Never has it been more true that our world is growing smaller and we are all more and more dependent on other peoples and places. Geography responds to the need for students trained with a broad background of Third World regions, peoples, and places. The department specializes in Latin America, Asia, and Africa. The department is the international home office of the Conference of Latin Americanist Geographers. An international focus provides an excellent minor for many professional and general studies programs. Travel and tourism is the second largest business in the world. title: Earth, Sea, and Sky: A Geographic View
description: Selected aspects of the physical environment and their relationship to human occupancy of the earth. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Geographic Landscapes: Northwestern United States and Southwestern Canada
description: Physical, cultural, and economic geography along specified highways and byways of the region. Surface physical features, the people, and the economic activities that provide for continued human occupancy; a roadside geography.

title: Geographic Landscapes: Southwestern United States
description: Physical, cultural, and economic geography along specified highways and byways of the region. Surface physical features, the people, and the economic activities that provide for continued human occupancy; a roadside geography.

title: Global Geography for Teachers
description: Introduction to the regional concept and regional method as related to elementary teaching. Geographic survey of the world. Selected topics and regions given detailed analysis. Prerequisite: major in elementary education or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Elements of Physical Geography
description: Physical systems of the geographic environment, including selected topics in weather and climate, water resources, landforms, vegetation, and soil. Not open to the student who has credit in GEOG 101.

title: Physical Geography and Earth Science Concepts for Teachers
description: Earthsun relationships, weather and climate, geologic processes (including earth structure and sculpturing of the earth's surface); conservation principles as they pertain directly to the material taught. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs. Not open to the student who has credit in GEOG 110.

title: Economic Geography and Contemporary Issues
description: A systematic approach to economic geography and current economic issues, emphasizing local, regional, national, and international economic developments in the geographic setting.

title: Geography of the Cultural Environment
description: A spatial analysis of the interaction of cultural development and the physical environment. Special emphasis upon the processes of cultural change and their impact on the landscape.

title: Global Geography
description: An analysis of geographic patterns in selected world regions.

title: Honors Seminar in Selected Studies in Geography
description: Smallgroup discussion of geographic studies selected by the instructional staff. Studies vary according to staff assignment. Open only to Honors College students.

title: The American Landscape: A Historical Geography of the United States
description: Geography of American landscape in earlier times. Selected regions examined to understand geographical influences on transformation of the wilderness. Emphasis placed on exploration, discovery, migration routes, settlement, adjustments to the land, and means of securing a livelihood.

title: Geography of the Developed World
description: Geographical conditions that affect socialeconomic development within the technically advanced societies. Primary focus given to Western Europe, North America, Japan, the Soviet Union, and Eastern Europe.

title: Geography of the Developing World
description: Spatial issues of development, particularly the distribution of resources, population, and agriculture, as they relate to solving development problems. Emphasis on Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

title: Land Use
description: Distribution of rural and urban activities and resulting landscape patterns. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Weather 1
description: How and why the weather changes, the characteristics of weather, and an examination of weather instruments.

title: Map Reading and Interpretation
description: Introduction to skills needed to use and appreciate maps as a form of communication and as a research tool. Topics include elements and sources of maps, history of mapmaking, techniques of analysis, and introduction to aerial photography and remote sensing.

title: Map Reading for Teachers
description: An introduction to the reading and interpretation of maps, especially as maps may be used in working with school children. The use of topographic maps, special purpose maps, dot distrubution maps, bar graphs, pie charts. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs. Not open to the student who has credit in GEOG 240.

title: Indiana: Crossroads of America
description: A geographic examination of the physical, cultural, and economic diversity of the state. Field experiences supplement classroom activities.

title: Geography of Travel and Tourism
description: Introduction to travel and tourism, including study of their geographic, economic, cultural, and social dimensions. Topics include basic principles of travel and tourism; industry organization; how, where, and why people travel; spatial aspects.

title: Geography of Soils and Vegetation
description: World patterns of soils and vegetation, with emphasis on regional differences and relationships to climate and physiography; their significance in man's use of the land. Prerequisite: GEOG 101, 110, GEOL 101, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Urban Geography
description: Distribution, classification, structure, and function of urban centers. Special attention given to the geographic factors affecting urban development and growth.

title: The Structure and Functions of Cities
description: A critical examination of the major structural and institutional parts of the city and of how topographic and climatic forces have influenced their development. An understanding of the city as a functionally interdependent structure and as a physical monument to its contemporary culture is fostered.

title: The Urban and Regional Form
description: A survey of the origins of the urban and regional form and its relation to economic, social, and functional needs with special emphasis on the modern American metropolis and its region. Prerequisite: GEOG 322 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Agricultural and Rural Geography
description: Analysis of the distribution of agricultural systems in different regions of the world with emphasis on the interrelationships among agriculture and other forms of land use.

title: Weather 2
description: Introduction to weather forecasting using applied examples. Students may gain practical experience by working in the university weather station. Prerequisite: GEOG 230 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Climate
description: Introduction to climate, with emphasis on regional distribution. How and why climates differ across the earth. Prerequisite: GEOG 230, its equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Cartography and Graphics 1
description: The construction and design of maps and graphs. Basic drafting techniques and methods of cartographic presentation. Although the emphasis is on graphic presentation of spatially disposed quantitative and qualitative data, the techniques and methods apply to a wide range of subjects.

title: Cartography and Graphics 2
description: Additional instruction and practice in the application of mapping and graphics techniques. Specific projects are selected within the students' fields of specialization or interest. Emphasis on data collection, compilation, and final drafting of projects suitable for reproduction and publication. Prerequisite: GEOG 340.

title: Remote Sensing and Aerial Photo Interpretation 1
description: Introduction to remote sensing techniques including aerial photo interpretation and aircraft and satellite sensors such as radar and multispectral scanners as applied to studies in the physical and social sciences.

title: Remote Sensing and Aerial Photo Interpretation 2
description: Additional instruction and practice in the use of remote sensing techniques, including manual and computer analysis of aircraftand satelliteobtained data as applied to studies in the physical and social sciences. Prerequisite: GEOG 342 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Geography of the United States and Canada
description: Comprehensive survey of geographic regions, settlement, land use, natural resources, and potentialities of the United States and Canada.

title: Geography of Latin America and the Caribbean
description: Physical and cultural patterns in a diverse world region. Emphasis on population and settlement, agriculture, and environmental hazards in the context of development.

title: Geography of Africa
description: A survey and analysis of the physical and cultural environment of Africa.

title: Geography of Asia
description: The geography of South, Southwest, Southeast, and East Asia. A survey and analysis of the physical geographic patterns, bases of cultural diversity, and changing spatial aspects of political organization.

title: Geography of Europe
description: The physical and cultural environment of Europe with emphasis on the economic and political conditions involved.

title: Geography of the Soviet Union
description: A survey and analysis of the physical and cultural features of the Soviet Union and the economic development of the country.

title: Domestic Travel and Tourism
description: Examination of the technical aspects of domestic travel and tourism. Develops skills for using professionally prepared materials related to travel planning, regulations, tariffs, services, and ticketing. Prerequisite: GEOG 260. Open to majors only.

title: International Travel and Tourism
description: Examination of the technical aspects of international travel and tourism. Develops skills for using professionally prepared materials related to travel planning, regulations, tariffs, services, and ticketing. Prerequisite: GEOG 260. Open to majors only.

title: Geography of Transportation
description: Geographic considerations of the major modes of transportation of the world, and of transportation patterns.

title: Population Geography
description: A systematic and regional analysis of areal patterns of population distribution, composition, migration, and growth, as well as their causes and the effects they produce on the cultural landscape.

title: Geography of Industrial Location
description: An analysis of the geography of industrial location with particular emphasis given to the effect of industrial location on urban and regional economies.

title: Advanced Studies in Weather
description: Studies in selected topics of atmospheric processes and weather. Prerequisite: GEOG 330, one year of college physics and mathematics through calculus, or permission of the department chairperson. Regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Climate and the Human Environment
description: The practical relationships of climate to the activities of people, especially in the cultural adjustment to the physical environment. Prerequisite: GEOG 110, 230, 331 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Weather Instruments
description: A comprehensive study of meteorological instruments used in weather station operation. Students actively participate in practical weather station operation. Regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: GEOG 230 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Regional Geography
description: Advanced study of the geography of a selected region or regions of the world. Prerequisite: an introductory regional geography course or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Automation and the Travel Industry
description: Introduction to the use of automation in the travel industry as it applies to information management and task functions, such as reservation and ticketing systems. Includes laboratory experience. Prerequisite: GEOG 360, 361. Open to majors only.

title: Internship in Travel and Tourism
description: Fullor parttime work with a travel agency, airline, governmental organization, tour operator, or other branch of the industry for practical Geology 243 experience. Assignments depend upon the student's interest and convenience of the sponsor. Prerequisite: GEOG 460. Open to majors only.

title: World Political Geography
description: Analysis of the contribution of physical and cultural characteristics of the nations of the world to domestic and foreign relations problems.

title: Distant Areas Field Studies
description: Physical, economic, and cultural geography in areas distant from the campus. Open to students in geography, earth science, and allied subjects. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 16 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Readings and Special Studies in Geography and Earth Science
description: Assigned special studies in geography and earth science, including readings, research projects, teaching problems, or assignment to an undergraduate class. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 hours may be earned in any one quarter or term.

title: Research Techniques
description: Basic library research and writing techniques applied to problems in the physical and social sciences. Designed to increase competence in preparing research papers using library materials.

title: Quantitative Techniques
description: Application of quantitative techniques to problems in the physical and social sciences. Special emphasis on the application of these techniques in research.

title: History and Philosophy of Geography
description: The development of geographic knowledge and the status of the profession as expressed in the writings of the past and present by geographers and people in related fields.

title: Geographic Field Methods
description: Introduction to the techniques of field study and analysis of physical and cultural spatial patterns. Department of Geology Orr, Chairperson; Roepke, Samuelson, Sans, Snow Geologists study the earth with primary attention to its history, materials, processes, and structure. Today geologists are concerned also with the study of the moon, the study of geologic hazards and other environmental problems, and discovery of new mineral and petroleum deposits. The departmental major in geology within the Professional Arts Curriculum is designed to prepare geologists for immediate employment in industry and government agencies and for graduate studies leading to research and teaching positions in industry, government, and universities. The departmental major in geology within the Liberal Arts Curriculum is designed to broaden the intellectual horizons of students who do not wish to enter the profession. Geology specialties within the department include geomorphology, geophysics, mineralogy, petrography/petrology, paleontology, geotectonics, oceanography, and stratigraphy. Students should contact the departmental advisers immediately upon electing to major or minor in geology. Thereafter, it is important to maintain contact with the advisers before completing registration with the university curricular advisers. Departmental advisers help students to develop curricular options and select appropriate elective courses toward career objectives. The Department of Geology also prepares students for entrance to colleges or universities that offer degrees in oceanographic studies. A student who wants to pursue this field toward an undergraduate degree should consult the departmental adviser as soon as possible upon entering Ball State University. Those who plan to continue oceanography at the graduate level elsewhere should seek this advice no later than the first quarter of the sophomore year. Acceptance into graduate work in oceanography will require a bachelor's degree in one of the sciences or mathematics and will generally include 4 hours of introductory oceanography, 28 hours of mathematics including analytical geometry and calculus, 12 to 14 hours of general physics, and 15 to 16 hours of general chemistry. Students interested in physical and geological oceanography should consult the adviser in the Department of Geology. Those interested in biological oceanography should consult the adviser in the Department of Biology.
