title: Weaving 1
description: Basic instruction in loom weaving with an emphasis on tapestry technique and color experimentation. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Weaving 2
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and the application of these techniques to a project. Also includes techniques in handdyeing of yarns. Specific techniques covered in a given semester will vary. Prerequisite: ACR 201.

title: Ceramics 1
description: Basic handbuilding techniques: wedging, slab, coiling, and pinch methods. Glazes, slips, bisquing, and firing will be part of the studio experience. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 1
description: Beginning throwing; use of the potter's wheel to develop skills in throwing. A continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Metal Design 1
description: Introduction to jewelry and object making using metal. Emphasis on design and techniques of sawing, soldering, forming, and finishing as well as other basic processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Metal Design 2
description: Introduction to metalsmithing with a strong emphasis on design. Basic techniques of hammering and forming metal with introduction to decorative processes used in metal. Prerequisite: ACR 221 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Weaving 3
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and application of these techniques to a project. Techniques introduced will vary from semester to semester. Further exploration of the color possibilities of handdyed yarns. The level of competency will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 202.

title: Weaving 4
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and application of these techniques to a project. Techniques introduced will vary from semester to semester. Further exploration of the color possibilities of handdyed yarns. The level of competency will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 303.

title: Ceramics: Hand 1
description: Continued study of handbuilding methods as well as form, idea, and glazing techniques. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 2
description: Use of the potter's wheel to develop production form; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 212.

title: Ceramics: Hand 2
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques to develop an integration of form, glaze, and idea. Individual problems will be set up according to the student's needs. Prerequisite: ACR 313.

title: Technical Problems
description: Technical study of at least one of the following: clays, glazes, and kiln building techniques. Problem will be set up on an individual basis according to the student's needs. Prerequisite: ACR 212 and 313.

title: Metal Design 3
description: Further study in the techniques used in the art of metalsmithing and jewelry design. Includes casting, enameling, and other processes with strong emphasis on design and research. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ACR 222.

title: Metal Design 4
description: Further study in the techniques used in the art of metalsmithing and jewelry design. Includes casting, enameling, and other processes. Prerequisite: ACR 323 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Weaving 5
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The students will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 304.

title: Weaving 6
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 405.

title: Weaving 7
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 406.

title: Senior Project in Weaving 1
description: Concentrated work in a particular individual direction in fibers under the supervision of an instructor; content, amount, and extent of work will be determined by mutual agreement of the student and the instructor. Prerequisite: completion of course work in major.

title: Senior Project in Weaving 2
description: Further work on an individual direction in a body of work. The guidelines for the amount and direction of the work will have been determined when the student enrolls in ACR 408. Course content includes the mounting of a senior exhibition. Prerequisite: ACR 408.

title: Independent Study in Crafts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 3
description: An indepth exploration of forming vertically and horizontally on the wheel; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 314.

title: Ceramics: Hand 3
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques, form, and idea based on individual student's needs. Prerequisite: ACR 315.

title: Senior Project in Ceramics
description: Synthesis and culmination of studio experiences in the major content area, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. In addition there must be documentation through slidesportfolio, résumé, and thesis. Prerequisite: completion of total course work.

title: Metal Design 5
description: Individual exploration of techniques of metalsmithing and jewelry design. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Prerequisite: ACR 324.

title: Metal Design 6
description: Individual exploration of techniques of metalsmithing and jewelry design. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Prerequisite: ACR 324.

title: Metal Design 7
description: Individual exploration of techniques of metalsmithing and jewelry design. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study that will best suit the student's needs and interests. Prerequisite: ACR 324.

title: Senior Project in Metals
description: Synthesis of student's experience in metals culminating in an exhibition of work. Course should be taken during student's final semester of undergraduate courses.

title: Seminar in Crafts
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in various concepts, media, and techniques as related to the crafts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of art courses and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foundations 1
description: Exploration of basic art principles, elements, and concepts with emphasis on spatial organization of the twodimensional plane. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on craftsmanship. Parallel recommended: AFA 101.

title: Foundations 2
description: Continued exploration and application of basic art principles and elements to organize threedimensional space. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on craftsmanship. Prerequisite: ADS 101. Parallel recommended: AFA 202.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: Basic visual investigations of line, shape, and color. Emphasis on specific communication problems for the student to resolve. Introduces the fundamental craft considerations and the tools of the graphic designer. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Interior Design Graphics 1
description: Fundamental instruction in drawing basic geometrical designs and orthographic projections. Emphasis upon skill building and media manipulation. Prerequisite: AFA 202.

title: Interior Design Graphics 2
description: Exploration of the principles of visual communication applied to interior/environmental design. Emphasis on conceptual drawing and the selection of appropriate visual technique for presentation. Prerequisite: ADS 205.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Graphic interpretation of objects through various media and techniques. Exploration of design potential and its application. Prerequisite: ADS 201.

title: Three -Dimensional Spatial Design
description: Advanced problems in threedimensional design. Emphasis on problem recognition and the development of a threedimensional vocabulary. Exploration in geometry and space. Prerequisite: ADS 206.

title: Photography 1
description: Introduction to photography as an expressive art form with emphasis on the development of photographic vision as well as technical proficiency. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 101 for art majors; for others, permission of department chairperson.

title: Graphic Design 3
description: Advanced studies in graphic design involving the combination of photographic, typographic, and handdrawn elements in a sequential communication problem. Involves applied professional problems and focuses on the photomechanical (graphic arts) processes of designing images for offset lithography. Prerequisite: ADS 212.

title: Typography
description: Advanced typography problems dealing with text and display type as well as supportive visual imagery and information, such as the development of a brochure or folder design involving sequence consideration. Includes study of grids, charts and graphs, and visual imagery such as photography or drawing. Prerequisite: ADS 304.

title: Environmental Design Programming
description: Studio exploration of interiorspace design with analysis of human activity for the threedimensional design of simple spaces. Prerequisite: ADS 206, 223; ARCH 218.

title: Interior Environments 1
description: Interiorspace problem research stressing the interaction of users, color, texture, and environments. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Photography 2
description: Emphasis on the further exploration of photographic vision, technical concerns, aesthetic aspects of photography, and further study of photo history; introduction to advertising photography. Prerequisite: ADS 102 and 231 for art majors; for others, ADS 231 and permission of department chairperson.

title: Color Photography
description: Focuses on ideas and assigned problems expressed through color photography. Students should have a basic knowledge of processing color film and color prints. Prerequisite: ADS 332 and ITGRA 387 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Commercial Photography
description: Investigates commercial applications of photographic medium with historical perspective. Weekly problems assigned with emphasis on practical application of photography to advertising. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Large Format Photography
description: Students become familiar with cameras larger than 35mm for personal expression and illustration. Emphasis will be on the 4" x 5" camera and its individual strengths and weaknesses. Students need not have large format camera but will find it helpful. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Graphic Design 4
description: Advanced design problems exploring concepts in threedimensional presentation, sequential presentation, or object design. Prerequisite: ADS 311.

title: Graphic Design 5
description: Seminar covering the following topics and how they relate to the graphic designer: contracts for the designer, copyright law, résumé development, portfolio development, and presentation skills. Examines the history of graphic design and current trends in the profession. Prerequisite: ADS 412.

title: Independent Study in Design
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Interior Environments 2
description: Design analysis and synthesis of complex interior spaces. Consideration of human activity as the determinant of the design solution.

title: Photography 3
description: Major emphasis on students' personal statements in color and blackandwhite photography through selection of their own projects under the guidance of an instructor. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332 for art majors: for others, permission of department chairperson.

title: Photography 4
description: A further intensification of students' personal statements. Students given occasional assignments to introduce new and varied directions in art. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 433.

title: Cinematography as an Art Form
description: Explores the use of video and super-8 media as sources of creative exploration with concerns for artistic expression, content, form, and technique. Covers a brief survey of film history. Prerequisite: ADS 332 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Professional Practices/Portfolio Organization
description: The mechanics of a professional design practice and the function of a portfolio with emphasis on its content and format.

title: Concept 20 Design Studio
description: A practicum studio designed to provide students with opportunities to deal with clients on design and advertising projects. Intended to give students experience that will enhance their marketability upon graduation. Requires portfolio review. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Senior Design Thesis
description: Intensive study with research and resolution of a current problem in graphic or interior design. Students arrange theses with faculty advisers during the fall semester of their senior year. Open only to seniors in graphic or interior design. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in one semester.

title: Seminar in Design
description: Group or individual investigation and experiences in the fine arts beyond the scope of regular course work. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Studio Fundamentals
description: Introduction to the basic studio processes of drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. Lecture and studio experiences related to the understanding of the elements and principles of art and the methods of art criticism. Not open to art majors.

title: Introduction to Art Education
description: Introduction to art education as a teaching profession. Emphasis given to investigating artistic growth of normal and special populations and the materials, techniques, tools, art concepts, and strategies appropriate for teaching art to these students. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint the student with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Stresses the developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques. Prerequisite: AED 100. Open only to nonart majors.

title: Art Curriculum and Instruction
description: Designed to develop the art student's ability to make artcurricular judgments by developing artcurriculum plans and designing art experiences. Prerequisite: AED 201, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Art Teaching and Learning Practicurn
description: Direct experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating teaching strategies. Includes observation of students participating in an artrelated environment. Laboratory teaching time is arranged. Prerequisite: AED 304 for majors; permission of department chairperson for minors.

title: Classroom Use of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary public school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 305 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum for majors; permission of department chairperson for minors. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Art Education
description: Permits the professionally oriented art student to select and explore more intensively an area of art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Seminar in Art Education
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in the various ideas, methods, and research in the field of art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to drawing: the application of basic principles and elements of art as they relate to drawing concepts. Emphasis will be on the development of perceptual awareness and familiarity with a broad range of media and techniques. Parallel recommended: ADS 101.

title: Drawing 2
description: A continuation of concepts and perceptions from Drawing 1 with emphasis on the human figure. Prerequisite: AFA 101. Parallel recommended: ADS 102.

title: Painting 1
description: Introduction to painting: study of basic considerations of image making with oil paint. Focuses on media, techniques, design elements, and concepts. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Painting 2
description: Explorations in painting designed to build on initial experiences by studio practice and through slidelectures on contemporary painting. Prerequisite: AFA 202 and

title: Watercolor 1
description: Exploration of materials and techniques of transparent watercolor as they apply toward the solution of painting problems. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Watercolor 2
description: Continued exploration of painting problems in watercolor with emphasis on the unique character of the medium. Prerequisite: AFA 217.

title: Sculpture 1
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of clay portraiture, relief sculpture, armature and plaster construction, mold making, and wood finishing. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 101.

title: Wood and Stone Carving
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of stone and wood carving, including the use of both power and hand tools; appropriate application of form to material; lamination; and critical analysis.

title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Beginning printmaking techniques with an emphasis on intaglio and relief processes. Prerequisite: ADS 101; AFA 101.

title: Relief Printmaking
description: Fundamental procedures of relief printing from the woodblock and other surfaces with emphasis on the use of color and new approaches. Students are expected to develop images that have a relationship to this print medium. Prerequisite: AFA

title: Intaglio Printmaking 1
description: Intermediatelevel printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques. Emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Drawing 3
description: Life drawing. An intensive study of the human figure, continuing the exploration of various drawing techniques and media. Prerequisite: AFA 202.

title: Drawing 4
description: Drawing experiences exploring varied materials and concepts related to drawing as a personal visual statement. Prerequisite: AFA 303.

title: Painting 3
description: Individualized instruction aimed at the continued mastery of technical skills and progress toward the solution of pictorial problems. Prerequisite: AFA 212.

title: Painting 4
description: Continued interest in the development of technical skills and the solution of pictorial problems with new emphasis on individual creative solutions. Prerequisite: AFA 313.

title: Painting 5
description: Emphasis on advancing from technical proficiency toward the development of individual conceptual goals relating to painting. Prerequisite: AFA 314.

title: Plastic Construction
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of plastic construction to include mold making, resin casting, pigmentation, and sheet forming. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Metal Welding and Forging
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, equipment, safety precautions, and concepts of forged and welded sculpture. Students develop an understanding of both ferrous and nonferrous metals. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 2
description: Advanced printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques including line etching, drypoint, engraving, softground, and aquatint. Openended problem solving and indepth study with emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 243.

title: Lithography 1
description: Fundamental processes of drawing and printing lithographs using stones and aluminum plates. Drawing and painting techniques are used to develop images. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Lithography 2
description: Further development and investigation of the processes of lithography, including color. Exploration of stone and metal plate techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 351.

title: Lithography 3
description: Investigation of additional drawing and painting techniques as they relate to lithography. Further development of printing skills and the lithographic image. Prerequisite: AFA 352. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Serigraphy 1
description: Introductory printmaking dealing with the processes of serigraphy, including the four basic stencil techniques and their variation. Silkscreen as a fine art form. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Drawing 5
description: Continuation of the drawing experience for advanced students developing further expertise in drawing skills while encouraging research into and experimentation with more personal imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 304.

title: Drawing 6
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 405. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Independent Study in Fine Arts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Painting 6
description: Individualized instruction, continuing the emphasis on student identification and development of personal concepts in painting. Prerequisite: AFA 315.

title: Metal Founding
description: Fundamental principles, techniques, skills, and concepts of metal founding with both aluminum and bronze to include green sand, ceramic shell, and traditional lostwax investment. Prerequisite: AFA 221 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Advanced Problems in Sculpture
description: Designed for students who wish to extend their technical understanding and aesthetic development beyond the fundamental level. Prerequisite: AFA 425 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Exploration of Sculptural Alternatives
description: Designed for students to develop an awareness of current sculptural trends and to experiment with nontraditional sculptural materials. Prerequisite: AFA 425 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 3
description: Advanced printmaking emphasizing aesthetic decision making involving the intaglio process through the knowledge of technique and use of personal artistic choices. Prerequisite: AFA 344. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Senior Project in Drawing
description: Synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in drawing, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 21 studio hours beyond the art core, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Painting
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in painting, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 18 credit hours in painting, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Sculpture
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in sculpture, with an exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 21 credit hours in sculpture, sponsorship by a sculpture faculty member, and permission of department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Printmaking
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experience in printmaking, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort at the undergraduate level. Prerequisite: 21 credit hours in printmaking, sponsorship by a printmaking faculty member, and permission of department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Fine Arts
description: Individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of department chairperson.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: An introduction to the elements of style within the fine arts and a survey of painting, sculpture, and architecture from the prehistoric through the Gothic eras.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: A continuation of the study of the elements of style within the fine arts and a survey of painting, sculpture, and architecture from the late Gothic to the present. Prerequisite: AHS 101.

title: Art: An Introduction
description: A general studies course providing introduction to understanding and appreciation of painting, sculpture, and architecture. Stresses the historical and social elements that shaped art in the past as well as contemporary influences. Not open to art majors.

title: Design History 1
description: A sequential study of design and function as applied to interior design, furniture design, and product design from antiquity through the eighteenth century. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Design History 2
description: A sequential study of design and function as applied to interior design, furniture design, and product design from nineteenth century to present with emphasis on American and European design. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Ancient Art
description: Focuses on the diverse styles of architecture, sculpture, and painting of three early civilizations: Egyptian, Greek, and Roman. Open to all students.

title: Medieval Art
description: Studies major European movements and personalities in architecture, painting, and sculpture from late antique times through the Gothic period; styles include Early Christian, Byzantine, Carolingian, Romanesque, and Gothic. Open to all students.

title: Renaissance Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of the Early and High Renaissance in Italy and Northern Europe. Emphasis on the growth of the artistic heritage of the Western world through the inventions and creations of Renaissance genius. Open to all students.

title: Mannerism and Baroque Art
description: Special emphasis on the works of the leading exponents of mannerism and baroque styles in architecture, painting, and sculpture as they appeared in Italy, France, Germany, Spain, Flanders, Holland, and England. Open to all students.

title: Nineteenth - Century Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture in Europe and the United States including the Palladian Revival through Symbolism and the forerunners of Cubism and Expressionism, Cezanne, and Munch. Other movements to be considered are Neo-Classicism, Romanticism, Realism, the Pre-Raphaelites, and Impressionism. Open to all students.

title: Twentieth - Century Art to 1945
description: European painting and sculpture from 1900 to 1945. Special attention to the development of styles leading to the contemporary art of the midcentury and later. Open to all students.

title: Art since 1945
description: Deals with the major movements and personalities in twoand threedimensional art in the United States and Europe since World War II. Emphasizes an understanding of the conceptual problems, materials, and techniques and their relationship to early twentiethcentury art and ideas. Open to all students.

title: History of Art in the United States
description: A survey of American cultural traditions as reflected in 350 years of art, architecture, and related forms. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Film History
description: Traces the history of the cinema from its beginning to contemporary times. Emphasizes the role of technique and art in film.

title: History of Photography
description: Surveys the history of photography from 1839 to present. Explores the relationship between equipment and conceptual progress.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Art in Living
description: A field course in which the student will have the opportunity to study at first hand the handicrafts, industrial arts, and arts of a particular geographic area. Open to all students. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Art History
description: Individual or group investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of department chairperson. The Divisions of Music Education, Music History and Musicology, and Music Theory and Composition are in Academic Studies in Music, and the Divisions of Keyboard, Voice, and Guitar, Symphonic Instruments, and Ensembles and Conducting are in Applied Studies in Music. A full range of large and small performing ensembles—the professional Musical Arts Woodwind Quintet, Da Camera Brass Quintet, the Ars Musica String Quartet, the American Piano Trio, the Chamber Choir, the Wind Ensemble, and the Symphony Orchestra—provide opportunities for listening or for active participation. Other groups, such as the Harp Ensemble, the Collegium Musicum, and the University Singers, accent the diversity of performing outlets on campus. Any student, regardless of major, may audition for membership in university concert organizations. Students interested in a concentration in music will consult with the coordinator of undergraduate programs in music. In addition to the regular entrance requirements of the university, students with concentrations in music must have proficiency in piano, voice, or some symphonic instrument and a working knowledge of the rudiments of music. Examinations in theory and applied music are required. If a student cannot meet requirements when entering the university, arrangements may be made to meet them later. Students with concentrations in music are expected to attend a weekly recital as well as to perform. Students will also participate in ensembles according to their curricular requirements. Those planning to become directors of instrumental ensembles or supervisors of instrumental music ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the university bands and university orchestras, and vocalists preparing to become directors of choral activities ordinarily will earn ensemble credits in the appropriate university choral groups. Additionally, students are expected to participate in ensembles outside their special fields. To satisfy these requirements properly, students should make plans early with the coordinator of undergraduate programs. Before completing registration, students will clear their requests for applied music instruction through the Office of Applied Studies in Music, where assignment to specific instructors will be made. Practice rooms should be reserved in the office of the School of Music at the beginning of each semester. Academic Studies in Music Academic Studies in Music is an academic unit that comprises three instructional divisions, each of which contributes to the School of Music, the university, and the community in distinctly different ways toward the common goal of musical and academic excellence. The Division of Music Education The mission of the Division of Music Education is to prepare students for state certification and licensing for teaching music in the public schools. Four specializations are offered for students seeking certification: the teaching area major prepares students to teach instrumental, choral, and general music in grades kindergarten through twelve; the teaching major in instrumental music prepares students to teach instrumental music in grades kindergarten through twelve; the teaching major in choral music prepares students to teach choral music in grades kindergarten through twelve; and the teaching major in general music prepares students to teach general music classes in grades kindergarten through twelve. These specializations may be combined with several minor concentrations in music. To graduate with a major in music teaching preparation, a student must be prepared to execute certain musical and educational tasks by successfully completing the curriculum and by demonstrating a commitment to teaching as well as a high level of competency in the primary and secondary performance media--a symphonic instrument, a keyboard instrument, or voice. Before enrolling in student teaching during the senior year students are required to have completed a piano proficiency examination and to have attained junior level on their primary instrument. The Division of Music History and Musicology This division serves not only music majors but also nonmusic majors through MUHIS 101, Introduction to Music, a course offered as part of the fine arts requirement in the general studies program. Music majors study the background of their discipline in a yearlong survey of music history, and many choose to enhance that survey with more detailed courses in music of the baroque, classical, romantic, or contemporary era. These courses are also open to qualified nonmusic majors. Courses in the history of such genres as opera and symphonic, chamber, and vocal music are offered as well as "composer" courses that include Bach, Brahms, Mozart, and Haydn, and "topics" courses such as the mass in the Renaissance, nineteenthcentury lieder, the classical string quartet, the history of jazz, and American music. The division also assists Bracken Library in building and maintaining a collection of music, music literature, and recordings. The Division of Music Theory and Composition The Division of Music Theory and Composition provides the basic core of courses in music theory. This sequence develops a basic understanding of music theory fundamentals that concentrate on music writing, reading, analysis, and aural skills including music dictation and sightsinging. These courses emphasize conventions that underlie the music of present and past Western civilization. Students may specialize their degrees with minors in composition and theory or choose majors with concentrations in theory, composition, or music engineering and technology. The Electronic Systems for Music Synthesis (ESMS) is a facility that plays a significant role in the evolving curricula of the School of Music. ESMS is an interdisciplinary studio complex that supports education, research, intermedia performance, pedagogy, and composition in electronic media as well as computerassisted composition, sound synthesis, and telecommunications applications for music. ESMS is well equipped and staffed and offers a complete curriculum for music engineering and technology.

title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Screening of potential music education candidates is built into the course.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 1
description: A basic inquiry into the value of craftsmanship and the principles of piano tuning. Discusses the problems and remedies of new and used pianos. An introductory course open to all students interested in the care and maintenance of the piano.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 2
description: Application of piano temperament tuning theory with emphasis on the development of proper tuning techniques. Prerequisite: MUSED 240 or permission of the director of school.

title: Piano Technology Workshop 3
description: Principles of basic action regulation and common minor repairs. Prerequisite: MUSED 241 or permission of the director of school.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Development and Administration of Choral Music
description: Analysis of the high school choral music teacher's position in the school and community and the administration and supervision of choral activities. Discussion of choral music suitable for various high school choirs.

title: Basic Music for Early Childhood Education
description: Designed to develop creative responsiveness in students enrolled in educational programs for young children and to demonstrate through laboratory experiences the application of creativity to the developmental characteristics of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled.

title: Music in the Primary Grades
description: A methods course for choral and general music education majors. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in the first three grades; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: Music in the Upper Elementary Grades
description: A continuation of MUSED 351. Intensive study of materials, methods, and skills for teaching music in grades four, five, and six; singing, rhythms, listening, creative activities, and instruments. Directed observation gives contact with actual teaching situations.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High Schools
description: A study of the philosophies, techniques, and materials for teaching the required nonperformance music courses in grades five through nine. Emphasizes the unique musical needs of young adolescents.

title: Teaching Instrumental Music
description: Examines problems in the teaching and administration of contemporary instrumental classes. Topics include program goals, inventory management, rehearsals, selection of materials, and techniques for the learning of musical concepts in performance classes. Prerequisite: minor skills in brasses, woodwinds, and strings. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary Classroom
description: Focuses on the implementation of music in the elementary classroom. Draws on the common heritage of music and suggests methods for presenting appropriate musical experience and materials to children. Prerequisite: MUSED 265.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, short -term course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experience with the materials and activities of nonperformance classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possiblities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: The Orff Workshop: Beginning
description: Stresses the basic approaches of the Orff method of teaching music to children in grades one through six. Emphasizes techniques of organized recorder playing and study of recorder literature.

title: The Orff Workshop: Intermediate
description: More advanced phases of instruction in the Orff approach. Emphasizes creative projects in orchestrating materials to be used with children in grades one through six. Includes techniques of organized recorder ensemble playing and study of recorder literature. Prerequisite: MUSED 443.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Approaches to the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods of Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction. Prerequisite: credit in classical guitar.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite or parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Methods of Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods of teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level or permission of the director of school.

title: Introduction to Orff - Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities involve movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative use of simple percussion instruments.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; singing and conducting opportunities of standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Handbell Techniques
description: An introduction to the history, literature, and playing techniques of handbells. Includes opportunities to conduct and to perform with handbell choirs. Discussion of administering handbell choirs in church and school situations.

title: Basic Movement and Choreography
description: Designed to acquaint the music therapist or teacher with the fundamentals of physical interpretations of music. Deals with techniques appropriate for swing choirs, small ensembles, and general staging practices in performance preparation.

title: Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school form the framework of this course designed for the music specialist.

title: Contemporary Techniques in Elementary School Music
description: Exploring the use of nonconventional, nontraditional, experimental musical sound sources and procedures in music education.

title: Stage Band Techniques
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the techniques and style characteristics of popular and jazz band performance. Includes preparation in the administration of school jazz ensembles.

title: Guitar for Social Use
description: Designed for development of basic skill in playing the guitar for accompanying. Focuses on chordal styles and their application to music such as folk songs and popular songs. Open to all students.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Stringed Instruments
description: Provides a fundamental working knowledge of skills required in maintaining and repairing stringed instruments at the elementary and secondary school levels. Study and application of school repair problems relating to the violin, viola,, cello, and double bass.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis on those specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Music in Therapy and Special Education
description: The theoretical aspects of music therapy and their appropriate application to special education in the public schools. Emphasizes the power of music to elicit normal interaction with peers from the child with a learning difficulty.

title: Recreational Music
description: Explores materials, sources, and elements of a recreational music program, organizational procedures, individual and group activities, and use of community musical resources. Open to all students; musical background not required.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: An opportunity for the superior student to do intensive study and research in a particular aspect of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Introduction to Music
description: Designed primarily to introduce students to the sound of music through the ages; no previous knowledge of music required.

title: Music and Popular Culture in America
description: A survey of the relationships between music and popular culture in twentiethcentury America. Topics include blues, jazz, and rock as well as classical music with emphasis on cultural rather than technical aspects of music.

title: Music History 1
description: The development of music from its beginnings through 1750. Origins, growth of early polyphony, instrumental music. Changes in style during medieval, Renaissance, and baroque periods.

title: Music History 2
description: Changes in music from the preclassic period through the present. The development of symphony, sonata, and related forms, the contributions of romanticists, and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 230.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Open only to students on the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of medieval, Renaissance, and baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. Open only to students on the Honors Program.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 1
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Bach through Liszt. Prerequisite: some music literature background and an ability to read music.

title: Standard Repertoire of the Piano 2
description: A survey of the standard masterworks for piano from Chopin through Samuel Barber. Prerequisite: some music literature background and an ability to read music.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: The vocal and instrumental music of western Europe during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including figured bass, opera, oratorio and cantata, and the development of such instrumental genres as concerto, sonata, and suite. Prerequisite: MUHIS 231.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles that marked the transition from baroque to classical music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 231.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in Western civilization in the nineteenth century, emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Studies important composers and works from the various time periods: early, middle, late, and post-Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUHIS 231 or permission of the director of the school.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and the student will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisite: MUHIS 231.

title: Jazz History 1
description: Historic examination of jazz from 1890 to 1950. Analyzes outstanding style characteristics of each period from their beginnings to the 1950s, including ragtime, the Jazz Age, the Swing Era, and the bebop and cool periods.

title: Jazz History 2
description: Continuation of MUHIS 439, covering the 1950s through the present. Progressive '50s, the rockjazz fusions of the 1960s, '70s, and '80stoday's trends.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design

title: Independent Study in Music History

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, 230, 231.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101, or 230, 231.

description: Introduces students to basic music notation and nomenclature. Includes such topics as intervals, scales, modes, keys, rhythm, and instrumental transposition. title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 111. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Music Theory
description: More complex elements of nineteenthand twentiethcentury music studied through composition and analysis. Advanced work in music reading and aural discernment provided in class and electronic laboratory drill. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 211. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: The components of the recording chain are introduced both theoretically and practically. A complete and thorough review of the recording process, the mixing process, and editing formats is presented.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An introduction to multichannel recording techniques, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing is presented. Requires laboratory time for recording practice and a final recording project. Prerequisite: MUSTH 225.

title: Music Calligraphy
description: Practical experience in calligraphic skills and layout procedures pertinent to the preparation of music scores and parts. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Composition

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic Music
description: A workshop in current practices of producing music by electronic means. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band and wind ensemble. Gives particular attention to voicing, sectional and crosssectional doubling, soloistic treatment of instruments, and other elements of contemporary treatment in scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Commercial Arranging Concepts
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques employed in commercial music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms with particular attention given to the composerarranger in the recording studio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Music Theory in the Secondary School
description: An investigation of pedagogical precepts and problems relating to music theory in the secondary school. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Twentieth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to principles and procedures of twentiethcentury music.

title: Electronic Music Studio 1
description: An introduction to the physical and perceptual dimensions of sound are presented as a basis for sound synthesis. An introduction to musique concrete operations and voltagecontrolled systems provides the basis for class projects. Studio laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Electronic Music Studio 2
description: An advanced course in electronic music synthesis. An introduction to large voltagecontrolled systems, advanced mixing procedures, and signal processing. Projects in composition, educational applications of electronic music, and research. Laboratory time is required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 425. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Computer Applications in Music
description: Presents an overview of computer systems and languages appropriate for musical analysis, musical composition, and sound synthesis. Presents a historical perspective and computer applications in the areas stated and introduces simple programming procedures. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Composition-Project Recital
description: Public performance of the student's compositions, public presentation of the student's music theory research, or both.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire. description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer or technician. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Musical Theatre in America
description: A study of the history of the American musical theatre. A general overview of the repertoire.

Department of Theatre LaCasse, Chairperson; Bloom, English, Hardin, Heady, Irving, Jaremski, Knight, Lund, Mangelsdorf, May, Schisla, Shawger, Urice, Yordon The Department of Theatre offers theatre students preprofessional training within the traditional liberal arts setting. Theatre graduates are prepared to enter the country's finest professional graduate programs, or, if exceptionally talented and dedicated, to pursue immediately a career in the professional world. The department also offers, through its general theatre option, a more broadly based program for students wanting preparation for careers in the academic world. The dance program offers students a broad coverage of performance. The focus is on the fundamentals of dance designed to develop basic technique and the ability to perform as well as a set of principles that lead to a fuller intellectual grasp of the art. In addition, course offerings and the departmental production programs offer a background of information and practical experience to students in other disciplines where a dance or theatre cognate is desirable. Curriculum. Students in dance and theatre receive intensive classroom instruction and gain valuable experience in all areas of theatre and dance. Theatre majors may specialize in performance (acting and directing), technical (design), or general theatre studies. Dance majors may select advanced course work in ballet, ethnic dance, modern dance, jazz, tap, and musical theatre dance styles. Theatre minors are available in theatre, oral interpretation, and children's theatre. Dance minors are offered in ballet, ethnic dance, modern dance, and musical theatre dance styles. Teacher licensing in speech communication and theatre for students planning to teach and direct in secondary school theatre is available through the Department of Speech Communication. Students are not required to audition for admission into the theatre programs. However, an audition/portfolio presentation is required for students near the end of the sophomore year for admission into the performance and technical (design) options. The dance program does not require an audition for admission. However, students will be evaluated at the end of their first year in the program and advised as to whether they should continue in the program. Dance Performance. The dance program includes two major performance groups: Ball State Dance Theatre, which features a broad range of such dance styles as ballet and contemporary dance, and Banevolks, organized in 1971, which emphasizes native dances from around the world. Dance performance groups are open to all students by audition. Production Program. For more than fifty years Ball State has produced plays for student training and for the enjoyment of the entire campus community. The department annually produces fourteen to eighteen plays in a variety of stylesfrom classical to contemporary, comedy to tragedy, musicals to operas. Auditions for department productions are open to all students and credit may be earned through Theatre Practicum, THEAT 280 or DANCE 489. Theatre students are expected to participate in productions. description: A lecturelaboratory course on the principles of acting with major emphasis on character analysis and development. Prerequisite: THEAT 232.

title: Voice and Movement
description: An intensive course for developing and adapting the actor's voice, articulatory mechanisms, and body for effective public performance. Techniques outlined in textual materials and lecture are augmented by practical demonstrations and exercises to implement and assess growth of skills. Prerequisite: THEAT 232, 233.

title: Theatre Practicum
description: Intensive experience in acting, stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, theatre management, and other production areas. Students should complete practicums in six different areas. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: History of Theatre 1
description: Study of the Western theatre from its origins through the Renaissance, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: History of Theatre 2
description: Study of the Western theatre from the Renaissance to the foundations of modern theatre in the late nineteenth century, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Modern Theatre
description: Study of major movements in modern Western theatre since 1875, with emphasis on theoretical documents, production elements, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Theatrical Design Skills
description: A lecturelaboratory class to present basic problemsolving skills involving theatrical design artwork. Emphasizes the development of technique and media competence. Prerequisite: THEAT 220.

title: Fundamentals of Stage Lighting
description: A lecturelaboratory course in the basic concepts, materials, hardware, and design principles of stage lighting. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Directing 1
description: Theory and practice of directing for the theatre. Exercises in movement, line interpretation, creation of atmosphere, and the effective use of stage areas. Prerequisite: THEAT 232 and 233.

title: Directing for the Musical Theatre
description: A detailed examination of the selection, organization, and direction of musical theatre productions. For practical laboratory work, the student may elect to concentrate on the production problems of either a specific musical comedy or an opera.

title: Children's Theatre
description: The principles of theatre devoted to creative dramatics. Twothirds of the course is devoted to formal dramatics. A public performance will be arranged.

title: Advanced Theatre Practice
description: Students design and execute a theatre project in such areas as scenery design, lighting, properties, acting, directing, oral interpretation, and house management. Prerequisite: 12 hours of credit in theatre courses and permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Studies in American Theatre
description: An investigation of significant movements in the American professional theatre and its drama.

title: Scene Design
description: Advanced training and experience in the problems of set design and lighting for theatrical productions in many forms and styles, including aspects of television design. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Advanced Scene Design
description: A detailed lecturelaboratory class for the design student emphasizing advanced problems of scenic rigging and design. Covers preparation and implementation of various genres including the musical theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 420.

title: Theatre Costume Design
description: Practice in the research, design, and building techniques involved in the preparation of period costumes for use in theatre productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 223 and 320.

title: Stage Lighting Design
description: Training and experience in the problems of stage lighting design for the proscenium and nonproscenium stage. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 326.

title: Styles of Acting
description: The study and performance of the styles of acting appropriate to major types of drama from antiquity to the present. Prerequisite: THEAT 234.

title: Advanced Study of Roles for Performance
description: An advanced course concentrating on the preparation of a script for performance. At all stages of preparation, students work closely with a faculty adviser of their choosing. The course will culminate in a live, adjudicated performance. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 and 433; INTRP 230; and permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Directing 2
description: Further investigation of the work of the director with special reference to directing the various styles, modes, and periods of theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 or the equivalent.

title: Creative Dramatics
description: Principles of developing original dramatizations through improvisational techniques. Students are expected to observe and work with children as well as with college adults.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop
description: Participation in the Summer Festival Theatre. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theatre Management
description: Study and practice in box office procedures, house management, publicity, and promotion as related to college, community, and professional theatres. Prerequisite: 9 hours of theatre courses.

title: Directed Study in Theatre
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects in design, playwriting, acting, interpretation, or directing, meeting the approval of the theatre staff. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Ballet 1
description: Classes in ballet technique for beginners, with special emphasis on body placement and alignment. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester. 111.Ballet 2. (1) Classes in ballet technique for advanced beginners, with special emphasis on the use of epaulement. Prerequisite: DANCE 110 or permission on department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Modern 1
description: For students interested in dance performance or career opportunities in dance. Basic techniques and performance skills are emphasized. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Modern 2
description: Designed to continue development of the basic performance skills of modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 120 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Ethnic Dance 1
description: Basic repertoire of ethnic dance steps, styles, and dances for use in performance. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: History of Dance
description: Basic dance forms and functions from the primitive era into the twentieth century.

title: Ballet 3
description: Ballet technique on a beginningintermediate level for those with previous training. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Ballet 4
description: A continuation of ballet technique for students on an intermediate level. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Modern 3
description: Designed for students with training in modern dance and introduction to improvisational performance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 121 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Modern 4
description: Designed to prepare students for advanced modern dance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 220 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Jazz 2
description: Designed for the student with dance training who has interest in developing technique in various jazz styles. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 120 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Tap 2
description: Advanced tap dance techniques for the dance student with previous tap dance training. Prerequisite: PEG 118 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Musical Theatre Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of contemporary dance styles for the Broadway and nightclub stages. Dance styles covered will change each semester. Prerequisite: PEG 118; DANCE 110, 120 or PEG 116. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Ethnic Dance Styles
description: An indepth study into the stylistic uniqueness of a particular ethnic region. Covers three to four styles during the semester. Prerequisite: DANCE 140. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Clogging
description: American ethnic dance form known as clogging. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Ball State Ballet
description: A broadbased dance company, emphasizing ballet technique, with performance interest extending from tap, jazz, and experimental to classical ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester. Open only to students by audition.

title: Contemporary Dance Theatre
description: Provides the dance student with experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance presentations. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester. Open only to students by audition.

title: International Folk Dance Company
description: Provides opportunity for students with interest in folk dance to learn and perform dances from many different countries. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester. Open by audition and permission of department chairperson.

title: Choreography 1
description: Work in choreographing dance by exploring musical and dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111, 120, 121, 140.

title: Ballet History
description: A survey of ballet from its inception to the present time. Prerequisite: DANCE 200.

title: Ballet 5
description: Intermediateadvanced level of ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 and 211 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Ballet 6
description: Advanced ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 310 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Partnering
description: Study of the art of partnering. Class is limited to not more than two females for each male partner. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Modern 5
description: Introduction to improvisational performance skills for students with training in modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 220, 221 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Modern 6
description: Designed to continue development of advanced modern dance performance skills and improvisational techniques. Prerequisite: DANCE 320 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Notation
description: Introduction to dance notation with an emphasis on such contemporary notation systems as Labonotation and Benesh. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240.

title: Dance Production
description: Designed to acquaint the student with various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Choreography 2
description: Work in choreographing traditional and nontraditional dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 287 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Dance Pedagogy
description: Indepth study of teaching methods for beginning, intermediate, and advanced dance students, includes pedagogy from preschool through adult level. Includes rehearsal technique for performance preparation. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester.

title: Dance Practicum
description: Intensive experience in stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, dance management, and other aspects of production. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in a semester.

title: Creative Project
description: Designed as a project in choreography for advanced dance students. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Directed Study in Dance
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects related to dance that meet the approval of the dance faculty. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Oral Interpretation
description: The study of prose fiction, poetry, and drama through the medium of oral performance.

title: Oral Interpretation of Prose Fiction
description: An indepth study of the novel through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Poetry
description: The study of poetry through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Drama
description: The study of dramatic literature through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Studies in Oral Interpretation
description: Students with an interest in oral interpretation pursue a particular area of study in depth. Prerequisite: INTRP 230. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester.

title: Presentational Theatre Forms
description: The creation and direction of presentational (readers theatre and chamber theatre) scripts—concentrating on literature not originally intended for the stage. Prerequisite: INTRP 230. Department of Anthropology Scruton, Chairperson; Bowers, Coffin, Flores-Meiser, Glenn, Hicks, Swartz, Whitehead The question of questions for mankind .. . is the ascertainment of the place which Man occupies in nature and of his relations to the universe of things. —T. H. Huxley Anthropology means literally "the study of man." Unlike the other social, behavioral, and life sciences, anthropology does not concentrate on only one aspect of human existence, but rather assumes we can achieve a true understanding of the workings of individuals and groups only by an integrated study of biology and culture, past and present, primitive and complex, as a whole. There are four major subdivisions of anthropology: cultural anthropology, archaeology, physical anthropology; and linguistics. Among the many topics of interest to those who study cultural anthropology are kinship and community social organization, childrearing practices, individual status and roles, ideology, economic and political organization, the interactions between societies and their environments, material goods, and how and why cultures change. Archaeology provides time depth for anthropology, particularly for those societies for which there are no written records. Cultural anthropology depends heavily on living informants, but archaeologists have only the physical remains left behind, which are much more difficult to interpret. Thus while archaeologists do gather information about social organization, they devote greater attention to subsistence practices, settlement patterns, technology, and the questions of why and how cultures change. Physical anthropology pays particular attention to the biological nature not only of humans but also of our nearest relatives, the other primates—prosimians, monkeys, and apes. Within physical anthropology there are further subspecialties: primate paleontology, which tries to trace the development of Homo sapiens and the other primates through fossil studies; primatology, which compares the anatomy, physiology, and behavior of the various primate species; and human biology, which studies growth and development, racial and other genetic differences, and the ways our bodies adapt to our natural and cultural environments. Anthropological linguistics concerns itself with the nature and history of language, an especially complex part of our cultural heritage. The influence of social situations on language performance is studied, as is language's role in the transmission of culture. By combining the studies of these four divisions we are able to see human nature as a whole, a system of interrelated parts. The nature of this system is often made clearest by comparative studies, by stepping outside our own culture or race or time to see how others are constituted. A major or minor in anthropology offers background to students preparing for law school, medical school, public health, international business, public administration, or urban planning. For students who wish to become professional anthropologists, graduate study is usually required and can lead either to a career in academic teaching and research or to work in a more applied field such as planning and development, environmental assessment, cultural or archaeological preservation, public health, or medical research. Special programs available within the department include opportunities for field experience in archaeological resources management and summer field schools in Indiana archaeology and in ethnography in Jamaica and among the Indians of the American Southwest. Arrangements can be made for field studies anywhere in the world. The student will be guided by the outline of baccalaureate degrees (pp. 56-58) and by the concentration areas listed below.
