Twining, Ulman, VanEvery, VanTassel The philosophy of special education encompasses the right of all children, youth, and adults to participate in educational and careerplanning experiences that will develop their capabilities to the fullest extent. Gradual acceptance of this philosophy by society has created a demand for highly skilled personnel who are certified in the various exceptionality areas represented within special education. The Department of Special Education offers undergraduate programs leading to teacher certification in deaf education; mildly mentally handicapped; moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped; and physically handicapped. Graduate programs are offered in teaching of learningdisabled and emotionally disturbed in addition to undergraduate preparation. These programs are designed in accordance with Indiana teacher licensure requirements. Elective courses in special education open to future teachers, psychologists, speech and hearing therapists, and social workers include a survey course of exceptional children, courses in the education of gifted children, a course in the education of slow learners, and a course in the education of children with learning disabilities. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE HEARING-IMPAIRED The legal right of all children to an appropriate education has created a need for teachers of the hearingimpaired. The emphasis on "mainstreaming" exceptional children into the regular classroom developed a need for teachers of the hearingimpaired with more general preparation in addition to the specialized course work for teachers of the deaf. The growth of different communication philosophies made it essential to provide additional course work options within the majors and minors. A major in the education of the deaf is offered to those who prefer some level of elementary teaching, and a minor is available for persons who wish to teach an academic subject at the junior high and high school levels. The state of Indiana, Ball State University, and the Department of Special Education have adopted extensive requirements for licensing and have developed flexible programs that can accommodate the above needs. The Ball State University program for training teachers of the hearingimpaired meets the approval of the Indiana Teacher Training and Licensing Commission, the Council on the Education of the Deaf (CED), and the U.S. Department of Education. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR THE MENTALLY HANDICAPPED Acceptance of the philosophy of special education has led to the development of specialized programs for mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults. These programs have provided the impetus to prepare specially trained teachers to work effectively with mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped children, youth, and adults in the least restrictive instructional setting. Teachers and other interested professional personnel are taught the necessary skills to implement accepted intervention strategies for appropriately meeting the mentally handicapped person's learning style and educational and career needs. In response to the nationwide demand for qualified teachers to serve mentally handicapped children, youth, and adults, the Department of Special Education offers a major in the teaching of the mildly handicapped and minors in the teaching of the mildly handicapped and moderately, severely, profoundly, and multiply handicapped. The teaching minor also serves as an endorsement in each of the exceptionality areas represented within the mentally handicapped area. SPECIAL EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN WITH PHYSICAL HANDICAPS OR SPECIAL HEALTH PROBLEMS Among children who have special educational needs are the physically handicapped (mildly and severely) and those who have other health conditions that make special class placement necessary. A typical classroom for these handicapped or healthimpaired children presents the teacher with a challenging variety of physical impairments as well as learning difficulties. To profit from their educational experience, these children are in need of specially prepared teachers with an understanding of the physical, psychological, and educational problems encountered in such a classroom, as well as knowledge of curriculum and methodology to meet these problems. The teachereducation program is designed to offer comprehensive professional preparation to future teachers of physically handicapped (mildly and severely) or healthimpaired children so that these children will have the opportunity to learn and grow to the best of their ability under the guidance of competent, special teachers. title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: An introduction to definitions, characteristics, and educational needs of children who deviate from normal in mental, physical, social, and emotional ways. Examines federal and state legal bases for education of exceptional children.

title: Management Strategies for the Preschool Handicapped
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for more effective management of the preschool handicapped child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or equivalent.

title: Developmental Methods with Preschool Handicapped
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool handicapped child's cognitive, language, creative, and physical environments. These developmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool handicapped children.

title: Practicum—Teaching Young Handicapped Children
description: Student works with handicapped children in a supervised teaching practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of handicapped children. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microcomputers and the Exceptional Learner
description: Introduction to microcomputer applications in special education through orientation to hardware, programming experience, word processing. and special purpose software. Also emphasizes teaching strategies for introducing microcomputers to children in the classroom.

title: History of Education of the Deaf and the Psychology of Deafness
description: A brief study of educational provisions for the deaf from the beginning to the present and a survey of the social, educational, and vocational problems of deafness.

title: Education of Preschool Hearing - and Language -Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Practicum in Special Education
description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: Designed for future teachers of crippled or other healthimpaired students. Includes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate students with physical disabilities. Prerequisite SPCED 372.

title: Psychology of Mental Retardation
description: Various types and degrees of retardation; the psychological, environmental, and cultural factors that contribute to retardation. Emphasizes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate retarded students. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, BIO 453 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Educational Methods with Moderately, Severely, and Profoundly Mentally Handicapped Children
description: Current instructional planning for the moderately, severely, and profoundly mentally handicapped will be reviewed and evaluated. Focuses on techniques for effecting innovative curricula for people at the preschool through postschool levels. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Educational Methods with Physically/Multiply Handicapped Children
description: Special class organization, curriculum, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of multiply and orthopedically handicapped children and children with special health problems. Prerequisite or parallel: EDEI, 380 and MATHS 391.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of psychological characteristics and educational needs of gifted and talented children in the schools. Definitions of giftedness and identification procedures are studied; review of current and past practices in the field.

title: Speech Development for the Deaf
description: The International Phonetic Alphabet, Northhampton Charts, diacritical markings, and other methods and techniques used to teach speech to the deaf. Prerequisite: SPCH 216 and SPCED 240, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Practicum in Speech for the Deaf
description: Observation of a person working with preschool children in developmental speech. Time will also be devoted to speech improvement for older children. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 and 446 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Manual Communications
description: Theory and research underlying the language of signs and fingerspelling (manual alphabet) is considered. Development of receptive and expressive skills in manual communications is required. Required of students intending to student teach in schools or classes using total communication.

title: Advanced Manual Communication
description: A course in manual communication designed to improve conversational skill in signs and fingerspelling to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in a classroom for hearingimpaired children. Prerequisite: SPCED 451 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Language for the Deaf
description: Compares language development of hearing children with that of deaf children. Levels of abstraction and the difficulty encountered in both receptive and expressive language are examined. The philosophy underlying various methods of language teaching is studied. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and SPAA 370 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Language Methods for the Deaf
description: Language systems are studied and used in practice situations. Includes Fitzgerald Straight Language for the Deaf, Barry Five-Slate, Wing Symbols, and the Natural Method. Language outlines from different schools are used as supplementary aids. Prerequisite: SPCED 240, 266, and 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to the Deaf
description: Principles and methods of teaching reading to deaf children in the lower and higher grades; methods of teaching such subjects as arithmetic and science. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and 266 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Student Teaching: Hearing-Impaired
description: Required preservice teaching practica for students seeking licensure in special education: hearingimpaired. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Expressive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Provides students who have basic manual communication skills with intensive training and practice in expressive interpreting for the deaf. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Receptive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Designed to provide students who have basic manual communication ability with professional skill for interpreting manual language in special situations. Opportunity for extensive practice and evaluation will be provided. Prerequisite: SPCED 468 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Handicapped
description: Special class organization, instructional materials, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally handicapped. Using the individualized education plan (IEP) and mainstreaming are incorporated. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (1 hr.), 372; EDRDG 430; and MATHS

title: Diagnostic and Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Handicapped
description: Continuation of methods and materials for the mildly handicapped, begun in SPCED 474, with emphasis on use of the diagnosticprescriptive model to determine the learners' special needs and prescription of required curricular modifications in the IEP. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (1 hr.) and 474.

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Handicapped
description: Required for licensure in special education: mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 9 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Student Teaching: Physically/Multiply Handicapped
description: Required for licensure in special education: physically/multiply handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Moderately Mentally Handicapped, Severely/Profoundly Mentally Handicapped, and Multiply Handicapped
description: Required for licensure in special education: moderately mentally handicapped, severely/profoundly mentally handicapped, and multiply handicapped. Center for International Programs Hicks, Director, Yuhas, Associate Director Life in the contemporary world requires a universal outlook and a sensitivity to other cultures not demanded by any previous age. To be effective, students must be aware of the varying and constantly changing cultural conditions of other societies. This premise is the attraction and the challenge of international studies. The international studies program is designed for students who desire an interdisciplinary approach to contemporary world problems. Although some students use the program to prepare for careers in the international field both at home and abroad, many are attracted by the wide range of disciplines and courses represented in the curricula and the resulting opportunity to cross disciplinary boundaries in search of a contemporary liberal education. The international studies programs in Asian studies and Latin-American studies are designed to meet the needs of both potential professionals in international affairs and those who have chosen a related major field of study—perhaps history, foreign languages, geography, political science, or economics—and who wish to include the international dimension as a minor field. The center offers two international studies programs: a minor in Asian studies and a major and minor in Latin-American studies. These programs are directed by committees of area specialists from a wide variety of disciplines. Students may expect to enroll in a broad range of courses developed by several academic departments. Students enrolled in international studies programs are ordinarily expected to gain some competence in foreign languages related to their study areas. The departmental major in Latin-American studies in liberal arts will also complete the language requirements for the bachelor of arts degree. In addition to instructional programs on campus, the international studies program provides students with the opportunity to study overseas. Any student may apply for the foreign study programs offered by Ball State University, other American universities, or foreign universities. Details on foreign courses and credit transfer are available from the associate director of the Center for International Programs, where students may inquire for special counsel and guidance. title: Honors Symposium in Contemporary Civilization
description: An examination of some of the critical issues that confront contemporary civilization. Open only to freshmen participating in the Honors College.

title: Introduction to Sport in American Life
description: A thorough examination of the various historical, sociological, and psychological aspects of sport in our society. Not sportappreciation oriented, but rather an examination of what occurs to both competitors and spectators as they become involved with a sport activity. Open to all undergraduate students.

title: Women's Studies
description: An analysis of the role of American women in sociology, history, and literature, and an attempt to define woman biologically and psychologically.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experiences meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the Office of Undergraduate Admissions and the registrar accordingly. The Office of Advising and Scheduling is informed of how the credit is to be applied to the student's program. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foreign Study
description: Foreign study provides a means of granting Ball State University credit for course work undertaken abroad at institutions of higher learning (e.g., universities, centers, and institutes) as part of approved study programs. Applicable toward majors, minors, or general education with departmental approval. Prerequisite: acceptance in a Ball State exchange program or approved studyabroad program. A total of 32 hours of credit may be earned. The course is offered for credit/nocredit only.

title: Honors Candidate
description: May be taken each semester by honors candidates who have already registered in previous semesters for all their undergraduate course work, including ID 499, but have not yet completed their senior honors projects. Enrollment in this course entitles enrollees to ordinary undergraduate student use of library, health, and other university facilities.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An inquiry culminating in an honors paper prepared in accordance with accepted standards of documentation and presentation under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to seniors participating in the Honors College or completing the requirements for departmental honors. title: Foreign Study
description: Foreign study is a means of granting Ball State University credit for course work undertaken abroad at institutions of higher learning (e.g., universities, centers, and institutes) as part of approved study programs. Applicable toward majors, minors, or general education with departmental approval. Prerequisite: acceptance in a Ball State exchange program or approved studyabroad program. A total of 32 hours of credit may be earned. The course is offered for credit/nocredit only.

title: Honors Symposium in Global Studies
description: Focuses on the commonalities and rich diversities in global culture, economy, history, politics, and society. Taught from varied perspectives or disciplines; emphasis is on the non-Western world—Asia, Africa, and Central and South America.

title: Honors Symposium in Contemporary Civilization
description: An examination of some of the critical issues that confront contemporary civilization. Open only to students participating in the Honors College.

title: Honors Humanities 2: Middle Ages, Renaissance, Enlightenment
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the Middle Ages, Renaissance, and Enlightenment. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Humanities 3: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Biology and Human Concerns
description: Basic introduction to biological principles using humans as the major organism and emphasizing the relationship of contemporary biology to human concerns and society. Included in the course are social and ethical consequences of scientific discoveries and their societal application. Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to the student who has credit in HONRS 299.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Human Genetics and Bioethics
description: A general studies science course. Applying personal knowledge toward the solution of some critical biological issues confronting contemporary society. Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to the student who has credit in HONRS 298.

title: Honors Colloquium
description: Exploration of selected issues linking several disciplines. Emphasis is on discussion, individual projects, and ways of combining information from several sources. Open only to honors students by permission.

title: Honors Candidate
description: May be taken each semester by honors candidates who have already registered in previous semesters for all of their undergraduate course work, including HONRS 499, but have not yet completed their senior honors projects. Students enrolled in this course are entitled to ordinary undergraduate student use of library, health, and other university facilities.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An inquiry culminating in an honors paper prepared in accordance with accepted standards of documentation and presentation under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to seniors participating in the Honors College or completing the requirements for departmental honors.

title: Introduction to Sport in American Life
description: A thorough examination of the various historical, sociological, and psychological aspects of sport in our society. Not sportappreciation oriented, but rather an examination of what occurs to both competitors and spectators as they become involved with a sport activity. Open to all undergraduate students.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experiences meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the Office of Undergraduate Admissions and the registrar accordingly. The Office of Advising and Scheduling is informed of how the credit is to be applied to the student's program. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. AFRO-AMERICAN STUDIES The Afro-American studies minor explores the culture of black Americans and Africans to help all students understand themselves and relationships between blacks and whites. The knowledge of American, Caribbean, and African societies prepares students for careers in multinational business, multicultural education, law, journalism, radio, television, social work, and urban planning. For more information on this program, call the history department at (317) 285-8700. DEPARTMENTAL MINOR IN AFRO-AMERICAN STUDIES, 18-20 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS

title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Survey of American studies as a field and as an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American civilization. Methods and theories of American studies will be discussed, along with major themes and topics in American life and thought. Not open to the student who has credit in HIST 101. title: Introduction to Home Economics
description: Career opportunities available in the profession of home economics; introduction to Ball State home economics programs, facilities, staff; development of home economics as a profession.

title: Internship in Home Economics
description: Gives students the opportunity to work in established internship settings to gain professional experience in their areas of study. Open to all departmental majors and will be substituted for required practicum with permission of program directors.

title: Home Economics Field Studies
description: Combines reading knowledge with field experiences in which students study special topics in home economics in a particular location. Open to all students with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Workshop: Home Economics
description: Activityoriented study of one topic in home economics. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Home Economics
description: Independent investigation and exploration of a topic in home economics. Emphasizes extensive reading and the development of research skills. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Home Economics
description: Presentations and discussions on selected topics of current interest in home economics. Focuses on a different topic in home economics each semester offered. Prerequisite: junior or senior standing and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Professional Development in Home Economics
description: Examines the skills needed in getting a job, emphasizing résumé writing, interviewing, and dress. Explores such topics as adjusting, succeeding, and growing as a professional in one's chosen career. Prerequisite: senior standing. HOME ECONOMICS: EDUCATION (HEED)

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Applies the principles and philosophies of vocational education to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image.

title: Home Economics Presentation Techniques
description: Analysis of audience and business needs and the development of presentations and projects to meet these needs. Includes selection and use of presentation methods, development and use of devices, and professional roles and expectations. Open to all departmental majors in home economics and dietetics. Not open to students with teaching majors in vocational home economics.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Home Economics
description: Organization of teaching units and lesson plans; selection and use of teaching methods and materials. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended EDSEC 280.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: HEED 392, 395.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: A study of how to coordinate class instruction and work experience; includes selecting and recruiting students, selecting training stations, role of the coordinator, techniques of coordination, and placement and followup of graduates. Prerequisite: HEED 392, 395. HOME ECONOMICS: FOODS AND

title: Food Preparation and Meal Planning
description: Designed for students not majoring in home economics. Fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals with emphasis on correct techniques and methods of food preparation. Not open to the student who has credit in HEFN 110.

title: Principles of Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation.

title: Food Experimentation and Comparison
description: Effects of different ingredients and methods of determining quality of products. Emphasizes recognition of standard products and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve standard products. Application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation. Prerequisite: HEFN 110. Not open to the student who has credit in HEFN 430.

title: Meal Management
description: Principles and fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals, with emphasis on resource management and the purchase and storage of food. Attention given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Prerequisite: HEFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis on fundamental principles of nutrition and application to diets of children and normal adults. Not open to the student who has credit in HEFN 340.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industry, and commercial operations. Experiences in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Parallel: HEFN 360 for dietetic or food management majors. HEFN 292 for dietetic technology students.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration
description: Emphasis on organizational structure, scientific management, and personnel administration. Experiences in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel. Parallel: HEFN 363 for majors in dietetics or food management. HEFN 292 for dietetic technology students.

title: Normal and Therapeutic Nutrition Supervised Field Experience
description: Experience with professional standards and supervision related to normal and therapeutic nutrition in clinical and community settings. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. Parallel: HEFN 342.

title: Experience
description: Selected experiences related to foodequipment use, sanitation, and employee training in a quantity foodservice setting. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. Parallel: HEFN 263; 360.

title: Quantity Food-Service Personnel Management Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience in personnel management in a quantity foodservice setting. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. Parallel: HEFN 263 and 363.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Purchasing Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experiences related to menu planning and purchasing in a variety of quantity foodservice organizations. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. Parallel: HEFN 364.

title: Nutrition
description: Nutritive value of foods and the use of food by the human body. Nutritional needs of people throughout the life cycle. Prerequisite: junioror seniorlevel standing; a major in nursing, food management, or dietetic technology; or permission of department chairperson.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Dietary modifications needed by people with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: HEFN 340. Parallel: HEFN 282 for dietetic technology students. Not open to the student who has credit in HEFN 441.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Nutrition problems and programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Investigation and observation of and participation in nutrition programs in the local community. Prerequisite: HEFN 340.

title: Quantity Food Production and Equipment
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Stationary and small equipment for food preparation. Layouts of kitchens. Prerequisite: HEFN 110, 220. Parallel: HEFN 262 for majors in food management. HEFN 292 for dietetic technology students.

title: Institutional Administration
description: Concepts of quantity food service in restaurants, schools, hospitals, and cafeterias. Emphasis on personnel, management, organization, cost control, and apportionment of labor. Field trips to institutional kitchens. Parallel: HEFN 263 for majors in food management. HEFN 293 for dietetic technology students.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing and Menu Planning
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers and important considerations in purchasing foods. Emphasizes menu planning with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs. Prerequisite: HEFN 220, 340. Parallel: HEFN 294 for dietetic technology students.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of foods in relation to their composition, physical and chemical properties, and circumstances affecting food quality. Investigates recipes and develops and evaluates methods of combining ingredients. Prerequisite: HEFN 110.

title: Advanced Nutrition
description: Advanced course in nutrition, emphasizing the use and metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Current research in the field of nutrition. Includes laboratory experiences. Prerequisite: HEFN 340 and CHEM 231; senior standing.

title: Diet in Disease and Nutrition Assessment
description: Dietary modifications and the planning of therapeutic diets for treating various nutritional diseases and problems. Techniques needed to identify persons at risk of nutritional deficiency. Includes laboratory experiences. Prerequisite: HEFN 292 or 440 or permission of department chairperson; senior standing.

title: Seminar in Dietetics
description: The professions involved in food service and dietetics; the roles and responsibilities of personnel, their relationships with other professionals, and standards to be attained; the code of professional ethics and the resources for continuing professional education. Prerequisite: 2 hours of credit in a nutrition or dietetic technology practicum or permission of department chairperson.

title: Nutrition, Weight Control, and Exercise
description: Designed for students in dietetics, physical education, and healthrelated fields. Information and experience for students preparing to provide nutrition counseling to people in weightcontrol and exercisetraining programs. Prerequisite: HEFN 340 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Nutrition Counseling Practicum
description: Students provide nutrition counseling for pregnant women, families with infants, young and teenage children, and people seeking guidance for weight control and special problems. Students are supervised by a member of the American Dietetic Association. Prerequisite: HEFN 340 and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Food Service Management Practicum
description: Experience in a food service organization, either in the private or public sector. Emphasizes development of food management expertise. Practicum approved and supervised by the Department of Home Economics. Prerequisite: HEFN 360, 364; senior standing; permission of department chairperson; and documented completion of at least 500 hours of appropriate foodservice experience.

title: Seminar in Foods and Nutrition
description: Student presentations and discussions on specific topics of current interest in foods and nutrition. Prerequisite: senior standing; permission of department chairperson. HOME ECONOMICS: HUMAN SERVICES (HEHS)

title: Family Wellness
description: Investigates the physical, mental, and social aspects of wellness, focusing on their interaction with the individual, family, and community.

title: Life Management
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Practical application of management principles to daily experience. Open to all students.

title: Energy and Equipment in the Home
description: The study of energy and equipment in the home. Current legislation, methods of conservation, cost and energy concerns of the future. Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Demonstrations by instructor, students, and guests.

title: Infant Development
description: Growth and development from conception through the second year of life. Includes physical, social, emotional, and cognitive aspects of development. Students observe and interact with infants and toddlers. Open to all students.

title: Child Development
description: Emphasis on the preschool child as a member of a family group. Includes principles of natural growth and development and child guidance based on the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual needs of the preschool child. Students will participate in and observe various early childhood programs and centers. Open to all students.

title: Home Management
description: Practical applications of the principles of life management. Prerequisite: HEFN 220. Prerequisite or parallel: HEHS 340.

title: Problems in Consumer Buying
description: The economic aspects of purchasing including marketing conditions, consumer credit, agencies that protect the consumer, and points to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Marriage
description: The dynamics of the marital relationship and the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasizes the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection, marital communication, sexual adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of department chairperson.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasizes marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of department chairperson.

title: Functional Home Design Practicum
description: Gives the student onthejob work experience with professional supervision in functional home design. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Family Relations
description: History and recent trends and developments in familylife education, career opportunities involved in familylife education, professional organizations, and ethical standards. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson and senior standing. HOME ECONOMICS: MERCHANDISING (HEMER)

title: Introduction to Clothing
description: Basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, the apparel industry, and social and psychological aspects of clothing.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Creative skills in stitchery used to embellish existing fabrics or to create new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, and needlepoint; rya, braided, and hooked rugs. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HEMER 104 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Consumer Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, aesthetic qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Textiles
description: Textiles and their components as they relate to care, performance, and consumer satisfaction. Open to all students.

title: Evolution of Costume
description: A study of Western costume from its beginning to the present. Emphasis on motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Prerequisite: HEMER 230 or permission of department chairperson.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: A survey of the business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, and promotion. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adapting standard patterns to individual proportions, designing garments, and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Use of computeraided design to produce pattern for original garment. Prerequisite: HEMER 104, 203.

title: Household Textiles
description: Raw materials, quality, performance, and comparative cost of textiles used in home furnishing. Planning and conducting tests with household textiles and evaluating results.

title: Fashion Buying and Merchandising
description: Gives potential retailers the knowledge base to make decisions on buying and merchandising to satisfy customers and maintain an adequate profit level. Prerequisite: HEMER 270.

title: Computer-Aided Design for Apparel
description: Basic knowledge of the use of computeraided design (CAD) in fashion apparel designing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Merchandising Practicum
description: Participation in a supervised work experience in a professional setting related to the area of study. Prerequisite: HEMER 270 or 210 and 220, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Fashion
description: Problems and issues facing the modern fashion merchandiser. Working and consulting with fashion merchandisers. Wright Preparing students for challenging careers in industry and teaching is the major focus of the Department of Industry and Technology. Bachelor's degree programs in industrial technology, graphic arts management, industrial technology teacher education, and vocational teacher education prepare students for a broad range of such careers. Associate degree programs in manufacturing technology, printing technology, and industrial supervision offer students the opportunity to obtain solid technical and supervisory preparation in many types of career. Credits earned in associate degree programs in industry and technology will transfer to related bachelor's degree programs in the department. Internships in a wide variety of industries are available to students seeking a firsthand look at the daytoday operations of contemporary industries. Students enrolled in bachelor's degree programs in industry and technology may choose cooperative education programs after completing their freshman year of study. ASSOCIATE DEGREES ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE— MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY, 65 hours This associate degree program is designed to prepare people for positions as technicians in the manufacturing industries. Graduates of the program accept jobs as computeraided drafting technicians, manufacturing technicians, production planners, and technical representatives. The program is designed for those who are currently employed as well as those desiring to obtain employment in a technical position in manufacturing. title: Introduction to Woods
description: Basic course in wood processing for persons interested in consumer information related to wood products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for studentdesigned product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance.

title: Cabinetry Design and Fabrication
description: Application of design and fabrication principles as they relate to residential, business, and industrial cabinetry. Activities will include the design and detailing of typical cabinets and the construction and finishing of a studentdesigned product. Prerequisite: ADS 205 and ARCH 217 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance, and to make simple modifications and installations in plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climatecontrol systems of the home.

title: Building Diagnostics
description: Overview of building construction and energy systems, energy audit techniques, principles of heat transfer, and air movement. Field and laboratory work to include pressurization and remote heatsensing devices to measure energy loss in building systems and thermal envelopes. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify the student for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to persons currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes that provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Examines and evaluates methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Society and Technology
description: Provides an overview of the development, societal impacts, and future implications of technology. Course work is designed to address human abilities to integrate resources to solve socialtechnical problems.

title: Technical Communication Systems
description: The elements, relationships, and operations of technical communication systems. Major emphasis on communication systems with laboratory experiences in the design, production, and transmission of various messages.

title: Construction Technology
description: Focuses on construction and management practices used to design, engineer, and construct residential, commercial, industrial, and civil structures.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: Properties of ceramic, metallic, polymeric, and composite materials and techniques used to convert these materials into products.

title: Product and Structure Design
description: Introduces the design process and methodology used to create and transmit technical ideas using graphic methods. Major emphasis on technical designing, sketching, pictorial drawing, orthographic projection, charting and graphing, and reprographics as applied to developing products and structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150.

title: Energy Systems
description: Focuses on inputs, processes, and outputs associated with energy systems. Emphasis on the sources of energy; methods of controlling, converting, and transmitting energy; and the use of energyconversion systems.

title: Manufacturing Material Processing
description: Provides experiences necessary to develop essential competencies required to perform common manufacturing processes with ceramic, metallic, polymeric, and composite materials. Prerequisite: ITEDU 153.

title: Graphic Communication Systems
description: Focuses on visual communication media as a technical communication system. Major laboratory activities emphasize design, development, production, and dissemination of graphic messages. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154.

title: Transportation Systems
description: Focuses on powered transportation systems used to move people and goods. Emphasizes land, water, air, and space vehicles and transportation systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158.

title: Vocational Student Organizations
description: Emphasizes the implementation, maintenance, and evaluation of vocational student organizations.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Analyzes legislation in the light of past and present issues of vocational education and its function as a vital component of the educational system.

title: Exploring Industrial Technology Education
description: Teaching of contemporary industrial technology education as a career. Students learn about the development and kinds of industrial technology programs and engage in activities that emphasize the curriculumdevelopment process.

title: Constructing Structures
description: Comprehensive study of the activities involved in preparing to build, construct, and complete residential, commercial, industrial, and civil structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154, and 253 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Electronic Communication Systems
description: Introduces the principles, components, and operation of electronic communication systems. Emphasizes design production and transmission in telecommunication, informationprocessing, and acoustical systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150, 158.

title: Industrial Control Systems
description: Overview of the various methods used in controlling power in the industrial setting. Emphasis on the application of computers and other controlling devices and systems within the manufacturing, construction, communication, and transportation industries. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158, 357 or ITMFG 270.

title: Manufacturing Enterprise
description: Introduces students to the managed activities used to design, engineer, produce, and market products with additional emphasis on providing financial and personnel support for these activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154, 253.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by breakdown into jobs, tasks, and processes.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Examines and evaluates educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching JH/MS Technology Education
description: Problems in developing and implementing instructional strategies; preparing evaluation instruments; planning, specifying, and managing the physical environment; and establishing and maintaining a cooperative classroom environment. Topics developed in the context of junior high and middle school, and field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298.

title: Strategies for Teaching Technology Education
description: Involves development and use of problemsolving, studentcentered, cooperative group, criticalthinking, and experiential strategies for teaching technology education. Includes opportunities to develop instructional media and work with students' special needs. Topics are developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 395.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Technology Education
description: Emphasizes contemporary approaches to curriculum development and the preparation of instructional materials for use in industrial technology education. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in a public school setting. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298 and 395.

title: Industrial Research and Development
description: Focuses on the methodology and practices of technical research and development as conducted in an industrial setting. Laboratory activities allow students to perform basic tasks associated with product and process research and development. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 161.

title: Community Planning
description: Activities involved in planning communities. Emphasizes construction, demand, and site factors as related to developing housing, streets, utilities, schools, transportation systems, parks, shopping areas, and recreational centers for public needs. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154.

title: Technical Experiences in Material Processing
description: Development of advanced competencies in casting and molding, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing processes. Prerequisite: ITEDU 253.

title: Technical Experience in Communication
description: Development of advanced competencies in the graphic, photographic, and electronic areas of communication technology. Prerequisite: ITEDU 254, 357.

title: Design and Evaluation of Transportation Systems
description: Design and operation of transportation systems. Emphasizes technical aspects typical of transportation systems: control, guidance, suspension, propulsion, structure, and support. Prerequisite: ITEDU 258.

title: Study in Industrial Technology Education
description: Special investigation in industrial technology education on an independent basis. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis on state functions. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY: GRAPHIC ARTS/PRINTING (ITGRA)

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: A comprehensive study of the graphic arts industry that focuses on products, reproduction processes, materials, equipment, and graphic arts careers. Related areas of instruction include design, relief printing, photooffset lithography, screen printing, color reproduction, and finishing operations.

title: Relief Printing and Bindery
description: A general applications course in relief printing and basic bindery operations found in the graphic arts industries. Major areas of instruction include copy preparation, typesetting, camerawork, conventional and photopolymer platemaking, presswork, paper, and ink.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 1
description: Introductory course in photooffset lithography that includes planning and layout, copy preparation, phototypesetting, line and halftone camerawork, platemaking, presswork, and introduction to fourcolorprocess printing.

title: Screen Printing
description: Screenprinting process as it relates to the graphic arts and printing industry and as an auxiliary manufacturing process in other industries. Topics include products, materials, equipment, techniques, inksubstrate relationships, estimating, and product design.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 2
description: Study of contemporary applications of photooffset lithography in commercial printing and publishing. Reviews layout and planning, pasteup, camera, stripping, plates, and press. Emphasis is on camera, stripping, and single and multicolor press operations. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182.

title: Photography
description: Emphasizes camera types, exposure techniques, film characteristics and selection, blackandwhite and color film processing, printmaking, print finishing, and composition. Related areas include special photographic applications and introduction to color photography.

title: Typesetting and Copy Preparation
description: The use, operation, and application of machine principles and mechanisms as related to typesetting. Typography, copy preparation, and copyfitting are emphasized in addition to various methods of type generation.

title: Printing Estimating 1
description: Introduction to contemporary estimating practices. Emphasizes production planning, development of hourly cost and production rate standards. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 182.

title: Graphic Arts Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a graphic arts industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for printing technology and graphic arts management majors. Prerequisite: permission of cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Graphic Arts Practicum
description: Emphasizes internal or external placement in a graphic arts setting selected and approved by the department. Provides opportunities to integrate and expand on theory gained during course work. Prerequisite: ITG RA 180, 181, 182, 183, and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Quality Control in the Graphic Arts
description: Explores the basic professional practices of quality control for printed products. Focuses on instrumentation used in evaluating material and products, inspection and sampling techniques, manufacturing specification, analysis techniques, and control systems found in the graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITG RA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Commercial Printing
description: Studies the organization and production systems of commercial printing and publishing. Emphasizes management and production systems, quality control, material control, scheduling, and production specifications. Class organizes a system and manufactures production jobs during semester. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Color as it relates to photography with emphasis on additive and subtractive color processes, films, film processing, printmaking (additively and subtractively), measurement, design and composition principles. Prerequisite: ITGRA 286 or ADS 231 or JOURN 130 or equivalent.

title: Color Separation and Process Printing
description: Study of color reproduction procedures in the graphic arts industries. Emphasizes additive and subtractive processes of color, direct and indirect separation procedures, color measurement, registration systems, and quality control procedures for color reproduction. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182, 286, 387.

title: Colloquium and Senior Project in Graphic Arts Management
description: Study and application of concepts, issues, and technological developments unique to the graphic arts. Topics include flexography, computer applications, electronic pagination, color scanning, and intaglio printing. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385.

title: Printing Management
description: Examines planning, organizing, controlling, and motivation as they relate to managing a business. Emphasis is on human relations, decision making, problem solving, and coordination of management, sales, and production for successful management. Prerequisite: ITGRA 381, 385.

title: Printing Estimating 2
description: Sheetfed and web estimating. Emphasizes obtaining and interpreting of specifications, pricing for profit margin, preparing quotations, printingtrade customs, multicolor presses, and signaturerelated bindery operations; application of the computer to estimating. Prerequisite: ITGRA 288.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Productioncontrol systems used in contemporary graphic arts industries. Topics include organization, systems approach, decision making, production planning and control, purchasing, inventory control, quality control, work measurement, and cost analysis. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Technical Drawing and Print Reading
description: The theory and practice of basic production drawings and print reading. Topics include graphics language and design, instrumental drawing, lettering, geometric constructions, sketching and shape description, multiview projection, sectional views, pictorial views, dimensioning, fasteners, working drawings, and computer graphics.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Industries
description: Introduction to manufacturing and its managed activities of research and development, production, marketing, industrial relations, and finance in manufacturing industries. Laboratory experiences involve organizing, staffing, and operating a model manufacturing enterprise. Prerequisite or parallel: ENG 103; appropriate 100-level math course. Open to all students except teaching majors in industrial education.

title: Computer-Aided Drafting and Computer-Applied Technology
description: Introduces computer drafting using an interactive software package on a microcomputer. Word processing and spreadsheet software packages are used to prepare and analyze technical reports. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105 or equivalent.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing Productionrelated detail and assembly drawings in selected specialized areas and indepth study of geometric dimensioning. Topics include auxiliary views, cams, machine components, and welding drawings. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105.

title: Industrial Plastics
description: Study of industrial plastics processes and materials. Subjects will include injection molding, extrusion, blow molding, compression and transfer molding, thermoforming, rotational molding, dip coating and casting, decorating and finishing processes. Polymer chemistry is included. Laboratory activities for all processes. Prerequisite: CHEM 111.

title: Machine Tool Processing
description: Metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling and grinding machines, bandsawing, and EDM. Discussions include tool design, precision measurement, metallurgy, heat treating, and safety. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 108.

title: Manufacturing Materials
description: Study of tests used to characterize properties of ceramic, polymeric, and metallic materials and how material properties influence their use and manufacturing. Laboratory exercises involve testing procedures recommended by ASTM and currently used by industry. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 108; CHEM 111.

title: Applied Quality Control
description: Variables, procedures, and processes of total quality control within the manufacturing industries. Topics include instrumentation for material evaluation, attribute inspection and sampling, supervising for organizational quality improvements, and statistical control. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161; MATHS 181 or MGS 221.

title: DC Circuit Analysis
description: Study of theories, measurement, and applications of direct current. Topics include electron theory, components, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuit analysis, voltage and current dividers, electromagnetism, and mesh analysis. Laboratories include basic measurement in electric circuits using VOM and DVM. Prerequisite: MATHS 108 and PHYCS 110.

title: Automation and Computer- Integrated Manufacturing Systems
description: A comprehensive technical introduction to automation in manufacturing. Topics include flowline production, material handling, group technology, and flexible and computerintegrated manufacturing. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 362; MATHS 115 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Manufacturing Design with CAD
description: Emphasizes creating product and tooling drawings using a major computeraided design (CAD) system. Topics include twodimensional drafting, threedimensional wireframe and surface models, testing, dimensioning, flat pattern development, section and mass properties, and component libraries. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205 and 233.

title: Three-Dimensional Modeling
description: Theory of surface and solid geometric models with applications in the manufacturing industries. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 305; MATHS 161.

title: Programming Computer Graphics
description: Programming in FORTRAN and a graphics language such as Tektronix Interactive Graphics Language (IGL). Emphasis is placed on writing programs to create technical drawings and other graphical representations. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205 and a computer programming language.

title: Plastic Production Systems
description: Plastics processing with automatic production equipment. Emphasizes injection molding, extrusion, and thermoforming. Appropriate quality control and flowanalysis tests performed on production parts. Charts, graphs, and reports on products are prepared. Includes field trips to local plastics industries. Prerequisite: ITMFG 225, 325.

title: Advanced Plastics Mold Making
description: Designing and building automatic molds and dies for injection, extrusion, and compression molding. Ejection pins, water cooling lines, stripper plates, and interchangeable inserts included in the mold design and construction using automated machining equipment. Field trips to mold and die shops. Prerequisite: ITMFG 325.

title: Automated Machines
description: Theory and application of automated machines in the manufacturing environment. The laboratory focuses on the programming and operation of NC machine tools. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205, 233; MATHS 115.

title: Manufacturing Machine Tool Processing
description: Focuses on factors that influence the control of metal manufacturing processes. Laboratory activities emphasize the significance of locators, power requirements, feeds, speeds, microstructure, coolants, and other variables. Complex operations are covered on grinding, milling, EDM, and other multifunctional machine tools. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233.

title: Casting and Bending Metals
description: Flatposition welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work with tungsten inert gas (TIG) and metal inert gas (MIG) equipment. Emphasizes various casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Applied Mechanics
description: Applications of statics and dynamics. Strength of materials with applications to problems in manufacturing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 262; MATHS 161; PHYCS 110.

title: Fixture Design for Metal Machining
description: Study of fixture design and other partholding systems used with metal machining. Discussion of common problems associated with fixtures when machining. Laboratory activities reinforce design concepts. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Fluid Power: Hydraulic Systems
description: An overview of the fundamentals of hydraulic systems with a review of basic equations regarding force, pressure, area, velocity, horsepower, volume, etc.; component types and designs; simplified hydraulic circuitry analysis; and basic maintenance and troubleshooting procedures. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270, 335; MATHS 161.

title: Industrial Safety and Health
description: Study of the practices used to optimize a safe and healthful environment for industrial personnel. Includes the requirements of safetyand healthregulating agencies, and hazard recognition and correction.

title: Manufacturing Processes
description: A systems approach to the analysis and planning of manufacturing processes. A quantitative evaluation of the parameters influencing product quality. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161, 233; MATHS 115 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Manufacturing Operations
description: Focuses on analyzing product designs and the design, engineering, and operation of industrial production systems through classroom and laboratory activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 105 and 161.

title: Technology Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a manufacturingrelated position in industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for industrial and manufacturing technology majors. Prerequisite: permission of cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: AC Circuit Analysis
description: Studies the behaviors of inductors and capacitors under DC and AC, RLC circuits, series and parallel resonance, diodes and transistors, and power supplies and filters. Includes handson experience and project construction. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270 and MATHS 115.

title: Digital Electronics
description: Digital technology and its applications. Laboratory activities include digital circuit construction using mediumscale integration (MSI) and largescale integration (LSI) chips. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270.

title: Industrial Robots
description: The technology, applications, and management of industrial robots. Includes such topics as classifications, controls, sensors, programming, machine vision, robot workcell design, coordinates transformation, and feasibility study in robotics. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161, 270, 370 and computer programming experience.

title: Training and Development in Industry
description: Training and development in industry and their relationship to the job and the organization. Emphasizes skills needed to systematically plan, implement, evaluate, and revise training and development programs. Provides opportunities for practical application and practice.

title: Computer Design of Plastics Molds
description: Design of molds for plastics products by computer. Plastics flow analysis, cooling analysis, part shrinkage, and cost analysis using computer programs. Use of electroniccomponent and database catalogs. Prerequisite: ITMFG 305 and 325. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 1
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. May include mold making, materials testing, and equipment design. Prerequisite: ITMFG 326, 327.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 2
description: A continuation of ITMFG

title: Research and Development in Metals
description: Research and development of problems related to metals manufacturing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 333 and 334, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: Guest lectures on contemporary topics in manufacturing. Student presentations on capstone projects. Information and guidance in seeking employment in manufacturing. Prerequisite or parallel: ITMFG 473. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Manufacturing Controls
description: Studies the controls of manufacturing. Topics include cost estimation and control, manufacturing resources planning (MRP), justintime (JIT), group technology, production and inventory controls, statistical process control, management information systems (MIS), and other advanced control technology. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 301; MATHS 162 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Industrial Programmable Controls
description: Emphasizes programmable controls in industry. Topics include relay controls, programmable controller controls, and incremental motion controls. Laboratory activities involve control applications using motor control panel, programmable controller panel, and stepper and servo control trainers. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Microprocessor and Microcomputer Systems
description: The architecture, programming, interfacing, and applications of microprocessor and microcomputer systems. Laboratories involve programming in assembly codes for basic operations and interfacing applications. Prerequisite: ITMFG 371 and computer programming experience.

title: Electric Machines and Controls
description: Principles and applications of power transformers, DC and AC generators, and DC and AC motors; controls and testing of various machines. Laboratory experiments. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Projects in Computer-Aided Manufacturing
description: Individual project applying CNC, CAD, CAM, robotics, and other computerbased technology in manufacturing systems. Extensive laboratory work required. Prerequisite: senior standing. Parallel: ITMFG 463.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Study semiconductor devices, rectifiers, SCR, frequency conversion, digital and analog transducers, optoelectronics, operational amplifiers, and the industrial applications of these devices. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Industrial Electronics Fabrication
description: Focuses on printed circuit board design, development, fabrication, and production. Electronic inventory and component assembly are studied as they relate to the manufacturing process. Prerequisite: ITMFG 475 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Problems in Industrial Technology
description: Individual advanced study and experimentation in one or more of the areas of concentration: metals, plastics, design, or factory electronics. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Prerequisite: permission of department PURDUE UNIVERSITY—MECHANICAL

title: Production Drawing
description: Application of principles of engineering drawing to detail, assembly, design layout, equipment installations, and related drawings. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105.

title: Industrial Organization
description: Organizational structures, operational, financial, marketing, and accounting activities; duties of management, planning, control, personnel, safety, wages, policy, and human factors necessary for effective management.

title: Applied Statics
description: A study of force systems, resultants and equilibrium, trusses, frames, beams, shear and moments in beams. Prerequisite: MATHS 115; PUMET 160.

title: Materials and Processes 1
description: Structures, properties, and applications of metals, ceramics, and polymers commonly used in industry. Includes primary production processes as well as heat treatments and hot or cold working to meet varied commercial needs. Introduces metallurgy and environmental aspects.

title: Materials and Processes 2
description: Basic casting, welding, and joining processes. Foundry areas include patterns, cores, molding, melting, and cleaning. Presents basic arc, gas, TIG, and MIG welding methods as well as the metallurgy of welding processes.

title: Applied Engineering Computational Analysis
description: Computations with the electronic calculator. The factor label method of unit conversion of commonly used engineering (including metric) units. Construction, drawing, and use of engineering graphs for both descriptive and computational purposes. Introduces computer programming using the BASIC language with emphasis on development of skills.

title: Applied Strength of Materials
description: Principles of applied strength of materials primarily with reference to application. Prerequisite: PUMET 111.

title: Dynamics
description: Applied fundamentals of dynamic forces, including displacement, velocities, accelerations, work energy, power, impulse, momentum, and impact. Prerequisite: PUMET 111; MATHS 161.

title: Machine Elements
description: Applies theories and methods developed in statics, dynamics, and strength of materials to the selection of basic machine components. Develops the fundamental principles required for the selection of the individual elements of which a machine is composed. Prerequisite: CS 118; PUMET 211; 213.

title: Heat and Power 1
description: Principles of thermodynamics and fluid dynamics as applied to the conservation laws of mass and energy, prime movers, and power cycles. Prerequisite: MATHS 161; PUMET 160.

title: Fluid Power
description: A study of compressible and incompressible fluid statics and dynamics as applied to industrial hydraulic and pneumatic circuits and controls. Prerequisite: MATHS 161.

title: Manufacturing Processes
description: Manufacturing processes and tools used by industry to convert bars, forgings, castings, plate, and sheet materials into finished products. Includes basic mechanics of materials removal and forming, measuring, quality control, and safety of operations. Prerequisite: PUMET 141.

title: Small Unit Tactics and Operations
description: Introduction to troopleading procedures; mission, organization, and composition of basic military units; the conduct of offensive and defensive operations, and military first aid.

description: Introduction to drill and ceremonies, role of the noncommissioned officer, logistics, intelligence, the Soviet army, principles of war, and tactics. Prerequisite: MIL 202 or approval of department chairperson.

description: Analysis of leadership and management problems. Military tactics at squad and platoon level, military skills including advanced land navigation, and radio communications. Prerequisite: MIL 301 or approval of department chairperson.

description: Seminar on ethics and professionalism, discussion and practical exercises in preparing military correspondence and conducting briefings. Prerequisite: MIL 302 or approval of department chairperson.

title: Taking Command
description: Continued study of leadership with emphasis on duties of an officer; introduction to laws of war and military justice system; discussion of training management. Prerequisite: MIL 401 or approval of department chairperson.

description: An opportunity to investigate a topic of particular interest to the student under the supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. Wolfe The nursing program is designed to prepare students for careers as professional nurses and for graduate study. Graduates of the program are eligible to take the national licensure examination for registered nurses. Most classes and laboratories are offered on the Ball State campus or in nearby hospital and healthagency facilities. Access to a car is periodically required during clinical courses. Before enrolling in the nursing program, students must take about two years of academic work in humanities and behavioral and biological sciences. The major in nursing is concentrated in the junior and senior years. Admission to the nursing programs is by the selection process outlined in Baccalaureate Major Admission and Progression Policies. The process for registered nurses is outlined in Admission and Progression Policies for Registered Nurse Students. Both policies are available from the School of Nursing. Each applicant will be required to sign an informed consent form related to risks and safeguards involved with possible exposure to infectious diseases. An applicant with a record of substance abuse or conviction of violation of federal, state, or local laws related to controlled substances for any offense—misdemeanor or felony—may not be able to obtain licensure as a registered nurse. To enroll in the first clinical course, NUR 212, students should apply during the first ten class days of the semester before they want to enroll in the course. Applicants are ranked based on all attempted undergraduate credit, including all attempted transfer hours. Students who are not admitted can reapply. Clearance from the Health Center, which usually takes two to three weeks, is required before taking NUR 212. To be admitted to NUR 212, students must have completed 45 credits, including credit in ANAT 201, BIO 113, CHEM 101, PHYSL 210 and 211, PSYSC 100, SOC 100, MATHS 125, SPCH 240, and NUR 211. A grade of at least C is required in NUR 211, ANAT 201, PHYSL 210 and 211, BIO 113, and CHEM 101. The minimum acceptable grade in all required nursing courses is C. Repetition of a clinical nursing course is permitted only once and for only two courses. Students who fail to earn the minimum required grades in clinical nursing courses and satisfactory performance evaluations may be dismissed from the program. The National League for Nursing Diagnostic Readiness Test is required during the last semester of the senior year. Registered nurses who do not have bachelor's degrees can enroll in a baccalaureate program to complete their degrees. The program is designed for both fulland parttime students. It takes into account students' previous education and experience. The nursing program is accredited by the National League for Nursing.
