Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 130; PEFWL (PEG F) 100, 103, 104, 117, 148, 217. Physical Education 75

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic exercise routines performed to music. Includes a total of fifteen hours of lecture emphasizing a common core of knowledge concerning physical fitness, health, and related topics. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 148; PEFWL (PEGF) 100, 103, 104, 117, 130, 217.

title: Fitness Swimming
description: Designed to PHYSICAL EDUCATION: GENERAL (PEG)

title: Physical Conditioning
description: Designed to help students become aware of their present fitness status and to appreciate the role of physical exercise in everyday life. Students will engage in a program of exercise to maintain and increase physical fitness and aid in weight control. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 100.

title: Water Adjustment for Swimming
description: Phase one of a program designed to help the nonswimmer to become an efficient swimmer. Open only to students who cannot swim in deep water. During the regular school year (September through May) the course is administered as either a learning or a testout program. Students enroll at the aquatics office of the Lewellen Aquatics Center. After students meet the skillperformance standards, further attendance is not required and they may register for credit and grade in either the current semester or a future semester; however, registration must be completed at least two weeks before the end of the semester chosen. Summer students use the same procedures to register for swimming class as they do for other classes.

title: Fitness Walking
description: Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through brisk walking. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 103.

title: Jogging
description: Designed to increase cardiovascular fitness through jogging. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 104.

title: Adapted Physical Education
description: Intended for students with physical handicaps or limiting conditions that would prevent full and unlimited participation as determined by the University Health Service. Students consult with a physical improve cardiovascular and muscular endurance and stroke efficiency through swimming and land conditioning. Includes a total of fifteen hours of lecture emphasizing a common core of knowledge concerning physical fitness, health, and related topics. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 217; PEFWL (PEGF) 100, 103, 104, 117, 130, 148. education faculty member and are assigned according to their interests, needs, and qualifications. Regular course requirements are adjusted for the individual. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Tai Chi Ch'uan
description: Designed to teach basic skills and knowledge of Tai Chi Ch'uan and to increase physical fitness through Chi Ch'uan exercises.

title: Beginning and Intermediate Judo
description: Designed to give the student an appreciation of judo, both as a sport and an art. Emphasis on understanding basic judo techniques and the development of selfconfidence and selfdefense.

title: Beginning Karate
description: Introductory skills for enjoyment of karate.

title: Beginning Modern Dance
description: Basic skills of modern dance through movement techniques and creative projects.

title: Beginning Modern Jazz Dance
description: Understanding and skill in basic techniques and styles (cool, hot, blues, urban, primitive) of the jazz dance.

title: Swimnastics
description: Physical conditioning through water exercise, using high potential fitness activities that can be used in a small pool or in a limited area of a crowded instructional pool. Prerequisite: ability to put face in water, to float on front or back in shallow water, and to regain standing position after floating. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 117.

title: Beginning Tap Dance
description: Designed to teach the basic tap steps and combinations along with their rhythmic analysis and style to be used in composition. Intended for the student with no experience in tap dancing.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through yoga exercises and yoga relaxation techniques.

title: Bowling
description: Introductory and intermediate skills designed to give the student knowledge in bowling on a team or in a league, keeping league records and team standings, computing and figuring handicaps, and basic fundamentals.

title: Beginning Badminton
description: Introductory skills for playing singles and doubles badminton. Stresses basic strategy, rules, and courtesy.

title: Horsemanship
description: Schooling and work toward perfecting form in three gaits: walk, trot, and canter. Harness driving and stable management are also emphasized.

title: Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 128.

title: Bicycling
description: Bicycling techniques involving maintenance of equipment; city, open country, and endurance riding primarily to introduce the student to family bicycling for lifetime use. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 130.

title: Cross-Country Snow Skiing
description: Designed to teach the beginning skier the skills necessary to reach the more advanced level of crosscountry skiing. Takes the skier from short, closein trails to longer, more challenging trails offered at several Indiana state parks.

title: Distance Running
description: Designed for people who like to run for physical fitness. Students are expected to start at oneto twomile distances and progress to thirtyfive to forty minutes of running. Prerequisite: must be in condition to run two miles on first day. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 135.

title: Flag Football
description: Introduction to fundamentals and rules of football through flag football; instruction in techniques, terminology, strategies, and rules.

title: Beginning Basketball
description: Information, practice, and experience in basic skills, strategies, and knowledge. Course includes passing, shooting, dribbling, offense, and defense.

title: Fencing
description: Basic techniques, terminology, strategy, rules, and courtesies. Includes positions, footwork, parries, and lunges.

title: Volleyball
description: Provides the beginner with an understanding of rules and skills underlying optimal enjoyment for power volleyball.

title: Orienteering
description: Introduces the student to the activity of orienteering, a sport in which the participant uses such landnavigation skills as mapand compassreading. Circulorespiratory fitness is emphasized in distance running for time.

title: Beginning Gymnastics
description: Instruction in beginning skills leading to various stunts on balance beam, rings, pommel horse, horizontal bars, parallel bars, uneven bars, and vaulting horse. Prerequisite: PEG 107 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Weight Training
description: Development of a basic personalized program for building and maintaining strength for both general conditioning and activities.

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic exercise routines performed to music. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 148.

title: Individualized Physical Education
description: Limited to nontraditional students with special problems that may keep them from enrolling in conventional physical education classes. Registration is by permission of the department. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Swimming 1
description: Phase two of a program designed to help the student to become an efficient swimmer. During the regular school year (September through May) the course is administered as either a learning or a testout program. Students enroll at the aquatics office of the Lewellen Aquatics Center. After students meet the skill performance standards, further attendance is not required and they may register for credit and grade in either the current semester or a future semester; however, registration must be completed at least two weeks before the end of the semester chosen. Summer students use the same procedures to register for swimming class as they do for other classes. Open only to students who can swim in deep water.

title: Swimming 2
description: Students who are interested in advancing their swimming skills or are preparing to specialize in aquatics should consider this course. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Aquatic Lifeguarding
description: A preparatory course for students who are highly skilled swimmers and are interested in becoming lifeguards. The American National Red Cross certification in lifesaving can be earned in this course. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Lifeguarding Training
description: Lecture and laboratory experiences in the pool designed to make the student more knowledgeable about the job of the lifeguard. Includes the skills and knowledge necessary to earn the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training certification. Prerequisite: Current advanced lifesaving or WSJ certificate and current first aid and CPR certification.

title: Beginning Springboard Diving
description: Designed to assist the student in developing the basic skills used in dives from a onemeterhigh springboard. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Scuba
description: Techniques of using selfcontained underwater breathing apparatus and the scientific laws pertaining to the activity. Nationally recognized certification may be earned in this class. Special course fee required. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of the aquatics director.

title: Synchronized Swimming
description: Designed to introduce basic positions, swimming strokes and stroke variations, sculls for propulsion and support, figures and hybrid figures in shallow and deep water. Upon mastery of the fundamentals, the synchronized swimmer will perform a compulsory routine to music. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or intermediate swimming ability.

title: Basic Canoeing
description: An introduction to movement control of a canoe as a type of small craft. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Fitness Swimming
description: Designed to improve cardiovascular and muscular endurance and stroke efficiency through swimming and land conditioning. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson. Not open to the student who has credit in PEFWL 217.

title: Racquetball
description: Instruction in the basic skills, strategies, and knowledge required to play racquetball.

title: Intermediate Golf
description: Designed to offer the golfing student an opportunity to learn and practice the finer points of the game.

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 127.

title: Intermediate Hatha Yoga
description: Designed for the student wanting to perfect previously learned asanas and to learn new ones. Prerequisite: PEG 119 or permission of department chairperson. PHYSICAL EDUCATION: GENERAL—

title: Pocket Billiards
description: Assists the student in the rudimentary skills and knowledge of the sport. PHYSICAL EDUCATION: PROFESSIONAL (PEP)

title: Conditioning, Fitness, and Exercise
description: Designed to emphasize the role of fitness; introduction to various activity forms and principles that underlie the development of fitness and wellness programs. Prerequisite: any PEFWL course.

title: Practicum 1
description: An introduction to the classroom setting for physical education students. Emphasis on observation, exploration, and interpersonal skills.

title: Movement Exploration
description: Introduction to theories of movement and strategies to enhance creative teaching.

title: Computer Applications for Physical Education, Exercise Science, and Sport
description: Introductory course in computer data processing with special emphasis on problem solving in the disciplines included in the School of Physical Education. Students may substitute CS 104, EDGEN 320, or BEOA 225.

title: Gymnastics 1
description: Introduction to basic techniques and progressions in tumbling and apparatus.

title: Gymnastics 2
description: Personal technique development; safety, instructional strategies, and principles of movement. Prerequisite: PEP 157.

title: Studio of Contemporary Dance
description: Provides preprofessional experiences for dance educators. Through a variety of movement settings, the student learns to organize, plan, compose, and select appropriate accompaniment for individual and group presentations in educational settings. Prerequisite: PEG 115. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foundations and Principles of Physical Education
description: Introduction to physical education and the role of the physical educator with emphasis on the educational process. Not open to the student who has credit in PEP 390.

title: Folk Dance Studio
description: Designed to emphasize the different styles existing in folk dance. Introduces the elements of ethnic dance choreography. Prerequisite: PEG 112 or PEP 306. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Badminton and Contemporary Activities 2
description: Elements of strategy, skill, and methodology in badminton; leisure and current activities for curricular variety. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Tennis and Contemporary Activities 3
description: Elements of tennis skill, methodology, and strategy; continued exploration of various leisure and recreational activities. Prerequisite: PEP 173 or permission of the director.

title: Softball and Volleyball
description: Beginning professional preparation in volleyball and softball including skills, rules, strategies, and teaching methods.

title: Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: For allgrade and secondary physical education teaching majors only, PEP 215 or equivalent.

title: Volleyball
description: Beginning professional preparation course in volleyball including the basic skills, rules, and courtesies associated with the game.

title: Soccer and Contemporary Activities 1
description: Designed to introduce preprofessional students to the elements of soccer, strategy, skills, and methods of teaching; introduction to a series of recreational and leisure activities. Prerequisite: for allgrade and secondary physical education teaching majors only, PEP 185.

title: Basketball; Field Hockey or Wrestling
description: Designed for preprofessional students with elements of skill and methodology included. Student selects either field hockey or wrestling; all students participate in basketball portion.

title: Introduction to Sports Medicine and Athletic Training
description: Discussion of responsibilities and occupational opportunities in athletic training and sports medicine. Includes evaluation of the student's aptitude for this type of work.

title: Games and Activities for the Older Adult
description: Designed to acquaint the student with a variety of recreational activities suitable for the older adult. Prerequisite: any PEFWL course.

title: Beginning Swimming for the Physical Educator
description: Introduces the nonswimmer or novice to basic skills and strokes of swimming and diving. Not open to deep water swimmers.

title: Aquatics
description: Designed for all physical education majors. The entrylevel course to the aquatics minor program emphasizes basic performance techniques in swimming, diving, and aquatic skills. A Red Cross Emergency Water Safety certificate is available upon successful completion. Prerequisite: PEP 214 or successful completion of entrylevel skills test.

title: Introduction to Adapted Physical Education
description: Basic knowledge of disabilities that affect physical education. Emphasizes referral, placement, and programming in physical education; federal and state laws that pertain to the education and physical education of special populations. Students required to participate in field experiences.

title: Principles and Organization of Coaching
description: Considers the philosophies and principles underlying junior and senior high school athletic programs; organizational strategies include seasonal and administrative planning.

title: Coaching Observation
description: Guided observation of coaching techniques and practices with analysis of teaching and coaching philosophies for competitive sports in schools. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Practicum in Aquatics
description: An onsite experience in aquatics at Ball State or another approved aquatics program. Prerequisite: PEP 315 or permission of aquatics director. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Dance Composition 1
description: Principal elements of dance composition. Simple compositional forms for small groups and solo work. Prerequisite: PEG 115, PEP 307.

title: Lacrosse (Women's Game)
description: Introduction to an aerial game played on an outdoor field with a netted stick or "crosse" and a hard rubber ball. This team sport challenges the physical endurance and manipulative skills of the player.

title: Games and Activities for the Handicapped
description: Designed to make students familiar with games and activities commonly used with the handicapped. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Anatomy
description: Basic concepts of anatomy for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching.

title: Physiology
description: Basic concepts of physiology for students with concentration areas in physical education and coaching. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Kinesiology
description: The anatomical and mechanical principles of human motion. Development of the ability to analyze movement mechanically and anatomically. Prerequisite: PEP 292 and general studies mathematics requirement.

title: Sports Officiating
description: Officiating techniques in a variety of sports. Different sport emphasis by semesters. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum 1: Athletic Training
description: An introduction to the practical application of athletic training methods such as protective taping, basic emergency procedures, and basic injury evaluation. The student will also be assigned to an athletic training setting. Prerequisite: admission into athletic training program or permission of athletic training program coordinator.

title: First Aid
description: First aid as outlined by the American Red Cross, leading to standard certification. Designed for the student pursuing a major or minor program in the School of Physical Education. Not open to the student who has credit in HSC 250.

title: The Law and Sport Administration
description: Essential elements of administrative law, arbitration, antitrust law, collective bargaining, constitutional law, contract law, labor law, and tort law. Major emphasis on their effect on sport. Prerequisite: BL 260 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Marketing, Promotions, and Fund Raising in Sport Administration
description: Study of the characteristics of sport marketing, promotional planning, and fund raising. Focuses on the planning processes involved in marketing and promotions and establishes guidelines and strategies for fund raising. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Practicum 2
description: Laboratory and classroom course involving the study and implementation of instructional strategies, growth and development factors, teaching progressions, and basic movement patterns. Prerequisite: PEP 394 or 491.

title: Business and Finance in Sport Administration
description: Investigation of the business and financial aspects of intercollegiate, interscholastic, and professional sport. Emphasis on the aspects of business that directly affect budgetary and fiscal control of each of the levels of sport. Prerequisite: FIN 350 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Dance 1
description: Introduction to dance forms—basic styles, rhythms, technique. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 112.

title: Dance 2
description: Expansion of basic rhythmic activities, including technique, patterns, principles of movement, and instructional strategies. Prerequisite: PEP 306. Not open to the student who has credit in PEG 113.

title: Developmental Activities
description: Introduction to psychomotor activities (locomotor, nonlocomotor, manipulative) that are fundamental to the elementary curriculum and enhance middle school and upperlevel programs.

title: Evaluation in Physical Education
description: Measurement and evaluation in physical education with emphasis on underlying philosophy, tests, construction, and use of test results. Prerequisite: for allgrade and secondary physical education teaching majors only, PEP 157, 173, 179, 184, 185.

title: Teaching Physical Activity to the Older Adult
description: Designed to teach the student to recognize the characteristics of the older adult and to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate a program of physical activity based upon the special needs of the older adult. Prerequisite: PEP 212.

title: Advanced Aquatics
description: Swimming and rescue skills necessary to complete American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor, Lifeguarding Instructor, YMCA Basic 10 Aquatics, and YMCA Lifeguarding certifications. Special emphasis is placed upon a broad range of other aquatic experience and teaching methodology. Prerequisite: PEP 215 or PEG 204 or permission of aquatic director.

title: Wellness through Aquatic Exercise
description: Introduction to the objectives, format, and conduct of instructional endurance swimming and water exercise classes, with emphasis on participation and application of fitness and related concepts to selected aquatic activities. Prerequisite: PEP 215.

title: Assessment in Adapted Physical Education
description: Introduction to appropriate instruments for assessing the motor and fitness needs of the disabled in physical education. Practical experience in administering standardized and normed referenced tests. Students develop IEPs. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or 494.

title: Wheelchair Recreational Activities and Pursuits
description: Wheelchair leisure activities, including basketball, softball, bowling, table tennis, soccer, and others. Emphasizes rules and regulations. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of instructor.

title: Physical Therapy Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze "normal" motor performance. Prerequisite: PHYCS 110, 112; ANAT 330, 405.

title: Sports Information
description: Designed primarily for the sports information student. Develops the student's knowledge and background in the terminology, strategy, scoring, and officiating of a variety of sports. Not open to physical education majors.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Learning theories, teaching strategies, and physical laws that affect learning and performance in the water. Emphasis on analysis and technique. Prerequisite: PEG 201 or permission of department chairperson.

title: American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor
description: Opportunity for students to earn the American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certificate. Prerequisite: an unexpired American National Red Cross Advanced Lifesaving certificate.

title: Internship in Aquatics
description: Permits the student to receive credit for aquatic experiences in categories of leadership, administration, or operation of aquatic programs or facilities. Prerequisite: permission of aquatic director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 157.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 185 or PEG 110.

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the early grades of the elementary school.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and use of accompaniment in modern dance. Prerequisite: PEG 115; PEP 307.

title: Diagnostic Techniques and Athletic Injury Mechanisms
description: An introduction to predisposing anatomical, kinesiological, growthstress, and other problems that contribute to athletic injuries. Presents the procedures needed to accurately recognize and evaluate these problems and the extent of an athletic injury. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Athletic Training Modalities and Therapeutic Techniques
description: Introduces mechanical therapies, thermal therapy, cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, and therapeutic exercise. Considers only treatments and their clinical uses that are of value to the athletic trainer in attending to athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 396.

title: Methods of Teaching Sports
description: Methods, materials, and organizational techniques in selected team and individual sports. Prerequisite: junior or senior standing.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 177.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball or Softball
description: Offered alternating years as baseball or softball. Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 180.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 281.

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 185.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 179.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 184.

title: Motor Learning
description: Introduction to principles related to the teaching, learning, and performance of motor skills. Emphasis on the application of this knowledge to teaching and learning strategies for motorskill acquisition. Designed for undergraduate students who plan to teach motor skills to people in all age ranges. Prerequisite: for allgrade and secondary physical education teaching majors only, PEP 310.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children, emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, using task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: junior standing or permission of the director. A total of 3 hours may be earned.

title: Neurophysiological Approach to Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Designed to give the student an understanding of the theoretical basis of selected neurophysiological programs for treatment of various handicaps and to teach the student how to administer such programs.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: PEP 392.

title: Methods/Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the student to plan, implement, and evaluate an array of teaching strategies that would be used in creating a safe environment for a publicschool physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Practice of athletic training principles and techniques necessary for care and prevention of athletic injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or permission of the instructor.

title: Practicum 2: Athletic Training
description: A practical application of athletic training methods that includes techniques of therapeutic massage, modalities, and cadaver anatomy of the musculoskeletal system. The student will also be assigned as a student trainer for an intercollegiate team. Prerequisite: PEP 370 and 396.

title: Methods/Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed with both theory and practicum aspects. Comprehensive planning, instructional design, materials, strategies. Includes management, organization, evaluation, curriculum development. Laboratory experiences emphasized. Prerequisite: PEP 395, junior standing, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar
description: Capstone experience for the preprofessional including but not limited to curriculum development, current trends, futures in physical education. Prerequisite: PEP 391.

title: Instructor of Lifeguarding
description: Concerned with skills pertinent to teaching lifeguarding. All aspects of lifeguarding including techniques for pools and fresh and salt water beaches. Red Cross certification available upon completion of course requirements. Prerequisite: PEG 204.

title: Psychological Dimensions of Coaching
description: Designed for those interested in coaching. Focuses on the dimensions of sport psychology by review and study of pertinent scientific literature, the principles derived from this literature and their practical application.

title: Internship in Exercise Programs for the Older Adult
description: A practical experience in leading physical activities for older adults in healthcare centers, senior citizen centers, retirement centers, or other places where older adults engage in exercise. Prerequisite: PEP 212, 292, 293, 294, 299, 312; HSC 469. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Sports for the Disabled
description: Official sports organizations recognized by the United States Olympic Committee. Class emphasis placed on classifications, organizational structure, sporting events, coaching disabled athletes. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the instructor.

title: Instructor of Adapted Aquatics
description: Concerned with the methodologies used to teach swimming to exceptional individuals. Important for rehabilitation education, agency personnel, postgraduate swimming education, Y organizations, boys' clubs, community and industrial programs. Certification is available upon successful completion. Prerequisite: PEP 315 or 353 or current Red Cross Water Safety Instructor.

title: Coaching Internship
description: Students assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teachingcoaching process. May not be taken at the same time as student teaching. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Athletic Governance
description: Directed mainly toward the sportsinformation student. Designed to discuss the various organizations that govern amateur and professional sports in the United States. Emphasis on the sportsinformation student's role in shaping sports in this country and in international competition. Not recommended for physical education majors and minors.

title: Swimming Pool Operation and Maintenance
description: Emphasizes water circulation and filtration, chemical treatment for disease control, sanitation, and administrative procedures for personal safety.

title: Aquatic Facilities Management
description: Study of organization and administration designed to prepare the aquatic professional for management of indoor and outdoor facilities. Includes facility design, safety procedures, activity, sport, and recreational aspects of pools, lakes, camps, and beach fronts. Prerequisite: PEP 315 and 454.

title: Teaching Modern Dance in the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEG 115; PEP 307.

title: Mainstreaming in Elementary School Physical Education
description: Designing physical education programs to meet the requirements of Public Law 94-142, which mandates that each handicapped child have an individualized physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Practicum in Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Designed to give students practical experience in working with handicapped children in a physical education setting. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the program coordinator.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching Modern Athletic Programs
description: Explores the historical development of modern athletics. Students develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program and learn to deal with everyday coaching and administration problems. Prerequisite: satisfactory completion of 22 hours of undergraduate sport administration courses, ENG 231, JOURN 261, BEOA 241, and foundations of business minor (21 hours) and permission of department chairperson.

title: Teaching Physical Education to the Developmentally Disabled
description: A study of people with developmental disabilities, including mental retardation, learning disabilities, and emotional disturbances that affect motor performance. Considers the characteristics, limitations, and special needs of these people, with implications for selection of activities in physical education.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Movement experiences appropriate for elementary school children; planning, teaching and evaluating a developmental program.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the anatomical structures and physiological functions in man during acute and chronic activity. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294 or permission of the program director.

title: Teaching Physical Education for the Handicapped
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitation each causes. Physical education and recreational activities for each type. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training
description: Students receive athletic training clinical experience in an Indiana high school, sports medicine clinic, or other qualified facility. The student must work under the direct supervision of an NATA certified athletic trainer. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 372, and 396.

title: Practicum 3: Athletic Training Administration
description: An advanced course in the practical application of athletic training methods. Will emphasize problems, principles, and objectives in the designing, planning, and operation of an athletic training program. The student will be assigned as a student trainer. Prerequisite: admission into athletic training program or permission of the athletic training program coordinator.

title: Independent Study in Physical Education
description: An opportunity to investigate an area of particular interest to the student, under supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Foundations of Exercise Science and Wellness
description: An introduction to such topics as career opportunities; exercise and nutrition; lifestyle changes; related professional organizations and publications; physiological and psychological research; and other current information for wellness and fitness professionals.

title: Certification in Exercise Science and Wellness
description: Evaluation and introduction to practical, oral, and written skills in exercise science needed in the advanced program. Increased information to update individual portfolio for evaluation. This course is the prerequisite for all advanced program offerings. Prerequisite: EXSCI 190, PEP 292, 294, 299. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Foundations of Exercise Leadership
description: Emphasizes fundamentals to lead group exercise activities effectively, e.g., aerobic dance and strength training. Teaching methodology and statistics as they relate to wellness and fitness will be developed. Prerequisite: advanced program status and permission of program coordinator.

title: Exercise Leader Cooperative Education
description: A paid work and learning experience in the application of exercise leadership knowledge and skills to fitness and rehabilitation programs both in the public and private sectors.

title: Exercise Leader Internship
description: An indepth practical experience in the application of exercise leadership knowledge and skills to fitness and rehabilitation programs owned and operated by private and corporate businesses and municipal organizations. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Principles of Interpretation of the Electrocardiogram
description: Introduction to basic concepts of the electrocardiogram as it relates to fitness programs for apparently healthy and cardiacrehabilitative individuals. Includes information concerning the effects of prescription medications on the electrocardiogram. Prerequisite: EXSCI 301. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Practicum and Statistics in Exercise Science
description: Practical experience in conducting Human Performance Laboratory fitness tests, e.g., treadmill (submaximal), exercise blood pressure, lung capacity, blood cholesterol, etc. Includes introduction to basic exercise science statistics. Prerequisite: EXSCI 401. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors. College of Architecture and Planning R. Fisher, Dean; J. title: Environmental Design and Planning 1
description: Basic problem solving related to abstract and historical and contemporary problems in environmental design. Elements of space, form, function, and human use as they affect the natural and built environments.

title: Environmental Design and Planning 2
description: Basic problem solving related to abstract and historical and contemporary problems in environmental design. Elements of space, form, function, and human use as they affect the natural and built environments. Prerequisite: CAP 101.

title: Design Communications Media 1
description: Methods for environmental design communications in a variety of media.

title: Design Communications Media 2
description: Methods for environmental design communications in a variety of media. Prerequisite: CAP 161.

title: Introduction to Architecture, Landscape Architecture and Urban Planning
description: A twoweek workshop in environmental design and planning, including lectures, field trips, and handson studio experience. Open only to high school juniors enrolled in the Honors College Summer Program.

description: Independent study in urban design, planning, landscape architecture, and architecture, offered in conjunction with the college's Community-Based Projects Program. title: Architectural Design

title: Structural Systems 2
description: Strength of structures and mechanics of materials, stressstrain behavior, modes of failure applied to beams, columns, and trusses. Prerequisite: ARCH 211.

title: Interior/Environmental Design and Structural Systems
description: Gives the interior design student a basic knowledge of building structures and materials. Emphasis on establishing objective criteria for making and evaluating decisions related to interior space planning.

title: Interior/Environmental Climate Control, Acoustical and Plumbing Systems
description: Gives the interior design student a basic background of climate control, acoustical, and plumbing systems. Emphasis on objective criteria for making and establishing decisions related to interior space planning.

title: Architectural Internship
description: A sixmonth period of approved paid professional employment under the supervision of a licensed architect, as required for the bachelor of architecture degree. Simultaneous enrollment in the National Intern-Architect Development Program (IDP) is required. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Environmental Systems 1
description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of heating, ventilating, air conditioning, plumbing, and fire protection systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 210.

title: Environmental Systems 2
description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of electrical, luminous, and acoustical systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 371.

title: Architecture for Non-Architects
description: Honors colloquium in architecture designed to introduce the nonmajor to the architectural design process, the determinants of building form, an understanding of the built environment, current trends in architecture, and architectural history and architects. Not open to the student who is majoring in architecture.

title: Architectural Design
description: Organization and design of multipurpose architectural and related environments at all scales in response to a complex set of criteria. Investigation of architectural and urban design principles, theories, and philosophies. Prerequisite: ARCH 302. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one fiveweek summer session.

title: Architectural Design
description: Organization and design of multipurpose architectural and related environments at all scales in response to a complex set of criteria. Investigation of architectural and urban design principles, theories, and philosophies. Prerequisite: ARCH 401. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 5 in any one semester or term.

title: Architectural Design
description: Design of multiuse projects on multiplebuilding sites with emphasis on research, programming, and systems integration through detail design development. Additional emphasis on circulation and movement systems. Exploration of presentation media. Prerequisite: ARCH 402 and admission to fifth year by Faculty Design Review Panel. Architecture 89

title: Architectural Thesis
description: Development of a thesis idea plus an architectural project to test or verify the thesis design position. Includes design, comprehensive site, and building prototype analysis. Emphasizes project management and design development including all major technical systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 403, 452.

title: Construction Management
description: Research and analysis in construction management.

title: History of Funerary and Religious Architecture
description: Analysis of funerary and religious architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: History of Technology in Architecture
description: Analysis of historical buildings with emphasis on the development of materials, structural systems, and technological concepts and their effects on architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: History of Public and Commercial Buildings
description: Analysis of public and commercial buildings in the history of architecture and independent research. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Seminar and Independent Research in Architectural History
description: Analysis of historical buildings, complexes, and cities. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Philosophy of Architecture
description: Seminars and independent study in the background and development of prevailing philosophies of architecture, ideas in design, and how they evolved in contemporary architecture since the beginning of the twentieth century, concluding with their influence on the current practice of architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: History of North American Architecture
description: A survey of North American architecture and urbanism from its colonial beginnings to the present. Emphasis on European antecedents, transformation by American conditions, and the rise of a distinctly American architecture. Methods of dissemination of architectural knowledge and conflicting points of view. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: History of Architecture 3
description: Survey of the movements and major figures in architecture and design, from the late nineteenth century to the present, with consideration given to the social and cultural context of design ideas. Prerequisite: ARCH 224.

title: Region
description: Analysis of the development of architecture, planning, engineering (canals, railroads, roads, bridges), and industrial architecture in the Midwest from the frontier period through the twentieth century. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Architecture
description: Readings, group discussions, individual research, and investigation of topics in the history of architecture, preservation, planning, and landscape architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Historic Architectural Interiors
description: A survey of European and American interiors, interior architecture, furnishings, and decorative arts, highlighting cultural influences from antiquity to the present with emphasis on eighteenthto twentiethcentury examples. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Preservation
description: Survey of the philosophy, history, theory, and scope of historic preservation in Europe and America. Explores such principles of historic preservation as ethical questions, practice versus theory, standards, and performance criteria. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Preservation Planning
description: Planning, law, and economics for urban and rural preservation, restoration, and conservation. Emphasis on strategies for preservation and implementation at various scales: neighborhood, district, town, region, and state. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Documentation of Historic Sites and Buildings
description: Methods of recording historic sites and buildings using both written and graphic means. Assembling and preserving data on the physical condition and history of historic properties. Prerequisite: permission of program director. Not open to the student who has credit in ARCH 226, 227, 326, 327. Open only to historic preservation minors or by permission of program director.

title: Field Workshop in Preservation
description: Exercises in surveying and the use of state inventory forms, National Register material, and environmental impact studies. Includes field trips. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Historic Preservation Restoration and Adaptive Use Cost Benefits
description: Analysis of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure; suggested restoration and cost benefits and restoration costs. Prerequisite: permission of department

title: Historic Preservation Technology 1: Construction and Pathology
description: Analysis of materials and systems of construction used in historic buildings. Identification and diagnosis of causes of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure. Some laboratory sessions are integrated into program. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: admission to historic preservation minor and permission of program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Historic Preservation Technology 2: Conservation Methods
description: General conservation methods for historic buildings including an introduction to specific techniques and philosophies. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: ARCH 447 and permission of program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Architectural Design Internship
description: Preparation for the internship experience; supplements the experience gained during the internship and serves as the basis for evaluation of student growth. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Architectural Research
description: Experience in architectural inquiry: the contexts, definitions, and processes of design creativity; relationships to scientific and environmental design and behavior research; technologyrelated research; strategies in building and testing concepts, assumptions, hypotheses, empirical evaluation; methods and procedures. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Programming and Thesis Preparation
description: Problems, theories, and methods leading to development of individual and group requirements and their translation into conventional and nonconventional performance criteria. Programming of thesis project. Prerequisite: admission to fifth year by the Faculty Design Review Panel.

title: Professional Practice and Management
description: Problems, processes, and philosophies of architectural practice. Emphasis on applied organizational and management theories, processes, tools. Prerequisite: ARCH 450.

title: Architectural Aspects of Archaeological Field Work
description: Archaeological methods applied to architectural remains. Principles of stratigraphic excavation, dating methods, and techniques for surveying and recording; technical and comparative analysis of building elements for dating, interpreting, and reconstructing. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: History of Urban Form
description: Analysis of urban centers and city planning, emphasizing spatial organization, order, and philosophy of planning in architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 224.

title: Life Safety in Architecture and Environmental Design
description: Survey of topics relevant to life safety encompassing wind, fire, ground motions; environmental factors including noise, criminal activity, and home accidents; and matters pertaining to the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA). Prerequisite: senior standing.

title: Advanced Graphic Techniques
description: Advanced graphic explorations of architectural subject matter, stressing fullcolor rendering. Includes demonstration of paint mixing, shades and shadows, reflections and material indication with application of these techniques to individual studio projects. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Computer Graphics Applications in Architecture
description: Basic training in the operation of a stateoftheart interactive computer graphics system. Introduction to twoand threedimensional graphics techniques and their applications within professional practice. Includes handson practice and exploration of the special capabilities of the interactive graphics system. Prerequisite: CAP 381.

title: Independent Projects
description: Independent study in environmental topics. Prerequisite: approval of program proposal by the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: History of Renaissance and Baroque Architecture
description: An analysis of theoretical concepts, architects, and significant examples of Renaissance and baroque architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 429 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Psychological Aspects of Environmental Design
description: Review of attempts to discover rational methods of predicting and evaluating environmental design. Presents basic research and analysis methods from the designer's point of view. Lecture, studio, and field activities. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson for students with majors other than architecture or landscape architecture. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Landscape Architecture History 1
description: The history of landscape architecture from ancient times to 1800. Examples of landscape expressions of the humanenvironment relationship resulting in the conscious shaping of urban and rural landscapes, and the creation of such landscapes as parks, gardens, and urban plazas.

title: Landscape Architecture History 2
description: The history of landscape architecture from 1800 to the present. Emphasis on the North American humanenvironment relationship, its relationship to European antecedents, and other cultural parallels in landscape design. Prerequisite: LA 220.

title: Landscape Architectural Design Communications
description: Methods of landscape architectural design communications; integrates techniques of handdrawn and computer graphics, photography, and video. Prerequisite: CAP 162.

title: Environmental Systems
description: Qualitative investigations and analysis of landscape systems. Studies include the assessment of vegetation, climate, hydrology, soils, and subsurface geology as determinants of landscape architectural form; natural processes as they relate to the principles of landscape architectural construction.

title: Housing and Community Design
description: Design projects focusing on social, political, economic, cultural, and environmental issues as they relate to landplanning and site design for housing developments and residential communities. Prerequisite: LA 202.

title: Planting Design
description: Design problems focusing on the functional, ecological, and aesthetic use of plants in the landscape. Prerequisite: LA 301, 341; and BIO 112 or 216.

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 1
description: Principles and practices of landscape engineering. Emphasis on the techniques and applications of land surveying, earthwork techniques including grading and estimation, and principles of site drainage. Prerequisite: LA 270.

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 2
description: Principles and practices of landscape architecture engineering and construction with emphasis on landscape materials, structures, planting, and fabrication techniques. Includes design implementation techniques and construction documents. Prerequisite: LA 311.

title: Landscape Plants 1
description: The study of woody landscape plants, including plant identification and plant adaptation to urban and natural environmental conditions.

title: Landscape Plants 2
description: The study of herbaceous landscape plants including plant identification and landscape cultural requirements. Emphasis on both outdoor and indoor planets.

title: Regional Landscape Design
description: The application of principles of landscape architectural design to largescale landscape settings. Topics include land planning, visual quality management, and natural and cultural landscape resource management. Prerequisite: LA 302.

title: Urban Design
description: Design studio emphasizing the physical and sociobehavioral influences on the design of cities. Projects may focus on the design of new urban environments or the redesign and revitalization of existing urban centers. May include interdisciplinary studies. Prerequisite: LA 401 or permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Architecture Comprehensive Project
description: Analytical, conceptual, and design development processes applied to a comprehensive project in landscape architecture. Emphasis on guided independent design work based on individual initiative. Prerequisite: LA 403 and 451.

title: Special Design Studio
description: Design studio emphasizing special or unique topics in landscape architecture. Studio may be offered at oncampus or offcampus sites; may be part of an approved foreign study program. Prerequisite: permission of instructor and department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 3
description: Principles and practices of landscape engineering and construction. Emphasis on roadway and parking lot engineering, practices of storm Landscape Architecture 93 water management, and advanced grading. Prerequisite: LA 312.

title: Philosophy of Landscape Architecture
description: Readings, seminars, and lectures in the background and development of historic and contemporary philosophies of landscape architecture. Includes discussions of design and environmental issues, land use, and professional ethics. Prerequisite: LA 221 or permission of the instructor.

title: Park and Recreation Planning and Design
description: Lectures, case studies, and readings related to the interdisciplinary role of the landscape architect in park and recreation planning, design, administration, and maintenance. Prerequisite: LA 202 or permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Operations
description: Techniques and practices of landscape grounds development and maintenance. Topics may include plant growth, development, and evaluation; plant and turf installation; pruning, irrigation, and landscape management plans. Prerequisite: LA 341 or permission of the instructor.

title: Interior Landscape Design
description: Techniques and practices of interior planting design, development, and maintenance. Topics may include environmental conditions affecting plant growth, principles of interior planting design, and interior plant management. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Architecture Research
description: Methods, procedures, and case studies of landscape architectural research. Includes guided development of an individual research program and proposal leading to the landscape architecture comprehensive project (LA 404). Prerequisite: LA 403.

title: Professional Practice
description: Methods and practices of the profession of landscape architecture. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics. Prerequisite: LA 302 and 368 or 369.

title: Landscape Architectural Design Communications 2
description: Advanced methods of landscape architectural design communications using a variety of media. Prerequisite: CAP 162.

title: Portfolio Preparation
description: The preparation of résumés, portfolios, and brochures related to securing internship positions and other landscape architectural employment.

title: Environmental Impact Analysis
description: Review of the environmental design arts and their implications relative to proposed actions that affect the environment. Covers procedures and methodologies used in impact analysis and documentation. Prerequisite: LA 302 or permission of the instructor.

title: Computer-Aided Landscape Design
description: Twoand threedimensional computeraided design techniques with emphasis on site design, master planning, and regional landscape design. Incorporates microcomputer or mainframebased CAD systems. Prerequisite: CAP 162 or permission of the instructor.

title: Independent Projects
description: An independent study in environmental topics. Prerequisite: approval of program proposal by faculty advisor, professor responsible for study assessment, and department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Urban Planning and Development

description: Site analysis and design principles for smallscale urban projects, including building complexes, subdivisions, and neighborhood development. Students present and defend designs for specific site locations. Prerequisite: PLAN 201.

title: Urban Impact Analysis
description: Techniques for estimating the environmental, socioeconomic, fiscal, and energy impacts of proposed plans and development projects.

title: Housing and Community Development

title: Urban Transportation Planning
description: Transportation planning methods and policy, including analysis of travel demand, links between land use and transportation, choice of transportation modes, and design of balanced transportation systems.

title: Environmental Planning

Palomba, G. Santoni, L Spector, D. Yoho, A. Zegeye All societies face a conflict between unlimited desires for higher living standards and limited resources to satisfy these desires. Economics studies how societies resolve this conflict. Because many of our nation's social, political, and economic problems can be traced to this conflict, a knowledge of economics is important not only for intelligent citizenship but also for careers in business, government, and the professions. The Department of Economics offers a major with a business option and one with a liberal arts option. The business option is designed primarily for students planning to pursue professional careers in business. The liberal arts option is designed for students wanting careers as professional economists. A minor in economics is also available. The department also offers an interdepartmental major in mathematical economics; for information on this major, see Interdepartmental Programs, p. 35. Students may also select economics as a concentration area in either the teaching major or the teaching minor in social studies. Some of the topics studied are consumer buying and the use of credit, banking, insurance, investment, budgeting, and taxation. Not open to juniors and seniors majoring in business.

title: Money, Banking, and Financial Institutions
description: The role of money, credit, and financial institutions in the U.S. financial system; deposit creation; the structure and functions of commercial banks, financial institutions, and their regulatory agencies; domestic and international aspects of monetary policy; competition and regulation of financial institutions. Prerequisite: ACC 201; ECON 202.

title: Principles of Finance
description: Designed to study different areas of financial decision making in a business firm. Specific topics include financial objectives of the firm, sources of funds, working capital management, capital budgeting, investment decisions under uncertainty, valuation, capital structure decisions, and dividend policy. Prerequisite: ACC 202; ECON 201; MGS 221; and junior standing.

title: Theory of Finance
description: A course devoted to the study of the current theory of finance. Topics include the nature and methodology of finance, efficient market hypothesis, portfolio theory and market equilibrium, optimal investment and financing decisions under certainty and uncertainty. Prerequisite: FIN 350.

title: Principles of Investments
description: Designed to introduce the student to areas of investment: securities markets, transaction of stocks and bonds, valuation and timing, fundamental and technical indicators, money markets, and funds. Prerequisite: FIN 350 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Financial Markets and the Economy
description: Nature and functions of financial markets; classification and interrelation of domestic and international financial markets; determination of the level and structure of interest rates; impact of monetary policy on financial markets and the economy. Prerequisite: FIN 250, 350.

title: Internship in Finance
description: Professional practice during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a banking institution, business firm, or government agency for pay under the supervision of the finance department. Requires periodic written reports of job experience. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in combination with FIN 481.

title: International Finance
description: The financial problems and opportunities that confront the management of international firms. Sources and instruments of international finance, import and export financing, interrelationship of governmental and international agencies, and the current status of some. Prerequisite: FIN 350 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Theory
description: An indepth analysis of valuation theory, capital market theory, and portfolio theory. Prerequisite: FIN 350, 355.

title: Managerial Decision Making in Finance
description: A summary course devoted to the compilation of knowledge and the application of financial analysis to decision making in various subareas of finance. The course is structured on the casestudy approach. Prerequisite: FIN 354.

title: Operations of Financial Institutions
description: To integrate the various topics of finance with a view toward applications to the management of financial institutions in the following decision areas: assetliability management, cost control, profitability, capital adequacy, business development. Cases will be integrated in the method of instruction. Prerequisite: FIN 354, 355, 356.

title: Finance Practicum
description: Professional practice (for no pay) during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a banking institution, business firm, or government agency, under the supervision of the finance department. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in combination with FIN 369.

title: Independent Study in Finance
description: Designed for academically qualified students who want to study some phase of finance. An intensive individualized program of reading, researching, or analyzing various finance topics under the guidance of a faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles of Insurance
description: A survey of the major kinds of insurance, such as fire, transportation, casualty, health, life insurance, and fidelity and surety bonds. Finance 115

title: Fundamentals of Life Insurance
description: Important methods of handling personal risks for business and individuals. An analysis of life insurance, annuities, pension plans, and social insurance. Special attention is given to the problems of underwriting, rate computation, and programming. Prerequisite: INS 370.

title: Legal Aspects of Insurance
description: The law as applied to the insurance industry, emphasizing the law of torts as the foundation of the insurer's liability, the law of contracts and agency as applied to the insurance policy, and government regulation of insurance. Prerequisite: BL 260 and INS 370.

title: Fundamentals of Liability Insurance
description: The study of liability insurance and worker's compensation insurance with special emphasis on the insurance needs of the commercial enterprise. Prerequisite: INS 370.

title: Fundamentals of Property Insurance
description: The study of property insurance, including fire and allied lines, inland and ocean marine, and crime insurance with special emphasis on the insurance needs of the commercial enterprise. Prerequisite: INS 370.

title: Current Topics in Insurance
description: Designed to meet the needs of advanced insurance students for study of current topics and problems in any insurance or risk management area. Topics may include nofault, competitive rating laws, variable life insurance, and state vs. federal regulations. Prerequisite: INS 370, 371, 375, and 376 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Insurance
description: Designed for academically qualified students who want to study some phase of insurance. An intensive individualized program of reading, research, or analyzing various insurance topics under the guidance of a faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Real Estate Principles
description: The economic import of real estate, real estate characteristics, land use and environmental controls, legal aspects of real estate, methods of valuation, mortgage credit sources, secondary mortgage markets and financing techniques, investment analysis, land development, and real estate operations.

title: Real Estate Finance
description: The contractual nature and legal implication of the instruments used in real estate finance; instrument, techniques, and strategies in the financing of real estate investment; and the structure and operation of both primary and secondary mortgage markets. Provides the student with background in real estate law and real estate finance. Prerequisite: RE 330.

title: Legal Aspects of Real Estate
description: Elementary concepts of real estate law and practice, particularly in the state of Indiana. Other topics include estates, property, leaseholds and ownerships, easements, transfers, escrows, contracts, zoning, brokers' regulations, license law, and title insurance.

title: Real Estate Analysis
description: The appraisal of real estate. In addition to the appraisal process, other analytical systems will be reviewed as they apply to the real estate industry, including the economic base analysis, feasibility studies, and investment analysis. Prerequisite: RE 330.

title: Real Estate Administration
description: An orientation of the real estate business using test cases, incidents, and walking cases. Guest speakers who are experts in real estate will be invited to speak and answer questions. Prerequisite: RE 431 and senior standing or permission of department DEPARTMENT OF MANAGEMENT SCIENCE J. Gupta, Chairperson; N. Ahmed, I. Baird, J. Green, T. Harris, J. Hornsby, D. Kuratko, W. LaFollette, M. Lyles, R. Montagno, I. Seeborg, J. Swart, E. Tunc, J. Walters Among modern organizations, there is a need for competent managers who can address emerging issues in a global economy. Dealing with environmental complexity, technology, employee productivity, international competition, and ethical issues is increasingly important in the managerial decision process. Programs leading to a bachelor of science degree in management are designed to give students the knowledge and skills in the latest concepts, tools, and techniques applicable to entrepreneurship and small business, human resources management, management information systems, production and operations management, and general management. Students can elect to specialize in one of the following five options: The production and operations management option prepares students to assume positions of responsibility in the production of goods and services. Students are introduced to the production functions in detail, are taught the methodology of making productionrelated decisions, and become acquainted with modern techniques used in motivating and leading personnel in a productionoriented occupation. The human resources management option prepares students to improve the effectiveness of employees in organizations. Students study the personnel function and learn the conceptual framework for analyzing and solving problems in the selection, development, and motivation of human resources. The management information systems option introduces students to the concepts and techniques necessary to use information in the support of operations, control, and planning in organizations. Graduates of this option are familiar with the concepts and techniques of computerized information systems. The entrepreneurship and small business option is designed to give students the knowledge needed to work in a smallbusiness environment. Students learn how to formulate a plan for a small business and how to implement that plan. They become acquainted with elements of managementinformation systems and business law that are tailormade for small businesses. Students also have the opportunity to assist small businesses as consultants in team practicums. The general management option acquaints students with the whole gamut of management: production, personnel, management information systems, and other management topics.
