title: Management Principles
description: Introduction to the basic concepts and principles of management. Focuses on structures within companies and processes within firms to bring principles to bear on the practical problems of managing organizations. Not open to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Business Application Programming
description: Basic COBOL and programming skills using illustrative examples, exercises, and topics that emphasize applications in commercial data processing. Prerequisite: BEOA 210 or CS 116. Not open to the student who has credit in CS 210.

title: Business Statistics
description: Introduction to various statistical and probabilistic concepts and techniques with application to business problems including random variables and probability distributions, measures of central tendency and dispersion, testing of hypotheses, simple linear regression, and correlation. Prerequisite: MATHS 132 or its equivalent. Prerequisite recommended: BEOA 210. Not open to the student who has credit in MATHS 181.

title: Introductory Operations Management
description: Introduction to the tools and techniques of management with practical applications to the production of goods and services. Prerequisite: MGS 200. Not open to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Personnel and Supervision
description: Introduction to the personnel and supervisory functions in organizations. Focuses on employee and union relationships; environmental, business, and social responsibilities; and leadership and supervision techniques, especially for the firstline supervisors. Prerequisite: MGS 200. Not open to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Principles of Management
description: Explores management principles, theories, and practices. Discusses current and emerging managerial topics including ethical decision making, international environment and organizational behavior, elements of leadership, motivation, communication, human relations, and group dynamics. Prerequisite: junior standing. Not open to the student who has credit in MGS 200.

title: International Management
description: Discussion of management issues relating to doing business in an international context, including moving a firm into international competition, and some issues that may be anticipated. Topics covered include exporting, joint venturing, or licensing as options for global expansion. Prerequisite: MGS 300 or equivalent.

title: Job Search and Transition
description: Prepares students for moving from college to careers. Topics covered include defining career goals, writing résumés, jobsearch correspondence, interviewing, and initial adjustments in the first job position. Open to juniors and seniors in all majors.

title: Information System Concepts and Techniques
description: Introduction to various concepts and techniques of information systems with application to solving managerial problems. Topics covered include information flows, application_of computerbased information systems, managerial decision making, and mutual influence of organizations and information systems. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221, 300.

title: Quantitative Business Analysis
description: Exploration and application of selected quantitative techniques to business problems. Topics covered include regression and correlation, analysis of variance and contingency tables, decision analysis, linear programming, and networkbased management techniques. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221.

title: Operations Research
description: Basic operations research concepts and techniques for managerial decisions including linear programming, network problems, decision analysis, and computer implementation of these models to solve practical problems. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221; MATHS 132.

title: Small Business Venture
description: Provides essential knowledge for students interested in small business including search for venture opportunities; economic, technical, and operational feasibility of ventures; financing, marketing, and legal operations; and franchising and partnering. Prerequisite: MGS 300.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: Development and management of an entrepreneurial organization including prestartup, startup, survival, growth, and the transition from entrepreneurial to professional management. Explains the function of entrepreneurship and corporate entrepreneurship. Prerequisite: MGS 341.

title: Introductory Production Management
description: Various functional fields of production and operations management including product analysis, work design and measurement, forecasting, production planning, scheduling and inventory control, facility location and layout, material handling, plant safety and maintenance, and quality control. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221, and 300.

title: Production Management in Service Sector
description: Various techniques for the design, operation, and control of service operations including service design and process selection, facility location and layout determination, staffing, equipment selection and operations, and scheduling of service operations. Prerequisite: MGS 351.

title: Managing Human Resources
description: Administration of personnel programs in business organizations so as to deal effectively with such problems as selection, training, compensation, promotion, and transfer of workers; working conditions; employee services; and industrial relations. Prerequisite: MGS 300.

title: Management Science Internship
description: Job experience (paid) in an organization with an approved innovative management program. Requires periodic written progress reports that will be evaluated by the assigned faculty member and the intern's supervisor. Topic selected will depend on student's option. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours may be earned including MGS 399.

title: Organizational Behavior
description: Dynamics of human behavior in business organizations with emphasis on problems of motivation and leadership. Examines the behavior of individuals and groups within organizations and the practical interpretation and management of behavioral phenomena. Prerequisite: MGS 300.

title: Business and Society
description: The interrelationships between business and its external environment and the multiple and complex ways business organizations are affected by governmental and societal expectations. Emphasizes contemporary issues through discussions and case analysis. Prerequisite: MGS 300.

title: Honors Colloquium: Readings in Contemporary Business
description: Seminar involving study of contemporary business literature. Interdisciplinary approach, comparing and contrasting ideas, deriving common themes, and drawing links to theory embodied in readings. Prerequisite: junior standing in College of Business and completion of "rule of nine." Open only to Honors students; others may enroll by permission of department chairperson.

title: Management Science Practicum
description: Professional practice (unpaid) in an organization with an approved innovative management program. Required periodic written progress reports that will be evaluated by the assigned faculty member and the intern's supervisor. Topic selected will depend on student's option. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned including MGS 369.

title: Problems in General Management
description: An integration of general management principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic and complex managerial problems in public and private organizations. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGS 341, 351, 361, 415, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Business Systems Analysis and Design
description: Various systems analysis and design concepts and techniques, including the key steps in the systemsdesign and development cycle. Emphasizes the consideration of practical applications within the business environment. Management Science 119 Prerequisite: MGS 311 and proficiency in a programming language.

title: Database: Sructures and Management
description: Logical and physical organization of data. Data description, command, and interrogation languages. Examines function of databases in information systems. Prerequisite: MGS 311 and proficiency in a programming language.

title: Information Systems of Small Business
description: Computerbased information systems in small business operations without access to an internal specialist. Includes the identification of information requirements and the use of mainframe and microcomputers and purchased software to satisfy the information needs in small business. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 341.

title: Information Systems Management
description: Equipment selection, equipment acquisition, computer operations management, project management, computer personnel management, financial control, systems security and control, and the relationship of the information systems function to an organization. Prerequisite: MGS 311 and senior standing.

title: Business Data Communications
description: Concepts and problem of transmitting, communicating, and managing business data needs through the use of computerbased telecommunication systems. Includes applications of integrated and distributed systems to problems in various functional areas of business. Prerequisite: BEOA 210, MGS 311, and proficiency in COBOL programming.

title: Problems in Information Systems
description: An integration of various information systems principles, theories, and techniques for implementing information systems in organizations, including strategic issues. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGS 351, 412, 415, 417, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Systems Simulation
description: Concepts and techniques of system modeling and simulation using computers. Includes computer simulation languages, statistical aspects of simulation, and application of computer simulation to various practical business situations in manufacturing and service sectors. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221, 351.

title: Small Business Practicum
description: Teams of students consult with local small businesses recommended by the Small Business Development Center. Students work on problems in such areas as accounting, production, marketing, personnel, finance, insurance, law, or information systems. Prerequisite: MGS 346.

title: New Venture Creation
description: Advanced smallbusinessmanagement entrepreneurship. Requires thorough research project culminating in the development of a finished plan for a smallbusiness venture to be approved by an outside board of professional experts. Prerequisite: MGS 346, 351; FIN 350; MKG 300; completion of all management core courses; senior standing.

title: Operations Planning and Inventory Management
description: Operations planning and inventory management in manufacturing and service industries, including capacity planning, resourcerequirements planning, productionactivity control, and related management models and systems. Prerequisite: MGS 321, 351.

title: Computer-Integrated Production and Operations Management
description: Current and emerging developments in computers and related technologies that affect manufacturing and service operations. Topics covered include flexible manufacturing, computeraided operations management, justintime concepts, and automated service operations and their managerial implications. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221, 351.

title: Quality Assurance
description: Study of assuring, controlling, and managing quality of goods and services, including the application of statistical techniques to problems of planning, feedback, and enhancement of process performance and operation effectiveness. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGS 221, 351.

title: Problems in Production and Operations Management
description: An integration of various production and operations management principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic operationsmanagement problems in manufacturing and service sectors. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGS 433, 453, 454, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Compensation Administration
description: Reviews basic compensation issues including internal, external, and individual equity, as well as benefits administration. Emphasis on design and implementation of compensation systems. Prerequisite: MGS 361.

title: Personnel Planning and Selection
description: Focuses on organization and manpower planning, including determination of organization and manpower needs, analysis and development of job requirements, and necessary qualifications for recruitment and selection procedures, placement and orientation, and evaluation of selection programs. Prerequisite: MGS 321, 361.

title: Problems in Personnel Administration
description: An integration of various principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic and complex personnel administration problems in public and private organizations. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGS 351, 461, 465, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Business Policy and Strategic Management
description: Integration of various functional areas of business. Development and administration of strategy and policy in private and public sector organizations. Case studies focus on strategic decisions that enable an organization to relate effectively to its industrial, national, and international environments. Normally taken during the last semester of the student's program. Prerequisite: senior standing; FIN 350; MGS 300; and MKG 300.

title: Colloquium in Business Policy
description: An honors colloquium in business policy studying advanced topics in industry, competitor, and firm analysis; critical thinking; analytic techniques; and strategy formulation culminating in required participation in the College of Business undergraduate case competition. Prerequisite or parallel: MGS 491. Open only to College of Business senior Honors students or College of Business seniors with a 3.0 or higher G.P.A.

title: Special Topics in Management Sciences
description: Exploration of special topics in management science of interest to faculty and students. May be repeated for credit with different topics. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Independent Study
description: Supervised study of some phase of management. May consist of an experiment, library research, or an analysis of current management practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Management Science
description: Explores current problems, theory, research, and trends in the management field. Will vary depending upon the current status of managerial research, the instructor, and the needs and interests of the students. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. title: Retail Merchandising
description: An introduction to the retail industry with a concentration on the merchandising activities of buying, selling, pricing, and inventory control. Prerequisite: GBA 101. Not open to the student who has credit in MKG 300 or to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Salesmanship
description: Fundamentals of retail, wholesale, outside, and service selling. Emphasizes sales approaches, presentation, closings, and postsale service. Prerequisite: GBA 101. Not open to the student who has credit in MKG 300 or to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Retail Advertising
description: Introduction to advertising with emphasis on the preparation, appeal, and media selection of retail advertising. Prerequisite: GBA 101. Not open to the student who has credit in MKG 300 or to the B.S. or B.A. candidate for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Principles of Marketing
description: Examines marketing as a productive system within our economy. Studies promotional activities, product policies, retail and wholesale activities, pricing policies, international marketing, and the role of marketing in society. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and junior standing or permission of department chairperson.

title: Honors Principles of Marketing
description: Principles of marketing for honors students. Examines marketing as a productive system within our economy. Substitutes for MKG 300. Prerequisite: ECON 201, junior standing; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Consumer Behavior
description: Practical business implications of the various aspects of consumer motivation and behavior. The student is provided with information to understand how and why a buyer reacts in a purchasing situation. Prerequisite: junior standing. Parallel recommended: MKG 300.

title: Advertising Management
description: Use of advertising as a communication tool in marketing management. Analysis of media selection, production and layout, measurement of effectiveness; and social and economic aspects of advertising. Prerequisite: MKG 300. Prerequisite recommended: MKG 310.

title: Professional Selling
description: Detailed introduction to and application of the principles of personal selling as applied to persons pursuing any vocation, as well as those aspiring to careers in marketing. Prerequisite: MKG 300. Not open to the student who has credit in MKG 327.

title: Sales Management
description: Policies and practices in organizing, recruiting, selecting, training, compensating, and controlling the sales force. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and 325 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Retail Management
description: An investigation of store policies, organization, location, layout, buying, stock control, pricing, and sales promotion for retail stores. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Transportation: An International Focus
description: The economics of transportation with an international focus; economic development of various means of transportation and accompanying regulatory problems. Rate, traffic service, and coordination problems; advantages and disadvantages, trends, and peculiarities of the various modes. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Research
description: The basic nature and scope of marketing research; scientific method and research design; specific marketing research procedures; techniques of sampling; and research report, followup, and evaluation of research process. Selected applications in motivation, advertising, and product and sales control research. Prerequisite: MKG 300; MATHS 132; and MGS 221.

title: Nonpaid Internship in Marketing
description: Professional practice during a summer or a semester as an intern in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization for no pay under the supervision of the Department of Marketing. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 369, 497, and 498. Open only to secondsemester junior marketing majors.

title: Professional Practice in Marketing
description: Professional practice during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization for pay under the supervision of the department of marketing. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 497, and 498. Open only to secondsemester junior and senior marketing majors.

title: Marketing and Consumer Issues
description: Analysis of the consumer issues that relate to marketing practices. Involves study of such topics as consumerism, ecology, fraudulent practices, and disadvantaged consumers. Reponsibilities include work experience in the Ball State University Better Business Bureau. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Channel Management
description: Study of marketing channels as economic, political, and social systems. Includes retailing, wholesaling, and other channel intermediaries. Strong emphasis on channel membership, structural and functional relationships, interorganizational management, and channel change and performance. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Promotion Management
description: Uses cases and problems to provide experience in making decisions on a firm's promotional mix. Analysis of markets, media scheduling, budget allocation, campaign design, and promotion research. Prerequisite: MKG 320.

title: Retail Strategy
description: Advanced course in retailing management using case studies and special projects to examine current topics and problems in retailing. Prerequisite: MKG 330.

title: Industrial Procurement Management
description: A basic course in industrial procurement management. Principal topics include make or buy analysis, quality and quantity control, value analysis, price determination, sources of supply, the purchasing system, and legal aspects of purchasing. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Logistics Management
description: Marketing linkage strategy. Focuses on efficient coordination of resources for physical distribution, manufacturing support, and purchasing. Activities include literature searches, professional meetings, guest speakers, and simulation. Prerequisite: MKG 300. Prerequisite recommended: MKG 340.

title: International Marketing
description: Examines legal, economic, and cultural factors influencing marketing abroad. Commercial policies, practices, and techniques needed to identify and evaluate foreign markets, as well as the problems of pricing, promoting, and distributing products in international markets. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Simulation Game
description: A simulation game in which students are divided into teams or companies. Management in each company makes decisions in marketing, finance, and production. Does not involve writing computer programs or using information from a dataprocessing class. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and junior standing.

title: Marketing Management
description: Marketing by manufacturers as viewed from the marketing manager's position. Principal topics are selecting channels of Marketing 123 distribution, determining demand, pricing policies, marketing legislation, advertising policies, and methods of selling. A casestudy approach. Prerequisite: 15 semester hours in marketing, including MKG 310, 325, 350, and senior standing, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Marketing
description: Advanced examination of such current marketing topics as marketing theory and quantitative, service, nonprofit, bank, comparative, and international marketing. Specific content announced when offered. Recommended for honors students. Prerequisite: MKG 300; senior standing; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Marketing
description: Independent study in some phase of marketing that may consist of an experiment, library research, or the analysis of current marketing practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing, overall GPA of 3.0, and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 credit hours may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 369, and 498. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to secondsemesterjunior marketing majors.

title: Practicum in the Better Business Bureau
description: Practical experience in mediating businessconsumer problems. Students use personnel skills in organizing and administering a Better Business Bureau. Prerequisite: MKG 380 and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 credit hours may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 369, and 497. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. GENERAL BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (GBA)

title: The Computer in the Fine Arts
description: An interdisciplinary approach to the philosophy, use, and limits of the computer in the visual arts, music, dance, and theatre; includes background on and implications of the computer as a functional tool in the arts. The department reserves the right to retain examples of student work for exhibition. title: Weaving 2
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and the application of these techniques to a project. Also includes techniques in handdyeing of yarns. Specific techniques covered in a given semester will vary. Prerequisite: ACR 201.

title: Ceramics 1
description: Basic handbuilding techniques: wedging, slab, coiling, and pinch methods. Glazes, slips, bisquing, and firing will be part of the studio experience. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 1
description: Beginning throwing; use of the potter's wheel to develop skills in throwing. A continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to jewelry and object making using metal. Emphasis on design and the techniques of sawing, soldering, forming, bezel setting, chain and wire working, as well as other basic processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Metalsmithing and Dieforming
description: Introduction to metalsmithing including raising and dieforming; basic hammering and forming techniques will be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 221. Open only to art majors.

title: Weaving 3
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and application of these techniques to a project. Techniques introduced will vary from semester to semester. Further exploration of the color possibilities of handdyed yarns. The level of competency will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 202.

title: Weaving 4
description: Exploration of woven fiber techniques and application of these techniques to a project. Techniques introduced will vary from semester to semester. Further exploration of the color possibilities of handdyed yarns. The level of competency will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 303.

title: Ceramics: Hand 1
description: Continued study of handbuilding methods as well as form, idea, and glazing techniques. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 2
description: Use of the potter's wheel to develop production form; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 212. ART: CRAFTS (ACR)

title: Weaving 1
description: Basic instruction in 6 loom weaving with an emphasis on tapestry technique and color experimentation. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Ceramics: Hand 2
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques to develop an integration of form, glaze, and idea. Individual problems will be set up according to the student's needs. Prerequisite: ACR 313.

title: Metals: Casting
description: Jewelry casting using the lostwax investment technique. Production casting will be covered, including rubbermold making and wax injecting for cast multiples. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ACR 222. Open only to art majors.

title: Color in Metal
description: Color in metal, including enameling and aluminum and refractory metal anodizing. Prerequisite: ACR 323. Open only to art majors or by permission of instructor.

title: Weaving 5
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit his or her needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 304.

title: Weaving 6
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit his or her needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 405.

title: Weaving 7
description: Individual exploration of techniques in fiber. More emphasis on an individual direction in the work. The student will work with the instructor to determine a course of study for the semester that will best suit his or her needs and interests. Proficiency and knowledge will increase in successive courses. Prerequisite: ACR 406.

title: Senior Project in Weaving 1
description: Concentrated work in a particular individual direction in fibers under the supervision of an instructor; content, amount, and extent of work will be determined by agreement of the student and the instructor. Prerequisite: completion of course work in major.

title: Senior Project in Weaving 2
description: Further work in an individual direction in a body of work. The guidelines for the amount and direction of the work will have been determined when the student enrolls in ACR 408. Course content includes the mounting of a senior exhibition. Prerequisite: ACR 408.

title: Independent Study in Crafts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 3
description: An indepth exploration of forming vertically and horizontally on the wheel; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 314.

title: Ceramics: Hand 3
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques, form, and idea based on individual student's needs. Prerequisite: ACR 315.

title: Senior Project in Ceramics
description: Synthesis and culmination of studio experiences in the major content area, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. In addition there must be documentation through slide portfolio, résumé, and thesis. Prerequisite: completion of total course work. Open only to ceramics majors.

title: Advanced Fabrication Techniques
description: Advanced construction techniques including catches, hinges, stone settings, etc. Basic forging will also be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 323. Open only to art majors or by permission of instructor.

title: Metals: Advanced Surface Techniques
description: Advanced surface techniques including chasing and repousse, metal inlays and laminations, patination, and other surface embellishments. Prerequisite: ACR 324. Open only to art majors.

title: New Technologies in Metals
description: New technologies in metalsmithing. Extended study of contemporary technologies such as electroforming, plastics, and photoetching. Prerequisite: ACR 425. Open only to art majors.

title: Senior Project in Metals
description: Synthesis of experience in metals culminating in an exhibition of work. In addition; There must be documentation through slide portfolio and résumé. Should be taken during the final semester of undergraduate work. Prerequisite: ACR 427. Open only to metals majors.

title: Seminar in Crafts
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in various concepts, media, and techniques as related to the crafts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of art courses and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be ART: DESIGN (ADS)

title: Foundations 1
description: Exploration of basic art principles, elements, and concepts with emphasis on spatial organization of the twodimensional plane. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on craftsmanship. Parallel recommended: AFA 101.

title: Foundations 2
description: Continued exploration and application of basic art principles and elements to organize threedimensional space. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on craftsmanship. Prerequisite: ADS 101. Parallel recommended: AFA 202.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: Basic visual investigations of line, shape, and color. Emphasis on specific communication problems for the student to resolve. Introduces the fundamental craft considerations and the tools of the graphic designer. Prerequisite: ADS 102.

title: Interior Design Graphics 1
description: Fundamental instruction in drawing basic geometrical designs and orthographic projections. Emphasis upon skill building and media manipulation. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Parallel: ARCH 217. Open only to art majors.

title: Interior Design Graphics 2
description: Exploration of the principles of visual communication applied to interior/ environmental design. Emphasis on conceptual drawing and the selection of appropriate visual techniques for presentation. Prerequisite: ADS 205; ARCH 217. Parallel: ARCH 218. Open only to art majors.

title: Photography 1
description: Introduction to photography as an expressive art form with emphasis on the development of photographic vision as well as technical proficiency. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Introduction to Graphic Design
description: Introduction and orientation to concepts and skills necessary for visual communication in two and three dimensions. The fundamentals of structure, color, typography, and tools are emphasized. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Typography and Image
description: Consideration of typography in relation to visual organization; color theory and its application to communication. Type and image are covered in experimental and practical formats. Prerequisite: ADS 241. Open only to art majors.

title: Environmental Design Programming
description: Studio exploration of interiorspace design with analysis on human activity for the threedimensional design of simple spaces. Prerequisite: ADS 206; ARCH 218. Open only to art majors.

title: Interior Environments 1
description: Interiorspace problem research stressing the interaction of users, color, texture, and environments. Prerequisite: ADS 324 and admission to interior/environmental design sequence through portfolio review. Open only to art majors.

title: Photography 2
description: Emphasis on the further exploration of photographic vision, technical concerns, aesthetic aspects of photography, and further study of photo history; introduction to advertising photography. Prerequisite: ADS 231. Open only to art majors.

title: Color Photography
description: Focus on ideas and assigned problems expressed through color photography. Students should have a basic knowledge of processing color film and color prints. Prerequisite: ADS 332 and ITGRA 387 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Commercial Photography
description: Investigates commercial applications of photographic medium with historical perspective. Weekly problems assigned with emphasis on practical application of photography to advertising. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Large Format Photography
description: Students become familiar with cameras larger than 35mm for personal expression and illustration. Emphasis will be on the 4" x 5" camera and its individual strengths and weaknesses. Students need not have large format camera but will find it helpful. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: Exploration of creative thematic development and its relation to the final stages of the design process. Technical aspects of type specification and indication and graphicdesign production are considered. Prerequisite: ADS 242 and admission to graphicdesign sequence through portfolio review. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Concentrated involvement in problem analysis with emphasis on symbology and image development. Prerequisite: ADS 341. Open only to art majors.

title: Independent Study in Design
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Interior Environment 2
description: Design analysis and synthesis of complex interior spaces. Consideration of human activity as the determinant of the design solution. Prerequisite: ADS 330. Parallel: ADS 480. Open only to art majors.

title: Photography 3
description: Major emphasis on students' personal statements in color and blackandwhite photography through selection of their own projects under the guidance of an instructor. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332 for art majors; for others, permission of department chairperson.

title: Photography 4
description: A further intensification of students' personal statements. Students given occasional assignments to introduce new and varied directions in art. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 433.

title: Cinematography as an Art Form
description: Explores the use of video and super-8 media as sources of creative exploration with concerns for artistic expression, content, form, and technique. Covers a brief survey of film history. Art 131 Prerequisite: ADS 332 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Professional Practices/Portfolio Organization
description: Mechanics of a professional design practice and the function of a portfolio with emphasis on its content and format. Prerequisite: ADS 426. Parallel: ADS 480. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 3
description: Advanced problem solving in sequential and threedimensional forms. Prerequisite: ADS 342. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 4
description: Advanced problem solving in graphic design. Refinement of presentation techniques and résumé and portfolio development. Prerequisite: ADS 441. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design Topic Studio
description: Intensive studio exploration of strategies and visual development within specific graphic design areas. Could include computer, letterpress, publications, exhibition and signage, package design, or development of concept and content. Prerequisite: ADS 341. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design Practicum
description: Problem solving within and outside of the university community. Group and individual projects for nonprofit clients. The Ball State University Art Gallery is ranked among the finer galleries in the United States. Requires portfolio review and permission of instructor. Prerequisite: ADS 341. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to art majors.

title: Senior Design Thesis
description: Intensive study with research and resolution of a current problem in interior design. Thesis must be arranged with faculty advisor during fall semester of senior year. Prerequisite: ADS 330. Parallel: ADS 426 (fall) or 436 (spring). A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to senior interior/ environmental design majors.

title: Seminar in Design
description: Group or individual investigation and experiences in the fine arts beyond the scope of regular course work. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ART: EDUCATION (AED)

title: Introduction to Studio Fundamentals
description: Introduction to the basic studio processes of drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. Lecture and studio experiences related to the understanding of the elements and principles of art and the methods of art criticism. Not open to art majors.

title: Introduction to Art Education
description: Introduction to art education as a teaching profession. Emphasizes investigating artistic growth of normal and special populations and the materials, techniques, tools, art concepts, and strategies appropriate for teaching art to such students. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint the student with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Stresses the developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques. Prerequisite: AED 100. Open only to nonart majors.

title: Art Curriculum and Instruction
description: Designed to develop the art student's ability to make artcurricular judgments by developing artcurriculum plans and designing art experiences. Prerequisite: AED 201, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Art Teaching and Learning Practicum
description: Direct experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating teaching strategies. Includes observation of students participating in an artrelated environment. Laboratory teaching time is arranged. Prerequisite: AED 304 for majors; permission of department chairperson for minors.

title: Classroom Use of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary public school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 305 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum for majors; permission of department chairperson for minors. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Art Education
description: Permits the professionally oriented art student to select and explore more intensively an area of art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art Education
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in the various ideas, methods, and research in art education. Open only to students with areas in art. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ART: FINE ARTS (AFA)

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to drawing: the application of basic principles and elements of art as they relate to drawing concepts. Emphasis will be on the development of perceptual awareness and familiarity with a broad range of media and techniques. Parallel recommended: ADS 101.

title: Drawing 2
description: A continuation of concepts and perceptions from Drawing 1 with emphasis on the human figure. Prerequisite: AFA 101. Parallel recommended: ADS 102.

title: Painting 1
description: Introduction to painting: study of basic considerations of image making with oil paint. Focuses on media, techniques, design elements, and concepts. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Painting 2
description: Explorations in painting designed to build on initial experiences by studio practice and through slidelectures on contemporary painting. Prerequisite: AFA 202 and 211.

title: Watercolor 1
description: Exploration of materials and techniques of transparent watercolor as they apply to the solution of painting problems. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Watercolor 2
description: Continued exploration of painting problems in watercolor with emphasis on the unique character of the medium. Prerequisite: AFA 217.

title: Sculpture 1
description: Introduction to sculpture; basic techniques, skills, and concepts associated with materials used to create traditional sculpture; clay, plaster, wire, and wood. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture 2
description: Continued exploration of materials used in formal sculpture; welded and forged metal, wood construction and carving, stone carving, clay, wax, and plastic. Prerequisite: AFA 221. Open only to art majors.

title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Beginning printmaking techniques with an emphasis on intaglio and relief processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Relief Printmaking
description: Fundamental procedures of relief printing from the woodblock and other surfaces with emphasis on the use of color and new approaches. Students are expected to develop images that have a relationship to this print medium. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 1
description: Intermediatelevel printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques. Emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Drawing 3
description: Life drawing. An intensive study of the human figure, continuing the exploration of various drawing techniques and media. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Drawing 4
description: Drawing experiences exploring varied materials and concepts related to drawing as a personal visual statement. Prerequisite: AFA 303.

title: Painting 3
description: Individualized instruction aimed at the continued mastery of technical skills and progress toward the solution of pictorial and conceptual problems. Prerequisite: AFA 212. Open only to art majors.

title: Painting 4
description: Continued interest in the development of technical skills and the solution of pictorial problems with new emphasis on individual creative solutions. Prerequisite: AFA 313.

title: Painting 5
description: Emphasis on advancing from technical proficiency toward the development of individual conceptual goals relating to painting. Prerequisite: AFA 314.

title: Water Media
description: Advanced study in water media on paper to expand painting skills while narrowing the search for personally significant imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 218. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture 3
description: Introduction to and emphasis on the basic techniques and concepts of mold making and casting aluminum, bronze, and plastics. Prerequisite: AFA 222. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture 4
description: Introduction to sculptural alternatives and nontraditional sculptural materials; visual and audio aids, performance, and antiart. Prerequisite: AFA 323. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture: Casting and Mold Making
description: Continuation of AFA 323. Advanced casting and mold making procedures. Individual development of the concepts and techniques associated with the casting process. Prerequisite: AFA 323. Open only to art majors.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 2
description: Advanced printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques including line etching, drypoint, engraving, softground, and aquatint. Openended problem solving and indepth study with emphasis on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 243.

title: Lithography 1
description: Fundamental processes of drawing and printing lithographs using stones and aluminum plates. Drawing and painting techniques are used to develop images. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Lithography 2
description: Further development and investigation of the processes of lithography, including color. Exploration of stone and metal plate techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 351.

title: Lithography 3
description: Investigation of additional drawing and painting techniques as they relate to lithography. Further development of printing skills and the lithographic image. Prerequisite: AFA 352. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Serigraphy 1
description: Introductory printmaking dealing with the processes of serigraphy, including the four basic stencil techniques and their variation. Silkscreen as a fineart form. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Sculpture 5
description: Individual instruction and supervision of experimentation in nontraditional materials. Prerequisite: AFA 324. Open only to art majors.

title: Drawing 5
description: Continuation of the drawing experience for advanced students developing further expertise in drawing skills while encouraging research into and experimentation with more personal imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 304.

title: Drawing 6
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 405. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Fine Arts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Painting 6
description: Individualized instruction, continuing the emphasis on student identification and development of personal concepts in painting. Prerequisite: AFA 315.

title: Advanced Problems in Sculpture
description: Designed for students who want to extend their technical understanding and aesthetic development beyond the fundamental level. Prerequisite: AFA 325 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 3
description: Advanced printmaking emphasizing aesthetic decision making involving the intaglio process through the knowledge of technique and use of personal artistic choices. Prerequisite: P. FA 344. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Senior Project in Drawing
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in drawing, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 18 credit hours in drawing, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to art majors.

title: Senior Project in Painting
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in painting, with a student exhibition and supporting written composition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: AFA 416, 18 credit hours in painting, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Sculpture
description: A synthesis and culmination of the student's undergraduate studio experiences in sculpture, with an exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 21 credit hours in sculpture, sponsorship by a sculpture faculty member, and permission of department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Printmaking
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experience in printmaking, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 27 credit hours in printmaking, sponsorship by a printmaking faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to art majors.

title: Seminar in Fine Arts
description: Individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Art
description: A general studies course that, through a survey of art and artifacts from ancient through modern times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of painting, sculpture, and architecture. Open only to students not majoring in art.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. Prehistoric through end of European Middle Ages.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. From the fifteenth century to the present.

title: Design History 1
description: Sequential study of design and function as applied to interior design, furniture design, and product design from antiquity through the eighteenth century. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Design History 2
description: Sequential study of design and function as applied to interior design, furniture design, and product design from the nineteenth century to the present with emphasis on American and European design. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Art in the United States 1
description: Investigation of the role visual culture has played in America throughout its history as Americans attempted to situate themselves geographically, culturally, economically, and politically within their own society and within the world at large.

title: Art in the United States 2
description: Traces the evolution of American visual arts from the beginning of the twentieth century to the present within the context of important social, historical, and intellectual events. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Early Civilizations
description: Art and architecture of cultures of the ancient Near East and Egypt. Use of archeological data, visual evidence, and literary records to reconstruct built environments. Special emphasis on cultural significance of monumental architecture, sculpture, painting, and diverse minor arts. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Aegean and the Greeks
description: Bronze Age through the Hellenistic period, covering architecture, pottery, painting, sculpture, and minor arts, and the interrelationships of the Aegean Islands and Greek mainland. Archeological data discussed in terms of revelations about the areas' artistic and cultural development. Open to all students.

title: Art of Rome
description: Art and architecture of early Rome and the Republic to the Late Empire. Architecture and urbanism as a vehicle for the political and cultural extension of the empire to the barbarian west and the Hellenized east; missionary role of historic reliefs; Roman concepts of personality and portraiture; and the growth of luxury arts: ornament, interior decoration, and collecting.

title: Early Medieval Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture from the fourth through the tenth centuries in relation to the religious, political, and technological conditions of the period. Rural northwest Europe will be discussed in relation to urban societies in the east. Periods to be covered include early Christian, Merovingian, Carolingian, Ottonian, and Byzantine. Open to all students.

title: Late Medieval Art
description: European art and architecture from the eleventh through the fourteenth centuries. Competing claims of royal and religious sponsors; shifts in centers of rural and religious sponsors; shifts in center of production from rural to urban markets, monasteries to bishops' towns, in a period of economic advance, political transformation, and social unrest. Open to all students.

title: Northern European Art 1300 -1600
description: Northern European Renaissance art as a specifically northern mode of expression and representation reflecting social, political, religious, and other cultural particularities of specific areas (France, Germany, and southern and northern Netherlands).

title: Art of the Italian Renaissance 1300-1600
description: Art and architecture examined in terms of style, cultural meaning, context, and ideology. Investigation of conditions of art production, change in role of artist, relationship between art theory and practice, and the question or concept of Renaissance.

title: Early Modern Europe 1: Art from 1600 to 1750
description: Exploration of art and architecture of Europe, from the Counter-Reformation shrine of St. Peter to Louis XIV's palace at Versailles; from the Jesuit altar pieces in Antwerp to the Dutch Republic of Vermeer and Rembrandt and more. Italy, Spain, France, Germany, England, Flanders, Netherlands. Open to all students.

title: Early Modern Europe 2: Art from 1750 to 1850
description: Art and architecture in the era of enlightenment and revolution, age of Napoleon, Restoration, reaction, reform, economic advance, and social unrest. From country gardens to urban boulevards. Rococo, neoclassicism, romanticism, historicism, realism. England, France, Germany, Italy, Spain. Open to all students.

title: Modern Art
description: Pan-European investigation of the visual arts from French impressionism to the post-World War II abstract expressionists. Special emphasis on cultural definitions of modernity and modernism and the appearance and ideologies of the avant garde. Open to all students.

title: Contemporary Art
description: Exploration of ideas and issues surrounding the production, reception, marketing, interpretation, and criticism of painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, installations, performance, and video and other mixed media since World War II. International in scope. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Film History
description: Traces the history of cinema from its beginning to contemporary times. Emphasizes the role of technique and art in film, modernism, and the appearance and idealogies of the avant garde. Open to all students.

title: History of Photography
description: Introduction to problems in theory, analysis, and history of photography. Study of institutional and discursive orders in which photography functions and produces meaning. Exploration of new forms of critical photographic practice. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in History of Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in art history with emphasis on those not covered in other courses (women in art, history of museums and collecting, problems in methodology, etc.). Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Graphic Design
description: Detailed analysis of graphic design from late nineteenth century to present, with emphasis on European and American design. Influential movements, artists, designers, and technology that shape current design thinking will be highlighted. Prerequisite: ADS 242, pass graphic design portfolio review, or instructor's permission. Open only to art majors.

title: Special Topics in American Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in American art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Ancient Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in ancient art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Medieval Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in medieval art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Renaissance and Early Modern Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem or issue in Renaissance or early modern art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in Modern and Contemporary Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in modern or contemporary art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Prehistoric and Non-Western Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in prehistoric or non-Western art with focus on subjects not covered in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art History

title: Introduction to Music
description: A general studies course that, through a survey of musical forms and compositions from early through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the broad range of musical creativity. Open only to students not majoring in music.

title: Music and Popular Culture in America
description: A survey of the origins and development of popular music in America. Discussion includes blues, jazz, musical theatre, and rock. Emphasis on cultural rather than technical aspects of music.

title: Survey of Music Literature
description: Survey of styles, forms, and masterworks of music with emphasis on the period 1700 to 1975. One hour lecture and two hours directed listening each week. Required for majors and minors. Open only to music majors and minors or by permission.

description: Changes in music from the preclassic period through the present and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 200 and 330 or departmental permission.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Open only to students on the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of medieval, Renaissance, and baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles that marked the transition from baroque to classical music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in Western civilization in the nineteenth century, emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Studies important composers and works from the various time periods: early, middle, late, and post-Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331 or permission of the director of the school.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and the student will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Jazz History 1
description: Historic examination of jazz from 1890 to 1950. Analyzes outstanding style characteristics of each period from their beginnings to the 1950s, including ragtime, the Jazz Age, the Swing Era, and the bebop and cool periods.

title: Jazz History 2
description: Continuation of MUHIS 439, covering the 1950s through the present. Progressive '50s, the rockjazz fusions of the 1960s, '70s, and '80s— today's trends.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque instruments and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Rameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: An opportunity for superior students to do guided reading and intensive study in topics in music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester.

title: Workshop in Music History and Musicology
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music history and musicology. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 331.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 101 or 331. MUSIC ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY (MUMET)

title: Introduction to Electronic Music
description: Topics include musique concrete, analog sound generation and processing, voltage controlled systems. In addition to lectures, a minimum of four hours of laboratory time is required each week. Projects include sound synthesis, sound structuring, and analysis.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic and Electro-Acoustic Music
description: Survey of the development of composition using the electronic medium. Topics include the study of electronic instruments, the analysis of music forms and structure in electronic and electroacoustic compositions, and the study of computerassisted composition.

title: Music Perception
description: An introduction to basic psychoacoustics and psychophysics. Topics include the ear as a frequency analyzer, the auditory pathway, fundamentals of auditory perception, special problems in the perception of music and music structures.

title: Sound Synthesis 1
description: Intermediate course in sound synthesis. Topics include FM and AM synthesis, filtration, basic mixing, iteration and reverberation, and the development of basic analog and digital electronic virtual instruments. Minimum of three hours of lab experience required weekly. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; MUMET 225.

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: An introduction to the basics of recording technology. Topics include the analog tape recorder, the tape medium, microphone design, and microphone placement. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; PHYCS 122.

title: Introduction to Computer Music
description: An intermediate course in computer music. Topics include computer systems appropriate for music composition, sound synthesis, and analysis. Computer and music instrument communications are introduced. Intermediate projects in music programming are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212, PHYCS 122.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire. Each project requires seminar and laboratory participation. Prerequisite: MUMET 326. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Sound Synthesis 2
description: An advanced course in sound synthesis. Topics include the development of complex virtual electronic instruments and their control. Structured sound projects are required. A minimum of five hours of lab experience each week is required. Prerequisite: MUMET 325, 327.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Topics include multitrack recording, multichannel mixing, signal processing, and problems in multiple microphone arrays and stereo imaging. A minimum of 3 hours of laboratory experience is required. Prerequisite: MUMET 326.

title: Advanced Projects in Computer Music
description: An advanced course in computer music applications. Topics include problems in MIDI communications, projects in algorhythmic composition, and problems in telemusic communications. Prerequisite: MUMET 425.

title: Production Workshop
description: An advanced course in technical applications of music production. This is an independentprojectoriented course. Projects require a production product such as a technical demonstration, a broadcast quality program, an album, or an intermedia performance. Prerequisite: MUMET 426.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are Wind Ensemble, Symphonic Band, Marching Show Band, Basketball Pep Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are Concert Band and Jazz Ensembles II and

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles normally rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Chamber Choir, Opera Chorus, University Singers, and Lab Choir.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are University Chorus, Women's Chorus, and the Statesmen. Registration will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, rehearsing normally five hours a week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, Symphony Band, Marching Show Band, Basketball Pep Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Band and Jazz Ensembles II and III.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles normally rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera/Musical Theatre, and the University Singers.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are the Women's Chorus, the Statesmen, the University Chorus, and the Lab Choir.

title: The Singing Actor
description: Acting techniques specifically related to musical theatre and opera. Vocal exercises, movement, song interpretation. Preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer or technician. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Musical Theatre in America
description: A study of the history of the American musical theatre. A general overview of the repertoire.

title: Workshop in Music
description: A one - or twoweek workshop on specialized interdisciplinary topics in music. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Recital
description: Attendance at recitals and concerts as specified in the music student handbook is the basis for the earning of recital credit.

title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Screening of potential music education candidates is built into the course.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Development and Administration of Choral Music
description: Analysis of the high school choral music teacher's position in the school and community and the administration and supervision of choral activities. Discussion of choral music suitable for various high school choirs

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled.

title: Elementary General Music 1
description: Introducing general music for grades K-6. Explores the philosophy of general music teaching, objectives of concepts and skills, developing teaching skills, use of materials and equipment, and specialized approaches to music education.

title: Elementary General Music 2
description: Continuing study of curriculum development, teaching methodology, use of materials and equipment, evaluation in general classroom music for grades K-6. Includes planning individual teaching projects, some observation and participation, integration with other curricular areas, mainstreaming, Orff and Kodaly approaches. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High Schools
description: A study of the philosophies, techniques, and materials for teaching the required nonperformance music courses in grades five through nine. Emphasizes the unique musical needs of young adolescents.

title: Teaching Instrumental Music
description: Examines problems in the teaching and administration of contemporary instrumental classes. Topics include program goals, inventory management, rehearsals, selection of materials, and techniques for the learning of musical concepts in performance classes. Prerequisite: minor skills in brasses, woodwinds, and strings.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary Classroom
description: Focuses on the implementation of music in the elementary classroom. Draws on the common heritage of music and suggests methods for presenting appropriate musical experience and materials to children. Prerequisite: MUSED 265.

title: Instrumental Laboratory
description: Laboratory ensemble taken as participant first, then as a conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 390. Focuses on instrumental rehearsal techniques and instrumental literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Choral Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus taken as participant first, then as a conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 391. Focus on choral rehearsal techniques and choral literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Show/Jazz Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus emphasizing show and jazz literature and styles. Stresses choreography and vocal techniques for the teacher of high school show choir and jazz choir. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Elementary
description: A concentrated, shortterm course that provides practical experience in all phases of music education for the elementary schools through participation in varied musical activities, including singing, listening, playing instruments, and dancing.

title: Practicum in Music Education: Secondary
description: Provides experience with the materials and activities of nonperformance classes in secondary schools. The chief concern is with possiblities of instruction in music for students who are not active in school performing groups.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Approaches to the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Methods of Teaching Classical Guitar
description: A methods course for those who have studied guitar at the university level. Intensive study of the specialized techniques, methods, and materials needed for teaching this style of playing in class or private instruction. Prerequisite: credit in classical guitar.

title: Voice Pedagogy
description: Evaluation of methods and principles of voice production for achieving technical excellence. Consideration given to tone quality, agility, legato, breathing, range, diction, study of anatomical aspects of tone production, the International Phonetic Alphabet, vocalization studies, and repertoire for singers.
