title: Instrumental Conducting Practice
description: Continuation of skills and techniques learned in MUSPE 290 with emphasis upon the instrumental ensembles. Rehearsal and conducting of instrumental literature with live ensembles. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Choral Conducting Practice
description: A continuation and application of skills and techniques learned in MUSPE 290 with emphasis upon the choral ensemble. Rehearsal and conducting of vocal literature with live ensembles. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Diction for Singers
description: Beginning voice students will learn effective pronunciation of English and Italian using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Techniques in producing vowel sounds and consonant articulation unique to the sung work will be emphasized. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Wind and Percussion Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for wind and percussion instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with winds or percussion as their major instrument.

title: String and Harp Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for stringed instruments and harp instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with strings or harp as their major instrument.

title: Keyboard Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for piano, organ, and harpsichord instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with piano, organ, or harpsichord as their major instrument.

title: Guitar Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for guitar instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with guitar as their major instrument.

title: Vocal Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for vocal instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with voice as their major instrument. 1430 Small Ensemble (Woodwinds). (1) Players of woodwind instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing. 1431 Small Ensemble (Brass). (1) Players of brass instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of brass ensemble literature. These groups may include trios and quartets of like instruments, or quintets, sextets, and octets of mixed brasses. 1432 Small Ensemble (Percussion). (1) Players of percussion instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of the literature designed for their public performance. These groups may range in size from trios and quintets to larger ensembles. 1433 Small Ensemble (Strings). (1) Players of string instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing. 1434 Small Ensemble (Harp). (1) Groups of harpists are organized to perform the specialized literature for this unusual combination of instruments. Original compositions and transcriptions are presented in public performances. 1435 Small Ensemble (Piano). (1) Study of sonata literature in conjunction with another instrument or literature for multiple pianos. Students will be organized into small groups according to proficiency and demands of the literature. 1436 Ensemble for New Music. (1) Players of all instruments are organized into small groups for the study of contemporary chamber music. Open to all students with sufficient proficiency. 1437 Small Ensemble (Organ and Church Music). (1) Performance projects of interest to the organist and church musician. Reading of anthems, motets, oratorio movements; music for organ and instruments; music for graded church choirs; conducting from the keyboard. 1438 Small Ensemble (Vocal). (1) Quartets, sextets, octets, and multiples of these units are arranged as student enrollment indicates. Music studied and performed ranges from the traditional quartet literature to material appropriate for glee clubs. 1439 Small Ensemble (Guitar). (1) Guitar players are organized into small groups to study and perform the duet, trio, and quartet repertoire for classical guitar. Upperclassmen generally study ensemble works involving other instrumentation such as guitar and flute; guitar and strings; and guitar and voice. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom
description: Application of melodyharmony relationship to instrumental performance. Students will be expected to play numerous standard tunes and jazz standards, and improvise with competency determined by the instructor. All chords, scales, sixths, sevenths, ninths, elevenths, thirteenths, modes, and transposition of modes.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom 2
description: Songs from swing, bebop, cool, and contemporary periods. Exploration of unitonal, unimodal, polytonal, polymodal melodies with small instrumental groups. Innovations in jazz improvisation. Musicians to be studied include Chick Corea, Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, Joe Farrell, and Miles Davis. Prerequisite: MUSPE 456.

title: Jazz Piano Class 1
description: All triads with the added sixth, or sixth chords played in block chordal harmony. All inversions of these chords and transpositions of chord types through four sharps and flats; introduction of the four types of seventh chords.

title: Jazz Piano Class 2
description: Continuation of MUSPE 460. Completion of seventh chords, inversion in remaining keys; additional experiences include minor seventh (flat 5), augmented seventh, and minor/major sevenths. All ninth chords, eleventh chords, and thirteenth chords played melodically and harmonically. Prerequisite: MUSPE 460.

title: Continuo Playing and Keyboard Improvisation
description: Development of facility in reading from figured basses or improvisation in the church service, free harmonization of hymns. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or MUSPE 226 or 377. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned. *490 Advanced Conducting. (1 -3) One onehour weekly lesson in conducting. Private or small class at the discretion of the instructor. Prerequisite: MUSPE 390 or 391. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Workshop in Music Performance
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Recital
description: Taken during the senior year by students with a performance major. The student will present a full recital as approved by the student's area committee and the director of school.

title: Independent Study in Musical Performance
description: An opportunity to cover specific needs or interests for which provisions are not made by the regular course offerings of the school. Prerequisite: permission of director of the school. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. MUSIC THEORY AND COMPOSITION (MUSTH)

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students deficient in elementary music language. Provides simplest basic concepts, symbols, readingskill drills, and terminology with supporting historical and systems information. Placement by level of experience.

title: Music Theory
description: In -depth study of music fundamentals including rhythm, melodic structure, fourpart harmony, elementary harmonic and structural analysis accompanied by writing, listening, score study, and sightsinging. Placement by level of experience. Must be taken in course number sequence.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 111 including more advanced fourpart writing, analysis, score study, listening, and sightsinging. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Acoustics
description: An introduction to physical acoustics with an emphasis on music and audio applications. Topics included are wave mechanics, acoustic measurements, tone and timbre analysis, tuning and temperament, and sound transduction.

title: Music Theory
description: Emphasis on nineteenthcentury procedures through studies of compositional styles and analysis. Required mastering of diatonic and chromatic modulations, and higher hierarchical chordal structures in tonal context and traditional forms. Advanced music reading, aural perception, laboratory drill in analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 211, emphasizing practices of the later nineteenth century and the twentieth century. Mastery of basic understanding of postromantic, impressionistic, expressionistic, neoclassical, serial, and other contemporary music required. Continued music reading, aural perception, laboratory analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Music Theory: Form and Analysis
description: An indepth study of large forms through intensive analysis, listening, research, and writing. Emphasis on individual student work done outside class to develop abilities in theoretical and composition investigation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. Open only to music majors.

title: Music Theory: Eighteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: In -depth study of eighteenthcentury counterpoint in which skills are developed in analyzing and composing canons, inventions, and fugues. Prerequisite: MUSTH 311. Open only to music majors.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Development of basic craft through the writing of shorter instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or by permission of division chairperson with the recommendation of the theory instructor.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Choral Arranging
description: Scoring for choir and choral ensembles. Gives particular attention to voicing, soloistic treatment of voices, texts, and other elements of traditional and contemporary scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band, wind ensemble, and other related groups. Emphasis on instrumentation, transposition, voicing, doubling, soloistic treatment, and scoring from piano or similar reduction. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Commercial Arranging
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques used in commercial music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms with particular attention given to the composerarranger in the recordingstudio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: Laboratory for skill development in arranging. Individualized and projectoriented to prepare musicians to score spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, and background and mood sequences, as well as to compose for TV, films, radio, and media. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theory of Nineteenth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Twentieth -Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Topics in Music Theory
description: A topic to be announced in advance that will be drawn from the compositional practices of the seventeenth, eighteenth, nineteenth, or twentieth century and discussed through selected works taken from the literature. Prerequisite: MUSTH 312. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Sixteenth -Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Continuation of MUSTH 332 and the writing of larger, longer works. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 431. Prerequisite: MUSTH 431.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. Studies the synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Study of a theoretical topic using readings, analysis, and research. Prerequisite: permission of division chairperson. A total of 6 hours may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Theory Seminar
description: Discussions, analyses, and projects concerning advanced theoretical problems from all periods and styles. Specific topics to be publicized one semester in advance. Prerequisite: permission of division chairperson.

title: Workshop in Music Theory and Composition
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music theory and composition. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Composition - Project Recital
description: Public performance of compositions completed in composition degree program or an indepth lecture or lecturerecital describing a completed music engineering and technology project. title: Ballet 1
description: Classes in ballet technique for beginners, with special emphasis on body placement and alignment. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Ballet 2
description: Classes in ballet technique for advanced beginners, with special emphasis on the use of epaulement. Prerequisite: DANCE 110 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 1
description: For students interested in dance performance or career opportunities in dance. Basic techniques and performance skills are emphasized. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 2
description: Designed to continue development of the basic performance skills of modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 120 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Luigi: Jazz Dance Technique and Philosophy of Movement
description: An introduction to dance technique and theatre movement for the nondancer interested in a movement technique philosophy. The movement technique can be used for theatre dance or athletic warmups, and the philosophy applies to all learning and performing situations. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Musical Theatre Tap Styles
description: Introduces basic meters used in musical theatre tap styles, such as soft shoe, waltz clog, and military. Develops tap vocabulary for performers and choreographers.

title: Ballet 3
description: Ballet technique on a beginningintermediate level for those with previous training. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Ballet 4
description: A continuation of ballet technique for students at an intermediate level. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term. 24 hrs DEPARTMENTAL MINOR IN CHILDREN'S THEATRE, 19 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS

title: Introduction to Dance History
description: Provides an understanding and appreciation of dance as an expression of people's imaginative and creative urges. Dance from the primitive to the twentieth

title: Modern 3
description: Designed for students with training in modern dance and introduction to improvisational performance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 121 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 4
description: Designed to prepare students for advanced modern dance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 220 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Jazz 2
description: Designed for the student with dance training who has interest in developing technique in various jazz styles. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 120, or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Tap 2
description: Advanced tap dance techniques for the dance student with previous tapdance training. Prerequisite: PEG 118 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Musical Theatre Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of contemporary dance styles for the Broadway and nightclub stages. Dance styles covered will change each semester. Prerequisite: PEG 118; DANCE 110, 120 or PEG 116. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance 1
description: Basic repertoire of ethnic dance steps, styles, and dances for use in performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Clogging
description: American ethnic dance form known as clogging. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Ball State Ballet
description: A broadbased dance company, emphasizing ballet technique, with performance interests extending from tap, jazz, and experimental to classical ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in a semester or term. Open only to students by audition.

title: Dance Theatre
description: Experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance presentations. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open only by audition.

title: International Folk Dance Company
description: Provides opportunity for students with interest in folk dance to learn and perform dances from many different countries. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term. Open by audition and permission of department chairperson.

title: Choreography 1
description: Work in choreographing dance by exploring musical and dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111, 120, 121, 140.

title: Ballet History
description: A survey of ballet from its inception to the present time. Prerequisite: DANCE 100.

title: Ballet 5
description: Intermediateadvanced ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 and 211 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Ballet 6
description: Advanced ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 310 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Partnering
description: Study of the art of partnering. Class is limited to not more than two females for each male partner. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 5
description: Introduction to improvisational performance skills for students with training in modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 220, 221 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 6
description: Designed to continue development of advanced modern dance performance skills and improvisational techniques. Prerequisite: DANCE 320 or permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Jazz 3
description: Advanced jazz dance emphasizing technique work in complex rhythms, syncopation, jazz jumps, and jazz turns. Prerequisite: DANCE 230 (4 hours) or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of the stylistic uniqueness of a particular ethnic region. Covers three to four styles during the semester. Prerequisite: DANCE 241. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Notation
description: Introduction to dance notation with an emphasis on such contemporary notation systems as Labonotation and Benesh. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240.

title: Dance Production
description: Designed to acquaint the student with various technical and performance aspects of dance production. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Choreography 2
description: Work in choreographing traditional and nontraditional dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 287 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Dance Pedagogy
description: In -depth study of teaching methods for beginning, intermediate, and advanced dance students, includes pedagogy from preschool through adult level. Includes rehearsal technique for performance preparation. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Dance Practicum
description: Intensive experience in stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, dance management, and other aspects of production. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Creative Project
description: Designed as a project in choreography for advanced dance students. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson.

title: Directed Study in Dance
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects related to dance that meet the approval of the dance faculty. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Oral Interpretation
description: The study of prose fiction, poetry, and drama through the medium of oral performance.

title: Oral Interpretation of Prose Fiction
description: An indepth study of the novel through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Poetry
description: The study of poetry through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Drama
description: The study of dramatic literature through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Studies in Oral Interpretation
description: Students with an interest in oral interpretation pursue a particular area of study in depth. Prerequisite: INTRP 230. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Presentational Theatre Forms
description: The creation and direction of presentational (readers' theatre and chamber theatre) scripts—concentrating on literature not originally intended for the stage. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Introduction to Theatre
description: A general studies course that, through a survey of plays selected from the major periods of dramatic productivity from the ancient Greeks through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the many faces of dramatic creativity. Open only to students not majoring in theatre.

title: Script Analysis
description: Systematic approach to play analysis with an emphasis on performance and production.

title: Stagecraft
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of the crafts involved in theatre production at the school, college, and community theatre levels. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Theatrical Costuming
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of costuming for educational and community theatre with attention given to stage makeup. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Principles of Stage Makeup
description: An investigation of the principles, techniques, and materials of stage makeup and practical experience in their application.

title: Acting 1
description: A lecturelaboratory class stressing the basic principles of acting.

title: Acting 2
description: A lecturelaboratory course on the principles of acting with major emphasis on character analysis and development. Prerequisite: THEAT 232.

title: Acting 3
description: Advanced scene study. Emphasis is on actor communication, listening skills, and selfexploration through the use of voice and movement. Prerequisite: THEAT 232, 233. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to theatre majors and minors.

title: Theatre Practicum
description: Intensive experience in acting, stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, theatre management, and other production areas. Students should complete practicums in six different areas. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: History of Theatre 1
description: Study of the Western theatre from its origins through the Renaissance, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: History of Theatre 2
description: Study of the Western theatre from the Renaissance to the foundations of modern theatre in the late nineteenth century, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Modern Theatre
description: Study of major movements in modern Western theatre since 1875, with emphasis on theoretical documents, production elements, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Theatrical Design Skills
description: A lecturelaboratory class to present basic problemsolving skills involving theatrical design artwork. Emphasizes the development of technique and media competence. Prerequisite: THEAT 220.

title: Fundamentals of Stage Lighting
description: A lecturelaboratory course in the basic concepts, materials, hardware, and design principles of stage lighting. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Audition Techniques and Repertory
description: How to select, prepare, and present appropriate material (monologues and songs) with honesty, style, and a sense of professionalism. Résumés and portfolio photo preparation are also covered, as are contracts and agents. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Directing 1
description: Theory and practice of directing for the theatre. Exercises in movement, line interpretation, creation of atmosphere, and the effective use of stage areas. Prerequisite: THEAT 232 and 233.

title: Directing for the Musical Theatre
description: A detailed examination of the selection, organization, and direction of musical theatre productions. For practical laboratory work, the student may elect to concentrate on the production problems of either a specific musical comedy or an opera.

title: Department of Theatre Unpaid Internship Program
description: Placement in an unpaid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in some aspect of a theatre program. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Department of Theatre Paid Internship Program
description: Placement in a paid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in some aspect of a theatre program. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Children's Theatre
description: The principles of theatre devoted to creative dramatics. Twothirds of the course is devoted to formal dramatics. A public performance will be arranged.

title: Advanced Theatre Practice
description: Students design and execute a theatre project: scenery designs, lighting, properties, acting, directing, oral interpretation, and house management. Prerequisite: 12 hours of credit in theatre courses and permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Studies in American Theatre
description: An investigation of significant movements in the American professional theatre and its drama.

title: Scene Design
description: Advanced training and experience in the problems of set design and lighting for theatrical productions in many forms and styles, including aspects of television design. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Advanced Scene Design
description: A detailed lecturelaboratory class for the design student emphasizing advanced problems of scenic rigging and design. Covers preparation and implementation of various genres including the musical theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 420.

title: Theatre Costume Design
description: Practice in the research, design, and building techniques involved in the preparation of period costumes for use in theatre productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 223 and 320.

title: Stage Lighting Design
description: Training and experience in the problems of stage lighting design for the proscenium and nonproscenium stage. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 326.

title: Styles of Acting
description: The study and performance of the styles of acting appropriate to major types of drama from antiquity to the present.

title: Advanced Study of Roles for Performance
description: An advanced course concentrating on the preparation of a script for performance. At all stages of preparation, students work closely with a faculty adviser of their choosing. The course will culminate in a live, adjudicated performance. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 and 433; INTRP 230; and permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Directing 2
description: Further investigation of the work of the director with special reference to directing the various styles, modes, and periods of theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 or the equivalent.

title: Creative Dramatics
description: Principles of developing original dramatizations through improvisational techniques. Students are expected to observe and work with children as well as with college adults.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop
description: Participation in the Summer Festival Theatre. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theatre Management
description: Study and practice in box office procedures, house management, publicity, and promotion as related to college, community, and professional theatres. Prerequisite: 9 hours of theatre courses.

title: Directed Study in Theatre
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects in design, playwriting, acting, interpretation, or directing, meeting the approval of the theatre staff. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
description: Introduces the diversity of human social life as shaped by culture, relating the origins and nature of culture to variations in such universal aspects of human experience as the food quest, family organization, social control, the arts, and religion.

title: Introduction to Archaeology
description: Nature of archaeological research—its methodology and principles of analysis— and its contributions to our understanding of human behavior and the development of human culture from the Stone Age to the present.

title: Introduction to Physical Anthropology
description: Humanity's place in nature and its relationships to other animals, especially monkeys and apes; evolutionary development and present diversity; the interaction of human biology and behavior. 3 201 Anthropology of a Changing World. (3) Anthropological survey of selected Anthropology 171 peoples of the world representing a variety of human lifeways. Focuses on global social change and issues related to contemporary human problems. Uses film and indepth studies and also discusses language and race.

title: Anthropology of American Culture
description: Examines how the values, beliefs, and norms of American culture are integrated into and symbolized in various media. Explores how we experience and resolve cultural tensions between individualism and community, equality and hierarchy, competition and cooperation.

title: Human Variation and Adaptation
description: Human biological variation in the contemporary world; examination of its distribution, inheritance, development, and adaptiveness. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor.

title: Ethnicity and Race
description: Explores the concepts of ethnicity and race and how they shape the interaction between individuals and groups in complex society. Devotes particular attention to the Western world, but also considers similar attitudes in other parts of the world.

title: Introduction to Folklore and Folklife
description: Introduction to the role of tradition in various aspects of American culture, from humor to architecture, the functions of these elements in society, and methodological and theoretical approaches to their study, with comparative examples from Ireland and Great Britain.

title: The African Background of American Black Culture
description: African cultural and historical roots of American blacks—origins of the human species, plant and animal domestication, metallurgy, art, and state formation. Focus is on West Africa, the source of most of the black population of the United States.

title: History of Method and Theory in Anthropology
description: Surveys the major ideas and issues of anthropology over time. Includes methods and theories from archaeology, physical anthropology, linguistics, and cultural anthropology.

title: Anthropology and Education
description: Applies anthropological theory and method to such educational concerns as socialization, peer dynamics, classroom networks, parentteacher interactions, modernization, and multicultural settings.

title: Classical Archaeology
description: Development of the Mediterranean areas from the Neolithic through the Classical period.

title: Bio-Cultural Evolutionary Theory
description: Traces development of evolutionary theory, explores its separate and interrelated application to social and physical anthropological thought, and, using genetic, ethological, and paleontological evidence, looks at contemporary theories about human evolutionary development.

title: Applied Anthropology
description: Investigates the problems and work that engage the attention of anthropologists outside the university setting. Examination of new skills needed to supplement those traditionally taught in anthropology.

title: Urban Anthropology
description: Explores the research carried out by anthropologists in urban areas around the world. Consideration will be given to the way anthropologists have modified their methods when confronted by the complexity of urban settings.

title: North American Indians
description: Cultures of the North American Indians emphasizing their economic, sociopolitical, and religious institutions.

title: Human Evolution
description: Fossil record of the evolution of humans and their primate predecessors. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor.

title: Topics in Old World Prehistory
description: Prehistory of various Old World regions and time periods. Topics will vary from semester to semester—for example, Europe, the Paleolithic, general survey. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Topics in New World Archaeology
description: Prehistory of various New World regions or developmental periods. Topics will vary from semester to semester—for example, Meso-America, the Southwest, general survey. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Art of Prehistoric and Non-Western Cultures
description: Exposes the liberal arts student to the artistic accomplishments of prehistoric and non-Western peoples. Art will be interpreted and functionally examined in regard to aesthetic, ceremonial, and informational content.

title: Special Topics in Native American Cultures
description: Detailed analysis of selected contemporary issues facing American Indians—for example, religious freedom, property rights—or a focus on the Indian cultures of a particular area, such as the Southwest, Great Lakes, or Northeast. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Anthropology and Women
description: Development of the female phenotype; variation in the roles assigned to women in cultures of differing levels of complexity from gathererhunters to industrial societies—both Western and non- Western—and the contributions of women anthropologists to understanding this variation.

title: Laboratory Methods in Archaeology
description: Surveys the methods of recovery, treatment, analysis, illustration, and interpretation of artifacts, soils, and faunal and botanical remains from archaeological sites; stresses the integration of research design, literature research, and laboratory methods.

title: Special Topics in Anthropology
description: Detailed analysis of a special problem in cultural anthropology, archaeology, linguistics, or physical anthropology. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Internship
description: Supervised onthejob training and work experience in which anthropology majors and minors apply what they have learned. Prerequisite: permission of the internship director. Open only to anthropology majors and minors. A total of 6 hours may be earned.

title: Culture Areas of the World
description: Anthropological survey of the culture patterns of a selected continent or region— for example, the Caribbean, Latin America, East Asia, Europe, and the island Pacific. May be repeated for different areas.

title: Honors Colloquium in Anthropology
description: Exploration of major issues in modern anthropology. Emphasis on individual study and development of results. Open to Honors College students only by permission of department chairperson.

title: Medical Anthropology
description: Focuses on conceptions of health and illness from a crosscultural perspective relating non- Western techniques to Western counterparts.

title: Primatology
description: Comparative survey of nonhuman primates, their biology and behavior. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor._

title: Human Osteology
description: Laboratory course dealing with the human skeleton including identification of whole and fragmentary bones and the assessment of the age, stature, sex, and race of a skeleton as applied to paleodemography, paleopathology, and forensic problems. Prerequisite: ANTH 105.

title: Historical Archaeology
description: Covers the major themes and philosophies of the archaeology of post-Columbian America as well as related literature and sources of information on architectural features and items of material culture likely to be encountered in the course of excavation.

title: Archaeological Resources Management
description: Special problems of what has also been called conservation archaeology, including relevant federal and state laws, regulations, and agencies; reconnaissance and sampling methods; and other responsibilities of consultant archaeologists.

title: The Development of Near-Eastern Cultures
description: Traces the development of cultures in the Near East through archaeological and documentary evidence and surveys modern cultural variability.

title: Anthropological Field Studies
description: Methods of field research in ethnography, archaeology, or physical anthropology. Stresses problem formulation, observation, data handling, and interpretation. Taught at various field locations. May be repeated for different topics. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but not more than 6 in any one

title: Witchcraft, Magic, and Religion
description: Anthropological study of mankind's ageold concern with life, death, sickness, and the unknown. Discusses human attempts to control life through supernatural beings, prayer, sacrifice, and techniques of magic and witchcraft.

title: Peoples of Southeast Asia
description: A general ethnographic survey of island and mainland Southeast Asia. Specific emphasis on cultural contrasts between rural and urban communities.

title: Ethnohistory
description: Methods and techniques of ethnohistory using information on traditional ethnographic groups, particularly in the Americas.

title: Economic Anthropology
description: Concerned with a substantive (as opposed to formal) view of allocation, conversion, and distribution of resources. Emphasizes Biology 173 economic development in Third and Fourth World countries. Prerequisite: ANTH 101 or 201 or permission of the instructor.

title: Independent Study in Anthropology
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Seminar in Anthropology
description: Integrates knowledge of current theoretical and methodological issues in the four quadrants of anthropology. Provides a setting for students to explore their own theoretical interests and present them coherently. Open only to seniors. DEPARTMENT OF BIOLOGY C. Warnes, Chairperson; D. Adalis, N. Behforouz, A. Noble, W. Rogers, S. Smith, B. Torke, C. Vann, T. Walker, C. Wise Biology is the study of life—its forms, its functions, and how living things relate to each other and their environments. Biologists work in such government agencies as state departments of natural resources, health departments, state or national parks, and environmental regulatory agencies. Businesses and industries also hire biologists to do technical research, to sell scientific equipment and supplies, and to be environmental consultants. The Department of Biology also prepares students for application to professional programs such as medical technology and entrance to medical and dental schools. The major is offered through a core program, intended to develop a common background in biology, as well as specialized course work in biology, botany, zoology, and science. Specific options are designed to prepare students for careers or graduate work in aquatic biology or fisheries, botany, cellular and molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, wildlife biology, and zoology. Students who want to become candidates for the National Registry of Microbiologists (ASM) should complete in addition to the major requirements the following recommended electives: BIO 344, 452, CHEM 225, 231; MATHS 108; and ZOOL 347. Students who plan to teach biology in the secondary schools should take a teaching major in science (biology primary or supporting area) or the teaching minor in biology along with the requirements for a teaching license. (See the requirements for science teaching programs under Interdepartmental Programs in the College of Sciences and Humanities.) Students interested in pursuing graduate work in a biological science should complete the following, which are generally required by graduate schools: • proficiency in at least one foreign language, computer science, or statistics • chemistry through the organic sequence; biochemistry recommended • one year of college physics • mathematics through the calculus sequence DEPARTMENTAL MAJOR IN BIOLOGY, 51-59 HOURS Students must have a minimum of 2 years of high school algebra or the college equivalent of MATHS 108. title: People and the Life Sciences
description: Introductory course designed for students not majoring in science. Emphasizes human and social aspects of biology: reproduction, birth control, genetic counseling, behavior, evolution, pollution, radiation and energy. Not open to the student who has credit in BIO 102, 111, or 112.

title: Biological Concepts for Teachers
description: Principles of biology as they relate to energy requirements and reproductive processes of living organisms, including the study of plants and conservation with emphasis on the human role in the environment. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs.

title: Principles of Biology 1
description: Designed for biology, allied health, and other science majors. Emphasis at cellular level: chemical and physical organization of life; prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell structure and function; bioenergetics; cell division; genetics, gene expression, protein synthesis, and evolution. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: one year of high school chemistry, one semester of college chemistry or equivalent.

title: Principles of Biology 2
description: Emphasis at organism, population, and community levels: major plant and animal phyla with emphasis on structure, function, classification, and phylogenetic relationships; ecology, including human ecology and environmental biology. Lecture and laboratory.

title: Microbiology for the Health Sciences
description: Introductory course for students in applied health curricula. Presents biomolecules of life, enzyme interaction, physiology and structure of representative microorganisms. Emphasis on bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa of health significance and the hostparasite relationship. Microbiological techniques emphasized in laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 101 or equivalent.

title: Microbiology
description: Microorganisms including representative bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi. Emphasis placed on morphology, physiology, genetics, and control. Some consideration of applied aspects of microbiology. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 111.

title: Genetics
description: Basic principles of heredity and variation emphasizing meiosis, Mendelian inheritance and probability considerations, sex and gene transmission and expression, linkage and crossingover, the nature of the hereditary material, gene action and genetic control of development. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 .

title: Cell Biology
description: An introduction to the biology of the cell, including cell differentiation and growth, the nature of the organization of the cell, basic bioenergetics and enzyme function, cell environment, membrane structure and function, cell metabolism, and the work performed by cells. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112; CHEM 231 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Ecology
description: Effects of physical and biotic factors on the distribution and abundance of plants and animals. Dynamics of ecological systems are examined at the population, community, and ecosystem levels, and from an evolutionary perspective. Practical applications are emphasized. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112.

title: Pathogenic Bacteriology
description: Study of pathogenic bacteria with emphasis on morphology and physiology. Laboratory techniques in culturing, isolating, and identifying bacteria. Prerequisite: BIO 113 or 213; CHEM 130 or 231

title: Laboratory Techniques in Biological Research
description: Principles and applications of procedures used in biological research. Emphasis on methods of preparation of solutions, using standard curves, determination of rates of enzyme reactions, separation and identification of cell organelles, identification of cell metabolites, and separation of macromolecules. Prerequisite: BIO 112 and permission of department chairperson.

title: Immunology-Virology
description: Examination of the basic principles of immunology and virology. Topics include the immune system, the variety of immune responses, immunoregulation, and characteristics of viruses. Emphasis will be placed on virushost interactions and serological diagnosis of viral infections. Prerequisite: BIO 213 and one course in organic chemistry.

title: Internship in Biology
description: Paid, supervised field and laboratory experiences in public or private agencies (or in the Department of Biology). Training involves application of biological principles in the work environment. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Colloquium in Biology
description: Exploration of selected issues in biology with emphasis upon individual projects, study, and discussion. Open only to honors students except by permission of department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Biology
description: Practical application of biology in a variety of situations including biology instruction as undergraduate teaching assistants and discussion leaders, and practical experience in government or industrial laboratories and field stations. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Developments in Modern Biology
description: Stresses recent discoveries in biology and integrates and enhances understanding of basic principles of the discipline. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Field Biology of Distant Areas
description: Includes study of the sciences peculiar to selected geographic areas. Ecology, flora, and fauna. Travel may be by air. Seminars may be scheduled regularly throughout the course. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be

title: Biophysics
description: The study of biologic phenomena in terms of contributing physical events. Transport processes. Absorption and emission radiation. Ionizing radiation; its effects on living tissue; use of isotopes in research projects. Prerequisite: BIO 215.

title: Evolution
description: Principles, evidence, and the historical context of modern evolution theory. Some attention given to the origin of life and the evolution of plants and animals. Prerequisite: BIO 100, 102, or 111; or permission of department chairperson.

title: Applied Microbiology
description: The study of microorganisms that are beneficial or detrimental to changes in foods (including milk and milk products) and industrial fermentations. This is a lecture/lab course. Prerequisite: BIO 213 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Biometry
description: Principles and application of statistics to biological problems. The use of parametric and nonparametric tests of significance in the analysis of data and the interpretation of experiments. Prerequisite: MATHS 108 or equivalent or permission of department chairperson.

title: Advanced Genetics
description: Course in bacterial and eukaryotic genetics with emphasis on recent developments in molecular genetics. Topics include alternative structures of DNA, mechanisms of DNA replication, mutagenesis, DNA rearrangements, regulation of gene expression, RNA processing, molecular and mutagenetic analysis of cell cycle. Prerequisite: BIO 214, CHEM 231. Prerequisite recommended: BIO 215.

title: Human Genetics and the Problems of Humanity
description: Current problems in human heredity. Human chromosome aberrations. DNA, the genetic code, and mutations. Consanguineous marriages and genetic defects. Mendelian principles applied to humans. Pedigrees and probability. Genetic screening and counseling. Social, ethical, and legal problems and advances in genetics.

title: Molecular Biology
description: Structure and function of macromolecules in living things. Emphasizes threedimensional structures; models for enzyme mechanisms; DNA replication; protein synthesis and membrane function; and applications of biotechnology. Prerequisite: BIO 215 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Advanced Cellular and Molecular Biology
description: Study of recent developments in cell growth and differentiation, DNA and RNA research, membrane biology, cellular and molecular evolution, and cellular control mechanisms. Prerequisite: BIO 457 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Bioenergetics
description: The study of flow of energy in biological systems with emphasis on application of laws of thermodynamics to biological processes, energy production metabolism in chemotrophs and phototrophs, and the major uses of energy in biological systems. Prerequisite: BIO 215, its equivalent, or permission of department chairperson.

title: Microtechniques
description: A lecture/lab course in the preparation of biological material for microscopic examination in teaching, research, and clinical applications. Emphasis on preparation of smears, squashes, whole mounts, paraffin and frozen plant and animal sections, and photomicrography. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112, 213 and one course of college chemistry.

title: Limnology
description: The physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of inland waters. Laboratory and several field trips will be devoted to exploring techniques for the evaluation of representative aquatic ecosystems. Prerequisite: BIO 216 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Aquatic Microbiology
description: Microorganisms indigenous to nonpolluted and polluted aquatic ecosystems. Emphasis on nutrient cycling and use of microorganisms as indicators of pollution. Morphology, physiology, and ecology of specific organisms. Lecture/laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 213.

title: Marine Biology
description: Introduction to marine environments. Properties of seawater, hydrodynamics. Phytoplankton and benthic plants. Primary production, nutrient cycles. Marine animals, surveys of major taxa. Adaptations for life on the bottom, open water, intertidal zones, estuaries, abyssal regions.

title: Bioethical Decision Making
description: Development of decisionmaking skills through the analysis and personal resolution of bioethical problems created by the application of new biological and biomedical knowledge and technologies. Prerequisite: junior standing and completion of the general studies science component or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Designed to give undergraduate biology students with special aptitude an opportunity to participate in scientific investigation. Prerequisite: permission of department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Forestry
description: A survey course in forestry with emphasis on management, problems, and use of midwestern wood lots. May include field work in addition to regular laboratory periods.

title: Plant Anatomy and Morphology
description: Forms, life cycles, and evolution of the major plant groups with emphasis on the origin and structure of cells, tissues, and organs in higher plants. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Taxonomy of Vascular Plants
description: Identification, use, and care of native and ornamental trees, shrubs, vines, and herbaceous plant material. The use of botanical keys, manuals, and texts in the identification of the plant taxa. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Economic Botany
description: The cultivation, processing, environmental requirements, and use of plants and plant derivatives for food, drugs, dwellings, clothing, and power.

title: Plant Propagation and Management
description: Practical experience in the different methods of plant propagation, care, and cultivation for use in the home, school, garden, and greenhouse. Also,some emphasis on diseases, pathogens, and pests of the plant.

title: Medical Mycology
description: Study of fungi with emphasis on pathogenic forms. Discusses methods for identification of fungi along with morphology and biochemistry of fungi. Prerequisite: BIO 213.

title: Plant Physiology
description: An introductory treatment of the physiological activities of green plants with emphasis on plant growth substances, photosynthesis, and intermediate metabolism. Prerequisite: BIO 112 and CHEM 231.

title: Dendrology
description: The identification and site characterization of woody plants with an emphasis on midwestern tree species. Use of botanical features and keys in field identification. Correlation of species with site factors, plant diseases, climatic parameters, associate species, and geographical distribution. Prerequisite: BIO 112.

title: Aquatic Botany
description: The collection and identification of nonvascular and vascular plants from fresh water ecosystems. Emphasizes the morphology, physiology, and ecology of these plants to explain their distribution in nature. Class project and field trips may be used to demonstrate ecological relationships. Two Saturday field trips required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Urinalysis
description: A study of basic renal anatomy, physiology, and pathology, as well as training in the preparation of patients and collection of urine samples, conduct of routine and special tests of urine, and identification of the various formed elements in urine sediment. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Serology
description: Principles of immunology. Histology and biochemistry of the immune system. Theory and practice of the detection of antibodies and other serum substances related to disease conditions, using various diagnostic procedures. Prerequisite: BIO 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microbiology
description: Study of pathogenic organisms (bacteria, mycobacteria, fungi, and animal parasites), emphasizing isolation, culture, identification, and antibiotic sensitivity. Experience in media preparation, staining techniques, and various biochemical and serological tests for identification and sensitivity. Prerequisite: BIO 341, 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Blood Bank
description: Theory and practice of blood bank organization and procedure. Genetics and immunology of blood group systems; selection of donors; collection, processing, and storage of blood; preparation of blood products; typing, compatibility, and pretransfusion tests. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Radioimmunoassay
description: Theory and practice of the use of radiolabeled substances in the detection of hormones, antigens, antibodies, drugs, and other clinically important molecules in blood and other body fluids. Experience in such related techniques as immunofluorescence and enzyme immunoassay. Prerequisite: BIO 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Medical Chemistry
description: Theory and application of physiology, biochemistry, and organic chemistry in the laboratory diagnosis of abnormal metabolism. Experience with a variety of manual and automated test procedures, including preparation of patient samples, instrument calibration and maintenance, and quality control. Prerequisite: CHEM 360. title: Hematology
description: Study of blood, other body fluids, and bone marrow: cells, coagulation factors, and pathological conditions. Practice in collection of samples, staining procedures, and various tests concerned with cells and clotting mechanisms, including experience with related instrumentation. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Structure and Development of Vertebrates
description: Comparative study of the anatomy, development, and evolutionary relationships of vertebrates. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Animal Parasitology
description: Helminth, protozoan, and arthropod parasites of animals and man. Emphasizes identification, life cycles, hostparasite relationships, and physiology of common species. Some emphasis on medical and clinical aspects of parasites in man, and tropical forms. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Invertebrate Zoology
description: Comparative morphology, physiology, ecology, life histories, and phylogeny of invertebrate animal phyla. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: A comparison of vital activities in the animal groups, particularly the invertebrates. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Ornithology
description: The study of birds including identification, systematics, anatomy, physiology, life histories, ecological relationships, and conservation. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Entomology
description: Anatomy, physiology, taxonomy, life histories, habits, and adaptations of insects. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Ichthyology
description: The study of fish with emphasis on identification, classification, anatomy and physiology, and ecology. Emphasizes Indiana species but other important species will be included. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Mammalogy
description: The evolutionary origin, characteristics, and distribution of recent mammals. The economic relationships of mammals. The collection and preservation of specimens. May require additional field work. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Wildlife Biology
description: The identification, population dynamics, and geographic distribution of wildlife species with particular emphasis on those of the United States. The harvest and management of wildlife. May require additional field work. Prerequisite: BIO 216 or permission of department chairperson.

title: Aquatic Entomology
description: Immature and adult stages of aquatic insects, including collecting techniques, identification, ecological requirements, morphology, and evolutionary adaptations to lentic and lotic conditions. Emphasis on aquatic insects as indicators of environmental quality and stress.

title: Physical Science 1
description: Concepts of matter and energy, mechanics, heat, magnetism, electricity, sound, and light with emphasis on understanding applications through fundamentals. Open only to students with majors in elementary education.

title: Physical Science 2
description: Structure of matter and nature of the universe; atomic structure, chemistry, nuclear physics, and planetary and stellar systems, with emphasis on recent advances in chemistry and the exploration of space. Prerequisite: SCI 290. Open only to students with a major in elementary education.

title: Teaching of Science in the Elementary School
description: Methods of teaching science concepts, process skills, and scientific attitudes are developed through direct experiences. Recent elementary science texts, courses of study, and curricular materials are examined and used as are experiments, field studies, demonstrations, and special methods. Prerequisite: 8 hours of science courses or permission of department chairperson.

title: Teaching of Science in the Junior High School
description: Recent curriculum developments in junior high school science. Science curriculum instruction related to the physical, mental, and emotional characteristics of the junior high school student. Experiences in public schools may be required. Prerequisite: 24 hours of science courses or permission of department chairperson.

title: Teaching Science in the Early Childhood and Primary Grades
description: Analysis of the cognitive, psychomotor, and affective processes inherent in science investigations for young children. Handson activities with science materials appropriate for early childhood and primary children. Designed primarily for students in early childhood and primary education programs. Prerequisite: 8 hours of science or permission of department chairperson.

title: Teaching of Science in the Secondary and Junior High/Middle School
description: Philosophy and methodology of science teaching. Emphasis on laboratory investigations, concepts and conceptual schemes, scienceoriented classroom management, evaluation of instructional activities, supplies, equipment, facilities, and curriculum materials. Experiences in public schools will be required. Prerequisite: 13 hours of science courses or permission of department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF CHEMISTRY S. Pattison, Chairperson; F. Ault, M.
