title: Canada: Cultural Crossroads
description: An interdepartmental introduction to the geography, history, government, economy, literature, art, and music defining Canada's individuality and international heritage. An examination of current issues on such topics as economic agreements, environment, education, health system, and multicultural relations.

title: Foreign Study
description: Foreign study is a means of granting Ball State University credit for course work undertaken abroad at institutions of higher learning (e.g., universities, centers, and institutes) as part of approved study programs. Applicable toward majors, minors, or general education with departmental approval. Prerequisite: acceptance in a Ball State exchange program or approved studyabroad program. A total of 32 hours of credit may be earned. The course is offered for credit/nocredit only.

title: Honors Symposium in Global Studies
description: Focuses on the commonalities and rich diversities in global culture, economy, history, politics, and society. Taught from varied perspectives or disciplines; emphasis is on the non-Western world—Asia, Africa, and Central and South America.

title: Honors Symposium in Contemporary Civilization
description: An examination of some of the critical issues that confront contemporary civilization. Open only to students participating in the Honors College.

title: Honors Humanities 2: Middle Ages, Renaissance, Enlightenment
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the Middle Ages, Renaissance, and Enlightenment. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Humanities 3: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Biology and Human Concerns
description: Basic introduction to biological principles using humans as the major organism and emphasizing the relationship of contemporary biology to human concerns and society. Included in the course are social and ethical consequences of scientific discoveries and their societal application . Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to students who have credit in HONRS 299.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Human Genetics and Bioethics
description: A General Studies science course. Applying personal knowledge toward the solution of some critical biological issues confronting contemporary society. Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to students who have credit in HONRS 298.

title: Honors Colloquium
description: Exploration of selected issues linking several disciplines. Emphasis is on discussion, individual projects, and ways of combining information from several sources. Open only to honors students by permission. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Candidate
description: May be taken each semester by honors candidates who have already registered in previous semesters for all of their undergraduate course work, including HONRS 499, but have not yet completed their senior honors projects. Students enrolled in this course are entitled to ordinary undergraduate student use of library, health, and other university facilities.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An inquiry culminating in an honors paper prepared in accordance with accepted standards of documentation and presentation under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to seniors participating in the Honors College or completing the requirements for departmental honors.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Available for advanced standing credit only and not through registration. Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experience meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the registrar. The Office of Academic Advising is informed of how the credit is to be applied to students' programs. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned. AFRICAN-AMERICAN STUDIES The African-American studies minor explores the culture of black Americans and Africans to help all students understand themselves and relationships between blacks and whites. The knowledge of American, Caribbean, and African societies prepares students for careers in multinational business, multicultural education, law, journalism, radio, television, social work, and urban planning. For more information about this program, call the history department at (317) 285-8700. DEPARTMENTAL MINOR IN AFRICAN-AMERICAN STUDIES, 18-20 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS

title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Survey of American studies as a field and as an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American civilization. Methods and theories of American studies will be discussed, along with major themes and topics in American life and thought. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 101.

title: Reading and Independent Study
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor who has expertise in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the American Studies director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Selected Topics in American Studies
description: Survey and investigation of a specific topic, issue, or problem in American studies. Particular subject matter will be announced before each offering. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ANCIENT STUDIES ASIAN STUDIES See College of Sciences and Humanities. Through the Department of Counseling Psychology and Guidance Services, the Institute of Gerontology offers a minor in the study of aging and the aged. The institute also consults with community organizations that provide direct services to the elderly, the Indiana State Commission on the Aging and Aged, the state network of Area Agencies on Aging, and nursing homes. For more information call the institute at (317) 285-1293. DEPARTMENTAL MINOR IN GERONTOLOGY, 24 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS

title: Women's Studies
description: Introduction to women's studies. Womancentered interdisciplinary investigation into women's experience in western culture and introduction to the discipline of women's studies.

title: Paid Internship
description: Supervised work in paid job settings in which students integrate job experiences with their acquired knowledge of women's studies. Involves assigned duties in an organization, agency, corporation, or business, with appropriate monetary compensation. Prerequisite: WMNST 210 and permission of the women and gender studies program director. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Mentorship
description: Supervised participation in a mentorship relationship in which students gain workrelated experience and apply acquired knowledge of women's studies. Involves voluntary participation in an organization, agency, corporation, or business. Prerequisite: WMNST 210 and permission of the women and gender studies program director A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Topics
description: Survey and investigation of genderrelated topics or issues in women's studies with emphasis on material not covered by existing courses. Exact content announced in advance of each offering. Prerequisite: permission of the women and gender studies program director. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with instructors with special competence in the topic involved. The credit hours may be accumulated in more than one semester. Prerequisite: permission of the women and gender studies program director. Wittig, Assistant Dean The College of Applied Sciences and Technology prepares men and women in five professional areas. Programs are administered through the Departments of Home Economics, Industry and Technology, and Military Science and the Schools of Nursing and Physical Education. Bachelor's degrees are offered in each area except for the Department of Military Science, which offers a minor in military science. Associate degrees are offered in the Department of Home Economics, Industry and Technology, and Nursing. As the name of the college implies, the programs emphasize the application of knowledge. DEPARTMENT OF HOME ECONOMICS S. Whitaker, Chairperson; L. Altman, R. Carr, L. Corso, C. Earhart, A. Finn, J. Jandiah, E. Lacey, W. Landis, J. Miller, J. Roepke, A. Spangler, H. Steele, J. Wittig The mission of the Department of Home Economics is to prepare a diversity of students who will be uniquely qualified and committed to improving the quality of life for individuals, families, and other groups. This mission is accomplished through the application and integration of knowledge and skills from home economics enhanced by those of the physica and behavioral sciences, technology, the humanities, business, and education. Specializations in this department will continue to evolve to meet the changing needs of society. The dietetics and dietetic technology programs are approved by the American Dietetics Association. ASSOCIATE DEGREES ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE—DIETETIC TECHNOLOGY, 65-66 hours Selection and Retention Standards Freshman Year. To qualify for selection to this program students must apply for the program during fall semester; enroll in HEFN 110, 262, and 340; earn grades of B or better in HEFN 262 and C or better in HEFN 110 and 340; have completed at least 12 hours; and have overall gradepoint averages of at least 2.0 at the end of fall semester. Sophomore Year. To qualify for retention students must complete HEFN 263, 292, 294, and 343 with grades of B or better and HEFN 342 and 352 with grades of C or better. Repetition of HEFN courses is permitted once. PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS General education, 19-20 hours

title: Introduction to Home Economics
description: Career opportunities available in the profession of home economics; introduction to Ball State home economics programs, facilities, staff; development of home economics as a profession. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles to be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Internship in Home Economics
description: Gives students the opportunity to work in established internship settings to gain professional experience in their areas of study. Open to all departmental majors and will be substituted for required practicum with permission of program directors.

title: Home Economics Field Studies
description: Combines reading knowledge with field experiences in which students study special topics in home economics in a particular location. Open to all students with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Workshop: Home Economics
description: Activityoriented study of one topic in home economics. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Home Economics
description: Independent investigation and exploration of a topic in home economics. Emphasizes extensive reading and the development of research skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Home Economics
description: Presentations and discussions on selected topics of current interest in home economics. Focuses on a different topic in home economics each semester the course is offered. Prerequisite: junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Professional Development in Home Economics
description: Examines the skills needed in getting a job, emphasizing résumé writing, interviewing, and dress. Explores such topics as adjusting, succeeding, and growing as a professional in one's chosen career. Prerequisite: senior standing. HOME ECONOMICS: EDUCATION (HEED)

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Applies the principles and philosophies of vocational education to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image.

title: Home Economics Presentation Techniques
description: Analysis of audience and business needs and the development of presentations and projects to meet these needs. Includes selection and use of presentation methods, development and use of devices, and professional roles and expectations. Open to all departmental majors in home economics and dietetics. Not open to students with teaching majors in vocational home economics.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Home Economics
description: Organization of teaching units and lesson plans; selection and use of teaching methods and materials. Prerequisite: identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Practicum in Home Economics
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of home economicsrelated work chosen by the student. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: HEED 392, 395.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: Coordination of class instruction and work experience. Includes recruiting, selecting, supervising, and evaluating students; selecting training stations; working with an advisory committee, role of coordinator, techniques and legal concerns of coordination, and placement and followup of graduates. Prerequisite: HEED 392, 395. HOME ECONOMICS: FOODS AND

title: Food Preparation and Meal Planning
description: Designed for students not majoring in home economics. Fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals with emphasis on correct techniques and methods of food preparation. Not open to students who have credit in HEFN 110.

title: Principles of Food Preparation
description: Fundamental principles underlying the preparation of food. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation.

title: Food Experimentation and Comparison
description: Effects of different ingredients and methods of determining quality of products. Emphasizes recognition of standard products and ability to recognize reasons for failure to achieve standard products. Application of scientific principles to manipulative techniques of food preparation. Prerequisite: HEFN 110. Not open to students who have credit in HEFN 430.

title: Meal Management
description: Principles and fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically appealing meals, with emphasis on resource management and the purchase and storage of food. Attention is given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Prerequisite: HEFN 110.

title: Nutrition
description: Emphasis is on fundamental principles of nutrition and application to diets of children and normal adults. Not open to students who have credit in HEFN 340.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industry, and commercial operations. Experience in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration
description: Emphasis is on organizational structure, scientific management, and personnel administration. Experience in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of home economics and food production personnel.

title: Food Equipment, Sanitation, Employee Training Experience
description: Selected experiences related to foodequipment use, sanitation, and employee training in a quantity foodservice setting. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Quantity Food-Service Personnel Management Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experience in personnel management in a quantity food_ service setting. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HEFN 263 and 363.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Purchasing Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experiences related to menu planning and purchasing in a variety of quantity foodservice organizations. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition
description: Nutritive value of foods and the use of food by the human body. Nutritional needs of people throughout the life cycle. Prerequisite: junioror seniorlevel standing; a major in nursing, food management, or dietetic technology; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Dietary modifications needed by people with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: HEFN 340. Not open to students who have credit in HEFN 441.

title: Normal and Therapeutic Nutrition Supervised Field Experience
description: Experience with professional standards and supervision related to normal and therapeutic nutrition in clinical and community settings. Prerequisite: HEFN 342 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Nutrition problems and programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Investigation and observation of and participation in nutrition programs in the local community. Prerequisite: HEFN 340.

title: Nutritional Management of Disease
description: Physiological basis for nutritional management of patients who have needs related to diabetes, cardiovascular disease, hemodialysis, nutrition support, inborn errors of metabolism, and metabolic stress. Documentation of nutrition care, quality assurance, and nutrition counseling are emphasized. Prerequisite: HEFN 342, 343, 490, and permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in HEFN 441. Open only to dietetic technology students.

title: Quantity Food Production and Equipment
description: Problems involved in quantity food production, distribution, and storage. Stationary and small equipment for food preparation. Kitchen layouts. Prerequisite: HEFN 110, 220.

title: Institutional Administration
description: Concepts of quantity food service in Home Economics 59 restaurants, schools, hospitals, and cafeterias. Emphasis on personnel, management, organization, cost control, and labor apportionment. Fi ▪ eld trips to institutional kitchens.

title: Quantity Food Purchasing and Menu Planning
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers and important considerations in purchasing foods. Emphasizes menu planning with consideration given to meeti ▪ ng nutritional needs. Prerequisite: HEFN 220, 340.

title: Nutrition Counseling
description: Integrates nutrition knowledge and techniques of nutrition counseling. Introduction to information gathering, assessment of problems, development of methods and materials for nutrition counseling intervention. Prerequisite: HEFN 340.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of foods in relation to their composition, physical and chemical properties, and circumstances affecting food quality. Investigates recipes and develops and evaluates methods of combining ingredients. Prerequisite: HEFN 110.

title: Advanced Nutrition
description: Advanced course in nutrition, emphasizing the use and metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Current research in the field of nutrition. Includes laboratory experiences. Prerequisite: HEFN 340 and CHEM 231; senior standing.

title: Diet in Disease and Nutrition Assessment
description: Dietary modifications and treatment of various nutritional diseases and problems. Techniques needed to identify persons at risk of nutritional deficiency. Includes laboratory experiences. Prerequisite: HEFN 440 or permission of the department chairperson, senior standing. Open only to dietetic students.

title: Seminar in Dietetics
description: The professions involved in food service and dietetics; the roles and responsibilities of personnel, their relationships with other professionals, and standards to be attained; the code of professional ethics and the resources for continuing professional education. Prerequisite: 2 hours of credit in a nutrition or dietetic technology practicum or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition, Weight Control, and Exercise
description: Designed for students in dietetics, physical education, and healthrelated fields. Information and experience for students preparing to provide nutrition counseling to people in weightcontrol and exercisetraining programs. Prerequisite: HEFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Nutrition Counseling Practicum
description: Students provide nutrition counseling for pregnant women, families with infants, young and teenage children, and people seeking guidance for weight control and special problems. Students are supervised by a member of the American Dietetic Association. Prerequisite: HEFN 340, 370, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Food Service Management Practicum
description: Experience in a food service organization, either in the private or public sector. Emphasizes development of food management expertise. Practicum approved and supervised by the Department of Home Economics. Prerequisite: HEFN 360, 364; senior standing; permission of the department chairperson; and documented completion of at least 500 hours of appropriate foodservice experience.

title: Seminar in Foods and Nutrition
description: Student presentations and discussions on specific topics of current interest in foods and nutrition. Prerequisite: senior standing; permission of the department chairperson. HOME ECONOMICS: HUMAN SERVICES (HEHS)

title: Family Wellness
description: Investigates the physical, mental, and social components of wellness, focusing on their interaction with the individual, family, and community.

title: Infant Development
description: Growth and development from conception through the second year of life. Includes physical, social, emotional, and cognitive development. Students observe and interact with infants and toddlers. Open to all students.

title: Child Development
description: Emphasis is on the preschool child as a member of a family group. Includes principles of natural growth and development and child guidance based on the physical, social, emotional, and intellectual needs of the preschool child. Students will participate in and observe various early childhood programs and centers. Open to all students.

title: Life Management
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desired goals in the family. Practical application of management principles to daily experience. Open to all students.

title: Energy and Equipment in the Home
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Current legislation, methods of conservation, energy concerns, and cost. Emphasis is on the role of technological developments in the home. Development and evaluation of presentation techniques.

title: Advanced Life Management
description: Practical application of the principles of life management. Emphasis on stress management, effective communication, and application of principles in relation to specific resources. Prerequisite: HEFN 220. Prerequisite or parallel: HENS 340.

title: Consumer Education
description: Economic considerations of purchasing for consumers, including current consumer legislation, marketing conditions, influence of advertising, consumer credit, agencies that protect consumers, and points to consider when buying consumer goods and services. Open to all students.

title: Marriage
description: The dynamics of the marital relationship and the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasizes the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection, marital communication, sexual adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasizes marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment. Open to juniors and seniors or by , permission of the department chairperson.

title: Functional Home Design Practicum
description: Gives students onthejob work experience with professional supervision in functional home design. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Family Relations
description: History and recent trends and developments in familylife education, career opportunities involved in familylife education, professional organizations, and ethical standards. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson and junior or senior standing. HOME ECONOMICS: MERCHANDISING (HEMER)

title: Clothing in the Environment
description: Analysis of dress and adornment with emphasis upon dimensions that affect the design, production, and end uses of textiles and clothing. Not open to students who have credit in HEMER 104.

title: Fundamentals of Apparel Construction
description: Basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, and art principles as applied to clothing design. Not open to students who have credit in HEMER 104.

title: Introduction to Clothing
description: Basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, the apparel industry, and social and psychological aspects of clothing.

title: Creative Stitchery
description: Creative skills in stitchery used to embellish existing fabrics or to create new ones. Techniques include macrame, crocheting, knitting, quilting, appliqueing, trapunto, embroidery, and needlepoint; rya, braided, and hooked rugs. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Merchandising Mathematics
description: Study of fundamental quantitative issues related to fashion merchandising and retail management. Basic mathematical computation used in the retail and wholesale markets.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: HEMER 104 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Interior Design and Home Furnishing
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior of the home and adapted to family needs. Open to all students.

title: Consumer Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, aesthetic qualities, and satisfying family life. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Textiles
description: Study of textiles and their components (fiber, yarn, fabric, and finishes) as they relate to care, performance, quality, and customer satisfaction. Required of students majoring in merchandising. Not open to students who have credit in HEMER 250.

title: Household Textiles
description: Study of the care, performance, quality, and customer satisfaction of household textiles. Required of students majoring in merchandising with a housing/home furnishings emphasis. Not open to students who have credit in HEMER 230.

title: Evolution of Costume
description: A study of Western costume from its beginning to the present. Emphasis on motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Prerequisite: HEMER 230 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: A survey of the business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, and promotion. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adapting standard patterns to individual proportions, designing garments, and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Use of computeraided design to produce a pattern for an original garment. Prerequisite: HEMER 104, 203.

title: Apparel Design by the Draping Method
description: Basic knowledge of apparel design using the draping method. Prerequisite: HEMER 101, 102, 203, 300.

title: Advanced Housing/Home Furnishing Design
description: Integration of design and furnishings and their application to home interiors. Technical presentations based on specialized problems of designing and planning home interiors. Prerequisite: HEMER 210, 250.

title: Furniture Design and Construction
description: Promotes awareness of available furniture materials, fabrication techniques, usage, and application in furniture construction. Study of furniture styles and design. Prerequisite: HEMER 210, 250.

title: Visual Merchandising
description: Study of the relationship between visual merchandise presentations and sales promotion in fashion retailing and wholesaling. Basic principles of art design, as applied to merchandise display, are examined.

title: Fashion Product Analysis
description: Study of conditions that contribute to the quality of fashionrelated merchandise. Provides an opportunity to become skillful in evaluating the materials and construction quality and techniques used in the textile and apparel industry. Prerequisite: HEMER 101, 102, 230.

title: Study of Fashion Designers and Forecasting
description: Study of present and historical fashion designers from around the world. Emphasis on understanding their contributions to the fashion industry and their influence in today's fashion markets. Prerequisite: HEMER 270.

title: Fashion Buying and Merchandising
description: Gives potential retailers the knowledge base to make decisions on buying and merchandising to satisfy customers and maintain an adequate profit level. Prerequisite: HEMER 270.

title: Fashion Illustration
description: Basic knowledge of drawing the fashion figure and of fashion illustration.

title: Computer-Aided Design for Apparel
description: Basic knowledge of the use of Industry and Technology 61 computeraided design (CAD) in fashion apparel designing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Apparel Manufacturing and Wholesaling
description: Study of garment manufacturing and the decision making involved in producing, marketing, and merchandising apparel and other fashionrelated products. Prerequisite: HEMER 101, 102, 203, 230, 270.

title: International Apparel Markets
description: An overview of the global textile and apparel industries. Considers the U.S. textile complex and market in an international context. Prerequisite: HEMER 230, 270; MKG 300; ECON 201.

title: Studio Design
description: Experience in designing, producing, and showing a line of clothing. Prerequisite: HEMER 260, 303, 365, 380, 401, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: HEMER 481.

title: Fashion Promotion
description: Study of promotional strategies used by fashion retailers and manufacturers. Students will analyze and evaluate the efficacy of various types of media in relationship to accomplishing a firm's promotional objectives. Prerequisite: HEMER 270; MKG 300.

title: Merchandising Practicum
description: Gives the trainee actual experience under professional standards, regulations, and supervision in an establishment chosen by the student. Prerequisite: HEMER 220, 310, 345, 370, senior standing, or permission of the instructor.

title: Developing a Portfolio
description: Opportunity to develop a suitable portfolio of graphic representations of work that can be used for job interviews. Prerequisite: HEMER 210, 220, 310, senior standing, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Merchandising
description: Exploration and integration of concepts related to the various elements of merchandising. Prerequisite: HEMER 270 and senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY D. Smith, Chairperson, W. Baldwin, S. Baylor, S. Byers, R. DeKeyser, T. Gurbach, R. Handy, R. Henak, J. Kirkwood, H. Khan, A. Leduc, C. McLaughlin, C. Ridgeway, R. Seymour, R. Shackelford, R. South, G. Steele, T. Tomlinson, J. Toppen, J. Wescott, J. Wickman, R. Wright Preparing students for challenging careers in industry and teaching is the major focus of the Department of Industry and Technology. Bachelor's degree programs in manufacturing engineering technology, industrial technology, graphic arts management, industrial technology teacher education, and vocational teacher education prepare students for a broad range of such careers. Associate degree programs in manufacturing technology, printing technology, and industrial supervision offer students the opportunity to acquire solid technical and supervisory preparation for many types of career. Credits earned in associate degree programs will transfer to related bachelor's degree programs in the department. Cooperative work experience and internships are optional in the technology and graphic arts programs and are arranged in a wide variety of industries for students seeking firsthand experience in the daytoday operations of contemporary industries. Qualified students enrolled in bachelor's degree programs in industry and technology may choose cooperative education programs after completing their freshman year of study. Students arrange coop jobs through the cooperative education coordinator. The university cannot guarantee a work assignment. ASSOCIATE DEGREES ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE— MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY, 63-66 hours This associate degree program is designed to prepare people for positions as technicians in the manufacturing industries. Graduates of the program accept jobs as computeraided drafting technicians, manufacturing technicians, production planners, and technical representatives. The program is designed for people who are currently employed as well as people desiring employment in technical positions in manufacturing. Graduates of this program may transfer to the baccalaureate program in Manufacturing Engineering Technology with little or no loss of credit. title: Introduction to Woods
description: Basic course in wood processing for persons interested in consumer information related to wood products and how wood can be worked to produce a desired effect or product. A portion of the class time will be set aside for studentdesigned product construction so that each student can receive individual assistance.

title: Cabinetry Design and Fabrication
description: Application of design and fabrication principles as they relate to residential, business, and industrial cabinetry. Activities will include the design and detailing of typical cabinets and the construction and finishing of a student designed product.

title: Maintaining a Home
description: Includes opportunities to learn basic terminology, to perform routine preventive maintenance and to make simple modifications and installations in plumbing, electrical circuits, general carpentry, painting, and climatecontrol systems of the home.

title: Building Diagnostics
description: Overview of building construction and energy systems, energy audit techniques, principles of heat transfer, and air movement. Field and laboratory work to include pressurization and remote heatsensing devices to measure energy loss in building systems and thermal envelopes. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Private Pilot Ground Training
description: Designed to qualify students for the Federal Aviation Agency written examination for the Private Pilot Certificate. Not open to persons currently holding any FAA certificates or ratings.

title: Industrial Arts for Elementary Grades
description: Industrial arts emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and industrial processes that provide an enrichment of the elementary program. Examines and evaluates methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Society and Technology
description: Provides an overview of the development, societal effects, and future implications of technology. Course work is designed to address human abilities to integrate resources to solve socialtechnical problems.

title: Technical Communication Systems
description: The elements, relationships, and operations of technical communication CR HRS Systems. Major emphasis is given to communication systems with laboratory experiences in the design, production, and transmission of various messages.

title: Construction Technology
description: Focuses on construction and management practices used to design, engineer, and construct residential, commercial, ndustrial, and civil structures.

title: Manufacturing Materials and processes
description: Properties of ceramic, metallic, polymeric, and composite materials and techniques used to convert these materials into products.

title: Product and Structure Design
description: Introduces the design process and methodology used to create and transmit technical ideas using graphic methods. Major emphasis is given to technical designing, sketching, pictorial drawing, orthographic projection, charting and graphing, and reprographics as applied to developing products and structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150.

title: Energy Systems
description: Focuses on inputs, processes, and outputs associated with energy systems. Emphasis on the sources of energy; methods of controlling, converting, and transmitting energy; and the use of energyconversion systems.

title: Manufacturing Material Processing
description: Provides experiences necessary to develop essential competencies required to perform common manufacturing processes with ceramic metallic polymeric, and composite materials. Prerequisite: ITEDU 153.

title: Graphic Communication Systems
description: Focuses on visual communication media as a technical communication system. Major laboratory activities emphasize design, development production, and dissemination of graphic messages. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154.

title: Transportation Systems
description: Focuses on powered transportation systems used to move people and goods. Emphasizes land, water, air, and space vehicles and transportation systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158.

title: Vocational Student Organizations
description: Emphasizes the implementation maintenance, and evaluation of vocational student organizations.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Analyzes legislation in the light of past and present issues of vocational education and its function as a vital component of the educational system.

title: Exploring Industrial Technology Education
description: Teaching contemporary industrial technology education as a Career. Students learn about the development and kinds of industrial technology programs and engage in activities that emphasize the curriculumdevelopment process.

title: Constructing Structures
description: Comprehensive study of the activities involved in preparing to build, construct, and complete residential, commercial industrial, and civil structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154, and 253 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Electronic Communication Systems
description: Introduces the principles, components, and operation of electronic communication systems. Emphasizes design production and transmission in telecommunication information processing, and acoustical systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150, 158.

title: Industrial Control Systems
description: Overview of the various methods used in controlling power in the industrial setting. Emphasis is on the application of computers and other controlling devices and systems within the manufacturing, construction, communication, and transportation industries. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158, 357, or ITMFG 270.

title: Manufacturing Enterprise
description: Introduces students to the managed activities used to design, engineer, produce, and market products with additional emphasis on providing financial and personnel support for these activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154, 253.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by breakdown into jobs, tasks, and processes.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance by the teacher. Examines and evaluates educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching JH/MS Technology Education
description: Problems in developing and implementing instructional strategies; preparing evaluation instruments, planning, specifying, and managing the physical environment; and establishing and maintaining a cooperative classroom environment. Topics developed in the context of junior high and middle school and field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298.

title: Strategies for Teaching Technology Education
description: Involves development and use of problemsolving, studentcentered, cooperative group, criticalthinking, and experiential strategies for teaching technology education. Includes opportunities to develop instructional media and work with students' special needs. Topics are developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 395.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Technology Education
description: Emphasizes contemporary approaches to curriculum development and the preparation of instructional materials for use in industrial technology education. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in a public school setting. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298 and 395.

title: Industrial Research and Development
description: Focuses on the methodology and practices of technical research and development as conducted in an industrial setting. Laboratory activities allow students to perform basic tasks associated with product and process research and development. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 161.

title: Community Planning
description: Activities involved in planning communities. Emphasizes construction, demand, and site conditions related to developing housing, streets, utilities, schools, transportation systems, parks, shopping areas, and recreational centers for public needs. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154.

title: Technical Experiences in Material Processing
description: Development of advanced competencies in casting and molding, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing processes. Prerequisite: ITEDU 253.

title: Technical Experience in Communication
description: Development of advanced competencies in the graphic, photographic, and electronic elements of communication technology. Prerequisite: ITEDU 254, 357

title: Design and Evaluation of Transportation Systems
description: Design and operation of transportation systems. Emphasizes technical elements typical of transportation systems: control, guidance, suspension, propulsion, structure, and support. Prerequisite: ITEDU 258.

title: Study in Industrial Technology Education
description: Special investigation in industrial technology education on an independent basis. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis on state functions. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY: GRAPHIC ARTS/PRINTING (ITGRA)

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: A comprehensive study of the graphic arts industry that focuses on products, reproduction processes, materials, equipment, and graphic arts careers. Related areas of instruction include design, relief printing, photooffset lithography, screen printing, color reproduction, and finishing operations.

title: Relief Printing and Bindery
description: A general applications course in relief printing and basic bindery operations found in the graphic arts industries. Major areas of instruction include copy preparation, typesetting, camerawork, conventional and photopolymer platemaking, presswork, paper, and ink.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 1
description: Introductory course in photooffset lithography that includes planning and layout, copy preparation, phototypesetting, line and halftone camerawork, platemaking, presswork, and introduction to fourcolorprocess printing.

title: Screen Printing
description: Screenprinting process as it relates to the graphic arts and printing industry and as an auxiliary manufacturing process in other industries. Topics include products, materials, equipment, techniques, inksubstrate relationships, estimating, and product design.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 2
description: Study of contemporary applications of photooffset lithography in commercial printing and publishing. Reviews layout and planning, pasteup, camera, stripping, plates, and press. Emphasis is on camera, stripping, and single and multicolor press operations. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182.

title: Photography
description: Emphasizes camera types, exposure techniques, film characteristics and selection, blackandwhite and color film processing, printmaking, print finishing, and composition. Related areas include special photographic applications and introduction to color photography.

title: Typesetting and Copy Preparation
description: The use, operation, and application of machine principles and mechanisms as related to typesetting. Typography, copy preparation, and copyfitting are emphasized in addition to various methods of type generation.

title: Printing Estimating 1
description: Introduction to contemporary estimating practices. Emphasizes production planning, development of hourly cost and production rate standards. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 182.

title: Graphic Arts Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a graphic arts industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for printing technology and graphic arts 'management majors. Prerequsie permission of the cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Graphic Arts Practicum
description: Emphasizes internal or external placement in a graphic arts setting selected and approved by the department. Provides opportunities to integrate and expand on theory gained during course work. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Quality Control in the Graphic Arts
description: Explores the basic professional practices of quality control for printed products. Focuses on instrumentation used in evaluating material and products inspection and sampling techniques, manufacturing specification, analysis techniques, and control systems found in the graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Commercial Printing
description: Studies the organization and production systems of commercial printing and publishing. Emphasizes management and production systems, quality control, material control, scheduling, and production specifications. Class organizes a system and manufactures production jobs during semester. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Color as it relates to photography with emphasis on additive and subtractive color processes, films, film processing, printmaking (additively and subtractively), measurement, design and composition principles. Prerequisite: ITGRA 286 or ADS 231 or JOURN 230 or the equivalent.

title: Color Separation and Process Printing
description: Study of color reproduction procedures in the graphic arts industries. Emphasizes additive and subtractive processes of color, direct and indirect separation procedures, color measurement, registration systems, and quality control procedures for color reproduction. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182, 286, 387.

title: Colloquium and Senior Project in Graphic Arts Management
description: Study and application of concepts, issues, and technological developments unique to the graphic arts. Topics include flexography, computer applications, electronic pagination, color scanning, and intaglio printing. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385.

title: Printing Management
description: Examines planning, organizing, controlling, and motivation as they relate to managing a business. Emphasis is on human relations decision making, problem solving, and coordination of management, sales, and production for successful management. Prerequisite: ITGRA 381, 385.

title: Printing Estimating 2
description: Sheetfed and web estimating. Emphasizes obtaining and interpreting specifications, pricing for profit margin, preparing quotations, printingtrade customs, multicolor presses, and signaturerelated bindery operations; application of the computer to estimating. Prerequisite: ITGRA 288.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Productioncontrol systems used in contemporary graphic arts industries. Topics include organization systems approach, decision making, production planning and control, purchasing, inventory control, quality control, work measurement, and cost analysis. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Technical Drawing and Print Reading
description: The theory and practice of basic production drawings and print reading. Topics include graphics language and design, instrumental drawing, lettering, geometric constructions, sketching and shape description, multiview projection, sectional views, pictorial views, dimensioning, fasteners, working drawings, and computer graphics.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Industries
description: Introduction to manufacturing and its managed activities of research and development, production marketing, industrial relations, and finance in manufacturing industries. Laboratory experiences involve organizing, staffing, and operating a model manufacturing enterprise. Prerequisite or parallel: ENG 103; appropriate 100-level math course. Open to all students except teaching majors in industrial education.

title: Computer-Aided Drafting and Computer-Applied Technology
description: Introduces computer drafting using an interactive software package on a microcomputer. Word processing and spreadsheet software packages are used to prepare and analyze technical reports. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105 or its equivalent.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: The theory and practice of preparing Productionrelated detail and assembly drawings in selected specialized areas and indepth study of geometric dimensioning. Topics include auxiliary views, cams, machine components, and welding drawings. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105.

title: Industrial Plastics
description: Study of industrial plastics processes and materials. Subjects will include injection molding, extrusion, blow molding, compression and transfer molding, thermoforming, rotational molding, dip coating and casting, decorating and finishing processes. Polymer chemistry is included. Laboratory activities for all processes. Prerequisite: CHEM 111.

title: Plastic Product Design and Mold Making
description: Plastic product design and moldmaking techniques. Individual problemsolving approach. Studies construction of the injection molds for thermoplastics. Appropriate moldmaking equipment demonstrated and used. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105, 225, 233.

title: Machine Tool Processing
description: Metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling and grinding machines, bandsawing, and EDM. Discussions include tool design, precision measurement, metallurgy, heat treating, and safety. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 108.

title: Manufacturing Materials
description: Study of tests used to characterize properties of ceramic, polymeric, and metallic materials and how material properties influence their use and manufacturing. Laboratory exercises involve testing procedures recommended by ASTM and currently used by industry. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 108; CHEM 111.

title: Applied Quality Control
description: Variables, procedures, and processes of total quality control within the manufacturing industries. Topics include instrumentation for material evaluation, attribute inspection and sampling, supervising for organizational quality improvements, and statistical control. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161; MATHS 181; or ECON 221.

title: DC Circuit Analysis
description: Study of theories, measurement, and applications of direct current. Topics include electron theory, components, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuit analysis, voltage and current dividers, electromagnetism, and mesh analysis. Laboratories include basic measurement in electric circuits using VOM and DVM. Prerequisite: MATHS 108 and PHYCS 110.

title: Automation and Computer- Integrated Manufacturing Systems
description: A comprehensive technical introduction to automation in manufacturing. Topics include flowline production, material handling, group technology, and flexible and computerintegrated manufacturing. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 362; MATHS 112 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Manufacturing Design with CAD
description: Emphasizes creating product and tooling drawings using a major computeraided design (CAD) system. Topics include twodimensional drafting, threedimensional wireframe and surface models, testing, dimensioning, flat pattern development, section and mass properties, and component libraries. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205 and 233.

title: Three-Dimensional Modeling
description: Theory of surface and solid geometric models with applications in the manufacturing industries. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 305; MATHS 161.

title: Programming Computer Graphics
description: Programming in FORTRAN and a graphics language such as Tektronix Interactive Graphics Language (IGL). Emphasis is placed on writing programs to create technical drawings and other graphical representations. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205 and a computer programming language.

title: Plastic Production Systems
description: Plastics processing with automatic production equipment. Emphasizes injection molding, extrusion, and thermoforming. Appropriate quality control and flowanalysis tests performed on production parts. Charts, graphs, and reports on products are prepared. Includes field trips to local plastics industries. Prerequisite: ITMFG 225, 325.

title: Advanced Plastics Mold Making
description: Designing and building automatic molds and dies for injection, extrusion, and compression molding. Ejection pins, water cooling lines, stripper plates, and interchangeable inserts included in the mold design and construction using automated machining equipment. Field trips to mold and die shops. Prerequisite: ITMFG 325.

title: Automated Machines
description: Theory and application of automated machines in the manufacturing environment. The laboratory focuses on the programming and operation of NC machine tools. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205, 233; MATHS 112.

title: Manufacturing Machine Tool Processing
description: Focuses on conditions that influence the control of metal manufacturing processes. Laboratory activities emphasize the significance of locators, power requirements, feeds, speeds, microstructure, coolants, and other variables. Complex operations are covered on grinding milling, EDM, and other multifunctionai machine tools. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233.

title: Casting and Bending Metals
description: Flatposition welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work with tungsten inert gas (TIG) and metal inert gas (MIG) equipment. Emphasizes various casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Applied Mechanics
description: Applications of statics and dynamics. Strength of materials with applications to problems in manufacturing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 262; MATHS 161; pHYCS 110.

title: Fixture Design for Metal Machining
description: Study of fixture design and other partholding systems used with metal machining. Discussion of common problems associated with fixtures when machining. Laboratory activities reinforce design concepts. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Fluid Power: Hydraulic Systems
description: An overview of the fundamentals of hydraulic systems with a review of basic equations regarding force, pressure, area, velocity, horsepower, volume, etc.; component types and designs; simplified hydraulic circuitry analysis; and basic maintenance and troubleshooting procedures. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270, 335; MATHS 161.

title: Industrial Safety and Health
description: Study of the practices used to optimize a safe and healthful environment for industrial personnel. Includes the requirements of safetyand healthregulating agencies, and hazard recognition and correction.

title: Manufacturing Processes
description: A systems approach to the analysis and planning of manufacturing processes. A quantitative evaluation of the parameters influencing product quality. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161, 233; MATHS 112 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Manufacturing Operations
description: Focuses on analyzing product designs and the design, engineering, and operation of industrial production systems through classroom and laboratory activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 105 and 161.

title: Technology Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a manufacturingrelated position in industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for industrial and manufacturing technology majors. Prerequisite: permission of the cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: AC Circuit Analysis
description: Studies the behaviors of inductors and capacitors under DC and AC, RLC circuits, series and parallel resonance, diodes and transistors, and power supplies and filters. Includes handson experience and project construction. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270 and MATHS 112.

title: Digital Electronics
description: Digital technology and its applications. Laboratory activities include digital circuit construction using mediumscale integration (MSI) and largescale integration (LSI) chips. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270.

title: Industrial Robots
description: The technology, applications, and management of industrial robots. Includes such topics as classifications, controls, sensors, programming, machine vision, robot workcell design, coordinates transformation, and feasibility study in robotics. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161, 270, 370, and computer programming experience.

title: Training and Development in Industry
description: Training and development in industry and their relationship to the job and the organization. Emphasizes skills needed to systematically plan, implement, evaluate, and revise training and development programs. Provides opportunities for practical application and practice.

title: Computer Design of Plastics Molds
description: Design of molds for plastics products by computer. Plastics flow analysis, cooling analysis, part shrinkage, and cost analysis using computer programs. Use of electroniccomponent and database catalogs. Prerequisite: ITMFG 305 and 325. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 1
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial plastics. May include mold making, materials testing, and equipment design. Prerequisite: ITMFG 326, 327.

title: Research and Development in Plastics 2
description: A continuation of ITMFG

title: Research and Development in Metals
description: Research and development of problems related to metals manufacturing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 333 and 334, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: Guest lectures on contemporary topics in manufacturing. Student presentations on capstone projects. Information and guidance in seeking employment in manufacturing. Prerequisite or parallel: ITMFG 473. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Manufacturing Controls
description: Studies the controls of manufacturing. Topics include cost estimation and control, manufacturing resources planning (MRP), justintime (JIT), group technology, production and inventory controls, statistical process control, management information systems (MIS), and other advanced control technology. A weekly laboratory is scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 301; MATHS 162 (waived for minors in industrial technology).

title: Industrial Programmable Controls
description: Emphasizes programmable controls in industry. Topics include relay controls programmable controller controls, and incremental motion controls. Laboratory activities involve control applications using motor control panel, programmable controller panel, and stepper and servo control trainers. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Microprocessor and Microcomputer Systems
description: The architecture, programming, interfacing, and applications of microprocessor and microcomputer systems. Laboratories involve programming in assembly codes for basic operations and interfacing applications. Prerequisite: ITMFG 371 and computer programming experience.

title: Electric Machines and Controls
description: Principles and applications of power transformers, DC and AC generators, and DC and AC motors; controls and testing of various machines. Laboratory experiments. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Projects in Computer-Aided Manufacturing
description: Individual project applying CNC, CAD, CAM, robotics, and other computerbased technology in manufacturing systems. Extensive laboratory work required. Prerequisite: senior standing. Parallel: ITMFG 463.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Study semiconductor devices, rectifiers, SCR, frequency conversion, digital and analog transducers, optoelectronics, operational amplifiers, and the industrial applications of these devices. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Industrial Electronics Fabrication
description: Focuses on printed circuit board design, development, fabrication, and production. Electronic inventory and component assembly are studied as they relate to the manufacturing process. Prerequisite: ITMFG 475 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Problems in Industrial Technology
description: Individual advanced study and experimentation in one or more of the areas of concentration: metals, plastics, design, or factory electronics. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. PURDUE UNIVERSITY—MECHANICAL

title: Production Drawing
description: Application of principles of engineering drawing to detail, assembly, design layout, equipment installations, and related drawings. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105.

title: Industrial Organization
description: Organizational structures, operational, financial, marketing, and accounting activities; duties of management, planning, control, personnel, safety, wages, policy, and human conditions necessary for effective management.

title: Applied Statics
description: A study of force systems, resultants and equilibrium, trusses, frames, beams, shear and moments in beams. Prerequisite: MATHS 112; PUMET 160.

Wolfe The nursing programs are designed to prepare students for careers as professional nurses and for graduate study. Graduates of the associate and baccalaureate degree programs are eligible to take the national licensure examination for registered nurses. Students pursuing the associate and baccalaureate degrees are classified as prenursing until selected into the nursing major. Registered nurses who do not have bachelor's degrees can enroll in a baccalaureate program to complete their degrees. The selection process for each nursing program is outlined in the program's statement of admission and progression policies. All policies are available from the School of Nursing. Applicants for the associate nursing program must submit a separate application and official copies of transcripts to the School of Nursing, as well as to the university. To enroll in NUR 111, students must have been selected into the associate nursing program. Students not selected must reapply to be considered for the next year. Applicants for the baccalaureate program selection must complete a minimum of 26 semester hours with a gradepoint average (G.RA.) of 2.3 or higher. Baccalaureate students must apply for permission to enroll in NUR 212 during the first ten days of the preceding semester. Applicants for NUR 212 are ranked based on the G.P.A. of all attempted undergraduate credit, including all attempted transfer hours. Students who are not admitted to NUR 212 must reapply for the next semester. Each applicant is required to sign an informed consent form related to risks and safeguards involved with possible exposure to infectious diseases. Applicants with records of substance abuse or convictions of violation of federal, state, or local laws related to controlled substances for any offense—misdemeanor or felony—may not be able to obtain licensure as registered nurses. Clearance from the Health Center, which usually takes two to three weeks, is required before taking NUR 111 or NUR 212. A grade of C or better is required in ANAT 201, PHYSL 210 and 211, BIO 113, and CHEM 101 in both nursing programs. Students who fail to earn the minimum required grades in clinical nursing courses and satisfactory performance evaluations may be dismissed from the program. The minimum acceptable grade in all required nursing courses is C. Repetition of a clinical nursing course is permitted only once and for only two courses. The National League for Nursing Diagnostic Readiness Test is required during the last semester of the program of study for the baccalaureate degree. The baccalaureate nursing program is accredited by the National League for Nursing; application for accreditation will be made in relation to the associate degree program. Most classes and laboratories are offered on the Ball State campus or in nearby hospitals and healthagency facilities. Access to a car is periodically required during clinical courses.
