description: Principles of basic keyboarding and typewriting application skills needed for using computer terminals or other office machines with typewriterstyle keyboards. For all students, particularly those for whom computer keyboarding skills are essential. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson for students with two or more semesters of high school or college keyboarding/typewriting credit.

title: Intermediate Keyboarding/ Typewriting
description: A refinement of basic keyboarding and touchtypewriting techniques, development of speed and accuracy, and the preparation of business letters, manuscripts, and tables. Prerequisite: BEOA 111 or one to two semesters of high school or college keyboarding/typewriting.

title: Advanced Keyboarding/Typewriting
description: Advanced problems in keyboarding/ typewriting, including reports, memoranda, letters, statistical tables, rough drafts, legal documents, and business forms. Continued speed and accuracy development. Prerequisite: BEOA 112 or three or more semesters of high school or college keyboarding/typewriting.

title: Business Information Systems
description: Basic concepts of information processing systems with emphasis on computer skills for generating business information, including computing concepts and procedures in business, computer applications, text editing, file processing, and use of commercial software packages on mainframe computers and microprocessors. Prerequisite: MATHS 108. Open only to business majors except by permission of the department chairperson.

title: BASIC Programming for Microcomputers
description: Introductory course in BASIC programming using microcomputer hardware and problemoriented programdevelopment techniques to analyze, design, and code BASIC programs in a structured environment. Prerequisite: Typewriting or keyboarding ability. Not open to students who have credit in CS 116.

title: Shorthand 1
description: Basic symbolic theory fundamentals with emphasis on abbreviated forms. Introduction to skills in writing and transcribing dictation. Student placement is based on departmental advising. Prerequisite: BEOA 112 or two semesters of high school or college keyboarding or typewriting.

title: Shorthand 2
description: Continued review of fundamentals; continued emphasis on taking dictation and developing transcription skills. Prerequisite: BEOA 222 or student placement based on departmental advising and BEOA 113 or three semesters of high school or college keyboarding or typewriting.

title: Microcomputer Applications for Business
description: Operation of microcomputers in processing business 3 hours from MGT 311 BEOA 251 applications using commercial software packages including spreadsheet, database manipulation, and text creation and editing. Prerequisite: typewriting or keyboarding ability.

title: Advanced Microcomputer Applications for Business
description: Advanced features of graphics, word processing, spreadsheets, and database application software. Emphasis is on the transfer of files and documents among various applications and systems. Prerequisite: BEOA 225 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Transcription
description: Designed to teach transcription skills as they apply to the typewritten production of business documents. Application of punctuation, number usage, word choice, spelling, proofreading, and use of reference sources through machine transcription. Prerequisite: BEOA 111 or two semesters of typewriting.

title: Machine Transcription
description: Designed to teach students to produce mailable copy from transcription equipment. Intensive drill on transcription skills with emphasis on quality production. Application of punctuation, spelling, vocabulary building, letter styles, placement, proofreading, and grammar to the transcription process. Prerequisite: BEOA 230.

title: Principles of Business Correspondence
description: Principles and basic elements of effective letter writing with emphasis on the psychological approach, reader point of view, positive tone, and appropriate format for personal and business letters and job applications.

title: Personal Word Processing and Graphics
description: Designed to acquaint nonmajors with the word processing and graphics capabilities of microcomputers. Handson instruction in information processing and presentation graphics. Cannot be substituted for BEOA 251. Prerequisite: BEOA 111 or high school typing credit. Not open to students who have credit in BEOA 251.

title: Introduction to Word and Information Processing
description: Focuses on understanding word processing concepts and how they fit into a total information processing system. Some handson experience with microcomputers. Prerequisite: BEOA 111 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Word and Information Processing Applications
description: Emphasizes advanced word and information processing applications, including merging, sorting, file management and transfer, macros, styles, graphics, and some desktop publishing. Prerequisite: BEOA 112 or permission of the department chairperson and BEOA 250 or 251. May not be taken concurrently with BEOA 253.

title: Word and Information Processing Hardware and Software
description: Comparison and evaluation of features and capabilities of a variety of word and information processing software and systems. Handson experience included. Emphasizes problem analysis to meet the needs of varying workplace situations. Prerequisite: BEOA 112 or permission of the department chairperson and BEOA 250 or 251. May not be taken concurrently with BEOA 252.

title: Secretarial Procedures and Administration
description: Operational functions of toplevel professional secretarial work through integration of basic skills, knowledge, human relations, and administrative elements of office work. Prerequisite: BEOA 112 and 241 or 441 and sophomore standing.

title: Office Technology Cooperative Education
description: Secretarial majors work in an office technologyrelated position to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. Paid work and learning experience for students accepted into the cooperative education program. Related class attendance is required. Prerequisite: permission of the cooperative education coordinator or the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Internship in Marketing Education
description: Fulltime employment in an approved marketing occupation under departmental supervision according to a formal training agreement with the employer. Provides experience in areas in which marketing education teachers instruct. Each hour of credit requires 375 hours of approved employment and submission of various reports by the intern and employer. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to students seeking licenses as marketing education teachers. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teleprocessing and Office Information Systems
description: Integration of electronic office equipment interconnected through telecommunications including concepts of data communications, electronic mail, and networks. Some handson laboratory experience with communicating word processors, microcomputers, and networks. Prerequisite: BEOA 210 or 225 or 251 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Desktop Publishing for Business
description: Preparation of materials for desktop publishing combining word processing and graphics based upon principles of page layout; comparative costs and appropriateness of various reprographic methods, software, and equipment. Some handson experience with microcomputers and laser printers. Prerequisite: Knowledge of microcomputer word processing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: International Business Communication
description: Explores the communication problems that executives face while working in an international business culture. Emphasis is placed on sensitizing students to important intercultural issues that can facilitate or frustrate international business transactions. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Records Administration
description: Administration and supervision of office records systems; knowledge, techniques, and skills involved in planning, controlling, organizing, selecting, and retaining records in business and industry. Some handson laboratory experience with office automation software for records processing and database management. Prerequisite: sophomore standing and BEOA 210 or 225 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Principles of Office Supervision
description: Principles of effective office supervision with emphasis on the function of the office and the role of the office supervisor. Prerequisite: MGT 200 or 300.

title: Internship in Office Systems Administration
description: Under a program approved and supervised by the business education and office administration department, students majoring in office systems administration will work in an office environment in a public or private organization. Written reports are required. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods of Teaching for the Marketing Education Teacher
description: The role of the marketing education teacher in the teaching of marketing, basic business, and bookkeeping/accounting subjects; courses to be taught and their objectives, teaching strategies, instructional materials, and lesson and unit planning. Prerequisite: ACC 201; ECON 201; EDPSY 251; and at least two courses in marketing. Open only to students majoring in marketing education.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Business Subjects, Majors 1 and 2
description: Objectives, planning, methods, techniques, devices for teaching typewriting, basic business, and office machines and office procedures courses. Prerequisite: BEOA 111 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280. Parallel: BEOA 338.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Accounting, Major 1
description: Objectives, planning, methods, materials, devices for teaching accounting. Prerequisite: ACC 201 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Parallel: BEOA 490. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Shorthand and Transcription, Major 2
description: Objectives, planning, methods, materials, and devices for teaching shorthand and transcription. Prerequisite: BEOA 112, 222; EDSEC 280; and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Parallel: BEOA 490.

title: Techniques of Coordinating Cooperative Marketing Education Programs
description: The special techniques and knowledge needed by a person who will be teaching and coordinating cooperative marketing education programs. Restricted to persons seeking licenses as teachers or coordinators of vocational marketing education. Prerequisite: BEOA 382 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Organization, Management, and Teaching: Vocational Marketing Education
description: The special techniques and knowledge needed by a person who will be teaching and managing inschool laboratory programs in vocational marketing education. Restricted to students seeking licenses as teachers or coordinators of vocational marketing education. Prerequisite: BEOA 382 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Philosophy, Organization, and Administration of Vocational Education
description: The principles upon which vocational education is organized, administered, and supervised; federal and state regulations; agencies that provide delivery systems for vocational education, relationship of vocational education to career education, vocational rehabilitation, and programs for persons with special needs. Prerequisite: BEOA 382 or 383 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Survey of the Vocational Education Program Areas
description: An overview of the six program areas in vocational education. Includes program administration and supervision, objectives, the occupations for which training is offered, curricula, equipment and facilities, student selection, inschool laboratories, fieldtraining opportunities, and youth organizations. Prerequisite: BEOA 382 or 383 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Microcomputers in Business Education
description: A handson approach to the use of microcomputers in the business education classroom; use of business software; analysis and design of programs for business education courses. Open only to students pursuing teaching majors in business or marketing teacher education or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Computerized Business Document Generation
description: An introduction to text editing capabilities of the computer for designing and processing business documents for the modern office. Development of an understanding of the use of the generalpurpose computer for text processing. Prerequisite: BEOA 210 or CS 116.

title: Communications for Business Organizations
description: Techniques used in managementoriented internal and external communications. Emphasis is on theory, planning, oral and written presentations, audience perceptions, data organization, media selection, and preparation techniques for business letters. Overview of reports. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Business Reports: Written and Oral
description: Techniques used in writing both formal and informal managementoriented reports, including collecting, interpreting, summarizing, and synthesizing data. Principles for selection of tabular and graphic data presentations. Includes written and oral presentations of functional reports with an overview of analytical reports. Prerequisite: sophomore standing.

title: Employment Communications
description: Determining job requirements and writing a letter of application and résumé; letters requesting reference permission appreciation of interview, acceptance and refusal of position, and resignation. Includes interview techniques. Open to all students.

title: Office Information Systems Management
description: Implementation and management of integrated office information systems. Study of managerial problems involved with people, procedures, and technology. Prerequisite: MGT 300 or its equivalent; BEOA 210 or 225 or 251; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Office Management and Control
description: The management of the business office as a producing unit and the relation of the office routine to managerial control of the other departments of a business through records, reports, and budgets. Prerequisite recommended: ECON 202 and MGT 300.

title: Principles of Business Education
description: The analysis of a total business education program and the integration of various facets that lead to sound instruction. The effects of past, present, and future legislative and societal developments. Parallel: BEOA 385 or 386. Open only to students approved to pursue a business teaching curriculum.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Marketing Education
description: An investigation of the current status, historical development, philosophy, and principles of marketing education. Components include secondary, postsecondary, and adult marketing education, DECA, and general and specialized curricula. Prerequisite: EDSEC 280. Open only to students pursuing the teaching major in marketing education.

title: Independent Study: Business or Marketing Education; Office Administration
description: For students with excellent academic records who wish to conduct an indepth study in some phase of business education, marketing education, or office administration. The project selected, methods, and credit hours must be approved by the department chairperson and supervising faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMICS T. Van Cott, Chairperson; C. Bohanon, C. Cheng, P. Coelho, C. Deitsch, M. Flowers, J. Horowitz, S. Keil, R. Lawson, T. Liu, J. McClure, H. Moehring, N. Palomba. G. Santoni, L. Spector, C. Stone, D. Yoho, A. Zegeye All societies face a conflict between unlimited desires for higher living standards and limited resources to satisfy these desires. Economics studies how societies resolve this conflict. Because many of our nation's social, political, and economic problems can be traced to this conflict, a knowledge of economics is important not only for intelligent citizenship but also for careers in business, government, and the professions. The Department of Economics offers a major with a business option and one with a liberal arts option. The business option is designed primarily for students planning to pursue professional careers in business. The liberal arts option is designed for students who want to Economics 117 pursue careers as professional economists. Both options make good prelaw school majors. A minor in economics is also available. The department also offers an interdepartmental major in mathematical economics. For information on this major, see Interdepartmental Programs, p. 43. Students may also select economics as a concentration area in either the teaching major or the teaching minor in social studies. DEPARTMENTAL MAJOR IN ECONOMICS, BUSINESS OPTION, 60 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS Common body of knowledge, 36 hours

title: Survey of Economic Ideas
description: The important conclusions of economics are surveyed and applied to topics chosen by 30 hrs CR HRS the instructor. Especially valuable to students with no high school background in economics. Not applicable to a major or minor in economics. Not open to students who have credit in ECON 201 or 202.

title: Elementary Microeconomics
description: A study of why people specialize as producers and exchange what they produce with others. Includes analysis of how market structure affects prices. Discusses the issue of whether selfinterested economic behavior promotes or hinders society.

title: Elementary Macroeconomics
description: Survey of the major explanations for fluctuations in general business conditions. Focuses on how the private sector's economic behavior is affected by various governmental policies and institutions. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Business Statistics
description: Introduction to various statistical and probabilistic concepts and techniques with application to business problems including random variables and probability distributions, measures of central tendency and ispersion, testing of hypotheses, simple linear regression, and correlation. Prerequisite: MATHS 132 or its equivalent. Prerequisite recommended: BEOA 210. Not open to students who have credit in MATHS 181.

title: Economic and Political Problems of Emerging Nations
description: A survey of historical and contemporary problems of the lessdeveloped nations. Conditions contributing to economic, political, and social change. Problems of economic development policies and programs within the institutional structure. Internal and external pressures that influence patterns of development. Not open to students who have credit in POLS 281.

title: Honors Colloquium in Economics
description: Exploration of selected issues, themes, problems, or interpretations with emphasis on individualized study and reporting. Restricted to honors students; others by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: An investigation of the ways in which economic units direct resources into production. Involves analyses of product pricing, output determination, resource pricing, and employment in various market structures. Includes graphical and, in some instances, simple algebraic analyses. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
description: Analyzes national income as a measure of economic activity. Emphasizes the determination of national income, employment, and price level and the rate of growth of the economic system. Includes examination of the theories of consumption and investment spending, interaction between money and national income, and implications of alternative models for public policy. Includes graphical and, in some instances, simple algebraic analyses. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Economic History of the United States
description: Survey of our commercial, financial, agricultural, and industrial history. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202, or a combination of ECON 201 and 3 hours of credit in United States history, or 6 hours of credit in United States history.

title: Environmental Economics
description: The application of economic principles to environmental problems. Emphasis is on applying the economist's decisionmaking model to environmental issues and the advantages and shortcomings of the economist's analysis. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 6 hours of credit in natural resources, NR 101, or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in NR 303.

title: Labor Economics
description: Economic problems of the wage earner; growth, structure, and policies of labor organization; and the employer and governmental policies toward labor. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Labor Relations and Law
description: Study of collective bargaining, the joint determination by employers and employees (through their representatives) of the problems of the employment relationship—encompassing both the negotiation and administration of the labor agreement with primary emphasis upon the rules governing these processes. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Economics of Government Budgets
description: Analysis of economic theory behind alternative methods of financing government budgets and debt management. Emphasizes economic consequences of budgets by examining incidence, shifting, and incentives regarding provision of public services and alleviation of economic insecurity. Inflation as tax is considered. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: International Economics
description: International trade, finance, and commercial policy. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Internship in Economics
description: Under a program approved and supervised by the Department of Economics, economics majors work fulltime for one semester as economics interns for private or public organizations. Periodic written reports of job experiences are required. Open only to secondsemester junior and senior economics majors. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Credit is not applicable toward meeting the requirements of a major in economics.

title: Industrial Organization
description: Monopolistic, oligopolistic, and competitive market structures. Unsettled issues concerning structure and conduct of industry; concentration, vertical integration, and problems of economic regulation by government. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Economic Growth
description: An analysis of the causes, mechanisms, and patterns of economic growth. Compares and analyzes growth rates of various countries. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: History of Economic Doctrines
description: The history of how humankind has looked at its economic life, surveys the changing ways economists have rationalized, articulated, and criticized economic organization from biblical times to the present. The successive reformulations place a major emphasis on the economic doctrines of the recent past and the present. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Mathematical Economics
description: Use of mathematics in the development of selected economic theories. Survey of inputoutput analysis and examination of the application of linear programming and the theory of games to selected economic problems. Prerequisite: ECON 201, 202; and MATHS 132 or its equivalent.

title: Introduction to Econometrics
description: Quantitative methods in economic Finance 119 research. Emphasis is on constructing economic models and testing their predictive power. Topics include correlation and regression techniques and the specific problems that arise in applying these to economic data. Prerequisite: ECON 201, 202, 221; MATHS 132 or its equivalent.

title: The Theory of Monetary Policy
description: A theoretical presentation of how the board of governors of the Federal Reserve System modifies the economic climate within which the institutions of the nation operate and of the problems of government finance as they relate to the board's goal of general economic stability. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Comparative Economic Systems
description: Historical and comparative study of economic theories and systems. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and 202.

title: Urban Economics
description: The systematic economic structure of cities and the component parts of that structure. Attention is given to the ways in which the economic structure of cities and regions obstructs or facilitates the attainment of the goals of the community. Prerequisite: ECON 201.

title: Readings and Directed Study in Economics
description: Students will pursue their interests in specialized economics subjects under the direction of a member of the economics staff. Subjects studied will differ from or be studied in greater depth than subjects treated in other economics courses. Prerequisite: 6 hours of credit in economics. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Economics
description: Topics center on economic problems and issues of special interest to students and instructor. Permits indepth studies of topics not formally treated in other courses, thereby exposing interested students to a wider variety of economic problemsolving situations. Prerequisite: ECON 201, 202, and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in one semester or term. DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE J. Fitzgerald, Chairperson; H. Banerjee, 0. Benkato, A. Caslan, C. Creviston, M. Engber, R. Groeber, H. Hammer, J. Hoban, P. Howard, K. Mantripragada, R. Rathinasamy, S. Sundaran, L. Sweeney, G. Wells, N. Williams Finance is the management of money to help businesses operate and grow. Businesses and financial institutions hire people to help plan and make decisions about using money and managing assets (property) and liabilities (debts). Programs in finance cover such topics as insurance, banking, financial management, and real estate. DEPARTMENTAL MAJOR IN FINANCE, 63 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS Common body of knowledge, 36 hours

title: Principles of Business Law
description: The nature, role, and historical development of the law and the structure and operation of our legal system. The essential elements of tort and contract law and the effect of the law in consumer credit and economic relationships. Prerequisite: sophomore standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: International Business Law
description: Examines legal problems that arise when multinational corporations conduct commercial activity in environments different in history, culture, economy and politics from domestic markets. Topics include treaties, constitutional law, antitrust, contract negotiation and drafting, civil procedure, and dispute resolution. Prerequisite: BL 260.

title: The Law of Business Associations
description: The principles of business law applicable to agencies including employer and employee rights and obligations, partnerships including limited partnership, corporations including fiduciary obligations of directors, security regulations, Finance 121 bankruptcy, and corporate reorganization in bankruptcy. Prerequisite: BL 260.

title: Uniform Commercial Code Law
description: Principal articles of the code including sales, commercial paper, and security interests, in addition to creditors' rights and property law. Includes state and federal consumer protection laws as they affect commercial law. Prerequisite: BL 260.

title: Law for Small Business
description: Analysis of the laws affecting small businesses. Emphasis is on the legal aspects and legal implications of formation of a business, employeremployee relationships, consumer protection laws, creditor rights, and closing the business. Prerequisite: BL 260.

title: Estate Planning and Administration
description: An introduction to problems associated with planning of financial resources during working life, retirement, and after the death of the principal income producer. Included are techniques for fact gathering, tax principles, use of trusts, and will drafting. Prerequisite: BL 260.

title: Current Topics in Business Law
description: Designed to meet the needs of advanced business students for study of current topics and problems in business law. Topics may include current activity in property law, commercial law, and government regulation of business. Prerequisite: BL 260 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Business Law
description: An opportunity for students with superior scholastic records to study some special phase of business law. The topic selected, methods of study, and credit hours allowed must be approved by the department chairperson. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Personal Finance
description: The fundamental principles of general business and related economic concepts are considered from the consumer's point of view. Some of the topics studied are consumer buying and the use of credit, banking, insurance, investment, budgeting, and taxation. Not open to juniors and seniors majoring in business.

title: Introduction to the U.S. Financial System
description: U.S. financial system and its functions; financial markets, instruments, and intermediaries; growing role of intermediaries in the saving and lending process and implications; regulation, regulatory agencies, and financial safety net; competition, innovation, and integration in financial services industry; globalization and international competition. Prerequisite: ACC 201; ECON 202. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles of Finance
description: Designed to study different areas of financial decision making in a business firm. Specific topics include financial objectives of the firm, sources of funds, working capital management, capital budgeting, investment decisions under uncertainty, valuation, capital structure decisions, and dividend policy. Prerequisite: ACC 202; ECON 201, 221; and junior standing.

title: Intermediate Financial Management
description: Devoted to the study of the current theory of finance. Topics include the nature and methodology of finance, efficient market hypothesis, portfolio theory and market equilibrium, optimal investment and financing decisions under certainty and uncertainty. Prerequisite: FIN 350.

title: Principles of Investments
description: Designed to introduce students to areas of investment: securities markets, transaction of stocks and bonds, valuation and timing, fundamental and technical indicators, money markets, and funds. Prerequisite: FIN 350 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Financial Markets and the Economy
description: Nature and functions of financial markets; classification and interrelation of domestic and international financial markets; determination of the level and structure of interest rates; effects of monetary policy on financial markets and the economy. Prerequisite: FIN 250, 350.

title: Internship in Finance
description: Professional practice during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a banking institution, business firm, or government agency for pay under the supervision of the finance department. Requires periodic written reports of job experience. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in combination with FIN 481.

title: International Finance
description: The financial problems and opportunities that confront the management of international firms. Sources and instruments of international finance, import and export financing, interrelationship of governmental and international agencies, and the current status of some. Prerequisite: FIN 350 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Theory
description: An indepth analysis of valuation theory, capital market theory, and portfolio theory. Prerequisite: FIN 350, 355.

title: Managerial Decision Making in Finance
description: A summary course devoted to the compilation of knowledge and the application of financial analysis to decision making in various subareas of finance. The course is conducted by means of case studies. Prerequisite: FIN 354.

title: Operations of Financial Institutions
description: To integrate the various topics of finance with a view toward applications to the management of financial institutions in the following decision areas: assetliability management, cost control, profitability, capital adequacy, business development. Cases will be integrated in the method of instruction. Prerequisite: FIN 354, 355, 356.

title: Finance Practicum
description: Professional practice (without pay) during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a banking institution, business firm, or government agency, under the supervision of the finance department. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in combination with FIN 369.

title: Independent Study in Finance
description: Designed for academically qualified students who want to study some phase of finance. An intensive individualized program of reading, researching, or analyzing various finance topics under the guidance of a faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles of Insurance
description: A survey of the major kinds of insurance such as fire, transportation, casualty, health, life insurance, and fidelity and surety bonds.

title: Fundamentals of Life Insurance
description: Important methods of handling personal risks for business and individuals. An analysis of life insurance, annuities, pension plans, and social insurance. Special attention is given to the problems of underwriting, rate computation, and programming. Prerequisite: INS 270.

title: Fundamentals of Liability Insurance
description: The study of liability insurance and worker's compensation insurance with special emphasis on the insurance needs of the commercial enterprise. Prerequisite: INS 270.

title: Fundamentals of Property Insurance
description: The study of property insurance, including fire and allied lines, inland and ocean marine, and crime insurance with special emphasis on the insurance needs of the commercial enterprise. Prerequisite: INS 270.

title: Legal Aspects of Insurance
description: The law as applied to the insurance industry emphasizing the law of torts as the foundation of the insurer's liability, the law of contracts and agency as applied to the insurance policy, and government regulation of insurance. Prerequisite: BL 260 and INS 270.

title: Current Topics in Insurance
description: Designed to meet the needs of advanced insurance students for study of current topics and problems in any insurance or risk management area. Topics may include nofault, competitive rating laws, variable life insurance, and state versus federal regulations. Prerequisite: INS 270, 371, 375, and 376 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Insurance
description: Designed for academically qualified students who want to study some phase of insurance. An intensive individualized program of reading, research, or analyzing various insurance topics under the guidance of a faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Real Estate Principles
description: The economic import of real estate, real estate characteristics, land use and environmental controls, legal aspects of real estate, methods of valuation, mortgage credit sources, secondary mortgage markets and financing techniques, investment analysis, land development, and real estate operations.

title: Real Estate Finance
description: The contractual nature and legal implication of the instruments used in real estate finance; instrument, techniques, and strategies in the financing of real estate investment; and the structure and operation of both primary and secondary mortgage markets. Gives students a background in real estate law and real estate finance. Prerequisite: RE 330.

title: Legal Aspects of Real Estate
description: Elementary concepts of real estate law and practice, particularly in the state of Indiana. Other topics include estates, property, leaseholds and ownerships, easements, transfers, escrows, contracts, zoning, brokers' regulations, license law, and title insurance.

title: Real Estate Analysis
description: The appraisal of real estate. In addition to the appraisal process, other analytical systems will be reviewed as they apply to the real estate industry, including the economic Management 123 base analysis, feasibility studies, and investment analysis. Prerequisite: RE 330.

title: Real Estate Administration
description: An orientation of the real estate business using test cases, incidents, and walking cases. Guest speakers who are experts in real estate will be invited to speak and answer questions. Prerequisite: RE 431 and senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF MANAGEMENT J. Gupta, Chairperson; N. Ahmed, I. Baird, J. Green, T. Harris, J. Hornsby, D. Kuratko, W. LaFollette, R. Montagno, D. Naffziger, R. Ramnarayanan, R. Ravichandran, I. Seeborg, B. Smith, J. Swart, E. Tunc, J. Walters Among modern organizations, there is a need for competent managers who can address emerging issues in a global economy. Dealing with environmental complexity, technology, employee productivity, international competition, and ethical issues is increasingly important in the managerial decision process. Programs leading to a bachelor of science degree in management are designed to give students the knowledge and skills in the latest concepts, tools, and techniques applicable to entrepreneurship and small business, human resources management, management information systems, production and operations management and general management. Students can elect to specialize in one of the following five options: The production and operations management option prepares students to assume positions of responsibility in the production of goods and services. Students are introduced to the production functions in detail, are taught the methodology of making productionrelated decisions, and become acquainted with modern techniques used in motivating and leading personnel in a productionoriented occupation. The human resources management option prepares students to improve the effectiveness of employees in organizations. Students study the personnel function and learn the conceptual framework for analyzing and solving problems in the selection, development, compensation, and motivation of human resources. The management information systems option introduces students to the concepts and techniques necessary to use information in the support of operations, control, and planning in organizations. Graduates of this option are familiar with the concepts and techniques of computerized information systems. The entrepreneurship and small business option is designed to give students the knowledge needed to work in a new venture environment. Students learn how to formulate a plan for an entrepreneurial venture and how to implement that plan. They become acquainted with elements of managementinformation systems and business law that are tailormade for small and new businesses. Students also have the opportunity to assist small firms as consultants in team practicums. The general management option acquaints students with the whole gamut of management: production, personnel, management information systems, and other management topics. title: Management Principles
description: Introduction to the basic concepts and principles of management. Focuses on structures within companies and processes within firms to bring principles to bear on the practical problems of managing organizations. Not open to B.S. or B.A. candidates for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Business Application Programming
description: Basic COBOL and programming skills using illustrative examples, exercises, and topics that emphasize applications in commercial data processing. Prerequisite: BEOA 210 or CS 116. Not open to students who have credit in CS 210.

title: Business Statistics
description: Introduction to various statistical and probabilistic concepts and techniques with application to business problems including random variables and probability distributions, measures of central tendency and dispersion, testing of hypotheses, simple linear regression, and correlation. Prerequisite: MATHS 132 or its equivalent. Prerequisite recommended: BEOA 210. Not open to students who have credit in MATHS 181.

title: The Family in Business
description: Focuses on the peculiar elements of familyowned businesses including initiation, development, management, growth, and succession. title: Introductory Operations Management
description: Introduction to the tools and techniques of management with practical applications to the production of goods and services. Prerequisite: MGT 200. Not open to B.S. or B.A. candidates for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Personnel and Supervision
description: Introduction to the personnel and supervisory functions in organizations. title: Principles of Management
description: Explores management principles, theories, and practices. title: International Management
description: Discussion of management issues related to doing business in an international context, including moving a firm into international competition, and some issues that may be expected. Topics covered include exporting, joint venturing, or licensing as options for global expansion. Prerequisite: MGT 300 or the equivalent.

title: Job Search and Transition
description: Prepares students for moving from college to careers. Topics covered include defining career goals, writing résumés, jobsearch correspondence, interviewing, and initial adjustments in the first job position. Open to juniors and seniors in all majors.

title: Information System Concepts and Techniques
description: Introduction to various concepts and techniques of information systems with application to solving managerial problems. Topics covered include information flows, application of computerbased information systems, managerial decision making, and mutual influence of organizations and information systems. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MGT 300.

title: Quantitative Business Analysis
description: Exploration and application of selected quantitative techniques to business problems. Topics covered include regression and correlation, analysis of variance and contingency tables, decision analysis, linear programming, and networkbased management techniques. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221.

title: Operations Research
description: Basic operations research concepts and techniques for managerial decisions including linear programming, network problems, decision analysis, and computer implementation of these models to solve practical problems. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MATHS 132.

title: Small Business Venture
description: Provides essential knowledge for students interested in small business including search for venture opportunities; economic, technical, and operational feasibility of ventures; financing, marketing, and legal operations; and franchising and partnering. Prerequisite: MGT 300.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: Development and management of an entrepreneurial organization including prestartup, startup, survival, growth, and the transition from entrepreneurial to professional management. Explains the function of entrepreneurship and corporate entrepreneurship. Prerequisite: MGT 341.

title: Introductory Production Management
description: Various functional fields of production and operations management including product analysis, work design and measurement, forecasting, production planning, scheduling and inventory control, facility location and layout, material handling, plant safety and maintenance, and quality control. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MGT 300.

title: Production Management in Service Sector
description: Various techniques for the design, operation, and control of service operations including service design and process selection, facility location and layout determination, staffing, equipment selection and operations, and scheduling of service operations. Prerequisite: MGT 351.

title: Managing Human Resources
description: Administration of personnel programs in business organizations so as to deal effectively with such problems as selection, training, compensation, promotion, and transfer of workers; working conditions; employee services; and industrial relations. Prerequisite: MGT 300.

title: Management Science Internship
description: Job experience (paid) in an organization with an approved innovative management program. Requires periodic written progress reports that will be evaluated by the assigned faculty member and the intern's supervisor. Topic selected will depend on student's option. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours may be earned including MGT 399.

title: Organizational Behavior
description: Dynamics of human behavior in business organizations with emphasis on problems of motivation and leadership. Examines the behavior of individuals and groups within organizations and the practical interpretation and management of behavioral phenomena. Prerequisite: MGT 300.

title: Business and Society
description: The interrelationships between business and its external environment and the multiple and complex ways business organizations are affected by governmental and societal expectations. Emphasizes contemporary issues through discussions and case analysis. Prerequisite: MGT 300.

title: Honors Colloquium: Readings in Contemporary Business
description: Seminar involving study of contemporary business literature. Interdisciplinary approach, comparing and contrasting ideas, deriving common themes, and drawing links to theory embodied in readings. Prerequisite: junior standing in College of Business and completion of "rule of nine." Open only to Honors students; others may enroll by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Management Science Practicum
description: Professional practice (unpaid) in an organization with an approved innovative management program. Required periodic written progress reports that will be evaluated by the assigned faculty member and the intern's supervisor. Topic selected will depend on student's option. Prerequisite: secondsemester junior or senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned including MGT 369.

title: Problems in General Management
description: An integration of general management principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic and complex managerial problems in public and private organizations. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGT 341, 351, 361, 415, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Business Systems Analysis and Design
description: Various systems analysis and design concepts and techniques, including the key steps in the systemsdesign and development cycle. Emphasizes the consideration of practical applications within the business environment. Prerequisite: MGT 311 and proficiency in a programming language.

title: Database: Structures and Management
description: Logical and physical organization of data. Data description, command, and interrogation languages. Examines function of databases in information systems. Prerequisite: MGT 311 and proficiency in a programming language.

title: Information Systems of Small Business
description: Computerbased information systems in small business operations without access to an internal specialist. Includes the identification of information requirements and the use of mainframe and microcomputers and purchased software to satisfy the information needs in small business. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGT 341.

title: Information Systems Management
description: Equipment selection, equipment acquisition, computer operations management, project management, computer personnel management, financial control, systems security and control, and the relationship of the information systems function to an organization. Prerequisite: MGT 311 and senior standing.

title: Business Data Communications
description: Concepts and problem of transmitting, communicating, and managing business data needs through the use of computerbased telecommunication systems. Includes applications of integrated and distributed systems to problems in various functional areas of business. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; MGT 311; and proficiency in COBOL programming.

title: Problems in Information Systems
description: An integration of various information systems principles, theories, and techniques for implementing information systems in organizations, including strategic issues. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGT 351, 412, 415, 417, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Systems Simulation
description: Concepts and techniques of system modeling and simulation using computers. Includes computer simulation languages, statistical aspects of simulation, and application of computer simulation to various practical business situations in manufacturing and service sectors. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MGT 351.

title: Small Business Practicum
description: Teams of students consult with local small businesses recommended by the Small Business Development Center. Students work on problems in such areas as accounting, production, marketing, personnel, finance, insurance, law, or information systems. Prerequisite: MGT 346.

title: New Venture Creation
description: Advanced smallbusinessmanagement entrepreneurship. Requires a thorough research project culminating in the development of a finished plan for a smallbusiness venture to be approved by an outside board of professional experts. Prerequisite: MGT 346, 351; FIN 350; MKG 300; completion of all management core courses; senior standing.

title: Operations Planning and Inventory Management
description: Operations planning and inventory management in manufacturing and service industries, including capacity planning, resourcerequirements planning, productionactivity control, and related management models and systems. Prerequisite: MGT 321, 351.

title: Computer-Integrated Production and Operations Management
description: Current and emerging developments in computers and related technologies that affect manufacturing and service operations. Topics covered include flexible manufacturing, computeraided operations management, justintime concepts, and automated service operations and their managerial implications. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MGT 351.

title: Quality Assurance
description: Study of assuring, controlling, and managing quality of goods and services, including the application of statistical techniques to problems of planning, feedback, and enhancement of process performance and operation effectiveness. Prerequisite: BEOA 210; ECON 221; MGT 351.

title: Problems in Production and Operations Management
description: An integration of various production and operations management principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic operationsmanagement problems in manufacturing and service sectors. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGT 433, 453, 454, and completion of all management core courses.

title: Compensation Administration
description: Reviews basic compensation issues including internal, external, and individual equity, as well as benefits administration. Emphasis on design and implementation of compensation systems. Prerequisite: MGT 361.

title: Personnel Planning and Selection
description: Focuses on organization and humanpower planning, including determination of organization and humanpower needs, analysis and development of job requirements, and necessary qualifications for recruitment and selection procedures, placement and orientation, and evaluation of selection programs. Prerequisite: MGT 321, 361.

title: Problems in Personnel Administration
description: An integration of various principles, theories, and techniques for solving realistic and complex personnel administration problems in public and private organizations. Includes lectures, tours, readings, cases, and the completion of a major individual project. Prerequisite: MGT 351, 461, 465, and completion of all management core courses. Marketing 127

title: Business Policy and Strategic Management
description: Integration of various functional areas of business. Development and administration of strategy and policy in private and public sector organizations. Case studies focus on strategic decisions that enable an organization to relate effectively to its industrial, national, and international environments. Normally taken during the last semester of a student's program. Prerequisite: senior standing; FIN 350; MGT 300; and MKG 300.

title: Colloquium in Business Policy
description: An honors colloquium in business policy studying advanced topics in industry, competitor, and firm analysis; critical thinking; analytic techniques; and strategy formulation culminating in required participation in the College of Business undergraduate case competition. Prerequisite or parallel: MGT 491. Open only to College of Business senior Honors students or College of Business seniors with 3.0 or higher G.P.A.'s.

title: Special Topics in Management
description: Exploration of special topics in management of interest to faculty and students. May be repeated for credit with different topics. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study
description: Supervised study of some phase of management. May consist of an experiment, library research, or an analysis of current management practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Management
description: Explores current problems, theory, research, and trends in management. Will vary depending upon the current status of managerial research, the instructor, and the needs and interests of the students. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. DEPARTMENT OF MARKETING J. Lowry, Chairperson; R. Avila, T. Baird, S. Borna, J. Brown, J. Chapman, E. Kumcu, W. Moser, H. Vanderleest, J. Vann, R. title: Retail Merchandising
description: An introduction to the retail industry with a concentration on the merchandising activities of buying, selling, pricing, and inventory control. Prerequisite: GBA 101. Not open to students who have credit in MKG 300 or to B.S. or B.A. candidates for a major or minor in the College of Business.

title: Selling
description: Fundamentals of retail, wholesale, outside, and service selling. Emphasizes sales approaches, presentation, closings, and postsale service. Prerequisite: GBA 101. description: Introduction to advertising with emphasis on the preparation, appeal, and media selection of retail advertising. Prerequisite: GBA 101. title: Principles of Marketing
description: Examines marketing as a productive system within our economy. Studies promotional activities, product policies, retail and wholesale activities, pricing policies, international marketing, and the role of marketing in society. Prerequisite: ECON 201 and junior standing or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Honors Principles of Marketing
description: Principles of marketing for honors students. Examines marketing as a productive system within our economy. Substitutes for MKG 300. Prerequisite: ECON 201, junior standing; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Consumer Behavior
description: Practical business implications of the various features of consumer motivation and behavior. Students are given information to understand how and why a buyer reacts in a purchasing situation. Prerequisite: junior standing. Parallel recommended: MKG 300.

title: Advertising Management
description: Use of advertising as a communication tool in marketing management. Analysis of media selection, production and layout measurement of effectiveness; and social and economic aspects of advertising. Prerequisite: MKG 300. Prerequisite recommended: MKG 310.

title: Professional Selling
description: Detailed introduction to and application of the principles of personal selling as applied to persons pursuing any vocation, as well as those aspiring to careers in marketing. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Retail Management
description: An investigation of store policies, organization location, layout, buying, stock control, pricing, and sales promotion for retail stores. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Transportation: An International Focus
description: The economics of transportation with an international focus; economic development of various means of transportation and accompanying regulatory problems. Rate, traffic service, and coordination problems, advantages and disadvantages, trends, and peculiarities of the various modes. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Research
description: The basic nature and scope of marketing research; scientific method and research design; specific marketing research procedures; techniques of sampling; and research report, followup, and evaluation of research process. Selected applications in motivation, advertising, and product and sales control research. Prerequisite: MKG 300; MATHS 132; and ECON 221.

title: Nonpaid Internship in Marketing
description: Professional practice during a summer or a semester as an intern in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization for no pay under the supervision of the Department of Marketing. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 369, 497, and 498. Open only to secondsemester junior marketing majors.

title: Professional Practice in Marketing
description: Professional practice during a summer or semester as an intern in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization for pay under the supervision of the Department of Marketing. Requires periodic written reports of job experiences. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to secondsemester junior and senior marketing majors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 497, and 498.

title: Marketing and Consumer Issues
description: Analysis of the consumer issues that relate to marketing practices. Involves study of such topics as consumerism, ecology, fraudulent practices, and disadvantaged consumers. Responsibilities include work experience in the Ball State University Consumer Education Council. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Channel Management
description: Study of marketing channels as economic, political, and social systems. Includes retailing, wholesaling, and other channel intermediaries. Strong emphasis is given to channel membership, structural and functional relationships, interorganizational management, and channel change and performance. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Promotion Management
description: Uses cases and problems to give experience in making decisions on a firm's promotional mix. Analysis of markets, media scheduling, budget allocation, campaign design, and promotion research. Prerequisite: MKG 320.

title: Sales Management
description: Policies and practices in organizing, recruiting, selecting, training, compensating, and controlling the sales force. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and 325 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Retail Strategy
description: Advanced course in retailing management using case studies and special projects to examine current topics and problems in retailing. Prerequisite: MKG 330.

title: Industrial Procurement Management
description: A basic course in industrial procurement management. Principal topics include make or buy analysis, quality and quantity control, value analysis, price determination, sources of supply, the purchasing system, and legal aspects of purchasing. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Logistics Management
description: Marketing linkage strategy. Focuses on efficient coordination of resources for physical distribution, manufacturing support, and purchasing. Activities include literature searches, professional meetings, guest speakers, and simulation. Prerequisite: MKG 300. Prerequisite recommended: MKG 340.

title: International Marketing
description: Examines legal, economic, and cultural conditions influencing marketing abroad. Commercial policies, practices, and techniques needed to identify and evaluate foreign markets, as well as the problems of pricing, promoting, and distributing products in international markets. Prerequisite: MKG 300.

title: Marketing Simulation Game
description: A simulation game in which students are divided into teams or companies. Management in each company makes decisions in marketing, finance, and production. Does not involve writing computer programs or using information from a dataprocessing class. Recommended for honors students. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and junior standing.

title: Marketing Management
description: Marketing by manufacturers as viewed from the marketing manager's position. Principal topics are selecting channels of distribution, determining demand, pricing policies, marketing legislation, advertising policies, and methods of selling. A casestudy approach. Prerequisite: 15 semester hours in marketing, including MKG 310, 325, 350, and senior standing, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Marketing
description: Advanced examination of such current marketing topics as marketing theory and quantitative, service, nonprofit, bank, comparative, and international marketing. Specific content is announced when offered. Recommended for honors students. Prerequisite: MKG 300; senior standing; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Marketing
description: Independent study in some phase of marketing that may consist of an experiment, library research, or the analysis of current marketing practices and methods. Prerequisite: senior standing, overall GPA of 3.0, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to secondsemester junior marketing majors. A total of 6 credit hours may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 369, and 498, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Practicum in the Consumer Education Council
description: Practical experience in mediating businessconsumer problems. Students use personnel skills in organizing and administering a Consumer Education Council. Prerequisite: MKG 380 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 credit hours may be earned toward major requirements in combination with MKG 367, 369, and 497, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. GENERAL BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (GBA)

title: Introduction to Business
description: Emphasizes the vital role of business in our society through a discussion of both the external environment of business and the internal environment of the business enterprise. Assesses the contribution of the social and behavioral sciences in the decisionmaking process. Open only to freshmen and sophomores except by permission of the department chairperson. title: The Computer in the Fine Arts
description: An interdisciplinary approach to the philosophy, use, and limits of the computer in the visual arts, music, dance, and theatre, includes background on and implications of the computer as a functional tool in the arts.

title: Seminar in Museum Studies
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to museums and museum collections through formal lectures and independent research on various components of a planned permanent collection exhibition. Participants act as interns in museum curation, education, registration, and preparation. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Zack The Department of Art educates artists, designers, and teachers. After completing the foundation year, which includes fundamental design, drawing, and a survey of art history, students specialize in one of the following: art education, ceramics, drawing, graphic design, threedimensional graphic design, metals design, painting, photography, printmaking, and sculpture. Approval to pursue the departmental major in art involves a selection process in addition to admission to the university. For more information write or call the Office of Admissions, (317) 285-8300. Transfer students from other universities are required to submit portfolios to the Department of Art as well as transcripts for evaluation and admittance. Transfer students should be aware that design programs involve a threeyear sequence beyond the foundation year, and it is unusual for students to be admitted at any point other than at the beginning of the sequence. Students specializing in any art program must enroll in the foundation core (ADS 101, 102; AFA 101, 202). All art majors, except those specializing in graphic design and threedimensional graphic design, must receive grades of C or higher in all foundation core courses before being admitted to areas of specialization in the second year of study. Students specializing in graphic design and threedimensional graphic design must receive Bs or better before enrolling in ADS 241. Students must repeat foundation courses in which they receive grades lower than C. Students specializing in the graphic design and threedimensional graphic design programs must undergo portfolio review after the completion of ADS 241 and while enrolled ADS 242. Admission to the third year of the graphic design and threedimensional graphic design sequences requires successful completion of a portfolio review. Information on design portfolio reviews is available from design faculty members. All students in the department undergo periodic reviews of their portfolios throughout their undergraduate education. The department reserves the right to retain examples of student work for exhibition. The bachelor of fine arts program in the studio areas requires a senior thesis or an exit portfolio evaluation, or both. Studio courses are open only to art majors except by permission of the instructor. All students in the university may enroll in the art history surveys. They also may take more specialized history courses in the art of a particular era or topical courses on particular problems in art.
