title: Ceramics 1
description: Basic handbuilding techniques: wedging, slab, coiling, and pinch methods. Glazes, slips, bisquing, and firing will be part of the studio experience. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 1
description: Beginning throwing; use of the potter's wheel to develop skills in throwing. A continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to jewelry and object making using metal. Emphasis is on design and the techniques of sawing, soldering, forming, bezel setting, chain and wire working, as well as other basic processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Metalsmithing and Dieforming
description: Introduction to metalsmithing including raising and dieforming; basic hammering and forming techniques will be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 221. Open only to art majors.

title: Ceramics: Hand 1
description: Continued study of handbuilding methods as well as form, idea, and glazing techniques. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 2
description: Use of the potter's wheel to develop production form; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 212.

title: Ceramics: Hand 2
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques to develop an integration of form, glaze, and CR HRS idea. Individual problems will be set up according to students' needs. Prerequisite: ACR 313.

title: Metals: Casting
description: Jewelry casting using the lostwax investment technique. Production casting will be covered, including rubbermold making and wax injecting for cast multiples. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ACR 222. Open only to art majors.

title: Color in Metal
description: Color in metal, including enameling and aluminum and refractory metal anodizing. Prerequisite: ACR 323. Open only to art majors or by permission of the instructor.

title: Independent Study in Crafts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 3
description: An indepth exploration of forming vertically and horizontally on the wheel; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 314.

title: Ceramics: Hand 3
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques, form, and idea based on individual students' needs. Prerequisite: ACR 315.

title: Senior Project in Ceramics
description: Synthesis and culmination of studio experiences in the major content area, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. In addition there must be documentation through slide portfolio, résumé, and thesis. Prerequisite: completion of total course work. Open only to ceramics majors.

title: Advanced Fabrication Techniques
description: Advanced construction techniques including catches, hinges, stone settings, etc. Basic forging will also be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 323. Open only to art majors or by permission of the instructor.

title: Metals: Advanced Surface Techniques
description: Advanced surface techniques including chasing and repousse, metal inlays and laminations, patination, and other surface embellishments. Prerequisite: ACR 324. Open only to art majors.

title: New Technologies in Metals
description: New technologies in metalsmithing. Extended study of contemporary technologies such as electroforming, plastics, and photoetching. Prerequisite: ACR 425. Open only to art majors.

title: Senior Project in Metals
description: Synthesis of experience in metals culminating in an exhibition of work. In addition, there must be documentation through slide portfolio and résumé. Should be taken during the final semester of undergraduate work. Prerequisite: ACR 427. Open only to metals majors.

title: Seminar in Crafts
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in various concepts, media, and techniques as related to the crafts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of art courses and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ART: DESIGN (ADS)

title: Foundations 1
description: Exploration of basic art principles, elements, and concepts with emphasis on spatial organization of the twodimensional plane. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on artisanship. Parallel recommended: AFA 101.

title: Foundations 2
description: Continued exploration and application of basic art principles and elements to organize threedimensional space. Also employs basic media, techniques, and tools with emphasis on artisanship. Prerequisite: ADS 101. Parallel recommended: AFA 202.

title: Photography 1
description: Introduction to photography as an expressive art form with emphasis on the development of photographic vision as well as technical proficiency. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Introduction to Graphic Design
description: Introduction and orientation to concepts and skills necessary for visual communication in two and three dimensions. The fundamentals of structure, color, typography, and tools are emphasized. Prerequisite: B or better grades in ADS 101, 102; AFA 101, and 202 for graphic design and threedimensional communication design majors. Open only to art majors.

title: Typography and Image
description: Consideration of typography in relation to visual organization; color theory and its application to communication. Type and image are covered in experimental and practical formats. Prerequisite: ADS 241. Open only to art majors.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 1
description: Studio exploration of the integration of twodimensional graphics with spacial environments. Emphasis is on conceptual spacial analysis and human activity. Prerequisite: ADS 242 and admission through successful portfolio review. Open only to art majors.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 2
description: Investigation of structures, materials, and lighting as determinants of threedimensional communication issues. Emphasis is on threedimensional model construction. Prerequisite: ADS 324. Open only to art majors.

title: Photography 2
description: Emphasis is on the further exploration of photographic vision, technical and aesthetic concerns of photography, and further study of photo history; introduction to advertising photography. Prerequisite: ADS 231. Open only to art majors.

title: Color Photography
description: Focus is on ideas and assigned problems expressed through color photography. Students should have a basic knowledge of processing color film and color prints. Prerequisite: ADS 332 and ITGRA 387 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Commercial Photography
description: Investigates commercial applications of the photographic medium with historical perspective. Weekly problems will be assigned with emphasis on practical application of photography to advertising. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Large Format Photography
description: Students become familiar with cameras larger than 35mm for personal expression and illustration. Emphasis will be on the 4" x 5" camera and its strengths and weaknesses. Students need not have large format cameras but will find them helpful. Prerequisite: ADS 332.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: Exploration of creative thematic development and its relation to the final stages of the design process. Technical elements of type specification and indication and graphicdesign production are considered. Prerequisite: ADS 242 and admission to the graphicdesign sequence through portfolio review. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Concentrated involvement in problem analysis with emphasis on symbology and image development. Prerequisite: ADS 341. Open only to art majors.

title: Independent Study in Design
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 3
description: Creative integration of conceptual spacial issues, graphic communication, and threedimensional environments. Topics include environmental graphics, exhibition design, and museum environments. Prerequisite: ADS 330. Open only to art majors.

title: Photography 3
description: Major emphasis is on students' personal statements in color and blackandwhite photography through selection of their own projects under the guidance of an instructor. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 332 for art majors; for others, permission of the department chairperson.

title: Photography 4
description: A further intensification of students' personal statements. Students will be given occasional assignments to introduce new and varied directions in art. Students furnish their own light meters and cameras with adjustable aperture, time setting, and focusing. Prerequisite: ADS 433.

title: Cinematography as an Art Form
description: Explores the use of video and super-8 media as sources of creative exploration with concerns for artistic expression, content, form, and technique. Covers a brief survey of film history. Prerequisite: ADS 332 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 4
description: Advanced design problem research stressing the interaction of creative threedimensional communication design within the constraints of the design profession. Professional portfolio preparation is emphasized. Prerequisite: ADS 426. Parallel: ADS 480. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 3
description: Advanced problem solving in sequential and threedimensional forms. Prerequisite: ADS 342. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design 4
description: Advanced problem solving in graphic design. Refinement of presentation techniques and résumé and portfolio development. Prerequisite: ADS 441. Open only to art majors.

title: Graphic Design Topic Studio
description: Intensive studio exploration of strategies and visual development within specific graphic design areas. Could include computer, letterpress, publications, exhibition and signage, package design, or development of concept and content. Prerequisite: ADS 341 or 324. Open only to art majors. A total of 9 hours of credit maybe earned, but no more than 3 in any one

title: Graphic Design Practicum
description: Problem solving within and outside the university community. Group and individual projects for nonprofit clients. Requires portfolio review and permission of the instructor. Prerequisite: ADS 341. Open only to art majors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Design Thesis
description: Intensive study with research and resolution of a current problem in twoor threedimensional design. Thesis must be arranged with a design faculty advisor. Prerequisite: ADS 426 or 441. Parallel: ADS 436, 442. Open only to graphic design and threedimensional graphic design majors.

title: Seminar in Design
description: Group or individual investigation and experiences in the fine arts beyond the scope of regular course work. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ART: EDUCATION (AED)

title: Introduction to Studio Fundamentals
description: Introduction to the basic studio processes of drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. Lecture and studio experiences related to the understanding of the elements and principles of art and the methods of art criticism. Not open to art majors.

title: Introduction to Art Education
description: Introduction to art education as a teaching profession. Emphasizes investigating artistic growth of normal and special populations and the materials, techniques, tools, art concepts, and strategies appropriate for teaching art to such students. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint students with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Stresses the developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques. Prerequisite: AED 100. Not open to art majors.

title: Art Curriculum and Instruction
description: Designed to develop art students' abilities to make artcurricular judgments by developing artcurriculum plans and designing art experiences. Prerequisite: AED 201 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Art Teaching and Learning Practicum
description: Direct experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating teaching strategies. Includes observation of students participating in an artrelated environment. Laboratory teaching time is arranged. Prerequisite: AED 304 for majors; permission of the department chairperson for minors.

title: Classroom Use of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary public school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 305 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum for majors; permission of the department chairperson for minors. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Art Education
description: Permits professionally oriented art students to select and explore more intensively an area of art education. Prerequisite: sponsorship of an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to students with areas in art. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art Education
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in the various ideas, methods, and research in art education. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to students with areas in art. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned. ART: FINE ARTS (AFA)

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to drawing: the application of basic principles and elements of art as they relate to drawing concepts. Emphasis will be on the development of perceptual awareness and familiarity with a broad range of media and techniques. Parallel recommended: ADS 101.

title: Drawing 2
description: A continuation of concepts and perceptions from Drawing 1 with emphasis on the human figure. Prerequisite: AFA 101. Parallel recommended: ADS 102.

title: Painting 1
description: Introduction to painting: study of basic considerations of image making with oil paint. Focuses on media, techniques, design elements, and concepts. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Painting 2
description: Explorations in painting designed to build on initial experiences by studio practice and through slidelectures on contemporary painting. Prerequisite: AFA 202 and 211.

title: Watercolor 1
description: Exploration of materials and techniques of transparent watercolor as they apply to the solution of painting problems. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Watercolor 2
description: Continued exploration of painting problems in watercolor with emphasis on the unique character of the medium. Prerequisite: AFA 217.

title: Sculpture 1
description: Requires research exploring sculptors or sculptural movements to inspire objects made for formal criticism. The basic skills and materials (plaster, wood, metal, clay, fabric, etc.) associated with additive, subtractive, and substitution techniques will be demonstrated. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors or minors.

title: Sculpture 2
description: Continued exploration of materials used in formal sculpture; welded and forged metal, wood construction and carving, stone carving, clay, wax, and plastic. Prerequisite: AFA 221. Open only to art majors.

title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Beginning printmaking techniques with an emphasis on intaglio and relief processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Relief Printmaking
description: Fundamental procedures of relief printing from the woodblock and other surfaces with emphasis on the use of color and new approaches. Students are expected to develop images that have a relationship to this print medium. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 1
description: Intermediatelevel printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques. Emphasis is on student's ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Drawing 3
description: Life drawing. An intensive study of the human figure, continuing the exploration of various drawing techniques and media. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Drawing 4
description: Drawing experiences exploring varied materials and concepts related to drawing as a personal visual statement. Prerequisite: AFA 303.

title: Painting 3
description: Individualized instruction aimed at the continued mastery of technical skills and progress toward the solution of pictorial and conceptual problems. Prerequisite: AFA 212. Open only to art majors.

title: Painting 4
description: Continued interest in the development of technical skills and the solution of pictorial problems with new emphasis on individual creative solutions. Prerequisite: AFA 313.

title: Painting 5
description: Emphasis is on advancing from technical proficiency toward the development of individual conceptual goals relating to painting. Prerequisite: AFA 314.

title: Water Media
description: Advanced study in water media on paper to expand painting skills while narrowing the search for personally significant imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 218. Open only to art majors. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Sculpture 3
description: Introduction to and emphasis on the basic techniques and concepts of mold making and casting aluminum, bronze, and plastics. Prerequisite: AFA 222. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture 4
description: Introduction to sculptural alternatives and nontraditional sculptural materials; visual and audio aids, performance, and antiart. Prerequisite: AFA 323. Open only to art majors.

title: Sculpture: Casting and Mold Making
description: Continuation of AFA 323. Advanced casting and mold making procedures. Individual development of the concepts and techniques associated with the casting process. Prerequisite: AFA 323. Open only to art majors.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 2
description: Advanced printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques including line etching, drypoint, engraving, softground, and aquatint. Openended problem solving and indepth study with emphasis on students' abilities to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 243.

title: Lithography 1
description: Fundamental processes of drawing and printing lithographs using stones and aluminum plates. Drawing and painting techniques are used to develop images. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Lithography 2
description: Further development and investigation of the processes of lithography, including color. Exploration of stone and metal plate techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 351.

title: Lithography 3
description: Investigation of additional drawing and painting techniques as they relate to lithography. Further development of printing skills and the lithographic image. Prerequisite: AFA 352. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Serigraphy 1
description: Introductory printmaking dealing with the processes of serigraphy, including the four basic stencil techniques and their variation. Silkscreen as a fineart form. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Sculpture 5
description: Individual instruction and supervision of experimentation in nontraditional materials. Prerequisite: AFA 324. Open only to art majors.

title: Drawing 5
description: Continuation of the drawing experience for advanced students developing further expertise in drawing skills while encouraging research into and experimentation with more personal imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 304.

title: Drawing 6
description: Advanced drawing, stressing individual problem solving with greater expectations of proficiency in each successive course. Prerequisite: AFA 405. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Fine Arts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Painting 6
description: Individualized instruction, continuing the emphasis on student identification and development of personal concepts in painting. Prerequisite: AFA 315.

title: Advanced Problems in Sculpture
description: Designed for students who want to extend their technical understanding and aesthetic development beyond the fundamental level. Prerequisite: AFA 325 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 3
description: Advanced printmaking emphasizing aesthetic decision making involving the intaglio process through the knowledge of technique and use of personal artistic choices. Prerequisite: AFA 344. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Project in Drawing
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in drawing, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 18 credit hours in drawing, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to art majors.

title: Senior Project in Painting
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in painting, with a student exhibition and supporting written composition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: AFA 416, 18 credit hours in painting, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Sculpture
description: A synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in sculpture, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 21 credit hours in sculpture, sponsorship by a sculpture faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Printmaking
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experience in printmaking, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 27 credit hours in printmaking, sponsorship by a printmaking faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to art majors.

title: Seminar in Fine Arts
description: Individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Art
description: A General Studies course that, through a survey of art and artifacts from ancient through modern times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of painting, sculpture, and architecture. Open only to students not majoring in art.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. Prehistoric through the end of European Middle Ages.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. From the fifteenth century to the present.

title: History of Three-Dimensional Design
description: Interdisciplinary study of threedimensional design and function as applied to graphic design, exhibition design, architecture, and industrial design from the eighteenth century to the present with an emphasis on American and European design. Prerequisite: sophomore standing. Open only to art majors.

title: Art in the United States 1
description: Investigation of the role visual culture has played in America throughout its history as Americans attempted to situate themselves geographically, culturally, economically, and politically within their own society and within the world at large.

title: Art in the United States 2
description: Traces the evolution of American visual arts from the beginning of the twentieth century to 1945 within the context of important social, historical, and intellectual events. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Early Civilizations
description: Art and architecture of cultures of the ancient Near East and Egypt. Use of archeological data, visual evidence, and literary records to reconstruct built environments. Special emphasis is given to the cultural significance of monumental architecture, sculpture, painting, and diverse minor arts. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Aegean and the Greeks
description: Bronze Age through the Hellenistic period, covering architecture, pottery, painting, sculpture, minor arts, and the interrelationships of the Aegean Islands and Greek mainland. Archeological data are discussed in terms of revelations about the areas' artistic and cultural development. Open to all students.

title: Art of Rome
description: Art and architecture of early Rome and the Republic to the Late Empire. Architecture and urbanism as a vehicle for the political and cultural extension of the empire to the barbarian West and the Hellenized East; missionary role of historic reliefs; Roman concepts of personality and portraiture; and the growth of luxury arts: ornament, interior decoration, and collecting.

title: Early Medieval Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture from the fourth through the tenth centuries in relation to the religious, political, and technological conditions of the period. Rural northwest Europe will be discussed in relation to urban societies in the East. Periods to be covered include early Christian, Merovingian, Carolingian, Ottoman, and Byzantine. Open to all students.

title: Late Medieval Art
description: European art and architecture from the eleventh through the fourteenth centuries. Competing claims of royal and religious sponsors; shifts in the center of production from rural to urban markets, monasteries to bishops' towns, in a period of economic advance, political transformation, and social unrest. Open to all students.

title: Northern European Art 1300-1600
description: Northern European Renaissance art as a specifically northern mode of expression and representation reflecting social, political, religious, and other cultural particularities of specific areas (France, Germany, and southern and northern Netherlands).

title: Art of the Italian Renaissance 1300-1600
description: Art and architecture examined in terms of style, cultural meaning, context, and ideology. Investigation of conditions of art production, change in role of artist, relationship between art theory and practice, and the question or concept of Renaissance.

title: Early Modern Europe 1: Art from 1600 to 1750
description: Exploration of art and architecture of Europe, from the Counter- Reformation shrine of St. Peter to Louis XIV's palace at Versailles; from the Jesuit altar pieces in Antwerp to the Dutch Republic of Vermeer and Rembrandt and more. Italy, Spain, France, Germany, England, Flanders, Netherlands. Open to all students.

title: Early Modern Europe 2: Art from 1750 to 1850
description: Art and architecture in the era of enlightenment and revolution, age of Napoleon, Restoration, reaction, reform, economic advance, and social unrest. From country gardens to urban boulevards, rococo, neoclassicism, romanticism, historicism, realism, and impressionism, England, France, Germany, Italy, Spain. Open to all students.

title: Modern Art
description: Pan-European investigation of the visual arts from French impressionism to the post-World War II abstract expressionists. Special emphasis is on cultural definitions of modernity and modernism and the appearance and ideologies of the avant garde. Open to all students.

title: Contemporary Art
description: Exploration of ideas and issues surrounding the production, reception, marketing, interpretation, and criticism of painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, installations, performance, and video and other mixed media since World War II. International in scope. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Film History
description: Traces the history of cinema from its beginning to contemporary times. Emphasizes the role of technique and art in film, modernism, and the appearance and idealogies of the avant garde. Open to all students.

title: History of Photography
description: Introduction to problems in theory, analysis, and history of photography. Study of institutional and discursive orders in which photography functions and produces meaning. Exploration of new forms of critical photographic practice. Open to all students.

title: History of Landscape Painting
description: Indepth survey of the major schools of landscape painting beginning with ancient Rome and continuing up to the present time. Political and economic conditions leading to the rebirth of landscape painting in the Renaissance will be discussed. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in History of Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in art history with emphasis on those not covered in other courses (women in art, history of museums and collecting, problems in methodology, etc.). Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Graphic Design
description: Detailed analysis of graphic design from the late nineteenth century to the present, with emphasis on European and American design. Influential movements, artists, designers, and technology that shape current design thinking will be highlighted. Prerequisite: ADS 242, pass graphic design portfolio review, or the instructor's permission. Open only to art majors.

title: Special Topics in American Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in American art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Ancient Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in ancient art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Medieval Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in medieval art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Renaissance and Early Modern Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in Renaissance or early modern art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in Modern and Contemporary Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in modern or contemporary art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Prehistoric and Non-Western Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in prehistoric or non-Western art with focus on subjects not covered in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art History
description: Individual or group investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Advanced Use of Computers in the Fine Arts
description: Advanced study in the use of computers in the visual arts. Includes specific study of imageenhancing technologies and computeraided design. Prerequisite: CFA 100, junior standing, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to art majors. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Computer Imaging
description: Advanced exploration and application of computer technology as related to the creation and production of threedimensional designs. Computer imaging, animation, and video are emphasized. Prerequisite: ART 201. Open only to art majors. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one

title: Department of Art Internship
description: Ten or more weeks of supervised summer workrelated experience. A selective review process must be passed before enrolling. Paid professional experience under supervision of department and professional sponsor. title: Introduction to Music
description: A General Studies course that, through a survey of musical forms and compositions from early through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the broad range of musical creativity. Open only to students not majoring in music.

title: Music and Popular Culture in America
description: A survey of the origins and development of popular music in America. Discussion includes blues, jazz, musical theatre, and rock. Emphasis is on cultural rather than technical aspects of music.

title: Survey of Music Literature
description: Survey of styles, forms, and masterworks of music with emphasis on the period 1700 to 1975. One hour lecture and two hours directed listening each week. Required for majors and minors. Open only to music majors and minors or by permission.

title: Music History
description: The development of music from its beginnings through 1750. Origins, growth of early polyphony, instrumental music. Changes in style during medieval, Renaissance, and baroque periods. Prerequisite: MUHIS 200 or departmental permission.

title: Music History
description: Changes in music from the preclassic period through the present and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 200 and 330 or departmental permission.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Open only to students in the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of medieval, Renaissance, and baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. Open only to students in the Honors Program.

title: Piano Literature
description: Survey of the standard literature for the piano from J. S. Bach through the midtwentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 330 and 331 or permission of the instructor.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: The vocal and instrumental music of western Europe during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including figured bass, opera, oratorio and cantata, and the development of such instrumental genres as concerto, sonata, and suite. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles that marked the transition from baroque to classical music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in Western civilization in the nineteenth century, emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Studies important composers and works from the various time periods: early, middle, late, and post-Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331 or permission of the director of the school.

title: Opera from the Time of Mozart
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and students will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Jazz History 1
description: Historic examination of jazz from 1890 to 1950. Analyzes outstanding style characteristics of each period from their beginnings to the 1950s, including ragtime, the Jazz Age, the Swing Era, and the bebop and cool periods.

title: Jazz History 2
description: Continuation of MUHIS 439, covering the 1950s through the present. Progressive fifties, the rockjazz fusions of the sixties, seventies, and eighties—today's trends.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis is on baroque instruments and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Rameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: An opportunity for superior students to do guided reading and intensive study in topics in music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester.

title: Workshop in Music History and Musicology
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music history and musicology. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis is on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 100 or 331.

title: Choral Music of the Church
description: Anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the sixteenth century to the present suitable for the church service. Prerequisite: MUHIS 100 or 331. MUSIC ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY (MUMET)

title: Introduction to Electronic Music
description: Topics include musique concrete, analog sound generation and processing, voltage controlled systems. In addition to lectures, a minimum of four hours of laboratory time is required each week. Projects include sound synthesis, sound structuring, and analysis.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic and Electro-Acoustic Music
description: Survey of the development of composition using the electronic medium. Topics include the study of electronic instruments, the analysis of music forms and structure in electronic and electroacoustic compositions, and the study of computerassisted composition.

title: Music Perception
description: An introduction to basic psychoacoustics and psychophysics. Topics include the ear as a frequency analyzer, the auditory pathway, fundamentals of auditory perception, special problems in the perception of music and music structures.

title: Sound Synthesis 1
description: Intermediate course in sound synthesis. Topics include FM and AM synthesis, filtration, basic mixing, iteration and reverberation, and the development of basic analog and digital electronic virtual instruments. Minimum of three hours of lab experience required weekly. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; MUMET 225.

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: An introduction to the basics of recording technology. Topics include the analog tape recorder, the tape medium, microphone design, and microphone placement. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; PHYCS 122.

title: Introduction to Computer Music
description: An intermediate course in computer music. Topics include computer systems appropriate for music composition, sound synthesis, and analysis. Computer and music instrument communications are introduced. Intermediate projects in music programming are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212; PHYCS 122.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire. Each project requires seminar and laboratory participation. Prerequisite: MUMET 326. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Sound Synthesis 2
description: An advanced course in sound synthesis. Topics include the development of complex virtual electronic instruments and their control. Structured sound projects are required. A minimum of five hours of lab experience each week is required. Prerequisite: MUMET 325, 327.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Topics include multitrack recording, multichannel mixing, signal processing, and problems in multiple microphone arrays and stereo imaging. A minimum of 3 hours of laboratory experience is required. Prerequisite: MUMET 326.

title: Advanced Projects in Computer Music
description: An advanced course in computer music applications. Topics include problems in MIDI communications, projects in algorhythmic composition, and problems in telemusic communications. Prerequisite: MUMET 425.

title: Production Workshop
description: An advanced course in technical applications of music production. This is an independentprojectoriented course. Projects require a production product such as a technical demonstration, a broadcast quality program, an album, or an intermedia performance. Prerequisite: MUMET 426.

description: A major performing ensemble, rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are Wind Ensemble, Symphonic Band, Marching Show Band, Basketball Pep Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are Concert Band and Jazz Ensembles II and

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles normally rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Chamber Choir, Opera Chorus, University Singers, and Lab Choir.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are University Chorus, Women's Chorus, and the Statesmen. Registration will not count toward minimum hourly requirements for graduation. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, rehearsing normally five hours a week. Included in this category are the Wind Ensemble, Symphony Band, Marching Show Band, Basketball Pep Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Band and Jazz Ensembles II and III.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles normally rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Opera/Musical Theatre, and the University Singers.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are the Women's Chorus, the Statesmen, the University Chorus, and the Lab Choir.

title: The Singing Actor
description: Acting techniques specifically related to musical theatre and opera. Vocal exercises, movement, song interpretation. Preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer or technician. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Musical Theatre in America
description: A study of the history of the American musical theatre. A general overview of the repertoire.

title: Workshop in Music
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on specialized interdisciplinary topics in music. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Recital
description: Attendance at recitals and concerts as specified in the music student handbook is the basis for earning recital credit.

title: Introduction to Music Education
description: An overview of the music teaching profession and its processes, with particular emphasis on basic concepts and foundations. Screening of potential music education candidates is built into the course.

title: Brass Techniques 1
description: A study of the brass instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Woodwind Techniques 1
description: A study of the woodwind instruments with emphasis on skill development and pedagogical understanding. Acoustical principles, basic maintenance, teaching methods, and materials. Meets two hours weekly.

title: Development and Administration of Choral Music
description: Analysis of the high school choral music teacher's position in the school and community and the administration and supervision of choral activities. Discussion of choral music suitable for various high school choirs.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled.

title: Elementary General Music 1
description: Introducing general music for grades K-6. Explores the philosophy of general music teaching, objectives of concepts and skills, developing teaching skills, use of materials and equipment, and specialized approaches to music education.

title: Elementary General Music 2
description: Continuing study of curriculum development, teaching methodology, use of materials and equipment, evaluation in general classroom music for grades K-6. Includes planning individual teaching projects, some observation and participation, integration with other curricular areas, mainstreaming, Orff and Kodaly approaches. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: General Music in the Junior and Senior High Schools
description: A study of the philosophies, techniques, and materials for teaching the required nonperformance music courses in grades five through nine. Emphasizes the unique musical needs of young adolescents.

title: Teaching Instrumental Music
description: Examines problems in the teaching and administration of contemporary instrumental classes. Topics include program goals, inventory management, rehearsals, selection of materials, and techniques for learning musical concepts in performance classes. Prerequisite: minor skills in brasses, woodwinds, and strings.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary Classroom
description: Focuses on the implementation of music in the elementary classroom. Draws on the common heritage of music and suggests methods for presenting appropriate musical experience and materials to children. Prerequisite: MUSED 265.

title: Instrumental Laboratory
description: Laboratory ensemble taken as participant first, then as a conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 390. Focuses on instrumental rehearsal techniques and instrumental literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Choral Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus taken as participant first, then as conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 391. Focus on choral rehearsal techniques and choral literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Show/Jazz Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus emphasizing show and jazz literature and styles. Stresses choreography and vocal techniques for the teacher of high school show choir and jazz choir. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education: A Practicum
description: Views the music program of early childhood education as a logical basis for creativity and as an effective and educationally sound means of eliminating inhibition from the responsiveness of three-, four-, and fiveyearold children.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Approaches to the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Voice Pedagogy
description: Evaluation of methods and principles of voice production for achieving technical excellence. Consideration given to tone quality, agility, legato, breathing, range, diction, study of anatomical aspects of tone production, the International Phonetic Alphabet, vocalization studies, and repertoire for singers.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: The principles and objectives of the organization and administration of the current idioms of a marching band. Show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite or parallel: MUSCH 340.

title: Methods of Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods of teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level or permission of the director of school.

title: Introduction to Orff-Schulwerk
description: The principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities involve movement, rhythm, and speech on basic and pre-Orff levels, along with creative use of simple percussion instruments.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; singing and conducting opportunities of standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Handbell Techniques
description: An introduction to the history, literature, and playing techniques of handbells. Includes opportunities to conduct and to perform with handbell choirs. Discussion of administering handbell choirs in church and school situations.

title: Basic Movement and Choreography
description: Designed to acquaint the music therapist or teacher with the fundamentals of physical interpretations of music. Deals with techniques appropriate for swing choirs, small ensembles, and general staging practices in performance preparation.

title: Kochily Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school form the framework of this course designed for music specialists.

title: Contemporary Techniques in Elementary School Music
description: Exploring the use of nonconventional, nontraditional, experimental musical sound sources and procedures in music education.

title: Stage Band Techniques
description: Designed to acquaint students with the techniques and style characteristics of popular and jazz band performance. Includes preparation in the administration of school jazz ensembles.

title: Guitar for Social Use
description: Designed for development of basic skill in playing the guitar for accompanying. Focuses on chordal styles and their application to music such as folk songs and popular songs. Open to all students.

title: Music in Society
description: The relationship between humanity and music from primitive culture through the present time. Emphasis is on specific contributions made by ethnic groups to the literature of music. The implications for music teachers regarding aesthetic experience.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: An opportunity for superior students to conduct intensive study and research in a particular component of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Workshop in Music Education
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music education. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Small Ensemble (Jazz Combo)
description: Players of appropriate instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of commercial and jazz music. These groups may include trios, quartets, quintets, and sextets. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Fundamentals of Jazz 1
description: Transposition techniques, principles of chordal progression, and harmonic motion. Extension and generalizations of standard cadential formulas. Chordal progression, chordal succession, the use of turnbacks, cycles, and the common principles of harmonic motion as used in standard song forms.

title: Fundamentals of Jazz 2
description: Transposition techniques, principles of chordal progression, and harmonic motion. Extension and generalizations of standard cadential formulas. Chordal progression, chordal succession, the use of turnbacks, cycles, and the common principles of harmonic motion as used in standard song forms. Prerequisite: MUSPE 250.

title: Introduction to Conducting
description: Principles of baton technique. description: A beginning piano class for students with no piano background. title: Popular Vocal Styles
description: Assists students in developing individual popular singing styles. Concentrates on all facets of performance including audienceperformer rapport, the performeraccompanist relationship, and microphone techniques. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Opera Productions
description: Study and public performance of standard operas of all periods. Combines the art forms of music, drama, stagecraft, and dance in the study of coaching, acting, and stage technique. Prerequisite: audition or previous experience. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Service Playing and Church Music Administration
description: Hymn playing and anthem accompaniments; formulation of adult and children's choirs in churches; congregational singing; service planning. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112 and one year of organ study, or permission of the instructor.

title: Instrumental Conducting Practice
description: Continuation of skills and techniques learned in MUSPE 290 with emphasis upon the instrumental ensembles. Rehearsal and conducting of instrumental literature with live ensembles. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Choral Conducting Practice
description: A continuation and application of skills and techniques learned in MUSPE 290 with emphasis upon the choral ensemble. Rehearsal and conducting of vocal literature with live ensembles. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Diction for Singers
description: Beginning voice students will learn effective pronunciation of English and Italian using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Techniques in producing vowel sounds and consonant articulation unique to the sung work will be emphasized. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Wind and Percussion Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for wind and percussion instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with winds or percussion as their major instrument.

title: String and Harp Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for stringed instruments and harp instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with strings or harp as their major instrument.

title: Keyboard Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for piano, organ, and harpsichord instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with piano, organ, or harpsichord as their major instrument.

title: Guitar Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for guitar instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with guitar as their major instrument.

title: Vocal Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for vocal instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. These groups may include trios and quartets of like instruments, or quintets, sextets, and octets of mixed brasses. 1432 Small Ensemble (Percussion). These groups may range in size from trios and quintets to larger ensembles. 1433 Small Ensemble (Strings). (1) Players of string instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing. 1434 Small Ensemble (Harp). (1) Groups of harpists are organized to perform the specialized literature for this unusual combination of instruments. Original compositions and transcriptions are presented in public performances. 1435 Small Ensemble (Piano). (1) Study of sonata literature in conjunction with another instrument or literature for multiple pianos. Students will be organized into small groups according to proficiency and demands of the literature. 1436 Ensemble for New Music. (1) Players of all instruments are organized into small groups for the study of contemporary chamber music. Open to all students with sufficient proficiency. 1437 Small Ensemble (Organ and Church Music). (1) Performance projects of interest to the organist and church musician. Reading of anthems, motets, oratorio movements; music for organ and instruments; music for graded church choirs; conducting from the keyboard. 1438 Small Ensemble (Vocal). (1) Quartets, sextets, octets, and multiples of these units are arranged as student enrollment indicates. Music studied and performed ranges from the traditional quartet literature to material appropriate for glee clubs. 1439 Small Ensemble (Guitar). (1) Guitar players are organized into small groups to study and perform the duet, trio, and quartet repertoire for classical guitar. Upperclass students generally study ensemble works involving other instrumentation such as guitar and flute; guitar and strings; and guitar and voice. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom
description: Application of melodyharmony relationship to instrumental performance. Students will be expected to play numerous standard tunes and jazz standards, and improvise with competency determined by the instructor. All chords, scales, sixths, sevenths, ninths, elevenths, thirteenths, modes, and transposition of modes.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom 2
description: Songs from swing, bebop, cool, and contemporary periods. Exploration of unitonal, unimodal, polytonal, polymodal melodies with small instrumental groups. Innovations in jazz improvisation. Musicians to be studied include Chick Corea, Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, Joe Farrell, and Miles Davis. Prerequisite: MUSPE 456.

title: Jazz Piano Class 1
description: All triads with the added sixth or sixth chords played in block chordal harmony. All inversions of these chords and transpositions of chord types through four sharps and flats; introduction of the four types of seventh chords.

title: Jazz Piano Class 2
description: Continuation of MUSPE 460. Completion of seventh chords, inversion in remaining keys; additional experiences include minor seventh (flat 5), augmented seventh, and minor/major sevenths. All ninth chords, eleventh chords, and thirteenth chords played melodically and harmonically. Prerequisite: MUSPE 460.

title: Continuo Playing and Keyboard Improvisation
description: Development of facility in reading from figured basses or improvisation in the church service, free harmonization of hymns. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or MUSPE 226 or 377. A total of 2 hours of credit may be *490 Advanced Conducting. (1-3) One onehour weekly lesson in conducting. Private or small class at the discretion of the instructor. Prerequisite: MUSPE 390 or 391. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Workshop in Music Performance
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Recital
description: Taken during the senior year by students with a performance major. Students will present a full recital as approved by their area committees and the director of the school.

title: Independent Study in Musical Performance
description: An opportunity to cover specific needs or interests for which provisions are not made by the regular course offerings of the school. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. MUSIC THEORY AND COMPOSITION (MUSTH)

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students deficient in elementary music language. Provides simplest basic concepts, symbols, readingskill drills, and terminology with supporting historical and systems information. Placement by level of experience.

title: Music Theory
description: Indepth study of music fundamentals including rhythm, melodic structure, fourpart harmony, elementary harmonic and structural analysis accompanied by writing, listening, score study, and sightsinging. Placement by level of experience. Must be taken in course number sequence.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 111 including more advanced fourpart writing, analysis, score study, listening, and sightsinging. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Acoustics
description: An introduction to physical acoustics with an emphasis on music and audio applications. Topics included are wave mechanics, acoustic measurements, tone and timbre analysis, tuning and temperament, and sound transduction.

title: Music Theory
description: Emphasis is on nineteenthcentury procedures through studies of compositional styles and analysis. Required mastering of diatonic and chromatic modulations, and higher hierarchical chordal structures in tonal context and traditional forms. Advanced music reading, aural perception, laboratory drill in analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 211, emphasizing practices of the later nineteenth century and the twentieth century. Mastery of basic understanding of postromantic, impressionistic, expressionistic, neoclassical, serial, and other contemporary music required. Continued music reading, aural perception, laboratory analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Music Theory: Form and Analysis
description: An indepth study of large forms through intensive analysis, listening, research, and writing. Emphasis is on individual student work completed outside class to develop abilities in theoretical and composition investigation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. Open only to music majors.

title: Music Theory: Eighteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Indepth study of eighteenthcentury counterpoint in which skills are developed in analyzing and composing canons, inventions, and fugues. Prerequisite: MUSTH 311. Open only to music majors.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Development of basic craft through the writing of shorter instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or by permission of the division chairperson with the recommendation of the theory instructor.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Choral Arranging
description: Scoring for choir and choral ensembles. Gives particular attention to voicing, soloistic treatment of voices, texts, and other elements of traditional and contemporary scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band, wind ensemble, and other related groups. Emphasis is on instrumentation, transposition, voicing, doubling, soloistic treatment, and scoring from piano or similar reduction. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Commercial Arranging
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques used in commercial music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms with particular attention given to the composerarranger in the recordingstudio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: Laboratory for skill development in arranging. Individualized and projectoriented to prepare musicians to score spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, and background and mood sequences, as well as to compose for TV, films, radio, and media. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Topics in Music Theory
description: A topic to be announced in advance that will be drawn from the compositional practices of the seventeenth, eighteenth, nineteenth, or twentieth century and discussed through selected works taken from the literature. Prerequisite: MUSTH 312. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Continuation of MUSTH 332 and the writing of larger, longer works. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 431. Prerequisite: MUSTH 431.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. Studies the synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Study of a theoretical topic using readings, analysis, and research. Prerequisite: permission of the division chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Theory Seminar
description: Discussions, analyses, and projects concerning advanced theoretical problems from all periods and styles. Specific topics to be publicized one semester in advance. Prerequisite: permission of the division chairperson.

title: Workshop in Music Theory and Composition
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music theory and composition. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Composition-Project Recital
description: Public performance of compositions completed in composition degree program or an indepth lecture or lecturerecital describing a completed music engineering and technology project.
