title: Introduction to Dance History
description: Provides an understanding and appreciation of dance as an expression of people's imaginative and creative urges. Dance from the primitive to the twentieth century is explored within its social and historical context.

title: Ballet 1
description: Classes in ballet technique for beginners, with special emphasis on body placement and alignment. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Ballet 2
description: Classes in ballet technique for advanced beginners, with special emphasis on the use of epaulement. Prerequisite: DANCE 110 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 1
description: For students interested in dance performance or career opportunities in dance. Basic techniques and performance skills are emphasized. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 2
description: Designed to continue development of the basic performance skills of modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 120 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Luigi: Jazz Dance Technique and Philosophy of Movement
description: An introduction to dance technique and theatre movement for the nondancer interested in a movement technique philosophy. The movement technique can be used for theatre dance or athletic warmups, and the philosophy applies to all learning and performing situations. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Musical Theatre Tap Styles
description: Introduces basic meters used in musical theatre tap styles, such as soft shoe, waltz clog, and military. Develops tap vocabulary for performers and choreographers.

title: Ballet 3
description: Ballet technique on a beginningintermediate level for students with previous training. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ballet 4
description: A continuation of ballet technique for students at an intermediate level. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 3
description: Designed for students with training in modern dance and introduction to improvisational performance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 121 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 4
description: Designed to prepare students for advanced modern dance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 220 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Jazz 2
description: Designed for students with dance training who have interest in developing technique in various jazz styles. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 120, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Tap 2
description: Advanced tap dance techniques for dance students with previous tapdance training. Prerequisite: PEG 118 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one

title: Musical Theatre Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of contemporary dance styles for the Broadway and nightclub stages. Dance styles covered will change each semester. Prerequisite: PEG 118; DANCE 110, 120; or PEG 116. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance 1
description: Basic repertoire of ethnic dance steps, styles, and dances for use in performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Clogging
description: American ethnic dance form known as clogging. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Ball State Ballet
description: A broadbased dance company, emphasizing ballet technique, with performance interests extending from tap, jazz, and experimental to classical ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open only to students by audition.

title: Dance Theatre
description: Experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance presentations. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open only by audition.

title: International Folk Dance Company
description: Opportunity for students with interest in folk dance to learn and perform dances from many different countries. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open by audition and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choreography 1
description: Work in choreographing dance by exploring musical and dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 111, 120, 121, 140. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Ballet History
description: A survey of ballet from its inception to the present time. Prerequisite: DANCE 100.

title: Ballet 5
description: Intermediateadvanced ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 and 211 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ballet 6
description: Advanced ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 310 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Partnering
description: Study of the art of partnering. Class is limited to not more than two females for each male partner. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 5
description: Introduction to improvisational performance skills for students with training in modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 220, 221, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 6
description: Designed to continue development of advanced modern dance performance skills and improvisational techniques. Prerequisite: DANCE 320 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Jazz 3
description: Advanced jazz dance emphasizing technique work in complex rhythms, syncopation, jazz jumps, and jazz turns. Prerequisite: DANCE 230 (4 hours) or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of the stylistic uniqueness of a particular ethnic region. Covers three to four styles during the semester. Prerequisite: DANCE 241. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Notation
description: Introduction to dance notation with an emphasis on such contemporary notation systems as Labonotation and Benesh. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240.

title: Dance Production
description: Designed to acquaint students with various technical and performance elements of dance production. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choreography 2
description: Work in choreographing traditional and nontraditional dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 287 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Dance Pedagogy
description: Indepth study of teaching methods for beginning, intermediate, and advanced dance students, includes pedagogy from preschool through adult level. Includes rehearsal technique for performance preparation. Prerequisite: DANCE 210, 211, 220, 221, 240. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Dance Practicum
description: Intensive experience in stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, dance management, and other elements of production. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Creative Project
description: Designed as a project in choreography for advanced dance students. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Directed Study in Dance
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects related to dance that meet the approval of the dance faculty. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Oral Interpretation
description: The study of prose fiction, poetry, and drama through the medium of oral performance. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Oral Interpretation of Prose Fiction
description: An indepth study of the novel through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Poetry
description: The study of poetry through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Oral Interpretation of Drama
description: The study of dramatic literature through the medium of oral performance. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Studies in Oral Interpretation
description: Students with an interest in oral interpretation pursue a particular area of study in depth. Prerequisite: INTRP 230. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Presentational Theatre Forms
description: The creation and direction of presentational (readers' theatre and chamber theatre) scripts—concentrating on literature not originally intended for the stage. Prerequisite: INTRP 230.

title: Introduction to Theatre
description: A General Studies course that, through a survey of plays selected from the major periods of dramatic productivity from the ancient Greeks through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the many faces of dramatic creativity. Open only to students not majoring in theatre.

title: Script Analysis
description: Systematic approach to play analysis with an emphasis on performance and production.

title: Stagecraft
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of the crafts involved in theatre prodtiction at the school, college, and community theatre levels. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Theatrical Costuming
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of costuming for educational and community theatre with attention given to stage makeup. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Principles of Stage Makeup
description: An investigation of the principles, techniques, and materials of stage makeup and practical experience in their application.

title: Acting 1
description: A lecturelaboratory class stressing the basic principles of acting.

title: Acting 2
description: A lecturelaboratory course on the principles of acting with major emphasis on character analysis and development. Prerequisite: THEAT 232.

title: Acting 3
description: Advanced scene study. Emphasis is on actor communication, listening skills, and selfexploration through the use of voice and movement. Prerequisite: THEAT 232, 233. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to theatre majors and minors.

title: Theatre Practicum
description: Intensive experience in acting, stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, theatre management, and other production areas. Students should complete practicums in six different areas. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: History of Theatre 1
description: Study of the Western theatre from its origins through the Renaissance, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: History of Theatre 2
description: Study of the Western theatre from the Renaissance to the foundations of modern theatre in the late nineteenth century, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Modern Theatre
description: Study of major movements in modern Western theatre since 1875, with emphasis on theoretical documents, production elements, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Theatrical Design Skills
description: A lecturelaboratory class to present basic problemsolving skills involving theatrical design artwork. Emphasizes the development of technique and media competence. Prerequisite: THEAT 220.

title: Fundamentals of Stage Lighting
description: A lecturelaboratory course in the basic concepts, materials, hardware, and design principles of stage lighting. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Audition Techniques and Repertory
description: How to select, prepare, and present appropriate material (monologues and songs) with honesty, style, and a sense of professionalism. Résumés and portfolio photo preparation are also covered, as are contracts and agents. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Directing 1
description: Theory and practice of directing for the theatre. Exercises in movement, line interpretation, creation of atmosphere, and the effective use of stage areas. Prerequisite: THEAT 232 and 233.

title: Directing for the Musical Theatre
description: A detailed examination of the selection, organization, and direction of musical theatre productions. For practical laboratory work, students may elect to concentrate on the production problems of either a specific musical comedy or an opera.

title: Department of Theatre Unpaid Internship Program
description: Placement in an unpaid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in a theatre program in some capacity. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Department of Theatre Paid Internship Program
description: Placement in a paid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in a theatre program in some capacity. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Children's Theatre
description: The principles of theatre devoted to creative dramatics. Twothirds of the course is devoted to formal dramatics. A public performance will be arranged.

title: Advanced Theatre Practice
description: Students design and execute a theatre project: scenery designs, lighting, properties, acting, directing, oral interpretation, and house management. Prerequisite: 12 hours of credit in theatre courses and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Studies in American Theatre
description: An investigation of significant movements in the American professional theatre and its drama.

title: Scene Design
description: Advanced training and experience in the problems of set design and lighting for theatrical productions in many forms and styles, including elements of television design. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Advanced Scene Design
description: A detailed lecturelaboratory class for design students emphasizing advanced problems of scenic rigging and design. Covers preparation and implementation of various genres including the musical theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 420.

title: Theatre Costume Design
description: Practice in the research, design, and building techniques involved in the preparation of period costumes for use in theatre productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 223 and 320.

title: Stage Lighting Design
description: Training and experience in the problems of stage lighting design for the proscenium and nonproscenium stage. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 326.

title: Styles of Acting
description: The study and performance of the styles of acting appropriate to major types of drama from antiquity to the present.

title: Advanced Study of Roles for Performance
description: An advanced course concentrating on the preparation of a script for performance. At all stages of preparation, students work closely with a faculty advisor of their choosing. The course will culminate in a live, adjudicated performance. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 and 433; INTRP 230; and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one

title: Directing 2
description: Further investigation of the work of the director with special reference to directing the various styles, modes, and periods of theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 or the equivalent.

title: Creative Dramatics
description: Principles of developing original dramatizations through improvisational techniques. Students are expected to observe and work with children as well as with college adults.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop
description: Participation in the Summer Festival Theatre. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theatre Management
description: Study and practice in box office procedures, house management, publicity, and promotion as related to college, community, and professional theatres. Prerequisite: 9 hours of theatre courses.

title: Directed Study in Theatre
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects in design, playwriting, acting, interpretation, or directing, meeting the approval of the theatre staff. The range of courses offered by the college encourages students to think critically, solve problems creatively, and communicate ideas clearly. SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING RESEARCH SEMESTER The U.S. Department of Energy, through its Office of Energy Research, sponsors an academicyear program at six national laboratories. This program, Science and Engineering Research Semester (SERS), is designed to help encourage undergraduate students to pursue advanced degrees in the sciences and engineering. Students selected to participate in this program become members of research teams engaged in leadingedge scientific and engineering research employing stateoftheart facilities and equipment. Ball State University students often select Argonne National Laboratory near Chicago for their semester of research in such disciplines as biological, environmental, and medical sciences; ceramics; chemistry; physics; computer science; mathematics; and materials science. Academic credit may be earned during this research semester. Students interested in including a research semester at one of the National Laboratories should plan early in their academic programs for such an experience. Additional information on this program can be obtained from the SERS coordinator, Dean's Office, College of Sciences and Humanities, NO 112 (285-1042). INTERDEPARTMENTAL PROGRAMS ASIAN STUDIES The Asian studies minor is designed to introduce students to Asian cultures and traditions and to help them become familiar with major cultural differences in customs and values. This minor prepares students for careers in multinational business and education and equips them with knowledge that is applicable to many liberal arts subjects. DEPARTMENTAL MINOR IN ASIAN STUDIES, 15 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS 15 hours from Three different departments

title: Contemporary East Asia 1. China, Japan, Korea: Land, People, Structures
description: Introduces the geographic, historic, anthropologic, and political bases for understanding East Asia, focusing on contemporary realities but giving sufficient background to understand the origins of contemporary problems.

title: Contemporary East Asia 2. China, Japan, Korea: Traditions, Culture, Arts
description: Introduces the religious beliefs, philosophies, and living traditions of East Asia and their expression in literature, art, architecture, and music.

title: Asian Studies: Selected Readings
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with the department and instructor involved. Prerequisite: permission of the program director. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. LATIN-AMERICAN STUDIES The Latin-American studies major and minor are interdepartmental programs designed to help students understand the common heritage and problems of and the differences that exist among Latin-American countries. These programs will be helpful to students majoring in such subjects as anthropology, bilingual education, business, history, political science, and Spanish. DEPARTMENTAL MAJOR IN LATIN-AMERICAN STUDIES, 30 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS 30 hours from Three different departments

title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
description: Introduces the diversity of human social life as shaped by culture, relating the origins and nature of culture to variations in such universal aspects of human experience as the food quest, family organization, social control, the arts, and religion.

title: Archaeology and Culture
description: The nature of archaeological research—its methodology and principles of analysis— and its contributions to our understanding of human behavior and the development of human culture from the Stone Age to the present.

title: Introduction to Physical Anthropology
description: Humanity's place in nature and its relationships to other animals, especially monkeys and apes; evolutionary development and present diversity; the interaction of human biology and behavior.

title: Anthropology of a Changing World
description: Anthropological survey of selected peoples of the world representing a variety of human lifeways. Focuses on global social change and issues related to contemporary human problems. Uses film and indepth studies and also discusses language and race.

title: Human Variation and Adaptation
description: Human biological variation in the contemporary world; examination of its distribution, inheritance, development, and adaptiveness. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor.

title: Ethnicity and Race
description: Explores the concepts of ethnicity and race and how they shape the interaction between individuals and groups in complex society. Devotes particular attention to the Western world, but also considers similar attitudes in other parts of the world.

title: Introduction to Folklore and Folklife
description: Introduction to the role of tradition in various aspects of American culture, from humor to architecture, the functions of these elements in society, and methodological and theoretical approaches to their study, with comparative examples from Ireland and Great Britain.

title: The African Background of American Black Culture
description: African cultural and historical roots of American blacks—origins of the human species, plant and animal domestication, metallurgy, art, and state formation. Focus is on West Africa, the source of most of the black population of the United States.

title: History of Method and Theory in Anthropology
description: Surveys the major ideas and issues of anthropology over time. Includes methods and theories from archaeology, physical anthropology, linguistics, and cultural anthropology.

title: Anthropology and Education
description: Applies anthropological theory and method to such educational concerns as socialization, peer dynamics, classroom networks, parentteacher interactions, modernization, and multicultural settings.

title: Classical Archaeology
description: Development of the Mediterranean areas from the Neolithic through the Classical period.

title: Fundamentals of Archaeology
description: Introduces the types of data dealt with by archaeology, approaches to data recovery, methods of analysis, and problems of interpretation. Differing problems of traditional research archaeology and modern archaeological resources management are considered.

title: Ontogeny: Human Physical Growth and Development and Its Evolution
description: Human ontogeny studies children's physical growth and development, human adaptive roles and evolutionary history, ranges of variation in presentday populations, effects of stress, changes through time, comparisons with nonhuman primates, and assessment methods. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or its equivalent.

title: Applied Anthropology
description: Investigates the problems and work that engage the attention of anthropologists outside the university setting. Examination of new skills needed to supplement those traditionally taught in anthropology.

title: Introduction to Anthropological Linguistics
description: Basic concepts, scope, and methodology of the science of language with particular emphasis on non- European languages and cultural components of language. No prerequisite, but knowledge of a foreign language is helpful.

title: Topics in Old World Prehistory
description: Prehistory of various Old World regions and time periods. Topics will vary from semester to semester—for example, Europe, the Paleolithic, general survey. May be repeated for different topics.

title: North American Indians
description: Cultures of the North American Indians emphasizing their economic, sociopolitical, and religious institutions.

title: Ecological Anthropology
description: Explores the system of relationships between any human population and its environment focusing on cultural behavior. Uses studies from ancient to modern times and models and theories from ecology and anthropology. Prerequisite: any one of ANTH 101, 103, 105, 201, or permission of the instructor.

title: Human Evolution
description: Fossil record of the evolution of humans and their primate predecessors. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor.

title: Topics in New World Archaeology
description: Prehistory of various New World regions or developmental periods. Topics will vary from semester to semester—for example, Meso-America, the Southwest, general survey. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Social Organization
description: A systematic crosscultural analysis of human organizations from kinshipbased societies to modern bureaucracies. Using an evolutionary approach, the course provides both theoretical perspectives and practical understanding. Prerequisite: ANTH 101, 201, or permission of the instructor.

title: Art of Prehistoric and Non-Western Cultures
description: Exposes liberal arts students to the artistic accomplishments of prehistoric and non-Western peoples. Art will be interpreted and functionally examined in regard to aesthetic, ceremonial, and informational content.

title: Laboratory Methods in Archaeology
description: Surveys the methods of recovery, treatment, analysis, illustration, and interpretation of artifacts, soils, and faunal and botanical remains from archaeological sites; stresses the integration of research design, literature research, and laboratory methods.

title: Special Topics in Native American Cultures
description: Detailed analysis of selected contemporary issues facing American Indians—for example, religious freedom, property rights—or a focus on the Indian cultures of a particular area, such as the Southwest, Great Lakes, or Northeast. May be repeated for different topics.

title: Indians of the Great Lakes
description: Indepth study of selected Native American cultures indigenous to the Great Lakes region from the time of European contact to the contemporary period.

title: Midwestern Archaeology
description: Archaeological development of the Midwest is traced through the Paleo- Indian, Archaic, Intermediate, Woodland, and Mississippi stages. Prerequisite recommended: ANTH 103 or 304.

title: Anthropology and Women
description: Development of the female phenotype; variation in the roles assigned to women in cultures of differing levels of complexity from gathererhunters to industrial societies—both Western and non- Western—and the contributions of women anthropologists to understanding this variation.

title: Anthropology of American Culture
description: Examines how the values, beliefs, and norms of American culture are integrated into and symbolized in various media. Explores how we experience and resolve cultural tensions between individualism and community, equality and hierarchy, competition and cooperation.

title: Historical Archaeology
description: Covers the major themes and philosophies of the archaeology of post-Columbian America as well as related literature and sources of information on architectural features and items of material culture likely to be encountered in the course of excavation.

title: Special Topics in Anthropology
description: Detailed analysis of a special problem in cultural anthropology, archaeology, linguistics, or physical anthropology. May be repeated for different topics.

title: European Prehistory
description: Prehistory of Europe from the Paleolithic through the Iron Age with an emphasis on the regions north and west of the Classical world. Not open to students who have credit in corresponding undergraduate courses.

title: Paid Internship in Anthropology
description: Paid, supervised field or laboratory experience in anthropology. Employment should supply an opportunity to use and further knowledge of anthropology. Prerequisite: permission of the internship director. Open only to anthropology majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Topics in Old World Ethnography
description: Anthropological survey of the cultural patterns of selected continents or regions, such as East Asia, Europe, the island Pacific. Prerequisite: ANTH 101.

title: Culture Areas of the World
description: Anthropological survey of the culture patterns of a selected continent or region— for example, the Caribbean, Latin America, East Asia, Europe, and the island Pacific. May be repeated for different areas.

title: Topics in New World Ethnography
description: Anthropological survey of the cultural patterns of selected continents or regions, such as the Caribbean, Latin America. Prerequisite: ANTH 101.

title: Honors Colloquium in Anthropology
description: Exploration of major issues in modern anthropology. Emphasis is on individual study and development of results. Open only to Honors College students by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Osteology
description: Laboratory dealing with the human skeleton including identification of whole and fragmentary bones and the assessment of the age, stature, sex, and race of a skeleton as applied to paleodemography, paleopathology, and forensic problems. Prerequisite: ANTH 105.

title: Medical Anthropology
description: Focuses on conceptions of health and illness from a crosscultural perspective relating non-Western techniques to Western counterparts.

title: Contemporary Problems of the American Indians
description: Detailed study of current issues facing Native Americans. particular issues facing tribes in specific regions and general issues of a pan-Indian nature will be covered. Taught in the field with seminars led by Native Americans. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Urban Anthropology
description: Explores the research carried out by anthropologists in urban areas around the world. Consideration will be given to the way anthropologists have modified their methods when confronted by the complexity of urban settings.

title: Anthropological Field Studies
description: Methods of field research in ethnography, archaeology, or physical anthropology. Stresses problem formulation, observation, data handling, and interpretation. Taught at various field locations. May be repeated for different topics. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but not more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Witchcraft, Magic, and Religion
description: Anthropological study of humankind's ageold concern with life, death, sickness, and the unknown. Discusses human attempts to control life through supernatural beings, prayer, sacrifice, and techniques of magic and witchcraft.

title: Primatology
description: Comparative survey of nonhuman primates, their biology and behavior. Prerequisite: ANTH 105 or permission of the instructor.

title: Archaeological Resources Management
description: Special problems of contract, conservation, and public archaeology, including laws and regulations, relations with government agencies, research design and methodology for reconnaissance and test excavations, site interpretation, and predictive modeling.

title: Quantitative and Qualitative Ethnographic Methods
description: Develops the ability to conduct and comprehend ethnographic research. Includes research design, data collection, analysis, reporting, basic statistics, and computer use. Emphasizes both quantitative and qualitative techniques for basic and applied research. Prerequisite: 15 hours ANTH or permission of the instructor.

title: Peoples of Southeast Asia
description: A general ethnographic survey of island and mainland Southeast Asia. Specific emphasis is on cultural contrasts between rural and urban communities.

title: Peoples of Latin America
description: General ethnographic survey of Latin America. Specific emphasis is on cultural contrasts between rural and urban communities.

title: Culture Change
description: Surveys the major concepts and processes of culture change, with an emphasis on the causes of change and their effects on individuals and groups.

title: Ethnohistory
description: Methods and techniques of ethnohistory using information on traditional ethnographic groups, particularly in the Americas.

title: The Development of Near- Eastern Cultures
description: Traces the development of cultures in the Near East through archaeological and documentary evidence and surveys modern cultural variability.

title: Unpaid Internship
description: Unpaid field or laboratory experience that uses knowledge of anthropology in a specific project or work content. Prerequisite: permission of the internship director. Open only to anthropology majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Economic Anthropology
description: Concerned with a substantive (as opposed to formal) view of allocation, conversion, and distribution of resources. Emphasizes economic development in third and fourth world countries. Prerequisite: ANTH 101 or 201 or permission of the instructor.

title: Indians of the American Southwest
description: Surveys prehistoric, historic, and contemporary cultures of selected southwest Indian groups. Emphasis is on culturespecific solutions to problems perceived in their relationship to their natural and social environments.

title: Independent Study in Anthropology
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Seminar in Anthropology
description: Integrates knowledge of current theoretical and methodological issues in the four quadrants of anthropology. Provides a setting for students to explore their own theoretical interests and present them coherently. Open only to seniors.

title: People and the Life Sciences
description: Introductory course designed for students not majoring in science. Emphasizes human and social aspects of biology: reproduction, birth control, genetic counseling, behavior, evolution, pollution, radiation, and energy. Not open to students who have credit in BIO 102, 111, or 112.

title: Biological Concepts for Teachers
description: Principles of biology as they relate to energy requirements and reproductive processes of living organisms, including the study of plants and conservation with emphasis on the human role in the environment. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs.

title: Principles of Biology 1
description: Designed for biology, allied health, and other science majors. Emphasis at cellular level: chemical and physical organization of life; prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell structure and function; bioenergetics; cell division; genetics, gene expression, protein synthesis, and evolution. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: one year of high school chemistry, one semester of college chemistry, or the equivalent.

title: Principles of Biology 2
description: Emphasis at organism, population, and community levels: major plant and animal phyla with emphasis on structure, function, classification, and phylogenetic relationships; ecology, including human ecology and environmental biology. Lecture and laboratory.

title: Microbiology for the Health Sciences
description: Introductory course for students in applied health curricula. Presents biomolecules of life, enzyme interaction, physiology and structure of representative microorganisms. Emphasis is on bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa of health significance and the hostparasite relationship. Microbiological techniques will be emphasized in laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 101 or its equivalent.

title: Microbiology
description: Microorganisms including representative bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi. Emphasis is placed on morphology, physiology, genetics, and control. Some consideration of applied microbiology. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 111.

title: Genetics
description: Basic principles of heredity and variation emphasizing meiosis, Mendelian inheritance and probability considerations, sex and gene transmission and expression, linkage and crossingover, the nature of the hereditary material, gene action, and genetic control of development. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 .

title: Cell Biology
description: An introduction to the biology of the cell, including cell differentiation and growth, the nature of the organization of the cell, basic bioenergetics and enzyme function, cell environment, membrane structure and function, cell metabolism, and the work performed by cells. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112; CHEM 231 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Ecology
description: Effects of physical and biotic conditions on the distribution and abundance of plants and animals. Dynamics of ecological systems are examined at the population, community, and ecosystem levels, and from an evolutionary perspective. Practical applications are emphasized. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems of Life Systems
description: Examines evolutionary solutions to problems of survival and reproduction faced by all organisms. Problems are investigated from a common basis rather than a taxonomical approach. Physiological processes are emphasized, including the selective pressures involved in the evolution of these mechanisms. Prerequisite: completion of all other core requirements for biology majors.

title: Pathogenic Bacteriology
description: Study of pathogenic bacteria with emphasis on morphology and physiology. Laboratory techniques in culturing, isolating, and identifying bacteria. Prerequisite: BIO 113 or 213; CHEM 130 or 231.

title: Laboratory Techniques in Biological Research
description: Principles and applications of procedures used in biological research. Emphasis is on methods of preparation of solutions, using standard curves, determination of rates of enzyme reactions, separation and identification of cell organelles, identification of cell metabolites, and separation of macromolecules. Prerequisite: BIO 112 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Immunology-Virology
description: Examination of the basic principles of immunology and virology. Topics include the immune system, the variety of immune responses, immunoregulation, and characteristics of viruses. Emphasis will be placed on virushost interactions and serological diagnosis of viral infections. Prerequisite: BIO 213 and one course in organic chemistry.

title: Internship in Biology
description: Paid, supervised field and laboratory experiences in public or private agencies (or in the Department of Biology). Training involves application of biological principles in the work environment. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Colloquium in Biology
description: Exploration of selected issues in biology with emphasis upon individual projects, study, and discussion. Open only to honors students except by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Biology
description: Practical application of biology in a variety of situations including biology instruction as undergraduate teaching assistants and discussion leaders, and practical experience in government or industrial laboratories and field stations. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Biological Communications
description: Introduces biology students to the literature of the life sciences. Focus is on information found in books, journals, indexes/abstracts, and related secondary sources such as handbooks, titles in series, and electronic databases: organization of information and methods of retrieval.

title: Developments in Modern Biology
description: Stresses recent discoveries in biology and integrates and enhances understanding of basic principles of the discipline. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Field Biology of Distant Areas
description: Includes study of the sciences peculiar to selected geographic areas: ecology, flora, and fauna. Travel may be by air. Seminars may be scheduled regularly throughout the course. Registration fee may include travel charges as well as the general fee. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Biophysics
description: The study of biologic phenomena in terms of contributing physical events. Transport processes. Absorption and emission radiation. Ionizing radiation; its effects on living tissue; use of isotopes in research projects. Prerequisite: BIO 215.

title: Evolution
description: Principles, evidence, and the historical context of modern evolution theory. Some attention will be given to the origin of life and the evolution of plants and animals. Prerequisite: BIO 100, 102, or 111 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Applied Microbiology
description: The study of microorganisms that are beneficial or detrimental to changes in foods (including milk and milk products) and industrial fermentations. This is a lecture/lab course. Prerequisite: BIO 213 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Biometry
description: Principles and application of statistics to biological problems. The use of parametric and nonparametric tests of significance in the analysis of data and the interpretation of experiments. Prerequisite: MATHS 108 or its equivalent or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Genetics
description: Bacterial and eukaryotic genetics with emphasis on recent developments in molecular genetics. Topics include alternative structures of DNA, mechanisms of DNA replication, mutagenesis, DNA rearrangements, regulation of gene expression, RNA processing, molecular and mutagenetic analysis of cell cycle. Prerequisite: BIO 214; CHEM 231. Prerequisite recommended: BIO 215.

title: Human Genetics and the Problems of Humanity
description: Current problems in human heredity. Human chromosome aberrations. DNA, the genetic code, and mutations. Consanguineous marriages and genetic defects. Mendelian principles applied to humans. Pedigrees and probability. Genetic screening and counseling. Social, ethical, and legal problems and advances in genetics.

title: Molecular Biology
description: Structure and function of macromolecules in living things. Emphasizes threedimensional structures; models for enzyme mechanisms; DNA replication; protein synthesis and membrane function; and applications of biotechnology. Prerequisite: BIO 215 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Cellular and Molecular Biology
description: Study of recent developments in cell growth and differentiation, DNA and RNA research, membrane biology, cellular and molecular evolution, and cellular control mechanisms. Prerequisite: BIO 457 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Bioenergetics
description: The study of flow of energy in biological systems with emphasis on application of laws of thermodynamics to biological processes, energy production metabolism in chemotrophs and phototrophs, and the major uses of energy in biological systems. Prerequisite: BIO 215, its equivalent, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Microtechniques
description: A lecture/lab course in the preparation of biological material for microscopic examination in teaching, research, and clinical applications. Emphasis on preparation of smears, squashes, whole mounts, paraffin and frozen plant and animal sections, and photomicrography. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112, 213, and one course of college chemistry.

title: Limnology
description: The physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of inland waters. Laboratory and several field trips will be devoted to exploring techniques for the evaluation of representative aquatic ecosystems. Prerequisite: BIO 216 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Aquatic Microbiology
description: Microorganisms indigenous to nonpolluted and polluted aquatic ecosystems. Emphasis on nutrient cycling and use of microorganisms as indicators of pollution. Morphology, physiology, and ecology of specific organisms. Lecture/laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 213.

title: Marine Biology
description: Introduction to marine environments. Properties of seawater, hydrodynamics. Phytoplankton and benthic plants. Primary production, nutrient cycles. Marine animals, surveys of major taxa. Adaptations for life on the bottom, open water, intertidal zones, estuaries, abyssal regions.

title: Bioethical Decision Making
description: Development of decisionmaking skills through the analysis and personal resolution of bioethical problems created by the application of new biological and biomedical knowledge and technologies. Prerequisite: junior standing and completion of the General Studies science component or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Designed to give undergraduate biology students with special aptitude an opportunity to participate in scientific investigation. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Forestry
description: General course in forestry with emphasis on forest policy, ecology, and management. Current issues are discussed with particular reference to their social, political, and environmental implications. Lecture and laboratory.

title: Plant Anatomy and Morphology
description: Forms, life cycles, and evolution of the major plant groups with emphasis on the origin and structure of cells, tissues, and organs in higher plants. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Taxonomy of Vascular Plants
description: Identification, use, and care of native and ornamental trees, shrubs, vines, and herbaceous plant material. The use of botanical keys, manuals, and texts in the identification of the plant taxa. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Economic Botany
description: The cultivation, processing, environmental requirements, and use of plants and plant derivatives for food, drugs, dwellings, clothing, and power.

title: Plant Propagation and Management
description: Practical experience in the different methods of plant propagation, care, and cultivation for use in the home, school, garden, and greenhouse. Also, some emphasis on diseases, pathogens, and pests of the plant.

title: Medical Mycology
description: Study of fungi with emphasis on pathogenic forms. Discusses methods for identification of fungi along with morphology and biochemistry of fungi. Prerequisite: BIO 213.

title: Plant Physiology
description: An introductory treatment of the physiological activities of green plants with emphasis on plant growth substances, photosynthesis, and intermediate metabolism. Prerequisite: BIO 112 and CHEM 231.

title: Dendrology
description: The identification and site characterization of woody plants with an emphasis on midwestern tree species. Use of botanical features and keys in field identification. Correlation of species with site conditions, plant diseases, climatic parameters, associate species, and geographical distribution. Prerequisite: BIO 112.

title: Aquatic Botany
description: The collection and identification of nonvascular and vascular plants from fresh water ecosystems. Emphasizes the morphology, physiology, and ecology of these plants to explain their distribution in nature. Class project and field trips may be used to demonstrate ecological relationships. Two Saturday field trips required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Urinalysis
description: A study of basic renal anatomy, physiology, and pathology, as well as training in the preparation of patients and collection of urine samples, conduct of routine and special tests of urine, and identification of the various formed elements in urine sediment. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Serology
description: Principles of immunology. Histology and biochemistry of the immune system. Theory and practice of the detection of antibodies and other serum substances related to disease conditions, using various diagnostic procedures. Prerequisite: BIO 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be

title: Microbiology
description: Study of pathogenic organisms (bacteria, my cobacteria fungi, and animal parasites), emphasizing isolation, culture, identification, and antibiotic sensitivity. Experience in media preparation, staining techniques, and various biochemical and serological tests for identification and sensitivity. Prerequisite: BIO 341, 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Blood Bank
description: Theory and practice of blood bank organization and procedure. Genetics and immunology of blood group systems; selection of donors; collection, processing, and storage of blood; preparation of blood products; typing, compatibility, and pretransfusion tests. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Radioimmunoassay
description: Theory and practice of the use of radiolabeled substances in the detection of hormones, antigens, antibodies, drugs, and other clinically important molecules in blood and other body fluids. Experience in such related techniques as immunofluorescence and enzyme immunoassay. Prerequisite: BIO 344. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Medical Chemistry
description: Theory and application of physiology, biochemistry, and organic chemistry in the laboratory diagnosis of abnormal metabolism. Experience with a variety of manual and automated test procedures, including preparation of patient samples, instrument calibration and maintenance, and quality control. Prerequisite: CHEM 360. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Hematology
description: Study of blood, other body fluids, and bone marrow: cells, coagulation processes, and pathological conditions. Practice in collection of samples, staining procedures, and various tests concerned with cells and clotting mechanisms, including experience with related instrumentation. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to medical technology students in the clinical year. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Structure and Development of Vertebrates
description: Comparative study of the anatomy, development, and evolutionary relationships of vertebrates. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Animal Parasitology
description: Helminth, protozoan, and arthropod parasites of animals and humans. Emphasizes identification, life cycles, hostparasite relationships, and physiology of common species. Some emphasis on medical and clinical aspects of parasites in humans, and tropical forms. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Invertebrate Zoology
description: Comparative morphology, physiology, ecology, life histories, and phylogeny of invertebrate animal phyla. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: A comparison of vital activities in the animal groups, particularly the invertebrates. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Ornithology
description: The study of birds including identification, systematics, anatomy, physiology, life histories, ecological relationships, and conservation. Field work in addition to regular laboratory periods may be required. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Entomology
description: Anatomy, physiology, taxonomy, life histories, habits, and adaptations of insects. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Ichthyology
description: The study of fish with emphasis on identification, classification, anatomy and physiology, and ecology. Emphasizes Indiana species but other important species will be included. Prerequisite: BIO 111 and 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Mammalogy
description: The evolutionary origin, characteristics, and distribution of recent mammals. The economic relationships of mammals. The collection and preservation of specimens. May require additional field work. Prerequisite: BIO 112 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Wildlife Biology
description: The identification, population dynamics, and geographic distribution of wildlife species with particular emphasis on those of the United States. The harvest and management of wildlife. May require additional field work. Prerequisite: BIO 216 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Aquatic Entomology
description: Immature and adult stages of aquatic insects, including collecting techniques, identification, ecological requirements, morphology, and evolutionary adaptations to lentic and lotic conditions. Emphasis is on aquatic insects as indicators of environmental quality and stress.

title: Physical Science 1
description: Concepts of matter and energy, mechanics, heat, magnetism, electricity, sound, and light with emphasis on understanding applications through fundamentals. Open only to students with majors in elementary education.

title: Physical Science 2
description: Structure of matter and nature of the universe; atomic structure, chemistry, nuclear physics, and planetary and stellar systems, with emphasis on recent advances in chemistry and the exploration of space. Prerequisite: SCI 290. Open only to students with majors in elementary education.

title: Teaching of Science in the Elementary School
description: Methods of teaching science concepts, process skills, and scientific attitudes are developed through direct experiences. Recent elementary science texts, courses of study, and curricular materials are examined and used as are experiments, field studies, demonstrations, and special methods. Prerequisite: 8 hours of science courses or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Teaching of Science in the Junior High School
description: Recent curriculum developments in junior high school science. Science curriculum instruction related to the physical, mental, and emotional characteristics of the junior high school student. Experiences in public schools may be required. Prerequisite: 24 hours of science courses or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Teaching Science in the Early Childhood and Primary Grades
description: Analysis of the cognitive, psychomotor, and affective processes inherent in science investigations for young children. Handson activities with science materials appropriate for early childhood and primary children. Designed primarily for students in early childhood and primary education programs. Prerequisite: 8 hours of science or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Teaching of Science in the Secondary and Junior High/Middle School
description: Philosophy and methodology of science teaching. Emphasis is on laboratory investigations, concepts and conceptual schemes, scienceoriented classroom management, evaluation of instructional activities, supplies, equipment, facilities, and curriculum materials. Experiences in public schools will be required. Prerequisite: 13 hours of science courses or permission of the department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF CHEMISTRY S. Pattison, Chairperson; F. Ault, M.
