title: Fundamentals of Human Health
description: Emphasizes lifestyle behaviors contributing to health promotion and disease prevention. General areas affecting health status are identified and suggestions made as to how healthrelated behaviors, selfcare, and individual decisions contribute to wellness and influence dimensions of health. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Community Health Problems
description: Organization of official and nonofficial health agencies at international, national, state, and local levels. Exploration of causative community conditions and diagnoses of disease and programs to combat these conditions. Focuses on selected communicable, noncommunicable, and behavior problems including traffic safety. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or another biological science course.

title: Introduction to Health Education
description: Basic philosophy and practice in health education with an emphasis on work settings and health educator roles. Early exposure to the literature and organizations that support health education. Contains a lab experience in working with a practitioner. Open only to majors or minors in health science.

title: Emergency Health Care
description: Prevention and emergency procedures of various emergency health problems and accidents, including cardiac arrest. First Aid and CPR American Red Cross certifications are offered. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Not open to students who have credit in PEP 299 or 396.

title: Health, Sexuality, and Family Life
description: Health concerns of human sexuality and family life with a focus on human reproduction, physiology of sexual response, sexual disorders and dysfunctions, sexually transmitted diseases, promotion of sexual health, and the family's role in sex education. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or permission of the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Elementary School Health Program
description: School's role in promoting health and preventing disease among preschool and elementary school children. Focus is on 2-3 HEFN HSC the school health program (instruction, services, and environment), community resources, and health problems common to school children. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Professional Experience
description: Paid professional experience in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization under supervision of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Public Health Practice
description: Public health organizations and available community health resources. Recent developments and problems in public health. Examination of recent literature on preventive medicine and human conservation. Prerequisite: HSC 160, 180, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Community Health Education
description: Introduction to a variety of community health education strategies and comprehensive health education models. Various health behavior theories and their implications for community health education program development are explored. Prerequisite: HSC 180.

title: Honors Colloquium in Health Science
description: Exploration of selected current issues in health science with an emphasis upon individualized study, reporting, and discussion. Restricted to honors students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Quantitative Methods in Health Science
description: Introduction to practical applications of quantitative methods in health. Various approaches to identify, evaluate, compare, and report existing and potential health problems in community settings. One twohour laboratory period weekly emphasizes data manipulation through advanced technology. Prerequisite: MATHS 125 or its equivalent.

title: Health Education Communication
description: Application of communication theory and skills to enhance the delivery of health education programs in various settings. A twohour weekly laboratory emphasizes the acquisition of practical skills typically used by the health education professional. Prerequisite: HSC 180, 200.

title: History of Medicine in Western Society
description: A survey of the ideas, attitudes, and institutions of medicine and public health in the Western world from antiquity to modern times, with special attention to social forces influencing medical knowledge and health care. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 460.

title: Sex Education and School Health
description: Development of an understanding of how to implement and teach a positive program of sex education aimed at helping young people develop constructive attitudes, values, and practices based on sound knowledge in accordance with American Medical Association recommendations and pertinent state guidelines. Prerequisite: HSC 261 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Patient Education: A Team Approach
description: Theories of client education and application of the education process to individuals and groups in healthcare settings. Emphasis is on the multidisciplinary team concept in planning, implementing, and evaluating client education. Application of knowledge of growth and development in meeting learning needs of clients.

title: Alcohol Problems
description: A study of alcohol as a mood modifier; its use, nonuse, and abuse in drinking societies. Critical and controversial issues relevant to alcohol ingestion will be explored for medical, economic, legal, educational, historical, physiological, and public health implications.

title: Drug Dependence and Abuse
description: Analyzes the medical, psychological, sociological, and legal dimensions of drug use in the United States. Examines the incidence and prevalence of drug abuse together with the roles played by school and community in dealing with this health problem. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Health Quackery
description: Health services and consumer protection organizations. An analysis of fraudulent health practices and nostrums, available healthcare systems, and health products. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Health and Aging
description: Dynamics of later life and the aging process with specific emphasis on health. The physiological and behavioral dimensions of the aging process will be analyzed and discussed.

title: Death and Dying
description: Analyzes the relationship between death and health with emphasis upon the physiological, medical, psychological, legal, and consumer aspects of dying in contemporary America. Investigates problems that relate to the meaning of death, care for the dying, death ritual, bereavement, and death education. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Women and Health
description: General overview of issues related to women and health: health needs of working women, special nutritional concerns, the gynecological exam, reproductive anatomy an d physiology, fertility and infertility, breast problems, wife abuse, and rape. 479 (475) practical Experience. (3) The intern will be assigned to an approved health agency or educational institution for A period of time commensurate with ic credit. Periodic and terminal a reports to an academic advisor and to the agency administrator are required for this nonpaid experience. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned in this course or in combination with HSC 675, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Environmental Health
description: Physical environment and its relationship to causes of disease. Review of environmental health problems and their solutions. Areas of study include air and water pollution, milk and food sanitation, disposal of human excreta and waste, radiological agents in the environment, and occupational health problems.

title: Epidemiology
description: Introduction to principles and methods of epidemiology, including appropriate uses of descriptive, analytical, and experimental approaches to the study of classic epidemics and contemporary health problems. Prerequisite: HSC 180, 380, and 392.

title: Public Health Education: Planning and Evaluation
description: Intended for persons planning to work in public health agencies. Emphasizes the need for planning, current settings for public health education, techniques used to identify health education components of health programs, program planning techniques, and evaluation methodologies. Prerequisite: HSC 380, 384, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Special Studies in Health Science
description: Designed to give undergraduate health science students who exhibit special aptitude and interest an opportunity to pursue special lines of scientific investigation individually. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques or skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Fundamentals of Mammalian Anatomy
description: Basic study of mammalian anatomy with detailed dissection of an animal or animal tissue with examination of representative microscopic structure. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or another biological science course. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Embryology
description: Normal development of the human organism including germ cell formation, fertilization, implantation, and organ formation. Consideration of embryonic environment, physiology, and abnormal development. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112; or ANAT 201.

title: Human Anatomy
description: Regional study of the structural and functional relations of the human body by means of dissection. Consideration of normal and abnormal development and microscopic structure of tissues and organs. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 210, 211.

title: Human Neuroanatomy
description: Offers strong background in the basic structural and functional relations of the central nervous system. Emphasis is on understanding the location of nerve cell centers and the fiber tracts entering and leaving these centers. Two twohour laboratory periods weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or ZOOL 330. Prerequisite recommended: ANAT 320 and 430.

title: Histology
description: Microscopic structure of organisms with special emphasis on the tissues of vertebrates. Introductory microtechnique. Three lectures and one laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or ZOOL 330.

title: Essentials of Human Physiology
description: Basic human physiology emphasizing the major function of each organ system including effects of nutrition, drugs, and drug abuse. Intended primarily for science teaching majors and minors in secondary education. Includes laboratory exercises designed to demonstrate physiological principles to high school students. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: BIO 102 or 111. Not open to students who have credit in PHYSL 210.

title: Fundamentals of Human Physiology
description: Physiological fundamentals as applied to human body systems with selected laboratory exercises to establish background for students entering the fields of radiology, nuclear medicine, and respiratory therapy. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: CHEM 101 or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students in nursing or teacher education.

title: Human Physiology 1
description: Vital processes with references to human functional biology. Group experimentation with recording apparatus. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: a course in biological science or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Physiology 2
description: Continuation of PHYSL 210. Functions of the human organ systems. Comparisons between vertebrate systems and mechanisms in humans. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Neurophysiology
description: The function of the nervous system. Emphasis is on electrical properties of excitable cells, synaptic transmissions, sensory and motor mechanisms, reflexes, higher sensory functions, and motor control. Prerequisite: ANAT 405.

title: Human Physiology—Selected Systems
description: Human organsystem functions with consideration of laboratory animals and their contributions to human physiology. Advanced instrumentation and animal handling techniques stressed in laboratory. One threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: one year of inorganic chemistry; BIO 111 and 112; ANAT 201.

title: Endocrinology
description: Endocrine functions in humans and mammals with special emphasis on mechanisms. Normal hormone regulation and pathophysiological principles. Laboratory experience with smallmammal surgery and endocrine testing. One threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 210 and 211; one year of general chemistry.

title: Renal Physiology
description: A detailed study of the urinary system and excretory functions. Emphasizes human physiology but also includes comparative vertebrate systems. Subject matter ranges from the embryogenicanatomic level to the biochemicalpathological level. Laboratory study includes gross and microscopic anatomy, physiologic demonstrations, and clinical testing procedures. One threehour laboratory a week. Prerequisite: general chemistry; organic chemistry; one course in anatomy; one course in physiology.

title: Cardiovascular Physiology
description: A study of the dynamics of the human cardiovascular system, stressing applications of basic physical principles and the operation of physical regulatory systems. Includes seminarstyle discussion of recent literature. Prerequisite: one course in physiology and one course in physics.

title: Human Toxicology
description: A survey of chemical, physical, zoological, and botanical toxicoses in human health. The implications and methodology of dealing with hazardous substances and poisons will be considered in detail. Prerequisite: one year of chemistry; on e year of biology; one course in physiology; one course in anatomy.

title: Neuroscience
description: Introductory study of the organization and function of the nervous system. Emphasizes integration of the structure and function of the nervous system. Prerequisite: one year of chemistry; on e year of biology or physiology.

title: Pathophysiology
description: The physiologic pathology of selected disease processes and dysfunctions. The pathogenesis of certain derangements with broad applicability. Underlying chemical, biological, and physical mechanisms will be studied. Laboratory experience will include demonstrations, specimen study, and visitations. One threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: a course in anatomy, physiology, and chemistry.

title: Special Studies in Physiology
description: Designed to give undergraduate physiology students who exhibit special aptitude and interest an opportunity to pursue special lines of scientific investigation on an individual basis. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques or skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Patient Care
description: An introduction to the hospital setting and patient care. Instruction in nursing skills and basic medical technology. Prerequisite: admission to an associate degree program in one of the allied health science options. Open only to allied health science students.

title: Cardiopulmonary-Renal Anatomy and Physiology
description: Designed to give students indepth knowledge of the respiratory, circulatory, and renal systems. Emphasis is on the respiratory system and how it interrelates with the other two systems. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Basic Respiratory Care
description: Designed to make students familiar with all types of basic respiratory care and equipment in preparation for clinical practice. Prerequisite: PHYCS 106. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Cardiopulmonary Medicine
description: An indepth study of cardiopulmonary diseases. Topics include an extensive study of pharmacology; acute, chronic, and congenital cardiopulmonary diseases; thoracic trauma. Prerequisite: CHEM 101. Open only to respiratory therapy students .

title: General Pathology
description: Designed to give respiratory therapy students an overview of human pathology. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Advanced Life Support
description: An indepth study of the management of cardiopulmonary emergencies. Topics include airway management, EKG interpretation, pharmacological resuscitation and defibrillation. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Pulmonary Function
description: Classroom and laboratory study of the measurement and interpretation of lung volumes and mechanics, diffusion and exercise physiology. Labs include basic spirometry, flowvolume loops, and plethysmography. Student must have completed all fall semester respiratory courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Basic Clinical Practice
description: Gives students the opportunity to practice clinical skills in oxygen therapy, aerosol and humidity therapy, various respiratory treatments, and bronchopulmonary hygiene. Students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses and must take all spring semester respiratory therapy courses concurrently. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Mechanical Ventilation
description: Designed to make students familiar with mechanical ventilation, including evaluation of the patient, selection of therapy, patient management, and the equipment used for these tasks. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Pediatric Respiratory Care
description: Designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge for pediatric and neonatal respiratory care. Indepth presentation of oxygen therapy, mechanical ventilation, resuscitation, and treatment modalities. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Respiratory Specialties
description: A variety of special topics pertinent to respiratory therapy. Includes hemodynamic monitoring, pulmonary rehabilitation, home care, and supervision. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Advanced Clinical Practice
description: Gives students the opportunity to practice clinical skills in the adult, pediatric, and neonatal critical care areas. Also includes experience in pulmonary functions, pulmonary rehabilitation, and home care. Skills learned in AHSC 208 will be reinforced. Prerequisite: students must have completed all spring semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 1
description: A comprehensive study of skeletal radiographic positioning procedures; introduction to radiography, radiographic terminology, procedural orientation, and an indepth description of human structure and function. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 210, 211. Parallel: AHSC 231. Open only to radiography students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 2
description: A continuation of AHSC 224, including skeletal radiographic positioning procedures and the study of special exams of all systems performed with and without contrast materials. Contrast materials, reactions, and patient care are included. Prerequisite: AHSC 224, 231. Parallel: AHSC 232. Open only to radiography students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 3
description: A continuation of AHSC 225, including additional special procedures and the equipment used for advanced imaging techniques. Introduction to computer literacy, computerized imaging techniques, and crosssectional anatomy. Prerequisite: AHSC 225, 232. Parallel: AHSC 233. Open only to radiography students.

title: Principles of Radiography 2
description: A study of radiographic film and processing, including exposure conditions and their effects and special equipment used to perform diagnostic procedures. Prerequisite: APHYS 228. Open only to radiography students.

title: Principles of Radiography 3
description: A study of clinical diseases and their effects on radiographs to include technical adjustments, film evaluation, and quality control. Prerequisite: AHSC 229. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 1
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system that includes introduction to routine radiography, file room, office, darkroom, and reading room procedures. Parallel: AHSC 224. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 2
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system that includes routine radiography and rotations through an outside affiliate. Provides the opportunity to master procedures practiced in the previous semester. Prerequisite: AHSC 224, 231. Parallel: AHSC 225. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 3
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system that includes routine radiography, tomography, nuclear medicine, radiation therapy, ultrasound, mammography, and rotations through an outside affiliate. Provides the opportunity to master routine procedures. Prerequisite: AHSC 225, 232. Parallel: AHSC 226. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 4
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system that includes computerized tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, vascular procedures, lithotripsy, and repeat rotations. Provides the opportunity to master procedures practiced in previous semesters. Prerequisite: AHSC 226, 233. Open only to radiography students.

title: Special Topics in Radiography
description: Designed to provide students with academic credit for the completion of a scientific project. Prerequisite: permission of program director. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Internship 1
description: An orientation to nuclear medicine technology. Emphasizes elementary patient care procedures and professional ethics. Prerequisite: admission to a general arts associate degree program with electives in nuclear medicine. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 2
description: Introduction to patient processing and nursing care in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: AHSC 240. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 3
description: Directed learning experiences in special areas of the nuclear medicine clinic. Introduction to scintillation camera and rectilinear imaging, in addition to related instrumentation, hot lab procedures, and dose preparation and administration. Prerequisite: AHSC 241. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 4
description: Directed learning experiences in nuclear medicine clinical procedures that include imaging, quality control of instrumentation, radiopharmaceuticals, and in vitro techniques. Prerequisite: AHSC 242. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Theory and Administration 1
description: Indepth study of the clinical theory of nuclear medicine technology as it applies to examinations performed in a nuclear medicine clinic. Introduces administrative and recordkeeping procedures required by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in the operation of a nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: admission to a general arts associate degree program with electives in nuclear medicine. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Radiopharmaceuticals
description: Preparation, quality control, and the diagnostic and therapeutic application of radiopharmaceuticals in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Radiation, Biology, and Safety
description: Somatic and genetic effects of radiation and the procedures for radiological control and safety. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation
description: Study of the components and performance characteristics of equipment and the mechanisms of detection and measurement of radioactive materials and descriptive and inductive statistics used in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Parallel: AHSC 252. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation Lab
description: A weekly laboratory for nuclear medicine technology students enrolled in AHSC 251. Parallel: AHSC 251. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: In Vitro Nuclear Medicine Procedures
description: An introduction to the basic principles of radioimmunoassay and in vitro nuclear medicine procedures. Prerequisite: AHSC 248 or APHYS 248. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Topics in Nuclear Medicine
description: Designed to offer students academic credit for the completion of a scientific project. Parallel: AHSC 243. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Introduction to Paramedicine
description: Introduction to the role and responsibilities of the paramedic, with an emphasis on response management in the prehospital environment. Topics include EMS systems, medicolegal matters, communication and documentation, trauma management, psychiatric emergencies,. stress management and crisis intervention, hazardous materials, and scene management. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 261, 262, 263.

title: Pathophysiological Origins of Emergency Therapeutics
description: Comprehensive study of the physiology of human body organ systems as they relate to the provision of emergency medical care. Overview of common pathophysiological conditions encountered by the paramedic. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 262, 263.

title: Clinical Practice 1
description: Provides the opportunity to review basic lifesupport management and practice communications and patient rapport in a controlled clinical environment. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 261, 263.

title: Field Internship 1
description: Provides practice in and evaluation of basic lifesupport knowledge and skills, and practice in the operational management of prehospital advanced emergency care. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 261, 262.

title: Pharmacological Therapeutics and Treatment Modalities
description: Comprehensive survey of drugs used in emergency medical care and overview of common home medications. Topics include pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, drug dosages, calculation, administration, terminology, and legal considerations. Prerequisite: AHSC 260, 261, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 265, 266, 267.

title: Cardiopulmonary Pathophysiology and Therapeutics
description: Diseases, evaluation, and management of the respiratory and cardiovascular systems. Management procedures include endotracheal and esophageal intubation, blood gas interpretation, surgical airway management, ECG interpretation, electrical and invasive therapeutic techniques. Prerequisite: AHSC 260, 261, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 266, 267.

title: Clinical Practice 2
description: Provides the opportunity to practice clinical skills in emergency medicine and trauma center, clinical laboratory, surgery, and cardiovascular care. Prerequisite: AHSC 262 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 265, 267.

title: Field Internship 2
description: Opportunity to practice clinical skills and scene management in the prehospital environment. Prerequisite: AHSC 263 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 265, 266.

title: Medical and Environmental Emergencies
description: Pathophysiology and treatment of medical and environmental emergencies. Topics include neurological trauma and disease; burns, bites, and stings; substance abuse and toxicological emergencies; OB and gynecological emergencies; pediatrics; geronotology; and communicable diseases. Prerequisite: AHSC 264, 265, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 269, 271, 272.

title: Advanced Cardiac Life Support
description: Overview of the principles and practices of emergency cardiac care and cardiopulmonary resuscitation as they relate to the standards of the American Heart Association. Includes case presentation and comprehensive oral, written, and practical examinations. Prerequisite: AHSC 264, 265, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 268, 271, 272.

title: Special Rescue Techniques
description: Introduction to specialized rescue techniques used in various prehospital situations. Labs include water survival, search and rescue, diving emergencies, hypothermia, cave rescue, rope rescue, and principles of patient extrication. Prerequisite: AHSC 260 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Field Internship 3
description: Opportunity to practice clinical skills and scene management in the prehospital environment. Prerequisite: AHSC 267 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 268, 269, 271. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles of Health-Care Management
description: Basic introduction to principles of managing healthcare services for students preparing for supervisory and middlemanagement positions. Includes the hospital as a workplace; hospital organization and management; job design, performance appraisals, compensation; finance, budgeting; planning, evaluation; and management information systems. Prerequisite: major or minor in a subject relating to course.

title: Advanced Concepts in Allied Health Sciences
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject to be studied. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Research Seminar
description: Knowledge and skills required to conduct clinical, educational, and managerial research in the healthcare setting. Prerequisite: health science major and senior class standing.

title: Independent Study in Allied Health
description: Designed to allow students to increase their knowledge and skills in both the technical and patientcare facets of allied health. Students may complete one of Methodist Hospital's "Adda-Comp" programs to earn credit in this course. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF POLITICAL SCIENCE R. title: Politics: Today and Tomorrow
description: An introduction to the contemporary issues of national and world politics. Emphasizes both current and political events and longterm trends in politics. 23 hrs 40 hrs CR HRS TEACHING MINOR IN SOCIAL STUDIES, 27 hours Government concentration, 15 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS

title: American National Government
description: The organization and operation of national government as it relates to such current issues as civil rights, welfare, ecology, consumer protection, and international relations.

title: Citizen and the Law
description: To help understand citizen encounters with the legal system, this course explains the operation of the legal system and the political elements of the pertinent legal issues. Uses a variety of activities, films, and lectures. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson or the paralegal program coordinator.

title: Introduction to Paralegalism
description: Provides students with concepts of paralegalism with emphasis on legal ethics and values, the development and future of the paralegal function in our present legal environment, and a presentation of the concepts of litigation and legal procedure. Prerequisite: POLS 140.

title: Legal Research and Writing
description: An analysis of court procedures and appeal procedures, an indepth examination of reference sources available to attorneys, and improvement of research and writing skills. Prerequisite: POLS 141.

title: Introduction to Planning
description: A survey of problems inherent in planning for cities and regions using contributions of such other disciplines as history, geography, sociology, and economics. Required of majors in urban studies and planning; elective for others with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Scope and methods of the study of political science. After probing the basic nature of politics, the course examines political science as a systematic empirical discipline concerned with describing and explaining political phenomena. Substantial emphasis is placed on the use of computers as tools in the scientific study of politics.

title: State and Local Politics
description: Practices, politics, and structures of state and local governments in the United States with an emphasis on the Indiana experience.

title: Urban Government in the United States
description: Structure, functions, problems, and trends in city, urban, and metropolitan governments.

title: Family Law
description: Designed to acquaint students with legal problems in domestic relations. Covers legal problems involved in marriage, separation, divorce, child custody, adoption, and nonsupport.

title: Comparative Political Systems
description: A comparison of modern political systems as represented by the principal nations•of the world.

title: Economic and Political Problems of Emerging Nations
description: Historical and contemporary problems of the lessdeveloped nations. Conditions contributing to economic, political, and social change. Problems of economic development policies and programs within the institutional structure. Internal and external pressures that influence patterns of development. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 280. Not open to students who have credit in ECON 279.

title: American Foreign Policy
description: A survey of major issues in foreign policy formulation, an introduction to the process of making U.S. foreign policy, and an analysis of relevant American strategic doctrines.

title: International Relations
description: A survey of the formal relations among sovereign states in the international system, emphasizing the operation of diplomacy, the elements of power, the procedures for the settlement of disputes, and the various modes of conflict resolution.

title: Early Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of political thought of the early Mediterranean and medieval worlds that became the foundation of modern political theories and systems of the West. Emphasis is on writings of Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, St. Augustine, St. Thomas Aquinas, and Machiavelli.

title: Modern Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of selected writings of leading political theorists from the Age of Reformation to the present.

title: Communist Political Thought: From Marx to Present
description: A critical analysis and evaluation of Marxism, Leninism, Stalinism, Khrushchevism, post- Khrushchev Communist ideology, and Maoism as a system of theoretical propositions and as an action program of an international movement.

title: Voter Polling Techniques
description: Methods by which information is obtained on the voting behavior and attitudes of the electorate. Emphasis is on producing a working knowledge of polling techniques. Includes such topics as sampling, interviewing, and questionnaire construction.

title: Introduction to Law and Enforcement
description: Survey of the development of law and contemporary law enforcement in the United States with special attention to various components of law enforcement systems, their interrelationships, purposes, and needs.

title: Problems in Public Policy
description: Current political, economic, and social problems in the United States. Consideration of relationships between government and elements of our free enterprise system, including agriculture, small and large firms, labor, public utilities, and finance.

title: National Defense Policy
description: An international survey of military capacity Political Science 271 and function provides the background for analysis of the national defense policy of the United States. Special emphasis is on American strategic interests and contr of weapons, technology, nuclear coontrlo e l, and disarmament.

title: Environmental Law and Policy
description: Significant facets of the legal system's response to conflicting demands upon environmental resources. Composition of environmental problems, control issues, policy formulation, and legal remedies.

title: Public Administration
description: Organization, personnel, and functions of the variousagencies of administration— national, state, and local.

title: Paid Internship in American Government
description: The student is paid on a parttime or fulltime basis for one semester in the office of a public official in national, state, or local government; or a candidate for public office; or a political party. Assignments depend upon the interests of students and convenience of sponsors. Prerequisite: POLS 130, 237, and 431 or 350 or 473. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Public Opinion and Political Behavior
description: The nature of public opinion, instruments, techniques, and institutions involved in formation of public opinion and the political uses and implications at home and abroad of public opinion and propaganda.

title: Public Interest Groups and Government
description: Internal government and external political strategy of private associations, such as trade associations, unions, and professional, church, and patriotic organizations. Implications of pressure group activities for constitutionalism, majoritarianism, and constituency, and the effects of pressure groups on the political process.

title: Political Campaigns
description: Considers political campaigns from theoretical and practical perspectives as the linkage between citizens and the government in a representative democracy. Designed to answer questions on the theory, strategies, and techniques of political campaigns.

title: Governments and Politics of Western Europe
description: An introduction to the concept of Europe as a political and cultural entity, to the government and political structures of the three major powers in Western Europe—Great Britain, France, and Germany—and to the current state of the Western European integration movement.

title: British Government and Politics
description: The political system of the United Kingdom, including a discussion of the Commonwealth and Britain's place in an expanding European community. Emphasis is also on Anglo-American relations and British contributions to American political arrangements.

title: Honors Colloquium in Political Science
description: Exploration of selected issues and topics in political science, with emphasis on individualized study and reporting. Open to students in the Honors College and to other outstanding students by permission of the department chairperson.

title: The United Nations and International Organization
description: Concentrated study of international organizations and the structure, functions, and current issues facing the United Nations. Students participate in a mock Security Council at Ball State and may have an opportunity to participate in the National Model United Nations Conference.

title: International Relations in Asia
description: A survey of contemporary international relations in Asia with a special emphasis on the roles of China, Japan, the United States, and the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics in this area.

title: International Relations: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics/Soviet Bloc
description: The role of the Soviet Union as a world power and the examination of Soviet strategic concepts in foreign policy.

title: Internship in American Government and Politics
description: The student works either partor fulltime for one semester in the office of a public official in national, state, or local government; a candidate for public office; or a political party. Assignments depend upon the interests of students and the convenience of sponsors. Prerequisite: POLS 130, 237, and 431 or 350 or 473. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Internship in Paralegalism
description: The internship course for the legal assistant and legal administration programs combines students' academic training with practical experience within a law firm, corporation, bank, or governmental agency. Prerequisite: POLS 140, 141, 142, permission of the program coordinator, and approval of the supervising employer.

title: Issues in Political Science
description: Investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in the field with emphasis on subfields, specialties, and materials not covered in established courses. Open to upperclass students with special interest in politics. The content is announced before each offering. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Reading and Special Study
description: Topics are chosen and investigated in consultation with the department chairperson and a professor with special competence in the area involved. Open to juniors and seniors with special aptitude and interests that qualify them to do semiindependent study. Prerequisite: basic courses in the area selected for special study and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Readings in Planning
description: Reading program developed in consultation with the department chairperson and a professor with special competence in planning. Open to juniors and seniors with special aptitude and interest in planning. Prerequisite: POLS 461 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Workshop in Political Science
description: Intensive study of selected problems in political science. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: American Political Thought
description: American political thought from the colonial period to the present. Includes the study of Puritanism, nature of rights, constitutionalism and federalism, nature of the Union, democracy, liberalism, conservatism, individualism and collectivism, welfare state, isolation and internationalism, and national security and freedom.

title: Research Methods in Political Science
description: A critical examination of methodological problems and practices in the formulation, execution, evaluation, and reporting of political science research, including a comparison of datagathering techniques, their respective limitations, and appropriate application.

title: Legislation
description: A functional study of legislative bodies and lawmaking, covering organization of legislative bodies, operation of the committee system, relations with interest groups, executive branches, bill drafting, legislative aids, controls over legislation, and movement for reform.

title: The American Chief Executive
description: An examination of the American concept of a political chief executive as a coordinate member along with the legislature and courts. Problems of jurisdiction, leadership, authority, public relations, and centralization are examined.

title: The American Judicial System
description: The nature and functions of state and federal judicial systems, including the role of courts in relation to individuals and the executive and legislative branches of government are analyzed.

title: State Legislatures
description: Legislative systems in American state government. External influences (constituencies, political parties, interest groups), internal influences (organizational structure, staff, norms, decision making), issues confronting state legislatures, and reform proposals.

title: Intergovernmental Relations
description: Analysis of relations among national, state, and local governments. Considerations of constitutional and legal bases and the nature of relations, such as grantsinaid, tax immunity, education, and interstate compacts.

title: Metropolitan Problems
description: Analysis of cities and metropolitan communities; examines the nature, characteristics, functions, governmental structure, intergovernmental relations, social makeup and problems, economic base, decisionmaking structure, and other related concerns; considers the present and future role of planning and citizen participation.

title: American Constitutional Law
description: The Constitution of the United States, its development and interpretations through principal statutes and judicial decisions. Congressional policies embodied in socioeconomic legislation and doctrines developed by the Supreme Court. Prerequisite: POLS 130.

title: Constitutional Liberties
description: Relations between the individual and the government as revealed through cases in constitutional law. Content includes cases involving the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Prerequisite: POLS 130 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Land-Use Regulation
description: An analysis of the legislative and constitutional aspects of the regulation of land use at various levels of government, including zoning, subdivision regulations, urban renewal, codes, enforcement, eminent domain, conservation, reclamation, interstate compacts, and metropolitan and regional agencies.

title: Politics and Administration of Local Government Budgets
description: Local government budgeting with emphasis on political and administrative issues in budget preparation and accountability. Topics include revenue development including tax and nontax sources, capital expenditure programming, financing pensions, contracting for services, costbenefit analysis, and federal and state grant mechanisms.

title: Administrative Law
description: Legal and political study of independent regulatory agencies; their powers, functions, and roles as determined by an analysis of relevant cases in which basic principles are identified and synthesized with other elements of public law.

title: Community Planning and Its Administration
description: Planning and development of improved land use and service activities of cities and predominantly urban communities. Consideration of scope, legal basis, implementation, and problems of planning for streets, utilities, education, recreation, transportation, zoning, and related community services.

title: Labor-Management Relations in Government
description: Examines public employee unionization, legal provisions for collective bargaining, determination and recognition of bargaining units, bilateral negotiation, and thirdparty involvement procedures, administration of agreements, and the processes and strategies in collective bargaining negotiations in public organizations.

title: Administrative Problems in State Government
description: An analysis of administrative procedures and o rganizational behavior at the state level. Special emphasis is given to the provision of government services and functions in the major areas of budgeting and taxation, education, environmental protection, public health, and public works. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 237 or 350.

title: American Political Parties
description: Organization and functions of political parties in the United States and their role in a representative democracy.

title: Women in Politics
description: A crossnational survey of women in politics with emphasis on women and public policy, the political roles of women, and the problems of women in politics within the context of contemporary public affairs.

title: Minority Group Politics
description: Deals with political impact of ethnic groups on American politics. Emphasis on both legal and extralegal means by which ethnic Psychological Science 273 groups become involved in and influence public policy. Prerequisite: POLS 130.

title: Government and Politics of the Soviet Union
description: A survey of the modes, methods, and policies by which communist philosophy is put into action by the Communist Party and by its authoritative extension, the Soviet government. Includes those peculiar governmental roles— economic planning, indoctrination, and purges—that are special trademarks of a communist political system.

title: Government and Politics of China
description: A comprehensive survey of the government and politics of modern China, both the Republic of China and Communist China.

title: International Law
description: A survey of the Law of Nations by the analysis of prominent decisions of international tribunals, examination of representative legal principles, the briefing of appropriate cases, and the conducting of mock court trials.

title: World Politics
description: Theories of contemporary interactions among states, especially the major powers. Particular attention will be given to conflict resolution.

title: Communist China's Foreign Policy
description: A comprehensive analysis of Communist China's role in international politics, with specific emphasis on the effects of Communist China's foreign policy and the response to it. Lovejoy, K. Masters, F Meeker, G. Meunier, D. Perkins, M. Stevenson, B. Whitley, A. Wittig Psychology is the science that studies the behavior of people as they interact with their environment. The behavior of lower animals is also studied, both for itself and because psychologists hope to find general principles of behavior that may apply across species. The department offers a major in psychology, designed for students intending to pursue graduate studies in psychology, as well as for students who do not plan to pursue advanced degrees in psychology. These latter students often find positions in industrial or service settings after graduation. The department also offers a minor in psychology that allows students to choose courses relevant to their majors and areas of interest. Students interested in teaching psychology at the high school level may complete social studies majors or minors with concentrations in psychology. title: General Psychology
description: Introduction to various branches of psychology and the contributions of each to an understanding of the behavior of people as they interact with their environment.

title: The Psychology of Human Adjustment
description: An introduction to how people can cope more effectively with common emotional, interpersonal, and situational problems. Selfmanagement strategies and positive coping techniques are introduced for the enhancement of personal growth and adjustment. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. Not open to students who have credit in PSYSC 317 or 432.

title: Applied Behavior Analysis
description: Introduction to the principles of operant psychology and application of these principles to situations with people outside formal educational settings. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Elementary Statistics
description: Descriptive statistics and statistics of inference. The computation, application, and interpretation of various elementary statistics. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100 and MATHS 125 or its General Studies equivalent.

title: Introduction to Biopsychology
description: Broadbased survey focusing on the methods and findings relating biological influences to behavior. Emphasis is on the anatomy and functions of the nervous system, as well as other related topics that help to explain behavior. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. Not open to students who have credit in PSYSC 468.

title: Psychology of Sexual Behavior
description: An examination of the determinants of human sexual behavior, focusing on the development of sexual identity and attitudes. Uses perspectives from social psychology, personality theory, and physiological psychology to build an understanding of this most complex behavior. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Research Methods in Psychology
description: An introduction to the use of the 3 hours from PSYSC 241 CR HRS Psychological Science 275 scientific method in the study of human behavior. Students analyze and evaluate experimental studies to gain experience with research techniques while using essential controls and acceptable procedures. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100 and a minimum grade of C in PSYSC 241. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. 301 psychology and Health. (3) Examines how psychological conditions influence disease prevention, medical treatment, stress and coping, and psychosocial adjustment to illness. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Introduction to Comparative psychology
description: Surveys the theoretical and empirical foundations of the study of animal behavior. Examination of topics associated with evolutionary principles, behavioral ecology, instinct, neuroethology, behavior genetics, perceptual systems, mate selection, and mating social systems is included. Examples are chosen from a variety of vertebrate and invertebrate species. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100 or permission of the instructor.

title: Introduction to Social Psychology
description: Overview of conditions that affect a person in a social context: attitudes, impression formation, interpersonal relations, and group membership. Examines current theories and relevant research. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Introduction to the Study of Personality
description: Presents and compares a wide variety of classical and modern theories of personality and pertinent empirical research. Considers the components of a good theory of personality and the applications of various personality theories. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Experimental Child Psychology
description: A survey of theory and research in child perception, memory, learning, cognition, and language. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241, 284.

title: Psychology of Women
description: Psychological study of women with emphasis on achievement motivation and dependency, attitudes toward women, sexrole identity, biological and social influences on women's behavior, selfconcepts and psychological conflicts, and a study of research in sex differences. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Environmental Psychology
description: Presents the current knowledge and research in environmental psychology, and studies its relevance to psychological planning for special needs of individuals. Investigates the psychological effects of selected conditions in various kinds of environments on individuals and groups. Prerequisite: PSYSC 316 or permission of the department chairperson. NR 101 is strongly recommended.

title: Intermediate Statistics for Psychological Research
description: Inferential statistics and research design, computation and interpretation of statistics in the context of psychological research design issues. Critical analysis of published research literature. Prerequisite: PSYSC 241.

title: Motivation and Emotion
description: Basic theory and research relating to motivation and emotion and applications to various facets of human behavior. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241.

title: Psychology of Learning
description: Nature of learning processes, possible influences upon these processes and resultant behavior, and applications of the psychology of learning. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241.

title: Orientation to Cooperative Education Experiences in Psychological Science
description: Seminar designed to orient people interested in cooperative education experiences to ethics, confidentiality, and other concerns of professional citizenship in human services and business settings. Prerequisite: permission of the cooperative education coordinator. Course offered on a credit/no credit basis.

title: Professional Experience
description: Designed to monitor the progress of students working in paid parttime psychologyrelated job settings and to assist them in relating and integrating job experiences with required knowledge of psychology. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Industrial Psychology
description: Application of psychological principles to personnel selection, training, and evaluation, worker motivation and morale, leadership and supervision, job design, and workplace health and safety. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Honors Colloquium in Psychology
description: Explorations of selected issues in psychology with emphasis on individualized study, reporting, and group discussion of such topics as psychobiology, social psychology, learning, personality, and abnormal psychology.

title: Special Topics in Psychology
description: Surveys theory and research on a selected topic in psychology using a lecture and discussion format. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned provided that no topic is repeated.

title: Sensation and Perception
description: Survey of theories, methods, and knowledge concerning sensory physiology, sensation, and perception. Emphasis is on studies of people. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. Prerequisite recommended: PSYSC 241, 284.

title: Psychology of Cognition
description: Survey of theories and research about human thought and memory. Topics include attention, memory, problem solving, and language. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. Prerequisite recommended: PSYSC 241 and 284.

title: Abnormal Psychology
description: Systematic study of behavior pathology. Primary emphasis is on the use of theoretical perspectives and empirical data to understand the description, etiology, prognosis, treatment, and prevention of abnormal behavior. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100. Prerequisite recommended: PSYSC 317.

title: Survey of Clinical Psychology
description: Introduction to the roles and functions of personnel in clinical psychology. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100.

title: Psychological Tests and Measurements
description: Theoretical and practical foundations underlying the construction, use, and interpretation of standardized psychological tests and inventories. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241, and 284.

title: Physiological Psychology
description: An introduction to the physical basis of behavior, involving primarily the nervous system and its structure and function. Emphasis is on the role of bodily systems in perception, learning, motivation, and conscious function. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100 and 241.

title: Organization Development
description: Presentation of techniques used to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of organizations. Critical examination of these techniques in the light of psychological theory and research. Prerequisite: PSYSC 373 or MGT 371.

title: Psychology of Selection and Placement
description: Introduction to principles of personnel testing as applied to the selection and placement process. Focus is on development of predictors and criteria, selection of an appropriate validation model, and the psychological dynamics of the interview processes. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241, or the equivalent.

title: Human Factors Psychology
description: Explores the relation between people and the physical things in their environments. Topics include design of objects based on psychological knowledge about information display, human control, and cognitive capacities. Prerequisite: PSYSC 241 or other statistics course.

title: Practical Experience
description: Monitors the progress of students participating in unpaid psychologyrelated settings and assists them in integrating such experiences with acquired knowledge of psychology. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Systematic Psychology
description: Major concepts of various schools of psychological thought and contemporary theoretical systems as they have evolved historically. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100, 241, and senior standing recommended.

title: Seminar in Psychology
description: Investigations of topics of interest in the current literature of psychology. Prerequisite: psychology major and senior standing.

title: Supervised Empirical Research Experience
description: Experience in the collection of behavioral data in the field or laboratory setting. Students work closely with a supervising faculty member. The credit hours may be accumulated in more than one semester. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Psychology
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with instructors with special competence in the area involved. The credit hours may be accumulated in more than one semester. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WORK H. title: Social Welfare and Social Work Practice 1 with Field Experience
description: Focuses on the historical development of social welfare, the social work profession, and the generalist problemsolving methods used by practitioners. Concurrent field experience required. Prerequisite: PSYSC 100; SOC 100; SOCWK 110. Open only to social work majors and minors. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment 1
description: Emphasis is on understanding the behavior of the macro social systems and the influence of these systems on human behavior. Prerequisite: SOCWK 110; SOC 100; PSYSC 100.

title: Social Work Practice 2 with Laboratory Experience
description: Content focus on core interactional skills in generalist social work practice. Emphasis is on the initial phases of the problemsolving process. Prerequisite: SOCWK 220, 230, or permission of the department chairperson. Open only to social work majors and minors.

title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment 2
description: Provides knowledge and research about major human behavior theories influencing individual and family behavior. Applies content to contemporary client situations affecting social work practice. Prerequisite: SOCWK 220, 230, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Development of Knowledge in Social Work
description: Helps students to develop beginninglevel skills for using their practice as a setting for gathering information about the effectiveness of practice. Prerequisite: SOCWK 220, 230.

title: Social Welfare Policy and Programs
description: Introduces students to social policy as a focus for social workers engaged in general practice. Prerequisite: SOCWK 220.

title: Social Services Internship
description: Work experience within a social service organization and a careerexploration opportunity. Emphasis is on paid field placements. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in SOCWK 460.

title: Selected Aspects of Social Work Practice
description: Exploration of social work practice with selected client populations and types of practice with emphasis on individualized study, reporting, and group discussion. Study will focus on social work practice and social service delivery within the identified field. Prerequisite: junior standing. Prerequisite recommended: SOCWK 110, 220, 230. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Social Work Practice 3
description: Advanced practice course that applies social work methods to individuals, families, and small groups from a generalist social work practice perspective. Integrates content from previous welfare policy, human behavior, practice, and research courses. Prerequisite: SOCWK 322, 332, 340, 350, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Social Work Practice 4
description: Advanced practice course taught in conjunction with SOCWK 424 with an emphasis on general practice in organizations. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson; SOCWK 322, 332, 340, 350.

title: Social Work Practicum
description: Provides a fulltime field placement in a social service organization selected and approved by the department. Assignments provide guided instruction, application, and development of general practice competencies. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson; SOCWK 424 and 426.

title: Social Work Practicum Seminar
description: Seminar completed concurrently with agencybased social work practicum; promotes integration and application of knowledge from previous social work curriculum sequences for social work practice, welfare policy, research and human behavior, and the environment. Prerequisite: SOCWK 424, 426, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Social Work
description: Topic to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with special competence in the subject involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. title: Principles of Sociology
description: An introduction to sociology including basic concepts used in sociological analysis. Attention is given to the world as a single society, the nature of society, culture, interpersonal and intergroup relations, and social institutions, world population, and worldwide economic and political arrangements. Intended for students unfamiliar with sociology. SOC 100 or or 9 hours from SOC 421

title: Introduction to Social Organization
description: Principles of sociology for more advanced students. The sociology of contemporary societies with emphasis on social institutions: the family, the political structure, religious groups and movements, medicine, the economy, and education.

title: The Black Community in America
description: The major social forces influencing the structure of the contemporary Black American subcommunity. Emphasis is also on an exploration of the strengths and weaknesses of this structure and its relations with the large community as bases of change in the accommodative patterns of Black-Caucasian relations.

title: Sociology of Women
description: A critical examination of the nature of women's roles and their effect on social organization. Considers the effects of changing patterns of socialization, roles, role strain, intergroup relations, and the social process.

title: Sociology of Deviant Behavior
description: An overview of theory and research on deviant behavior. Reviews three essential forms: deviance arising from disability in social and physical functioning, deviance arising from violation of social norms, and deviance arising from membership in groups observing radical social ideologies.

title: Social Problems
description: A survey of the nature and range of social problems, the conditions that give rise to them, and the methods by which our society attempts to cope with them.

title: Society and the Individual
description: Analysis of processes involved in the interaction between person and group, including the dynamics of group influence on personal behavior and the effect of personal variables on the functioning of primary and secondary groups in contemporary society. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Sociological Research Design
description: A basic course in principles and techniques for organizing, conducting, and analyzing sociological research; research strategies and selection of appropriate techniques for a variety of research problems. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Social Statistics
description: The calculation, application, and interpretation of statistics used in social and behavioral sciences. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Leisure and Popular Culture
description: Discussion of issues related to the uses and distribution of nonwork time and activities. Trends in recreation, folk arts, and the growing leisure industries. The effect of leisure activities on the natural environment and other "qualityoflife" issues.

title: Social Stratification and Inequality
description: An analysis of United States and world stratification systems with attention to the unequal distribution of wealth, status, and power. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: The Sociology of Modernization
description: The sociology of social and industrial change—modernization in the non- Western world. Study of reasons for change, for example, demographicurban, familysocial, and international pressures. Discussions of Third-World social problems and the social change models and ideologies. Prerequisite recommended: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Blue Collar Society and Culture
description: Examines the social realities, lifestyles, and selfperceptions of bluecollar society and culture. Investigates socioeconomic and demographic patterns. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Social Aspects of Illness
description: Analysis of the social components of illness and its treatment; social factors in differential disease incidence, social problems experienced and presented by patients, conditions affecting use of treatment programs, and interaction patterns within healthcare institutions.

title: Sociological Internship Experience
description: Paid supervised field experience in a public agency or business setting. Training involves data analysis, evaluation research, and implementation of agency programs under the supervision of the employer and the Department of Sociology. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Honors Colloquium in General Sociology
description: Designed to acquaint honors students with a sociological perspective of life through an openended discussion of a wide variety of fundamental social questions. Prerequisite: junior standing in the Honors College.

title: Classical Sociological Theory
description: Study of sociological theories and theorists in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, and relating these theories to contemporary social dynamics and theories in sociology. Examines the cultural and intellectual milieux in which the theories were created. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Racial and Cultural Minorities in the United States
description: The nature of minority groups and their distribution in American society; expressions, causes, and consequences of intergroup tensions and proposals for their reduction. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Social Trends in Mass Society
description: Major trends of mass society and changes in those trends. Students are encouraged Sociology 281 to perform their own analyses of changing trends using existing information. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Industrial Sociology
description: The social aspects of modern, largescale industrial and business organization, social and technological contributions to its development, and its implications for the individual worker, the community, and society. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: The Family
description: The role of the family in contemporary society, conditions influencing trends in family structure, functions, roles, stability, and their implications for both the community and individuals at varying stages of the family lifecycle. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Sociology of Religion
description: Examines why people are religious, the consequences of religiosity, and the future of religion.

title: Social Gerontology
description: Social aspects of aging in contemporary American society and elsewhere, with emphasis on special needs and emerging community and national programs for meeting them.

title: Sociology of Mental Health
description: A sociological analysis of mental health with attention to social definitions of mental illness, selfrecognition of illness, the process of seeking care, treatment institutions, and the aftermath of treatment. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Sociology of Human Sexual Behavior
description: Human sexuality (behavior and attitudes) as related to sociological variables. Sociological correlates of human sexuality (premarital, marital, and nonmarital). Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Changing Societies
description: Analysis of social change processes within societies in the modern world with attention to social movement, institutional change, and organizational change. Discussion of implementing, controlling, and measuring change. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220 or the equivalent.

title: Sociology of Childhood
description: The place of children in contemporary society, the study of socialization in various cultures and subcultures, and the child's relation to various societal institutions: family, religion, stratification, and education. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Population Problems
description: An examination of population trends and their implications for social problems and social policy, with special attention to the American scene. Conditions influencing the quality and quantity, composition, distribution, growth, and movement of populations. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Urban Dynamics and Problems
description: The historical functions and institutional dynamics of the city with special reference to contemporary urban problems, especially the inner city. Issues of community diversity and solidarity. Both industrialized and nonindustrialized urban matrixes of the late twentieth century.

title: Sociology of the Inner City
description: Analysis of the social dynamics of the urban core in metropolitan areas. Attention is given to the development of cities and their cores, stressing ecological and demographic issues. Examines the social issues associated with the concept of the inner city and policy alternatives for alleviating undesirable conditions. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220.

title: Seminar on Middletown
description: Focuses on two works by the Lynds, Middletown and Middletown in Transition, sociological classics about Muncie. Updates by teams of scholars have been undertaken. Students participate in a continuing sociological project. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220 or the equivalent.

title: Evaluation Research
description: Considerations and problems in developing and conducting research to evaluate social action programs. Topics include the unique nature of evaluation research, operationalizing and assessing variables, goal attainment measures, needs assessments, and development of guidelines for programmatic change.

title: Internship in Sociology
description: Supervised field experience in a business, industrial, governmental, educational, or other setting. Training involves data analysis, research, evaluation, or other applications of sociological theories and methods. Supervision will be jointly provided by the employer and the Department of Sociology. Prerequisite: permission of the sociology internship coordinator and the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study of Sociology
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with special competence in the subject involved. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Topics in Sociology
description: Investigations of topics of interest in the current literature of sociology. Prerequisite: SOC 100 or 220. title: Fundamentals of Public Communication

title: Argumentation and Debate
description: Theory and principles of argumentation and debate, including construction of debate cases, practice in debating, administration of a forensics program, and tournament direction. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Human Speech Communication
description: Focus on understanding human speech communication as a dynamic and complex system of interactions rather than on the skills of platform speaking. Stresses the importance of understanding and applying communication theory in everyday speech communication situations. CR HRS CR HRS

title: Voice and Diction
description: Speech improvement, dealing with voice and articulation.

description: Critical survey of major concepts in crosscultural and intercultural interaction.
