Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Historical and Contemporary Public Address
description: Speechmaking as a force in political and intellectual history; critical analysis of selected speeches in relation to political, social, and economic issues. Analysis of issues dealing with problems of progress, reform, and revolution. Emphasis is on public address in American social and political institutions. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Persuasion
description: Use of persuasion in oral and written discourse. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Contemporary Forms of Persuasion
description: Examines the modes of persuasion reflected in dimensions of American popular culture. Attention focuses on the persuasive appeals used in forms of popular culture and methods of evaluating their persuasive potential and effect. Stresses the importance of applying communication theory in everyday transactions.

title: Interviewing
description: Examines the principles and types of interviews, with application of the principles in informational, persuasive, and employment interviews. Special attention is given to the various communication elements of the employment interview process: résumés, cover letters, selection interviews, and appraisal interviews. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Discussion and Leadership
description: Principles and types of discussion as viewed by the participants as well as the leader. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Topics in Speech Communication
description: Critical examination of selected topics and issues in speech communication. Designed to help students become familiar with current trends and theoretical and methodological issues in the discipline. May be repeated once by permission of the instructor and the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Meeting Management
description: Focuses on the communication elements of effective meetings including the study and practice of parliamentary procedure. Examines how these various communication concepts relate to business, professional, labor, service, and fraternal organizations. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Business and Professional Communication
description: Focuses on communication activities in business and the professions: oral reports, persuasive presentations, interpersonal skills, and communication problemsolving strategies. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Communication Theory
description: Introduction to the varied and complex theoretical underpinnings of the human communication phenomenon. Several theoretical perspectives and applications will be explored. Topics include message theories, intrapersonal and interpersonal theories, group and public communication theories. Prerequisite: SPCH 240.

title: Professional Experience
description: Paid, supervised work and learning experience related to careers in speech communication with business firms or public agencies. Job description may include, but is not limited to, research, training, organization, and planning informative or persuasive campaigns, problem solving, and conflict management. Prerequisite: SPCH 210, 240, and 350, or 451, and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Nonverbal Communication in Human Interaction
description: Examines the nature, forms, and functions of nonverbal codes in human speech communication. Focuses on understanding one's own nonverbal communication and that of others. Prerequisite: SPCH 240 for speech communication majors; recommended for nonmajors.

title: Presentational Communication
description: Preparation and delivery of presentations and longer speeches. Examination and analysis of current theories and research in persuasion as they pertain to managers, executives, and other professionals who submit proposals, ideas, and recommendations to the scrutiny of clients, peers, and superiors. Prerequisite: SPCH 210.

title: Speech for Elementary Teachers
description: Designed for elementary and special education majors. Focuses on the development of the communication skills necessary for the classroom including creative dramatic arts, interpersonal communication, and public speaking. Speech Communication 285 Not open to speech communication majors or minors. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Speech Communication
description: Practical experience in intercollegiate debate, individual events, applied communication research, or alternate speech communication projects. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Colloquium in Human Speech Communication
description: Seminartype class focusing on various aspects and problems of speech communication as they relate to people in their personal and professional relationships. Open to honors students and to students with areas in speech with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Speech
description: Materials and methods to be used in helping students acquire desirable attitudes, habits, and speaking, including discussion forms, debating, dramatics, and radio. Prerequisite: SPCH 210, 216, and THEAT 220 or 232; identification to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: The Rhetoric of Political Campaigns
description: Examines the nature, forms, and effects of persuasion in organized political campaigns that seek to influence mass publics. Focuses on the skills needed to describe, analyze, and evaluate persuasive uses of language and to understand better the role of campaign persuasion in influencing voter behavior. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 372.

title: Rhetorical Criticism
description: The description, analysis, interpretation, and evaluation of persuasive uses of language. Theories and methodologies of selected classical and modern critics. Prerequisite: SPCH 320 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Classical Rhetorical Theory
description: Analytical studies of classical rhetoric. Primarily a systematic study of the rhetorical treatises of Aristotle, Cicero, and Quintilian.

title: Interpersonal Communications
description: Examines contemporary theories, concepts, models, and pertinent research related to the communication process in relatively unstructured facetoface settings. Particular emphasis is given to understanding message exchanges between people and how they affect the people involved. Introduces students to the approaches, variables, and topics that influence social interaction. Special attention is given to communication models, perception, symbols, systems, selfconcept, attitudes, meaning, and nonverbal message cues. Prerequisite: SPCH 240.

title: Communication and Group Process
description: Survey and analysis of smallgroup literature relevant to speech communication. Major areas included are group formation and structure, group effectiveness and efficiency, group tasks, individual versus group conformity goals, intragroup lines of communication, status and leadership problems, problem solving and conflict resolution, role relationships, and organizational techniques and problems. Prerequisite: SPCH 330 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Communication in Organizations
description: Oral communication processes in organizations, with special emphasis upon causes of communication problems and correctives for the problems. Examination of the systems of oral communication within organizations. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240, 350.

title: Communication Consultation
description: Focuses on the role and obligations of the communication consultant. Emphasis is placed upon interpersonal and team decisionmaking skills as well as developing breadth of knowledge, theoretical coherence, and the capacity to employ practical communication analysis and intervention consistent with organizational goals. Prerequisite: SPCH 451.

title: Human Communication Inquiry
description: Introduces, reviews, and evaluates the various methods of research in the field of human communication from which the disciplines's body of knowledge is derived. Open only to juniors and seniors.

title: Practical Experience
description: Unpaid supervised work experience with business firms or public agencies related to careers in speech communication. Job possibilities may include, but are not limited to, working on political campaigns, in business offices, or at summer camps. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to majors or minors in Speech Communication. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Directed Study in Speech
description: Students with areas in the Department of Speech Communication pursue a specific subject in depth in consultation with a member of the faculty. title: Survey of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
description: Introduction to speechlanguage pathology and audiology and a survey of communication disorders. Particularly helpful for persons thinking about careers in communication disorders or in related fields (teaching, nursing, gerontology, etc.).

title: Clinical Phonetics
description: Study of phonetics as applied to communication disorders. Transcription practice of normal and abnormal speech. Relationship of phonological transcription and analysis to communication disorders.

title: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing
description: Study of the Speech Pathology and Audiology 287 anatomy and physiology of the speech and hearing mechanisms. Includes respiratory, phonatory, articulatoryresonance, and hearing mechanisms.

title: Disorders of Articulation and Phonology 1
description: Overview of articulatory phonetics and normal/disordered phonological development. Discussion of structural, neurologic, and environmental conditions contributing to phonologic disability in children. Assessment and treatment procedures for children with phonological disorders. Prereqisite: SPAA 101.

title: Computer Applications in Speech- Language Pathology and Audiology
description: Introduction to computer applications in speechlanguage pathology and audiology. Overview of computer use in general, then consideration of applications. Word processing, speechlanguage analysis programs, and programs for patient use in therapy will be included. Open only to SPAA majors.

title: Language Development
description: Overview of language and language development. Consideration of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Theories of language acquisition. Cultural diversity as related to language. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Clinical Procedures and Observations
description: Methods course to prepare speechlanguage pathology and audiology students for clinical practicum. Overview of professional, ethical, diagnostic, and therapy topics. Observation of therapy is required. Prerequisite: SPAA 101, 210, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Diagnosis and Appraisal
description: Techniques in the diagnosis of speech, language, and hearing disorders. Recognizing and understanding the components of differential diagnosis. Practice in the administration and interpretation of selected tests. Prerequisite: SPAA 101, 210, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to approved clinical SPAA majors.

title: Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology Clinical Practicum
description: Clinical practicum in speechlanguage pathology and audiology. Students perform observations and provide supervised clinical services for persons with various communication disorders. Prerequisite: SPAA 311 and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to approved clinical SPAA majors. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 in any one semester or term.

title: Hearing 1: Anatomy/ Physiology, Disorders, and Assessment
description: Overview of the anatomy and physiology of hearing, hearing disorders, and hearing assessment. Hearing screening. Practice in hearing testing.

title: Hearing 2: Aural Habilitation
description: Overview of aural habilitation. Practical implications of various types of hearing losses and appropriate habilitative procedures. Amplification, auditory training, speechreading, education and vocational considerations, and psychosocial implications of hearing loss. Prerequisite: SPAA 343.

title: Speech Acoustics
description: Introduction to the physical nature of speech and its relationship to speech production and perception.

title: Neuroanatomy and Neurophysiology of Speech, Language, and Hearing
description: Overview of neuroanatomy and neurophysiology with a concentration on neurological mechanisms related to speech, language, and hearing. Prerequisite: SPAA 161.

title: Child Language Disorders 1
description: Introduction to the nature, cause, and treatment of language disorders in children. Prerequisite: SPAA 270.

title: Stuttering 1: Research and Theory
description: An introduction to the disorder of stuttering with attention directed to its symptoms and development. Reviews the research and theoretical formulations regarding stuttering and its treatment. Prerequisite: SPAA 210.

title: Organic Speech and Language Disorders
description: An overview of speech and language disorders resulting from organic problems. Areas covered include cerebral palsy, aphasia, cleft palate, dysphagia, vocal abuse, head trauma, and laryngectomy. Prerequisite: SPAA 161.

title: Orientation and Clinical Practicum in School Settings
description: Provides orientation and clinical practicum in speechlanguage pathology and audiology in school settings. Prerequisite: SPAA 319 and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to approved clinical SPAA majors.

title: Directed Study in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
description: Individual directed study in speechlanguage pathology and audiology. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. description: Historical review of the development of telecommunications as an industry. Emphasis is on growth of radio and television as a communication system in a social setting. Special attention is given to technological advances past and current in the industry.

title: Writing for Telecommunications
description: Designed to provide an understanding of and practice with the styles and techniques used in writing for the media in telecommunications. Includes extensive writing, producing scripts for commercials, news, and programs presented using electronic media. Prerequisite: TCOM 200. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles to be announced before each semester. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Media Analysis and Criticism
description: Covers the fundamental critical approaches to narrative study as applied to the telecommunications discipline. Prerequisite: TCOM 200.

title: Regulations of Telecommunications
description: Legal regulations that are foundations of telecommunications. Legal history from 1910 to the present. Actions by Congress, the Supreme Court, federal courts, and the states. Case study of rulings that most affect daily broadcasting. Prerequisite: TCOM 200.

title: Programs: Evaluation and Analysis
description: Analysis and appreciation of the complexity of programming decisions through examination of concepts, strategies, and techniques practiced by broadcasters. Includes an examination of programmatic content in order to evaluate program quality. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Organizational Video Production
description: Video production that meets the requirements of business, industry, medicine, and special interest organizations. Identifying needs; planning, executing, and evaluating productions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses, and TCOM 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: News Writing and Performance
description: Study and practice in the methods of gathering, writing, and reporting broadcast news. Practical experience in the uses of audio tape recorders and telephone recording, electronic news gathering (ENG) equipment, and other similar equipment used by radio and television news reporters. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Electronic News Gathering
description: Study and practice in the methods of gathering, shooting, editing, and reporting news with electronic news gathering (ENG) video equipment. Students will plan, shoot, edit, and produce a varied series of news reports. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Not open to students who have credit in JOURN 385. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Audio Production
description: Emphasizes techniques and skills needed for audio production. Typical experiences in radio broadcasting. A practical test is part of the final examination, and students are expected to maintain a record of their productions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. fo r these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Video Production
description: Covers the basic skills of equipment operation in miniproductions that simulate television station programming. A practical test is part of the final examination, and students must maintain a record of their course work. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Single Camera Video Production
description: Orientation and practice in producing, directing, and designing projects in the singlecamera style used in film and television. Preand postproduction processes including planning, writing, editing, and camera operation will be studied as well as film theory and techniques. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. in these four courses, and TCOM 330, 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Radio Sales
description: Study and practice of the skills for selling radio time. Both selling strategies and the use of marketing research tools are emphasized. Includes practice in preparing sales presentations for clients. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Broadcast Promotion
description: Promotional concepts, strategies, and methodologies available for carrying out efficient and effective promotional campaigns for broadcast stations. Includes practice designing and executing audience, image, and sales promotions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Television Sales
description: Skills needed for selling television time. Emphasizes the use of quantitative audience research tools. Includes practice in preparing sales presentations for clients. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: World Film History 1
description: History of world cinema from its beginning until World War II. Study of the continuing influence of American cinema, as well as key movements in other national cinemas Telecommunications 291 before 1941, such as German Expressionism and the Soviet Montage School. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: World Film History 2
description: Continues the study of world cinema from World War II until the present. Study of the continuing influence-1 9of American cinema, as well as the post national cinema movements exemplified by Italian Neo-Realism and the French New Wave films. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Film Genres
description: Study of the general types and forms of film expressions, each identified with a specific tradition. Film genres include westerns, screwball comedies, gangster films, musicals, etc. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Announcing
description: Concentrates on training and practice in the vocal interpretive skills necessary for speech presentation. Studies the structure and use of the human vocal system; analysis of copy; and delivery of verbal messages in radio, television, and recording. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Sports Announcing
description: Research, writing, production, and performance with emphasis on the remote broadcast. Study of rules, organization and planning, promotion and selling, techniques of playbyplay, and color description of major sports. Lab includes onsite practical experience. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Independent Study
description: Special service, directed by a faculty member or an approved representative of an outside agency directly related to the subject. Term project is a written report. A written proposal for a project in telecommunications must be submitted to the department four weeks before the term of study. Prerequisite: junior standing, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Internship Study
description: Presents an opportunity to gain practical, applied onthejob experience with an approved agency directly related to the business. Must make written application to the department and meet criteria before enrollment. Prerequisite: junior standing, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum
description: Production of an audio or audiovideo project. Requires submission of a detailed outlined proposal of the project to the faculty member who will direct it. A written proposal for a project must be submitted four weeks before the term of study. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Honors Colloquium in Telecommunications
description: Exploration of selected issues in telecommunications, with emphasis on individualized study and reporting. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Open only to Honors students.

title: Social Responsibility
description: Political, economic, social, and governmental influences on telecommunications. Examines contemporary issues that confront broadcasters today and the ethics surrounding them. Prerequisite: senior standing, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Organizational Media Management
description: Examination of the special requirements of business, industrial, medical, and other uses of television for instruction, information, public relations, etc. Special emphasis on budgeting and management. Corporate program sources are considered. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Advanced R-TV News Reporting
description: Instruction and practice in reporting, writing, and producing indepth broadcast news stories. Emphasis is on investigative techniques, interviewing, and strategies for finding information from public records and databases. Assignments designed for use in campus electronic media programs. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses, and TCOM 320. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Newscasting
description: Planning, gathering, writing, and presenting a television and radio newscast. Discussion of current events; evaluation of commercial station newscasts; onair production of typical news programs. Productionclass periods are three hours long. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, and TCOM 320, 323, 380. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Advanced Audio Production
description: Application of advanced audio techniques to radio, television, motion pictures, and other electronic media presentation environments. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses and TCOM 330. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Advanced Video Production
description: Advanced television production with more original and longer productions. Format for programs written and produced duplicates typical programming in the commercial broadcast operation. Requires a record of produced projects. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses and TCOM 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Management of Telecommunications
description: Problems and responsibilities of management in the telecommunications industry. Consists largely of guest lecturers, class discussion, management roleplaying, and computer projects to become familiar with administrative practices in the industry. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses, and TCOM 306, 340, 345. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Film Censorship
description: Emphasizes the moral measurements and restraints that have affected the film industry almost since its inception. A chronology of events influencing both the direction and content of motion pictures. Examines governmental, legal, church, and community pressures and restraints. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Seminar in Film Theory
description: Analysis of the key theorists in the history of world cinema as well as some influential critics of film. A special focus on the documentary film. Examines many dimensions of the documentary film: historical, commercial, informational, educational, and propaganda applications. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Film Production
description: Basic introduction to super-8 film production, as well as the theory behind the technique. Includes planning, writing, and producing minifilms. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses, permission of the instructor, and TCOM 363. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Communications Technologies
description: Explores technologies beyond the conventional broadcast and organizational systems. Topics include computer incorporation into video, fiber optic and laser transmission, teledata, home access, and interactive video. Changes in topics will reflect the newest technologies incorporated into electronic media. Prerequisite: senior standing, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Seminar in Television Production
description: Requires planning, writing, and producing a major project in television. Each project, as it moves through development, will serve as a case study for the class to discuss and evaluate. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 332, 434; THEAT 101.

title: Video Graphics Technology
description: Provides working knowledge of video computer graphic programs using Cubicomp graphics generators. Manipulating DOS files, drawing backgrounds with True Color Paint, creating threedimensional objects with Build, and combining Draw and Build for animation images in Motion program are included. Prerequisite: senior standing and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Research in Telecommunications
description: Covers the principles and methodologies of scholarly research; illustrates applications of research within electronic communication, both for scholarly investigation and for use in support of the functions of broadcasting. Principles and practice in writing about results of research. Prerequisite: senior standing and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 G.P.A. for these four courses. PROFESSIONAL LABORATORY EXPERIENCES PRE-STUDENT TEACHING PROFESSIONAL LABORATORY EXPERIENCES The purpose of prestudent teaching professional laboratory experiences is to give students pursuing teacher education a systematic, planned sequence of experiences in appropriate educational settings. These experiences are designed to make students familiar with principles of classroom management and the teachinglearning process in practical and real school environments and to help them learn how to teach. The prestudent teaching laboratory experiences culminate in EDEL 360; EDJHM 285; or EDSEC 280 which require assignment to classrooms in appropriate educational settings for the semester to observe, prepare instructional presentations, and undertake other instructional tasks appropriate for students before student teaching. The university provides laboratory settings for EDEL 360; EDJHM 285; and EDSEC 280 in the oncampus Burris Laboratory School as well as in affiliated public school systems in Muncie and others within commuting distance. Weekly seminars with a college supervisor are an integral part of the laboratory experience for these courses. STUDENT TEACHING Student teaching gives students an opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professionally licensed teachers cooperating with the university in the studentteaching program. Application for Student Teaching Students should apply for studentteaching assignments in October of the year before that in which they expect to student teach. See the Office of Professional Laboratory Experiences for additional information. Official notification of the studentteaching assignment will be mailed to students after the final eligibility determination, usually during the semester before student teaching. Students needing information about their assignments before this notification may inquire at the studentteaching office. General Consideration Students must be free of outside commitments that might interfere with fulltime studentteaching obligations. Students should not be regularly employed, nor should they carry heavy loads of extracurricular activities. Enrollment for course overload during the semester is permitted only with approval of the coordinator for student teaching. Student teaching requirements also include a set number of days in seminars conducted by the university supervisor at the beginning and end of the semester. Students should be prepared to accept studentteaching assignments wherever the university can place them for the best professional experience. Although requests for particular supervising teachers, schools, or school systems are considered, the placement process requires close cooperation with the public school systems, and there are instances when circumstances within the local school system make it impossible to honor a specific placement request. Student Teaching: Senior High, Junior High/Middle School License, grades 5-12 Student teachers preparing to teach at the senior high, junior high, and middle school levels are required to spend full time for a minimum of ten weeks in student teaching. They must enroll in EDSEC 460 (4 hours) and EDSEC 462 (3 hours). Students may take EDSEC 465, Elective Student Teaching (3-5 hours), to complete an additional part or the rest of the semester. Student Teaching: All-Grade License Student teachers preparing to teach at the allgrade level are required to spend full time for a minimum of ten weeks in student teaching. They must enroll in EDALG 470 (4 hours) and EDALG 472 (3 hours). Students may take EDSEC 465, Elective Student Teaching (3-5 hours), to complete part or the rest of the semester. Student Teaching: Elementary Standard License Students seeking licensure in elementary education must enroll for 9 semester hours in EDEL 463 (3 hours) and EDEL 464 (6 hours) and spend full time for ten weeks in student teaching. Students who want to take elective credits in student teaching may enroll for up to 3 hours in EDEL 465, Elective Student Teaching, for assignment for the rest of the semester. Student Teaching: Early Childhood Standard License Students seeking licensure in early childhood education must enroll in EDEL 461 for 6 hours and EDEL 462 for 3 hours and spend full time for ten weeks in student teaching. Student Teaching: Kindergarten-Primary Standard License Students seeking licensure in kindergartenprimary education must enroll for 12 hours in EDEL 467 (6 hours) and EDEL 468 (6 hours) and spend the entire semester in student teaching. Student Teaching: Kindergarten Endorsement Students completing the kindergarten endorsement on the standard license for early childhood or elementary education must enroll in EDEL 465 for 3 hours— student teaching in kindergarten fulltime for six weeks. Student Teaching: Special Education Students with allgrade majors in special education will complete 12 hours in either SPCED 489 (Mild Disabilities) or SPCED 491 (Serious Emotional Handicaps) or SPCED 492 (Severe Disabilities). Students with allgrade majors in special education: hearing impairments will complete SPCED 466 (1-12 hours) for a minimum of 12 hours for sixteen weeks of fulltime student teaching. Students pursuing teaching minors or endorsements in special education must complete student teaching requirements in the area of concentration as follows: mildly mentally handicapped, 8 hours (eight weeks); severe disabilities, 12 hours (sixteen weeks); hearing impairments, 6-9 hours (six to nine weeks). title: Career and Life Planning
description: Focuses on helping people make career and life plans. A series of such techniques as role playing, psychodrama, sociodrama, values clarification, and decision making are used to help students examine interrelated value systems associated with education, work, leisure, and selfexpression. Not open to juniors and seniors except by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Relationship Development
description: An introduction to the basic psychological principles and techniques of enhancing relationships with self and others. Emphasis is given to understanding selflimiting behavior, selfunderstanding, and skill development and knowledge in the dynamics of interaction with others. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Interrelational Aspects of Sexuality
description: Emphasizes the psychological aspects of human sexuality, especially in relation to emotions, attitude, and values. Stresses the psychological importance of responsibility for self in sexuality. Considers the psychological aspects of human sexual development, adjustment, dysfunction, and remediation. Designed to increase students' understanding and acceptance of their own sexuality and that of others.

title: Workshop in Applied Gerontology
description: Preor inservice education in selected areas of applied gerontology using a workshop format of concentrated study, presentation, demonstration, and practice. Specific content will depend upon the problems or interest area to which the workshop is addressed. Learners are encouraged to work out a program of personal study with help from other workshop participants and resource persons. Credit may be applied to the minor in gerontology only with permission of the director of the Institute of Gerontology. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Topical Seminar in Applied Gerontology
description: Individual and group investigation of topics, problems, or issues in applied gerontology with discussion by all seminar participants under the guidance of the instructor. Credit may be applied to the minor in gerontology only with permission of the director of the Institute of Gerontology. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Fundamentals of Counseling
description: Introduces the principles, purposes, and nature of counseling, including a review of basic counseling theories and the history of counseling, an exposure to research, and a discussion of issues in the practice of counseling.

title: Techniques of Psychological Interventions
description: Basic psychological principles and techniques of counseling. Intended as an exploratory didactic and experimental course for students planning to do graduate work in counseling and related areas or for those in other fields requiring skills in interviewing.

title: Introduction to Cross-Cultural Counseling
description: An opportunity to build expertise in counseling people of Black, Hispanic, Asian, and American Indian heritage. Emphasis is placed upon understanding the social and political bases of counseling and therapy. Prerequisite: CPSY 400 or permission of the instructor.

title: Issues in Counseling
description: Intensive study in selected areas of student need and interest in counseling. Opportunity for students to choose particular areas for indepth study under faculty supervision. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Internship in Gerontology
description: Experience in one or more of the agencies, institutions, or programs now supplying gerontological services or otherwise related to the field of gerontology. The internship is carried out under the joint supervision of the Institute of Gerontology and a practitioner representing the agency, institution, or program. Each student chooses the internship setting with the guidance of a faculty sponsor and approval of the practitioner. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. description: A seminar course for nontraditional students that offers an opportunity to explore, discuss, and reinforce changes in themselves as learners and group participators. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Evolving Roles and Job Opportunities
description: Nontraditional students will examine the evolving roles of men and women and the job opportunities available now and possibly in the future in order to make realistic career decisions.

title: Seminar on Comprehensive Programming for Lifelong Learning
description: Helps nontraditional students to prepare portfolios on learning acquired through life experiences and to develop comprehensive plans for continuing learning throughout their life spans.

title: The Adult Learner in the Undergraduate Classroom
description: A seminar for adult learners that offers an opportunity to examine the university setting, values expressed in the classroom by faculty and students, and the dynamics of higher education in terms of students' own developing values.

title: Assertive Behavior and the Adult Learner
description: A seminar that focuses on the specific need to express oneself openly and fully without fear of ridicule, rejection, or guilt. Emphasizes assertive behavior as a means of accomplishing this end. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Educational Gerontology
description: Study of education and aging with emphasis on a lifespan approach. Topics include education about aging for children and youth, career educational opportunities in gerontology, education for paraprofessionals and volunteers in aging, retirement planning education, and educational opportunities for older adults.

title: Adult Psychology
description: Developmental study of psychological stages of adulthood. Not open to students who have credit in EDPSY 355. EDUCATION: ADMINISTRATION (EDAD)

title: Legal Aspects of Education for Future Teachers
description: Special attention will focus on legal foundations of education, on rights and responsibilities of teachers (employment, tenure, fringe benefits, liability, and negotiations), and rights and responsibilities of students (attendance, discipline, and due process). description: Helps students to translate learning principles into teaching practices, to design and implement behavior analysis procedures that enhance motivation and learning in educational settings and decrease behavior problems, and to assess the effects of such instructional techniques.

description: A study of the later years of life with emphasis on the adaptations required. Includes theories of aging, physical and social changes taking place, and coping strategies.

title: Basic Concepts in Developmental Psycholinguistics
description: Overview of learning theory, developmental theory, and research design as applied to current research on developmental aspects of language acquisition and behavior. Applications of these concepts to language assessment, instruction, and remediation. Recommended prerequisites: EDPSY 250 or 251; EDPSY 290 or ENG 420.

title: Applied Study in Developmental Psycholinguistics
description: Research or laboratory experience in language acquisition or language behavior. Prerequisite: EDPSY 469 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Educational Psychology
description: Group or individual investigation and study of current issues, problems, and developments in human development, classroom learning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may earned. DEPARTMENT OF ELEMENTARY EDUCATION L. Smith, Chairperson; N. Clements, N. DePillo, S. Drake, C. title: Introduction to Teaching in the Elementary School: Seminar and Laboratory
description: Work with elementaryschoolaged children of a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds. Through seminars and counseling to plan and evaluate experiences, begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children as orientation to teaching in elementary school.

title: Laboratory Experiences: Multiethnic Young Children
description: Labseminar orientation working with preschoolaged children of a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds. Opportunities through seminars and conferences to begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Interaction Skills for the Young Child
description: Introduces students to basic skills every young child needs to acquire in order to use language competently in society. Deals with materials, methods, principles of learning, and conditions necessary for optimum learning.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood Education 1
description: Lab and seminar experience focusing on the organization, management, and control of learning environments for young children. Prerequisite: permission of the coordinator of early childhood education or the chairperson of elementary education.

title: Organization and Management of the Multicultural Classroom
description: The role of the teacher as the facilitator for learning in the elementary classroom with opportunites through seminars and counseling to plan and evaluate experiences and to begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children of various ethnic and cultural groups. Prerequisite: EDEL 101. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Handwriting
description: Development of skills in manuscript and cursive writing, methods of teaching handwriting in the elementary school, and relationship of manuscript and cursive writing to the language arts.

title: Principles of Organization and Management in Early Childhood
description: Development of understanding and skills needed for effective teacherpupil, teacherparent, and teacherteacher relationships in school settings for young children.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood 2
description: Lab and seminar experience focusing on the selection and organization of learning experiences developmentally appropriate for young children. Integrating math and science into Tch Read Sch Corrective Rdg Rdg Strat Pr Read Mid Sch (3) Read Sec Sch (3) 3 Linguistics 3 CR HRS the curriculum is an essential part of the course. Prerequisite: EDEL 160 or EDEL 190 and permission of the coordinator of early childhood education or the department chairperson.

title: Creative Experiences for Young Children
description: Designed to develop knowledge of creativity play that is developmentally appropriate for the young child. Skill in providing creative and play experiences. Work with children is an integral part of the course. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood 3
description: A field and seminar experience to assist classroom teachers in the implementation of educational opportunities for young children under supervision of a university faculty member or agency representative. Prerequisite: minimum of 36 hours in early elementary education courses, always including EDEL 160, 190, 241, and permission of the early childhood coordinator or the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit nay be earned.

title: Materials and Techniques for Teaching Children of Multiethnic Backgrounds
description: Designed to offer multisensory approaches to learning. Attempts will be made to identify learning methods and materials best suited to the students' style of learning.

title: Principles of Teaching and Classroom Management: Elementary School
description: Problems of school organization, management, control, and environment in relation to the learning activities of children. Stresses legal rights and responsibilities of teachers as well as use of instructional media and computer. Prerequisite: EDEL 101 or 160, 201, and permission of the department chairperson. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 250, except for majors in special education or speech pathology and audiology.

title: The Teaching of Language Arts in the Lower Elementary Grades
description: Development of language arts skills— listening, speaking, reading, and writing— in the primary grades.

title: Social, Historical, and Philosophical Foundations of Elementary Education
description: Emphasizes historical and social derivations of contemporary educational ideas, philosophical foundations of educational practices, alternatives for ethical decisions in education, and formulation of a personal philosophical position related to educational issues in elementary education.

title: Computer Literacy in the Elementary School Classroom
description: Develops computer literacy and application for elementary school instruction. Introduces programming in BASIC, evaluation of software, and methods of developing literacy in children. Handson experience with microcomputers.

title: Discipline and Classroom Management: Some Practical Approaches
description: Designed to help beginning elementary school teachers create and maintain effective learning environments. Emphasizes practical approaches to prevention and remediation of disruptive classroom behavior.

title: Parent and Community Relations
description: Explores important and complex roles of parents and parent substitutes in the educational development of young children. Conditions affecting parentchild interactions and skills needed for effective parenting are studied and related to the educational process. Parent involvement as a significant component of early childhood education.

title: Kindergarten Education
description: Development of the kindergartenprimary curriculum with special emphasis on kindergarten children and procedures to be used in their development.

title: Educational Programs for Pre- Kindergarten
description: Activities of young children in prekindergarten. Organization, administration, and educational program of prekindergarten care. Child development and parent education as part of prekindergarten education.

title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education
description: Involves experiences to enrich the relationships among parents, teachers, and children in the home, school, and community environments and to acquaint and involve students with the variety of community resources concerned with the welfare of young children and their families.

title: Psychology of Early Childhood
description: Study of young children of nursery school and kindergarten age, involving lectures, readings, discussions, and conferences to give individual guidance to students and help them interpret their study of the physical, mental, social, and emotional development of selected young children. Consideration is given to growth in perception, language, expression, and interests.

title: Student Teaching: Pre-Kindergarten
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 461 (6) and EDEL 462 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Pre-Kindergarten
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 461 (6) and 462 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching .

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 463 (3) and EDEL 464 (6) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 464 (6) and EDEL 463 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 463.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Elementary
description: Student teaching for six weeks in an area of endorsement or extended experience. In addition to regular student teaching requirement for elementary education. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Primary Grades
description: Designed to give future primarygrade teachers the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 468.

title: Student Teaching: Kindergarten
description: Designed to give future kindergarten teachers the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 467.

title: Practicum in Elementary Education
description: Laboratory and seminar course involving a study of progressive school practices; the philosophy of education underlying and the possibilities of using progressive practices in the public school. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Elementary Education
description: Independent study and research in elementary education. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Elementary Education
description: An analysis of one's professional preparation for teaching, identifying areas in which students need to bolster weaknesses and augment strengths and arranging for more preparation in these areas. Prerequisite: one term of student teaching. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned. EDUCATION: READING (EDRDG)

title: Self-Improvement in Reading
description: A remedial course designed to improve comprehension skills, reading speed, vocabulary, notetaking, and content reading. Students who do not achieve the 30th percentile in comprehension on the Diagnostic Reading Tests or a selected reading test administered by Reading Programs and Services must repeat the course. The course is offered on a credit/nocredit basis, and credit hours do not count toward graduation requirements. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: College Reading Skills
description: Emphasizes development of the ability to read collegelevel materials critically from a variety of subject areas and to develop flexibility of rate.

title: Rapid Reading Techniques
description: Rapid reading techniques of previewing, skimming, and scanning will be practiced. Machines will be available. Rate of comprehension and flexibility of rate will be emphasized. Techniques will be applied to student's reading assignments. Open to all graduate and undergraduate students who have basic mastery of reading skills.

title: Prereading Development
description: Basic understanding of environments and planned activities that foster positive attitudes and interests related to reading, procedures that stimulate prereading development, and related practical experiences with young children.

title: Teaching of Reading in Elementary School
description: Designed to review the current thinking, approaches, and methodology of teaching reading in today's schools. Attention is directed to readiness, word recognition and analysis, comprehension, and planning of the total developmental reading program, with emphasis on reading at the elementary level. Prerequisite: EDEL 380 or permission of the director of reading.

title: Developmental and Corrective Reading
description: Designed to review current thinking, approaches, and methodology of teaching developmental reading in the elementary schools. Provides prospective teachers with understanding of difficulties in reading and practical experiences in assessing reading difficulties and in study of corrective treatment. Includes guided laboratory experience. Prerequisite: EDRDG 400 or EDRDS 320 or EDRDM 321.

title: Using Computers in Reading Instruction
description: Prepares prospective elementary school teachers to make appropriate and effective use of the computer in a classroom reading program. Includes attention to commercially prepared courseware and teacherdeveloped applications. Prerequisite: EDGEN 320 for students pursuing the computer endorsement. EDRDG 400 or its equivalent for all others.

title: Reading Strategies and Practicum
description: Provides prospective classroom teachers (K-12) with opportunities to study and try various approaches and strategies in teaching reading. Provides experience in grouping students of varying reading abilities and in planning and implementing a classroom reading program appropriate for these students. Prerequisite: EDRDG 400,430.

title: Independent Study in Reading
description: Designed to meet the needs of students wanting to study in individually selected areas of reading education. Prerequisite: 6 hours of credit in reading education and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. DEPARTMENT OF LABORATORY SCHOOL M. Myers, Principal; P. title: Student Teaching: All-Grade
description: Required for the standard license in allgrade education. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public elementary, junior high/middle, or secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDALG 472. Open only to allgrade teaching majors.

title: Student Teaching: All-Grade
description: Required for the standard license in allgrade education. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public elementary, junior high/middle, or secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDALG 470. Open only to allgrade teaching majors. EDUCATION: FOUNDATIONS (EDFON)

title: International Dialogue on American Education and Life
description: Perspectives on American education and its cultural setting developed through interaction among international and American students and comparative study of educational and other social institutions as they relate to education.

title: Introduction to Personnel Services in Residence Halls
description: Principles involved in selfawareness, developing interand intrapersonal skills, and examining the development of community within the residence hall. Prerequisite: sophomore standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Leadership and Development of Student Organizations
description: Examines philosophical bases, group processes, and skills relevant to leadership and development of student organizations in higher education. Focuses on understanding and skills needed for effective involvement in student groups. EDUCATION: JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE (EDJHM)

title: The Junior High/Middle School Curriculum
description: Several curricular approaches appropriate for students ages ten to fourteen years will be examined in relation to current research. Legal rights and the significance of positive human relations are studied. Direct development of alternative curricular programs and appropriate use of merging structures and nontraditional materials will be emphasized.

title: Principles of Teaching, Curriculum and Classroom Management: Middle School
description: Combines the theory and practice of teaching at the middle school level. Includes direct teaching experiences with early adolescents in public school settings; seminars concerned with such topics as curriculum, instructional strategies, legal concerns, discipline, and advanced microteaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205; EDPSY 250 or 251; and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Parallel: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Independent study and research in junior high/middle school topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Instructional Strategies and Approaches in Junior High/Middle School
description: Conditions affecting the total instructional responsibilities in junior h igh/middle schools are studied. Students are required to develop skills in individualizing instruction to serve the full range of students, the ability to work cooperatively with other professional personnel, and instructional techniques and evaluation procedures especially appropriate for junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 and EDPSY 251 or 351.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Junior High/Middle School
description: Designed to prepare prospective junior high/middle school educators to cope with discipline problems in all junior high/middle school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures in preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by junior high/middle school students and ways to create positive environments for learning.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Junior High/Middle School
description: Elective studentteaching experience enables students to complete a fullsemester assignment in a fullday student teaching assignment in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDJHM 460 and 462. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Advanced Undergraduate Practicum in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Provides direct, supervised experiences for students wanting to gain increased skill and knowledge regarding Junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 280. EDUCATION: LIBRARY (EDLIB)

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

title: Selection and Management of Audiovisual Equipment
description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment and related devices. Preparation of bid specifications.

title: School Media Center and Library Administration
description: Principles of planning, organizing, supervising, and evaluating schoolmediacenter and public library services. Includes originating model program plans.

title: Technical Processing: Cataloging and Classification
description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of book, audiovisual, computer, and other materials by use of the Dewey Decimal Classification and the construction of a library catalog. Working knowledge of OCLC terminal for searching, input, and manipulation of cataloging data.

title: Technical Processing: Online and Automation
description: Practice in cataloging and organization of materials of all types. Study of principles of online systems and microcomputerbased technical processing.

title: Media Design and Production
description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work concerning production of materials and maintenance of audiovisual equipment. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Media Practicum
description: Supervised field experience for students in school media centers or libraries. Prerequisite: EDLIB 280 and approval of the program coordinator or the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Microcomputers and Library Automation
description: An introduction to microcomputers and information systems in library automation.

title: Online Information Retrieval Techniques
description: An overview of online information services and principles of information retrieval. Students develop search strategies to meet clients' information needs and conduct online searches in a supervised laboratory.

title: Methods and Materials for School Library Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching skills necessary for successful completion of assignments using resources of school library media centers and libraries.

title: Selection of Audiovisual Materials and Microcomputer Software
description: Selection and evaluation of audiovisual materials and microcomputer software for instructional and management use in libraries. Systematic identification of sources and selection tools. Practice in selection and evaluation.

title: Production of Audiovisual Media
description: A project course that meets the individual needs of undergraduate students in the production of such instructional media as 8- and 16-mm films, filmstrips, slide sets, and tape recordings.

title: Selection of Library Materials
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection of library materials. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials for public, academic, and school libraries.

title: Materials for Children
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for young adult programs. EDUCATION: READING MIDDLE (EDRDM)

title: Improving General Reading Skills in Junior High/Middle Schools
description: A general course for all junior high/middle school teachers that examines reading problems and provides specific methodology for improvement of reading skills in junior high/middle schools. General diagnostic teaching techniques appropriate for teachers in all curricular areas are to be achieved. Exit competencies are required. Lab included. EDUCATION: READING SECONDARY (EDRDS)

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: Practical procedures for developing effective reading skills to be applied by all secondary classroom teachers. Focuses on relationships between the process of reading and learning of content, on planning to meet the total range of student reading needs, and on methods and materials to enhance comprehension and study skills in all areas of secondary school curriculum. Lab included. EDUCATION: SECONDARY (EDSEC)

title: Basic Concepts of Secondary Education
description: Using classroom investigation and practical field experiences, examines the structure, function, and development of secondary education in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about preparing for and functioning in teaching careers by studying professionalism, job requirements, employment opportunities, secondary school curricula, and the role of secondary education within the entire educational process.

title: Introduction to Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Introduces prospective teachers to responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 206 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intermediate Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Advanced study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, supporting personnel, and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 200.

title: Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Secondary Schools
description: Analyzes conditions that influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis is on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American secondary schools. Lab included.

title: Advanced Study of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior
description: Focuses on indepth analyses of many of the concepts introduced in EDSEC 205. Particular emphasis is on variables that contribute to the development and maintenance of prejudice, stereotypes, racism, and oppressive conditions. Equal emphasis will be given to instructional strategies for combating such behaviors. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Laboratory Experience in Secondary Education
description: Provides direct experiences in working with students, teachers, paraprofessionals, community agencies, and other appropriate assignments for undergraduate students who plan to enter secondary school teaching. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Microcomputers in the Secondary School
description: Provides a basic understanding of the functions and applications of microcomputers in the classroom setting. Topics include evaluation and use of available software, introduction to the development of teachermade software, and the availability and selection of hardware.

title: Secondary School
description: Inducts students into the teaching act. Includes specific technical skill development, study of principles of teaching and evaluation, use of instructional media equipment, curriculum development and organizaticn , and clasromanagement. Intensive inschool assignments, observation skills, participation, and direct contact with adolescents are required. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205; EDPSY 250 or 251; and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290. Parallel: EDJHM 285. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Instructional Strategies in Multicultured Schools
description: Theory and application of special instructional strategies of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms with special emphasis on multicultured educational situations. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Planning and Assessing Instructional Programs
description: Designed to supply secondary school teachers with methods of establishing instructional programs with feedback networks that will encourage continuous assessment and appropriate alterations of the educational environment. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Intermediate Study of Microcomputers in the Secondary School
description: Designed to help students understand and develop the application of computerassisted instruction to their respective disciplines. Prerequisite: EDGEN 320 for students pursuing the computer endorsement. EDSEC 255 for all others.

title: Independent Study in Secondary Education
description: Independent study and research in secondary education. Topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Education and Professional Concerns of the Beginning Teacher
description: Opportunity to examine critically and to focus educational experience and knowledge on contemporary and personally significant problems of education. Emphasizes immediate professional concerns of prospective firstyear teachers. Prerequisite: EDSEC 301 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: High School Curriculum
description: General perspectives of curriculum principles, practices, and procedures common to secondary schools. Organizational structures, innovations, and intimate relationships between instruction and curriculum. Concurrently, students will choose areas of concentration or preparation as they relate to the total high school curriculum.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Secondary Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective secondary teachers to cope with discipline problems in all secondary school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures for preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by secondary students and ways to create a positive environment for learning.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Secondary, Junior High/Middle, or All- Grade
description: Involves a fullday assignment for either three or six weeks in a public school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDSEC 460, 462 or EDALG 470, 472. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned.

title: General Innovations in Secondary Education
description: Innovative practices will be identified, defined, and analyzed relative to their effect on secondary schools. Creative, innovative instructional approaches will be used. Field trips or visitations to innovative secondary schools will be arranged when practical, and students will concentrate on innovative practices. DEPARTMENT OF SPECIAL EDUCATION J. Van Tassel The Department of Special Education prepares teachers for people who are hearing Impaired as well as for people who have mild, moderate, or severe disabilities or serious emotional handicaps.
