title: American Sign Language 1
description: Introduction to sign language systems including fingerspelling and American Sign Language (ASL). Development of receptive and expressive skills in sign language is emphasized.

title: American Sign Language 2
description: Designed to improve conversational skills in American Sign Language to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in educational and other settings. Introduction to issues related to deaf culture. Prerequisite: SNLNG 351 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 3
description: Emphasizes the development of conversational skills in ASL and stresses SPCED 201 SPAA 270 SPCH 216 SPCED 201 EDPSY 306 EDRDG 400 MATHS 391 vocabulary building and interpretation of culturally related cues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 452 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 4
description: Advanced development of ASL fluency in occupational and professional settings. Special emphasis is given to sign dialects and related deaf cultural issues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 453 and permission of the department chairperson. SIGN LANGUAGE INTERPRETATION (SNITP)

title: Interpreting Process: Theories and Practice
description: Discussion of models of interpreting, analysis, and monitoring in both English and ASL. Prerequisite: admission into interpreter training program, SPCED 240 or the equivalent, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 320, 330.

title: Interpreting Practicum
description: Lecture and supervised field experience in a variety of interpreting settings. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Survey of the Interpreting Field
description: Overview of the field of interpreting including observations of working interpreters, discussion of roles and responsibilities, and the RID Code of Ethics. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305.

title: Interpreting Video Laboratory
description: Observation, simulation, and related practice of interpreting skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Survey of Interpreting Field 2
description: Advanced examination of various interpreter placements including educational, medical, legal, etc. Emphasizes development of specialized vocabularies for placements. Prerequisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310.

title: Interpreting Process: Transliteration
description: Advanced techniques of expressive and receptive interpreting and transliteration. An indepth examination of RID ethics. Includes lecture, discussion, and opportunities for conversing with deaf people. Prerequisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Advanced Interpreting
description: Continuation of SNITP 400 with emphasis on developing fluency in expressive and receptive communication at all levels. Topics include signtovoice and voicetosign interpretation issues and tactics and an analysis of unique problems associated with translation between oral and signbased language systems. Prerequisite: SNITP 400 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Interpreting Internship
description: Intensive field experience with placements in at least two different interpreting settings over a fifteenweek period. Supervision and regular performance feedback and discussion are stressed. Prerequisite: preprofessional checkout and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 440.

title: Professional Seminar
description: Discussion and examination of problems and issues arising during the interpreting internship. Contemporary issues in interpreting will also be presented and discussed. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 420.

title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: An introduction to definitions, characteristics, and educational needs of children who deviate from normality in mental, physical, social, and emotional ways. Examines federal and state legal bases for education of exceptional children.

title: Management Strategies for Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for effective management of the preschool disabled child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or its equivalent.

title: Developmental Methods with Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool disabled child's cognitive, language, creative, and physical environments. These developmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool disabled children.

title: Practicum—Teaching Young Disabled Children
description: Students work with disabled children in a supervised teaching practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of disabled children. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microcomputers and the Exceptional Learner
description: Introduction to microcomputer applications in special education through orientation to hardware, programming experience, word processing, and special purpose software. Also emphasizes teaching strategies for iin troducing microcomputers to children in the classroom.

title: History of Education of the Deaf and Psychology of Deafness
description: Brief study of educational provisions for the deaf from the beginning to the present and a survey of the social, educational, and vocational problems of deafness.

title: Education of Preschool Hearingand Language-Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Practicum in Special Education
description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Relations and Consulting Skills for Special Educators
description: Examines human relations strategies and skills that will help teachers of exceptional children build trust and understanding with other professionals and parents of the child. Skills are acquired through simulation and practicum modules. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C or permission of the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study
description: Designed to meet the needs of students who wish to conduct independent study, fieldwork, or research in special education. Prerequisite: Permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Legal and Procedural Foundations of Special Education
description: Studies court cases, statelevel legislation, and related historical events that preceded passage of PL 94-142. Covers definitions, procedural requirements, and legal safeguards of PL 94-142 and PL 99-457 as implemented in Indiana Rule 5-1. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Principles of Behaviorology in Special Education
description: Intermediatelevel course designed to enable special education professionals to increase their contributions to the field by virtue of adding the scientific foundations of behaviorology to their repertoires. Prerequisite: EDPSY 306 or its equivalent.

title: Introduction of Behavior Disorders
description: Introduction to the history of educating children with behavior disorders; the problems of defining, assessing, and treating behavior disorders; and types and causes of disordered behavior. Prerequisite: SPCED 201.

title: Educating Elementary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled elementary school children. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Prerequisite: SPCED 332 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Educating Secondary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled youth. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Prerequisite: SPCED 332, 334, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: Designed for future teachers of disabled or other healthimpaired students. Includes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate students with physical disabilities. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Introduction to Mild Disabilities
description: Studies psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to mild disabilities. Compares and differentiates historical and contemporary definitions of mental retardation and learning disabilities. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 301, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Persons with Mental Retardation
description: Studies various types and degrees of retardation; the psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to retardation. Emphasizes etiology, assessment, and issues. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; BIO 453; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Developmental Language Skills for Persons with Mild Disabilities
description: Compares and contrasts the language development of exceptional children with that of nondisabled children. Language difficulties are viewed as they relate to the teaching of listening skills, oral expression, written expression, and reading and other academic subjects. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; SPAA 270.

title: Assessment in Special Education
description: Educational assessment practices with exceptional children with emphasis on curriculumbased assessment and informal tests. Role of the special educator on the multidisciplinary evaluation team. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 371; EDPSY

title: Method of Teaching the Mildly Disabled
description: Studies techniques of teaching children and adults with mild disabilities. Emphasis is placed on the process by which content is taught to students of all age levels within the least restrictive environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 301, 371, 375; MATHS 391 or 392; EDRDG 400.

title: Educating Persons with Severe Disabilities
description: Studies persons with moderate, severe, or profound mental retardation, orthopedic or other health impairments, or autism. Topics include assessment strategies, instructional planning, and research on education in the least restrictive environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Educational Methods for Persons with Physical and Multiple Disabilities
description: Examines environmental adaptations, curriculum, and teaching and management methods for the instruction of persons with orthopedic impairments or special health problems. Emphasizes multidisciplinary practices and procedures based on research in education and allied fields. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378.

title: Educating Youth and Adults with Severe Disabilities
description: Introduction to the concept of lifelong educational needs of persons with severe disabilities. Topics include career education, vocational and employment programming, transition from school to work, and other educational issues for youth and adults. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378, 379; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assessment of the Young Disabled Child
description: Procedures for assessing young children with disabilities, infancy through age six. Use of observational techniques and formal and informal assessment methodology will be investigated.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of psychological characteristics and educational needs of gifted and talented children in the schools. Definitions of giftedness and identification procedures are studied; review of current and past practices in the field.

title: Speech Development for the Deaf
description: The International Phonetic Alphabet, Northhampton Charts, diacritical markings, and other methods and techniques used to teach speech to the deaf. Prerequisite: SPCH 216 and SPCED 240 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum in Speech for the Deaf
description: Observation of a person working with preschool children in developmental speech. Time will also be devoted to speech improvement for older children. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 and 446 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Language for the Deaf
description: Compares language development of hearing children with that of deaf children. Levels of abstraction and the difficulty encountered in both receptive and expressive language are examined. The philosophy underlying various methods of language teaching is studied. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and SPAA 270 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Language Methods for the Deaf
description: Language systems are studied and used in practice situations. Includes Fitzgerald Straight Language for the Deaf, Barry Five- Slate, Wing Symbols, and the Natural Method. Language outlines from different schools are used as supplementary aids. Prerequisite: SPCED 240, 266, and 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to the Deaf
description: Principles and methods of teaching reading to deaf children in the lower and higher grades; methods of teaching such subjects as arithmetic and science. Prerequisite: SPCED 240 and 266 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Student Teaching: Hearing Impaired
description: Required preservice teaching practica for students seeking licensure in special education hearingimpaired. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to .12.

title: Expressive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Gives students who have basic manual communication skills intensive training and practice in expressive interpreting for the deaf. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Receptive Interpreting for the Deaf
description: Designed to develop in students who have basic manual communication ability professional skill for interpreting manual language in special situations. Opportunity for extensive practice and evaluation will be available. Prerequisite: SPCED 468 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Special class organization, instructional materials, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally disabled. Using the individualized education plan (IEP) and mainstreaming are incorporated. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (1 hr), 372; EDRDG 430; and MATHS 391.

title: Diagnostic and Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Disabled
description: Continuation of methods and materials for the mildly handicapped, begun in SPCED 474, with emphasis on use of the diagnosticprescriptive model to determine the learner's special needs and prescription of required curricular modifications in the IEP. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 474, or 376.

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education:, mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 9 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Student Teaching: Mild Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: mild disabilities. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Special Education 325

title: Student Teaching: Physically/ Multiply Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: physically/multiply handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Seriously Emotionally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: seriously emotionally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Moderately Mentally Disabled, Severely/ Profoundly Mentally Disabled, and Multiply Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: moderately mentally handicapped, severely/profoundly mentally handicapped, and multiply handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be Indiana Academy for Science, Mathematics, and Humanities P. Borders, Director; R. Crawford, P. Freyberg, J. Margenau, J. Nemitz The Indiana Academy for Science, Mathematics, and Humanities is a residential school for three hundred of Indiana's most academically gifted high school juniors and seniors. In addition to core courses required for all students, the exploratory curriculum gives students the opportunity to sample advanced courses from the university's curriculum and to pursue individualized research and experiential education opportunities in cooperation with businesses, university faculty members, and practicing professionals. Students are also required to donate time to both academy and community service. The academy also offers opportunities for outstanding educators from throughout Indiana to teach in and study at the academy for a semester or a year. An interactive telecommunications system delivers selected academy classes to gifted pupils in other schools. In addition, academy faculty members will develop and distribute curriculum materials for the gifted and organize regular workshops for teachers of the gifted. Experiential Education Students are more likely to achieve their potential if they can apply what they are learning in an educational program that gives them experience in the world beyond the boundaries of the campus. Such experiences can also enhance students' personal and career development. Therefore, the university's goal is to offer each student the opportunity to participate in some form of experiential education. This experience may include such noncredit oncampus opportunities as working with Student Voluntary Services, becoming a research assistant, or providing tutorial services. Students may also receive academic credit through their major or minor areas of study for cooperative education or internship experiences.

title: Internship
description: For students participating in a careerrelated work experience recognized by faculty as a valid experiential assignment, but who for a variety of reasons are unable to earn academic credit. A $50 affiliation fee will be charged. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Alternating Cooperative Education
description: For students participating in a paid careerrelated work experience alternating periods of fulltime work with semesters of academic study, but who for a variety of reasons are unable to earn academic credit. A $50 affiliation fee will be charged. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Parallel Cooperative Education
description: For students participating in a paid careerrelated work experience while enrolled in university courses halftime (for at least 6 credit hours), but who for a variety of reasons are unable to earn academic credit. A $50 affiliation fee will be charged. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Study Abroad
description: Recognition of intercultural learning acquired beyond formal instruction by participants in group or individual study/travel abroad programs. Required predeparture orientation identifies criteria by which skills gained are to be measured. Prerequisite: permission of the Center for International Programs.

title: Student Leadership Development
description: Involvement in programs that significantly enhance campus life or leadership education; may include effective leadership of campus organizations, participation in programs designed to develop leadership skills, or contribution to activities that require student involvement. Prerequisite: permission of the appropriate student leadership unit or department.

title: Student Mentoring Programs
description: Opportunities (beyond the traditional orientation period) for more experienced students to assist others in making the transition and adjustment to school. Prerequisite: permission of the appropriate student leadership unit.

title: Research with a Faculty Mentor
description: Oncampus scholarly or professional experience with a faculty mentor. For example, conducting directed research in the faculty mentor's area of expertise. Departmental or academic unit guidelines must be met. Prerequisite: permission of the departmental advisor.

title: Tutorial Service: Peer Tutor
description: For anyone employed as a peer tutor for the University College Learning Center who plans, executes, and evaluates lessons. Prerequisite: permission of University College Learning Center.

title: Tutorial Service: Supplemental Instruction Leader
description: For anyone employed as a supplemental instruction leader for the University College Learning Center who plans, executes, and evaluates lessons. Prerequisite: permission of University College Learning Center.

title: Student Voluntary Services
description: Through community service, students develop social and civic responsibility that enhances their educational experience. May include work in a variety of community agencies throughout east central Indiana. Prerequisite: permission of the Student Voluntary Services.

title: Art Museum Education Assistant
description: Assists the curator of education with educational programs in the gallery such as the docent (volunteer tour guide) program and the school tour program. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the Art Museum.

title: Student Media
description: For students directly involved with the writing or production of student or university media, for example, WIPB, WBST, University Media Services, Daily News, Orient, Sports Information, News Bureau, and the Alumni Association.

title: University Computing Services Intern
description: Available for students who have technical responsibilities in an area of University Computing Services. For example, lab managers, software trainers , lab technicians, software and hardware consultants, computer operators and programmers. Prerequisite: permission of a UCS representative. title: Canada: Cultural Crossroads
description: An interdepartmental introduction to the geography, history, government, economy, literature, art, and music defining Canada's individuality and international heritage. An examination of current issues on such topics as economic agreements, environment, education, health system, and multicultural relations.

title: Honors Symposium in Global Studies
description: Focuses on the commonalities and rich diversities in global culture, economy, history, politics, and society. Taught from varied perspectives or disciplines; emphasis is on the non-Western world—Asia, Africa, and Central and South America.

title: Honors Symposium in Contemporary Civilization
description: An examination of some of the critical issues that confront contemporary civilization. Open only to students participating in the Honors College.

title: Honors Humanities 2: Middle Ages, Renaissance, Enlightenment
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the Middle Ages, Renaissance, and Enlightenment. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Humanities 3: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
description: Study of major intellectual and cultural movements of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Open only to honors students.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Biology and Human Concerns
description: Basic introduction to biological principles using humans as the major organism and emphasizing the relationship of contemporary biology to human concerns and society. Included in the course are social and ethical consequences of scientific discoveries and their societal application . Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to students who have credit in HONRS 299.

title: Honors Symposium in Biology: Human Genetics and Bioethics
description: A General Studies science course. Applying personal knowledge toward the solution of some critical biological issues confronting contemporary society. Open only to students participating in the Honors Program except by permission of the Department of Biology chairperson or the dean of the Honors College. Not open to students who have credit in HONRS 298.

title: Honors Foreign Study
description: Study in a foreign country as part of honors programs at the university. Coursework undertaken at institutions of higher learning in other countries is granted Ball State University Honors credit. Offered for letter grades or credit/no credit. A total of 32 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to honors college students accepted in a Ball State exchange or study abroad program.

title: Honors Professional Experience
description: Paid, supervised work and learning experience related to Honors education. Prerequisite: permission of the dean of the Honors College. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to Honors College students.

title: Honors Colloquium
description: Exploration of selected issues linking several disciplines. Emphasis is on discussion, individual projects, and ways of combining information from several sources. Open only to honors students by permission. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Candidate

title: Honors Practical Experience
description: Unpaid, supervised work and learning experience related to Honors education. Prerequisite: permission of the dean of the Honors College. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to Honors College students.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An inquiry culminating in an honors paper prepared in accordance with accepted standards of documentation and presentation under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to seniors participating in the Honors College or completing the requirements for departmental honors.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Available for advanced standing credit only and not through registration. Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experience meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the registrar. The Office of Academic Advising is informed of how the credit is to be applied to students' programs. description: A laboratory in technology education emphasizing the use of tools, materials, and processes which provide enrichment of the elementary program. Methods of planning and developing individual and group activity units are examined and evaluated. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Society and Technology
description: Provides an overview of the development, societal effects, and future implications of technology. Course work is designed to address human abilities to integrate resources to solve socialtechnical problems.

title: Technical Communication Systems
description: The elements, relationships, and operations of technical communication systems. Major emphasis is given to communication systems with laboratory experiences in the design, production, and transmission of various messages.

title: Construction Technology
description: Focuses on construction and management practices used to design, engineer, and construct residential, commercial, industrial, and civil structures.

title: Manufacturing Materials and Processes
description: Properties of ceramic, metallic, polymeric, and composite materials and techniques used to convert these materials into products.

title: Product and Structure Design
description: Introduces the design process and methodology used to create and transmit technical ideas using graphic methods. Major emphasis is given to technical designing, sketching, pictorial drawing, orthographic projection, charting and graphing, and reprographics as applied to developing products and structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150.

title: Energy Systems
description: Focuses on inputs, processes, and outputs associated with energy systems. Emphasis on the sources of energy; methods of controlling, converting, and transmitting energy; and the use of energyconversion systems.

title: Manufacturing Material Processing
description: Provides experiences necessary to develop essential competencies required to perform common manufacturing processes with ceramic, metallic, polymeric, and composite materials. Prerequisite: ITEDU 153.

title: Graphic Communication Systems
description: Focuses on visual communication media as a technical communication system. Major laboratory activities emphasize design, development, production, and dissemination of graphic messages. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154.

title: Transportation Systems
description: Focuses on powered transportation systems used to move people and goods. Emphasizes land, water, air, and space vehicles and transportation systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158.

title: Vocational Student Organizations
description: Emphasizes the implementation, maintenance, and evaluation of vocational student organizations.

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Introduction to the foundation and operation of various vocational educational programs. Analyzes legislation in the light of past and present issues of vocational education and its function as a vital component of the educational system.

title: Exploring Technology Education
description: Teaching of contemporary technology education as a career. Covers the development and kinds of technology programs and includes activities that emphasize the curriculumdevelopment process.

title: Constructing Structures
description: Comprehensive study of the activities involved in preparing to build, construct, and complete residential, commercial industrial, and civil structures. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154, and 253 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Electronic Communication Systems
description: Introduces the principles, components, and operation of electronic communication systems. Emphasizes design production and transmission in telecommunication information processing, and acoustical systems. Prerequisite: ITEDU 150, 158.

title: Industrial Control Systems
description: Overview of the various methods used in controlling power in the industrial setting. Emphasis is on the application of computers and other controlling devices and systems within the manufacturing, construction, communication, and transportation industries. Prerequisite: ITEDU 158, 357, or ITMFG 270.

title: Manufacturing Enterprise
description: Introduces students to the managed activities used to design, engineer, produce, and market products with additional emphasis on providing financial and personnel support for these activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 154, 253.

title: Trade and Occupational Analysis
description: A study of the fundamentals of analyzing trades and occupations. Techniques of identifying occupations by breakdown into jobs, tasks, and processes.

title: Vocational Related Class Content
description: A study of the sources of related materials and techniques of developing and using these materials.

title: Vocational Guidance
description: Principles, purposes, and practices of guidance bythe teacher. Examines and evaluates educational and occupational information, testing programs, school records, occupational trends, and jobtraining programs.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching JH/MS Technology Education
description: Problems in developing and implementing instructional strategies; preparing evaluation instruments, planning, specifying, and managing the physical environment; and establishing and maintaining a cooperative classroom environment. Topics developed in the context of junior high and middle school and field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298.

title: Strategies for Teaching Technology Education
description: Involves development and use of problemsolving, studentcentered, cooperative group, criticalthinking, and experiential strategies for teaching technology education. Includes opportunities to develop instructional media and work with students' special needs. Topics are developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: ITEDU 395.

title: Curriculum Laboratory in Industrial Technology Education
description: Emphasizes contemporary approaches to curriculum development and the preparation of instructional materials for use in industrial technology education. Students plan and execute a teaching unit in a public school setting. Prerequisite: ITEDU 298 and 395.

title: Industrial Research and Development
description: Focuses on the methodology and practices of technical research and development as conducted in an industrial setting. Laboratory activities allow students to perform basic tasks associated with product and process research and development. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 161.

title: Community Planning
description: Activities involved in planning communities. Emphasizes construction, demand, and site conditions related to developing housing, streets, utilities, schools, transportation systems, parks, shopping areas, and recreational centers for public needs. Prerequisite: ITEDU 152, 154.

title: Technical Experiences in Material Processing
description: Development of advanced competencies in casting and molding, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing processes. Prerequisite: ITEDU 253.

title: Technical Experience in Communication
description: Development of advanced competencies in the graphic, photographic, and electronic elements of communication technology. Prerequisite: ITEDU 254, 357.

title: Design and Evaluation of Transportation Systems
description: Design and operation of transportation systems. Emphasizes technical elements typical of transportation systems: control, guidance, suspension, propulsion, structure, and support. Prerequisite: ITEDU 258.

title: Study in Industrial Technology Education
description: Special investigation in industrial technology education on an independent basis. Prerequisite: senior standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Organization and Coordination of Vocational Education
description: The organizational structure, responsibilities, and roles recognized in the operation of vocational education programs. Major emphasis on state functions. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY: GRAPHIC ARTS/PRINTING (ITGRA)

title: Introduction to Graphic Arts
description: A comprehensive study of the graphic arts industry that focuses on products, reproduction processes, materials, equipment, and graphic arts careers. Related areas of instruction include design, relief printing, photooffset lithography, screen printing, color reproduction, and finishing operations.

title: Relief Printing and Bindery
description: A general applications course in relief printing and basic bindery operations found in the graphic arts industries. Major areas of instruction include copy preparation, typesetting, camerawork, conventional and photopolymer platemaking, presswork, paper, and ink.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 1
description: Introductory course in photooffset lithography that includes planning and layout, copy preparation, phototypesetting, line and halftone camerawork, platemaking, presswork, and introduction to fourcolorprocess printing.

title: Screen Printing
description: Screenprinting process as it relates to the graphic arts and printing industry and as an auxiliary manufacturing process in other industries. Topics include products, materials, equipment, techniques, inksubstrate relationships, estimating, and product design.

title: Photo-Offset Lithography 2
description: Study of contemporary applications of photooffset lithography in commercial printing and publishing. Reviews layout and planning, pasteup, camera, stripping, plates, and press. Emphasis is on camera, stripping, and single and multicolor press operations. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182.

title: Photography
description: Emphasizes camera types, exposure techniques, film characteristics and selection, blackandwhite and color film processing, printmaking, print finishing, and composition. Related areas include special photographic applications and introduction to color photography.

title: Typesetting and Copy Preparation
description: The use, operation, and application of machine principles and mechanisms as related to typesetting. Typography, copy preparation, and copyfitting are emphasized in addition to various methods of type generation.

title: Printing Estimating 1
description: Introduction to contemporary estimating practices. Emphasizes production planning, development of hourly cost and production rate standards. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 182.

title: Graphic Arts Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a graphic arts industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for printing technology and graphic arts management majors. Prerequisite: permission of the cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Graphic Arts Practicum
description: Emphasizes internal or external placement in a graphic arts setting selected and approved by the department. Provides opportunities to integrate and expand on theory gained during course work. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Quality Control in the Graphic Arts
description: Explores the basic professional practices of quality control for printed products. Focuses on instrumentation used in evaluating material and products inspection and sampling techniques, manufacturing specification, analysis techniques, and control systems found in the graphic arts industries. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Commercial Printing
description: Studies the organization and production systems of commercial printing and publishing. Emphasizes management and production systems, quality control, material control, scheduling, and production specifications. Class organizes a system and manufactures production jobs during semester. Prerequisite: ITGRA 180, 181, 182, 183.

title: Techniques of Color Photography
description: Color as it relates to photography with emphasis on additive and subtractive color processes, films, film processing, printmaking (additively and subtractively), measurement, design and composition principles. Prerequisite: ITGRA 286 or ADS 231 or JOURN 230 or the equivalent.

title: Color Separation and Process Printing
description: Study of color reproduction procedures in the graphic arts industries. Emphasizes additive and subtractive processes of color, direct and indirect separation procedures, color measurement, registration systems, and quality control procedures for color reproduction. Prerequisite: ITGRA 182, 286, 387.

title: Colloquium and Senior Project in Graphic Arts Management
description: Study and application of concepts, issues, and technological developments unique to the graphic arts. Topics include flexography, computer applications, electronic pagination, color scanning, and intaglio printing. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385.

title: Printing Management
description: Examines planning, organizing, controlling, and motivation as they relate to managing a business. Emphasis is on human relations decision making, problem solving, and coordination of management, sales, and production for successful management. Prerequisite: ITGRA 381, 385.

title: Printing Estimating 2
description: Sheetfed and web estimating. Emphasizes obtaining and interpreting specifications, pricing for profit margin, preparing quotations, printingtrade customs, multicolor presses, and signaturerelated bindery operations; application of the computer to estimating. Prerequisite: ITGRA 288.

title: Production Control in the Printing Industry
description: Productioncontrol systems used in contemporary graphic arts industries. Topics include organization systems approach, decision making, production planning and control, purchasing, inventory control, quality control, work measurement, and cost analysis. Prerequisite: ITGRA 385. INDUSTRY AND TECHNOLOGY:

title: Technical Design Graphics
description: Theory and practice of production drawings and introduction to design. Includes graphics, language, design, lettering, geometric constructions, sketching, shape description, projection, sectional and pictorial views, dimensioning, fasteners. Includes manual and computer graphics. Two weekly laboratories scheduled.

title: Introduction to Manufacturing Industries
description: Introduction to mallufacAuri ii% arid its managed activities._ research and development, production, marketing, industrial relations, and finance. Laboratory experiences involve organizing, staffing, and operating a model manufacturing enterprise. Prerequisite: appropriate 100-level mathematics course.

title: Computer-Aided Design
description: Introduces computeraided mechanical design using an interactive software package on a microcomputer. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105 or the equivalent. Parallel: appropriate 100-level mathematics course.

title: Industrial Plastics
description: Study of industrial plastics processes, materials, and product design. Includes polymer chemistry, processing nomenclature, injection molding, extrusion, extrusion blow molding, compression and transfer molding, thermoforming, and other topics. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: CHEM 111.

title: Machine Tool Processing
description: Metal separation with lathes, shapers, milling and grinding machines, bandsawing, and electrodischarge machining. Discussion of tool design, precision measurement, and safety with an emphasis on manufacturing applications. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 109 or 131.

title: Manufacturing Materials
description: Study of tests used to characterize properties of ceramic, polymeric, and metallic materials and how material properties influence their application in manufacturing. Laboratory includes ASTM and industrial testing procedures. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161; CHEM 111; MATHS 109.

title: Applied Quality Control
description: Evaluation of the quality issue. Includes data collection and analysis, manager versus operator errors, sampling, inspection, gage R&R, statistical process control, vendor quality surveys, instrumentation, TIM, Baldridge, ISO 9000, and selected topics. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161; MATHS 181 or ECON 221.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Theory and application of electronics in industry. Includes electron theory, circuit analysis, electromagnetism, motors, and generators. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: MATHS 109 or 131; PHYCS 110.

title: Automation and Computer Integrated Manufacturing Systems
description: Comprehensive technical introduction to automation in manufacturing. Includes flow line production, material handling, group technology, and flexible and computerintegrated manufacturing. Weekly labor at.ory scheduled Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 362; MATHS 112 or 132.

title: Manufacturing Design with CAD
description: Design of tools and fixtures for manufacturing. Includes general purpose workholders, modular and dedicated fixtures, jigs, fixturing principles, degrees of freedom, locating and clamping components, wireframe and solid modeling, and 3D to 2D conversion. Students design solid models of fixtures. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205, 233, 335.

title: Advanced Technical Drawing
description: Theory and practice of preparing productionrelated detail and assembly drawings in selected areas using CAD. Indepth study of geometric dimensioning. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205.

title: Programming Computer Graphics
description: Programming in FORTRAN and a graphics language such as Tektronix Interactive Graphics Language (IGL). Emphasis is placed on writing programs to create technical drawings and other graphical representations. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205 and a computer programming language.

title: Plastic Product Design
description: Includes plastic materials testing, ASTM standards, mold design and process considerations, material rheology, failure analysis, mold bases, molding problems and solutions, snap fit design, competitive processes, and other selected topics. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105, 225, 233.

title: Plastic Production Systems
description: Plastics processing with automated production equipment. Emphasizes injection molding, extrusion, and thermoforming. Appropriate applications of process capability, Ishikawa diagrams, control charts, and other process variation identification tools for both process and product analysis. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 265, 325.

title: Advanced Plastics Product Design
description: Emphasizes rheology, additives, and their impact on processing and final part characteristics, part design, mold flow, cavity fabrication, cavity material selection, part failure, cooling calculations, and rapid prototyping. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 265, 325.

title: Automated Machines
description: Theory and application of automated machines in the manufacturing environment. Laboratory focuses on the programming and operation of NC machine tools. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205, 233; MATHS 112.

title: Manufacturing Machine Tool Processing
description: Focuses on conditions that influence the control of metal manufacturing processes. Laboratory activities emphasize the significance of locators, power requirements, feeds, speeds, microstructure, coolants, and other variables. Complex operations are covered on grinding milling, EDM, and other multifunctional machine tools. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233.

title: Casting and Bending Metals
description: Flatposition welding with electric and oxyacetylene equipment. Limited work with tungsten inert gas (TIC) and metal inert gas (MIG) equipment. Emphasizes various casting methods, gating, sands, pattern design, cores, automated foundry practices, pouring, and furnace techniques. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Applied Mechanics
description: Combined statics and strength of materials with applications in manufacturing. Includes design of bolted connections, simple structures, centroids, moments of inertia, and beam design. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 262; MATHS 161; PHYCS 110.

title: Fixture Design for Metal Machining
description: Study of fixture design and other partholding systems used with metal machining. Discussion of common problems associated with fixtures when machining. Laboratory activities reinforce design concepts. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 333.

title: Fluid Power: Hydraulic Systems
description: Fundamentals of hydraulic systems emphasizing applications of Bernoulli's equation. Includes component types and designs, hydraulic circuit analysis, and design of hydraulics stems. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270, 335.

title: Industrial Safety and Health
description: Study of the practices used to establish a safe and healthful environment for industrial personnel. Includes the requirements of safetyand healthregulating agencies, and hazard recognition and correction.

title: Manufacturing Processes
description: Systems approach to the analysis and planning of manufacturing processes. Quantitative evaluation of the processing parameters influencing product quality. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 233, 262; MATHS 161 or 132.

title: Manufacturing Operations
description: Focuses on analyzing product designs and the design, engineering, and operation of industrial production systems through classroom and laboratory activities. Prerequisite: ITEDU 361 or ITMFG 105 and 161.

title: Technology Cooperative Education
description: Student works in a manufacturingrelated position in industry to integrate and expand upon theory learned in courses. A paid work and learning experience for industrial and manufacturing technology majors. Prerequisite: permission of the cooperative education coordinator. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: AC Circuit Analysis
description: Studies the behaviors of inductors and capacitors under DC and AC, RLC circuits, series and parallel resonance, diodes and transistors, and power supplies and filters. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270; MATHS 112.

title: Digital Instrumentation
description: Digital technology and its applications in manufacturing. Weekly scheduled laboratory activities include digital circuit design and instrumentation. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270.

title: Industrial Robots
description: The technology, applications, and management of industrial robots. Includes such topics as classifications, controls, sensors, programming, machine vision, robot workcell design, coordinates transformation, and feasibility study in robotics. Prerequisite: ITMFG 161, 270, 370, and computer programming experience.

title: Training and Development in Industry
description: Training and development in industry and their relationship to the job and the organization. Emphasizes skills needed to systematically plan, implement, evaluate, and revise training and development programs. Provides opportunities for practical application and practice.

title: Quantitative Design of Plastics Molds
description: Numerical and computer design of molds. Flow and cooling analysis, part shrinkage and cost analysis. Use of component and properties database catalogs. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 205, 325, 340. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Three-Dimensional Modeling
description: Theory of three dimensional coordinate geometry, viewing operations, surface and solid models with applications in manufacturing. Computer aided manufacturing using solid, surface, and wireframe models. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 305; MATHS 161.

title: Design of Experiments in Manufacturing
description: Extensive study and experimentation in industrial materials and processing research. Includes but is not limited to singlefactorial, multifactorial, ANOVA, Taguchi design of experiments. Prerequisite: ITMFG 326, 327; or 362, 463.

title: Research and Development in Plastics
description: Development of research started in ITMFG 425. includes aspects of materials. testing, literature searches/review, and others. Capstone course. Extensive laboratory work required. Prerequisite: ITMFG 340, 425.

title: Research and Development in Metals
description: Research and development of problems related to metals manufacturing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 333 and 334, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Industrial Seminar
description: Guest lectures on contemporary topics in manufacturing. Student presentations on capstone projects. Information and guidance in seeking employment in manufacturing. Prerequisite or parallel: ITMFG 473. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Manufacturing Controls
description: Studies the controls of manufacturing. Topics include cost estimation and control, manufacturing resources planning (MRP), justintime (JIT), production and inventory controls, management information systems (MIS), and other advanced control technology. Weekly laboratory scheduled. Prerequisite: ITMFG 301, 362; MATHS 162 or 132.

title: Industrial Programmable Controls
description: Emphasizes programmable controls in industry. Topics include relay controls, programmable controller controls, and incremental motion controls. Laboratory activities involve control applications using motor control panel, programmable controller panel, and stepper and servo control trainers. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Microprocessor and Microcomputer Systems
description: Architecture, programming, interfacing, and applications of microprocessor and microcomputer systems. Weekly scheduled laboratory work includes assembly language programming and machine to computer interfacing. Prerequisite: ITMFG 270 and programming experience.

title: Electric Machines and Controls
description: Principles and applications of power transformers, DC and AC generators, and DC and AC motors; controls and testing of various machines. Laboratory experiments. Prerequisite: ITMFG 370.

title: Projects in Computer-Aided Manufacturing
description: Individual project applying CNC, CAD, CAM, robotics, and other computerbased technology in manufacturing systems. Capstone course. Extensive laboratory work required. Prerequisite: senior standing. Parallel: ITMFG 340, 425, 463.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Study semiconductor devices, rectifiers, SCR, frequency conversion, digital and analog transducers, optoelectronics, operational amplifiers, and the industrial applications of these devices.

title: Industrial Electronics Fabrication
description: Focuses on printed circuit board design, development, fabrication, and production. Electronic inventory and component assembly are studied as they relate to the manufacturing process. Prerequisite: ITMFG 475 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Problems in Industrial Technology
description: Individual advanced study and experimentation in one or more of the areas of concentration: metals, plastics, design, or factory electronics. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. PURDUE UNIVERSITY—MECHANICAL ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY (PUMET)

title: Production Drawing
description: Application of principles of engineering drawing to detail, assembly, design layout, equipment installations, and related drawings. Prerequisite: ITMFG 105.

title: Industrial Organization
description: Organizational structures, operational, financial, marketing, and accounting activities; duties of management, planning, control, personnel, safety, wages, policy, and human conditions necessary for effective management.

title: Applied Statics
description: A study of force systems, resultants and equilibrium, trusses, frames, beams, shear, and moments in beams. Prerequisite: MATHS 112; PUMET 160.

title: Materials and Processes 1
description: Structures, properties, and applications of metals, ceramics, and polymers commonly used in industry. Includes primary production processes as well as heat treatments and hot or cold working to meet varied commercial needs. Introduces metallurgy and environmental considerations.

title: Materials and Processes 2
description: Basic casting, welding, and joining processes. Foundry areas include patterns, cores, molding, melting, and cleaning. Presents basic arc, gas, TIG, and MIG welding methods as well as the metallurgy of welding processes.

title: Applied Engineering Computational Analysis
description: Computations with the electronic calculator. The factor label method of unit conversion of commonly used engineering (including metric) units. Construction, drawing, and use of engineering graphs for both descriptive and computational purposes. Introduces computer programming using the BASIC language with emphasis on development of skills. title: Dynamics
description: Applied fundamentals of dynamic forces, including displacement, velocities, accelerations, work energy, power, impulse, momentum, and impact. Prerequisite: PUMET 111; MATHS 161.

title: Machine Elements
description: Applies theories and methods developed in statics, dynamics, and strength of materials to the selection of basic machine components. Develops the fundamental principles required for the selection of the elements of which a machine is composed. Prerequisite: CS 118; PUMET 211, 213.

title: Heat and Power 1
description: Principles of thermodynamics and fluid dynamics as applied to the conservation laws of mass and energy, prime movers, and power cycles. Prerequisite: MATHS 161; PUMET 160.

description: Manufacturing processes and tools used by industry to convert bars, forgings, castings, plate, and sheet materials into finished products. Includes basic mechanics of materials removal and forming, measuring, quality control, and safety of operations. Prerequisite: PUMET 141.

title: Introduction to the U.S. Army
description: Studies the organization, history, and functions of the United States Army. Includes basic subjects such as rappelling, land navigation, combat communications, and individual weapons. Military leadership and tactics are also taught in both the classroom and the field. Open to all students.

title: Introduction to Basic Military Leadership
description: Examines numerous Army skills and tasks needed to become an effective officer. Subjects range from orienteering, rifle markmanship, and survival techniques, to weapons assembly, chemical protection, and leadership. Taught in the classroom and the field. Open to all students.

title: Squad Tactics and Leadership
description: Examines light infantry tactics at squad level. Encompasses tactical techniques such as movement to contact, ambush, recon patrols, and special operations. Also includes air assault operations, command and control techniques. Taught in the classroom and the field. Open to all students.

title: Platoon Tactics and Leadership
description: Focusing on platoons, continued study of tactics at a higher level. description: Introduction to drill and ceremonies, role of the noncommissioned officer, logistics, intelligence, the Soviet army, principles of war and tactics. Prerequisite: MIL 202 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Military Leadership
description: Analysis of leadership and management problems. Military tactics at squad and platoon level, military skills including advanced land navigation, and radio communications. Prerequisite: MIL 301 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Military Profession
description: Seminar on ethics and professionalism, discussion and practical exercises in preparing military correspondence and conducting briefings. Prerequisite: MIL 302 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Taking Command
description: Continued study of leadership with emphasis on duties of an officer; introduction to laws of war and military justice system; discussion of training management. Prerequisite: MIL 401 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Independent Study in Military Science
description: An opportunity to investigate a topic of particular interest to the student under the supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing.
