Prerequisite: MKG 300 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Business and Finance in Sport Administration
description: Investigation of the business and financial aspects of intercollegiate, interscholastic, and professional sport. Emphasis is on the elements of business that directly affect budgetary and fiscal control of each of the levels of sport. Prerequisite: FIN 350 and permission of the sport studies program director Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Evaluation in Physical Education
description: Measurement and evaluation in physical education with emphasis on underlying philosophy, tests, construction, and use of test results.

title: Teaching Physical Activity to the Older Adult
description: Designed to teach students to recognize the characteristics of the older adult and to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate a program of physical activity based upon the special needs of the older adult. Prerequisite: PEP 212.

title: Advanced Aquatics for the Physical Educator
description: Swimming and rescue skills necessary to complete American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor Program. Emphasizes a broad range of other aquatic experiences and teaching methodologies. WSI certification may be obtained. Prerequisite: PEP 215.

title: Wellness through Aquatic Exercise
description: Introduction to the objectives, format, and conduct of instructional endurance swimming and water exercise classes, emphasizing participation and application of fitness and related concepts to selected aquatic activities. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Adapted Aquatics
description: Concerned with methodologies used to teach swimming to exceptional persons. Important for aquatics instructors, rehabilitation personnel, prephysical therapy, adapted physical education, exercise science, and athletic training. Concentrates on practical application. Prerequisite: PEP 315 or 353 or permission of the instructor.

title: Assessment in Adapted Physical Education
description: Introduction to appropriate instruments for assessing the motor and fitness needs of disabled people in physical education. Practical experience in administering standardized and normed referenced tests. Students develop IEPs. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or 494.

title: Wheelchair Recreational Activities and Pursuits
description: Wheelchair leisure activities, including basketball, softball, bowling, table tennis, soccer, and others. Emphasizes rules and regulations. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the instructor.

title: Program Development/Fitness Assessment for People with Disabilities
description: Designed to provide, in a clinical setting, learning experience associated with fitness assessment, program development, and implementation for people with disabilities. Recommended for exercise science, athletic training, and prephysical therapy majors.

title: Organization and Planning for Coaching Sports
description: Designed to introduce procedures involved in the organization, training, and planning of team and individual sports at the scholastic level. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Physical Therapy Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze "normal" motor performance. Prerequisite: PHYCS 110, 112; ANAT 330, 405.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Introduction to the prevention, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and rehabilitation of common athletic injuries. Essential information concerning the nutritional, psychological, and legal aspects of athletic health care is also presented. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Parallel: PEP 341.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries Laboratory
description: Application of a variety of commercial protective equipment and taping, padding, and wrapping techniques consistent with anatomical and biomechanical principles. Emphasizes the prevention of sport and exercise injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Prerequisite or parallel: PEP 340.

title: Sports Information
description: Designed primarily for sports information students. Develops students' knowledge and background in the terminology, strategy, scoring, and officiating of a variety of sports. Not open to physical education majors.

title: Teaching and Coaching Water Polo and Synchro
description: Introduces the rules, necessary equipment, skills, and drills to teach and coach water polo successfully. Also introduces basic body positions, swimming strokes, and stroke variations, sculls for propulsion and support and figures arra' hytirid tkures in shallow and a\er . Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel swimming skill test.

title: Teaching and Coaching Springboard Diving
description: Introduction to teaching progressions of dives from one and three meter springboards and basic platform diving. Developed for the novice teacher, coach, or performer. Includes forward and back dives, reverse and inward dives, and twist and somersault dives. Emphasizes fundamentals and flexibility of teaching method. The degree of difficulty increases progressively as ability increases. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Learning theories, teaching strategies, and physical laws that affect learning and performance in the water. Emphasizes analysis and technique.

title: American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor
description: Opportunity for students to earn the American National Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certificate.

title: Internship in Aquatics
description: Permits credit for aquatic experiences in categories of leadership, administration, or operation of aquatic programs or facilities. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the early grades of the elementary school.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and use of accompaniment in modern dance. Prerequisite: PEP 107, 115.

title: Lower Extremity Injury Evaluation in Athletic Training
description: Procedures and techniques for recognition and evaluation of athletic injuries to the lower extremities. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper methods and techniques in evaluating lower extremity pathologies. Technology Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or PEP 292, permission of the instructor. Prerequisite or parallel: PEP 340. Open only to athletic training majors admitted into the professional preparation program.

title: Upper Extremity Injury Evaluation in Athletic Training
description: Procedures and techniques for recognition and evaluation of athletic injuries that occur to the upper extremities. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper methods and techniques in evaluating upper extremity injuries. permission of the instructor. Prerequisite or parallel: PEP 340. Open only to athletic training majors admitted to the professional preparation program.

title: Therapeutic Exercise and Techniques in Athletic Training
description: Principles and goals of common rehabilitative procedures for athletic injuries. Learn the use of contemporary manual therapy and rehabilitative exercises in a comprehensive rehabilitative program. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper rehabilitative techniques of common injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, permission of the instructor. Open only to athletic training majors admitted into the professional preparation program.

title: Teaching and Coaching Golf
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball or Softball
description: Offered alternating years as baseball or softball. Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Motor Learning
description: Introduction to principles related to the teaching, learning, and performance of motor skills. Emphasis on the application of this knowledge to teaching and learning strategies for motorskill acquisition. Designed for undergraduate students who plan to teach motor skills to people in all age ranges.

title: Practicum 1 in Athletic Training
description: Student athletic trainers develop sports medicine knowledge and skills relevant to the allied medical and high school setting. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, permission of the instructor. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Neurophysiological Approach to Physical Education for Disabled People
description: Designed to give students an understanding of the theoretical basis of selected neurophysiological programs for treatment of various disabling conditions and to teach students how to administer such programs.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: PEP 291.

title: Methods/Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the planning, implementation, and evaluation of an array of teaching strategies that would be used in creating a safe environment for a public school physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence, preliminary admission to a teaching curriculum, and permission of the program director or designate. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Applied Anatomy in Athletic Training
description: Detailed review of applied human anatomy for Athletic Training majors. Emphasizes conceptual understanding of the interrelationahip of the anatomical structures as they relate to an injury episode. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Parallel: PEP 340, 341, 370. Open only to athletic training majors admitted to the professional preparation program.

title: Methods/Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed with both theory and practicum elements. Comprehensive planning instructional design, materials, strategies. Includes management, organization, evaluation, curriculum development. Laboratory experiences emphasized. Prerequisite: PEP 395, junior standing, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Curriculum Design in Physical Education
description: Introduction to curriculum and curriculum design covering all facets of physical education in the public school setting.

title: Seminar
description: Designed to permit sport administration majors to consider current issues and topics in sport. Prerequisite: permission of the coordinator of sport administration.

title: Instructor of Lifeguarding
description: Concerned with skills pertinent to teaching lifeguarding. All aspects of lifeguarding including techniques for pools and fresh and salt water beaches. Red Cross certification available upon completion. Prerequisite: PEP 216.

title: Psychological Dimensions of Coaching
description: Designed for students interested in coaching. Focuses on the dimensions of sport psychology by review and study of pertinent scientific literature, the principles derived from this literature, and their practical application.

title: Internship in Exercise Programs for the Older Adult
description: A practical experience in leading physical activities for older adults in healthcare centers, senior citizen centers, retirement centers, or other places where older adults engage in exercise. Prerequisite: PEP 212, 292, 293, 294, 299, 312; HSC 469. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Sports for Individuals with Disabilities
description: Provides a working knowledge of the official sports organizations recognized by the United States Olympic Committee. Emphasizes classifications, organizational structure, sporting events, coaching athletes with disabilities. Prerequisite: PEP 331 for coaching minors and endorsements.

title: Coaching Internship
description: Students assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teachingcoaching process. May not be taken at the same time as student teaching. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Athletic Governance
description: Directed mainly toward sportsinformation students. Designed to discuss the various organizations that govern amateur and professional sports in the United States. Emphasis is on the sportsinformation student's role in shaping sports in this country and in international competition. Not recommended for physical education majors and minors.

title: Swimming Pool Operation and Maintenance
description: Provides information on pool circulation, filtration, sanitation, and administrative procedure for the pool operator or aquatics specialist.

title: Aquatic Facilities Management and Programming
description: Study of organization and administration to prepare the aquatic professional for management of indoor and outdoor facilities. Includes facility design, safety procedures, activity, sport, and recreational aspects of pools, lakes, camps, and beach fronts. Prerequisite: PEP 454.

title: Teaching Modern Dance in the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEP 107, 115.

title: Mainstreaming and Inclusion in Physical Education
description: Designing physical education programs to meet the requirements of Public Law 101-476, IDEA, which requires that each child with disabilities have an individualized physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Practicum in Physical Education for Disabled People
description: Designed to give students practical experience in working with disabled children in a physical education setting. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the program coordinator.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching Modern Athletic Programs
description: Explores the historical development of modern athletics. Students develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program and learn to deal with everyday coaching and administration problems. Prerequisite: satisfactory completion of 22 hours of undergraduate sport administration courses; ENG 231; JOURN 261; BEOA 241; foundations of business minor (21 hours); and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Movement experiences appropriate for elementary school children; planning, teaching, and evaluating a developmental program.

title: Practicum 2 in Athletic Training
description: Student athletic trainers develop sports medicine knowledge and skills relevant to the sport and workenhancement physical therapy settings. Prerequisite: PEP 372, 373, permission of the instructor. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the anatomical structures and physiological functions in humans during acute and chronic activity. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294, or permission of the program director.

title: Teaching Individuals with Disabilities in Physical Education
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitation each causes. Physical education and recreational activities for each type. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training
description: Students receive athletic training clinical experience in an Indiana high school, sports medicine clinic, or other qualified facility. Students must work under the direct supervision of an NATA certified athletic trainer. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 372, and 396.

title: Current Concepts in Athletic Training
description: Designed to advance educational and clinical experiences. Advanced concepts in sports medicine, review of case studies, and application of applied research in athletic training will be presented. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 372.

title: Organization and Administration of Athletic Training
description: Advanced organization and administration of an Athletic Training Program. Emphasizes the objectives, principles, and problems in management of a comprehensive athletic training program. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Independent Study in Physical Education
description: An opportunity to investigate an area of particular interest to the student, under supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness and self awareness through yoga exercise, breathing and relaxation techniques.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to enhance muscular strength and endurance through weight training.

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic workouts performed to music.

title: Foundations of Exercise Science and Wellness
description: An introduction to such topics as career opportunities, exercise and nutrition, lifestyle changes, related professional organizations and publications, physiological and psychological research, and other current information for wellness and fitness professionals.

title: Introduction to Fitness Assessment
description: Evaluation of and introduction to practical and written skills in exercise science needed in the advanced program, i.e., exercise prescription, submaximal ergometer testing, etc. Prerequisite: EXCSI 190. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors and adapted physical education minors.

title: Foundations of Exercise Leadership and Prescription
description: Emphasizes fundamentals of leading group exercise activities effectively based on exercise prescription applications. Applicable teaching methodology in various activity and lecture situations will be developed. Individual portfolios will be developed and evaluated. Prerequisite: advanced program status and permission of the program director.

title: Exercise Leader Professional Experience
description: Fulltime paid work and learning offcampus practical experience in a health/fitness program, e.g., cardiac rehabilitation, wellness and health promotion, sports medicine, corporate fitness. YMCA, etc. Enhances professional preparation by offering opportunities to apply fundamental concepts and principles in an actual work setting. Prerequisite: permission of the program director. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Principles of the Electrocardiogram and Cardiac Assessments
description: Introduction to basic principles and interpretation of the electrocardiogram (EKG) as it relates to fitness programs involving apparently healthy people and cardiac rehabilitation patients. Includes cardiac assessments and emphasis on prescription medication use and intervention in various cardiac problems. Prerequisite: EXSCI 301. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Advanced Fitness Assessments in Exercise Science
description: Laboratory designed to present and refine skills in conducting various health fitness tests, e.g., resting and exercise blood pressure, body composition, submaximal aerobic capacity, maximal graded exercise tests, and blood cholesterol, as well as implications of test results. Prerequisite: EXSCI 401 and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Exercise Leader Internship
description: Fulltime offcampus practical experience in a health and fitness program, e.g., cardiac rehabilitation, wellness/health promotion, sports medicine, corporate fitness, YMCA, etc. Enhances professional preparation by offering opportunities to apply fundamental concepts and principles in an actual work setting. title: Design Communications Media 2
description: Methods for environmental design communications in a variety of media. Prerequisite: CAP 161.

description: A twoweek workshop in environmental design and planning including lectures, field trips, and handson studio experience. Open only to high school juniors enrolled in the Honors College Summer Program.

description: Independent study in urban design, planning, landscape architecture, and architecture, offered in conjunction with the college's Community-Based Projects Program. title: Special Projects in College of Architecture and Planning
description: Special projects in the College of Architecture and Planning undertaken by groups of students. Prerequisite: junior standing and permission of the project director. The Department of Architecture offers a fiveyear undergraduate bachelor of architecture degree, accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board. Approval to pursue the departmental major in architecture involves a selection process in addition to admission to the university. For more information write or call the Office of Admissions, (317) 285-8300. A student receiving two consecutive grades below C in any two sequential architecture courses must repeat both courses. The policy remains in effect for students repeating these courses. Acceptance into the first semester of the fourth year of the Bachelor of Architecture curriculum requires submission of an application for admission and a faculty review of general academic performance as well as work produced in design communication and design studios through the first semester of the third year. Acceptance requires minimum accumulative gradepoint averages of 2.0 for the university, 2.20 for architecture, and 2.25 for design. Acceptance into the fifthyear architectural curriculum for the professional program is contingent upon application for admission and a review of general performance and all work produced in design studios through the final semester of the fourth year. Transfer students with less than one year of design status in an architecture or architecturerelated degree program must apply to the College of Architecture and Planning for admission to the First Year Program. Transfer students with one year or more of design credit from other accredited professional degree programs in architecture who are seeking advanced placement should inquire directly at the Department of Architecture about the submission of portfolios as well as transcripts for evaluation. All transfer applicants must first be admitted to the university before the process of admission to the major can begin. Advanced placement in architecture requires review by the Department of Architecture of transfer application materials to determine the student's best starting point in the curriculum. Admission to the university does not automatically imply admission to the major in architecture, and no guarantee can be made or should be inferred, until the department's final decision on placement has been made, regarding the length of time or number of credits to complete the degree. description: Covers statistics, equilibrium, external loading and force systems, and properties of materials, with a focus on developing a basic understanding of structural concepts. Prerequisite: MATHS 125 or the equivalent. Open only to architecture majors.

description: Covers internal force determinations, modes of failure, and strength of structures as applied to beams, columns, and trusses. Prerequisite: ARCH 211.

description: Analysis and research in the recording of sites, significant architectural examples, and other artifacts of architectural significance. Prerequisite: CAP 102.

title: Historic American Buildings Survey 2
description: Analysis and research in the recording of sites, significant architectural examples, and other artifacts of architectural significance. Prerequisite: ARCH 226.

title: Design Communications Media 3
description: Exploration of a variety of communications media including pencil, ink, pastel, markers, watercolor, and photography. Prerequisite: CAP 162. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Design Communications Media 4
description: Continuation of ARCH 261. Prerequisite: ARCH 261.

description: Integration of all facets of design including design, research, programming, technolo gy, function, human behavior, scheduling, time management, communication, use of materials, and systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

description: Integration of all facets of design including design, research, programming, technology, function, human behavior, scheduling, time management, communication, use of materials, and systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 301 and admission by a faculty design review panel.

description: Structural design in steel and wood. Application of structural analysis to proportioning building materials for use in beams, columns, trusses, and simple frames. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 212.

title: Design of Structural Systems 2
description: Structural designcontinuation of ARCH

description: Methods and materials of architectural construction. Emphasizes interface of material selections and construction technology in the design/production/ construction process. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

title: Architectural Building Technology 2
description: Methods and materials of architectural construction. Emphasizes interface of material selections and construction technology in the design/production/ construction process. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 315.

title: Historic American Buildings Survey 3
description: Analysis and research in the recording of sites, significant architectural examples, and other artifacts of architectural and engineering significance. Prerequisite: ARCH 227

title: Historic American Buildings Survey 4
description: Analysis and research in the recording of sites, significant architectural examples, and other artifacts of architectural and engineering significance. Prerequisite: ARCH 326.

description: Survey of the movements and major figures in architecture and design from the late nineteenth century to the present, with consideration given to the social and cultural context of design ideas. Prerequisite: ARCH 224.

description: Preparation for the internship experience; supplements the experience gained during the internship and serves as the basis for evaluation of student growth. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

title: Design Communications Media 5
description: Continuation of ARCH 262 with an emphasis on portfolio preparation. Prerequisite: ARCH 262.

description: A sixmonth period of approved paid professional employment under the supervision of a licensed architect, as required for the bachelor of architecture degree. Simultaneous enrollment in the National Intern-Architect Development Program (IDP) is required. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of heating, ventilating, airconditioning, plumbing, and fire protection systems. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 202. Architecture 109

title: Environmental Systems 2
description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of electrical, luminous, and acoustical systems. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 371.

title: Architecture for Non -Architects
description: Honors colloquium in architecture designed to introduce nonmajors to the architectural design process, the determinants of building form, an understanding of the built environment, current trends in architecture, and architectural history and architects. Not open to students majoring in architecture.

title: Architectural Design
description: Organization and design of multipurpose architectural and related environments at all scales in response to a complex set of criteria. Investigation of architectural and urban design principles, theories, and philosophies. Prerequisite: ARCH 302, 350. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Architectural Design
description: Organization and design of multipurpose architectural and related environments at all scales in response to a complex set of criteria. Investigation of architectural and urban design principles, theories, and philosophies. Prerequisite: ARCH 401 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Architectural Design
description: Design of multiuse projects on multiplebuilding sites with emphasis on research, programming, and systems integration through detail design development. Additional emphasis on circulation and movement systems. Exploration of presentation media. Prerequisite: ARCH 402, 451. Parallel: ARCH 452. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Architectural Thesis
description: Development of a thesis idea plus an architectural project to test or verify the thesis design position. Includes design, comprehensive site, and building prototype analysis. Emphasizes project management and design development including all major technical systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 403, 452.

title: Integration of Architectural Technologies
description: Indepth development of a building project, from conceptual design through the execution of construction documents. Integration of structural, material, and environmental systems and methodologies. Project management is stressed during all phases. Prerequisite: ARCH 312, 316, 372. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 210.

title: Topics in the History of Oriental Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from the Islamic world to the Far East. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Philosophy of Architecture
description: Seminars and independent study in the background and development of prevailing philosophies of architecture, ideas in design, and how they evolved in contemporary architecture since the beginning of the twentieth century, concluding with their influence on the current practice of architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: History of North American Architecture
description: Survey of North American architecture and urbanism from its colonial beginnings to the present. Emphasis on European antecedents, transformation by American conditions, and the rise of a distinctly American architecture. Methods of dissemination of architectural knowledge and conflicting points of view. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: History of Architecture, Planning, and Engineering in the Midwest
description: Analysis of the development of architecture, planning, engineering(canals, railroads, roads, bridges), and industrial architecture in the Midwest from the frontierperiod through the twentieth century. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Historic Architectural Interiors
description: Survey of European and American interiors, interior architecture, furnishings, and decorative arts, highlighting cultural influences from antiquity to the present with emphasis on eighteenthto twentiethcentury examples. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of Ancient Greek and Roman Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from classical antiquity. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of Western Medieval Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from the Byzantine through the Romanesque and Gothic periods. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of Renaissance and Baroque Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from Europe between 1400 and the late 1700s. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the Ancient Traditions of Architecture
description: Analysis of cultural and anthropological concepts, and of representative examples of prehistoric and protohistoric architecture, from the Neolithic Revolution to the rise of the first literate civilizations, while tracing the survival of those traditions into more recent global vernaculars. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of 19thand 20th-Century Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from around 1800 to the present. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Philosophy, History, and Theory of Historic Preservation
description: Survey of the philosophy, history, theory, and scope of historic preservation in Europe and America. Explores such principles of historic preservation as ethical questions, practice versus theory, standards, and performance criteria. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Preservation Planning, Law, and Economics
description: Planning, law, and economics for preservation, restoration, conservation, rehabilitation, and revitalization. Emphasis is on strategies for preservation and implementation, and the development process at various scales: neighborhood, district, community, and state. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Documentation of Historic Sites and Buildings
description: Methods of recording historic sites and buildings using both written and graphic means. Assembling and preserving data on the physical condition and history of historic properties. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 226, 227, 326, and 327.

title: Field Workshop in Preservation
description: Exercises in surveying and the use of state inventory forms, National Register material, and environmental impact studies. Includes field trips. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Historic Preservation, Restoration, and Adaptive Use Cost Benefits
description: Analysis of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure; suggested restoration and cost benefits and restoration costs. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Historic Preservation Technology 1: Construction and Pathology
description: Analysis of materials and systems of construction used in historic buildings. Identification and diagnosis of causes of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure. Some laboratory sessions are integrated into the program. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: admission to the historic preservation minor and permission of the program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Historic Preservation Technology 2: Conservation Methods
description: General conservation methods for historic buildings including an introduction to specific techniques and philosophies. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: ARCH 447 and permission of the program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Architectural Design Internship
description: Preparation for the internship experience; supplements the experience gained during the internship and serves as the basis for evaluation of student growth. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Architectural Research
description: Experience in architectural inquiry: the contexts, definitions, and processes of design creativity; relationships to scientific and environmental design and behavior research; technologyrelated research; strategies in building and testing concepts, assumptions, hypotheses, empirical evaluation; methods and procedures. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Programming and Thesis Preparation
description: Problems, theories, and methods leading to the development of individual and group requirements and their translation into conventional and nonconventional performance criteria. Programming of a thesis project. Prerequisite: ARCH 402.

title: Professional Practice and Management
description: Problems, processes, and philosophies of architectural practice. Emphasis is on applied organizational and management theories, processes, tools. Prerequisite: ARCH 369.

title: Architectural Aspects of Archaeological Field Work
description: Archaeological methods applied to architectural remains. Principles of stratigraphic excavation, dating methods and techniques for surveying and recording; technical and comparative analysis of building elements for dating, interpreting, and reconstructing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Life Safety in Architecture and Environmental Design
description: Survey of topics Landscape Architecture 111 relevant to life safety encompassing wind, fire, ground motions, environmental factors including noise, criminal activity, and home accidents; and matters pertaining to the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA). Prerequisite: senior standing.

title: Advanced Graphic Techniques
description: Advanced graphic explorations of architectural subject matter, stressing fullcolor rendering. Includes demonstration of paint mixing, shades and shadows, reflections and material indication with application of these techniques to individual studio projects. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Computer Graphics Applications in Architecture
description: Basic training in the operation of a stateoftheart interactive computer graphics system. Introduction to twoand threedimensional graphics techniques and their applications in professional practice. Includes handson practice and exploration of the special capabilities of the interactive graphics system. Prerequisite: senior standing, permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Independent Projects
description: Independent study in environmental topics. Prerequisite: approval of a program proposal by the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 in any one semester or term. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Psychological Aspects of Environmental Design
description: Review of attempts to discover rational methods of predicting and evaluating environmental design. Presents basic research and analysis methods from the designer's point of view. Lecture, studio, and field activities. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson for students with majors other than architecture or landscape architecture. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Projects in Architecture
description: Timely architectural projects undertaken by groups of students. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to architecture majors. Young Landscape architecture involves applying natural and aesthetic principles to the planning, design, preservation, and management of the land. Ball State University's programs in landscape architecture are fully accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board of the American Society of Landscape Architects. title: Introduction to Landscape Architecture
description: An introduction to landscape architecture: lectures, site observations, and environmental experiences that focus on landscape architectural practice, representative projects, philosophy, and areas of specialization within the field.

title: People and the Environment
description: Lectures and seminars from disciplines on and off campus relating to influences of people on the environment and the environment on people as they relate to architecture and landscape architecture. Open to all students.

title: Site Design
description: Application of basic design principles, programming, and analysis to smallscale sitespecific landscape design problems. Visual and functional design principles as they relate to natural and cultural influences in landscape design. Prerequisite: CAP 102. Parallel: LA 214.

title: Park and Open Space Design
description: Design projects emphasizing park design, park and recreational master planning, and openspace design in rural, suburban, or urban settings. Prerequisite: LA 201.

title: Field Studies
description: Onsite studies of landscape architectural projects and practices, natural areas, and historic sites and landscapes. Urban or rural field trips; may include visits to professional offices and public planning and design agencies. One threetofiveday field trip is required. This course is offered for credit/no credit only. Parallel: LA 201.

title: Field Studies 2
description: Group field studies of landscape architectural projects and practices, natural areas, and historic sites and landscapes. Urban and rural field trips may include visits to professional offices and public planning and design agencies. A minimum of one threetofiveday field trip is required. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Landscape Architecture History 1
description: The history of landscape architecture from ancient times to 1800. Examples of landscape expressions of the humanenvironment relationship resulting in the conscious shaping of urban and rural landscapes, and the creation of such landscapes as parks, gardens, and urban plazas.

title: Landscape Architecture History 2
description: The history of landscape architecture from 1800 to the present. Emphasis is on the North American humanenvironment relationship, its relationship to European antecedents, and other cultural parallels in landscape design. Prerequisite: LA 220.

title: Landscape Architectural Design Communications
description: Methods of landscape architectural design communications; integrates techniques of handdrawn and computer graphics, photography, and video. Prerequisite: CAP 162.

title: Environmental Systems
description: Qualitative investigations and analysis of landscape systems. Studies include the assessment of vegetation, climate, hydrology, soils, and subsurface geology as determinants of landscape architectural form; natural processes as they relate to the principles of landscape architectural construction.

title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
description: An introduction to the use of microcomputers in landscape architecture. Emphasis is on twoand threedimensional computeraided design and drawing, landscape data inventory and analysis, and landscape engineering. Prerequisite: CAP 162. Parallel: LA 202.

title: Housing and Community Design
description: Design projects focusing on social, political, economic, cultural, and environmental issues as they relate to landplanning and site design for housing developments and residential communities. Prerequisite: LA 202.

title: Planting Design
description: Design problems focusing on the functional, ecological, and aesthetic uses of plants in the landscape. Prerequisite: LA 301, 341; and BIO 112 or 216. Landscape Architecture 113

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 1
description: Principles and practices of landscape engineering. Emphasis is on the techniques and applications of land surveying, earthwork techniques including grading and estimation, and principles of site drainage. Prerequisite: LA 270.

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 2
description: Principles and practices of landscape architecture engineering and construction with emphasis on landscape materials, structures, planting, and fabrication techniques. Includes design implementation techniques and construction documents. Prerequisite: LA 311.

title: Landscape Plants 1
description: The study of woody landscape plants, including plant identification and plant adaptation to urban and natural environmental conditions.

title: Landscape Plants 2
description: The study of herbaceous landscape plants including plant identification and landscape cultural requirements. Emphasis is on both outdoor and indoor plants.

title: Landscape Architecture Internship
description: A minimum of one semester of supervised, unpaid employment under the direction of a registered landscape architect. Departmental approval required in advance of qualified employment. Requires employer and selfevaluation reports. This course is offered for credit/no credit only. Prerequisite: LA 302. Not open to students who have credit in LA 369.

title: Landscape Architecture Internship
description: A minimum of ten weeks of supervised, paid employment under the direction of a registered landscape architect or allied design professional. Departmental approval required in advance of qualified employment. Requires employer and selfevaluation reports. Offered for credit/nocredit only. Not open to students who have credit in LA 368.

title: Regional Landscape Design
description: The application of principles of landscape architectural design to largescale landscape settings. Topics include land planning, visual quality management, and natural and cultural landscape resource management. Prerequisite: LA 302.

title: Urban Design
description: Design studio emphasizing the physical and sociobehavioral influences on the design of cities. Projects may focus on the design of new urban environments or the redesign and revitalization of existing urban centers. May include interdisciplinary studies. Prerequisite: LA 401 or permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Architecture Comprehensive Project
description: Analytical, conceptual, and design development processes applied to a comprehensive project in landscape architecture. Emphasis on guided independent design work based on individual initiative. Prerequisite: LA 403 and 451.

title: Special Design Studio
description: Design studio emphasizing special or unique topics in landscape architecture. Studio may be offered at oncampus or offcampus sites, may be part of an approved foreign study program. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Landscape Architectural Engineering 3
description: Principles and practices of landscape engineering and construction. Emphasis on roadway and parking lot engineering, practices of storm water management, and advanced grading. Prerequisite: LA 312.

title: Historic Landscape Preservation
description: Survey of the history, theory, and methodologies of historic landscape preservation. Includes topics in both vernacular and designed historic landscape preservation, primarily in North America. Prerequisite: LA 221 or permission of the instructor.

title: Philosophy of Landscape Architecture
description: Readings, seminars, and lectures in the background and development of historic and contemporary philosophies of landscape architecture. Includes discussions of design and environmental issues, land use, and professional ethics. Prerequisite: LA 221 or permission of the instructor.

title: Park and Recreation Planning and Design
description: Lectures, case studies, and readings related to the interdisciplinary role of the landscape architect in park and recreation planning, design, administration, and maintenance. Prerequisite: LA 202 or permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Operations
description: Techniques and practices of landscape grounds development and maintenance. Topics may include plant growth, development, and evaluation; plant and turf installation; pruning, irrigation, and landscape management plans. Prerequisite: LA 341 or permission of the instructor.

title: Interior Landscape Design
description: Techniques and practices of interior planting design, development, and maintenance. Topics may include environmental conditions affecting plant growth, principles of interior planting design, and interior plant management. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Landscape Architecture Research
description: Methods, procedures, and case studies of landscape architectural research. Includes guided development of an individual research program and proposal leading to the landscape architecture comprehensive project (LA 404). Prerequisite: LA 403.

title: Professional Practice
description: Methods and practices of the profession of landscape architecture. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics. Prerequisite: LA 302 and 368 or 369.

title: Landscape Architectural Design Communications 2
description: Advanced methods of landscape architectural design communications using a variety of media. Prerequisite: CAP 162.

title: Portfolio Preparation
description: The preparation of resumes, portfolios, and brochures related to securing internship positions and other landscape architectural employment.

title: Environmental Impact Analysis
description: Review of the environmental design arts and their implications relative to proposed actions that affect the environment. Covers procedures and methodologies used in impact analysis and documentation. Prerequisite: LA 302 or permission of the instructor.

title: Computer-Aided Landscape Design
description: Twoand threedimensional computeraided design techniques with emphasis on site design, master planning, and regional landscape design. Incorporates microcomputer or mainframebased CAD systems. Prerequisite: LA 280 or permission of the instructor.

title: Independent Projects
description: An independent study in environmental topics. Prerequisite: approval of the program proposal by a faculty advisor, the professor responsible for study assessment, and the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Projects in Landscape Architecture
description: Special and timely landscape architectural projects undertaken by groups of students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. title: Introduction to Urban Planning and Development
description: An introduction to urban planning and development. Open to all students.

title: Community Analysis and Design Studio
description: Analysis and design principles on an urban and metropolitan scale, including location criteria for land use and analysis of environmental suitability for development. Introduces computerassisted models for landsuitability analysis. Prerequisite: CAP firstyear core program.

title: Project Analysis and Design Studio
description: Site analysis and design principles for smallscale urban projects, including building complexes, subdivisions, and neighborhood development. Students present and defend designs for specific site locations. Prerequisite: PLAN 201.

title: History and Theory of Planning 1
description: Growth and evolution of cities. Evolution theories and practice of urban planning, with emphasis on the United States before 1940.

title: History and Theory of Planning 2
description: Evolution of theories and practice of urban planning, with emphasis on the United States since 1940. Interaction of public and private initiatives directed toward urban and environmental problems.

title: Planning and Private Development
description: The process of privatesector land development, including market analysis and site selection, physical design, financing, legal constraints, and assembly of the development package.

title: Communication and Presentation Techniques
description: Development of graphic and visualization skills for planners. Use of a variety of communication techniques and media for public presentation. Open only to planning majors and minors.

title: Information Management for Economic Development Planning
description: Information management and tools and strategies for community economic development, including use of census and other published data sources, generation of community data, community assessment, recommendations, and presentation of findings. Prerequisite: PLAN 202

title: Information Management for Urban and Neighborhood Planning
description: Information management for urbanand neighborhoodscale planning, including design and implementation of data surveys, use and interpretation of census and other published data sources, and analysis and presentation of findings. Use of computers for data storage and manipulation. Prerequisite: PLAN 301.

title: Urban Land- Use Planning
description: Principles of urban landuse planning for newly developing areas and for changing older communities. Attention to environmental, efficiency, and aesthetic concerns in urban growth. Preparation of the comprehensive urban landuse plan.

title: Theory of Urban Spatial Planning
description: Seminar in theories of location and development of principal urban activities including transportation, housing, industry, commercial centers, and public facilities. Implications for urbanplanning policies.

title: Computer Applications in Planning
description: Microcomputer applications using spreadsheets, databases, and modeling and mapping packages suitable for planning and development office use. Brief overview of Intergraph graphic and mapping applications.

title: Economic Development Planning
description: Strategies and tools for stimulation of local economic growth including government incentives, financing alternatives, and examples of publicprivate partnership in strategic planning.

title: Planning Paid Internship
description: Supervised paid work experience for at least 450 hours in public agency, private firm, or other urban planning and development setting. May not be taken before completing the third year of the program. Normally finished before the fifth year of the program. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Field Studio
description: Analysis and application of planning skills in a realworld setting, involving an actual community or outside client. Emphasis on smaller town or rural planning issues. Prerequisite: PLAN 302.

title: Field Studio
description: Analysis and application of planning skills in a realworld setting, involving an actual community or outside client. Emphasis on urban planning issues. Prerequisite: PLAN 302.

title: Theory of Urban Design
description: Urban design with emphasis on its vocabulary and scope, especially space, form, scale, time, and function. Aspects of physical planning in relation to social, economic, and political forces, as well as the role of the urban designer in the planning process.

title: Planning Research Studio
description: Research techniques for developing and testing planning proposals. Design and submission of a formal research proposal, typically the basis for the student's thesis project. Prerequisite: PLAN 402.

title: Planning Thesis
description: Development of an individual project or urban development design, with emphasis on the evaluation of alternative solutions and presentation of final report. Prerequisite: PLAN 405.

title: Planning Internship
description: Supervised unpaid work experience for at least 450 hours in a public agency, private firm, or other urban planning and development setting. May not be taken before completing the third year of the program. Normally finished before the fifthyear of the program. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems for Urban Planning
description: Designed to introduce principles of GIS and GIS applications in an urban environment. Topics include GIS components, modeling methodology, and management of environments. Implications for urban and environmental policy development.

title: Advanced Concepts in Geographic Information Systems for Urban Planning
description: Advanced topics in modeling and analysis of urban and regional environments. Techniques for database organization, database development, and analytical processes (algorithm development). Prerequisite: PLAN 412.

title: Theory of Comprehensive Planning
description: Seminar in issues of comprehensive planning, including the planning process, public participation in planning, and the role of political, social, and economic conditions in planning decisions.

title: Urban Impact Analysis
description: Techniques for estimating the environmental, Urban Planning 117 socioeconomic, fiscal, and energy effects of proposed plans and development projects.

title: Housing and Community Development
description: Analysis of public programs and market conditions affecting housing and community development. Housing supply and demand, finance, the role of government subsidies.

title: Urban Transportation Planning
description: Transportation planning methods and policy, including analysis of travel demand, links between land use and transportation, choice of transportation modes, and design of balanced transportation systems.

title: Environmental Planning
description: Introduction to the fundamental issues and technologies associated with planning for sensitive use of environmental resources. Topics include waste management, air and water quality planning, ecological systems, and methods of environmental analysis and implementation.

title: Energy Planning
description: Energy resource issues in urban planning. Strategies for incorporating energy efficiency in housing, land use, transportation, social services, and community development. Analysis of energy policy, with emphasis on innovative public and private sector initiatives at the community level.

title: Community Facilities Planning
description: Design principles and economic conditions in planning for urban physical facilities, including recreation facilities, streets, sidewalks, drainage, water supply systems, sewerage, waste treatment, and others.

title: Philosophy, History, and Theory of Historic Preservation
description: Survey of the philosophy, history, and theory of historic preservation, primarily in Europe and North America. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 440; LA 440.

title: Preservation Techniques and Policies
description: Planning and programming for preservation, restoration, and neighborhood conservation, economic and legal consideration in federal, state, and private programs in preservation and restoration. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 441.

title: Documentation of Historic Sites and Buildings
description: Methods of documenting historic sites and buildings using various survey and inventory forms. Extensive oral and written descriptive analysis of historic buildings. Not open to students who have credit in LA 442.

title: Field Workshop in Preservation
description: Exercises in surveying and the use of state inventory forms, National Register material, and environmental impact studies; field trips. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 443.

title: Neighborhood Planning
description: Planning strategies for revitalization of older residential neighborhoods and neighborhood commercial areas. Includes community organization and the role of public and private neighborhood organizations.

title: Issues of Planning Practice
description: Capstone seminar to explore application of theory to planning practice and management. Issues of planning ethics, citizen participation, styles and strategies for effective implementation of planning. Prerequisite: PLAN 369 or 410, 401 or 402.

title: Urban Planning Law
description: Legal tools for plan implementation, including zoning, subdivision regulations, planned unitdevelopment regulations, and other techniques for guiding urban development while balancing community interests and private property rights.

title: Center City Revitalization
description: Strategies for revitalization of core urban areas, including case studies of successful cities. Examples include employmentbased, recreation and conventionbased, and residentially based revitalization.

title: Alternative and Sustainable Community Planning
description: Seminar course examining nontraditional approaches to community planning and design. Focuses on concepts associated with the design of sustainable communities. Historical precedent, case study, and utopian alternatives are synthesized to project alternative futures for present community planning and design issues.

title: Independent Study in Planning
description: Independent study in urban planning and development topics, undertaken on an individual basis with guidance of a faculty member. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Projects in Urban Planning and Development
description: Special projects in urban planning and development undertaken by groups of students under faculty direction. N. Palomba, Dean, J. Fitzgerald, Associate Dean All undergraduate programs in the College of Business are accredited by the American Assembly of Collegiate Schools of Business. The Department of Accounting has earned separate AACSB Accreditation. Requirements for Admission Students interested in pursuing majors in the College of Business will be classified as prebusiness students until they have • Attained junior standing (63 hours) with a minimum gradepoint average of 2.0 • Completed the following courses with a gradepoint average of at least 2.25: ACC 201, 202; BEOA 210; ECON 201, 202, 221; ENG 103, 104; MATHS 132. Students may register for 300- and 400-level business courses only if they have completed the admission courses or if they are currently enrolled in one final course necessary to complete the courses required for admission and if they have met the gradepoint requirement at the time of enrollment. A College of Business major is composed of the business core requirement and major specific requirements. Degree Requirements A bachelor's degree in business is awarded to students who conform to the following university and College of Business requirements: • Have completed a minimum of 126 credit hours. • Have completed all university general studies requirements. • Have completed the specific requirements of the major. • Have completed at least 50 percent of courses (63 hours) from outside the College of Business (for this purpose Economics is considered outside the College of Business). • Have taken 30 of the last 40 hours at Ball State University. In addition to this university requirement, students majoring in a program in the College of Business must earn the last 30 credits of their major in residence. • Be in good academic standing with a minimum gradepoint average of 2.0. Transfer of Credit Transfers from Other Colleges and Universities Acceptance of credit from other institutions will be determined by the Office of Admissions. The applicability of credit toward degree requirements in the College of Business will be determined by the college. Courses in upper division business subjects (300/400-level) may be accepted for specific equivalency if the course work has been taken in the junior or senior year at a fouryear institution that is accredited by the AACSB. If the institution is not so accredited, credit in upper division courses accepted for transfer will be applicable only if prerequisites are similar to those of courses at Ball State University. This decision will be made by each department. A transfer student who is enrolling at Ball State University to complete a second undergraduate degree will be required to finish 30 hours in the major at Ball State University, usually amounting to all upper division classes in the second major and the business policy class (MGT 491). These 30 hours are in addition to any general requirements that may be outstanding. Business courses taken at twoyear institutions will not be applied to upper division requirements. Credit by Self-Acquired Competency The College of Business does not award credit in business courses on the basis of selfacquired competency. However, the college will give examinations for credit in specific courses. Consult the appropriate department chairperson for information. The college will not accept the transfer of credit for business courses from other institutions if the credit was awarded on the basis of selfacquired competency. Statute of Limitation If seven or more years have elapsed since last enrollment the student will be required to meet the degree requirements as stated in the current catalog. Business Courses 300/400 Level: Enrollment in business courses numbered 300-499 is limited to • Admitted College of Business students; • Nonbusiness students who are pursuing minors in the College of Business (Economics, Foundations of Business, Office Technology, and Marketing); • Nonbusiness students who are pursuing majors that require specific business courses; and • Nonbusiness students who have met all course prerequisites. Prerequisites are vigorously monitored. Students who enroll in classes for which they do not have the prerequisite will be dropped from the class. In addition to the associate and baccalaureate degree programs, the college offers a 3/2 program that allows students to earn both bachelor's degrees in sciences or humanities and master's of business administration (M.B.A.) degrees in five years. This special program is designed to give students an opportunity to combine their undergraduate studies in the sciences and humanities with graduate study in the College of Business. The following departments participate in the 3/2 program: anthropology, biology, chemistry, computer science, economics, English, modern languages and classics, geography, history, journalism, philosophy, political science, psychological science, sociology, social work, and speech communication. Consult the director of undergraduate programs in the College of Business for 3/2 program information.
