title: Conceptual Physics
description: Includes a survey of physics with conceptual emphasis on basic classical and modern concepts of matter, motion, energy, and forces with application to mechanics, heat, sound, electricity and magnetism, light, atomic, nuclear, and elementary particles.

title: Physical Science Concepts for Teachers
description: Principles and concepts of the laws of nature involving mechanical, heat, light, electrical, nuclear, and chemical energy and the conservation laws associated with these forms of energy. Emphasis is on applications appropriate to the classroom. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Preparation of Physical Science Teaching Materials
description: Selected topics in physical science stressing the construction of models and experimentation appropriate to the classroom. Designed primarily for students in elementary education programs. Prerequisite: PHYCS 101 or permission of the department chairperson. Open only to students in the teachereducation curriculum.

title: Basic Physics for the Allied Health Sciences
description: A condensed study of basic physics with special emphasis on principles and applications pertinent to the health sciences. Three lectures and one twohour laboratoryrecitation weekly. Prerequisite: one year of high school algebra and one year of high school geometry or permission of the department chairperson. Open only to students in the allied health sciences program in respiratory therapy, radiologic technology, nuclear therapy, and ultrasound technology or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: General Physics 1
description: Studies the laws of Newtonian mechanics. Introductory fluid statics and dynamics, heat and thermodynamics, and wave motion and sound. Prerequisite: MATHS 108 (algebra). Recommended prerequisite: MATHS 112 (trigonometry).

title: General Physics 2
description: Static and current electricity, magnetism, light and optics, and an introduction to modern physics including relativity and elements of atomic and nuclear physics. Prerequisite: PHYCS 110 or 130.

title: General Physics 1
description: First course in calculusbased physics for students in preengineering, the physical sciences, or mathematics. Topics include Newtonian mechanics, work and energy, motion, impulse and momentum, elasticity and wave motion, sound, and hydrostatics and hydrodynamics. Prerequisite or parallel: MATHS 161 or 171.

title: General Physics 2
description: Continuation of

title: Physics for Architects
description: Emphasizes the applications of mechanics and heat. Topics include particle dynamics, resolution of forces, friction, work, energy, static equilibrium, torque, properties of materials, fluids, temperature, thermal expansion, heat energy, heat transfer, phase changes in matter, and thermodynamic engines. Prerequisite: MATHS 112 or an equivalent course in secondary school mathematics. Not open to students who have credit in PHYCS 110 or 120.

title: Sound and Light
description: For music and art students. Sound as a basis of music and light as a basis of art. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Topics in Physics
description: Discussion of specific topics in physics, such as lasers, holography, and solidstate electronics. Designed for students not majoring in physics, the course requires no math or science background. Students may consult their curricular advisors or the Department of Physics and Astronomy for the specific topics being studied during a given semester. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Solar Energy Technology and Applications
description: Descriptive study of various techniques and systems using sunlight as a nonpolluting alternative energy source. Principles and design of solar systems for space heating, air conditioning, and heating water for residential and commercial buildings, and systems for the generation of electric power. Includes other related topics. Prerequisite: PHYCS 100 or MATHS 108.

title: Introduction to Modem Physics
description: The underlying principles and theories of modern physics. Topics include introductory relativity, atomic and nuclear structure, quantum theory, and the theory of solids. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122.

title: Modem Physics Laboratory
description: Classic experiments such as the Cavendish measurement of G, determination of Planck's Constant, Rutherford Scattering, Millikan Oil Drop Experiment, Franck- Hertz Experiment, and the Hall Effect will be performed. Use of computer software for report generation will be stressed. Prerequisite: PHYCS 260.

title: Mechanics
description: Basic concepts of particle mechanics. Simple and damped harmonic motion. Particle dynamics in noninertial frames of reference, central forces. Dynamics of a system of particles. Dynamics of a rigid body and the moment of inertia tensor. The wave equation, elasticity, and rigid body vibrations. Prerequisite: PHYCS 120; MATHS 162. Prerequisite recommended: MATHS 273.

title: Physical Optics
description: The electromagnetic wave theory of light, spectra, interference, diffraction, polarization, and double refraction. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122.

title: Acoustics
description: Elements of pure and applied acoustics. Topics include solutions to the wave equation, acoustic impedances, electromechanicalacoustic analogies, directradiator loudspeaker and enclosure theory, and a discussion of room acoustics. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122.

title: Electronics 1
description: Introductory DC and AC circuit theory, semiconductor components, power supplies, transistor amplification; integrated circuit operational amplifiers, active filters, oscillators, and function generators. Basic combinational logic circuits and Boolean algebra. Emphasizes applications of integrated circuits. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Electronics 2
description: Sequential logic circuits including scalars, displays, memories, shift registers, analogtodigital and digitaltoanalog conversion techniques. Microprocessor architecture and support electronics for microcomputer design. IC chips and circuits for experimenttomicrocomputer interfacing. Use of a microprocessor development system. Prerequisite: PHYCS 354 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introductory Nuclear Techniques
description: Emphasis is on experimental studies of radioactive disintegrations and decay products and their relation to nuclear structure. Instrumentation in radioisotope measurements. Two lectures and two twohour laboratory periods a week. Prerequisite: PHYCS 260.

title: Professional Experience
description: Paid work and learning experience in applied or theoretical physics or astronomy in an institutional, industrial, or university research or development setting. May occur during one or more semesters. Prerequisite: approval of proposed program by the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introductory Mathematical Physics 1
description: Application of mathematical techniques to the formulation and solution of physical problems, particularly those that occur in classical mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetic theory, and quantum mechanics. Topics include vector methods, generalized coordinates, and methods of applications of differential equations in physics. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122 and 260 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introductory Mathematical Physics 2
description: Application of mathematical techniques to the formulation and solution of physical problems. Topics include boundary value problems. Transforms, special functions of mathematical physics, and applications of tensor analysis in physics. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122, 260, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Descriptive Astronomy
description: The celestial sphere, the solar system, formation and decay of stars, instruments and basic laws of astronomy, nebulae, galactic structure, theories of the origin of the universe; constellation and telescope work.

title: Honors Colloquium in Physics
description: Exploration of selected topics in physics, with emphasis on individual projects, study, and discussion. Open only to honors students or with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: The Teaching of Physics in the Secondary School
description: Aims, nature of the subject matter, calculus concepts, and applications in the teaching of physics, amount and nature of laboratory work, standardized tests, and textbooks used in the teaching of physics. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: 16 hours of credit in physics or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Thermodynamics
description: Laws of thermodynamics and introduction to the kinetic theory of gases. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: PHYCS 330 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Celestial Mechanics
description: An application of the laws of classical mechanics to objects under the influence of inversesquare gravitational forces, leading to the theory of orbits and perturbative effects on orbits. Prerequisite: PHYCS 330.

title: Electromagnetic Theory 1
description: Application of vector analysis to electrostatics, dipole and multipole fields, and dielectric theory. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122; MATHS 273.

title: Electromagnetic Theory 2
description: Continuation of PHYCS 450 with emphasis on dynamic electrical problems, alternating currents, magnetic fields, and Maxwell's equations. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: PHYCS 450.

title: Elementary Particles
description: The nature and behavior of elementary particles through the study of the symmetries and dynamics responsible for their production, reactions, and decays. Prerequisite: PHYCS 465.

title: Nuclear Physics
description: Nucleus and nuclear interactions. Emphasizes experimental facts about nuclear processes in discussions of particle accelerators, detectors, radioactivity (alpha, beta, and gamma decay), interaction of radiation with matter, nuclear reactions, nuclear structure, nuclear models, and nuclear applications in science and technology. Prerequisite: PHYCS 260.

title: Quantum Mechanics 1
description: De Broglie's postulate, the uncertainty principle, the Schroedinger equation, the free particle, square well potentials, harmonic oscillator, the hydrogen atom, and other selected wave mechanics problems. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: PHYCS 260.

title: Quantum Mechanics 2
description: A continuation of PHYCS 464. Course material includes perturbation theory, oneelectron atoms, magnetic moments, spin, relativistic effects, symmetric and antisymmetric eigenfunctions, the helium atom, the Thomas-Fermi theory, the Hartree theory, and transition rates. Prerequisite: PHYCS 464.

title: Solid State Physics 1
description: An investigation of the structure and physical properties of matter in the solid state. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Prerequisite: PHYCS 260.

title: Solid State Physics 2
description: A continuation of PHYCS 466. Topics include the electrical and magnetic properties of solids and the band theory of solids with special emphasis on semiconductors. Examines the optical properties of solids and the effects of lattice defects. Prerequisite: PHYCS 466.

title: Practical Experience
description: Unpaid work and learning experience in applied or theoretical physics or astronomy in an institutional, industrial, or university research or development setting. May occur during one or more semesters. Prerequisite: approval of a proposed program by the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Studies in Physics
description: Pursuit of special lines of scientific investigation in physics on an individual basis. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques and skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Radiation Physics and Protection
description: Overview of radiation physics including properties of radiation, biological effects, xray production and interaction, and radiation protection. Prerequisite: MATHS 108; PHYCS 100 or 106.

title: Introduction to Radioactivity
description: Mechanisms and characteristics of nuclear decay and interaction of radiation with matter. Prerequisite: admission to a general arts associate degree program with electives in nuclear medicine.

title: Radiopharmaceuticals
description: Preparation, quality control, and the diagnostic and therapeutic application of radiopharmaceuticals in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: APHYS 247.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation
description: Indepth study of the components and performance characteristics of equipment commonly used in the nuclear medicine clinic. Parallel: APHYS 252.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation Lab
description: A weekly laboratory for nuclear medicine technology students enrolled in APHYS 251.

title: Lasers and Applied Electro-Optic Techniques
description: Principles of laser operation, design, and safety considered within the context of the field of electrooptic techniques. Optical detection devices, photographic techniques, and laser applications stressed in the handson laboratoryoriented portion of the course. Prerequisite: PHYCS 112 or 122 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Fluid Mechanics
description: The forces and motions in fluids. Fluid characteristics and the basic theories of fluid statics and dynamics. Applications of solar energy systems, hydraulics, aerodynamics, meteorology, hydrology, and fluidics, environmental conditioning systems, and other subjects. Prerequisite: MATHS 162; PHYCS 330.

title: Applied Solar Energy 1
description: A study of physics and engineering facets of the solar energy resource: solar collection, concentration, thermal conversion, energy storage, and the design and performance of solar thermal energy systems. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122 and MATHS 172 or 162.

title: Applied Solar Energy 2
description: Physics and engineering of solar electric power generation with emphasis on properties of solar cells and design, operation, and performance of photovoltaic systems. Prerequisite: APHYS 420.

title: Heat Transfer
description: The basic heat transfer processes in nature. Conduction, convection, and radiation in applied problems using electricalmodelanalogue, graphical, and computerized numerical methods. Prerequisite: MATHS 162; PHYCS 122; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introductory Astronomy: A Study of the Solar System and Beyond
description: Study of the physical nature of objects in the universe and methods used by astronomers to understand them. Topics selected from basic laws of nature, the Solar System, stars, nebulae, galaxies, and cosmology.

title: Astronomy Materials for the Teacher
description: Fundamentals of astronomy including historical aspects and modern astronomy concepts. Emphasis is on construction of models and experimentation appropriate to the classroom. Designed primarily for students in education programs.

title: Observational Astronomy
description: Continuation of ASTRO 100 providing practical experience in observing celestial objects by using telescopes and other astronomical apparatus. Prerequisite: ASTRO 100 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: General Astronomy 1
description: Essential points of modern astronomy, emphasizing the underlying physical principles. Topics include coordinate systems in astronomy, orbital laws, relativity, planetary physics, measurement of stellar distances, and spectral classification of stars. Prerequisite: MATHS 108.

title: General Astronomy 2
description: A continuation of ASTRO 120. Topics include atomic structure and stellar spectra, stellar atmospheres and interiors, multiple star systems and clusters, galactic structure, cosmology, and the origin of the universe. Prerequisite: ASTRO 120.

title: Topics in Astronomy
description: Discussion of specific topics in astronomy, such as comets, eclipses, UFOs, and interstellar travel. Designed for students not majoring in physics, the course requires no math or science background. Students may consult their curricular advisors or the Department of Physics and Astronomy for specific topics being studied during a given semester. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Astronomy and Astrophysics 1
description: A review of mechanics, electromagnetic radiation, and atomic structure in the context of modern observational astrophysics. Solar system astrophysics— including an introduction to celestial mechanics and astronomical coordinate and time systems—are surveyed, and astronomical instruments are discussed. Prerequisite: PHYCS 120, 122.

title: Astronomy and Astrophysics 2
description: An examination of observational stellar astronomy with applications to the study of stellar structure and evolution, and a review of the physics of stellar systems such as star clusters, galaxies, and clusters of galaxies. Prerequisite: ASTRO 330.

title: Seminar in Modern Astronomy
description: Selected topics in contemporary astronomy. Extensive use of library facilities including current journals and periodicals in astronomy. Topics for study may include astronomical research in progress and such esoteric subjects as U.F.O.'s and extraterrestrial life. Prerequisite: PHYCS 122 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Instruments and Techniques in Planetarium Operations
description: Use of planetarium instruments, console, and chamber. Creation and presentation of planetarium programs including slideduplicating techniques, slide opaquing, and the production of sound tracks. Prerequisite: permission of the planetarium director.

title: Theories and Instruments of the Astronomer
description: Reviews of various atlases, catalogs, ephemerides, and charts. The development of methods used to compute and update stellar positions. Discusses astronomical instruments in the context of their use by research astronomers. Analyzes specific techniques employed in astronomical photometry, spectroscopy, and photography. Prerequisite: ASTRO 332.

title: Advanced Astrophysics
description: A detailed investigation of the frontier areas of modern astrophysics. Possible topics include stellar structure, nucleosynthesis, stellar evolution, stellar atmospheres, and the interstellar material. Prerequisite: ASTRO 330, 332. Womack The Department of Physiology and Health Science offers a variety of programs in allied health science, basic science, health promotion, and disease prevention. Program emphases include anatomy and physiology, community health education, public health, school health education (leading to 7-12 certification and K-6 endorsements), emergency medical services, nuclear medicine technology, radiography, and respiratory therapy. The latter four programs are offered in cooperation with Methodist Hospital of Indiana, Inc. In addition, the department houses the Public Health Entomology Laboratory. ASSOCIATE DEGREES These associate degree programs prepare students for careers in emergency medical services, nuclear medicine technology, radiography, and respiratory therapy. The first phase of the programs takes place on the Ball State campus, and the second phase is offered in Indianapolis, where medical, technical, and clinical courses are taught at Methodist Hospital of Indiana, Inc., and other affiliated medical centers. Students may apply for admission to the professional/clinical phases of the programs after completing a minimum of 15 required general education hours, including at least 6 hours of the required mathematics and/or sciences courses. Applicants for the clinical phase of any of the programs must have overall gradepoint averages of at least 2.5 on a scale of 4.0 as well as grades of C or higher for all science and mathematics courses. Acceptance to the clinical part of the programs is conditional upon satisfactory completion of the remaining courses. ASSOCIATE IN SCIENCE— EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES, 68 hours Additional Requirement for Admission Before admission to the professional/clinical portion of the Emergency Medical Services associate degree program, students must show evidence of current Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) certification. title: Fundamentals of Human Health
description: Emphasizes lifestyle behaviors contributing to health promotion and disease prevention. General areas affecting health status are identified and suggestions made as to how healthrelated behaviors, selfcare, and individual decisions contribute to wellness and influence dimensions of health. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Principles of Community Health
description: Introduction to community health including its foundations, the tools of community health such as epidemiology, community organization, disease control, and health promotion. Focuses on the populations, settings, and special issues of community health.

title: Introduction to Health Education
description: Basic philosophy and practice in health education emphasizing work settings and health educator roles. Early exposure to the literature and organizations that support health education. Lab experience working with a practitioner. Open only to health science and teaching health and safety majors and minors.

title: Scientific Foundations of Health Science
description: Overview of human anatomy and physiology as it relates to the recognition and assessment of health and diseases. Also presents strategies for preventing health problems. Prerequisite: HSC 160.

title: Emergency Health Care
description: Prevention and emergency procedures of various emergency health problems and accidents, including cardiac arrest. First Aid and CPR American Red Cross certifications are offered. No regularly scheduled laboratory. Not open to students who have credit in PEP 299 or 396.

title: Health, Sexuality, and Family Life
description: Health aspects of human sexuality and family life with a focus on human reproduction, physiology of sexual response, sexual disorders and dysfunctions, sexually transmitted diseases, promotion of sexual health, and the family's role in sex education. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Elementary School Health Program
description: School's role in promoting health and preventing disease among preschool and elementary school children. Focus is on the school health program (instruction, services, and environment), community resources, and health problems common to school children. No regularly scheduled laboratory.

title: Professional Experience
description: Paid professional experience in an approved program with a business firm, government agency, or nonprofit organization under supervision of the department. Prerequisite: HSC 486, permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Public Health Practice
description: Overview of public health programs and management issues. Examines the importance of health promotion policy, grantwriting skills, and cultural sensitivity in public health practice. Prerequisite: HSC 180.

title: Health Education Theory and Practice
description: Introduction to a variety of community health education strategies and models. Explores various health behavior theories and their implications for community health education program development. Prerequisite: HSC 200.

title: Quantitative Methods and Epidemiology
description: Introduction to practical applications of quantitative methods in health science. Uses of health statistics and epidemiology are explored. Weekly onehour laboratory period emphasizes data manipulation by means of advanced technology. Prerequisite: HSC 180; MATHS 108 or higher.

title: Honors Colloquium in Health Science
description: Exploration of selected current issues in health science with an emphasis upon individualized study, reporting, and discussion. Restricted to honors students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Health Education Communication
description: Application of communication theory and skills to enhance the delivery of health education programs in various settings. Twohour weekly laboratory emphasizes the acquisition of practical skills typically used by the health education professional. Prerequisite: HSC 200.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Health and Safety
description: Application of the roles of the health teacher in a school setting. Functions considered include needs assessment, program planning, direct instruction, and evaluation. Prerequisite: EDSEC 280 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum.

title: History of Medicine in Western Society
description: A survey of the ideas, attitudes, and institutions of medicine and public health in the Western world from antiquity to modern times, with special attention to social forces influencing medical knowledge and health care. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 460.

title: Sex Education and School Health
description: Development of an understanding of how to implement and teach a positive program of sex education that will help young people develop constructive attitudes, values, and practices based on sound knowledge in accordance with American Medical Association recommendations and pertinent state guidelines. Prerequisite: HSC 261 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Patient Education: A Team Approach
description: Theories of client education and application of the education process to individuals and groups in healthcare settings. Emphasis is on the multidisciplinary team concept in planning, implementing, and evaluating client education. Application of knowledge of growth and development in meeting learning needs of clients.

title: Alcohol Problems
description: A study of alcohol as a mood modifier; its use, nonuse, and abuse in drinking societies. Critical and controversial issues relevant to alcohol ingestion will be explored for medical, economic, legal, educational, historical, physiological, and public health implications.

title: Drug Dependence and Abuse
description: Analyzes the medical, psychological, sociological, and legal dimensions of drug use in the United States. Examines the incidence and prevalence of drug abuse together with the roles played by school and community in dealing with this health problem.

title: Consumer Health Issues
description: Health services and consumer protection organizations. Analysis of fraudulent health practices and nostrums, available health care systems, and health products.

title: Health and Aging
description: Dynamics of later life and the aging process with specific emphasis on health. The physiological and behavioral dimensions of the aging process will be analyzed and discussed.

title: Death and Dying
description: Analyzes the relationship between death and health with emphasis upon the physiological, medical, psychological, legal, and consumer aspects of dying in contemporary America. Investigates problems that relate to the meaning of death, care for the dying, death ritual, bereavement, and death education. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Women and Health
description: General overview of issues related to women and health: health needs of working women, special nutritional concerns, the gynecological exam, reproductive anatomy and physiology, fertility and infertility, breast problems, wife abuse, and rape.

title: Practical Experience
description: Intern assignment to an approved health agency or educational institution for a period of time commensurate with academic credit. Periodic and terminal reports to an academic advisor and to the agency administrator are required for this nonpaid experience. Prerequisite: HSC 486, permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Environmental Health
description: Physical environment and its relationship to causes of disease. Review of environmental health problems and their solutions. Areas of study include air and water pollution, milk and food sanitation, disposal of human excreta and waste, radiological agents in the environment, and occupational health problems.

title: Public Health Education: Planning and Evaluation
description: Intended for persons planning to work in public health agencies. Emphasizes the need for planning, current settings for public health education, techniques used to identify health education components of health programs, program planning techniques, and evaluation methodologies. Prerequisite: HSC 380, 384, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Special Studies in Health Science
description: Designed to give undergraduate health science students who exhibit special aptitude and interest an opportunity to pursue special lines of scientific investigation individually. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques or skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Fundamentals of Mammalian Anatomy
description: Basic study of mammalian anatomy with detailed dissection of an animal or animal tissue and examination of representative microscopic structure. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: HSC 160 or another biological science course. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Embryology
description: Normal development of the human organism including germ cell formation, fertilization, implantation, and organ formation. Consideration of embryonic environment, physiology, and abnormal development. Prerequisite: BIO 111, 112; or ANAT 201.

title: Human Anatomy
description: Regional study of the structural and functional relations of the human body by means of dissection. Consideration of normal and abnormal development and microscopic structure of tissues and organs. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 210, 211.

title: Human Neuroanatomy
description: Offers strong background in the basic structural and functional relations of the central nervous system. Emphasis is on understanding the location of nerve cell centers and the fiber tracts entering and leaving these centers. Two twohour laboratory periods weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or ZOOL 330. Prerequisite recommended: ANAT 320 and 430.

title: Histology
description: Microscopic structure of organisms with special emphasis on the tissues of vertebrates. Introductory microtechnique. Three lectures and one laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or ZOOL 330.

title: Essentials of Human Physiology
description: Basic human physiology emphasizing the major function of each organ system including effects of nutrition, drugs, and drug abuse. Intended primarily for science teaching majors and minors in secondary education. Includes laboratory exercises designed to demonstrate physiological principles to high school students. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: BIO 102 or 111. Not open to students who have credit in PHYSL 210.

title: Fundamentals of Human Physiology
description: Physiological fundamentals as applied to human body systems with selected laboratory exercises to establish background for students entering the fields of radiology, nuclear medicine, and respiratory therapy. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: CHEM 101 or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students in nursing or teacher education.

title: Human Physiology 1
description: Vital processes with references to human functional biology. Group experimentation with recording apparatus. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: a course in biological science or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Physiology 2
description: Continuation of PHYSL 210. Functions of the human organ systems. Comparisons between vertebrate systems and mechanisms in humans. Includes use of animals or animal tissue. Prerequisite: PHYSL 210. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Neurophysiology
description: The function of the nervous system. Emphasis is on electrical properties of excitable cells, synaptic transmissions, sensory and motor mechanisms, reflexes, higher sensory functions, and motor control. Prerequisite: ANAT 405.

title: Endocrinology
description: Endocrine functions in humans and mammals with special emphasis on mechanisms. Normal hormone regulation and pathophysiological principles. Laboratory experience with smallmammal surgery and endocrine testing. One threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 210 and 211; one year of general chemistry.

title: Renal Physiology
description: A detailed study of the urinary system and excretory functions. Emphasizes human physiology but also includes comparative vertebrate systems. Subject matter ranges from the embryogenicanatomic level to the biochemicalpathological level. Laboratory study includes gross and microscopic anatomy, physiologic demonstrations, and clinical testing procedures. One threehour laboratory a week. Prerequisite: general chemistry; organic chemistry; one course in anatomy; one course in physiology.

title: Cardiovascular Physiology
description: A study of the dynamics of the human cardiovascular system, stressing applications of basic physical principles and the operation of physical regulatory systems. Includes seminarstyle discussion of recent literature. Prerequisite: one course in physiology and one course in physics.

title: Human Toxicology
description: A survey of chemical, physical, zoological, and botanical toxicoses in human health. The implications and methodology of dealing with hazardous substances and poisons will be considered in detail. Prerequisite: one year of chemistry; one year of biology; one course in physiology; one course in anatomy.

title: Neuroscience
description: Introductory study of the organization and function of the nervous system. Emphasizes integration of the structure and function of the nervous system. Prerequisite: one year of chemistry; one year of biology or physiology.

title: Pathophysiology
description: The physiologic pathology of selected disease processes and dysfunctions. The pathogenesis of certain derangements with broad applicability. Underlying chemical, biological, and physical mechanisms will be studied. Laboratory experience will include demonstrations, specimen study, and visitations. One threehour laboratory period weekly. Prerequisite: a course in anatomy, physiology, and chemistry.

title: Research Techniques in Physiology
description: Introduction to experimental design, laboratory techniques, and data analysis and interpretation in anatomy and physiology. Laboratory will include methods employing animal preparations, modern cellular/molecular techniques, and general histological procedures. Introduction to computer data acquisition and analysis. Prerequisite: one course in physiology or permission of the instructor. Prerequisite recommended: CHEM 360 or 463.

title: Special Studies in Physiology
description: Designed to give undergraduate physiology students who exhibit special aptitude and interest an opportunity to pursue special lines of scientific investigation on an individual basis. Experimental work, wide reading, and development of research techniques or skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Patient Care
description: An introduction to the hospital setting and patient care. Instruction in nursing skills and basic medical technology. Prerequisite: admission to an associate degree program in one of the allied health science options. Open only to allied health science students.

title: Cardiopulmonary-Renal Anatomy and Physiology
description: Designed to give students indepth knowledge of the respiratory, circulatory, and renal systems. Emphasis is on the respiratory system and how it interrelates with the other two systems. Prerequisite: PHYSL 207. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Basic Respiratory Care
description: Designed to make students familiar with all types of basic respiratory care and equipment in preparation for clinical practice. Prerequisite: PHYCS 106. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Cardiopulmonary Medicine
description: An indepth study of cardiopulmonary diseases. Topics include an extensive study of pharmacology; acute, chronic, and congenital cardiopulmonary diseases; and thoracic trauma. Prerequisite: CHEM 101. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: General Pathology
description: Designed to give respiratory therapy students an overview of human pathology. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Advanced Life Support
description: An indepth study of the management of cardiopulmonary emergencies. Topics include airway management, EKG interpretation, pharmacological resuscitation, and defibrillation. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Pulmonary Function
description: Classroom and laboratory study of the measurement and interpretation of lung volumes and mechanics, diffusion and exercise physiology. Labs include basic spirometry, flowvolume loops, and plethysmography. Student must have completed all fall semester respiratory courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Basic Clinical Practice
description: Gives students the opportunity to practice clinical skills in oxygen therapy, aerosol and humidity therapy, various respiratory treatments, and bronchopulmonary hygiene. Students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses and must take all spring semester respiratory therapy courses concurrently. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Mechanical Ventilation
description: Designed to make students familiar with mechanical ventilation, including evaluation of the patient, selection of therapy, patient management, and the equipment used for these tasks. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Pediatric Respiratory Care
description: Designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge for pediatric and neonatal respiratory care. Indepth presentation of oxygen therapy, mechanical ventilation, resuscitation, and treatment modalities. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Respiratory Specialties
description: A variety of special topics pertinent to respiratory therapy. Includes hemodynamic monitoring, pulmonary rehabilitation, home care, and supervision. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Advanced Clinical Practice
description: Gives students the opportunity to practice clinical skills in adult, pediatric, and neonatal critical care. Also includes experience in pulmonary functions, pulmonary rehabilitation, and home care. Skills learned in AHSC 208 will be reinforced. Prerequisite: students must have completed all spring semester respiratory therapy courses. Open only to respiratory therapy students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 1
description: A comprehensive study of skeletal radiographic positioning procedures; introduction to radiography, radiographic terminology, procedural orientation, and an indepth description of human structure and function. Prerequisite: ANAT 201; PHYSL 207. Parallel: AHSC 231. Open only to radiography students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 2
description: Continuation of AHSC 224, including skeletal radiographic positioning procedures and the study of special exams of all systems performed with and without contrast materials. Includes contrast materials, reactions, and patient care. Prerequisite: AHSC 224, 231. Parallel: AHSC 232. Open only to radiography students.

title: Radiographic Procedures 3
description: Continuation of AHSC 225, including additional special procedures and the equipment used for advanced imaging techniques. Introduction to computer literacy, computerized imaging techniques, and crosssectional anatomy. Prerequisite: AHSC 225, 232. Parallel: AHSC 233. Open only to radiography students.

title: Principles of Radiography 2
description: Study of radiographic film and processing, including exposure factors and their effects and special equipment used to perform diagnostic procedures. Prerequisite: APHYS 228. Open only to radiography students.

title: Radiographic Pathology
description: Study of clinical diseases and their effects on radiographs including technical adjustments, film evaluation, and quality control. Prerequisite: AHSC 229. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 1
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system including an introduction to routine radiography, file room, office, darkroom, and reading room procedures. Parallel: AHSC 224. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 2
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system including routine radiography and rotations through an outside affiliate. Offers the opportunity to master procedures practiced the previous semester. Prerequisite: AHSC 224, 231. Parallel: AHSC 225. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 3
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system including routine radiography, tomography, nuclear medicine, radiation therapy, ultrasound, mammography, and rotations through an outside affiliate. Offers the opportunity to master routine procedures. Prerequisite: AHSC 225, 232. Parallel: AHSC 226. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Applications 4
description: Directed learning experiences in radiographic clinical procedures through a rotational system that includes computerized tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, vascular procedures, lithotripsy, and repeat rotations. Offers the opportunity to master procedures practiced in previous semesters. Prerequisite: AHSC 226, 233. Open only to radiography students.

title: Special Topics in Radiography
description: Designed to give students the opportunity to receive academic credit for the completion of a scientific project. Prerequisite: permission of program director. Open only to radiography students.

title: Clinical Internship 1
description: An orientation to nuclear medicine technology. Emphasizes elementary patient care procedures and professional ethics. Prerequisite: admission to a general arts associate degree program with electives in nuclear medicine. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 2
description: Introduction to patient processing and nursing care in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: AHSC 240. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 3
description: Directed learning experiences in special areas of the nuclear medicine clinic. Introduction to scintillation camera and rectilinear imaging, in addition to related instrumentation, hot lab procedures, and dose preparation and administration. Prerequisite: AHSC 241. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Internship 4
description: Directed learning experiences in nuclear medicine clinical procedures that include imaging, quality control of instrumentation, radiopharmaceuticals, and in vitro techniques. Prerequisite: AHSC 242. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Clinical Theory and Administration 1
description: Indepth study of the clinical theory of nuclear medicine technology as it applies to examinations performed in a nuclear medicine clinic. Introduces administrative and recordkeeping procedures required by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in the operation of a nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: admission to a general arts associate degree program with electives in nuclear medicine. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Radiopharmaceuticals
description: Preparation, quality control, and the diagnostic and therapeutic application of radiopharmaceuticals in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Radiation, Biology, and Safety
description: Somatic and genetic effects of radiation and the procedures for radiological control and safety. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation
description: Study of the components and performance characteristics of equipment, the mechanisms of detection and measurement of radioactive materials, and descriptive and inductive statistics used in the nuclear medicine clinic. Prerequisite: APHYS 247. Parallel: AHSC 252. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Nuclear Medicine Instrumentation Lab
description: A weekly laboratory for nuclear medicine technology students enrolled in AHSC 251. Parallel: AHSC 251. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: In Vitro Nuclear Medicine Procedures
description: An introduction to the basic principles of radioimmunoassay and in vitro nuclear medicine procedures. Prerequisite: AHSC 248 or APHYS 248. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Topics in Nuclear Medicine
description: Designed to offer students academic credit for the completion of a scientific project. Parallel: AHSC 243. Open only to nuclear medicine technology students.

title: Introduction to Paramedicine
description: Introduction to the role and responsibilities of the paramedic, with an emphasis on response management in the prehospital environment. Topics include EMS systems, medicolegal matters, communication and documentation, trauma management, psychiatric emergencies, stress management and crisis intervention, hazardous materials, and scene management. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 261, 262, 263.

title: Pathophysiological Origins of Emergency Therapeutics
description: Comprehensive study of the physiology of human body organ systems as they relate to the provision of emergency medical care. Overview of common pathophysiological conditions encountered by the paramedic. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 262, 263.

title: Clinical Practice 1
description: Provides the opportunity to review basic lifesupport management and to practice communications and patient rapport in a controlled clinical environment. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 261, 263. Physiology and Health Science 291

title: Field Internship 1
description: Provides practice in and evaluation of basic lifesupport knowledge and skills, and practice in the operational management of prehospital advanced emergency care. Prerequisite: admission to the paramedic program and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 260, 261, 262.

title: Pharmacological Therapeutics and Treatment Modalities
description: Comprehensive survey of drugs used in emergency medical care and overview of common home medications. Topics include pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, drug dosages, calculation, administration, terminology, and legal considerations. Prerequisite: AHSC 260, 261, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 265, 266, 267.

title: Cardiopulmonary Pathophysiology and Therapeutics
description: Diseases, evaluation, and management of the respiratory and cardiovascular systems. Management procedures include endotracheal and esophageal intubation, blood gas interpretation, surgical airway management, EKG interpretation, and electrical and invasive therapeutic techniques. Prerequisite: AHSC 260, 261, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 266, 267.

title: Clinical Practice 2
description: Provides the opportunity to practice clinical skills in emergency medicine and trauma center, clinical laboratory, surgery, and cardiovascular care. Prerequisite: AHSC 262 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 265, 267.

title: Field Internship 2
description: Opportunity to practice clinical skills and scene management in the prehospital environment. Prerequisite: AHSC 263 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 264, 265, 266.

title: Medical and Environmental Emergencies
description: Pathophysiology and treatment of medical and environmental emergencies. Topics include neurological trauma and disease; burns, bites, and stings; substance abuse and toxicological emergencies; OB and gynecological emergencies; pediatrics; geronotology; and communicable diseases. Prerequisite: AHSC 264, 265, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 269, 271, 272.

title: Advanced Cardiac Life Support
description: Overview of the principles and practices of emergency cardiac care and cardiopulmonary resuscitation as they relate to the standards of the American Heart Association. Includes case presentation and comprehensive oral, written, and practical examinations. Prerequisite: AHSC 264, 265, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 268, 271, 272.

title: Special Rescue Techniques
description: Introduction to specialized rescue techniques used in various prehospital situations. Labs include water survival, search and rescue, diving emergencies, treatment of hypothermia, cave rescue, rope rescue, and principles of patient extrication. Prerequisite: AHSC 260 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Field Internship 3
description: Opportunity to practice clinical skills and scene management in the prehospital environment. Prerequisite: AHSC 267 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: AHSC 268, 269, 271.

title: Orientation to Radiation
description: Introduces the equipment, procedures, and terminology of the radiation therapist. Presents material covering all phases, functions, and roles of the technologist. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Clinical Applications 1
description: Directed learning experiences in basic radiation therapy treatment procedures, equipment, patient care skills, and professional ethics. Parallel: APHYS 247; AHSC 200, 249. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Radiation Oncology Physics
description: Basic theory of radiation therapy physics covering the fundamental concepts, properties, treatment applications, units, and terms relating to the role of the radiation therapist. Prerequisite: APHYS 247 or its equivalent. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Oncologic Pathology 1
description: Didactic experience studying the principles of clinical oncology, anatomy, and malignancies. Learning experiences on the etiology, treatment, and prognosis of cancer. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Clinical Applications 2
description: Directed learning experiences in basic radiation therapy treatment procedures, equipment, planning, and patient interactions. Oneonone skills evaluation through rotation in various technical areas. Prerequisite: AHSC 281. Parallel: AHSC 285. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Technical Radiation Oncology 1
description: Basic concepts in clinical applications of patient setups, treatment conditions, equipment, new procedures, quality assurance, and geometric considerations. Prerequisite: AHSC 281. Parallel: AHSC 284. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Oncologic Pathology 2
description: Didactic experience studying the principles of clinical oncology, anatomy, and malignancies. Learning experiences on the etiology, treatment, and prognosis of cancer. Prerequisite: AHSC 283. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Technical Radiation Oncology 2
description: Intermediate concepts in clinical applications of patient setups, treatment conditions, equipment, new procedures, quality assurance, and geometric considerations. Prerequisite: AHSC 285. Parallel: AHSC 289. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Treatment Planning and Dosimetry
description: Didactic experience providing the basic concepts of clinical radiation oncology treatment planning and dosimetry. Study of fundamental procedures in dose determination, distribution, measurements, and calibration. Prerequisite: AHSC 282. Parallel: AHSC 287. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Clinical Applications 3
description: Directed learning experiences in advanced radiation therapy treatment procedures, equipment, and planning patient interactions. Oneonone skills evaluation through rotation in various technical areas. Prerequisite: AHSC 288. Parallel: AHSC 282. Open only to radiation therapy students.

title: Clinical Applications 4
description: Directed learning experiences in advanced radiation therapy procedures, equipment, planning, patient care assessment by examination; oneonone skills evaluation by rotating through various technical areas. Prerequisite: AHSC 289. Open only to radiation therapy students. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Principles of Health-Care Management
description: Basic introduction to principles of managing healthcare services for students preparing for supervisory and middlemanagement positions. Includes the hospital as a workplace; hospital organization and management; job design, performance appraisals, compensation; finance, budgeting; planning, evaluation; and management information systems. Prerequisite: major or minor in a subject relating to course. ASSOCIATE DEGREES ASSOCIATE IN ARTS—LEGAL ASSISTANCE, 67 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE General education, 16 hours

title: Advanced Concepts in Allied Health Sciences
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject to be studied. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Research Seminar
description: Knowledge and skills required to conduct clinical, educational, and managerial research in the healthcare setting. Political Science 293 Prerequisite: health science major and senior class standing.

title: Independent Study in Allied Health
description: Designed to allow students to increase their knowledge and skills in both the technical and patientcare components of allied health. Students may complete one of Methodist Hospital's "Adda-Comp" programs to earn credit in this course. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. DEPARTMENT OF POLITICAL SCIENCE R. Scheele, Chairperson; R. Baker, C. Barker Lemay, T. Chang, M. Corbett, J. Cranor, G. Crawley, B. Fife, G. Frankland, F. Friedman, R. Hollands, J. Losco, F. Meyer, T. Perry, D. Reagan, J. Rouse, S. Vasicko The world and its problems are both the main concern and the principal laboratory of the modern political scientist. Political scientists study the political behavior of people, groups, and nations in an effort to understand why they behave as they do, to predict what they will do next, and sometimes to suggest how they should behave in the future. For information on the major in legal administration see Interdepartmental Programs, p. 56.

title: Politics: Today and Tomorrow
description: An introduction to the contemporary issues of national and world politics. Emphasizes both current and political events and longterm trends in politics.

title: American National Government
description: The organization and operation of national government as it relates to such current issues as civil rights, welfare, ecology, consumer protection, and international relations.

title: Citizen and the Law
description: To help understand citizen encounters with the legal system, this course explains the operation of the legal system and the political elements of the pertinent legal issues. Uses a variety of activities, films, and lectures. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson or the paralegal program coordinator.

title: Introduction to Paralegalism
description: Explores concepts of paralegalism with emphasis on legal ethics and values, the development and future of the paralegal function in our present legal environment, and a presentation of the concepts of litigation and legal procedure. Prerequisite: POLS 140.

title: Legal Research and Writing
description: An analysis of court procedures and appeal procedures, an indepth examination of reference sources available to attorneys, and improvement of research and writing skills. Prerequisite: POLS 141.

title: Litigation
description: For the advanced paralegal major focusing on litigation and related areas of paralegal responsibilities such as drafting interrogatories and writing complaints. Special attention given to learning the compilation of a trial notebook in preparation for litigation. Prerequisite: POLS 140, 141, 142, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to legal assistance and legal administration majors.

title: Introduction to Planning
description: A survey of problems inherent in planning for cities and regions using contributions of such other disciplines as history, geography, sociology, and economics. Required of majors in urban studies and planning; elective for others with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Scope and methods of the study of political science. After probing the basic nature of politics, the course examines political science as a systematic empirical discipline concerned with describing and explaining political phenomena. Substantial emphasis is placed on the use of computers as tools in the scientific study of politics.

title: State and Local Politics
description: Practices, politics, and structures of state and local governments in the United States with an emphasis on the Indiana experience.

title: Urban Government in the United States
description: Structure, functions, problems, and trends in city, urban, and metropolitan governments.

title: Family Law
description: Designed to acquaint students with legal problems in domestic relations. Covers legal problems involved in marriage, separation, divorce, child custody, adoption, and nonsupport.

title: Comparative Political Systems
description: A comparison of modern political systems as represented by the principal nations of the world.

title: Economic and Political Problems of Emerging Nations
description: Historical and contemporary problems of the lessdeveloped nations. Conditions contributing to economic, political, and social change. Problems of economic development policies and programs within the institutional structure. Internal and external pressures that influence patterns of development. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 280. Not open to students who have credit in ECON 279.

title: American Foreign Policy
description: A survey of major issues in foreign policy formulation, an introduction to the process of making U.S. foreign policy, and an analysis of relevant American strategic doctrines.

title: International Relations
description: A survey of the formal relations among sovereign states in the international system, emphasizing the operation of diplomacy, the elements of power, the procedures for the settlement of disputes, and the various modes of conflict resolution.

title: Early Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of political thought of the early Mediterranean and medieval worlds that became the foundation of modern political theories and systems of the West. Emphasis is on writings of Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, St. Augustine, St. Thomas Aquinas, and Machiavelli.

title: Modern Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of selected writings of leading political theorists from the Age of Reformation to the present.

title: Communist Political Thought: From Marx to Present
description: A critical analysis and evaluation of Marxism, Leninism, Stalinism, Khrushchevism, post- Khrushchev Communist ideology, and Maoism as a system of theoretical propositions and as an action program of an international movement.

title: Voter Polling Techniques
description: Methods by which information is obtained on the voting behavior and attitudes of the electorate. Emphasis is on producing a working knowledge of polling techniques. Includes such topics as sampling, interviewing, and questionnaire construction.

title: Introduction to Law and Enforcement
description: Survey of the development of law and contemporary law enforcement in the United States with special attention to various components of law enforcement systems, their interrelationships, purposes, and needs.

title: Problems in Public Policy
description: Current political, economic, and social problems in the United States. Consideration of relationships between government and elements of our free enterprise system, including agriculture, small and large firms, labor, public utilities, and finance.

title: National Defense Policy
description: An international survey of military capacity and function provides the background for analysis of the national defense policy of the United States. Special emphasis is on American strategic interests and problems of weapons, technology, nuclear control, and disarmament.

title: Environmental Law and Policy
description: Significant facets of the legal system's response to conflicting demands upon environmental resources. Composition of environmental problems, control issues, policy formulation, and legal remedies.

title: Public Administration
description: Organization, personnel, and functions of the various agencies of administration— national, state, and local.

title: Paid Professional Experience in American Government and Law
description: Paid partor fulltime experience for one or more semesters in the office of a public official in national, state, or local government; a candidate for public office; a political party; or private firm or organization. Assignments depend upon the interest of the student and convenience of the sponsors. Prerequisite: POLS 130, 237, and one from POLS 342, 350, 431, or 473. For legal assistance and legal administration majors, POLS 140, 141, 142 and permission of the program coordinator. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Public Opinion and Political Behavior
description: The nature of public opinion; instruments, techniques, and institutions involved in formation of public opinion; and the political uses and implications at home and abroad of public opinion and propaganda.

title: Public Interest Groups and Government
description: Internal government and external political strategy of private associations, such as trade associations, unions, and professional, church, and patriotic organizations. Implications of pressure group activities for constitutionalism, majoritarianism, and constituency, and the effects of pressure groups on the political process.

title: Political Campaigns
description: Considers political campaigns from theoretical and practical perspectives as the link between citizens and the government in a representative democracy. Designed to answer questions on the theory, strategies, and techniques of political campaigns.

title: Governments and Politics of Western Europe
description: An introduction to the concept of Europe as a political and cultural entity, to the government and political structures of the three major powers in Western Europe—Great Britain, France, and Germany—and to the current state of the Western European integration movement.

title: British Government and Politics
description: The political system of the United Kingdom, including a discussion of the Commonwealth and Britain's place in an expanding European community. Emphasis is also on Anglo-American relations and British contributions to American political arrangements.

title: Politics of the European Community
description: Study of the development of the European Community as an evolving political entity—its politics, institutions, policies—and the prospects for European unification. Not open to the student who has credit in EURO 385.

title: Politics of Russia and the Successor States
description: Evaluation of political, economic, and social change and performance in Russia and other successor states of the former Soviet Union. Historical and geographical factors are also treated. Not open to the student who has credit in EURO 386.

title: Honors Colloquium in Political Science
description: Exploration of selected issues and topics in political science, with emphasis on individualized study and reporting. Open to students in the Honors College and to other outstanding students by permission of the department chairperson.

title: The United Nations and International Organization
description: Concentrated study of international organizations and the structure, functions, and current issues facing the United Nations. Students participate in a mock Security Council at Ball State and may have an opportunity to participate in the National Model United Nations Conference.

title: International Relations in Asia
description: A survey of contemporary international relations in Asia with a special emphasis on the roles of China, Japan, the United States, and the former Soviet Union in this area. Political Science 297

title: Issues in Political Science
description: Investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in the field with emphasis on subfields, specialties, and materials not covered in established courses. Open to upperclass students with special interest in politics. The content is announced before each offering. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Reading and Special Study
description: Topics are chosen and investigated in consultation with the department chairperson and a professor with special competence in the area involved. Open to juniors and seniors with special aptitude and interests that qualify them to do semiindependent study. Prerequisite: basic courses in the area selected for special study and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Readings in Planning
description: Reading program developed in consultation with the department chairperson and a professor with special competence in planning. Open to juniors and seniors with special aptitude and interest in planning. Prerequisite: POLS 461 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Workshop in Political Science
description: Intensive study of selected problems in political science. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: American Political Thought
description: American political thought from the colonial period to the present. Includes the study of Puritanism, nature of rights, constitutionalism and federalism, nature of the Union, democracy, liberalism, conservatism, individualism and collectivism, welfare state, isolation and internationalism, and national security and freedom.

title: Legislation
description: A functional study of legislative bodies and lawmaking, covering organization of legislative bodies, operation of the committee system, relations with interest groups, executive branches, bill drafting, legislative aids, controls over legislation, and movement for reform.

title: The American Chief Executive
description: An examination of the American concept of a political chief executive as a coordinate member along with the legislature and courts. Problems of jurisdiction, leadership, authority, public relations, and centralization are examined.

title: The American Judicial System
description: The nature and functions of state and federal judicial systems, including the role of courts in relation to individuals and the executive and legislative branches of government are analyzed.

title: State Legislatures
description: Legislative systems in American state government. External influences (constituencies, political parties, interest groups), internal influences (organizational structure, staff, norms, decision making), issues confronting state legislatures, and reform proposals.

title: Intergovernmental Relations
description: Analysis of relations among national, state, and local governments. Considerations of constitutional and legal bases and the nature of relations, such as grantsinaid, tax immunity, education, and interstate compacts.

title: Government and Politics in Indiana
description: Survey of Indiana's political culture and tradition as compared to other states'. Critical examination of Indiana's contemporary political processes and governmental policies. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 130, 237.

title: Metropolitan Problems
description: Analysis of cities and metropolitan communities; examines the nature, characteristics, functions, governmental structure, intergovernmental relations, social makeup and problems, economic base, decisionmaking structure, and other related concerns; considers the present and future role of planning and citizen participation.

title: American Constitutional Law
description: The Constitution of the United States, its development and interpretations through principal statutes and judicial decisions. Congressional policies embodied in socioeconomic legislation and doctrines developed by the Supreme Court. Prerequisite: POLS 130.

title: Constitutional Liberties
description: Relations between the individual and the government as revealed through cases in constitutional law. Content includes cases involving the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Prerequisite: POLS 130 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Land-Use Regulation
description: An analysis of the legislative and constitutional aspects of the regulation of land use at various levels of government, including zoning, subdivision regulations, urban renewal, codes, enforcement, eminent domain, conservation, reclamation, interstate compacts, and metropolitan and regional agencies.

title: Politics and Administration of Local Government Budgets
description: Local government budgeting with emphasis on political and administrative issues in budget preparation and accountability. Topics include revenue development including tax and nontax sources, capital expenditure programming, financing pensions, contracting for services, costbenefit analysis, and federal and state grant mechanisms.

title: Administrative Law
description: Legal and political study of independent regulatory agencies; their powers, functions, and roles as determined by an analysis of relevant cases in which basic principles are identified and synthesized with other elements of public law.

title: Community Planning and Its Administration
description: Planning and development of improved land use and service activities of cities and predominantly urban communities. Consideration of scope, legal basis, implementation, and problems of planning for streets, utilities, education, recreation, transportation, zoning, and related community services.

title: Labor-Management Relations in Government
description: Examines public employee unionization, legal provisions for collective bargaining, determination and recognition of bargaining units, bilateral negotiation, and thirdparty involvement procedures, administration of agreements, and the processes and strategies in collective bargaining negotiations in public organizations.

title: Administrative Problems in State Government
description: An analysis of administrative procedures and organizational behavior at the state level. Special emphasis is given to the provision of government services and functions in the major areas of budgeting and taxation, education, environmental protection, public health, and public works. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 237 or 350.

title: American Political Parties
description: Organization and functions of political parties in the United States and their role in a representative democracy.

title: Women and Politics
description: National survey of women and the political process, with an emphasis on women and contemporary public policy issues.

title: Minority Group Politics
description: Deals with political impact of ethnic groups on American politics. Emphasis on both legal and extralegal means by which ethnic groups become involved in and influence public policy. Prerequisite: POLS 130.

title: Practical Experience in American Government and Law
description: Unpaid fullor parttime assignment for one or more semesters in the office of a public official in national, state, or local government; a candidate for public office; a political party; or private firm or organization. Assignments depend upon the interest of the student and convenience of the sponsor. Prerequisite: POLS 130, 237, and one from POLS 342, 350, 431, or 473. For legal assistance and legal administration majors, POLS 140, 141, 142, and permission of the program coordinator and approval of the supervising employer. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Government and Politics of China
description: A comprehensive survey of the government and politics of modern China, both the Republic of China and Communist China.

title: International Law
description: A survey of the Law of Nations by the analysis of prominent decisions of international tribunals, examination of representative legal principles, the briefing of appropriate cases, and the conducting of mock court trials.

title: World Politics
description: Theories of contemporary interactions among states, especially the major powers. Particular attention will be given to conflict resolution.

title: Communist China's Foreign Policy
description: A comprehensive analysis of Communist China's role in international politics, with specific emphasis on the effects of Communist China's foreign policy and the response to it. Wittig Psychology is the science that studies the behavior of people as they interact with their environment. The behavior of lower animals is also studied, both for itself and because psychologists hope to find general principles of behavior that may apply across species. Psychological Science 299 The department offers a major in psychology, designed for students intending to pursue graduate studies in psychology, as well as for students who do not plan to pursue advanced degrees in psychology. The latter often find positions in industrial or service settings after graduation. The department also offers a minor in psychology that allows students to choose courses relevant to their majors and areas of interest. Students interested in teaching psychology at the high school level may complete social studies majors or minors with concentrations in psychology.
