description: A seminar course for nontraditional students that offers an opportunity to explore, discuss, and reinforce changes in themselves as learners and group participators. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Evolving Roles and Job Opportunities
description: Nontraditional students will examine the evolving roles of men and women and the job opportunities available now and possibly in the future in order to make realistic career decisions.

title: Seminar on Comprehensive Programming for Lifelong Learning
description: Helps nontraditional students prepare portfolios on learning acquired through life experiences and develop comprehensive plans for continuing learning throughout their life spans.

title: The Adult Learner in the Undergraduate Classroom
description: A seminar for adult learners that offers an opportunity to examine the university setting, values expressed in the classroom by faculty and students, and the dynamics Educational Psychology 331 of higher education in terms of students' own developing values.

description: A seminar that focuses on the specific need to express oneself openly and fully without fear of ridicule, rejection, or guilt. title: Educational Gerontology
description: Study of education and aging with emphasis on a lifespan approach. Topics include education about aging for children and youth, career educational opportunities in gerontology, education for paraprofessionals and volunteers in aging, retirement planning education, and educational opportunities for older adults.

title: Adult Psychology
description: Developmental study of psychological stages of adulthood. Not open to students who have credit in EDPSY 355. EDUCATION: ADMINISTRATION (EDAD)

title: Legal Aspects of Education for Future Teachers
description: Special attention will focus on legal foundations of education, rights and responsibilities of teachers (employment, tenure, fringe benefits, liability, and negotiations), and rights and responsibilities of students (attendance, discipline, and due process). title: Study Skills for College Students
description: Provides empirically supported study strategies and skills to increase the probability of university success. Focuses on techniques for successful study and test taking. Includes laboratory experiences.

title: Human Growth and Development
description: Development of personality in the Western world from birth through adolescence and application to life in the family, school, community, and broader social situations. Emphasis on physical, motor, social, emotional, and cognitive development and their interweaving relationships, particularly as they apply to the school setting. Should be taken during the sophomore year. PSYSC 100 is a strongly recommended elective.

title: Human Growth and Development
description: Development of personality in the Western world, beginning at birth, but placing special emphasis upon the period from preadolescence through adolescence. Emphasis is on physical, motor, social, emotional, and cognitive development and their interweaving relationships, particularly as they apply to the school setting. Should be taken during the sophomore year and is intended for students planning to teach in secondary schools. PSYSC 100 is a strongly recommended elective.

title: Educational Psychology
description: Psychological principles underlying learning and the improvement of teaching, tests, and measurements. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250 or 251, except for students with a departmental major in dietetics. PSYSC 100 is a strongly recommended elective.

title: Independent Study: Educational Psychology
description: Individually planned experiences, extensive independent research in educational psychology. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Behavior Analysis in Education
description: Helps students to translate learning principles into teaching practices, to design and implement behavior analysis procedures that enhance motivation and learning in educational settings and decrease behavior problems, and to assess the effects of such instructional techniques.

title: Psychology of Later Life
description: A study of the later years of life with emphasis on the adaptations required. Includes theories of aging, physical and social changes taking place, and coping strategies.

title: Educational Tests and Measurement
description: Standard educational tests and the use of such tests as instruments for the evaluation of learning. Techniques of test construction.

title: Child Psychology
description: Study of the psychology of childhood, with special emphasis on various psychological influences contributing to child development.

title: Adolescent Psychology
description: Study of childhood influences upon and psychology of adolescent development and of the effects of that development during young adulthood. Emphasis is on various contributing psychological influences.

title: Adult Psychology
description: Developmental study of psychological stages of adulthood. Not open to students who have credit in EDAC 355.

title: Mental Hygiene
description: Psychological principles underlying mental health and the application of these principles in and out of the classroom. Prerequisite: 6 hours of psychology.

title: Basic Concepts in Developmental Psycholinguistics
description: Overview of learning theory, developmental theory, and research design as applied to current research on developmental aspects of language acquisition and behavior. Applications of these concepts to language assessment, instruction, and remediation. Recommended prerequisites: EDPSY 250 or 251; EDPSY 290 or ENG 420.

title: Applied Study in Developmental Psycholinguistics
description: Research or laboratory experience in language acquisition or language behavior. Prerequisite: EDPSY 469 and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Seminar in Educational Psychology
description: Group or individual investigation and study of current issues, problems, and developments in human development, classroom learning, and evaluation. description: Students work with elementaryschoolaged children of a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds. Through seminars and counseling they plan and evaluate experiences and begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children as orientation to teaching in elementary school.

title: Laboratory Experiences: Multiethnic Young Children
description: Labseminar orientation working with preschoolaged children of a variety of cultural and ethnic backgrounds. Opportunities through seminars and conferences to begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Interaction Skills for the Young Child
description: Introduces students to basic skills every young child needs to acquire in order to use language competently in society. Deals with materials, methods, principles of learning, and conditions necessary for optimum learning.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood Education 1
description: Lab and seminar experience focusing on the organization, management, and control of learning environments for young children. Prerequisite: permission of the coordinator of early childhood education or the chairperson of elementary education.

title: Organization and Management of the Multicultural Classroom
description: The role of the teacher as the facilitator for learning in the elementary classroom with opportunites through seminars and counseling to plan and evaluate experiences and to begin to develop skills, attitudes, and understanding necessary for successful communication with children of various ethnic and cultural groups. Prerequisite: EDEL 101. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Handwriting
description: Development of skills in manuscript and cursive writing, methods of teaching handwriting in the elementary school, and relationship of manuscript and cursive writing to the language arts.

title: Principles of Organization and Management in Early Childhood
description: Development of understanding and skills needed for effective teacherpupil, teacherparent, and teacherteacher relationships in school settings for young children.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood 2
description: Lab and seminar experience focusing on the selection and organization of learning experiences developmentally appropriate for young children. Integrating math and science into the curriculum is an essential part of the course. Prerequisite: EDEL 160 or EDEL 190 and permission of the coordinator of early childhood education or the department chairperson.

title: Creative Experiences for Young Children
description: Designed to develop knowledge of creative activities that are developmentally appropriate for the young child. Skill in providing creative and play experiences. Work with children is an integral part of the course. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Curriculum and Lab Experiences in Early Childhood 3
description: A field and seminar experience to assist classroom teachers in the implementation of educational opportunities for young children under supervision of a university faculty member or agency representative. Prerequisite: minimum of 36 hours in early elementary education courses, always including EDEL 160, 190, 241, and permission of the early childhood coordinator or the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Elementary Education 337 Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Materials and Techniques for Teaching Children of Multiethnic Backgrounds
description: Designed to offer multisensory approaches to learning. Will attempt to identify learning methods and materials best suited to the students' style of learning.

title: Principles of Teaching and Classroom Management: Elementary School
description: Problems of school organization, management, control, and environment in relation to the learning activities of children. Stresses legal rights and responsibilities of teachers as well as use of instructional media and computer. Prerequisite: EDEL 101 or 160, 201, and permission of the department chairperson. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 250, except for majors in special education or speech pathology and audiology.

title: The Teaching of Language Arts in the Lower Elementary Grades
description: Development of language arts skills— listening, speaking, reading, and writing—in the primary grades.

title: Social, Historical, and Philosophical Foundations of Elementary Education
description: Emphasizes historical and social derivations of contemporary educational ideas, philosophical foundations of educational practices, alternatives for ethical decisions in education, and formulation of a personal philosophical position related to educational issues in elementary education.

title: Computer Literacy in the Elementary School Classroom
description: Develops computer literacy and application for elementary school instruction. Introduces programming in BASIC, evaluation of software, and methods of developing literacy in children. Handson experience with microcomputers.

title: Discipline and Classroom Management: Some Practical Approaches
description: Designed to help beginning elementary school teachers create and maintain effective learning environments. Emphasizes practical approaches to prevention and remediation of disruptive classroom behavior.

title: Parent and Community Relations
description: Explores important and complex roles of parents and parent substitutes in the educational development of young children. Conditions affecting parentchild interactions and skills needed for effective parenting are studied and related to the educational process. Parent involvement as a significant component of early childhood education.

title: Kindergarten Education
description: Development of the kindergartenprimary curriculum with special emphasis on kindergarten children and procedures to be used in their development.

title: Educational Programs for Pre- Kindergarten
description: Activities of young children in prekindergarten. Organization, administration, and educational program of prekindergarten care. Child development and parent education as part of prekindergarten education.

title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education
description: Involves experiences to enrich the relationships among parents, teachers, and children in the home, school, and community environments and to acquaint and involve students with the variety of community resources concerned with the welfare of young children and their families.

title: Psychology of Early Childhood
description: Study of young children of nursery school and kindergarten age, involving lectures, readings, discussions, and conferences to give students individual guidance and help them interpret their study of the physical, mental, social, and emotional development of selected young children. Consideration is given to growth in perception, language, expression, and interests.

title: Student Teaching: Pre-Kindergarten
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 461 (6) and EDEL 462 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Pre-Kindergarten
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 461 (6) and 462 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 463 (3) and EDEL 464 (6) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Elementary School
description: Students enroll simultaneously for EDEL 464 (6) and EDEL 463 (3) for a total of 9 semester hours. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 463.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Elementary
description: Student teaching for six weeks in an area of endorsement or extended experience. In addition to regular student teaching requirement for elementary education. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Primary Grades
description: Designed to give future primarygrade teachers the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 468.

title: Student Teaching: Kindergarten
description: Designed to give future kindergarten teachers the opportunity to develop teaching competence under supervision of professional teachers cooperating with the university in the student teaching program. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDEL 467.

title: Practicum in Elementary Education
description: Laboratory and seminar course involving a study of progressive school practices; the philosophy of education underlying and the possibilities of using progressive practices in the public school. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Elementary Education
description: Independent study and research in elementary education. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Elementary Education
description: An analysis of one's professional preparation for teaching, identifying areas in which students need to bolster weaknesses and augment strengths and arranging for more preparation in these areas. Prerequisite: one term of student teaching. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned. EDUCATION: READING (EDRDG)

title: Self-Improvement in Reading
description: A remedial course designed to improve comprehension skills, reading speed, vocabulary, notetaking, and content reading. Students who do not achieve the 30th percentile in comprehension on the Diagnostic Reading Tests or a selected reading test administered by Reading Programs and Services must repeat the course. The course is offered on a credit/nocredit basis, and credit hours do not count toward graduation requirements. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: College Reading Skills
description: Emphasizes development of the ability to read collegelevel materials critically from a variety of subject areas and to develop flexibility of rate.

title: Rapid Reading Techniques
description: Rapid reading techniques of previewing, skimming, and scanning will be practiced. Machines will be available. Rate of comprehension and flexibility of rate will be emphasized. Techniques will be applied to student's reading assignments. Open to all graduate and undergraduate students who have basic mastery of reading skills.

title: Prereading Development
description: Basic understanding of environments and planned activities that foster positive attitudes and interests related to reading, procedures that stimulate prereading development, and related practical experiences with young children.

title: Teaching of Reading in Elementary School
description: Designed to review the current thinking, approaches, and methodology of teaching reading in today's schools. Attention directed to readiness, word recognition and analysis, comprehension, and planning of the total developmental reading program, emphasizing reading at the elementary level. Open only to juniors and seniors or by permission of the director of reading.

title: Developmental and Corrective Reading
description: Designed to review current thinking, approaches, and methodology of teaching developmental reading in the elementary schools. Provides prospective teachers with understanding of difficulties in reading and practical experiences in assessing reading difficulties and in study of corrective treatment. Includes guided laboratory experience. Prerequisite: EDRDG 400 or EDRDS 320.

title: Using Computers in Reading Instruction
description: Prepares prospective elementary school teachers to make appropriate and effective use of the computer in a classroom reading program. Includes attention to commercially prepared courseware and teacherdeveloped applications. Prerequisite: EDGEN 320 for students pursuing the computer endorsement. EDRDG 400 or its equivalent for all others.

title: Reading Strategies and Practicum
description: Provides prospective classroom teachers (K-12) with opportunities to study and try various approaches and strategies in teaching reading. Provides experience in grouping students of varying reading abilities and in planning and implementing a classroom reading program appropriate for these students. Prerequisite: EDRDG 400, 430.

title: Independent Study in Reading
description: Designed to meet the needs of students wanting to study in individually selected areas of reading education. Prerequisite: 6 hours of credit in reading education and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be DEPARTMENT OF SECONDARY, HIGHER, AND FOUNDATIONS OF EDUCATION A. title: Student Teaching: All-Grade
description: Required for the standard license in allgrade education. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public elementary, junior high/middle, or secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDALG 472. Open only to allgrade teaching majors.

title: Student Teaching: All-Grade
description: Required for the standard license in allgrade education. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public elementary, junior high/middle, or secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDALG 470. Open only to allgrade teaching majors. EDUCATION: FOUNDATIONS (EDFON)

title: Social, Historical, and Philosophical Foundations of Education
description: Education as an institution in society and its relationship to the individual and 39-42 hours Preeducation program, 6-8 Recommended elective: American culture from sociological, philosophical, historical, economic, political, and anthropological perspectives. Such contemporary issues as cultural values, social class, legal concerns, ethnic groups, political pressure, and the role of the teacher will be stressed. Open only to juniors and seniors. EDUCATION: HIGHER (EDHI)

title: Introduction to Personnel Services in Residence Halls
description: Principles involved in selfawareness, developing interand intrapersonal skills, and examining the development of community within the residence hall. Prerequisite: sophomore standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Leadership and Development of Student Organizations
description: Examines philosophical bases, group processes, and skills relevant to leadership and development of student organizations in higher education. Focuses on understanding and skills needed for effective involvement in student groups. EDUCATION: JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE (EDJHM)

title: The Junior High/Middle School Curriculum
description: Several curricular approaches appropriate for students ages ten to fourteen years will be examined in relation to current research. Legal rights and the significance of positive human relations are studied. Direct development of alternative curricular programs and appropriate use of merging structures and nontraditional materials will be emphasized.

title: Principles of Teaching, Curriculum and Classroom Management: Middle School
description: Combines the theory and practice of teaching at the middle school level. Includes direct teaching experiences with early adolescents in public school settings; seminars concerned with such topics as curriculum, instructional strategies, legal concerns, discipline, and advanced microteaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205; EDPSY 250 or 251; and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Parallel: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Independent study and research in junior high/middle school topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Instructional Strategies and Approaches in Junior High/Middle School
description: Conditions affecting the total instructional responsibilities in junior high/middle schools are studied. Students are required to develop skills in individualizing instruction to serve the full range of students, the ability to work cooperatively with other professional personnel, and instructional techniques and evaluation procedures especially appropriate for junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 and EDPSY 251 or 351.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Junior High/Middle School
description: Designed to prepare prospective junior high/middle school educators to cope with discipline problems in all junior high/middle school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures in preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by junior high/middle school students and ways to create positive environments for learning.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Junior High/Middle School
description: Elective studentteaching experience enables students to complete a full semester in a fullday student teaching assignment in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDJHM 460 and 462. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Advanced Undergraduate Practicum in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Provides direct, supervised experiences for students wanting to gain increased skill and knowledge regarding junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 280. EDUCATION: LIBRARY (EDLIB)

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

title: Selection and Management of Audiovisual Equipment
description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment and related devices. Preparation of bid specifications.

title: School Media Center and Library Administration
description: Principles of planning, organizing, supervising, and evaluating schoolmediacenter and public library services. Includes originating model program plans.

title: Technical Processing: Cataloging and Classification
description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of book, audiovisual, computer, and other materials by using the Dewey Decimal Classification and constructing a library catalog. Working knowledge of OCLC terminal for searching, input, and manipulation of cataloging data.

title: Technical Processing: Online and Automation
description: Practice in cataloging and organizating materials of all types. Study of principles of online systems and microcomputerbased technical processing.

title: Media Design and Production
description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work concerning production of materials and maintenance of audiovisual equipment. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Media Practicum
description: Supervised field experience for students in school media centers or libraries. Prerequisite: EDLIB 280 and approval of the program coordinator or the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Microcomputers and Library Automation
description: An introduction to microcomputers and information systems in library automation.

title: Online Information Retrieval Techniques
description: An overview of online information services and principles of information retrieval. Students develop search strategies to meet clients' information needs and conduct online searches in a supervised laboratory.

title: Methods and Materials for School Library Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching skills necessary for successful completion of assignments using resources of school library media centers and libraries.

title: Selection of Audiovisual Materials and Microcomputer Software
description: Selection and evaluation of audiovisual materials and microcomputer software for instructional and management use in libraries. Systematic identification of sources and selection tools. Practice in selection and evaluation.

title: Production of Audiovisual Media
description: A project course that meets the individual needs of undergraduate students in the production of such instructional media as 8- and 16-mm films, filmstrips, slide sets, and tape recordings.

title: Selection of Library Materials
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection of library materials. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials for public, academic, and school libraries.

title: Materials for Children
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for young adult programs. EDUCATION: READING SECONDARY (EDRDS)

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: Practical procedures for developing effective reading skills to be applied by all secondary classroom teachers. Focuses on relationships between the process of reading and learning of content, on planning to meet the total range of student reading needs, and on methods and materials to enhance comprehension and study skills in all areas of secondary school curriculum. Lab included. EDUCATION: SECONDARY (EDSEC)

title: Basic Concepts of Secondary Education
description: Using classroom investigation and practical field experiences, examines the structure, function, and development of secondary education in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about preparing for and functioning in teaching careers by studying professionalism, job requirements, employment opportunities, secondary school curricula, and the role of secondary education within the entire educational process.

title: Introduction to Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Introduces prospective teachers to responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 206 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intermediate Cross-Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Advanced study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, supporting personnel, and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDSEC 200.

title: Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Secondary Schools
description: Analyzes conditions that influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Particular emphasis is on the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in the American secondary schools. Lab included.

title: Advanced Study of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior
description: Focuses on indepth analyses of many of the concepts introduced in EDSEC 205. Particular emphasis is on variables that contribute to the development and maintenance of prejudice, stereotypes, racism, and oppressive conditions. Equal emphasis will be given to instructional strategies for combating such behaviors. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Laboratory Experience in Secondary Education
description: Provides direct experiences in working with students, teachers, paraprofessionals, community agencies, and other appropriate assignments for undergraduate students who plan to enter secondary school teaching. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Microcomputers in the Secondary School
description: Provides a basic understanding of the functions and applications of microcomputers in the classroom setting. Topics include evaluation and use of available software, introduction to the development of teachermade software, and the availability and selection of hardware.

title: Secondary School
description: Inducts students into the teaching act. Includes development of specific technical skills, study of principles of teaching and evaluation, use of instructional media equipment, curriculum development and organization, and classroom management. Intensive inschool assignments, observation skills, participation, and direct contact with adolescents are required. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205; EDPSY 250 or 251; and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290. Parallel: EDJHM 285. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Instructional Strategies in Multicultured Schools
description: Theory and application of special instructional strategies of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms with special emphasis on multicultured educational situations. Prerequisite: EDSEC 205 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intermediate Study of Microcomputers in the Secondary School
description: Designed to help students understand and develop the application of computerassisted instruction to their respective disciplines. Prerequisite: EDGEN 320 for students pursuing the computer endorsement. EDSEC 255 for all others.

title: Independent Study in Secondary Education
description: Independent study and research in secondary education. Topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Problems in Education and Professional Concerns of the Beginning Teacher
description: Opportunity to examine critically and to focus educational experience and knowledge on contemporary and personally significant problems of education. Emphasizes immediate professional concerns of prospective firstyear teachers. Prerequisite: EDSEC 301 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: High School Curriculum
description: General perspectives of curriculum principles, practices, and procedures common to secondary schools. Organizational structures, innovations, and intimate relationships between instruction and curriculum. Concurrently, students will choose areas of concentration or preparation as they relate to the total high school curriculum.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Secondary Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective secondary teachers to cope with discipline problems in all secondary school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures for preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by secondary students and ways to create a positive environment for learning.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for ten weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Secondary, Junior High/Middle, or All-Grade
description: Involves a fullday assignment for either three or six weeks in a public school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDSEC 460, 462 or EDALG 470, 472. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned.

title: General Innovations in Secondary Education
description: Innovative practices will be identified, defined, and analyzed relative to their effect on secondary schools. Creative, innovative instructional approaches will be used. Field trips or visitations to innovative secondary schools will be arranged when practical, and students will concentrate on innovative practices. DEPARTMENT OF SPECIAL EDUCATION J. TEACHING MAJOR IN SPECIAL EDUCATION (ALL-GRADE): HEARING IMPAIRMENTS, 129-131 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS General Studies, 51-53 hours Humanities

title: American Sign Language 1
description: Introduction to sign language systems including fingerspelling and American Sign Language (ASL). Development of receptive and expressive skills in sign language is emphasized.

title: American Sign Language 2
description: Designed to improve conversational skills in American Sign Language to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in educational and other settings. Introduction to issues related to deaf culture. Prerequisite: SNLNG 351 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 3
description: Emphasizes the development of conversational skills in ASL and stresses vocabulary building and interpretation of culturally related cues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 452 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 4
description: Advanced development of ASL fluency in occupational and professional settings. Special emphasis is given to sign dialects and related deaf cultural issues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 453 and permission of the department chairperson. SIGN LANGUAGE INTERPRETATION (SNITP)

title: Interpreting Process: Theories and Practice
description: Discussion of models of interpreting, analysis, and monitoring in both English and ASL. Prerequisite: admission into interpreter training program, SPCED 240 or the equivalent, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 320, 330.

title: Interpreting Practicum
description: Lecture and supervised field experience in a variety of interpreting settings. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Survey of the Interpreting Field
description: Overview of the field of interpreting including observations of working interpreters, discussion of roles and CR HR responsibilities, and the RID Code of Ethics. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305.

title: Interpreting Video Laboratory
description: Observation, simulation, and related practice of interpreting skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Survey of Interpreting Field 2
description: Advanced examination of various interpreter placements including educational, medical, legal, etc. Emphasizes development of specialized vocabularies for placements. Prerequisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310.

title: Interpreting Process: Transliteration
description: Advanced techniques of expressive and receptive interpreting and transliteration. An indepth examination of RID ethics. Includes lecture, discussion, and opportunities for conversing with deaf people. Prerequisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Advanced Interpreting
description: Continuation of SNITP 400 with emphasis on developing fluency in expressive and receptive communication at all levels. Topics include signtovoice and voicetosign interpretation issues and tactics and an analysis of unique problems associated with translation between oral and signbased language systems. Prerequisite: SNITP 400 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Interpreting Internship
description: Intensive field experience with placements in at least two different interpreting settings over a fifteenweek period. Supervision and regular performance feedback and discussion are stressed. Prerequisite: preprofessional checkout and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 440.

title: Professional Seminar
description: Discussion and examination of problems and issues arising during the interpreting internship. Contemporary issues in interpreting will also be presented and discussed. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 420.

title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: An introduction to definitions, characteristics, and educational needs of children who deviate from normality in mental, physical, social, and emotional ways. Examines federal and state legal bases for education of exceptional children.

title: Management Strategies for Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for effective management of the preschool disabled child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or its equivalent.

title: Developmental Methods with Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing the preschool disabled child's cognitive, language, creative, and physical environments. These developmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool disabled children.

title: Practicum—Teaching Young Disabled Children
description: Students work with disabled children in a supervised teaching practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of disabled children. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microcomputers and the Exceptional Learner
description: Introduction to microcomputer applications in special education through orientation to hardware, programming experience, word processing, and special purpose software. Also emphasizes teaching strategies for introducing microcomputers to children in the classroom.

title: History of Education of Deaf Persons and Psychology of Deafness
description: Introduces a comprehensive sociohistorical and contemporary overview of deaf culture and psychoeducational issues in America and Europe.

title: Education of Preschool Hearingand Language-Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Practicum in Special Education
description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Relations and Consulting Skills for Special Educators
description: Examines human relations strategies and skills that will help teachers of exceptional children build trust and understanding with other professionals and parents of the child. Skills are acquired through simulation and practicum modules. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C or permission of the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study
description: Designed to meet the needs of students who wish to conduct independent study, fieldwork, or research in special education. Prerequisite: Permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Legal and Procedural Foundations of Special Education
description: Studies court cases, statelevel legislation, and related historical events that preceded passage of PL 94-142. Covers definitions, procedural requirements, and legal safeguards of PL 94-142 and PL 99-457 as implemented in Indiana Rule S-1. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Principles of Behaviorology in Special Education
description: Intermediatelevel course designed to enable special education professionals to increase their contributions to the field by adding the scientific foundations of behaviorology to their repertoires. Prerequisite: EDPSY 306 or its equivalent.

title: Introduction of Behavior Disorders
description: Introduction to the history of educating children with behavior disorders; the problems of defining, assessing, and treating behavior disorders; and types and causes of disordered behavior. Prerequisite: SPCED 201.

title: Educating Elementary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled elementary school children. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Prerequisite: SPCED 332 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Educating Secondary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled youth. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Prerequisite: SPCED 332, 334, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: Designed for future teachers of disabled or other healthimpaired students. Includes etiology, assessment, and understanding necessary to educate students with physical disabilities. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Introduction to Mild Disabilities
description: Studies psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to mild disabilities. Compares and differentiates historical and contemporary definitions of mental retardation and learning disabilities. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 301, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Persons with Mental Retardation
description: Studies various types and degrees of retardation; the psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to retardation. Emphasizes etiology, assessment, and issues. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; BIO 453; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Developmental Language Skills for Persons with Mild Disabilities
description: Compares and contrasts the language development of exceptional children with that of nondisabled children. Language difficulties are viewed as they relate to the teaching of listening skills, oral expression, written expression, and reading and other academic subjects. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; SPAA 270.

title: Assessment in Special Education
description: Educational assessment practices with exceptional children with emphasis on curriculumbased assessment and informal tests. Role of the special educator on the multidisciplinary evaluation team. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 371; EDPSY 345.

title: Methods of Teaching the Mildly Disabled
description: Studies techniques of teaching children and adults with mild disabilities. Emphasis is placed on the process by which content is taught to students of all age levels within the least restrictive environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 301, 371, 375; MATHS 391 or 392; EDRDG 400.

title: Educating Persons with Severe Disabilities
description: Studies persons with moderate, severe, or profound mental retardation, orthopedic or other health impairments, or autism. Topics include assessment strategies, instructional planning, and research on education in the least restrictive environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Educational Methods for Persons with Physical and Multiple Disabilities
description: Examines environmental adaptations, curriculum, and teaching and management methods for the instruction of persons with orthopedic impairments or special health problems. Emphasizes multidisciplinary practices and procedures based on research in education and allied fields. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378.

title: Educating Youth and Adults with Severe Disabilities
description: Introduction to the concept of lifelong educational needs of persons with severe disabilities. Topics include career education, vocational and employment programming, transition from school to work, and other educational issues for youth and adults. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378, 379; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assessment of the Young Disabled Child
description: Procedures for assessing young children with disabilities, infancy through age six. Use of observational techniques and formal and informal assessment methodology will be investigated.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of psychological characteristics and educational needs of gifted and talented children in the schools. Definitions of giftedness and identification procedures are studied; review of current and past practices in the field.

title: Speech Development for Deaf Persons
description: Historical and current views of teaching speech to deaf children are studied with emphasis on current methods. Includes the knowledge foundation and practical methodology for teaching spoken English to deaf children. Writing behavioral objectives and an Individual Education Plan for spoken English is also included. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SPCH 216 or SPAA 201.

title: Practicum in Speech for Deaf Persons
description: Includes work with deaf children from different age ranges. Participants will practice planning, writing, and implementing relevant behavioral objectives. Prerequisite: SPCED 446.

title: Introduction to Language for Deaf Persons
description: Philosophy underlying various methods of language will be reviewed. Participants will compare and contrast various aspects of communication strategies. Topics include interactive language, written language, and reading. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SPAA 270.

title: Language Methods for Deaf Persons
description: Indepth view of various approaches to teaching language to deaf children. Emphasizes analyzing language samples taken from deaf children and forming taxonomies from the analysis. Includes writing behavioral objectives in the language areas of form, content, and use for inclusion in Individual Educational Plans. Prerequisite: SPCED 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to Deaf Persons
description: Explores various approaches to teaching reading and applies them to reading instruction for deaf children. Reviews reading assessment for deaf children as well as reading in other school subjects. Writing behavioral objectives and Individual Education Plans is included. Prerequisite: SPCED 454; EDRDG 400

title: Student Teaching: Hearing Impaired
description: Required preservice teaching practica for students seeking licensure in special education hearingimpaired. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Special class organization, instructional materials, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally disabled. Using the Individualized Education Plan (IEP) and mainstreaming are incorporated. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 (1 hr), 372; EDRDG 430; and MATHS 391.

title: Diagnostic and Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Disabled
description: Continuation of methods and materials for the mildly handicapped, begun in SPCED 474, with emphasis on use of the diagnosticprescriptive model to determine the learner's special needs and prescription of required curricular modifications in the IEP. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 474, or 376.

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 9 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Student Teaching: Mild Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: mild disabilities. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Physically/ Multiply Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: physically/multiply handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Seriously Emotionally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: seriously emotionally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Severe Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: moderately mentally disabled, severely/profoundly mentally disabled, and multiply disabled. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching in Special Education 2
description: Continuation of SPCED 488, 489, 490, 491 or 492 in a different instructional placement. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: either SPCED 488, 489, 490, 491 or 492. Weber Burris School is a laboratory school in which preservice and inservice teachers can observe education practices; prospective teachers can have experience working with young people before student teaching; and teachers can develop, study, and test ideas and methods for improving education. The school publicizes its findings and offers consulting and leadership services for public schools. Burris School enrolls students in kindergarten through the twelfth grade. Nemitz The Indiana Academy for Science, Mathematics, and Humanities is a residential school for three hundred of Indiana's most academically gifted high school juniors and seniors. In addition to core courses required for all students, the exploratory curriculum gives students the opportunity to sample advanced courses from the university's curriculum and to pursue individualized research and experiential education opportunities in cooperation with businesses, university faculty members, and practicing professionals. Students are also required to donate time to both academy and community service. The academy also offers opportunities for outstanding educators from throughout Indiana to teach and study at the academy for a semester or a year. An interactive telecommunications system delivers selected academy classes to gifted pupils in other schools. Academy faculty members will develop and distribute curriculum materials for the gifted and organize regular workshops for teachers of the gifted. Academic year and summer residential workshops are conducted at the academy for Indiana classroom teachers from throughout the state. description: Survey of American studies as a field and as an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American civilization. Methods and theories of American studies will be discussed, along with major themes and topics in American life and thought. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 101.

title: Reading and Independent Study
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor who has expertise in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the American Studies director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Selected Topics in American Studies
description: Survey and investigation of a specific topic, issue, or problem in American studies. Particular subject matter will be announced before each offering. title: Contemporary Europe
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to historical, geographical, political, social, economic, and cultural features of Europe. Current issues such as integration prospects, ethnic conflict, and environmental problems will also be examined.

title: European Women Writers
description: Readings in English translation of selected works of major twentiethcentury women writers in European languages. Topics and works may vary. May not be applied to foreign language majors or minors. Not open to students who have credit in FL 307.

title: European Culture through Films
description: Study of the cultures of European countries through the medium of films. Topics and films may vary. May not be applied to foreign language majors or minors. Not open to students who have credit in FL 308.

title: Geography of Central Europe
description: Treats the spatial aspects of the physical and human environments of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia and Yugoslavia. Attention is given to physiographic, climatological, ethnocultural, political, and economic development processes. Not open to students who have credit in GEOG 357.

title: Professional Experience
description: Involves assigned duties in an organization, agency, corporation, or business dealing with European affairs, with appropriate monetary compensation. Prerequisite: permission of the program director. Not open to students who have credit in EURO 479.

title: Politics of the European Union
description: Study of the development of the European Union as an evolving political entity—its politics, institutions, policies—and the prospects for European unification. Not open to students who have credit in POLS 385.

title: Politics of Russia and the Successor ' States
description: Evaluation of political, economic, and social change and performance in Russia and other successor states of the former Soviet Union. Historical and geographical details are also treated. Not open to students who have credit in POLS 386. Gerontology 39

title: Strategy and Diplomacy of the European Great Powers Since 1860
description: Examines, interprets, and evaluates British, German, Russian, French, Italian and Austrian strategy and diplomacy— economic, geographic, ideological, and military foundations of national power—focusing upon the "German Question," Eurocentrism, imperialism, two world wars, renewed multipolarity, the European Community, and the Cold War. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 458.

title: Seminar in European Community Marketing
description: Examines the effect of the Single European Market—political and economic integration of and removal of trade barriers in Europe—on the marketing strategies of American and European firms. Recommended for honors students. Prerequisite: MKG 300; senior standing; or permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in MKG 472.

description: Involves assigned duties in an organization, agency, corporation, or business dealing with European affairs, without monetary compensation. Wittig The mission of the Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is to prepare diverse students to be uniquely qualified and committed to improving the quality of life for individuals, families, communities, and the environment in which they function. Further, the mission is to empower individuals and families across the life span to manage the challenges of living and working in a diverse, global society. This is accomplished through the integration and application of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviors from family and consumer sciences as well as a variety of other disciplines. Specializations include apparel design, dietetics, fashion merchandising, food management, housing and home furnishings, and education. Programs continue to evolve to meet the needs of a changing society. The dietetics and dietetic technology programs are approved by the American Dietetics Association.
