title: Introduction to Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Career opportunities available in the profession of family and consumer sciences; introduction to Ball State programs, facilities, staff; development as a profession. Open only to family and consumer sciences majors and minors.

title: Internship in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Gives the opportunity to work in established internship settings to gain professional experience in specific areas of study. Prerequisite: permission of the de artment chairperson. en only to departmental majors; will be substituted for required practicum with permission of the program directors.

title: Field Studies in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Combines reading knowledge with field experiences in which special topics in family and consumer sciences are studied in a particular location. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of family and consumer sciencesrelated work chosen. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Workshop: Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Activity oriented study of one topic in family and consumer sciences. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Investigation and exploration of a topic in family and consumer sciences. Emphasizes extensive reading and the development of research skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Presentations and discussions on selected topics of current interest in family and consumer sciences. Each seminar focuses on a different topic. Prerequisite: junior or senior standing; permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Professional Development in Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Examines the skills needed in getting a job, emphasizing résumé writing, interviewing, and dress. Explores such topics as adjusting, succeeding, and growing as a professional in a global society. Prerequisite: senior standing. FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES: EDUCATION (FCSED)

title: Principles and Philosophy of Vocational Education
description: Applies the principles and philosophies of vocational education to program organization, content area, teacher qualifications, leadership preparation, curriculum design, and image.

title: Presentation Techniques for Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Analysis of audience and business needs and the development of presentations and projects to meet these needs. Includes selection and use of presentation methods, development and use of devices, and professional roles and expectations. Not open to teaching majors in vocational family and consumer sciences.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Family and Consumer Sciences
description: Organization of teaching units and lesson plans; selection and use of teaching methods and materials. Prerequisite: identification t_ o pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Practicum in Family and Consumer Sciences Education
description: Individual or group studies and experiences. Experience with professional standards, regulations, and supervision in the type of family and consumer sciences related work chosen. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Implementation of Vocational Education Programs
description: Emphasis on techniques for implementing vocational education programs, including applications to management, public relations, and professionalism in vocational home economics. Prerequisite: FCSED 392, 395.

title: Coordination of Cooperative Programs in Vocational Education
description: Coordination of class instruction and work experience. Includes recruiting, selecting, supervising, and evaluating students; selecting training stations; working with an advisory committee; role of coordinator; techniques and legal concerns of coordination; and placement and followup of graduates. Prerequisite: FCSED 392, 395. FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES: FOOD AND NUTRITION (FCSFN)

title: Introduction to the Foodservice Industry
description: An overview of the food management profession. An indepth analysis of the academic preparation required, identification with the role of the food manager and multiple career options in hospitality and health care.

title: Principles of Food Preparation and Food Science
description: Introduces the principles of food preparation and food science. Correct techniques and methods of food preparation are stressed.

title: Customer Relations for Service Industries
description: Preparation to provide and train subordinates to render effective service to both internal and external customers in service industries. Open to all students.

title: Meal Management
description: Fundamentals of planning, preparing, and serving nutritionally adequate, appetizing, and aesthetically pleasing meals, with emphasis on resource management. Attention given to foods and types of table service suitable for various occasions. Introducing the use of computers in foodservice. Prerequisite: FCSFN 110.

title: Nutrition for Educators
description: General principles of nutrition as related to growth, development and health of the infant, child, adolescent, and adult. Classroom application and integration of strategies. Notopen to students who have credit in FCSFN 340.

title: Practicum in Food Service Planning, Layout and Equipment
description: Designing and equipping food facilities for schools, colleges, hospitals, industry, and commercial operations. Experience in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of qualified food production personnel.

title: Practicum in Institutional Administration
description: Emphasizes organizational structure, scientific management, and personnel administration. Experience in quantity foodproduction kitchens under supervision of qualified food production personnel.

title: Personal Nutrition
description: Emphasizes the principles of nutrition and their application to daily living. The relationship between diet and health, the role of nutrition in reducing individual health risk, and contemporary issues in nutrition will be discussed. Not open to students who have credit in FCSFN 340

title: Sanitation and Employee Training
description: Selected experiences and supervised practice related to sanitation, safety, and employee training. Become eligible to write the National Restaurant Association Sanitation certification examination. Prerequisite: FCSFN 220.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Purchasing Supervised Field Experience
description: Selected experiences related to menu planning and purchasing in a variety of quantity foodservice organizations. Experience with professional standards and supervision. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Cost Control in Foodservice
description: Controlling cost from a management perspective in a foodservice operation. Prerequisite or parallel: ACC 201.

title: Principles of Human Nutrition
description: Addresses the principles of nutrition, life cycle nutrition, and the relationship of diet to health and disease. Prerequisite or parallel: CHEM 100 or 101 or 111 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Therapeutic Dietetics
description: Dietary modifications needed by people with certain disease conditions. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340; permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: FCSFN 370. Not open to students who have credit in FCSFN 446.

title: Normal and Therapeutic Nutrition and Supervised Field Experience
description: Experience with professional standards and supervision related to normal and therapeutic nutrition in community and longterm care settings. Prerequisite: FCSFN 342, 370; permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in FCSFN 446.

title: Community Nutrition
description: Community nutrition programs and problems at the local, state, national, and international levels, related to special populations, including various stages of the life cycle. Observation of and participation in local nutrition programs. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340.

title: Nutritional Management of Disease
description: Physiological basis for nutritional management of patients who have needs related to diabetes, cardiovascular disease, hemodialysis, nutrition support, inborn errors of metabolism, and metabolic stress. Documentation of nutrition care, quality assurance and nutrition counseling emphasized. Prerequisite: FCSFN 343; permission of the department chairperson. Not open to students who have credit in FCSFN 446. Open only to dietetic technology students.

title: Institutional Administration
description: A systems approach to management theories, concepts, and functions of integrated healthcare and hospitality foodservice operations. Emphasizes effective human resources management and fiscal responsibility.

title: Quantity Menu Planning and Food Purchasing
description: Information needed by quantity food buyers and important concepts in purchasing foods. Emphasizes menu planning with consideration given to meeting nutritional needs and consumer satisfaction. Prerequisite: FCSFN 220, 275 or 340.

title: Nutrition Counseling
description: Integrates nutrition knowledge and techniques of nutrition counseling. Introduction to information gathering, assessment of problems, development of methods, and materials for nutrition counseling intervention. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340.

title: Nutrition Assessment, Counseling and Education
description: Assessment methods, techniques of nutrition counseling, education principles and implementation, development of counseling materials. Includes assessment of various populations and counseling experiences. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340.

title: Quantity Food Production
description: Issues involved in quantity food production, distribution and storage, and service. Covers principles and processes of quantity food production and equipment use. Laboratory experiences in the Allegre restaurant and thequantity foods laboratory. Prerequisite: FCSFN 364.

title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental studies of foods in relation to their composition, physical and chemicalproperties, and circumstances affecting food quality. Investigates recipes and develops and evaluates methods of combining ingredients. Prerequisite: FCSFN 110.

title: Professional Development in Dietetics
description: Topics dealing with the profession of dietetics; roles and responsibilities of dietetic practitioners; professional standards and code of ethics; legislative issues related to health care; career and professional education opportunities and marketing of dietetic service.

title: Nutrition, Weight Control, and Exercise
description: Designed for students in dietetics, physical education and healthrelated fields. Information and experience for students preparing to provide nutrition counseling to people in weightcontrol and exercisetraining programs. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Nutrition
description: Emphasizes the use and metabolism of nutrients at the cellular level in the human body. Significance and interpretation of current research in the field is discussed. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340; CHEM 360; senior standing.

title: Clinical Nutrition
description: Medical nutritional therapy principles and intervention strategies for atrisk populations. Includes clinical experiences. Prerequisite: FCSFN 475, 445, senior standing.

title: Computer Applications in Nutrition and Food Systems Management
description: Emphasizes applications of computer use in dietetics and food management. Software, including spreadsheet, database, graphics, word processing, and internetting is employed. Selection and application of software specific to dietetics and food management included.

title: Catering for Profit
description: Fundamentals of planning, organizing, preparing, and serving profitable and unique catering functions. Emphasizes menu development, customer service, marketing and food production. Prerequisite: FCSFN 220. Not open to students who have credit in FCSFN 446.

title: Nutrition Counseling Practicum
description: Provide nutrition counseling for pregnant women, families with infants, young and teenage children, and people seeking guidance for weight control and special problems, supervised by a member of the American Dietetic Association. Prerequisite: FCSFN 340, 370 or 375; permission of the instructor. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Food Service Management Practicum
description: Experience in a food service organization, either in the private or public sector. Emphasizes development of food management expertise. Practicum approved and supervised by the Department of Family and Consumer Sciences. Prerequisite: FCSFN 364, 400; senior standing permission of the department chairperson; documented completion of at least 500 hours of appropriate foodservice experience.

title: Seminar in Foods and Nutrition
description: Presentations and discussions on specific topics of current interest in foods and nutrition. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term. FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES: HUMAN SERVICES (FCSHS)

title: Family Wellness
description: Investigates the physical, mental, and social aspects of wellness, focusing on the interaction of these with the individual, family, and community.

title: Infant Development
description: Growth and development from conception through the second year of life. Includes physical, social, emotional, and cognitive development. Students observe and interact with infants and toddlers. Open to all students.

title: Life Management
description: Management of family and community resources to achieve desiredgoals in the family. Practical application of management principles to daily ex erience. en to all students.

title: Energy and Equipment in the Home
description: Selection, use, and care of household equipment. Current legislation, methods of conservation, energy concerns and cost. Emphasis on the role of technological developments in the home. Development and evaluation of presentation techniques.

title: Advanced Life Management
description: Practical application of the principles of life management. Emphasis on stress, management, effective communication, and application of principles in relation to specific resources. Prerequisite: FCSFN 220. Prerequisite or parallel: FCSHS 340.

title: Consumer Education
description: Economic considerations of purchasing for consumers, including current consumer legislation, marketing conditions, influence of advertising, consumer credit, agencies that protect consumers, and points to consider when bu ing consumer goods and services. en to all students.

title: Marriage
description: The dynamics of the marital relationship and the changes influencing marriages today. Emphasizes the individual and marriage, dating, mate selection, marital communication, sexual adjustment, choosing parenthood, marriage dissolution, and marital growth. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Family Relations
description: Dynamics of family relationships and changes influencing family life and structure. Emphasizes marriage, family life cycle, family problems, parent education, family enrichment. Open to juniors and seniors or by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Functional Home Design Practicum
description: Gives the student onthejob work experience with professional supervision in functional home design. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Family Relations
description: History and recent trends and developments in familylife education, career opportunities involved in familylife education, professional organizations, and ethical standards. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson and junior or senior standing. FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES: MERCHANDISING (FCSMR)

title: Dimensions of Clothing
description: Analysis of dress and adornment emphasizing dimensions that affect the design, production and end use of textiles and clothing.

title: Fundamentals of Apparel Construction
description: Basic knowledge of garment construction, clothing selection, and art principles as applied to clothing. Prerequisite: FCSMR 101.

title: Merchandising Mathematics
description: Study of fundamental quantitative issues related to fashion merchandising and retail management. Covers basic mathematical computation used in the retail and wholesale markets.

title: Consumer Housing
description: Selection of housing to meet family needs. Evaluation of house plans for convenience, aesthetic qualities, activities, and furnishings. Legal and financial aspects of home ownership. Open to all students.

title: Interior Design and Furnishings
description: Selection and arrangement of home furnishings to create attractive, functional interiors that are in harmony with the exterior. Prerequisite: FCSMR 200; ITEDU 154.

title: Textiles for Apparel
description: Study of textiles and their components (fiber, yarn, fabric, and finishes) as they relate to care, performance, quality, and customer satisfaction. Required for merchandising majors. Prerequisite: CHEM 100 or permission of the instructor. Not open to students who have credit FCSMR 250.

title: Textiles for Interiors
description: Study of the care, performance, quality, and customer satisfaction of textiles for interiors. Required for merchandising majors with a housing/home furnishings emphasis. Prerequisite: CHEM 100 or permission of the instructor. Not open to students who have credit in FCSMR 230.

title: Evolution of Costume
description: A study of Western costume from its beginning to the present. Emphasis on motivating influences of each period as well as on the costume itself. Prerequisite: FCSMR 230; CHEM 100 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: The Fashion Industry
description: A survey of the business of fashion through design, manufacture, distribution, and promotion. Explores career possibilities. Open to all students.

title: Apparel Design by the Flat Pattern Method
description: Adapting standard patterns to individual proportions, designing garments, and creating an original garment by the flat pattern method. Use of computeraided design to produce pattern for original garment. Prerequisite: FCSMR 102.

title: Tailoring
description: Selection and construction of tailored garments and advanced clothing problems. Prerequisite: FCSMR 102.

title: Apparel Design by the Draping Method
description: Provides basic knowledge of apparel design using the draping method. Prerequisite: FCSMR 300.

title: Three Dimensional Graphics
description: Three dimensional visualization of design concepts using oneand twopoint perspectives, quick sketch techniques, and a variety of media to communicate interior design ideas. Prerequisite: FCSMR 210.

title: Advanced Interior Design and Furnishings
description: Integration of design and furnishings and their application to interiors. Technical presentations based on specialized problems of designing and planning interiors. Prerequisite: FCSMR 210, 250; ITDPT 213.

title: Visual Merchandising
description: Study of the relationship between visual merchandise presentations and sales promotion in fashion retailing and wholesaling. Basic principles of art design, as applied to merchandise display, are examined.

title: Fashion Product Analysis
description: Study of factors which contribute to the quality of fashionrelated merchandise. Provides an opportunity to become skillful in evaluating the materials, workmanship and construction techniques used in the textile and apparel industry. Prerequisite: FCSMR 102, 230, 270.

title: Study of Fashion Designers and Forecasting
description: Study of present and historical fashion designers from around the world. Emphasis will be placed on understanding their contributions to the fashion industry and their influence in today's fashion markets. Prerequisite: FCSMR 270.

title: Fashion Buying and Merchandising
description: Gives potential retailers the knowledge base to make decisions on buying and merchandising to satisfy customers and maintain an adequate profit level. Prerequisite: FCSMR 170, 270.

title: Fashion Illustration
description: Provides basic knowledge of drawing of the fashion figure and of fashion illustration.

title: Computer-Aided Design for Apparel
description: Basic knowledge of the use of Computer- Aided Design in fashion apparel designing. Prerequisite: FCSMR 300, 380.

title: Computer-Aided Design for Interiors
description: Computer application in interior design emphasizing computeraided design and drafting. Prerequisite: FCSMR 310; senior standing.

title: Evolution of Interiors

description: Exploration and integration of concepts related to the various elements of merchandising. Wright (George and Frances Ball Distinguished Professor of Industry and Technology) Preparing students for challenging careers in industry and teaching is the major focus of the Department of Industry and Technology. Bachelor's degree programs in manufacturing engineering technology, industrial technology, graphic arts management, technology teacher education, and vocational teacher education prepare students for a broad range of such careers. Associate degree programs in manufacturing technology, printing technology, and industrial supervision offer students the opportunity to acquire solid technical and supervisory preparation for many types of careers. Credits earned in associate degree programs will transfer to related bachelor's degree programs in the department. Cooperative work experience and internships are optional in the technology and graphic arts programs and are arranged in a wide variety of industries for students seeking firsthand experience in the daytoday operations of contemporary industries. Qualified students enrolled in bachelor's degree programs in industry and technology may choose cooperative education programs after completing their freshman year of study. Students arrange coop jobs through the cooperative education coordinator. The manufacturing engineering technology program is accredited by the Technology Accreditation Commission of the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET). The teaching major in technology education program is accredited by the National Council for Accreditation of Teacher Education (NCATE). The department's curricular coordinators will assist students in selecting appropriate majors, minors, endorsements, courses, and provide career counseling. An exit assessment must be completed by all majors in the department. Graduates of the program accept jobs as computeraided drafting technicians, manufacturing technicians, production planners, and technical representatives. The program is designed for people who are currently employed as well as people desiring employment in technical positions in manufacturing. Graduates of this program may transfer to the baccalaureate program in Manufacturing Engineering Technology with little or no loss of credit. title: Photography

description: Applied fundamentals of dynamic forces, including displacement, velocities, accelerations, work energy, power, impulse, momentum, and impact. Prerequisite: PUMET 111; MATHS 161.

description: Applies theories and methods developed in statics, dynamics, and strength of materials to the selection of basic machine components. Develops the fundamental principles required for the selection of the elements of which a machine is composed. Prerequisite: PUMET 211, 213.

description: Principles of thermodynamics and fluid dynamics as applied to the conservation laws of mass and energy, prime movers, and power cycles. Prerequisite: MATHS 161; PUMET 160.

title: Fluid Power
description: A study of compressible and incompressible fluid statics and dynamics as applied to industrial hydraulic and pneumatic circuit and controls. Prerequisite: MATHS 161.

description: Manufacturing processes and tools used by industry to convert bars, forgings, castings, plate, and sheet materials into finished products. Includes basic mechanics of materials removal and forming, measuring, quality control, and safety of operations Prerequisite: PUMET 141.

General Information • Admission to Ball State University does not guarantee admission to the baccalaureate nursing program (also called the major in nursing or the clinical nursing major) in the School of Nursing. The School of Nursing designates the number of students admitted to the baccalaureate nursing program on a term by term basis. Space is limited and there typically is not enough space for every applicant who meets the minimum requirements. • Applicants with a record of substance abuse or conviction of violations of federal, state, or local laws related to controlled substances for any offense (misdemeanor or felony) should know they may not be eligible for licensure as a registered nurse. • Applicants who have met the prerequisite course requirements and have earned the highest GPA stand the best chance of being admitted to the program. Students who have achieved the minimum GPA required to apply for admittance to the program should understand they may not be selected for admission due to their GPA rank. • There are two ways to attempt to earn admission to the baccalaureate nursing program, Prenursing and General Applicant. The Prenursing route (which might be described as "early" admission) is an option only for students who meet certain criteria which are outlined as the Prenursing Pool. Space available in the Prenursing Pool is extremely limited so admission is highly competitive. The General Applicant route is for other students, including transfer students, competing for the remaining open slots in the baccalaureate nursing program in a given semester. • Admission to the first nursing course requires the signing of an informed consent related to risks and safeguards inherent in the study of clinical nursing. ADMISSION Prenursing Pool Students in the Prenursing Pool are guaranteed placement in the baccalaureate nursing major during the assigned semester. They must meet certain criteria to be eligible to be admitted. If admitted students meet the criteria to remain in the Prenursing Pool, and complete (at the specified time) an application to enter the baccalaureate program they will have priority placement in the baccalaureate nursing major. title: Canoeing and Sailing
description: Introduction to movement control of the canoe and sailboat, including skill techniques, environmental and safety factors of canoeing and sailing small craft. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Developmental Aquatics for Preschoolers
description: Through lecture and pool laboratory experience, provides a model for aquatic instruction with a motor development basis for preschool children.

title: Aquatic Sports Officiating
description: An introduction to the theory and practice of officiating selected sport activities.

title: Basic Scuba
description: Beginning scuba composed of lecture sessions, confined water (pool) and open water sessions. Provides a level of understanding to participate in skin and scuba diving activities safely. Special fee required. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Silver Star Advanced Diver and Scuba Lifesaving/Accident Management
description: Series of open water dives and lectures on advanced diving and lifesaving subjects. Two certifications can be earned. Prerequisite: PEP 220 or basic level certification with permission of the instructor.

title: YMCA Assistant Instructor
description: Provides knowledge and practical experience needed to teach YMCA scuba while working with a YMCA instructor. Includes experience in classroom, pool, and open water activities. Prerequisite: PEP 221.

title: YMCA Silver Star and SLAM Instructor
description: Provides experience and knowledge necessary to teach YMCA scuba as an instructor. Scuba lifesaving and accident management instructor received as dual certifications. Prerequisite: PEP 224.

title: Introduction to Adapted Physical Education
description: Basic knowledge of disabilities that affect physical education. Emphasizes referral, placement, and programming in physical education; federal and state laws thatpertain to the education and physical education of special populations. Students are required to participate in field experiences.

title: Principles and Philosophies of Coaching Sports
description: Considers the principles and philosophies underlying coaching in scholastic athletic programs.

title: Coaching Observation
description: Guided observation of coaching techniques and practices with analysis of teaching and coaching philosophies for competitive sports in schools. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Practicum in Aquatics
description: Administrative and teaching experience at Ball State University or another approved aquatic program. Prerequisite: PEP 315 or 353, permission of coordinator of aquatics programs.

title: Dance Composition 1
description: Principal elements of dance composition. Simple compositional forms for small groups and solo work. Prerequisite: PEP 107, 115.

title: Practicum in Adaptive Physical Education 1: Survey/Introduction
description: Provides an overview of practicum opportunities both on and off campus related to working with students with disabilities in a physical education/ exercise setting. Will rotate approximately every five weeks across three practicum settings.

title: Motor Development of Young Children
description: Human motor development theory and practice for early childhood and primary school children, emphasizing behaviors related to nonlocomotor, locomotor, transitory, and manipulatory motor patterns as they emerge and become controlled, using task analysis, assessment, program planning, physical activities, and evaluation. Prerequisite: PEP 154 for teaching majors in physical education. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Anatomy
description: Introduction to human anatomy. Provides basic knowledge upon which physiological biomechanical concepts can be built.

title: Physiology
description: Introduction to human physiology. Emphasizes the organization, function, and control of the organs and systems of the body. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Kinesiology
description: The anatomical and mechanical principles of human motion. Development of the ability to analyze movement mechanically and anatomically. Prerequisite: PEP 292 and General Studies mathematics requirement.

title: First Aid
description: First aid, CPR, and Bloodborne Pathogens Training and certification as outlined by nationally recognized agencies. Designed for majors or minors in the School of Physical Education. Not open to students who have credit in HSC 250. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: The Law and Sport Administration
description: Essential elements of administrative law, arbitration, antitrust law, collective bargaining, constitutional law, contract law, labor law, and tort law. Major emphasis is on their effect on sport. Prerequisite: BL 260 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Instructor of CPR and First Aid
description: Emphasizes teaching methodologies and delivery of nationally recognized programs in first aid, CPR, and bloodbornpathogens. Instructor certification available. Prerequisite: PEP 299 or current basic level first aid and CPR certification.

title: Marketing, Promotions, and Fund Raising in Sport Administration
description: Study of the characteristics of sport . Physical Education 91 marketing, promotional planning, and fund raising. Focuses on the planning processes involved in marketing and promotions and establishes guidelines and strategies for fund raising. Prerequisite: MKG 300 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Business and Finance in Sport Administration
description: Investigation of the business and financial aspects of intercollegiate, interscholastic, and professional sport. Emphasis is on the elements of business that directly affect budgetary and fiscal control of each of the levels of sport. Prerequisite: FIN 350 and permission of the sport studies program director. Open only to sport administration majors.

title: Evaluation in Physical Education
description: Measurement and evaluation in physical education with emphasis on underlying philosophy, tests, construction, and use of test results.

title: Teaching Physical Activity to the Older Adult
description: Designed to teach students to recognize the characteristics of the older adult and to successfully plan, implement, and evaluate a program of physical activity based upon the special needs of the older adult. Prerequisite: PEP 212.

title: Advanced Aquatics for the Physical Educator
description: Swimming and rescue skills necessary to complete certification for nationally recognized instructor program. Emphasizes a broad range of other aquatic experiences and teaching methodologies. Prerequisite: PEP 215.

title: Wellness through Aquatic Exercise
description: Introduction to the objectives, format, and conduct of instructional endurance swimming and water exercise classes, emphasizing participation and application of fitness and related concepts to selected aquatic activities. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Adapted Aquatics
description: Concerned with methodologies used to teach swimming to exceptional persons. Important for aquatics instructors, rehabilitation personnel, prephysical therapy, adapted physical education, exercise science, and athletic training. Concentrates on practical application. Prerequisite: PEP 315 or 353 or permission of the instructor.

title: Assessment in Adapted Physical Education
description: Introduction to appropriate instruments for assessing the motor and fitness needs of disabled people in physical education. Practical experience in administering standardized and normed referenced tests. Students develop IEPs. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or 494.

title: Practicum in Adaptive Physical Education 2: Educational
description: Focuses on an educational setting (communitybased schools). Requires fulfilling a sixteenweek practicum assignment under the supervision of an adapted physical educator. Involvement with lessonplans, program development, and evaluation. Prerequisite: PEP 288.

title: Program Development/Fitness Assessment for People with Disabilities
description: Designed to provide, in a clinical setting, learning experience associated with fitness assessment, program development and implementation for people with disabilities. Recommended for exercise science, athletic training, and prephysical therapy majors. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the instructor.

title: Organization and Planning for Coaching Sports
description: Designed to introduce procedures involved in the organization, training, and planning of team and individual sports at the scholastic level. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Physical Therapy Kinesiology
description: The mechanics of motion as applied to the human body. Development of the ability to analyze "normal" motor performance. Prerequisite: PHYCS 110, 112; ANAT 330, 405.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: Introduction to the prevention, recognition, evaluation, treatment, and rehabilitation of common athletic injuries. Essential information concerning the nutritional, psychological, and legal aspects of athletic health care is also presented. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Parallel: PEP 341.

title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries Laboratory
description: Application of a variety of commercial protective equipment and taping, padding, and wrapping techniques consistent with anatomical and biomechanical principles. Emphasizes the prevention of sport and exercise injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Prerequisite or parallel: PEP 340.

title: Sports Information
description: Designed primarily for sports information students. Develops students' knowledge and background in the terminology, strategy, scoring, and officiating of a variety of sports. Not open to physical education majors.

title: Teaching and Coaching Water Polo and Synchro
description: Introduces the rules, necessary equipment, skills, and drills to teach and coach water polo successfully. Also introduces basic body positions, swimming strokes, and stroke variations, sculls for propulsion and support and figures and hybrid figures in shallow and deep water. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel swimming skill test.

title: Teaching and Coaching Springboard Diving
description: Introduction to teaching progressions of dives from one and three meter springboards and basic platform diving. Developed for the novice teacher, coach, or performer. Includes forward and back dives, reverse and inward dives, and twist and somersault dives. Emphasizes fundamentals and flexibility of teaching method. The degree of difficulty increases progressively as ability increases. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel skill test.

title: Teaching and Coaching Swimming
description: Learning theories, teaching strategies, and physical laws that affect learning and performance in the water. Emphasizes analysis and technique.

title: Swimming Instructor
description: Preparation to teach others how to swim. Emphasizes methodology for teaching beginners through skilled swimmers. Aquatic leadership for the pool, beach, camp, or school setting is also stressed. Prerequisite: successful completion of entrylevel swim test.

title: Internship in Aquatics
description: Permits credit for aquatic experiences in categories of leadership, administration, or operation of aquatic programs or facilities. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching and Coaching Gymnastics
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Wrestling
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Dance for Children
description: Basic rhythms, exploration of movement, and creative dance for the early grades of the elementary school.

title: Accompaniment for Modern Dance
description: Exploration and use of accompaniment in modern dance. Prerequisite: PEP 107, 115.

title: Lower Extremity Injury Evaluation in Athletic Training
description: Procedures and techniques for recognition and evaluation of athletic injuries to the lower extremities. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper methods and techniques in evaluating lower extremity pathologies. Prerequisite: ANAT 201 or PEP 292, permission of the instructor. Prerequisite or parallel: PEP 340. Open only to athletic training majors admitted into the professional preparation program.

title: Upper Extremity Injury Evaluation in Athletic Training
description: Procedures and techniques for recognition and evaluation of athletic injuries that occur to the upper extremities. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper methods and techniques in evaluating upper extremity injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201, permission of the instructor. Prerequisite or'parallel: PEP 340. Open only to athletic training majors admitted to the professional preparation program.

title: Therapeutic Modalities in Athletic Training
description: Examination of the treatment of athletic injuries through the use of cryotherapy, hydrotherapy, and electrotherapy. Indications and contraindications for the use of therapeutic modalities program will be explored. Laboratory experiences emphasize the proper application of therapeutic modalities. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, permission of the instructor. Open only to athletic training majors admitted into the professional preparation program.

title: Therapeutic Exercise and Techniques in Athletic Training
description: Principles and goals of common rehabilitative procedures for athletic injuries. Learn the use of contemporary manual therapy and rehabilitative exercises in a comprehensive rehabilitative program. Laboratory eriences emphasize the proper rehabilitative techniques of common injuries. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, permission of the instructor. Open only to athletic training majors admitted into the professional preparation program.

title: Teaching and Coaching Golf
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Tennis
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Baseball or Softball
description: Offered alternating years as baseball or softball. Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Track and Field
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Football
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Basketball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Volleyball
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Teaching and Coaching Soccer
description: Prerequisite: PEP 331.

title: Advanced Computer and Technology Applications in Physical Education
description: Learning and application of advanced computer and technology skills such as advanced word processing, using the computer for presentations, worldwide communications, and designing interactive programs. Prerequisite: PEP 155 or permission of the director.

title: Motor Learning
description: Introduction to principles related to the teaching, learning, and performance of motor skills. Emphasis on the application of this knowledge to teaching and learning strategies for motorskill acquisition. Designed for undergraduate students who plan to teach motor skills to people in all age ranges.

title: Practicum 1 in Athletic Training
description: Student athletic trainers develop sports medicine knowledge and skills relevant to the allied medical and high school setting. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 371, permission of the instructor. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Neurophysiological Approach to Physical Education for Disabled People
description: Designed to give students an understanding of the theoretical basis of selected neurophysiological programs for treatment of various disabling conditions and to teach students how to administer such programs.

title: Teaching of Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Methods and consideration for teaching physical education in the elementary school that include purpose, growth and development, motor learning, program planning, and evaluation. Prerequisite: PEP 291.

title: Methods/Materials for Teaching Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed to analyze and develop teaching methods that enable the planning, implementation, and evaluation of an array of teaching strategies that would be used in creating a safe environment for a public school physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP activity sequence, preliminary admission to a teaching curriculum, and permission of the program director or designate. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Applied Anatomy in Athletic Training
description: Detailed review of applied human anatomy for athletic training majors. Emphasizes conceptual understanding of the interrelationship of the anatomical structures as they relate to an injury episode. Prerequisite: PEP 292 or ANAT 201. Parallel: PEP 340, 341, 370. Open only to athletic training majors admitted to the professional preparation program.

title: Methods/Materials for Physical Education in the Secondary Schools
description: Designed with both theory and practicum elements. Comprehensive planning instructional design, materials, strategies. Includes management, organization, evaluation, curriculum development. Laboratory experiences emphasized. Prerequisite: PEP 395, junior standing, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Curriculum Design in Physical Education
description: Introduction to curriculum and curriculum design covering all facets of physical education in the public school setting.

title: Seminar
description: Designed to permit sport administration majors to consider current issues and topics in sport. Prerequisite: !permission of the coordinator of sport administration.

title: Instructor of Lifeguarding
description: Concerned with skills pertinent to teaching lifeguarding. All aspects of lifeguarding including techniques for pools and fresh and saltwater beaches. Nationally recognized certification available upon completion. Prerequisite: PEP 216 or current lifeguard certificate.

title: Psychological Dimensions of Coaching
description: Designed for students interested in coaching. Focuses on the dimensions of sport psychology by review and study of pertinent scientific literature, the principles derived from this literature, and theirpractical application.

title: Internship in Exercise Programs for the Older Adult
description: A practical experience in leading physical activities for older adults in healthcare centers, senior citizen centers, retirement centers, or other places where older adults engage in exercise. Prerequisite: PEP 212, 292, 293, 294, 299, 312; HSC 469. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Disability Sport
description: Provides a working knowledge of the official sports organizations recognized by the United States Olympic Committee. Emphasizes classifications, organizational structure, sporting events, coaching athletes with disabilities. Prerequisite: PEP 331 for coaching minors and endorsements; PEP 227 for adapted physical education minors; or permission of the instructor.

title: Coaching Internship
description: Students assist in coaching competitive sports in schools. Includes internship in coaching and indepth classroom discussions centering on selfawareness and the teachingcoaching process. May not be taken at the same time as student teaching. Prerequisite: PEP 231.

title: Athletic Governance
description: Directed mainly toward sportsinformation students. Designed to discuss the various organizations that govern amateur and professional sports in the United States. Emphasis is on the sportsinformation student's role in shaping sports in this country and in international competition. Not recommended for physical education majors and minors.

title: Swimming Pool Operation and Maintenance
description: Provides information on pool circulation, filtration, sanitation, and administrative procedure for the pool operator or aquatics specialist.

title: Aquatic Facilities Management and Programming
description: Study of organization and administration to prepare the aquatic professional for management of indoor and outdoor facilities. Includes facility design, safety procedures, activity, sport, and recreational aspects ofpools, lakes, camps, and beach fronts. Prerequisite: PEP 454.

title: Teaching Modern Dance in the Secondary Schools
description: Methods and materials for teaching modern dance in the secondary schools. Prerequisite: PEP 107, 115.

title: Mainstreaming and Inclusion in Physical Education
description: Designing physical education programs to meet the requirements of Public Law 101-476, IDEA, which requires that each child with disabilities have an individualized physical education program. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Practicum in Adaptive Physical Education 3: Clinical
description: Focuses on a clinical emphasis in exercise and fitness for persons with disabilities. Requires a sixteenweek practicum assignment under the supervision of an adapted physical educator. Involves weight training, water exercise, and general fitness activity sessions for persons with disabilities. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or permission of the instructor.

title: History, Philosophy, Administration, and Coaching Modern Athletic Programs
description: Explores the historical development of modern athletics. Students develop a philosophical relationship to the total school program and learn to deal with everyday coaching and administration problems. Prerequisite: satisfactory completion of 22 hours of undergraduate sport administration courses; ENG 231; JOURN 261; BEOA 241; foundations of business minor (21 hours); and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
description: Movement experiences appropriate for elementary school children; planning, teaching, and evaluating a developmental program.

title: Practicum 2 in Athletic Training
description: Student athletic trainers develop sports medicine knowledge and skills relevant to the sport and workenhancement physical therapy settings. Prerequisite: PEP 372, 373, permission of the instructor. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: The effect of exercise on the anatomical structures and physiological functions in humans during acute and chronic activity. Prerequisite: PEP 292, 293, 294, or permission of the program director.

title: Teaching Individuals with Disabilities in Physical Education
description: Recognition of various abnormalities and physical handicaps and the limitation each causes. Physical education and recreational activities for each type. Prerequisite: PEP 227 or SPCED 201.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training
description: Students receive athletic training clinical experience in an Indiana high school, sports medicine clinic, or otherqualified facility. Students must work under the direct supervision of an NATA certified athletic trainer. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 372, and 340.

title: Current Concepts in Athletic Training
description: Designed to advance educational and clinical experiences. Advanced concepts in sports medicine, review of case studies, and application of applied research in athletic training will be presented. Prerequisite: PEP 370, 372.

title: Organization and Administration of Athletic Training
description: Advanced organization and administration of an Athletic Training Program. Emphasizes the objectives, principles, and problems in management of a comprehensive athletic training program. Open only to athletic training majors accepted into the professional preparation program.

title: Independent Study in Physical Education
description: An opportunity to investigate an area of particular interest to the student, under supervision of a faculty member. Extensive reading, research, analysis, and writing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Hatha Yoga
description: Designed to increase physical fitness and self awareness through yoga exercise, breathing and relaxation techniques.

title: Weight Training
description: Designed to enhance muscular strength and endurance through weight training.

title: Rhythmic Aerobics
description: Designed to increase physical fitness through aerobic workouts performed to music.

title: Foundations of Exercise Science and Wellness
description: An introduction to such topics as career opportunities, exercise and nutrition, lifestyle changes, related professional organizations and publications, physiological and psychological research, and other current information for wellness and fitness professionals.

title: Introduction to Fitness Assessment
description: Evaluation of and introduction to practical and written skills in exercise science needed in the advanced program, i.e., exercise prescription, submaximal ergometer testing, etc. Prerequisite: EXSCI 190. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors and adapted physical education minors.

title: Exercise Leader Professional Experience
description: Fulltime paid work and learning offcampus practical experience in a health/ fitness program, e.g., cardiac rehabilitation, wellness and health promotion, sports medicine, corporate fitness, YMCA, etc. Enhances professional preparation by offering opportunities to apply fundamental concepts and principles in an actual work setting. Prerequisite: permission of the program director. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Principles of the Electrocardiogram and Cardiac Assessments
description: Introduction to basic principles and interpretation of the electrocardiogram (EKG) as it relates to fitness programs involving apparently healthy people and cardiac rehabilitation patients. Includes cardiac assessments and emphasis on prescription medication use and intervention in various cardiac problems. Prerequisite: EXSCI 301. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Advanced Fitness Assessments in Exercise Science
description: Laboratory designed to present and refine skills in conducting various health fitness tests, e.g., resting and exercise blood pressure, body composition, submaximal aerobic capacity, maximal graded exercise tests, and blood cholesterol, as well as implications of test results. Prerequisite: EXSCI 401 and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to exercise science and wellness majors.

title: Exercise Leader Internship
description: Full time offcampus practical experience in a health and fitness program, e.g., cardiac rehabilitation, wellness/health promotion, sports medicine, corporate fitness, YMCA, etc. Enhances professional preparation by offering opportunities to apply fundamental concepts and principles in an actual work setting. title: Environmental Design and Planning 1
description: Basic problem solving related to abstract and historical and contemporary problems in environmental design. Elements of space, form, function, and human use as they affect the natural and built environments.

title: Environmental Design and Planning 2
description: Basic problem solving related to abstract and historical and contemporary problems in environmental design. Elements of space, form, function, and human use as they affect the natural and built environments. Prerequisite: CAP 101.

title: Design Communications Media 1
description: Methods for environmental design communications in a variety of media.

title: Design Communications Media 2
description: Methods for environmental design communications in a variety of media. Prerequisite: CAP 161.

title: Introduction to Architecture, Landscape Architecture, and Urban Planning
description: A twoweek workshop in environmental design and planning including lectures, field trips, and handson studio experience. Open only to high school juniors enrolled in the Honors College Summer Program.

title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design 1
description: Introduction to twodimensional computeraided design using microand large computer CAD systems. Hardware and operatin system concepts, drawing and e iting commands. Emphasizes environmental design and planning applications. Prerequisite: permission of the dean of the College of Architecture and Planning.

title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design 2
description: A continuation of CAP 381 in a threedimensional environment. Introduction to the drawing environment, view manipulation, projections, coordinate systems, and hidden line and hidden surface shading. Emphasizes environmental design and planning applications. Prerequisite: CAP 381 and permission of the dean of the College of Architecture and Planning.

title: Community-Based Projects
description: Independent study in urban design, planning, landscape architecture, and architecture, offered in conjunction with the college's Community-Based Projects Program. A multidisciplinary approach to problem solving in collaboration with faculty and professional consultants. Prerequisite: permission of the Community-Based Projects coordinator. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Projects in College of Architecture and Planning
description: Special projects in the College of Architecture and Planning undertaken by groups of students. Prerequisite: junior standing and permission of the project director. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. ARCHITECTURE M. Rosenman, Chairperson, M Chiuini, A. Wyman Architects design buildings and the spaces around them to be used and enjoyed. Architects combine their design skills with technical knowledge to achieve beauty, safety, economic and environmental benefits, and comfort. The Department of Architecture offers a fiveyear undergraduate bachelor of architectuie degree, accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board. Approval to pursue the departmental major in architecture involves a selection process in addition to admission to the university. For more information, write or call the Office of Admissions, (317) 285-8300. A student receiving two consecutive grades below C in any two sequential architecture courses must repeat both courses. The policy remains in effect for students repeating these courses: Acceptance into the first semester of the fourth year of the Bachelor of Architecture curriculum requires submission of an application for admission and a faculty review of general academic performance as well as work produced in design communication and design studios through the first semester of the third year. Acceptance requires minimum cumulative gradepoint averages of 2.0 for the university, 2.20 for architecture, and 2.25 for design. Transfer students with less than one year of design status in an architecture or architecturerelated degree program must apply to the College of Architecture and Planning for admission to the First Year Program. Transfer students with one year or more of design credit from other accredited professional degree programs in architecture who are seeking advanced placement should inquire directly at the Department of Architecture about the submission of portfolios as well as transcripts for evaluation. All transfer applicants must first be admitted to the university before the process of admission to the major can begin. Advanced placement in architecture requires review by the Department of Architecture of transfer application materials to determine the student's best starting point in the curriculum. Admission to the university does not automatically imply admission to the major in architecture. No guarantee can be made or should be inferred until the department's final decision on placement has been made regarding the length of time or number of credits to complete the degree. In order to receive the Bachelor of Architecture degree, all transfer students must complete a minimum of three semesters of design course work at Ball State. title: Introduction to Architecture
description: An introduction to architecture through an exploration of products of the built environment.

title: Architectural Design
description: Introduction to the architectural design sequence. Projects focus on conceptual architectural design and design methodologies in small and intermediatescale projects, introduction of architectural technology, research, analysis, and programming. Prerequisite: CAP 102.

title: Architectural Design
description: Conceptual architectural design and design methodologies in largescale projects; introduction of architectural technology, research, analysis, and programming. Prerequisite: ARCH 201.

title: Introduction to Technology
description: Introduction to a holistic approach to technology and its effect on architecture. Emphasis is placed on the interface, integration, and effect of systems in a comprehensive approach to architectural design. Team taught. Prerequisite: ARCH 100.

title: Introduction to Structural Systems
description: Covers statics, equilibrium, external loading and force systems, and properties of materials, with a focus on developing a basic understanding of structural concepts. Prerequisite: MATHS 125 or the equivalent. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Analysis of Structural Systems
description: Covers internal force determinations, modes of failure, and strength of structures as applied to beams, columns, and trusses. Prerequisite: ARCH 211.

title: History of Architecture 1
description: Introduction to architecture as historical document and cultural artifact, including corresponding developments in the visual arts and landscape and urban design through the fifteenth century. Open only to architecture majors except by permission of the department chairperson.

title: History of Architecture 2
description: An introduction to architecture as historical document and cultural artifact, including corresponding developments in the visual arts and landscape and urban design from the fifteenth to the nineteenth centuries. Prerequisite: ARCH 223. Open only to architecture majors except by permission of the department chairperson.

title: Design Communications Media 3
description: Exploration of a variety of communications media including pencil, ink, pastel, markers, watercolor, and photography. Prerequisite: CAP 162. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Design Communications Media 4
description: Continuation of ARCH 261. Prerequisite: ARCH 261.

title: Architectural Design
description: Integration of all facets of design including design, research, programming, technology, function, human behavior, scheduling, time management, communication, use of materials, and systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

title: Architectural Design
description: Integration of all facets of design including design, research, programming, technology, function, human behavior, scheduling, time management, communication, use of materials, and systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 301 and admission by a faculty design review panel.

title: Design of Structural Systems 1
description: Structural design in steel and wood. Application of structural analysis to proportioning building materials for use in beams, columns, trusses, and simple frames. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 212.

title: Design of Structural Systems 2
description: Structural design—continuation of

title: Architectural Building Technology 1
description: Methods and materials of architectural construction. Emphasizes interface of material selections and construction technology in the design/production/construction process. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

title: Architectural Building Technology 2
description: Methods and materials of architectural construction. Emphasizes interface of material selections and construction technology in the design/production/construction process. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 315.

title: History of Architecture 3
description: Survey of the movements and major figures in architecture and design from the late nineteenth century to the present, with consideration given to the social and cultural context of design ideas. Prerequisite: ARCH 224.

title: Architectural Internship Preparation
description: Preparation for the internship experience; supplements the experience gained during the internship and serves as the basis for evaluation of student growth. Prerequisite: ARCH 202. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 450.

title: Design Communications Media 5
description: Continuation of ARCH 262 with an emphasis on portfolio preparation. Prerequisite: ARCH 262.

title: Architectural Internship
description: A sixmonth period of approved paid professional employment under the supervision of a licensed architect, as required for the bachelor of architecture degree. Simultaneous enrollment in the National Intern-Architect Development Program (IDP) is required. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Environmental Systems 1
description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of heating, ventilating, airconditioning, plumbing, and fire protection systems. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 202.

title: Environmental Systems 2
description: Application of the principles of physics to the design and engineering of electrical, luminous, and acoustical systems. Production of a resource package for ARCH 417. Prerequisite: ARCH 371.

title: Architecture for Non-Architects
description: Honors colloquium in architecture designed to introduce nonmajors to the architectural design process, the determinants of building form, an understanding of the built environment, current trends in architecture, and architectural history and architects. Not open to students majoring in architecture.

title: Architectural Design
description: Organization and design of multipurpose architectural and related environments at all scales in response to a complex set of criteria. Investigation of architectural and urban design principles, theories, and philosophies. Prerequisite: ARCH 302, 350. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Architectural Design
description: Design of multiuse projects on multiplebuilding sites with emphasis on research, programming, and systems integration through detail design development. Additional emphasis on circulation and movement systems. Exploration of presentation media. Prerequisite: ARCH 400, 451. Parallel: ARCH 452. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Architectural Thesis
description: Development of a thesis idea plus an architectural project to test or verify the thesis design position. Includes design, comprehensive site, and building prototype analysis. Emphasizes project management and design development including all major technical systems. Prerequisite: ARCH 403, 452.

title: Integration of Architectural Technologies
description: Indepth development of a building project, from conceptual design through the execution of construction documents. Integration of structural, material, and environmental systems and methodologies. Project management stressed during all phases. Prerequisite: ARCH 312, 316, 372. Parallel: ARCH 400. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 210.

title: Topics in the History of Oriental Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from the Islamic world to the Far East. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Preservation and Documentation of Historic Buildings
description: Introduces the special qualities of design and craftsmanship in historic buildings, districts and landscapes. Emphasizes skills needed to document historic properties through written and graphic means. Surveys guidelines for rehabilitation and criteria for identifying historic properties. Prerequisite: ARCH 329.

title: Philosophy of Architecture
description: Seminars and independent study in the background and development of prevailing philosophies of architecture, ideas in design, and how they evolved in contemporary architecture since the beginning of the twentieth century, concluding with their influence on the current practice of architecture. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: History of North American Architecture
description: Survey of North American architecture and urbanism from its colonial beginnings to the present. Emphasis on European antecedents, transformation by American conditions, and the rise of a distinctly American architecture. Methods of dissemination of architectural knowledge and conflicting points of view. Prerecluisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: History of Architecture, Planning, and Engineering in the Midwest
description: Analysis of the development of architecture, planning, engineering (canals, railroads, roads, bridges), and industrial architecture in the Midwest from the frontier period through the twentieth century. Prereoluisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Historic Architectural Interiors
description: Survey of European and American interiors, interior architecture, furnishings, and decorative arts, highlighting cultural influences from antiquity to the present with emphasis on eighteenthto twentiethcentury examples. Prerecluisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of Ancient Greek and Roman Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from classical antiquity. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of Western Medieval Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from the Byzantine through the Romanesque and Gothic periods. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics. in the History of Renaissance and Baroque Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from Europe between 1400 and the late 1700s. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the Ancient Traditions of Architecture
description: Analysis of cultural and anthropological concepts, and of representative examples of prehistoric and protohistoric architecture, from the Neolithic Revolution to the rise of the first literate civilizations, while tracing the survival of those traditions into more recent global vernaculars. Prereopisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Topics in the History of 19thand 20th-Century Architecture
description: Analysis of theoretical, cultural, and historical determinants as they may be applied to a selected array of architects and buildings from around 1800 to the present. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Philosophy, History, and Theory of Historic Preservation
description: Survey of the philosophy, history, theory, and scope of historic preservation in Europe and America. Explores such principles of historicpreservation as ethical questions, practice versus theory, standards, and performance criteria. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Preservation Planning, Law, and Economics
description: Planning, law, and economics for preservation, restoration, conservation, rehabilitation, and revitalization. Emphasis is on strategies for preservation and implementation, and the development process at various scales: neighborhood, district, community, and state. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Documentation of Historic Sites and Buildings
description: Methods of recording historic sites and buildings using both written and graphic means. Assembling and preserving data on the physical condition and history of historic properties. Prerequisite: ARCH 329 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Field Workshop in Preservation
description: Exercises in surveying and the -use of state inventory forms, National Register material, and environmental impact studies. Includes field trips. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Historic Preservation, Restoration, and Adaptive Use Cost Benefits
description: Analysis of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure; suggested restoration and cost benefits and restoration costs. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Historic Preservation Technology 1: Construction and Pathology
description: Analysis of materials and systems of construction used in historic buildings. Identification and diagnosis of causes of building deterioration, obsolescence, and failure. Some laboratory sessions are integrated into the program. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: admission to the historic preservation minor and permission of the program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Historic Preservation Technology 2: Conservation Methods
description: General conservation methods for historic buildings including an introduction to specific techniques and philosophies. Field trips to selected sites. Prerequisite: ARCH 447 and permission of the program director. Open only to historic preservation minors.

title: Architectural Design Internship
description: Preparation for the internship experience; supplements the experience gained during the internship and serves as the basis for evaluation of student growth. Prerequisite: ARCH 302. Not open to students who have credit in ARCH 350.

title: Architectural Research
description: Experience in architectural inquiry: the contexts, definitions, and processes of design creativity; relationships to scientific and environmental design and behavior research; technologyrelated research; strategies in building and testing concepts, assumptions, hypotheses, empirical evaluation; methods and procedures. Prerequisite: ARCH 302.

title: Programming and Thesis Preparation
description: Problems, theories, and methods leading to the development of individual and group requirements and their translation into conventional and nonconventional performance criteria. Programming of a thesis project. Prerequisite: ARCH 400.

title: Professional Practice and Management
description: Problems, processes, and philosophies of architectural practice. Emphasis is on applied organizational and management theories, processes, tools. Prerequisite: ARCH 369.

title: Architectural Aspects of Archaeological Field Work
description: Archaeological methods applied to architectural remains. Principles of stratigraphic excavation, dating methods and techniques for surveying and recording; technical and comparative analysis of building elements for dating, interpreting, and reconstructing. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Life Safety in Architecture and Environmental Design
description: Survey of topics relevant to life safety encompassing wind, fire, ground motions, environmental factors including noise, criminal activity, and home accidents; and matters pertaining to the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA). Prerequisite: senior standing.

title: Advanced Graphic Techniques
description: Advanced graphic explorations of architectural subject matter, stressing fullcolor rendering. Includes demonstration of paint mixing, shades and shadows, reflections and material indication with application of these techniques to individual studio projects. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Computer Graphics Applications in Architecture
description: Basic training in the operation of a stateoftheart interactive computer graphics system. Introduction to twoand threedimensional graphics techniques and their applications in professional practice. Includes handson practice and exploration of the special capabilities of the interactive graphics system. Prerequisite: senior standing, permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Independent Projects
description: Independent study in environmental topics. Prerequisite: approval of a program proposal by the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 4 in any one semester or term. Open only to architecture majors.

title: Psychological Aspects of Environmental Design
description: Review of attempts to discover rational methods of predicting and evaluating environmental design. Presents basic research and analysis methods from the designer's point of view. Lecture, studio, and field activities. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson for students with majors other than architecture or landscape architecture. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Special Projects in Architecture
description: Timely architectural projects undertaken by groups of students. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to architecture majors. A total of 15 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term. ('"-)LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE D. Ferguson, Chairperson; R. Benson, M. Cairns, A. Coffin, S. Collard, J. Young Landscape architecture involves applying natural and aesthetic principles to the planning, design, preservation, and management of the land.
