title: Mass Media in Society
description: Study of mass media in their historical and societal contexts with emphasis on practitioner issues including ethics, state of the art, and future.

title: Communications Graphics
description: Theory of visual communication emphasizing the layout of journalistic publications. Content focuses on typography, design, photo selection and use, and printing processes. Includes one hour of lab each week. Requires attendance at an outofclass computer workshop. Open only to journalism majors and minors.

title: Mass Media Writing and Editing 1
description: Theory and practice in writing and editing for journalistic media publications. Includes one hour of lab each week.

title: Mass Media Writing and Editing 2
description: Theory and practice in writing and editing for journalistic media publications. Emphasis is on developing editing skills. Prerequisite: JOURN 210.

title: Editorial Presentation
description: Survey of journalistic visual/verbal relationships and analysis needed to train news editors. Introduces the concept of journalistic visual reporting, visual editing, and journalistic graphics technology. Preparatory for journalism graphics sequence students. Prerequisite: JOURN 125 and enrollment in the journalism graphics prejournalism program. Recommended parallel: JOURN 211.

title: Introduction to Photojournalism
description: Emphasis is on preparing students to take,process, and caption photographs for newspapers, magazines, public relations, and advertising purposes. Students must provide their own 35mm cameras and photographic supplies.

title: Photographic Lighting
description: An indepth study of photographic lighting procedures and equipment for studio and field use by media photographers. Students must provide their own 35mm cameras and photographic supplies. Prerequisite: JOURN 230 or other basic photography class.

title: Introduction to Advertising
description: A survey of the advertising communication process. Focuses on communication research, creative strategy, campaign planning, function of mass media as carriers of advertising, and evaluation of advertising effectiveness.

title: Principles of Public Relations
description: Survey of the theory, philosophy, and function of public relations practices and programs in American institutions with special attention given to public relations in various fields.

title: Introduction to Newspaper Journalism
description: Analysis of daily and weekly newspapers. Examination of reporting and editing functions and orientations brought to the newswriting profession. Brief look at newspaper management principles and history of newspapers will be included.

title: Magazine Writing
description: Introduction to the magazine industry and magazine writing. Practice in preparing, writing, and marketing magazine articles. Includes a study of markets for magazine articles and exercises in writing for general and specialized magazines. Prerequisite: JOURN 210. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: History of Journalism
description: History of journalism in the United States from colonial times to the present, presenting the press as an institution against the background of the history of the nation.

title: Newspaper Reporting
description: Beat coverage, visual and computerassisted reporting, including accessing online services. Special emphasis on public affairs reporting, such as coverage of school boards, police and fire departments, city, county, state, and federalgovernments, business and nongovernmental organizations. Prerequisite: JOURN 211. Not open to prejournalism majors. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Feature, Column, and Opinion Writing
description: Researching and writing feature stories, columns, and editorials for newspapers and magazines. Discussion of feature, column, and editorial types and campaigns. Prerequisite: JOURN 211. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Magazine Editing
description: Theory and practice in magazine editing. Includes editorial planning and direction of magazines; shaping and developing article ideas; and graphics editing;; and copy editing. Prerequisite: JOURN 280. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to magazine sequence majors.

title: Newspaper Design
description: Theory of layout, grid systems, typography, color, and use of photography for newspapers. Emphasizes design problem solving in the editing process and editorial judgment in the newspaper desi process. Computerbased production methods will be employed. Prerequisite: JOURN 125. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Sportswriting and Reporting
description: Study and practice in covering and writing about sports events and the people connected with them. Story assignments and research combined with classroom lectures and analysis of best sports stories provide students with skills to cover a wide range of sports activities. Prerequisite: JOURN 211 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Magazine Composition and Layout
description: Study of magazine layout and production from an editor's point of view. Explores journalistic visual literacy, visual/verbal interpretation, and composition unique to magazines and newspaper magazine supplements. Prerequisite: JOURN 125. Open only to journalism graphics, magazine and teaching majors or with permission of the department chairperson.

title: Magazine Writing Styles
description: Advanced writing styles for those interested inpublishing their work in magazines and other publications. Emphasizes techniques for learning to write different types of articles. Prerequisite: JOURN 211. Not open to prejournalism students or magazinesequence majors. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Journalism Law
description: Constitutional and statutory law and regulating agencies affecting the operations of the print and broadcast media with special attention given to recent Supreme Court rulings.

title: Magazine Production and Publishing
description: Analysis of all facets of magazine publishing: editorial, advertising, circulation, and art. Designed for students interested in workin g for professional magazines. Prerequisite: JOURN 315. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to magazine sequence majors.

title: Color Photojournalism
description: Principles, techniques, and materials of color photography as they apply to color art work andphotographs in printed publications. Students must provide their own 35mm cameras and photographic supplies. Prerequisite: JOURN 236. Not open to prejournalism students.

title: Journalistic Visual Reporting
description: Examination of the facets of informational graphics and the job of the modernday graphics reporter. Experience gained in creating and researching explanatory charts, diagrams, maps, and graphics editing. Computers are an integral tool. Prerequisite: JOURN 211, 225. Not open to students in prejournalism. Open only to students with other journalism areas.

title: Advertising Media
description: Strategy and procedures for planning, executing, and controlling the placement of advertising. Examines characteristics of media, techniques of media budgeting and selection, and methods of evaluating media effectiveness. Prerequisite: JOURN 250. Not open to prejoumalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advertising Copy and Layout
description: Instruction in preparing copy for mass media advertising. Major emphasis is on creative thinking and basic writing skills. Students prepare copy strategies, write copy, prepare layouts and storyboards. Discussion of fundamentals of consumer motivation and selecting target audiences. Prerequisite: JOURN 250. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas and minors in campaign communication.

title: Public Relations Writing and Publicity Techniques
description: Theory and practice of producing publicity tools for various media used in campaigns to promote and interpret personal, institutional, and organizational objectives and activities. Emphasis is on writing and publicity problem solving. Prerequisite: JOURN 211 and 261. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Public Relations Publication Design and Production
description: Institutional and industrial publications as an important means of internal and external communications. Design and production techniques. Includes one hour of lab each week. Prerequisite: JOURN 261. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Journalism Internship
description: Onthejob training in which journalism or public relations majors get practical experience in applying what they have learned in the classroom. Involves assigned duties in an offcampus communications organization with appropriate compensation. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson, completion of prejournalism curriculum. Notopen to students who have credit in JOURN 379. Open only to journalism majors.

title: Introduction to Mass Media Research Strategies
description: Practical approaches to research in journalism and media campaigns. Emphasizes survey research, questionnaire construction, interviewing techniques, attitude measurement, copy testing, audience analysis, computer database searches, evaluation of externally supplied research, and data interpretation.

title: Electronic Journalistic Production Techniques
description: Theory, principles, and handson experience in writing for electronic media; camera and videocassette recorder operation; microphones and audio recording; electronic editing; studio production; field production and delivery systems. Prerequisite: JOURN 211. Open only to journalism majors and minors.

title: Honors Colloquium in Journalism
description: Readings and indepth exploration and discussion of pertinent issues, movements, and problems in journalism and mass communications research. Open to honors students and to students with areas in journalism by permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Journalism
description: The procedures and problems in teaching journalism classes or units and the role of student publications in school journalism programs. Subjects included are curriculum, finance, textbooks, and resources. Discussion of school publicity is included as time permits. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Advanced Reporting and Newswriting
description: Theory and practice in reporting, writing and editing indepth news stories, including the use of computerassisted reporting techniques, professional development and theories of community and public journalism. Emphasizes reporting, analysis and interpretation; writing publishable stories. Prerequisite: JOURN 211, 310. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to journalism majors and minors.

title: World Press Systems
description: Survey of the international news media, with particular attention to the four press theories; ownership, structure, and access to the media; the political, economic, and social environment in which the media operate; governmentmedia relations. Comparison with the American media.

title: Science and Technical Writing
description: Description of methods and techniques of technical and scientific writing and editing. Emphasis on clarity in technical writing and ability to translate terminology into lay language in science writing.

title: Advanced Magazine Writing
description: A workshop in writing articles. Emphasizes targeting markets for freelance articles and writing for magazines that publish articles of 2,500 words or more. Prerequisite: JOURN 315. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Picture Editing
description: Selecting, editing, and using photographic and other illustrative graphic materials. Includes layout and design of picture pages for newspapers, magazines, books, brochures, and pamphlets.

title: Advertising Photography
description: Advertising, commercial, and concept illustration photography for the print media. Students must provide their own 35mm cameras and photographic supplies. Prerequisite: JOURN 236. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advanced Photojournalism
description: An extended study of the theory and practice of making photographs and using photography as a communicative art. Students must provide their own 35mm cameras andphotographic supplies. Prerequisite: JOURN 335. Not open to prejournalism students.

title: Advanced Advertising Media
description: Extended study in developing a comprehensive media plan. Emphasizes consumer research, media habits, creative selection of media vehicles, and use of the computer in planning and buying. Prerequisite: JOURN 352. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advertising Creative Seminar
description: Extended study in the conceptualization and creation of advertising with emphasis on creative direction and visual presentation. Prerequisite: JOURN 352, 354. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advanced Copy Writing
description: Advanced studies in the strategy and creation of advertising for the mass media. Prerequisite: JOURN 354. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advertising Campaigns
description: Synthesis of skills and concepts acquired in the specialized advertising courses. Research, plan, write, schedule, budget, and evaluate a complete advertising campaign. Enhances career development skills andportfolioready material. Prerequisite: either JOURN 452, 453, 454, or 455. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Public Relations Campaigns
description: Allows public relations majors to apply research and problemsolving techniques to actual or simulated public relations case problems using all of the methodologies earned previously. Portfolio and professional development including personal presentation skills and needs are components. Prerequisite: JOURN 360, 368. Not open to prejournalism students. Open only to students in other journalism areas.

title: Advising High School Publications
description: Theories of staff organization and content of high school yearbooks, newspapers, and magazines. Emphasizes the role of the advisor, financial management, staff motivation, and trends in scholastic publications. Includes portfolio development and career planning.

title: Writing, Editing, and Design Seminar
description: Further develops writing, editing; and design skills for journalistic publications. Specialized writing and design projects within the areas of newspaper, magazine, and information graphics. Topics also include analysis, career planning, and portfolio development. Prerequisite, graphics reporting: JOURN 321, 345, 382; visual editing: JOURN 321, 323, 345, 432.

title: Nonpaid Internship
description: Onthejob training in which journalism or public relations majors get practical experience in applying what they have learned in the classroom. Involves assigned duties in a communications organization without compensation. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson, completion of prejournalism curriculum. Not open to students who have credit in JOURN 369. Open only to journalism majors and minors.

title: Individual Studies in Journalism.
description: Group and individual investigations and experiences in journalistic media and techniques with special attention to social, political, and economic roles of the press in society. title: Argumentation and Debate
description: Theory and principles of argumentation and debate, including construction of debate cases, practice in debating, administration of a forensics program, and tournament direction. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Human Speech Communication
description: Focuses on understanding human speech communication as a dynamic and complex system of interactions rather than on the skills of platform speaking. Stresses the importance of understanding and applying communication theory in everyday speech communication situations.

title: Voice and Diction
description: Speech improvement, dealing with voice and articulation.

title: Business and Professional Communication
description: Survey that focuses on a variety of communication facets, skills, and problems commonly found in business and professional careers. Emphasis is on pragmatics to recognize, analyze and evaluate the various elements of assorted content modules.

description: Speechmaking as a force in political and intellectual history; critical analysis of selected speeches in relation to political, social, and economic issues. title: Persuasion
description: Concerned with current theories and research related to persuasion and social influence. Specifically examines variables affecting implementation of persuasion principles and strategies. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Contemporary Forms of Persuasion
description: Examines the modes of persuasion reflected in dimensions of American popular culture. title: Interviewing
description: Examines the principles and types of interviews, with application of the principles in informational, persuasive, and employment interviews. Special attention is given to the various communication elements of the employment interview process: resumes, cover letters, selection interviews, and appraisal interviews. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Small. Group Decision Making
description: Focuses on the theories, concepts, and processes of small group decision making and problem solving. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240.

title: Topics in Speech Communication
description: Critical examination of selected topics and issues in speech communication. Designed to help students become familiar with current trends and theoretical and methodological issues in the discipline. May be repeated once by permission of the instructor and the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Communication Leadership
description: Examines the history of leadership theories with primary emphasis on transformational leadership. Participation in enacting leadership is encouraged with a focus on abilities to communicate transformational leadership. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240

title: Human Communication Theory
description: Introduction to the varied and complex theoretical underpinnings of the human communication phenomenon. Several theoretical perspectives and applications will be explored. Topics include message theories, intrapersonal and interpersonal theories, and group and public communication theories. Prerequisite: SPCH 240.

title: Professional Experience
description: Paid, supervised work and learning experience related to careers in speech communication with business firms or public agencies. Job description may include, but is not limited to, research, training, organization, and planning informative or persuasive campaigns, problem solving, and conflict management. title: Nonverbal Communication in Human Interaction
description: Examines the nature, forms, and functions of nonverbal codes in human speech communication. Focuses on understanding one's own nonverbal communication and that of others. Prerequisite: SPCH 240 for speech communication majors; recommended for nonmajors.

title: Presentational Communication
description: Focuses on the preparation and delivery of presentations and longer speeches within a wide variety of communication settings. Uses both theory and practice in analyzing, organizing, and delivering presentations. Prerequisite: SPCH 210.

title: Speech for Elementary Teachers
description: Designed for elementary and special education majors. Focuses on the development of the communication skills necessary for the classroom including creative dramatic arts, interpersonal communication, and public speaking. Not open to speech communication majors or minors A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Practicum in Speech . Communication
description: Practical experience in intercollegiate debate, individual events, applied communication research, or alternate speech communication projects. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Colloquium in Human Speech Communication
description: Seminartype class focusing on various aspects and problems of speech communication as they relate to people in their personal and professional relationships. Open to honors students and to students with areas in speech with permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for Teaching Speech and Theatre
description: Concentrates on selection and application of materials, methods, and resources used in teaching speech and theatre. Focuses on skills needed for curriculum planning, teaching effectiveness, and directing cocurricular speech, theatre, radio-TV-film, and interpretive and forensic events. Prerequisite: SPCH 210 and THEAT 220 or 232. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: The Rhetoric of Political Campaigns
description: Examines the nature, forms, and effects of persuasion in organized political campaigns that seek to influence mass publics. Focuses on the skills needed to describe, analyze, and evaluate persuasive uses of language and to understand better the role of campaign persuasion in influencing voter behavior. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 372.

title: Rhetorical Criticism
description: The description, analysis, interpretation, and evaluation of persuasive uses of language. Theories and methodologies of selected classical and modern critics. Prerequisite: SPCH 320 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Classical Rhetorical Theory
description: Explores the roots of rhetorical theory development by examining contributions of seminal theorists such as Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, and Cicero. Designed to provide insight into persuasion's role within Greek and Roman culture and modern society.

title: Interpersonal Communications
description: Examines contemporary theories, concepts, models, and pertinent research related to the communication process in relatively unstructured facetoface settings. Particular emphasis is given to understanding message exchanges between people and how they affect the people involved. Introduces students to the approaches, variables, and topics that influence social interaction. Special attention is given to communication models, perception, symbols, systems, selfconcept, attitudes, meaning, and nonverbal message cues. Prerequisite: SPCH 240 (not required for applied communication minors, but recommended).

title: Organizational Culture
description: Examines various types of organizational culture and how culture influences the nature of communication. An analysis of organizational communication as cultural performance is examined. Prerequisite: SPCH 251 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Communication and Conflict Management
description: Explores the strategies of productive and nonproductive conflict within the organizational setting. Theories of conflict are examined and explanations of the sources that stimulate conflict are investigated. Prerequisite: SPCH 240, 360 or perniission of the department chairperson.

title: Communication in Organizations
description: Introduces contemporary understandings of fundamental organizational communication concepts and the basic functions of communication in organizations. Content is approached from a variety of theoretical perspectives. Prerequisite recommended: SPCH 240, 251. •

title: Applied Organizational Communication
description: Focuses on the diagnostic skills and pragmatic analyses necessary to undertake needs assessments, communication audits, training and development, and communication consultation. Prerequisite: SPCH 220, 251, 320, 330, 340, 360, 375, 451 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Human Communication Inquiry
description: Introduces, reviews, and evaluates the various methods of research in the field of human communication from which the discipline's body of knowledge is derived. Open only to juniors and seniors.

title: Practical Experience
description: Nonpaid supervised work experience with business firms or public agencies related to careers in speech communication. job possibilities may include, but are not limited to, working on political campaigns, in business offices, or at summer camps. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Open only to majors or minors in Speech Communication. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Directed Study in Speech
description: Students with areas in the Department of Speech Communication pursue a specific subject in depth in consultation with a member of the faculty. The Letterman Telecommunications Scholarships are offered to majors and minors in telecommunications. One fully funded scholarship (tuition, room and board, personal expenses, and transportation) for one year is awarded annually. The specific amount is determined by the Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid. A number of partially funded scholarships are also awarded each year. Before students can declare telecommunications (TCOM) majors and enroll in courses from a telecommunications option or the telecommunications minor, they must complete the pretelecommunications program of TCOM 200, 202, 302, and 304, earning C (2.0) or better in each with a 2.5 overall GPA for these four courses. Students must also participate in a Pre- TCOM orientation session. Students then complete a major or minor application (available in the department office BC 217) and declare an option in the major or the TCOM minor before pursuing additional telecommunications course work. The application should be completed early in the semester (September or February), allowing students to preregister for courses. Students cannot declare more than one option in telecommunications. If they major in telecommunications they cannot select the telecommunications minor, but can select the film minor. TCOM majors/minors should have keyboarding skills of at least 30 wordsperminute. Majors must have grades of C (2.0) or better and a 2.5 GPA for all classes taken in an option including the language and pretelecommunications courses. They must earn credit for four semesters or the equivalent of study in one modern or classical language. Students may be able to earn some language credit by passing an exam and should consult the Department of Modern Languages and Classics about credit by exam. 2. Telecommunications minors must earn grades of C (2.0) or better and have a 2.5 GPA for all classes taken in the minor including the pretelecommunications courses. They must also earn credit for two semesters or the equivalent of study in one modern or classical language. 3. Film minors must earn grades of C (2.0) or better and have a 2.5 GPA for all classes taken in the minor. It is strongly recommended that students completing the film minor also take at least two semesters of either Italian or French. Statement of Policy Governing Application of Transfer Credit The Department of Telecommunications is pleased to work with students from all areas of the United States in their desire to transfer to Ball State University as telecommunications majors or minors. In so doing it has become clear that there are both twoyear and fouryear programs within the state of Indiana and across the country providing extensive courses in radio, television, and film. Not all these many programs reflect the scope, nature, and quality of accomplishment and understanding expected of Ball State graduates by the Department of Telecommunications. Therefore, the department follows this policy to govern acceptance and application of credits transferred in the fields of radio, television, and film: 1. A maximum of 12 semester hours may be applied toward fulfillment of major requirements and a maximum of 9 semester hours toward minor requirements. 2. All 300- and 400-level telecommunications courses required for completion of a required option in the major must be completed at Ball State. The single exception to this policy is in the production option, where a student may transfer and substitute credit equivalent to TCOM 330 and 332. That student would then be eligible for and required to complete 400-level audio and video production courses. title: Organizational Video Production
description: Video production that meets the requirements of business, industry, medicine, and special interest organizations. Identifying needs; planning, executing, and evaluating productions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, and TCOM 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. title: News Writing and Performance
description: Study and practice in the methods of gathering, writing, and reporting broadcast news. Practical experience in the uses of audio tape recorders and telephone recording, electronic news gathering (ENG) equipment, and other similar equipment used by radio and television news reporters. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades, a 2.5 GPA for these four courses or permission of the instructor. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Electronic News Gathering
description: Study and practice in the methods of gathering, shooting, editing, and reporting news with electronic news gathering (ENG) video equipment. Students will plan, shoot, edit, and produce a varied series of news reports. Prerequisite: TCOM 320. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Audio Production
description: Emphasizes techniques and skills needed for audio production. Typical experiences in radio broadcasting. A practical test is part of the final examination, and students are expected to maintain a record of their productions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Video Production
description: Covers the basic skills of equipment operation in miniproductions that simulate television station programming. A practical test is part of the final examination, and students must maintain a record of their course work. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Single Camera Video Production
description: Orientation and practice in producing, directing, and designing projects in the singlecamera style used in film and television. Preand postproduction processes including planning, writing, editing, and camera operation will be studied as well as film . theory and techniques. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA in these four courses, and TCOM 330, 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Radio Sales
description: Study and practice of the skills for selling radio time. Both selling strategies and the use of marketing research tools are emphasized. Includes practice in preparing sales presentations for clients. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Broadcast Promotion
description: Promotional concepts, strategies, and methodologies available for carrying out efficient and effective promotional campaigns for broadcast stations. Includes practice designing and executing audience, image, and sales promotions. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses and TCOM 306. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Television Sales
description: Skills needed for selling television time. Emphasizes the use ofquantitative audience research tools. Includes practice in preparing sales presentations for clients. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: World Film History 1
description: History of world cinema from its beginning until World War II. Study of the continuing influence of American cinema, as well as key movements in other national cinemas before 1941, such as German Expressionism and the Soviet Montage School. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: World Film History 2
description: Continues the study of world cinema from World War II until the present. Study of the continuing influence of American cinema, as well as the post-1945 national cinema movements exemplified by Italian Neo-Realism and the French New Wave films. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Film Genres
description: Study of the general types and forms of film expressions, each identified with a specific tradition. Film genres include westerns, screwball comedies, gangster films, musicals, etc. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Announcing
description: Concentrates on training and practice in the vocal interpretive skills necessary for speech presentation. Studies the structure and use of the human vocal system; analysis of copy; and delivery of verbal messages in radio, television, and recording. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Sports Announcing
description: Research, writing, production, and performance with emphasis on the remote broadcast. Study of rules, organization and planning, promotion and selling, techniques of playbyplay, and color description of major sports. Lab includes onsite practical experience. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Independent Study
description: Special service, directed by a faculty member or an approved representative of an outside agency directly related to the subject. Term project is a written report. A written proposal for a project in telecommunications must be submitted to the department four weeks before the term of study. Prerequisite: junior standing, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Internship Study
description: Presents an opportunity to gain practical, applied onthejob experience with an approved agency directly related to the business. Must make written application to the department and meet criteria before enrollment. Prerequisite: junior standing, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Honors Colloquium in Telecommunications
description: Exploration of selected issues in telecommunications with emphasis on individualized study and reporting. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Open only to honors program students.

title: Production Practicum
description: Production of an audio or audio/video project. Requires submission of detailed outlined proposal to faculty member supervising practicum. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses; permission of the instructor. Open only to approved telecommunication majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of practicum (TCOM 396, 397, 398, 399) may be earned but no more than 3 in any one semester of term.

title: Corporate Practicum
description: Production of an audio or audio/video project directly related to corporate training. Requires submission of detailed outlined proposal to faculty member supervising practicum. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses; permission of the instructor. Open only to approved telecommunication majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of practicum (TCOM 396, 397, 398, 399) may be earned but no more than 3 in any one semester of term.

title: News Practicum
description: Work in a news related area. Requires submission of a completed application and a detailed outlinedproposal to faculty member supervising practicum. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses and permission of the instructor. Open only to approved telecommunication majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of practicum (TCOM 396, 397, 398, 399) may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Sales Practicum
description: Practical experience relating to sales and marketing broadcast stations. Requires submission of completed application and detailed outlined proposal to faculty member supervising practicum. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses and permission of the instructor. Open only to approved telecommunication majors or minors. A total of 6 hours of practicum (TCOM 396, 397, 398, 399) may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Social Responsibility
description: Political, economic, social, and governmental influences on telecommunications. Examines contemporary issues that confront broadcasters today and the ethics surrounding them. Prerequisite: senior standing, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Organizational Media Management
description: Examination of the special requirements of business, industrial, medical, and other uses of television for instruction, information, public relations, etc. Special emphasis on budgeting and management. Corporate program sources are considered. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Advanced R-TV News Reporting
description: Instruction and practice in reporting, writing, and producing indepth broadcast news stories. Emphasis is on investigative techniques, interviewing, and strategies for finding information from public records and databases. Assignments designed for use in campus electronic media programs. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, and TCOM 320. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Newscasting
description: Planning, gathering, writing, and presenting a television and radio newscast. Discussion of current events; evaluation of commercial station newscasts; onair production of typical news programs. Productionclass periods are three hours long. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, and TCOM 320, 323. Open only to approved telecommunications majors and minors.

title: Advanced Audio Production
description: Application of advanced audio techniques to radio, television, motion pictures, and other electronic media presentation environments. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses and TCOM 330. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Advanced Video Production
description: Advanced television production with more original and longer productions. Format for programs written and produced duplicates typical programming in the commercial broadcast operation. Requires a record ofproduced projects. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses and TCOM 332. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Directing Drama for Television
description: Introduction to the processes and skills required to design and direct television drama. Emphasizes the effective use of the audiovisual language, camera blocking, and communication between directors and actors. Prerequisite: TCOM 332, 334, and permission of the instructor. Not open to students who have credit in THEAT 299X. Open only to telecommunications production majors.

title: Management of Telecommunications
description: Problems and responsibilities of management in the telecommunications industry. Consists largely of guest lecturers, class discussion, management roleplaying, and computer projects to become familiar with administrative practices in the industry. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, and TCOM 306, 340, 345. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Film Censorship
description: Emphasizes the moral measurements and restraints that have affected the film industry almost since its inception. A chronology of events influencing both the direction and content of motion pictures. Examines governmental, legal, church, and community pressures and restraints. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Seminar in Film Theory
description: Analysis of the key theorists in the history of world cinema as well as some influential critics of film. A special focus on the documentary film. Examines many dimensions of the documentary film: historical, commercial, informational, educational, and propaganda applications. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor.

title: Film Production
description: Basic introduction to super-8 film production, as well as the theory behind the technique. Includes planning, writing, and producing minifilms. Prerequisite: TCOM 200,202,302,304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, permission of the instructor, and TCOM 363. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Communications Technologies
description: Explores technologies beyond the conventional broadcast and organizational systems. Topics include computer incorporation into video, fiber optic and laser transmission, teledata, home access, and interactive video. Changes in topics will reflect the newest technologies incorporated into electronic media. Prerequisite: senior standing, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Seminar in Television Production
description: Requires planning, writing, and producing a major project in television. Each project, as it moves through development, will serve as a case study for the class to discuss and evaluate. Prerequisite: TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses, permission of the department chairperson, and TCOM 332, 434; THEAT 101.

title: Video Graphics Technology
description: Provides working knowledge of video computer graphic programs using Cubicomp graphics generators. DOOSS files, drawing backgrounds with True Color Paint, creating threedimensional objects with Build, and combining Draw and Build for animation images in Motion program are included. Prerequisite: senior standing and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. Open only to approved telecommunications majors or minors.

title: Senior Telecommunications Seminar
description: Covers the principles of media research. Illustrates applications of research within electronic communication, both for scholarly investigation and for use in support of the functions of broadcasting. Principles and practice in writing about results of research. Prerequisite: senior standing, and TCOM 200, 202, 302, 304 with C or better grades and a 2.5 GPA for these four courses. title: Introduction to the Fine Arts: Art, Drama, Music, Dance
description: Interdisciplinary General Studies course offering students experiences with visual art, dance, music, and theatre as approaches to reality. Emphasizes developing basic vocabulary and exploring a range of historical styles. Attendance at several evening performances will be required.

title: Seminar in Museum Studies
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to museums and museum collections through formal lectures and independent research on various components of a planned permanent collection exhibition. Hall, S. Johnson, N. Marshall, S. Minor, S. Myers, P. Nelson, C. Paul, K. Preston, R. Rarick, P. Repp, M. Sawrie, P. Wolfe, B. Zack The Department of Art educates artists, designers, and teachers. After completing the foundation year, which includes fundamental design, drawing, and a survey of art history, students specialize in one of the following: art education, ceramics, drawing, graphic design, environmental/exhibition design, metal design, painting, photography, printmaking, and sculpture. Approval to pursue the departmental major in art involves a selection process in addition to admission to the university. Transfer students from other universities are required to submit portfolios to the Department of Art as well as transcripts for evaluation and admittance. Transfer students should be aware that design programs involve a threeyear sequence beyond the foundation year, and it is unusual for students to be admitted at any point other than at the beginning of the sequence. Students specializing in any art program must enroll in the foundation core (ADS 101, 102; AFA 101, 202). All art majors must receive grades of C or higher in all foundation core courses before being admitted to areas of specialization in the second year of study. Students must repeat foundation courses in which they receive grades lower than C. Students specializing in the graphic design and environmental/ exhibition design programs must undergo portfolio review after the completion of ADS 241 and while enrolled in ADS 242. Admission to the third year of the graphic design and environmental/exhibition design sequences requires successful completion of a portfolio review. Information on design portfolio reviews is available from design faculty members. All students in the department undergo periodic reviews of their portfolios throughout their undergraduate education. The department reserves the right to retain examples of student work for exhibition. The bachelor of fine arts program in the studio areas requires a senior thesis or an exit portfolio evaluation, or both. Studio courses are open only to art majors and minors except by permission of the instructor. All students in the university may enroll in the art history surveys and in more specialized history courses in the art of a particular era or topical courses on particular problems in art. title: Ceramics 1
description: Basic handbuilding techniques: wedging, slab, coiling, and 15 pinch methods. Glazes, slips, bisquing, and firing will be part of the studio experience. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 1
description: Beginning throwing; use of the potter's 6 wheel to develop skills in throwing. A continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Introduction to Metals
description: Introduction to jewelry and object • making using metal. Emphasis is on design and the techniques of sawing, soldering, forming, bezel setting, chain and wire working, as well as other basic processes. Prerequisite: ADS 201; AFA 202.

title: Metalsmithing and Dieforming
description: introduction to metalsmithing including raising and dieforming; basic hammering and forming techniques will be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 221.

title: Ceramics: Handbuilding 1
description: Continued study of handbuilding methods as well as form, idea, and glazing techniques. Prerequisite: ACR 211.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 2
description: Use of the potter's wheel to develop production form; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 212.

title: Ceramics: Handbuilding 2
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques to develop an integration of form, glaze, and idea. Individual problems will be set up according to student needs. Prerequisite: ACR 313.

title: Metals: Casting
description: Jewelry casting using the lostwax investment technique. Production casting will be covered, including rubber moldmaking and wax injecting for cast multiples. Courses must be taken in sequence. Prerequisite: ACR 222.

title: Metals: Color
description: Color in metal, including enameling and aluminum and refractory metal anodizing. Prerequisite: ACR 323.

title: Independent Study in Crafts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special area. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Ceramics: Throwing 3
description: An indepth exploration of forming vertically and horizontally on the wheel; continued study of form, glaze, and idea. Prerequisite: ACR 314.

title: Ceramics: Handbuilding 3
description: Continued study of handbuilding techniques, form, and idea based on individual student needs. Prerequisite: ACR 315.

title: Ceramics: Senior Project
description: Synthesis and culmination of studio experiences in the major content area, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. In addition there must be documentation through slide portfolio, résumé, and thesis. Prerequisite: ACR 416, 417, permission of the ceramics faculty and the department chairperson.

title: Metals: Advanced Fabrication
description: Advanced construction techniques including catches, hinges, stone settings, etc. Basic forging will also be covered. Prerequisite: ACR 323.

title: Metals: Advanced Surface Techniques
description: Advanced surface techniques including chasing and repousse, metal inlays and laminations, patination, and other surface embellishments. Prerequisite: ACR 324

title: Metals: New Technologies
description: New technologies in metalsmithing. Extended study of contemporary technologies such as electroforming, plastics, and photoetching. Prerequisite: ACR 425.

title: Metals: Senior Project
description: Synthesis of experience in metals culminating in an exhibition of work. In addition, there must be documentation through slide portfolio and résumé. Should be taken during the final semester of undergraduate work. Prerequisite: ACR 427, permission of the metals faculty and the department chairperson.

description: Emphasizes the further exploration of fine art photography, technical and aesthetic concerns of photographic image making, and an introduction to contemporary photographic history, theories and issues. Prerequisite: ADS 231 or permission of the instructor.

description: Introduction and orientation to concepts and skills necessary for visual communication in two and three dimensions. Fundamentals of structure, color, typography, and tools are emphasized. Prerequisite: ADS 101, 102; AFA 101, 202. Open only to art majors. Offered only fall semester.

title: Typography and Image
description: Consideration of typography in relation to visual organization; color theory and its application to communication. Type and image are covered in experimental and practical formats. Prerequisite: ADS 241. Open only to art majors. Offered only spring semester.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 1
description: Studio exploration of the integration of twodimensional graphics with spatial environments. Emphasis is on conceptual spatial analysis and human activity. Prerequisite: ADS 242 and admission through successful portfolio review.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 2
description: . Investigation of structures, materials, and lighting as determinants of threedimensional communication issues. Emphasis is on threedimensional model construction. Prerequisite: ADS 324.

title: Studio Photography
description: Emphasizes the artistic manipulation of lighting equipment in the studio and on location as well as introducing the creative potential of medium and large format photography. Professional applications will also be addressed. Prerequisite: ADS 232 or permission of the instructor.

title: Advanced Studio Photography
description: Further exploration in the creative and expressive use of controlled lighting and the technical and creative attributes of medium and large format photography. Color processes and professional applications will also be addressed. Prerequisite: ADS 331, 336 or permission of the instructor.

title: Beginning Color
description: Introduction to color printing and processing. Principles, techniques, and nuances of color photography are covered with emphasis on their fine art applications. Cameras with adjustable fstops, shutterspeeds and focus are necessary. Prerequisite: ADS 232 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Color Photography
description: Focus on ideas and assigned problems expressed through color photography. Basic knowledge of processing color film and color prints is necessary. Prerequisite: ADS 232, 336 or permission of the instructor.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: Exploration of creative thematic development through all stages of the design process. Technical elements of type specification, computer implementation, graphic design production and printing are considered. Prerequisite: ADS 242; admission to the graphic design sequence through portfolio review. Open only to graphic design majors.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Concentrated problem analysis emphasizing symbology, typography, and image development. Continued integration of computers in the design process. Prerequisite: ADS 341. Open only to graphic design majors.

title: Three-Dimensional Communication Design 4
description: Advanced design problem research stressing the interaction of creative threedimensional communication design within the constraints of the design profession. Professional portfolio preparation is emphasized. Prerequisite: ADS 426. Parallel: ADS 480.

description: Further exploration and experimentation in the manipulation of video imagery through both artistic concepts and techniques. The use of video in performance art and installation situations will be addressed. Prerequisite: ADS 435 or permission of the instructor.

title: Graphic Design 4

title: Special Topics in Graphic Design
description: Intensive exploration of strategies and visual development within specific design areas. Could include computer, letterpress, exhibition and signage, packaging, typography, publications, illustration, or development of concept and content. Prerequisite: ADS 341 or permission of the instructor. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Graphic Design Practicum
description: Problem solving within and outside of the university community. Group and individual projects for nonprofit clients. Requires portfolio review and permission of the instructor. Prerequisite: ADS 341. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Design Thesis
description: Intensive study with research and resolution of a current problem in twoor threedimensional design or photography. Thesis must be arranged with a design or photography faculty advisor. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Design
description: Group or individual investigation and experiences in the fine arts beyond the scope of regular course work. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Understanding Art
description: Introduction to the basic studio processes of drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. Lecture and studio experiences related to the understanding of the elements and principles of art and methods of art criticism. Not open to art majors.

title: Introduction to Art Education
description: Introduction to art education as a teaching profession. Emphasizes investigating artistic growth of normal and special populations and the materials, techniques, tools, art concepts, and strategies appropriate for teaching art to such students. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202. Open only to art majors.

title: Art in the Elementary School
description: Designed to acquaint students with current teachinglearning strategies in art education. Stresses the developmental stages of artistic growth, curriculum planning, evaluation, aesthetic awareness, and craft media and techniques. Prerequisite: AED 200. Not open to art majors.

title: Art Curriculum and Instruction
description: Designed to develop art students' abilities to make artcurricular judgments by developing artcurriculum plans and designing art experiences. Prerequisite: AED 201 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Art Teaching and Learning Practicum
description: Direct experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating teaching strategies. Includes observation of students participating in an artrelated environment. Laboratory teaching time is arranged. Prerequisite: AED 304 for majors; permission of the department chairperson for minors.

title: Classroom Use of Methods and Materials: Art
description: A study of classroom management techniques, introductory involvement in teaching art, evaluation of instructional activities, and discussion of rationale for the inclusion of art in the secondary public school curriculum. Topics will be developed in the context of field experiences whenever possible. Prerequisite: AED 305 and identification to pursue a teaching curriculum for majors; permission of the department chairperson for minors. Prerequisite recommended: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Art Education
description: Permits professionally oriented art students to select and more intensively explore an area of art education. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art Education
description: Group or individual investigation and experience in the various ideas, methods, and research in art education.
