ART: FINE ARTS (AFA)

title: Drawing 1
description: Introduction to drawing, the application of basic principles and elements of art as they relate to drawing concepts. Emphasis will be on the development of perceptual awareness and familiarity with a broad range of media and techniques. Parallel recommended: ADS 101. Open only to art majors and minors.

title: Drawing 2
description: Life drawing. Intensive study of the human figure. Descriptive, expressive, and interpretive methods of imaging the figure are explored, and a variety of materials and techniques are introduced. Preiequisite: AFA 101. Parallel: ADS 102.

title: Painting 1
description: Introduction to painting: study of basic considerations of image making with oil paint. Focuses on media, techniques, design elements, and concepts. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Painting 2
description: Explorations in painting designed to build on initial experiences by studio practice and through slide lectures on contemporary painting. Prerequisite: AFA 211.

title: Watercolor 1
description: Exploration of materials and techniques of transparent watercolor as they apply to the solution of painting problems. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Watercolor 2
description: Continued exploration of painting problems in watercolor with emphasis on the unique character of the medium. Prerequisite: AFA 217.

title: Sculpture 1
description: Introduction to traditional and contemporary sculpture. The materials associated with additive, subtractive, and substitution techniques will be demonstrated. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Sculpture 2
description: Continued exploration of materials used in formal sculpture; welded and forged metal, wood construction and carving, stone carving, clay, wax, and plastic. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Beginning printmaking techniques with an emphasis on intaglio and relief processes. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 1
description: Intermediatelevel printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques. Emphasizes ability to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Lithography 1
description: Fundamental processes of drawing and printing lithographs using stones and aluminum plates. Drawing and painting techniques are used to develop images. Prerequisite: AFA 231.

title: Relief Printmaking 1
description: Fundamental procedures of relief printing from the woodblock and other surfaces emphasizing the use of color and new approaches. Developed images are expected to have a relationship to this print medium. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Serigraphy 1
description: Introductory printmaking dealing with the processes of serigraphy, including the basic stencil techniques and their variations, photo silkscreen processes, and the use of color. Emphasizes the ability to deal creatively with the silkscreen process; silkscreen as a fine art form. Prerequisite: AFA 231. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Drawing 3
description: Analytical and descriptive aspects of drawing are explored. Emphasizes thematic and conceptual development and encourages experimentation with a broad range of techniques and materials. Prerequisite: ADS 102; AFA 202.

title: Drawing 4
description: Drawing experiences exploring varied materials, methods and concepts. Emphasis on developing a more personalized visual statement. Prerequisite: AFA 303.

title: Painting 3
description: Individualized instruction aimed at the continued mastery of technical skills and progress toward the solution ofpictorial and conceptual problems. Prerequisite: AFA 212.

title: Painting 4
description: Continued interest in the development of technical skills and the solution of pictorial problems with new emphasis on individual creative solutions. Prerequisite: AFA 313.

title: Painting 5
description: Emphasis is on advancing from technical proficiency toward the development of individual conceptual goals relating to painting. Prerequisite: AFA 314.

title: Water Media
description: Advanced study in water media on paper to expand painting skills while narrowing the search for personally significant imagery. Prerequisite: AFA 218. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Sculpture: Introduction to Casting
description: Introduction to and emphasis on the basic techniques and concepts of mold making and casting aluminum, bronze, and plastics. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Sculpture: Wood
description: Introduction to wood fabrication, shaping, and finishing as it applies to functional and nonfunctional objects. Prerequisite: AFA 221.

title: Sculpture: Casting and Mold Making
description: Continuation of AFA 323. Advanced casting and moldmaking procedures. Individual development of the concepts and techniques associated with the casting process. Prerequisite: AFA 323.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 2
description: Advanced printmaking dealing with basic intaglio techniques including line etching, drypoint, engraving, softground, and aquatint. Openended problem solving and in; depth study emphasizing abilities to deal creatively and conceptually with the technical process. Prerequisite: AFA 241

title: Lithography 2
description: Further development and investigation of the processes of lithography, including color. Exploration of stone and metal plate techniques. Prerequisite: AFA 251.

title: Drawing 5
description: Continuation of the drawing experience for the more advanced emphasizing greater expertise in drawing skills while also encouraging research, experimentation and thematic exploration. Prerequisite: AFA 304.

title: Drawing 6
description: Advanced drawing, stressing problem solving and research with an increased expectation of aesthetic, technical and conceptual proficiency with each successive enrollment. Prerequisite: AFA 405. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Fine Arts
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Painting 6
description: Individualized instruction, continuing the emphasis on student identification and development of !Personal concepts in painting. Prerequisite: AFA 315.

title: Sculpture: Advanced Materials
description: Individual instruction and supervision of experimentation in traditional and nontraditional materials. Prerequisite: AFA 222 or 323 or 324.

title: Sculpture: Advanced Problems
description: Designed to extend technical understanding and aesthetic development beyond the fundamental level. Prerequisite: AFA 425 or permission of the instructor. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Intaglio Printmaking 3
description: Advanced printmaking emphasizing aesthetic decision making involving the intaglio process through the knowledge of technique and use of personal artistic choices. Prerequisite: AFA 342. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Lithography 3
description: Investigation of additional drawing and painting techniques as they relate to lithography. Further development of printing skills and the lithographic image. Prerequisite: AFA 352. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Project in Drawing
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in drawing, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 18 credit hours in drawing, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Painting
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in painting, with a student exhibition and supporting written composition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: AFA 416, 18 credit hours in painting, sponsorship by an art faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Sculpture
description: A synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experiences in sculpture, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 21 credit hours in sculpture, sponsorship by a sculpture faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Senior Project in Printmaking
description: Synthesis and culmination of undergraduate studio experience in printmaking, with a student exhibition as the concluding effort. Prerequisite: 27 credit hours in printmaking, sponsorship by a printmaking faculty member, and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Seminar in Fine Arts
description: Individual investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Art
description: A General Studies course that, through a survey of art and artifacts from ancient through modern times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of painting, sculpture, and architecture. Open only to students not majoring in art.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. Prehistoric through the end of European Middle Ages.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. From the fifteenth century to the present.

title: History of Three-Dimensional Design
description: Interdisciplinary study of threedimensional design and function as applied to graphic design, exhibition design, architecture, and industrial design from the eighteenth century to the present with an emphasis on American and European design. Prerequisite: sophomore standing. Open only to art majors.

title: Art in the United States 1
description: Investigation of the role visual culture has played in the United States as Americans attempted to situate themselves geographically, culturally, economically, and politically within their own society and within the world at large from circa 1600 to circa 1876. Open to all students.

title: Art in the United States 2
description: Traces the evolution in the United States of American visual arts from circa 1876 to 1945 within the context of important social, historical, and intellectual events. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Early Civilizations
description: Art and architecture of cultures of the ancient Near East and Egypt. Use of archeological data, visual evidence, and literary records to reconstruct built environments. Special emphasis is given to the cultural significance of monumental architecture, sculpture, painting, and diverse minor arts. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Aegean and the Greeks
description: Bronze Age through the Hellenistic period, covering architecture, pottery, painting, sculpture, minor arts, and the interrelationships of the Aegean Islands and Greek mainland. Archeological data are discussed in terms of revelations about the areas' artistic and cultural development. Open to all students.

title: Art of Rome
description: Art and architecture of early Rome and the Republic to the Late Empire. Architecture and urbanism as vehicles for the political and cultural extension of the empire to the barbarian West and the Hellenized East; missionary role of historic reliefs; Roman concepts of personality and portraiture; and the growth of luxury arts: ornament, interior decoration, and collecting.

title: Early Medieval Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture from the fourth through the tenth centuries in relation to the religious, political, and technological conditions of theperiod. Rural northwest Europe will be discussed in relation to urban societies in the East. Periods to be covered include early Christian, Merovingian, Carolingian, Ottonian, and Byzantine. Open to all students.

title: Late Medieval Art
description: European art and architecture from the eleventh through the fourteenth centuries. Competing claims of royal and religious sponsors; shifts in the center of production from rural to urban markets, monasteries to bishops' towns, in a period of economic advance, political transformation, and social unrest. Open to all students.

title: Northern European Art 1300-1600
description: Northern European Renaissance art as a specifically northern mode of expression and representation reflecting social, political, religious, and other cultural particularities of specific areas (France, Germany, and southern and northern Netherlands).

title: Art of the Italian Renaissance 1300-1600
description: Art and architecture examined in terms of style, cultural meaning, context, and ideolo gy. Investigation of conditions of art production, change in role of artist, relationship between art theory and practice, and the question or concept of Renaissance.

title: Early Modern Europe 1: Art from 1600 to 1750
description: Exploration of art and architecture of Europe, from the Counter-Reformation shrine of St. Peter to Louis XIV's palace at Versailles; from the Jesuit altarpieces in Antwerp to the Dutch Republic of Vermeer and Rembrandt and more. Italy, Spain, France, Germany, England, Flanders, Netherlands. Open to all students.

title: Early Modern Europe 2: Art from 1750 to 1850
description: Art and architecture in the era of enlightenment and revolution, age of Napoleon, Restoration, reaction, reform, economic advance, and social unrest. From country gardens to urban boulevards, rococo, neoclassicism, romanticism, historicism, realism, and impressionism, England, France, Germany, Italy, Spain. Open to all students.

title: Modern Art
description: Pan-European investigation of the visual arts from French impressionism to the post-World War II abstract expressionists. Special emphasis is on cultural definitions of modernity and modernism and the appearance and ideologies of the avant garde. Open to all students.

title: Contemporary Art
description: Exploration of ideas and issues surrounding the production, reception, marketing, interpretation, and criticism of painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, installations, performance, and video and other mixed media since World War II. International in scope. Open to all students.

title: Film History and Criticism
description: Emphasizes the understanding of cinematic works through the analysis of styles and techniques employed by filmmakers. The historical evolution of these styles and techniques will be addressed, as well as social, cultural, and political influences. Open to all students.

title: History of Photography
description: Introduction to problems in theory, analysis, and history of photography. Study of institutional and discursive orders in whichphotography functions and produces meaning. Exploration of new forms of critical photographic practice. Open to all students.

title: History of Landscape Painting
description: In depth survey of the major schools of landscape painting beginning with ancient Rome and continuing up to the present time. Political and economic conditions leading to the rebirth of landscape painting in the Renaissance will be discussed. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in History of Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in art histo with emphasis on those not covered ry in other courses (women in art, history of museums and collecting, problems in methodology, etc.). Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Graphic Design
description: Detailed analysis of graphic design from the late nineteenth century to the present, with emphasis on European and American design. Influential movements, artists, designers, and technology that shape current design thinking will be highlighted. Prerequisite: ADS 242 or permission of the instructor. Open only to art majors.

title: Special Topics in American Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in American art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Ancient Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in ancient art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Medieval Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in medieval art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Renaissance and Early Modern Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in Renaissance or early modern art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students.

title: Special Topics in Modern and Contemporary Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in modern or contemporary art with focus on subjects not emphasized in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. Open to all students. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Prehistoric and Non-Western Art
description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in prehistoric or non- Western art with focus on subjects not covered in other courses. Exact content will be announced before each offering. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Independent Study in Art History
description: Designed for professionally oriented students, allowing them to select and explore more intensively a special topic. Prerequisite: sponsorship by an art faculty member and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Seminar in Art History
description: Individual or group investigation and experience in the fine arts. Prerequisite: completion of 30 hours of credit in art or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Computers
description: Introduction to image, pagination, and wordprocessing programs applicable to the visual arts. Concentration on Macintosh hardware, including scanners and output devices. Concentrates on building technical knowledge and skills for computer use. Creative development is considered. Open only to art majors.

title: Advanced Use of Computers in the Fine Arts
description: Advanced study in the use of computers in the visual arts. Includes specific study of imageenhancing technologies and computeraided design. Prerequisite: ART 101; permission of the instructor. Open only to art majors. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Computer Imaging
description: Advanced exploration and application of computer technology as related to the creation and production of threedimensional designs. Computer imaging, animation, and video are emphasized. Prerequisite: ART 201. Open only to art majors. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Department of Art Internship
description: Ten or more weeks of supervised summer work related experience. A selective review process must be passed before enrolling. Paid professional experience under supervision of department and professional sponsor. Prerequisite: portfolio review by area faculty, overall gradepoint average of 2.75, junior standing, and permission of the department chairperson. Open only to , art majors. SCHOOL OF MUSICe G. title: Introduction to Music
description: A General Studies course that, through a survey of musical forms and compositions from early through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, offers an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the broad range of musical creativity. Open only to students not majoring in music.

title: Music and Popular Culture in America
description: A survey of the origins and development of popular music in America. Discussion includes blues, jazz, musical theatre, and rock. Emphasis is on cultural rather than technical aspects of music.

title: Survey of Music Literature
description: Survey of styles, forms, and masterworks of music with emphasis on the period 1700 to 1975. One hour lecture and two hours directed listening each week. Required for majors and minors. Open only to music majors and minors or by permission.

title: Music History
description: The development of music from its beginnings through 1750. Origins, growth of early polyphony, instrumental music. Changes in style during medieval, Renaissance, and baroque periods. Prerequisite: MUHIS 200 or departmental permission.

title: Music History
description: Changes in music from the preclassic period through the present and trends of the twentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 200 and 330 or departmental permission.

title: Honors Colloquium in Music
description: Readings, reports, and discussions of various aspects of music. Open only to students in the Honors Program.

title: Collegium Musicum
description: The study, realization, and performance of medieval, Renaissance, and baroque music. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. Open only to students in the Honors Program.

title: Piano Literature
description: Survey of the standard literature for the piano from J. S. Bach through the midtwentieth century. Prerequisite: MUHIS 330 and 331 or permission of the instructor.

title: Music in the Baroque Era
description: The vocal and instrumental music of western Europe during the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, including figured bass, opera, oratorio and cantata, and the development of such instrumental genres as concerto, sonata, and suite. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Music in Preclassic and Classic Eras
description: Vocal and instrumental music of the eighteenth century, including the various styles that marked the transition from baroque to classical music, the rise of comic opera, and the development of the symphony, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and keyboard literature. ' Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Music in the Romantic Era
description: Vocal and instrumental music in Western civilization in the nineteenth century, emphasizing lieder, choral, operatic, piano, chamber, and orchestral literature. Studies important composers and works from the various periods: early, middle, late, and post- Romanticism. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331 or permission of the director of the school.

title: Opera History from 1780 to 1980
description: Types of opera and changing styles from the mideighteenth century to the present. Works from the standard repertoire will be considered in detail, and students will also be encouraged to explore less familiar operas. Prerequisite: MUHIS 331.

title: Jazz History 1
description: Historic examination of jazz from 1890 to 1950. Analyzes outstanding style characteristics of each period from their beginnings to the 1950s, including ragtime, the Jazz Age, the Swing Era, and the bebop and cool periods.

title: Jazz History 2
description: Continuation of MUHIS 439, covering the 1950s through the present. Progressive fifties, the rock jazz fusions of the sixties, seventies, and eighties—today's trends.

title: History of Harpsichord Literature and Design
description: The harpsichord and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis is on baroque instruments and the music of Bach, Couperin, Handel, Rameau, and Scarlatti. The harpsichord revival, contemporary instruments, and literature. Prerequisite: previous keyboard study.

title: Independent Study in Music History
description: An opportunity for superior students to do guided reading and intensive study in topics in music history of particular interest to them and for which provision is not made by the regular course offerings of the department. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester.

title: Workshop in Music History and Musicology
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music history and musicology. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: History of Organ Literature and Design
description: The organ and its music from the Renaissance. Emphasis is on baroque, romantic, and contemporary instruments and literature. Field trips to nearby instruments. Prerequisite: MUHIS 100 or 331.

title: Choral Music and Hymnody of the Church
description: Hymns, anthems, motets, cantatas, and oratorios from the fifteenth century to the present; their musical, theological, and liturgical contexts and contemporary use. MUSIC ENGINEERING

title: Introduction to Electronic Music
description: Topics include musique concrete, analog sound generation and processing, voltage controlled systems. In addition to lectures, a minimum of four hours of laboratory time is required each week. Projects include sound synthesis, sound structuring, and analysis.

title: Compositional Practices in Electronic and Electro-Acoustic Music
description: Survey of the development of composition using the electronic medium. Topics include the study of electronic instruments, the analysis of music forms and structure in electronic and electroacoustic compositions, and the study of computerassisted composition.

title: Music Perception
description: An introduction to basic psychoacoustics and psychophysics. Topics include the ear as a frequency analyzer, the auditory pathway, fundamentals of auditory perception, special problems in the perception of music and music structures.

title: Sound Synthesis 1
description: Intermediate course in sound synthesis. Topics include FM and AM synthesis, filtration, basic mixing, iteration and reverberation, and the development of basic analog and digital electronic virtual instruments. Minimum of three hours of lab experience required weekly. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; MUMET 225.

title: Introduction to Recording Technology
description: An introduction to the basics of recording technology. Topics include the analog tape recorder, the tape medium, microphone design, and microphone placement. Prerequisite: MUSTH 125, 212; PHYCS 122.

title: Introduction to Computer Music
description: An intermediate course in computer music. Topics include computer systems appropriate for music composition, sound synthesis, and analysis. Computer and music instrument communications are introduced. Intermediate projects in music programming are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212; PHYCS 122.

title: Recording Workshop
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Individual problems in recording master tapes of solo, ensemble, and large group repertoire. Each project requires seminar and laboratory participation. Prerequisite: MUMET 326. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Sound Synthesis 2
description: An advanced course in sound synthesis. Topics include the development of complex virtual electronic instruments and their control. Structured sound projects are required. A minimum of five hours of lab experience each week is required. Prerequisite MUMET 325, 327.

title: Advanced Recording Technology
description: An advanced course in recording technology. Topics include multitrack recording, multichannel mixing, signal processing, and problems in multiple microphone arrays and stereo imaging. A minimum of 3 hours of laboratory experience is required. Prerequisite: MUM ET 326.

title: Advanced Projects in Computer Music
description: An advanced course in computer music applications. Topics include problems in MIDI communications, projects in algorhythmic composition, and problems in telemusic communications. Prerequisite: MUMET 425.

title: Production Workshop
description: An advanced course in technical applications of music production. This is an independentprojectoriented course. Projects require a production product such as a technical demonstration, a broadcast quality program, an album, or an intermedia performance. Prerequisite: MUMET 426.

title: Jazz: A Multicultural Legacy
description: Study of the development of jazz with emphasis on multicultural contributions and interdisciplinary context—historical, political, economic, and social.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: A major performing ensemble, rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are Wind Ensemble, Symphonic Band, Marching Show Band, Basketball Pep Band, Symphony Orchestra, and Jazz Ensemble I.

title: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are Concert Band and Jazz Ensembles II and HI.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Major performing ensembles normally rehearsing five hours a week. Included in this category are the Concert Choir, Chamber Choir, Opera Chorus, University Singers, and Lab Choir.

title: Large Vocal Ensemble
description: Organizations normally rehearsing two hours a week. Included in this category are University Chorus, Women's Chorus, and the Statesmen. title: The Singing Actor
description: Acting techniques specifically related to musical theatre and opera. Vocal exercises, movement, song interpretation. Preparation of roles and scenes for laboratory presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Study and performance of works for the musical theatre combining the art forms of music, drama, dance, and stagecraft as a performer or technician. A total of 10 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Musical Theatre in America
description: A study of the history of the American musical theatre. A general overview of the repertoire.

title: Workshop in Music
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on specialized interdisciplinary topics in music. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Recital
description: Attendance at recitals and concerts as specified in the music student handbook is the basis for earning recital credit.

title: Principles of Music Teaching: Seminar and Practicum
description: Overview of the music teaching profession with emphasis on basic terminology, instructional procedures, and curricular concepts. Practicum includes directed observation, demonstration, and supervised participation experiences in K-12 music programs.

title: Brass Techniques
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on two or more brass instruments. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, and other specialized topics related to brass instruction in school settings.

title: Woodwind Techniques
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on flute, clarinet, and saxophone (minimum of two instruments). Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, and other specialized topics related to woodwind instruction in school settings.

title: Woodwind Techniques 2
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on oboe and bassoon. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, and other specialized topics related to double reed instruction in school settings.

title: Percussion Techniques
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on concert percussion (snare drum, bass drum, cymbals), timpani, and keyboard percussion. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, and other specialized topics related to percussion instruction in school settings.

title: String Techniques
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on two or more string instruments. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, and other specialized topics related to string instruction in school settings.

title: Voice Techniques
description: Development of fundamental vocal performance technique. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, vocal anatomy and acoustics, care of the voice, and other specialized topics related to singing instruction in school settings.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary Classroom
description: Development of basic music reading skills and classroom and keyboard instrument skills; focus on methods for presenting appropriate musical experiences and materials to children. Open only to elementary education, special education and early childhood education majors.

title: Field Experience in Music Teaching
description: Observation and application of specialized music teaching techniques. Prerequisite: MUSED 200. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term. Open only to students registered in MUSED 351, 352, 353, 355, or 356.

title: Elementary General Music Methods 1
description: Introduction to general music for grades K-6. Explores the philosophy of general music teaching, concepts and skills, use of materials and equipment, and specialized approaches to elementary music education. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Elementary General Music Methods 2
description: Continuing study of music teaching methodology for grades K-6. Emphasis on curriculum development. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: Secondary General Music Methods
description: Focuses on philosophy, techniques, and materials needed to teach a required general music course in middle and high school settings. Emphasizes teaching skill development as well as the musical characteristics and needs of adolescents. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Instrumental Music Methods
description: Examines issues related to the teaching of instrumental music. Special emphasis on program goals and curriculum development, instructional planning, and materials and techniques designed for teaching musical concepts in performance class or lesson settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Choral Music Methods
description: Examines issues related to the teaching of choral music. Special emphasis on program goals and curriculum development, instructional planning, and materials and techniques designed for teaching musical concepts in performance class or lesson settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Administration of School Music Programs
description: Explores practical ideas, print resources, and computer applications related to efficient administration of instrumental and choral music programs. Topics include recruitment, handbooks, scheduling, budgets, purchasing, libraries, inventories, fund raising, parent groups, facilities, concerts, and trips. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Instrumental Laboratory
description: Laboratory ensemble taken as participant first, then as a conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 390. Focuses on instrumental rehearsal techniques and instrumental literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or term.

title: Choral Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus taken as participant first, then as conductor in conjunction with MUSPE

title: Orchestra Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of orchestra literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recordings. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Band Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of band literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recordings. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Choral Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of choral literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recording. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education
description: Study of musical development from birth to age eight, with emphasis on the preschool years. Appropriate musical play and small group activities are explored. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Approaches to the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications, a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: Organization and administration of marching bands in school settings. Principles and objectives, show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite: MUSED 200; MUSCH 340.

title: Directing Musicals, Madrigals, and Jazz Show Choirs
description: Examines issues related to organizing and directing madrigal singers, vocal jazz ensembles, swing and show choirs, and musical productions at the middle and high school levek Topics include auditions, rehearsal techniques, choreography, literature, scheduling, performing, and management. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Instrument Maintenance and Repair
description: Laboratory setting used to develop practical skills in cleaning, lubricating, and repairing wind, percussion, and string instruments. Focuses on proper diagnostic techniques, tool and material selection, and minor repair procedures. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Methods of Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods of teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level or permission of the director of the school.

title: Introduction to Orff-Schulwerk
description: Explores the principles of the childcentered approach to music developed by Carl Orff. Classroom activities involve movement, rhythm, speech, and the creative use of instruments. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; opportunities to sing and conduct standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Introduction to Dalcroze Eurhythmics
description: Introduction to the philosophy, principles, and techniques of Dalcroze Eurhythmics. Emphasizes the application of movement techniques to music teaching in elementary and secondary schools. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosophical principles and the practical applications of these principles in teaching music in the elementary school form the framework of this course designed for music specialists.

title: Jazz Ensembles Techniques
description: Designed to introduce the style characteristics of jazz performance. Includes preparation in the administration and teaching of jazz ensembles in school settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200 except for jazz/commercial music minors.

title: Class Guitar
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on the guitar for classroom and social use. Focuses on chordal accompaniment styles and their application to folk, popular, and children's song literature.

title: Teaching Multicultural Music
description: Exploration of music from various ethnic groups and cultures. Emphasizes techniques and materials to present music from various cultures to elementary and secondary students. Includes teaching projects and integration with traditional music curricula. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: An opportunity for superior students to conduct intensive study and research in a particular component of music education. Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Music Education
description: Consideration of topics, problems, and issues in music education of special interest but not formally treated in other courses. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Workshop in Music Education
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music education. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Small Ensemble (Woodwinds)
description: Players of woodwind instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of allperiods with emphasis on chamber music style of playing.

title: Small Ensemble (Brass)
description: Players of brass instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of the brass ensemble literature. May include trios and quartets of like instruments, or quintets, sextets, and octets of mixed brasses.

title: Small Ensemble (Percussion)
description: Players of percussion instruments are organized into small groups for the study and performance of literature designed for their public performance. May range in size from trios and quintets to larger ensembles.

title: Small Ensemble (String)
description: Players of string instruments are organized into small groups according to proficiency for the study of music of all periods with emphasis on the chamber music style of playing.

title: Small Ensemble (Harp)
description: Groups of harpists are organized to perform the specialized literature for this unusual ensemble. Original compositions and transcriptions are presented in public performance.

title: Small Ensemble (Piano)
description: Study of sonata literature in conjunction with another instrument or literature for multiple pianos. Small groups are organized according to proficiency and demands of the literature.

title: Ensemble for New Music
description: Players of all instruments are organized into small groups for the study of contemporary chamber music.

title: Small Ensemble (Organ and Church Music)
description: Performance projects of interest to the organist and church musician. Reading of anthems, motets, oratorio movements; music for organ and instruments; music for graded church choirs; and conducting frOill the keyboard.

description: Quartets, sextets, octets, and multiples of these units are arranged as enrollment indicates. Music studied and performed ranges from traditional quartet literature to material appropriate for glee clubs.

title: Opera Workshop
description: Fosters appreciation of and familiarity with operatic literature through public performance of excerpts from chamber and standard operas, either as a soloist or as a member of the opera chorus. Prerequisite: audition. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Popular Vocal Styles
description: Assists students in developing individual popular singing styles. Concentrates on all facets of performance including audienceperformer rapport, the performeraccompanist relationship, and microphone techniques. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Opera Productions
description: Study and public performance of standard operas of all periods. Combines the art forms of music, drama, stagecraft, and dance in the study of coaching, acting, and stage technique. Prerequisite: audition or previous experience. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Service Playing and Church Music Administration
description: Hymn playing and anthem accompaniments; formulation of adult and children's choirs in churches; congregational singing service planning. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112 and oneyear of organ study, or permission of the instructor.

title: Instrumental Conducting and Rehearsal Techniques
description: Score interpretation, rehearsal preparation, and teaching strategies in a laboratory setting. Practical experiences include warmups; tuning procedures; error detection; solving problems of balance, blend, and intonation; and performance practice. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Chord Conducting and Rehearsal Techniques
description: Score interpretation, rehearsal preparation, and teaching strategies in a laboratory setting. Practical experiences include warmups; error detection; solving problems of balance, blend, and intonation; and performance practice. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Diction for Singers
description: Beginning voice students will learn effective pronunciation of English and Italian using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Techniques in producing vowel sounds and consonant articulation unique to the sung work will be emphasized. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Wind and Percussion Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for wind and percussion instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with winds or percussion as their major instrument.

description: Music and materials for stringed instruments and harp instruction. Includes audition and recital te preparation, repertoire, practice chniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with strings or harp as their major instrument.

description: Music and materials for piano, organ, and harpsichord instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experience. Open only to bachelor of music students with piano, organ, or harpsichord as their major instrument.

title: Guitar Literature and Pedagogy
description: Music and materials for guitar instruction. Includes audition and recital preparation, repertoire, practice techniques, and internship experienc e. Open only to bachelor of music students with guitar as their major instrument.

title: Vocal Diction and Literature
description: Advanced study of diction in major western languages as it pertains to singing, and applications in performance of music literature for singers. Prerequisite: MUSPE 398 or permission of the instructor.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom
description: Application of melodyharmony relation ship to instrumental performance. Students will be expected to pray numerous standard tunes and jazz standards, and improvise with competency determined by the instructor. All chords, scales, sixths, sevenths, ninths, elevenths, thirteenths, modes, and transposition of modes.

title: Improvisation in the Jazz Idiom 2
description: Songs from swing, bebop, cool, and contemporary periods. Exploration of unitonal, unimodal, polytonal, polymodal melodies with small instrumental groups. Innovations in jazz improvisation. Musicians to be studied include Chick Corea, Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, Joe Farrell, and Miles Davis. Prerequisite: MUSPE 456.

title: Jazz Piano Class 1
description: All triads with the added sixth or sixth chords played in block chordal harmony. All inversions of these chords and transpositions of chord types through four sharps and flats; introduction of the four types of seventh chords.

title: Jazz Piano Class 2
description: Continuation of MUSPE 460. Completion of seventh chords, inversion in remaining keys; additional experiences include minor seventh (flat 5), augmented seventh, and minor/major sevenths. All ninth chords, eleventh chords, and thirteenth chords played melodically and harmonically. Prerequisite: MUSPE 460.

title: Continuo Playing and Keyboard Improvisation
description: Development of facility in reading from figured basses or improvisation in the church service, free harmonization of hymns. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or MUSPE 226 or 377. description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Senior Recital
description: Taken during the senior year by students with a performance mayor. Students will present a full recital as approved by their area committees and the director of the school.

title: Independent Study in Musical Performance

title: Introduction to Communication Skills in Music
description: Recommended for students deficient in elementary music language. Provides simplest basic concepts, symbols, readingskill drills, and terminology with supporting historical and systems information. Placement by level of experience.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Training
description: Indepth study and application of sight singing techniques, dictation, chord recognition, error detection, and related activities. Placement by level of experience. Parallel: MUSTH 111.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Training
description: Continuation of MUSTH 101 including more advanced sight singing, dictation, chord recognition, error detection, and related activities. Prerequisite: MUSTH 101.

title: Music Theory
description: Indepth study of music fundamentals including rhythm, melodic structure, fourpart harmony, elementary harmonic and structural analysis accompanied by writing, listening, and score study. Placement by level of experience.Must be taken in sequence. Parallel: MUSTH 101.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 111 including more advanced fourpart writing, analysis, score study, and listening. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Acoustics
description: An introduction to physical acoustics with an emphasis on music and audio applications. Topics included are wave mechanics, acoustic measurements, tone and timbre analysis, tuning and temperament, and sound transduction.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Training
description: Continuation of MUSTH 102 emphasizing chromatic materials, modulating lines, fourpart dictation and aural analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 102.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Training
description: Continuation of MUSTH 201 emphasizing advanced chromatic and twentieth century aural materials. Prerequisite: MUSTH 201.

title: Music Theory
description: Emphasis is on nineteenthcentury procedures through studies of compositional styles and analysis. Required mastering of diatonic and chromatic modulations, and higher hierarchical chordal structures in tonal context and traditional forms. Advanced laboratory drill in analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 112.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 211, emphasizing practices of the later nineteenth century and the twentieth century. Mastery of basic understanding of postromantic, impressionistic, expressionistic, neoclassical, serial, and other contemporary music required. Continued laboratory analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Music Theory: Form and Analysis
description: An indepth study of large forms through intensive analysis, listening, research, and writing. Emphasis is on individual student work completed outside class to develop abilities in theoretical and composition investigation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. Open only to music majors.

title: Music Theory: Eighteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Indepth study of eighteenthcentury counterpoint in which skills are developed in analyzing and composing canons, inventions, and fugues. Prerequisite: MUSTH 311. Open only to music majors.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Development of basic craft through the writing of shorter instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or by permission of the division chairperson with the recommendation of the theory instructor.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Choral Arranging
description: Scoring for choir and choral ensembles. Gives particular attention to voicing, soloistic treatment of voices, texts, and other elements of traditional and contemporary scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arranging
description: Scoring for symphonic band, wind ensemble, and other related groups. Emphasis is on instrumentation, transposition, voicing, doubling, soloistic treatment, and scoring from plano or similar reduction. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Commercial Arranging
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques used in commercial music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms with particular attention given to the composerarranger in the recordingstudio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: Laboratory for skill development in arranging. Individualized and projectoriented to prepare musicians to score spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, and background and mood sequences, as well as to compose for TV, films, radio, and media. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shaping forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, notation, and other elements that characterize the compositional practices of twentiethcentury music. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Topics in Music Theory
description: A topic to be announced in advance that will be drawn from the compositional practices of the seventeenth, eighteenth, nineteenth, or twentieth century and discussed through selected works taken from the literature. Prerequisite: MUSTH 312. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Exercises in contrapuntal writing designed to develop sensitivity to sixteenthcentury polyphonic practice. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Analytical Technique
description: The development of techniques for the identification and analysis of significant compositional elements as determined by the musical context. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Continuation of MUSTH 332 and the writing of larger, longer works. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322.

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH 431. Prerequisite: MUSTH 431.

title: Composition
description: Composition in the electronic media. Presents composition techniques involving electronic and electroacoustic instruments. Studies the synthesizer, the computer, and the electronic processing of acoustic sound as schema and materials for musical composition. Prerequisite: MUSTH 322. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Music Theory
description: Study of a theoretical topic using readings, analysis, and research. Prerequisite: permission of the division chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Theory Seminar
description: Discussions, analyses, and projects concerning advanced theoretical problems from all periods and styles. Specific topics to be announced one semester in advance. Prerequisite: permission of the division chairperson.

title: Workshop in Music Theory and Composition
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music theory and composition. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Composition-Project Recital
description: Public performance of compositions completed in composition degree program or an indepth lecture or lecturerecital describing a completed music engineering and technology project. title: Introduction to Dance History
description: Provides an understanding and appreciation of dance as an expression of people's imaginative and creative urges. Dance from the primitive to the twentieth century is explored within its social and historical context.

title: Ballet 1
description: Classes in ballet technique for beginners, with special emphasis on body placement and alignment. Open to all students. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Ballet 2
description: Classes in ballet technique for advanced beginners, with special emphasis on the use of epaulement. Prerequisite: DANCE 110 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 1
description: Introduction to modern dance techniques and performance skills with emphasis on alignment and body awareness in moving through space. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 2
description: Designed to continue development of the basic techniques and dance performance skills for advanced beginners in modern dance. Prerequisite: DANCE 120 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Luigi: Jazz Dance Technique and Philosophy of Movement
description: An introduction to dance technique and theatre movement for the nondancer interested in a movement technique philosophy. The movement technique can be used for theatre dance or athletic warmups, and the philosophy applies to all learning and performing situations. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Musical Theatre Tap Styles
description: Introduces basic meters used in musical theatre tap styles, such as soft shoe, waltz clog, and military. Develops tap vocabulary for performers and choreographers.

title: Jazz Styles 1
description: Continuation of jazz dance techniques on an advanced beginning level for those with some previous dance training or practical experience through performance. Prerequisite: DANCE 130 or permission of the instructor. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Ballet 3
description: Ballet technique on a beginningintermediate level for those with previous training. Prerecluisite: DANCE 111 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Ballet 4
description: Continuation of ballet technique for students on an intermediate level. Prerequisite: DANCE 210 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 3
description: Designed for students with training in modern dance and introduction to improvisational performance skills. Prerequisite: DANCE 121 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Modern 4
description: Designed to prepare students for advanced modern dance skills. Prerecruisite: DANCE 220 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Jazz 2
description: Designed for students with dance training who have interest in developing technique in various jazz styles. Prerequisite: DANCE 110, 120, or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Tap 2
description: Advanced tap dance techniques for the dance student with previous tap dance training. Prerequisite: DANCE 131 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in one semester or term.

title: Musical Theatre Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of contemporary dance style's for the Broadway and nightclub stages. Dance styles covered will change each semester. Prerequisite: DANCE 110 or 120 or 130 and 131 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance 1
description: Basic repertoire of ethnic dance steps, styles, and dances for use in performance. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Clogging
description: American ethnic dance form known as clogging. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Ball State Ballet
description: A broadbased dance company, emphasizing ballet technique, with performance interests extending from tap, jazz, and experimental to classical ballet. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open only to students by audition

title: Dance Theatre
description: Experience in performing with a company of dancers who plan, rehearse, and perform both informal and formal dance presentations. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open only by audition.

title: International Folk Dance Company
description: Opportunity for students with interest in folk dance to learn and perform dances from many different countries. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. Open by audition and permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choreography 1
description: Work in choreographing dance by exploring musical and dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 211, 221, 241 or permission of the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Ballet History
description: A survey of ballet from its inception to the present time. Prerequisite: DANCE 100.

title: Ballet 5
description: Intermediateadvanced level of ballet technique. Prerequisite: DANCE 211 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Ballet 6
description: Advanced ballet technique. Prerecluisite: DANCE 310 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in one semester or term.

title: Partnering
description: Study of the art of partnering. Prerequisite: DANCE 211 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 5
description: Advanced modern dance techniques. Prerequisite: 221 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Modern 6
description: Designed to continue development of advanced modern dance performance skills and improvisational techniques. Prerequisite: DANCE 221 or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned; but no more than 2 in one

title: Jazz 3
description: Advanced jazz dance emphasizing technique work in complex rhythms, syncopation, jazz jumps, and jazz turns.. Prerequzstte: DANCE 230 (4 hours) or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Ethnic Dance Styles
description: Indepth study of the stylistic uniqueness of a particular ethnic region. Covers three to four styles during the semester. Prerequisite: DANCE 241. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Notation
description: Introduction to dance notation with an emphasis on such contemporary notation systems as Labonotation and Benesh. Prerequisite: DANCE 211, 221, 241.

title: Dance Production
description: Designed to acquaint students with various technical andperformance elements of dance production. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Choreography 2
description: Work in choreographing traditional and nontraditional dance forms. Prerequisite: DANCE 287 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Dance Pedagogy
description: Indepth study of teaching methods for beginning, intermediate, and advanced dance students, includes pedagogy from preschool through adult level. Includes rehearsal technique for performance preparation. Prerequisite: DANCE 211, 221, 241. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Dance Practicum
description: Intensive experience in stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, dance management, and other elements ofproduction. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Creative Project
description: Designed as a project in choreography for advanced dance students. Prerequisite: senior standing, permission of the department chairperson.

title: Directed Study in Dance
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects related to dance that meet the approval of the dance faculty. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Performance Studies
description: The study of prose fiction, drama, and poetry through the medium of solo performance. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles to be announced before each semester. Prerequisite: PS 230. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Chamber Theatre
description: A directing course featuring the staging of narrative literature. Prerequisite: PS 230.

title: Readers Theatre
description: A directing course focusing on the creation and staging of nondramatic literature and compilation scripts. Prerequisite: PS 230.

title: Performance of Prose Fiction
description: Indepth study of the novel and short story through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: PS 230.

title: Performance of Poetry
description: The study of poetry through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: PS 230.

title: Performance of Shakespeare
description: Study of six of Shakespeare's plays through the medium of solo performance. Prerequisite: PS 230. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Performance Studies Seminar
description: A changing topics course for advanced performance studies students who wish to investigate a particular area of study in depth. Prerequisite: PS 230. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Theatre
description: A General Studies course that offers, through a survey of plays selected from the major periods of dramatic productivity from the ancient Greeks through contemporary times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, an introduction to the understanding and appreciation of the many faces of dramatic creativity. Open only to students not majoring in theatre.

title: Script Analysis
description: Systematic approach to play analysis with an emphasis on performance and production.

title: Computers in Theatre and Dance
description: Introduction to computer usage in theatre and dance. Emphasis is on computer competency and the development of simple computer applications.

title: Stagecraft
description: A practical introduction to the fundamentals of the crafts involved in theatre production at the school, college, and community theatre levels. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Theatrical Costuming
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of costuming for educational and community theatre with attention given to stage makeup. Two hours of lecture and three arranged hours of laboratory a week.

title: Principles of Stage Makeup
description: An investigation of the principles, techniques, and materials of stage makeup and practical experience in their application.

title: Acting 1
description: A lecturelaboratory class stressing the basic principles of acting.

title: Acting 2
description: A lecturelaboratory course on the principles of acting with major emphasis on character analysis and development. Prerequisite: THEAT 232.

title: Acting 3
description: Advanced scene study. Emphasizes actor communication, listening skills, and selfexploration through the use of voice and movement. Prerequisite: THEAT 233. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term. Open only to theatre majors and minors..

title: Theatre Practicum
description: Intensive experience in acting, stage management, scenery and costume preparation, running crews, theatre management, and other production areas. Students should complete practicums in six different areas. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: History of Theatre 1
description: Study of the Western theatre from its origins through the Renaissance, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: History of Theatre 2
description: Study of the Western theatre from the Renaissance to the foundations of modern theatre in the late nineteenth century, with emphasis on theatre architecture, production elements, theory, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Modern Theatre
description: Study of major movements in modern Western theatre since 1875, with emphasis on theoretical documents, production elements, and representative dramatic literature.

title: Theatrical Design Skills
description: A lecturelaboratory class to present basic problem solving skills involving theatrical design artwork. Emphasizes the development of technique and media competence. Prerequisite: THEAT 220.

title: Rendering for the Theatre
description: Handson individual instruction in the processes and techniques of using selected media for the rendering of scenic and costume designs for the theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 223.

title: Costume History
description: Survey of clothing from the Greeks through Art Nouveau emphasizing the design adaptation of historical clothing for practical stage usage while maintaining period authenticity.

title: Fundamentals of Stage Lighting
description: Lecturelaboratory course in the basic concepts, materials, hardware, and design principles of stage lighting. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions.

title: Audition Techniques and Repertory
description: How to select, prepare, and present appropriate material (monologues and songs) with honesty, style, and a sense of professionalism. Résumés and portfolio photo preparation are also covered, as are contracts and agents. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Acting for the Camera
description: Introduction to skills required to adapt stage acting techniques to the camera. Emphasis on simplification and communication with the director. Prerequisite: THEAT 233 and permission of the instructor. Open only to theatre majors on performance option.

title: Playwriting 1
description: Introduction to the art and craft of playwriting. Emphasizes plotting and the use of dramatic language in the writing of effective scenes, culminating in a oneact play . Prerequisite: THEAT 101 or permission of the instructor. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Directing 1
description: Theory and practice of directing for the theatre. Exercises in movement, line interpretation, creation of atmosphere, and the effective use of stage areas. Prerequisite: THEAT 100 or 101, 220, 233, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Directing for the Musical Theatre
description: A detailed examination of the selection, organization, and direction of musical theatre productions. For practical laboratory work, the student may elect to concentrate on the production problems of either a specific musical comedy or an opera. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Department of Theatre Unpaid Internship Program
description: Placement in an unpaid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in a theatre program in some capacity. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Department of Theatre Paid Internship Program
description: Placement in paid position in a semiprofessional or professional theatre for one semester in order to gain valuable practical experience by participating in a theatre program in some capacity. Prerequisite: senior standing or permission of the department chairperson. A total of 9 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Children's Theatre
description: The principles of theatre devoted to creative dramatics. Twothirds of the course is devoted to formal dramatics. A public performance will be arranged.

title: Advanced Theatre Practice
description: Students design and execute a theatre project: scenery designs, lighting, properties, acting, directing, oral interpretation, and house management. Prerequisite: 12 hours of credit in theatre courses and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Studies in American Theatre
description: An investigation of significant movements in the American professional theatre and its drama.

title: Scene Design
description: Advanced training and experience in the problems of set design and lighting for theatrical productions in many forms and styles, including elements of television design. Prerequisite: THEAT 320.

title: Theatre Costume Design
description: Practice in the research, design, and building techniques involved in the preparation of period costumes for use in theatre productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 223 and 320.

title: Stage Lighting Design
description: Training and experience in the problems of stage lighting design for the proscenium and nonproscenium stage. Practical laboratory work in stage lighting of university productions. Prerequisite: THEAT 326.

title: Styles of Acting
description: Study and performance of the styles of acting appropriate to major types of drama from antiquity to the present. Prerequisite: THEAT 234.

title: Advanced Study of Roles for Performance
description: An advanced course concentrating on the preparation of a script for performance. At all stages of preparation, students work closely with a faculty advisor of their choosing. The course will culminate in a live, adjudicated performance. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 and 433; PS 230; and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Directing 2
description: Further investigation of the work of the director with special reference to directing the various style s, modes, and periods of theatre. Prerequisite: THEAT 350 or the equivalent.

title: Creative Dramatics
description: Principles of developing original dramatizations through improvisational techniques. Students are expected to observe and work with children as well as with college adults.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop
description: Participation in the Summer Festival Theatre. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theatre Management
description: Study and practice in box office procedures, house management, publicity, and promotion as related to college, community, and professional theatres. Prerequisite: 9 hours of theatre courses.

title: Directed Study in Theatre
description: Individual and directed study of research or creative projects in design, playwriting, acting, interpretation, or directing, meeting the approval of the theatre staff.
