description: Emerging leadership styles. Theoretical and experiential bases for developing leadership skills and ethics through seminars and mentoring. Attention given to defining individual leadership styles and setting developmental goals. Open only to "Excellence in Leadership" phase one program participants. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Introduction to Personnel Services in Residence Halls
description: Principles involved in selfawareness, developing interand intrapersonal skills, and examining the development of community within the residence hall. Prerequisite: sophomore standing and permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Students as Group Leaders
description: Examines the dynamics of group leadership. Focuses on the theoretical and experiential bases for developing group leadership skills and ethics. Attention is given to involvement in student organizations through workshops and faculty mentoring. Open only to "Excellence in Leadership" phase two program participants. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Student Leaders in Community Service
description: Focuses on leadership in community services. The student will study the theoretical and experiential bases for leadership and service in the greater community beyond the campus. By working with a human services agency, the student will help meet needs and explore underlying causes of community problems. Open only to "Excellence in Leadership" phase three program participants. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term.

title: Leadership and Development of Student Organizations
description: Examines philosophical bases, group processes, and skills relevant to leadership and development of student organizations in higher education. Focuses on understanding and skills needed for effective involvement in student groups.

title: Student Leaders and Global Citizenship
description: Focuses on leadership for global citizenship. Capstone experience in identifying and addressing societal problems. Through participation in seminars and lectures and a oneday retreat, the student will prepare for leadership after college. Open only to "Excellence in Leadership" phase four program participants. A total of 2 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 1 in any one semester or term. EDUCATION: JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE (EDJHM)

title: The Junior High/Middle School Curriculum
description: Several curricular approaches appropriate for students ages 10 to 14 years will be examined in relation to current research.. Legal rights and the significance of positive human relations are studied. Direct development of alternative curricular programs and appropriate use of merging structures and nontraditional materials will be emphasized.

title: Principles of Teaching, Curriculum and Classroom Management: Middle School
description: Combines the theory and practice of teaching at the middle school level. Includes direct teaching experiences with early adolescents in public school settings; seminars concerned with such topics as curriculum, instructional strategies, legal aspects, and discipline. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205; EDPSY 250 or 251; and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Parallel: EDSEC 280.

title: Independent Study in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Independent study and research in junior high/middle school topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Instructional Strategies and Approaches in Junior High/Middle School
description: Conditions affecting the total instructional responsibilities in junior high/middle schools are studied. Students are required to develop skills in individualizing instruction to serve the full range of students, the ability to work cooperatively with other professional personnel, and instructional techniques and evaluation procedures especially appropriate for junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205; EDPSY 251 or 351.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Junior High/Middle School
description: Designed to prepare prospective junior high/middle school educators to cope with discipline problems in all junior high/middle school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures in preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by junior high/ middle school students and ways to create positive environments for learning.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for 10 weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching in the Junior High/Middle School
description: Required for the standard license in junior high/middle school education. Simultaneous registration in EDJHM 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for 10 weeks in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Junior High/Middle School
description: Elective studentteaching experience enables students to complete a full semester in a fullday student teaching assignment in a public junior high/middle school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDJHM 460 and 462. A total of 5 hours of credit may be

title: Advanced Undergraduate Practicum in Junior High/Middle School Education
description: Provides direct, supervised experiences for students wanting to gain increased skill and knowledge regarding junior high/middle school teaching. Prerequisite: EDSEC 280. EDUCATION: LIBRARY (EDLIB)

title: Information Resources in Libraries
description: An examination of the most essential information sources in libraries, such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, periodical indexes, and special reference works in subject areas. Open to all students who desire a better understanding of the library as an information center.

title: School Media Center and Library Administration
description: Principles of planning, organizing, supervising, and evaluating school media center and public library services. Includes originating model program plans.

title: Technical Processing: Cataloging and Classification
description: Accepted procedures for systematic organization of book, audiovisual, computer, and other materials by using the Dewey Decimal Classification and constructing a library catalog. Working knowledge of OCLC terminal for searching, input, and manipulation of cataloging data.

title: Technical Processing: Online and Automation
description: Practice in cataloging and organizing materials of all types. Study of principles of online systems and microcomputerbased technical processing. Prerequisite: EDLIB 342.

title: Media Practicum
description: Supervised field experience for students in school media centers or libraries. Prerequisite: EDLIB 280 and approval of the program coordinator or the department chairperson. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Methods and Materials for School Library Media Centers
description: Methods and materials for teaching skills necessary for successful completion of assignments using resources of school library media centers and libraries.

title: Selection of Library Materials
description: Fundamental principles and objectives of selection of library materials. Development of skill in using reliable aids for selection and evaluation of materials for public, academic, and school libraries.

title: Materials for Children
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for the enrichment of library programs for preschool through upper elementary.

title: Materials for Young Adults
description: Reading and examining books and other materials for young adult programs. EDUCATION: MULTICULTURAL (EDMUL)

title: Introduction to Cross- Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Introduces prospective teachers to responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, and supporting personnel and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDMUL 206 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Intermediate Cross- Role Experiences in Secondary Schools
description: Advanced study of responsibilities assigned to various educational personnel in secondary schools through direct contact with teachers, counselors, administrators, supporting personnel, and students. Role differentiation will be explored. Prerequisite: EDMUL 200 or permission of the program director.

title: Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior in American Schools
description: Analyzes conditions that influence the behavior of ethnic and cultural group members in schools and educational settings. Lab included.

title: Advanced Study of Ethnic and Multicultural Group Behavior
description: Focuses on indepth analyses of many of the concepts introduced in EDMUL 205. Particular emphasis is on variables that contribute to development and maintenance of prejudice, stereotypes, racism and oppressive conditions. Equal emphasis will be given to instructional strategies for combating such behaviors. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205 or permission of the program director.

title: Instructional Strategies in Multicultured Schools
description: Theory and application of special instructional strategies of teaching and learning in secondary school classrooms with special emphasis on multicultured educational situations. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205, permission of the program director.

title: Bilingual Theory and Program Development
description: Survey of linguistic, cognitive, and cultural characteristics of bilingualism emphasizing the effects of these languagerelated features on bilingual/bicultural education in the United States. Emphasizes program design, model programs in operation, and legislative mandates.

title: Bilingual Evaluation and Methods
description: Considers the educational needs of bilingual students with specific regard to the evaluation of existing materials and appropriate bilingual classroom methodology.

title: Issues in Education and Professional Concerns of the Beginning Teacher
description: Opportunity to examine critically and to focus educational experience and knowledge on contemporary and personally significant problems of education. Emphasizes immediate professional concerns of prospective firstyear teachers. Prerequisite: EDMUL 301 or permission of the program director.

title: Understanding Cultural Diversity in American Education
description: Designed to prepare prospectiVe teachers to analyze lifestyles of different cultural groups. Emphasizing children's strengths within their cultural contexts will be an important focus. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205 or permission of the program director. EDUCATION: READING

title: Reading in Secondary School
description: Practical procedures for developing effective reading skills to be applied by all secondary classroom teachers. Focuses on relationships between the process of reading and learning of content, on planning to meet the total range of student reading needs, and on methods and materials to enhance comprehension and study skills in all areas of secondary school curriculum. Lab included. EDUCATION: SECONDARY (EDSEC)

title: Basic Concepts of Secondary • Education
description: Using classroom investigation and practical field experiences, examines the structure, function, and development of secondary education in the United States. Designed to help students make valid decisions about preparing for and functioning in teaching careers by studying professionalism, job requirements, employment opportunities, secondary school curricula, and the role of secondary education within the entire educational process.

title: Field Experience in Secondary Education
description: Provides direct experiences in working with students, teachers, educational organizations, community agencies, and other appropriate assignments for undergraduates who plan to enter secondary school teaching. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Teaching Principles, Curriculum, Classroom Management: Secondary School
description: Inducts the student into the teaching act. Includes development of specific technical skills, study of principles of teaching and evaluation, use of instructional media equipment, curriculum development and organization, and classroom management. Intensive inschool assignments, observation skills, participation, and direct contact with adolescents are required. Prerequisite: EDMUL 205; EDPSY 250 or 251, and approval to pursue a teaching curriculum. Prerequisite or parallel: EDPSY 290. Parallel: EDJHM 285. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Course titles will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study in Secondary Education
description: Independent study and research in secondary education. Topics and activities to be chosen in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject involved. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 3 hours of credit may be

title: High School Curriculum
description: General perspectives of curriculum principles, practices, and procedures common to secondary schools. Organizational structures, innovations, and intimate relationships between instruction and curriculum. Concurrently, students will choose areas of concentration or preparation as they relate to the total high school curriculum.

title: Discipline: Improving Student Behavior in Secondary Schools
description: Designed to prepare prospective secondary teachers to cope with discipline problems in all secondary school settings. Emphasizes skills and procedures for preventing or remedying disruptive behavior by secondary students and ways to create a positive environment for learning.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 462 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for 10 weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Secondary School
description: Required for the standard license in secondary education. Simultaneous registration in EDSEC 460 is required. Involves a fullday assignment for 10 weeks in a public secondary school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Elective Student Teaching: Secondary, Junior High/Middle, or All- Grade
description: Involves a fullday assignment for either three or six weeks in a public school. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. Parallel: EDSEC 460, 462 or EDALG 470, 472. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned.

title: General Innovations in Secondary Education
description: Innovative practices will be identified, defined, and analyzed relative to their effect on secondary schools. Creative, innovative instructional approaches will be used. Field trips or visitations to innovative secondary schools will be arranged when practical, and students will concentrate on innovative practices. EDUCATION: TECHNOLOGY (EDTEC)

title: Selection and Management of Audiovisual Equipment
description: Sources and principles of selection and management of audiovisual equipment and related devices. Preparation of bid specifications.

title: Introduction to Computers for Teachers K-12
description: Designed to provide prospective teachers with a basic understanding of curricular uses of computers in grades K-12.

title: Educational Technology 1
description: Theory and application of educational media and technology to improvement of teaching and learning in elementary and secondary schools. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Educational Technology 2
description: Basic knowledge and laboratory work concerning the uses of hypermedia and associated technologies for educational purposes. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Intermediate Study of Computers in the Schools
description: Designed to help students understand and develop the application of interactive technologies in teaching and learning. Prerequisite: EDTEC 320 or its equivalent.

title: Introduction to Computers and Library Automation
description: An introduction to computers and information systems available in libraries.

title: Electronic Information Retrieval Techniques
description: An overview of electronic information services and principles of information retrieval. Students develop search strategies to meet clients' information needs and conduct electronic searches in a supervised laboratory.

title: Selection of Audiovisual Materials and Microcomputer Software
description: Selection and evaluation of audiovisual materials and microcomputer software for instructional and management use in libraries. Systematic identification of sources and selection tools. Practice in selection and evaluation.

title: Production of Audiovisual Media
description: A project that meets the individual needs of undergraduates in the production of such instructional media as video recordings, filmstrips, slide sets, and tape recordings.

title: Educational Information Systems
description: The study of design, installation and administration of educational information systems: computers, local area networks, extended local area networks, and Internet. Prerequisite: EDTEC 355 or permission of the instructor. EDUCATION j. Merbler, Chairperson; D. Ahlersmeyer, L. DuncanMalone, D. Feldman, A. Hadadian, L. Hargrove, E. Lynch, J. Poteet, J. Yssel The Department of Special Education prepares teachers to work with those who are deaf as well or who have mild, moderate, or severe disabilities or serious emotional handicaps. The department also provides training in early childhood special education and American Sign Language interpretation. TEACHING MAJOR IN SPECIAL EDUCATION (ALL-GRADE): HEARING IMPAIRMENTS, 129-131 hours PREFIX NO SHORT TITLE CR HRS General Studies, 51-53 hours Humanities

title: American Sign Language 1
description: Introduction to sign language systems including fingerspelling and American Sign Language (ASL). Development of receptive and expressive skills in sign language is emphasized.

title: American Sign Language 2
description: Designed to improve conversational skills in American Sign Language to a functional level for expressive and receptive use in educational and other settings. Introduction to issues related to deaf culture. Prerequisite: SNLNG 351 or permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 3
description: Emphasizes the development of conversational skills in American Sign Language and stresses vocabulary building and interpretation of culturally related cues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 452 and permission of the department chairperson.

title: American Sign Language 4
description: Advanced development of American Sign Language fluency in occupational and professional settings. Special emphasis is given to sign dialects and related deaf cultural issues. Prerequisite: SNLNG 453 and permission of the department chairperson. SIGN LANGUAGE

title: Interpreting Process: Theories and Practice
description: Discussion of models of interpreting, analysis, and monitoring in both English and American Sign Language. Prerequisite: admission into interpreter trainingprogram, SPCED 240 or the equivalent, and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 320, 330.

title: Interpreting Practicum
description: Lecture and supervised field experience in a variety of interpreting settings. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Survey of the Interpreting Field
description: Overview of the field of interpreting including observations of working interpreters, discussion of roles and responsibilities, and the RID Code of Ethics. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305.

title: Interpreting Video Laboratory
description: Observation, simulation, and related practice of interpreting skills. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 305, 400, or 410. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Survey of Interpreting Field 2
description: Advanced examination of various interpreter placements including educational, medical, legal, etc. Emphasizes development of specialized vocabularies for placements. Prerequisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310.

title: Interpreting Process: Transliteration
description: Advanced techniques of expressive and receptive interpreting and transliteration. An indepth examination of RID ethics. Includes lecture, discussion, and opportunities for conversing with deaf people. Prerecyuisite: SNITP 320 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Advanced Interpreting
description: Continuation of SNITP 400 with emphasis on developing fluency in expressive and receptive communication at all levels. Topics include signtovoice and voicetosign interpretation issues and tactics and an analysis of unique problems associated with translation between oral and signbased language systems. Prerequisite: SNITP 400 and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 310, 330.

title: Interpreting Internship
description: Intensive field experience with placements in at least two different interpreting settings over a 15-week period. Supervision and regular performance feedback and discussion are stressed. Prerequisite: preprofessional checkout andpermission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 440.

title: Professional Seminar
description: Discussion and examination of problems and issues arising during the interpreting internship. Contemporary issues in interpreting will also be presented and discussed. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SNITP 420.

title: Introduction to Exceptional Children
description: An introduction to definitions, characteristics, and educational needs of children who deviate from normality in mental, physical, social, and emotional ways. Examines federal and state legal bases for education of exceptional children.

title: Management Strategies for Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for effective management of the preschool disabled child's home and preschool learning environments. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 or its equivalent.

title: Developmental Methods with Preschool Disabled Children
description: Examines instructional methodology and curricular practices for developing thepreschool disabled child's cognitive, language, creative, and physical environments. Thesedevelopmental components will be studied based on current instructional practices with preschool disabled children.

title: Practicum—Teaching Young Disabled Children
description: Students work with disabled children in a supervised teaching practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of disabled children. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Microcomputers and the Exceptional Learner
description: Introduction to microcomputer applications in special education through orientation to hardware, programming experience, word processing, and special purpose software. Also emphasizes teaching strategies for introducing microcomputers to children in the classroom.

title: History of Education of Deaf Persons and Psychology of Deafness
description: Introduces a comprehensive sociohistorical and contemporary overview of deaf culture and psychoeducational issues in America and Europe.

title: Education of Preschool Hearingand Language-Impaired Children
description: The development of oral communication in preschool hearingimpaired children. Directed observations of both hearing and hearingimpaired classes, home visitations, and the parenttraining program. Prerequisite: EDPSY 250.

title: Practicum in Special Education
description: Observation and assistance of teachers in special classes for exceptional children. Prerequisite: SPCED 201. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Human Relations and Consulting Skills for Special Educators
description: Examines human relations strategies and skills that will help teachers of exceptional children build trust and understanding with other professionals and parents of the child. Skills are acquired through simulation and practicum modules. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C or permission of the department chairperson. 299X Experimental/Developmental Topics. (3-6) Topics relevant to the discipline. Topics will be announced before each semester. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Independent Study
description: Designed to meet the needs of students who wish to conduct independent study, field work, or research in special education. Prerequisite: Permission of the department chairperson. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Legal and Procedural Foundations of Special Education
description: Studies court cases, statelevel legislation, and related historical events that preceded passage of PL 94-142. Covers definitions, procedural requirements, and legal safeguards of PL 94-142 and PL 99-457 as implemented in Indiana Rule S-1. Prerequisite: SPCED 201 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Principles of Behaviorology in Special Education
description: Intermediatelevel course designed to enable special education professionals to increase their contributions to the field by adding the scientific foundations of behaviorology to their repertoires. Prerequisite: EDPSY 306 or its equivalent.

title: Introduction of Behavior Disorders
description: Introduction to the history of educating children with behavior disorders; the problems of defining, assessing, and treating behavior disorders; and types and causes of disordered behavior. Prerequisite: SPCED 201.

title: Educating Elementary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled elementary school children. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Educating Secondary Students with Behavior Disorders
description: Educational assessments, methods, materials, and programs for seriously emotionally disabled youth. For future teachers of students with behavior disorders. Prerequisite: SPCED 332, 334, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Advanced Practicum in Special Education
description: A continuation of SPCED 266 emphasizing the application of teaching methodologies. Projects associated with specialty methods courses (SPCED 334 or 366 or 376 or 378 or 474) will be completed. Prerequisite: SPCED 266 with agrade of C or better. Parallel: SPCED 334 or 366 or 376 or 378 or 474. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Psychology and Physiology of Physical Disability
description: Designed for future teachers of disabled or other healthimpaired children with special emphasis on research findings in regard to children with cerebral palsy and other organic conditions. Topics include etiology, assessment, and dynamic understanding necessary to educate children with physical disabilities in the classroom. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Introduction to Mild Disabilities
description: Studies psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to mild disabilities. Compares and differentiates historical and contemporary definitions of mental retardation and learning disabilities. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 301, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Persons with Mental Retardation
description: Studies various types and degrees of retardation; the psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to retardation. Emphasizes etiology, assessment, and issues. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; BIO 453; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assessment in Special Education
description: Educational assessment practices with exceptional children with emphasis on curriculumbased assessment and informal tests. Role of the special educator on the multidisciplinary evaluation team. Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 371; EDPSY 345.

title: Methods of Teaching the Mildly Disabled
description: Studies techniques of teaching children and adults with mild disabilities. Emphasis is placed on the process by which content is taught to students of all age levels within the least restrictive environment. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Educating Persons with Severe Disabilities
description: Studies persons with moderate, severe, orprofound mental retardation, orthopedic or other health impairments, or autism. Topics include assessment strategies, instructional planning, and research on education in the least restrictive environment. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Educational Methods for Persons with Physical and Multiple Disabilities
description: Examines environmental adaptations, curriculum, and teaching and management methods for the instruction of persons with orthopedic impairments or special health problems. Emphasizes multidisciplinary practices and procedures based on research in education and allied fields. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378.

title: Educating Youth and Adults with Severe Disabilities
description: Introduction to the concept of lifelong educational needs of persons with severe disabilities. Topics include career education, vocational and employment programming, transition from school to work, and other educational issues for youth and adults. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378, 379; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assessment of the Young Disabled Child
description: Procedures for assessing young children with disabilities, infancy through age 6. Use of observational techniques and formal and informal assessment methodology will be investigated.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of psychological characteristics and educational needs of gifted and talented children in the schools. Definitions of giftedness and identification procedures are studied; review of current and past practices in the field.

title: Speech Development for Deaf Persons
description: Historical and current views of teaching speech to deaf children are studied with emphasis on current methods. Includes the knowledge foundation and practical methodology for teaching spoken English to deaf children. Writing behavioral objectives and an Individual Education Plan for spoken English is also included. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SPCH 216 or SPAA 101.

title: Practicum in Speech for Deaf Persons
description: Includes work with deaf children from different age ranges. Participants will practice planning, writing, and implementing relevant behavioral objectives. Prerequisite: SPCED 446.

title: Introduction to Language for Deaf Persons
description: Philosophy underlying various methods of language will be reviewed. Participants will compare and contrast various aspects of communication strategies. Topics include interactive language, written language, and reading. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SPAA 270.

title: Language Methods for Deaf Persons
description: Indepth view of various approaches to teaching language to deaf children. Emphasizes analyzing language samples taken from deaf children and forming taxonomies from the analysis. Includes writing behavioral objectives in the language areas of form, content, and use for inclusion in Individual Educational Plans. Prerequisite: SPCED 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to Deaf Persons
description: Explores various approaches to teaching reading and applies them to reading instruction for deaf children. Reviews reading assessment for deaf children as well as reading in other school subjects. Writing behavioral objectives and Individual Education Plans is included. Prerequisite: SPCED 454; EDRDG 400.

title: Student Teaching: Hearing Impaired
description: Required preservice teaching practica for students seeking licensure in special education hearingimpaired. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Special class organization, curriculum practices and procedures, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally disabled. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 372; EDRDG 430; MATHS 391. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Diagnostic and Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Disabled
description: Continuation of methods and materials for the mildly handicapped, begun in SPCED 474, with emphasis on use of the diagnostic prescriptive model to determine the learner's special needs and prescription of required curricular modifications in the IEP. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 474, or 376.

title: Educating Adolescents with Mild Disabilities
description: Includes transition models and planning, curriculum considerations, career and vocational education, collaboration with adult service agencies, and academic planning for secondary students with mild disabilities. A practicum experience in learning strategies is included. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 371 or 372.

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 9 hours' of credit must be earned, but a student may earn up to 12.

title: Student Teaching: Mild Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: mild disabilities. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Physically/ Multiply Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: physically/multiply handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Student Teaching: Seriously Emotionally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: seriously emotionally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: Severe Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: moderately mentally disabled, severely/profoundly mentally disabled, and multiply disabled. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. title: Canada: Cultural Crossroads
description: An interdepartmental introduction to the geography, history, government, economy, literature, art, and music defining Canada's individuality and international heritage. An examination of current issues on such topics as economic agreements, environment, education, health system, and multicultural relations. INfERDEPARTMENTAL (ID)

title: Freshman Seminar
description: Through individual assessment, readings on issues in education, and academic portfolios, skills necessary for freshman­year success are learned. Prerequisite: permission of the freshman academic advisor.

title: Related Field Experiences
description: Available for advanced standing credit only and not through registration. Departments may use this course to grant students university credit on programs under their jurisdiction for field experience meeting departmental crediting criteria. Students must apply formally to the department chairperson for such credit and supply supporting documentation. The department determines the amount of credit to be granted and notifies the registrar. The Office of Academic Advising is informed of how the credit is to be applied to students' programs. , A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Creating a Sustainable Future: The Clustered Minors Capstone
description: Capstone course for minor programs in environmentally sustainable practices. Topics vary. title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Survey of American studies as a field and as an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American civilization. Methods and theories of American studies will be discussed, along with major themes and topics in American life and thought. Not open to students who have credit in HIST 101.

title: Reading and Independent Study
description: Topics for independent study and research to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor who has expertise in the area involved. Prerequisite: permission of the American Studies director. A total of 3 hours of credit may be earned.

Space is limited and there may not be enough space for every applicant who meets the minimum requirements. •Applicants with a record of substance abuse or conviction of violations of federal, state, or local laws related to controlled substances for any offense (misdemeanor or felony) should know they may not be eligible for licensure as a registered nurse. • Applicants who have met the prerequisite course requirements and have earned the highest gradepoint average stand the best chance of being admitted to the program. Students who have achieved the minimum gradepoint average required to apply for admittance to the program should understand they may not be selected for admission because of their gradepoint average rank. • There are two ways to earn admission to the baccalaureate nursing program, Prenursing and General Applicant. The Prenursing route (which might be described as "early" admission) is open only for students who meet certain criteria that define the Prenursing Pool. Space available in the Prenursing Pool is limited; therefore admission is highly competitive. The General Applicant route is for other students, including transfer students, who compete for any remaining open slots in the baccalaureate nursing program in a given semester. •Admission to the first nursing course requires that the student sign an informed consent related to risks and safeguards inherent in the study of clinical nursing. ADMISSION Prenursing Pool Nursing 77 Students in the Prenursing Pool are guaranteed placement in the baccalaureate nursing major during the assigned semester. They must meet certain criteria to be eligible to be admitted. If admitted students meet the criteria to remain in the Prenursing Pool and complete (at the specified time) an application to enter the baccalaureate program, they will have priority placement in the baccalaureate nursing major. This means they are guaranteed placement in the baccalaureate nursing major during an assigned semester. Minimum Requirements (Regular track) • Admission to Ball State University •SAT minimum composite score of 1120 (with minimum of 480 verbal and 440 math) for a single SAT administration (one test settingscores from separate SAT test settings will not be combined); or ACT minimum composite score of 25 • High school rank in the upper 25% or a 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on Academic Honors Diploma, or GED of 57 • Successful completion of the following high school college prep courses: 3 years of high school math, including 1 year of algebra and 3 years of high school science, including biology and chemistry For other requirements and admission information contact the School of Nursing. General Pool Students who are interested in a baccalaureate nursing program but do not meet the criteria or are not selected as prenursing students may take course work from the Plan of Study for the Baccalaureate Degree Nursing Program. No application or permission is required to do this. However, after taking particular courses in the plan of study and meeting minimum requirements, students must complete an application form if they want to be considered for admission to the baccalaureate nursing major. It should be noted that satisfactory completion of the nursing prerequisites and fulfillment of minimum requirements do not guarantee admission to the baccalaureate nursing major. Minimum Requirements • Cumulative undergraduate gradepoint average of 2.75 or higher based upon a minimum 30 semester hours completed (preference will be shown to students who matriculated at Ball State University who meet this requirement). Students who meet the above criteria except for the gradepoint average of 2.75 may apply for provisional admission on a space available basis. • Credit in CHEM 101 and BIO 113 with a grade of C or better • Credit in PSYSC 100 and SOC 100 •Credit in ANAT 201 and PHYSL 210 with a grade of C or better or these courses in progress at time application is filed For other requirements and admission information contact the School of Nursing. Minimum Requirements (Registered nurse track) • Graduation from an accredited National League of Nursing (NLN) school. The department also offers an interdepartmental major in mathematical economics. For information on this major, see Interdepartmental Programs, p. 44. Students may also select economics as a concentration area in either the teaching major or the teaching minor in social studies. A minor in economics is available to business and nonbusiness majors. Not all of these programs reflect the scope, nature, and quality of accomplishment and understanding expected of Ball State graduates by the Department of Telecommunications. Therefore, the department follows this policy to govern acceptance and application of credits transferred in the fields of radio, television, and film: 1. All 300- and 400-level telecommunications courses required for completion of a required option in the major must be completed at Ball State. title: Introduction to Art
description: Through a survey of art and artifacts from ancient through modern times and the historical and social elements that helped to shape them, course offers an intro<luction to the understanding and appreciation of painting, sculpture, and architecture. Open only to students not majoring in art.

title: History of Art Survey 1
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. Prehistoric through the end of European Middle Ages.

title: History of Art Survey 2
description: Introduction to art and architecture as social products of a global human history. Both the comparability and diversity of human social organizations and the role of visual culture in them will be discussed. From the fifteenth century to the present.

title: History of Three-Dimensional Design
description: Interdisciplinary study of Art 183 threedimensional design and function as applied to graphic design, exhibition design, architecture, and industrial design from the eighteenth century to the present with an emphasis on American and European design. Prerequisite: sophomore standing; AHS 100 or 102 or permission of the instructor. Open only to art majoni.

title: Art in the United States 1
description: Investigation of the role visual culture has played in the United States as Americans attempted to situate themselves geographically, culturally, economically, and politically within their own society and within the world at large from ca. 1600 to ca. 1876. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Art in the United States 2
description: Traces the evolution in the United States of American visual arts from ca. 1876 to 1945 within the context of important social, historical, and intellectual events. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Aegean and the Greeks
description: Bronze A~e throu~h the Hellenistic period, covenng architecture, pottery, painting, sculpture, minor arts, and the mterrelationships of the Aegean Islands and Greek mairiland. Archeological data are discussed in terms of revelations about the areas' artistic and cultural development. Prerequisite: AHS 100or101 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Art of Rome
description: Art and architecture of early Rome and the Republic to the Late Empire. Architecture and urbanism as a vehicle for the political and cultural extension of the empire to the barbarian West and the Hellenized East; missionary role of historic reliefs; Roman concepts of personality and portraiture; and the growth of luxury arts: ornament, interior decoration, and collecting. Prerequisite: AHS 100or101 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Early Medieval Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture from the fourth through the tenth centuries in relation to the religious, political, and technological conditions of the period. Rural northwest Europe will be discussed in relation to urban societies in the East. Periods to be covered include early Christian, Merovingian, Carolingian, Ottonian, and Byzantine. Prerequisite: AHS 100 or 101 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Late Medieval Art
description: European art and architecture from the eleventh through the fourteenth centuries. Competing claims of royal and religious sponsors; shifts in center of production from rural to urban markets, monasteries to bishops' towns, in a period of economic advance, political transformation, and social unrest. Prerequisite: AHS 100or101 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Northern European Art 1300-1600
description: Northern European Renaissance art as a specifically northern mode of expression and representation reflecting social, political, religious, and other cultural particularities of specific areas (France, Germany, and southern and · northern Netherlands). Prerequisite: AHS 100or101 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Art of the Italian Renaissance 1300-1600
description: Art and architecture examined in terms of style, cultural meaning, context, and ideology. Inves­tigation of conditions of art production, change in role of artist, relationship between art theory and practice, and the question or concept of Renaissance. Prerequisite: AHS 100 or 102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Early Mddern Europe 1: Art from 1600 to 1750
description: Exploration of art and architecture of Europe, from the Counter-Reformation shrine of St. Peter to Louis XIV's palace at Versailles; from the Jesuit altarpieces in Antwerp to the Dutch Republic of Vermeer and Rembrandt and more. Italy, Spain, France, Germany, England, Ffanders, Netherlands. Prerequisite: AHS 100 or 102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Early Modern Europe 2: Art from 1750to1850
description: Art and architecture in the era of enlightenment and revolution, age of Napoleon, Restoration, reaction, reform, economic advance, and social unrest. From country gardens to urban boulevards, rococo, neoclassicism, romanticism, historicism, realism, and impressionism; England, France, Germany, Italy, Spain. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Modern Art
description: Pan-European investigation of the visual arts from French impressionism to the post-World War II abstract expressionists. Special emphasis is on cultural definitions of modernity and modernism and the appearance and ideologies of the avant garde. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Contemporary Art
description: Exploration of ideas and issues surrounding the production, reception, marketing, interpretation, and criticism of painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, installations, performance, and video and other mixed media since World War II. International in scope. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Film History and Criticism
description: Emphasizes understanding cinematic works through the analysis of styles and techniques employed by filmmakers. The historical evolution of these styles and techniques will be addressed, as well as social, cultural, and political influences. Open to all students.

title: History of Photography
description: Introduction to problems in theory, analysis, and history of photography. Study of institutional and discursive orders in which photography functions and produces meaning. Exploration of new forms of critical pnotographic practice. Prerequisite: AHS 100or102 or permission of the instructor. Open to all students.

title: Asian Art
description: General survey of art and architecture in south, southeast, central, and east Asia from the prehistoric era to the advent of the industrial era. Emphasizes characteristic forms, techniques, and art theory in the context of developments in society and religion. Prerequisite: AHS 100 or 101 or permission of the instructor.

description: Survey and investigation of a particular topic, problem, or issue in art history with emphasis on those not covered in other courses (women in art, history of museums and collecting, problems in methodology, etc.). title: Voice Techniques
description: Development of fundamental vocal performance technique. Examination of performance problems, diagnostic techniques, teaching strategies, vocal anatomy and acoustics, care of the voice, and other specialized topics related to singing instruction in school settings.

title: Basic Music for Classroom Teachers
description: Designed to build on the future teacher's sensory musical experience toward development of basic music reading, use of social and keyboard instruments, and expansion of acquaintance with the heritage of the world's music. A correlated laboratory session is scheduled.

title: Teaching Music in the Elementary Classroom
description: Development of basic music reading skills and classroom and keyboard instrument skills; focuses on methods for presenting appropriate musical experiences and materials to children. Open only to elementary education, special education, and early childhood education majors.

title: Field Experience in Music Teaching
description: Observation and application of specialized music teaching techniques. Prerequisite: MUSED 200. Open only to students registered in MUSED 351, 352, 353, 355, or 356. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 2 in any one semester or term.

title: Elementary General Music Methods 1
description: Introduction to general music for grades K~. Explores the philosophy of general music teaching, concepts and skills, use of materials and equipment, and specialized approaches to elementary music education. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Elementary General Music Methods 2
description: Continuing study of music teaching methodology for grades K~. Emphasis on curriculum development. Prerequisite: MUSED 351.

title: Secondary General Music Methods
description: Focuses on philosophy, techniques, and materials needed to teach a required general music course in middle and high school settings. Emphasizes teaching skill development as well as the musical characteristics and needs of adolescents. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Instrumental Music Methods
description: Examines issues related to the teaching of instrumental music. Special emphasis on program goals and curriculum development, instructional planning, and materials and techniques designed for teaching musical concepts in performance class or lesson settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200. ·

title: Choral Music Methods
description: Examines issues related to the teaching of choral music. Special emphasis on program goals and curriculum develop­ment, instructional planning, and materials and techniques designed for teaching musical concepts in performance class or lesson settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Administration of School Music Programs
description: Explores practical ideas, print resources, and computer applications related to efficient administration of instrumental and choral music programs. Topics include recruitment, handbooks, scheduling, budgets, purchasin~ libraries, . inventories, fund raising, parent groups, facilities, concerts, and trips. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Music in the Elementary School
description: Covers current teaching and learning strategies in music. Focuses on appropriate musical experiences and matenals for children. Prerequisite: MUSED 265. Not open to music majors.

title: Instrumental Laboratory
description: Laboratory ensemble taken as participant first, then as a conductor in conjunction with MUSPE 390. Focuses on instru­mental rehearsal techniques and instrumental literature for the secondary school teacher. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than .5 in any one semester or tenn.

title: Choral Laboratory
description: Laboratory chorus taken as participant first, then as conductor in conjunction with MUSPE

title: Orchestra Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of orchestra literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching Music 199 problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recordings. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Band Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of band literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recordings. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Choral Literature for School Ensembles
description: Review of choral literature appropriate for elementary and secondary school ensembles. Major publishers, composers, arrangers, and common performance and teaching problems will be considered. Seminar discussion will use sample scores and recordings. Prerequisite: MUSPE 290.

title: Music in Early Childhood Education
description: Study of musical development from birth to age eight, with emphasis on the preschool years. Appropriate musical play and small group activities are explored. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Recent Trends in Teaching Piano 1
description: Approaches to the child beginner, the adult beginner, class procedures in public school, educational publications; a graded curriculum, basic musicianship through keyboard study, and the analysis and development of specific pianistic skills.

title: Marching Band Techniques
description: Organization and administration of marching bands in school settings. Principles and objectives, show construction, field maneuvers, rehearsal techniques, music selection, and charting techniques will be studied. Prerequisite: MUSED 200; MUSCH 340.

title: Directing Musicals, Madrigals, and Jazz Show Choirs
description: Examines issues related to organizing and directing madrigal singers, vocal jazz ensembles, swing and snow choirs, and musical productions at the middle and high school levels. Topics include auditions, rehearsal techniques, choreography, literature, scheduling, performing, and management. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Instrument Maintenance and Repair
description: Laboratory setting used to develop practical skills in cleaning, lubricating, and repairing wind, percussion, and string instruments. Focuses on proper diagnostic techniques, tool and material selection, and minor repair procedures. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Methods of Organ Teaching
description: An examination of the methods of teaching the pipe organ. An application of these methods to recital literature and the music of the church. Prerequisite: previous organ study at the university level or permission of the director of the school.

title: Introduction to Orff-Schulwerk
description: Explores the principles of the child­centered aprroach to music developed by Carl Orf . Classroom activities involve movement, rhythm, speech, and the creative use of instruments. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Choral Literature and the Adolescent Voice
description: The adolescent voice and its development. Includes choral materials suitable for secondary school students; opportunities to sing and conduct standard choral literature; and consideration of newer publications for ensemble and solo singing.

title: Introduction to Dakroze Eurhythmics
description: Introduction to the philosophy, principles, and techniques of Dalcroze Eurhrthmics. Emphasizes the application o movement techniques to music teaching in elementary and secondary schools. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Kodaly Concept of Music Education
description: The philosof hical principles and the practica applications of these principles m teaching music in the elementary school form the frame­work of this course designed for music specialists.

title: Jazz Ensembles Techniques
description: Designed to introduce the style charac­teristics of jazz performance. Includes preparation in tbe administration and teaching of jazz ensembles in school settings. Prerequisite: MUSED 200 except for jazz/commercial music minors.

title: Class Guitar
description: Development of fundamental performance skills on the guitar for classroom and social use. Focuses on chordal accompaniment styles and their application to folk, popular, and children's song literature.

title: Teaching Multicultural Music
description: Exploration of music from various ethnic groups and cultures. Emphasizes techniques and materials to present music from various cultures to elementary and secondary students. Includes teaching projects and integration with traditional music curricula. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Independent Study in Music Education
description: An opportunity for superior students to conduct intensive stu.dy and research in a particular component of music education. . Prerequisite: permission of the director of the school. A total of 5 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

title: Special Topics in Music Education
description: Consideration of topics, problems, and issues in music education of special interest but not formally treated in other courses. Prerequisite: MUSED 200.

title: Workshop in Music Education
description: A oneor twoweek workshop on special topics in music education. A total of6 hours of credit may be earned, but no more than 3 in any one semester or term.

description: Assists students in developing individual popular singing styles. Concentrates on all facets of performance including audience­performer rapport, the performer­accompanist relationship, and microphone techniques. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

description: Study and public performance of standard operas of all periods. Combines the art Music 205 forms of music, drama, stagecraft, and dance in the study of coaching, acting, and stage technique. Prere.quisite: audition or previous experience. A total of 6 hours of credit may be earned.

description: Hymn playing and anthem accompaniments; formulation of adult and children's choirs in churches; congregational singing; service planning. Prere.quisite: MUSTH 112 and one year of organ study, or permission of the instructor.

description: Recommended for students deficient in elementary music language. Provides simplest basic concepts, symbols, readingskill drills, and terminology with supporting historical and systems information. Placement by level of experience.

description: Indepth study and application of sight singing techniques, dictation, chord recognition, error detection, and related activities. Placement by level of experience. Parallel: MUSTH 111.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Trainin~
description: Continuation of MUSTH 101 including more advanced sight singing, dictation, chord reco~tion, error detection, and related activities. Prerequisite: MUSTH 101.

title: Music Theory
description: Indepth study of music fundamentals including rhythm, melodic structure, fourpart harmony, elementary harmonic and structural analysis accompanied by writing, listening, and score study. Placement by level of experience. Must be taken in sequence. Parallel: MUSTH 101.

title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 111 including more advanced fourpart writing, analysis, score study, and listenin~. Prerequisite: MUSTH 111.

title: Acoustics
description: An introduction to physical acoustics with an emphasis on music and audio applications. Topics included are wave mechanics, acoustic measurements, tone and timbre analysis, tuning and temperament, and sound transduction.

description: Continuation of MUSTH 102 empha­sizing chromatic materials, modulating lines, fourpart dictation and aural analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 102.

title: Sight Singing and Ear Training

description: Emphasizes nineteenthcentury procedures through studies of comp<>sitional styles and analysis. Reci,wred mastering of diatonic and chromatic modulations and higher hierarchical chordal structures in tonal context and traditional forms. Advanced laboratory drill in analysis. title: Music Theory
description: Continuation of MUSTH 211, emphasizing practices of the later nineteenth century and the · twentieth century. Mastery of basic understanding of postromantic, impressionistic, expressionistic, neoclassical, serial, and other contemporary music required. Continued laboratory analysis. Prerequisite: MUSTH 211.

title: Music Composition 1
description: Study of music composition. Development of basic craftsmanship through use of compositional exercises, notational study, and creation of short instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 1~, 112.

title: Music Composition 2
description: Study of music composition. Development of basic craftsmanship through use of compositional exercises, notational study, and creation of short instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 102, 112.

title: Music Theory: Form and Analysis
description: An indepth study of large forms through intensive analysis, listening, research, and writing. Emphasizes individual student work coml'leted outside class to develop abilities in theoretical and composition investigation. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. Open only to music majors.

title: Music Theory: Eighteenth-Century Counterpoint
description: Indepth study of eighteenthcentury counterpoint that develops skills in analyzing and composing canons, inventions, and fugues. Prerequisite: MUSTH 311. Open only to music majors.

title: Composition
description: Private study. Development of basic craft through the writing of shorter instrumental and vocal compositions. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212 or by permission of the division chairperson with the recommendation of the theory instructor. ·

title: Composition
description: Continuation of MUSTH321. Prerequisite: MUSTH 321.

title: Choral Arranging
description: Scoring for choir and choral ensembles. Gives particular attention to voicing, soloistic treatment of voices, texts, and other elements of traditional and contemporary scoring. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Instrumentation and Orchestration
description: Instruments and their uses in orchestral practice. Develops creative writing concepts through orchestration. Principles of solo and combination writing are presented through analysis. Projects in solo and ensemble writing are required. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Compositional Practices of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
description: Studies .embracing general trends with focus (to be announced) on one or more composers, major works, or special developments of the period. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Band Arrangin~
description: Scoring for symphonic band, wmd ensemble, and other related groups. Emphasizes instrumentation, transposition, voicing, doubling, soloistic treatment, and scoring from piano or similar reduction. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Commercial Arranging
description: The study and analysis of arranging techniques used in commerciaf music. Emphasizes conventional and stylized conceptions of writing in commercial idioms with particular attention given to the composerarranger in the recording­s tudio environment. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Arranging Workshop
description: Laboratory for skill development in arranging. Individualized and project­oriented to prepare musicians to score spot commercials, show components, marching band shows, and background and mood sequences, as well as to compase for TV, films, radio, and media. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212. A total of 4 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Theory of Nineteenth-Century Music
description: Vocabulary, devices, tonal organization, and shapin~ forces that characterize the compositional practices of nineteenthcentury romanticism. Prerequisite: MUSTH 212.

title: Theory of Twentieth-Century Music

Edmonds, Assistant Dean The Honors College offers special courses, colloquia, seminars, and independent study designed to challenge talented students. In their first two years, students in the Honors College take honors sections of University Core Curriculum courses. Required core courses include three symposia in American contemporary civilization, global studies, and science, as well as a threecourse sequence in the humanities that investigates the great ideas of literature, science, philosophy, politics, and the fine arts. Honors professors often invite guest lecturers to furnish additional perspectives on topics under study. In the sophomore, junior, and senior years, students take at least two colloquia especially developed by honors faculty members to focus on critical issues in their areas of expertise. As seniors, students undertake the capstone of their work in honorsthe senior thesis or creative project, prepared under the guidance of a professor selected by the student. ~tudents also have the opportunity to do specialized departmental honors work in their majors and to apply for the Undergraduate Fellows Competition, which awards stipends for independent work with a faculty mentor. Students are often invited to meet with visiting lecturers or dignitaries in small groups and to take advantage of special programs. The Honors College curriculum is interdepartmental in nature, consisting of courses from a variety of departments. Admission to the Honors College is based primarily on high school preparation, test scores, and class rank. Students admitted to the Honors College must maintain a gradepoint average of at least 3.0 and must finish with a cumulative gradepoint average of at least 3.25. Transfer students may also enroll. For more information, write or call the dean of the Honors College, (765) 285-1024.
