title: Patient Care
description: Patient care skills needed to function in the clinical courses. Topics include medical terminology, basic life support, universal precautions and blood borne pathogens, first aid, and patient/staff interaction skills. Prerequisite: admission to the respiratory therapy program Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Cardiopulmonary Anatomy and Physiology
description: Designed to give an in­depth knowledge of the pulmonary and cardiac systems. Emphasizes the inter­relationships between the two systems. Prerequisite: PHYSL 207. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Basic Respiratory Care
description: Designed to familiarize students with all types of basic respiratory care and equipment in preparation for clinical practice. Prerequisite: PHYCS 106; admission to respiratory therapy program Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: General Pathology
description: A survey of disorders of the human body. Etiology, pathophysiology, and treatment will be discussed. Prerequisite: admission to the respiratory therapy program Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Cardiopulmonary Pharmacology
description: Indepth study of pharmacology, with special emphasis on cardiovascular and pulmonary medicines. Includes pharmacodynamics, dosage calculation, and clinical applications. Prerequisite: admission to the respiratory therapy program Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Clinical Practice 1
description: The student will administer oxygen and aerosol therapy, perform various respiratory treatments, and assess the effectiveness of therapy. Procedures will be performed at various clinical sites. Prerequisite: AHSC 300, 301, 302, 303, 304. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Pediatric Respiratory Care
description: Preparation to practice perinatal, neonatal, and pediatric respiratory care. Oxygen therapy, treatment modalities, mecnanical ventilation, and cardiopul­monary resuscitation will be addressed. Prerequisite: AHSC 300, 301, 302, 303, 304. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Mechanical Ventilation
description: Designed to familiarize students with mechanical ventilation, including evaluation of the patient, selection of therapy, patient management, and the equipment used for these tasks. Prerequisite: students must have completed all spring semester respiratory therapy courses, AHSC 300, 301,302,303,304. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Advanced Concepts in Allied Health Sciences
description: Topics to be chosen and investigated in consultation with an instructor with competence in the subject to be studied. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson.

title: Clinical Practice 2
description: The student will perform clinical activities required of advanced respiratory care practitioners. Emphasizes adult, pediatric, and neonatal patients in the critical care setting. Tecnniques learned in Clinical Practice 1 will be reinforced. Various clinical sites will be used. Prerequisite: AHSC 306, 307, 309. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Cardiopulmonary Monitoring and Diagnostics
description: The student will perform respiratory and hemodynamic monitoring and interpret the results. The student will also learn to perform and interpret pulmonary function tests, cardiopulmonary stress tests, and sleep studies. Instrumentation will be included. Prerequisite: AHSC 306, 307, 309. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Diseases of the Chest
description: The student will study the pathophysiology of cardiovascular, pulmonary, and chest wall diseases, as well as thoracic trauma. Etiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention will be discussed. Physiology and Health Science 341 Prerequisite: AHSC 306, 307, 309. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Cardiopulmonary Rehab and Home Care
description: The student will learn to evaluate patients with chronic cardiopulmonary illnesses, as well as develop a plan for their rehabilitation and home care. Applicable federal and state health care regulations will also be studied. Prerequisite: AHSC 306, 307, 309. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Respiratory Specialties
description: A variety of special topics pertinent to respiratory therapy. Prerequisite: students must have completed all summer semester respiratory therapy courses, AHSC 306, 307, 309. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Advanced Life Support
description: An in­depth study of the management of cardiopulmonary emergencies. Topics include airway management, EKG interpretation, pharmacological resuscitation, and defibrillation. Prerequisite: students must have completed all fall semester respiratory therapy courses, AHSC 406, 408, 409, 410, 411. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Clinical Practice 3
description: Continued management of patients in the critical care setting, emphasizing cardio­respiratory monitoring and assessment. Participation in patient rehabilitation and home care, advanced life support, pulmonary function and sleep studies, and special procedures will be included. Prerequisite: AHSC 406, 408, 409, 410, 411. Open only to respiratory therapy majors.

title: Independent Study in Allied Health

title: Politics: Today and Tomorrow
description: An introduction to the contemporary issues of national and world politics. Emphasizes both current and political events and longterm trends in politics.

title: American National Government
description: The organization and operation of national government as it relates to such current issues as civil rights, welfare, ecology, consumer protection, and international relations.

title: Citizen and the Law
description: To help understand citizen encounters with the legal system, this course explains the operation of the legal system and the palitical elements of the pertinent legal issues. Uses a variety of activities, fifrns, and lectures. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson or the paralegal program coordinator.

title: Introduction to Paralegalism
description: Explores concepts of paralegalism with emphasis on legal ethics and values, the development and future of the paralegal function in our present legal environ­ment, and a presentation of the concepts of litigation and legal procedure. Prerequisite: POIS 140.

title: Le~al Research and Writing
description: An analysis of court procedures a,nd appeal procedures, an indepth examination of reference sources available to attorneys, and improvement of research and writing skills. Prerequisite: POIS 141.

title: Litigation
description: For the advanced paralegal major focusing on litigation and related areas of paralegal responsi­bilities such as drafting interrogatories and writing complaints. Special attention given to learning the compilation of a trial notebook in preparation for litigation. Prerequisite: POIS 140,141,142, and permission of the department chairperson. °F!' only to legal assistance and legal adrrunistrahon majors.

title: Introduction to Planning
description: A survey of problems inherent in planning for cities and regions using contributions of such other disciplines as history, geography, sociology, and economics.

title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Scope and methods of the study of political science. After probing the basic nature of politics, the course examines political science as a systematic empirical discipline concerned with describing and explaining political phenomena. Substantial emphasis is placed on the use of computers as tools m the scientific study of politics.

title: State and Local Politics
description: Practices, politics, and structures of state and local governments in the United States with an emphasis on the Indiana experience.

title: Urban Government in the United States
description: Structure, functions, problems, and trends in city, urban, and metro­politan governments.

title: Family Law
description: Designed to acquaint students with legal problems in domestic relations. Covers legal problems involved in marriage, separation, divorce, child custody, adoption, and nonsupport.

title: Comparative Political Systems
description: A comparison of modem political systems as represented by the principal nations of the world.

title: Economic and Political Problems of Emerging Nations
description: Historical and contemporary problems of the less­developed nations. Conditions contributing to economic, political, and social change. Problems of economic development policies and programs within the institutional structure. Internal and external pressures that influence patterns of development. Prerequisite recommended: POLS 280. Not open to students who have credit inECON279.

title: American Foreign Policy
description: A survey of major issues in foreign policy formulation, an introduction to the process of making United States foreign policy, and an analysis of relevant American strategic doctrines.

title: International Relations
description: A survey of the formal relations among sovereign states in the international system, emphasizing the operation of diplomacy, the elements of power, the procedures for the settlement of disputes, and the various modes of conflict resolution.

title: Early Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of political thought of the early Mediterranean and medieval worlds that became the foundation of modem political theories and systems of the West. Emphasizes the writings of Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, St. Augustine, St. Thomas Aquinas, and Machiavelli.

title: Modern Western Political Thought
description: Analysis of selected writings of leading political theorists from the Age of Reformation to the present.

title: Communist Political Thought: From Marx to Present
description: A critical analysis and evaluation of Marxism, Leninism, Stalinism, Khrushchevism, pest-Khrushchev Communist ideology, and Maoism as a system of theoretical propositions and as an action program of an international movement.

title: Voter Polling Techniques

Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 266 (SNLNG 351 for hearing impairment majors), and 301 with grades of C or better and permission of the department chairperson. Parallel: SPCED 334 or 366 or 376 or 378 or 454 or 474. A total of 8 hours of credit may be earned.

title: Introduction to Persons with Physical Disabilities and Other Health Care Needs
description: Designed for future teachers and rehabilitation counselors of persons with physical, sensory, or health impairments. Etiology, physical and socialemotional characteristics, and educational considerations and implications are emphasized within a transdisqplinary habilitative/ rehabilitative team perspective. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Introduction to Mild Disabilities
description: Studies psychological, environ­mental, and cultural conditions that contribute to mild disabilities. Compares and differentiates historical and contemporary definitions of mental retardation and learning disabilities. Special Education 401 Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 301, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Introduction to Persons with Mental Retardation
description: Studies various types and degrees of retardation; the psychological, environmental, and cultural conditions that contribute to retardation. Emp.hasizes etiology, assessment, and issues. Prerequisite: SPCED 201; BIO 102; or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Assessment in Special Education
description: Educational assessment practices with exceptional children with emphasis on curriculumbased assessment and informal tests. Role of the special educator on the multidisciplinary evaluation team Prerequisite: SPCED 201, 371; EDPSY 345.

title: Methods of Teaching the Mildly Disabled
description: Studies tecfiniques of teaching children and adults with mild disabilities. Emphasizes the process by which content is taught to students of all age levels within the least restrictive environment. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Educating Children and Youth with Severe Disabilities
description: Introduces future teachers to students with moderate to profound mental retardation, multiple disabilities, or autism. Contemporary best practices and standards in integration opportunities, curriculum design, and positive supports for chalfenging behavior are presented and applied at the elementary and middle school levels. Prerequisite: SPCED 372.

title: Instructional Methods for Children and Youth with Severe Disabilities
description: Contemporary best practices and standards in Individual Education Plan development and instructional design and implementation in natural settings for students with severe disabilities are presented and applied at the elementary and middle school levels. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Educational Methods for Children and Youth with Physical and Multiple Disabilities
description: Contemporary best practices in curriculum design, instructional adaptations featuring high and low technology, environmental modifications, and physical and medical management suitab1e for students with physical and multiple disabilities or health impairments are presented within a transdisciplinary teaming model Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378.

title: Educating High School Students with Severe Disabilities
description: Contemporary best practices in instructional design, implementation, and monitoring for students with severe disabilities are presented and applied at the high school level. Topics include transitional planning, job training, group instruction, and advanced positive supports for challenging behavior. Prerequisite: SPCED 372, 377, 378, or permission of the department chairperson.

title: Practicum: Infants/foddlers and Preschoolers with Special Needs
description: Work with young children with special needs/disabilities in a supervised teaching practicum to acquire practical skills for planning and organizing activities to meet the needs of young children and their families. Prerequisite: permission of the department chairperson. A total of 12 hours of credit may he earned, hut no more than 6 in any one semester or term.

title: Education of Gifted Children
description: Examination of psychological charac­teristics and educational needs of gifted and talented children in the schoofs. Definitions of giftedness and identifi­cation procedures are studied; review of current and past practices in the field.

title: Speech Development for Deaf Persons
description: Historical and current views of teaching speech to deaf children are studied with emphasis on current methods. Includes the knowledge foundation and practical methodology for teaching spoken English to deaf children. Writing behavioral objectives and an Individual Education Plan for spoken En~lish is also included. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SPCH 216 or SPAA 101.

title: Practicum in Speech for Deaf Persons
description: Includes work with deaf children from different age ranges. Participants will practice planning, writin~ and implementing relevant behavioral objectives. Prerequisite: SPCED 446.

title: Introduction to Language for Deaf Persons
description: Philosophy underlying various methods of language will 0e .reviewed. Participants will compare and contrast various aspects of communi­cation strategies. Topics include interactive language, written language, and reading. Prerequisite: SPCED 240; SP AA 270.

title: Language Methods for Deaf Persons
description: Indepth view of various approaches to teaching language to deaf children. Emphasizes analyzing · language samples taken from deaf children and forming taxonomies from the analysis. Includes writing behavioral objectives in the language areas of form, content, and use for incfusion in Individual Educational Plans. Prerequisite: SPCED 454.

title: Teaching Reading and Elementary School Subjects to Deaf Persons
description: Explores various approaches to teaching reading and applies them to reading instruction for deaf children. Reviews reading assessment for deaf children as well as reading in other school subjects. The writing ofbehavioral objectives and IndividuarEducation Plans is included. Prerequisite: SPCED 454; ED ROG 400.

title: Student Teaching: Hearing Impaired
description: Required preservice teaching practica for students seeking licensure in special education hearing impaired. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 6 hours of credit must be earned; a student may earn up to 12.

title: Methods and Materials for the Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Special class organization, curriculum practices and procedures, and methods and techniques used in the instruction of the mildly mentally disabled. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 372; EDRDG 430; MATHS 391. Parallel: SPCED 361.

title: Diagnostic and Prescriptive Teaching of the Mildly Disabled
description: Continuation of methods and materials for the mildly handicapped, begun in SPCED 474, with emphasis on use of the diagnostic prescriptive model to determine the learner's special needs and prescription of required curricular modifications in the Individual Education Plans. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 474, or 376.

title: Educating Adolescents with Mild Disabilities
description: Includes transition models and planning, curriculum considerations, career and vocational education, collaboration with adult service agencies, and academic planning for secondary students with mild disabilities. A practicum experience in learning strategies is included. Prerequisite: SPCED 266, 371, or 372.

title: Student Teaching: Mildly Mentally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: mildly mentally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 9 hours of credit must be earned; a student may earn up to 12.

title: Student Teaching: Mild Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education: mild disabilities. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student, Teaching: Children and Youth with Physical Disabilities and Health Impairments
description: Required for licensure in special education areas of physical disabilities and health impairments. Special Education 403 Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may he earned.

title: Student Teaching: Seriously Emotionally Disabled
description: Required for licensure in special education: seriously emotionally handicapped. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching.

title: Student Teaching: q1ildren and Youth with Severe Disabilities
description: Required for licensure in special education areas of moderate mental retardation, severe mental retardation, profound mental retardation, multiple disabilities, and autism. Prerequisite: admission to student teaching. A total of 12 hours of credit may be earned.
